title: E04-027 Network sampler: rates, totals, state
description:
## Context
The network sampler behind the engine's `Net` worker (1 Hz while network is demanded): per-interface download and upload rates from one `pread` of `/proc/net/dev`, totals since boot, and the connection state. Sources: ADR-016 (network row), ADR-008 (rates from elapsed time, counter rules, generations, suspend), PERF-054 (state read per 1 Hz tick), PERF-055 (download = rx), PERF-056 (Total downloaded, Total uploaded), R-052.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/sample/net.rs`:
```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct IfaceId { pub name: Arc<str>, pub generation: u32 }

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct NetIfReading {
    pub name: Arc<str>,
    pub rx_bps: Measured<f64>, pub tx_bps: Measured<f64>,        // bytes per second; bits are a UI unit choice
    pub total_rx_bytes: Measured<u64>, pub total_tx_bytes: Measured<u64>,
    pub state: Measured<OperState>,
    pub flags: SampleFlags,
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct NetReading { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub validity: Validity, pub ifaces: Vec<NetIfReading> }   // order of set_interfaces

pub struct NetSampler { /* root, net/dev KeptFile, buf, lines, counters keyed by name, prev clock */ }
impl NetSampler {
    pub fn new(root: SysRoot) -> Self;
    pub fn set_interfaces(&mut self, ifaces: &[IfaceId]);           // after each enumeration
    pub fn sample(&mut self, out: &mut NetReading);                 // = sample_at(Clock::now(), out)
    pub fn sample_at(&mut self, clock: Clock, out: &mut NetReading);
    pub fn reset_baselines(&mut self);
}
```
Rules:
- Match `/proc/net/dev` lines to interfaces by name. `rx_bps = Counter::update(rx_bytes, t, generation).per_sec`, same for tx. Totals are the raw counters (`Valid` whenever the line exists).
- Counter rules as in E04-003: first sample `WarmingUp`; backwards gives `WarmingUp` with `RESET`; new generation gives `WarmingUp` with `GAP_BEFORE`; resume (`resumed_between`) or `reset_baselines` gives `WarmingUp` and `flags = GAP_BEFORE` for every interface.
- `state` from `netif::read_oper_state` on every sample.
- An interface in `set_interfaces` with no line in the file: every field `Missing`.
- Read failure of `/proc/net/dev`: `out.validity = err.validity()` and every rate and total takes it.

Hand fixture `tests/fixtures/net-two-steps/step0/` and `step1/`: `proc/net/dev` with `eth0` (rx 1,000,000 then 3,500,000; tx 500,000 then 1,500,000) and `sys/class/net/eth0/{ifindex,type,operstate}` (`2`, `1`, `up`), plus `step2` where `eth0` rx is 100.

- **Given** step2 at t = 2 s **Then** `rx_bps` is `WarmingUp` and `flags` contains `RESET`.

title: E04-028 Network interface details: speed, MAC, driver
description:
## Context
P2 network details rows from sysfs: Link speed, MAC address, Interface index and Driver. Read at enumeration time, not per tick. Adapter name (udev hwdb), IP addresses and Wi-Fi bitrates are other sources (open item E04-OI-2; NetworkManager in E12). Sources: PERF-056 (sysfs `speed` in Mb/s, -1 shows `Not reported`; `address`, `ifindex`, `device/driver` basename).

## Deliverable
Add to `crates/tl-collect/src/parse/netif.rs`:
```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct IfaceDetails {
    pub speed_mbps: Measured<u32>,       // -1 or EINVAL on read -> Unsupported ("Not reported")
    pub mac: Measured<Option<Arc<str>>>, // contents of `address`, trimmed; empty -> None
    pub ifindex: u32,
    pub driver: Option<Arc<str>>,        // basename of readlink(device/driver)
}
pub fn read_details(root: &SysRoot, name: &str, buf: &mut Vec<u8>) -> IfaceDetails;
```
Rules:
- `speed`: decimal; the value `-1`, or a read that fails with `EINVAL` (the kernel returns it for interfaces that are down), gives `Unsupported`; other errors give `err.validity()`.
- `address`: `00:00:00:00:00:00` is still returned as-is (the UI shows it).
- `driver`: `readlink` of `device/driver`, last path component; absent gives `None`.

Fixture additions to `tests/fixtures/netif-kinds/sys/class/net/`: `eth0/speed` = `1000`, `eth0/address` = `aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:01`, `eth0/device/driver` symlink to `../../../bus/pci/drivers/e1000e`; `wlan0/speed` = `-1`; `tailscale0` without `speed`.

- **Given** `wlan0` **Then** `speed_mbps.validity == Unsupported`.
- **Given** `tailscale0` **Then** `speed_mbps.validity == Missing` and `driver == None`.

title: E04-029 Sensors sampler: temperatures and fans
description:
## Context
The sensors sampler behind the engine's `Sensors` worker (1 Hz while sensors or fans are demanded): every hwmon temperature and fan with its label, RPM, PWM percent and control mode. GPU hwmon chips are left to the GPU page. Sources: ADR-016 (sensors and fans row, hwmon files kept open), ADR-003 (`DeviceIdentity::Sensor { chip, label }`, `Fan { chip, index }`), PERF-068 (GPU fan and temperature are not on the Fans pages), PERF-076 (fan rows: Fan speed, PWM %, Control mode, Chip; `fanN_max`), PERF-077, PERF-005 (fan key uses the hwmon name, device path and index).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/sample/sensors.rs`:
```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct TempReading { pub chip: Arc<str>, pub chip_device_path: Option<Arc<str>>, pub n: u16, pub label: Arc<str>, pub celsius: Measured<f32> }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct FanReading {
    pub chip: Arc<str>, pub chip_device_path: Option<Arc<str>>, pub n: u16, pub label: Option<Arc<str>>,
    pub rpm: Measured<u32>, pub max_rpm: Option<u32>,
    pub pwm_pct: Measured<f32>,          // Unsupported when the chip has no pwm<n>
    pub control: Measured<FanControl>,   // Unsupported when there is no pwm<n>_enable
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct SensorsReading { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub temps: Vec<TempReading>, pub fans: Vec<FanReading> }

pub struct SensorsSampler { /* root, chips, KeptFiles per input, buf */ }
impl SensorsSampler {
    pub fn new(root: SysRoot) -> Self;                      // runs rescan()
    pub fn rescan(&mut self);                               // hwmon::enumerate again (device enumeration, every 5 s)
    pub fn chips(&self) -> &[HwmonChip];
    pub fn sample(&mut self, out: &mut SensorsReading);     // = sample_at(Clock::now(), out)
    pub fn sample_at(&mut self, clock: Clock, out: &mut SensorsReading);
}
```
Rules:
- Chips whose `name` is in `hwmon::GPU_HWMON_NAMES` are skipped entirely.
- Temps: one `TempReading` per `temp<n>_input` of every other chip, in chip then n order. `label` is the `temp<n>_label` text, else `temp<n>`. Value from `parse_millidegrees`.
- Fans: one `FanReading` per `fan<n>_input`. `max_rpm` read once at `rescan` from `fan<n>_max` (absent gives `None`). `pwm_pct` from `pwm<n>` (same n) with `parse_pwm_pct`; `control` from `pwm<n>_enable` with `parse_fan_control`.
- Every value file is a `KeptFile` (ADR-016), created at `rescan`. Read errors set that value's validity from `err.validity()`.
- Hiding fans that read 0 RPM for the whole session with no label (PERF-076 "not connected") is decided by the engine and UI from the readings; the sampler reports every fan.
- No rates, so no `WarmingUp`: the first sample is `Valid` where readable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the `fans` fixture (E04-011) **When** sampled **Then** fans are `nct6797` fan1 (rpm 1200, `pwm_pct == Valid(50.19608)`, `control == Valid(Automatic)`), `nct6797` fan2 (rpm 0, `pwm_pct` and `control` `Unsupported`), `single` fan1 (rpm 900); no fan or temp from the `amdgpu` chip.
- **Given** the `fans` fixture **Then** temps are `nct6797` `temp1` 40.0 and `temp2` 45.0, and `single` `temp1` 35.0, with labels `temp1`, `temp2`, `temp1`.
- **Given** `no-fans` **Then** `fans` is empty and the `k10temp` temp has label `Tctl` and value 48.25.
- **Given** a temp file made unreadable in a temp copy (non-root) **Then** that reading is `Restricted` and others stay `Valid`.
- **Given** `owner-desktop` **When** sampled **Then** the result matches the insta snapshot.
- **Given** a hwmon chip added to a temp copy after `new` **When** `rescan` then `sample` **Then** the new chip's readings appear.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/sample/sensors.rs`: replace the stub (code plus tests)

## Tests
- `src/sample/sensors.rs::tests::fans_fixture_fans`, `::fans_fixture_temps`, `::gpu_chip_skipped` (covered by the first two, assert explicitly), `::no_fans_fixture`, `::unreadable_temp_restricted` (skips as root), `::owner_desktop_snapshot`, `::rescan_picks_up_new_chip`.

- Validity: `Valid`, `Unsupported`, `Missing`, `Restricted`, `Failed`.

- Privacy: N/A

title: E04-001 tl-collect crate skeleton, module tree and CollectError
E04-002 SysRoot, KeptFile and bounded read helpers
E04-003 Counter rules: rates, resets, suspend gap, stale threshold
E04-004 smaps_rollup fd cache (128 entries)
E04-005 cargo xtask capture-fixture with scrubbing
description:
## Context
`cargo xtask capture-fixture <name>` copies the files tasklens reads from the running machine into `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/<name>/` as a fake root, scrubbing anything personal. Parser and sampler tests in E04, E05 and E06 run against these fixtures. This bead writes the subcommand module; E04-006 wires it into `xtask/src/main.rs`. Sources: ADR-013 (parser fixtures, scrub rules), ADR-016 (the files read), ADR-015 (what is never exported), PERF entries of E04 for the `/sys` file list.

## Deliverable
`xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs` (xtask may use only `serde`, `serde_json`, `anyhow` and std, ADR-001):
```rust
pub fn run(args: &[String]) -> anyhow::Result<()>;   // CLI entry: capture-fixture <name> [--force]
pub struct CaptureOpts { pub max_pids: usize /* 50 */, pub force: bool }
/// Testable core: copies from `src_root` (normally "/") into `out_dir`.
pub fn capture(src_root: &Path, out_dir: &Path, opts: &CaptureOpts) -> anyhow::Result<CaptureReport>;
pub struct CaptureReport { pub copied: Vec<PathBuf>, pub skipped: Vec<(PathBuf, String)> }
// scrub helpers, pub(crate) for tests:
fn user_map(passwd: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)>;      // [(real name, "userN")]
fn scrub_text(text: &str, users: &[(String, String)], hostname: Option<&str>) -> String;
fn scrubbed_cmdline(comm: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>;            // b"<comm>\0--arg\0"
fn is_serial_file(basename: &str) -> bool;
```
CLI rules:
- `<name>` must match `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, else exit with the error `fixture name must be lowercase letters, digits and dashes`.
- Output directory: `<workspace root>/crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/<name>/`, where the workspace root is the parent of `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` (the `xtask` directory). If it exists and `--force` is absent, exit with `fixture <name> exists; pass --force to replace it`. With `--force`, delete it first.
- At the end print, to stdout, `copied N files, skipped M` and then one line per skipped path with its reason (xtask may print; `clippy::print_stdout` is allowed locally in xtask with `#[allow(clippy::print_stdout)]` on `run`).
- Also write `<out>/CAPTURE.txt`: line 1 `kernel <contents of /proc/sys/kernel/osrelease>`, line 2 `captured-by cargo xtask capture-fixture`, then `copied:` and `skipped:` sections listing relative paths. No date, no hostname, no user name.

Files copied (paths relative to `src_root`; a path that does not exist is silently left out; a read error such as `EACCES` puts it in `skipped` with the reason `permission denied` or the error text):
- `proc/stat`, `proc/meminfo`, `proc/vmstat`, `proc/diskstats`, `proc/net/dev`, `proc/loadavg`, `proc/sys/fs/file-nr`, `proc/swaps`, `proc/cpuinfo`, `proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, `proc/sys/kernel/osrelease`.
- `proc/self/mountinfo` written to `proc/self/mountinfo` with `proc/self` as a real directory; `proc/self/ns/net` recreated as a symlink with the same target text (for example `net:[4026531840]`).
- Per process: the first `max_pids` (50) numeric entries of `proc/`, in ascending numeric order, whose `stat` can be read. For each: `stat`, `statm`, `status`, `io`, `comm`, `cgroup`, and `cmdline` replaced by `scrubbed_cmdline(comm)` where `comm` is the file's content without the trailing newline. A file that fails to read (often `io` of another user) goes to `skipped`.
- `/sys`, expanding `*` as a directory glob and `N` as any decimal suffix:
  - `sys/devices/system/cpu/{online,possible,present}`; `cpuN/online`; `cpuN/cpu_capacity`; `cpuN/topology/{core_id,physical_package_id,die_id,thread_siblings_list,core_siblings_list}`; `cpuN/cache/indexN/{level,type,size,shared_cpu_list}`; `cpuN/acpi_cppc/nominal_freq`; `cpufreq/policyN/{related_cpus,affected_cpus,cpuinfo_avg_freq,scaling_cur_freq,base_frequency,bios_limit,cpuinfo_max_freq,cpuinfo_min_freq,scaling_driver,scaling_governor,energy_performance_preference,amd_pstate_prefcore_ranking}`
  - `sys/devices/cpu_core/cpus`, `sys/devices/cpu_atom/cpus`, `sys/firmware/acpi/platform_profile`
  - `sys/class/hwmon/hwmonN/{name,tempN_input,tempN_label,fanN_input,fanN_label,fanN_max,pwmN,pwmN_enable}` and the `device` symlink of each `hwmonN`
  - `sys/block/*/{dev,size,removable,ro,stat,queue/rotational,device/model,device/type,dm/name}`; `sys/block/*/*/{dev,size,partition,start}` (partitions); the symlinks in `sys/block/*/holders/` and `sys/block/*/slaves/`; `sys/block/zram*/{disksize,mm_stat,comp_algorithm}`; `sys/block/*/device/hwmonN/...` and `sys/block/*/device/hwmon/hwmonN/...` with the hwmon files above
  - `sys/class/net/*/{ifindex,type,operstate,carrier,speed,address,tun_flags}`; the symlinks `sys/class/net/*/phy80211`, `device` and `device/driver`; the directories `wireless/` and `bridge/` as markers (an empty directory with a `.keep` file)
  - `sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl:*/{name,energy_uj,max_energy_range_uj}`
  - `sys/module/zswap/parameters/{enabled,compressor,max_pool_percent}`
- Never copied, enforced by the allowlist above and checked again before every write: any path whose final component is `environ`, `maps`, `smaps`, `smaps_rollup`, `mem`, `fd`, `fdinfo` or `cwd`, and any path containing a `/fd/` component (ADR-013, ADR-015).

Symlinks (sysfs is mostly symlinks): for each wanted path, walk its components from `src_root`. Every component that is a symlink is recreated in the fixture as a symlink with its original target text (sysfs targets are relative, so they resolve inside the fixture). The file content is written at its canonical location, so `sys/block/nvme0n1/size` lands under `sys/devices/.../block/nvme0n1/size` and `sys/block/nvme0n1` is a symlink to it, exactly like the real tree. A symlink whose target is not copied (for example `device/driver` pointing into `sys/bus`) is still recreated; code only reads its target's basename.

Scrubbing (ADR-013), applied to every copied text file:
- Users: from `<src_root>/etc/passwd`, every entry with uid >= 1000 and uid != 65534, sorted by uid, maps to `user1`, `user2`, …. Every whole-word occurrence (the characters before and after are not `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`) is replaced.
- Hostname: the trimmed contents of `proc/sys/kernel/hostname`; every occurrence is replaced by `REDACTED` when the hostname is at least 3 characters long. `proc/sys/kernel/hostname` itself is not copied.
- Serials: a file whose basename is `serial`, `wwid`, `wwn`, `eui`, `nguid`, `uuid`, `product_serial`, `board_serial`, `chassis_serial` or `product_uuid` is written as `REDACTED\n`.
- MAC addresses: `sys/class/net/*/address` is written as `00:00:00:00:00:00\n` (writer choice pending open item E04-OI-3 in the B2 plan).
- `cmdline`: `<comm>\0--arg\0`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake source tree in a temp dir with `proc/1/{stat,statm,status,comm,cmdline,environ,maps}`, `proc/stat`, `etc/passwd` (uid 1000 `alice`, uid 1001 `bob`, uid 0 `root`) and `proc/sys/kernel/hostname` = `myhost` **When** `capture` runs **Then** the output has `proc/1/stat` and `proc/1/cmdline`, and has no `environ` or `maps` file.
- **Given** that tree with `proc/1/comm` = `bash\n` and a real cmdline `bash\0-c\0secret\0` **When** captured **Then** `proc/1/cmdline` is exactly `bash\0--arg\0`.
- **Given** a copied file containing `/home/alice/x bob alicex myhost` **When** scrubbed **Then** it reads `/home/user1/x user2 alicex REDACTED`.
- **Given** a file `sys/block/sda/device/serial` in the allowlist expansion **When** captured **Then** its content is `REDACTED\n`.
- **Given** 60 numeric pid dirs **When** captured with `max_pids = 50` **Then** exactly the 50 lowest pids are copied.
- **Given** `sys/block/sda` is a symlink to `../devices/x/block/sda` in the source **When** captured **Then** the fixture has the same symlink and `sys/devices/x/block/sda/size` holds the content.
- **Given** a file that returns `EACCES` **When** captured **Then** it is absent from the output and listed in `CAPTURE.txt` under `skipped:`.
- **Given** the name `Owner_Desktop` **When** `run` is called **Then** it fails with `fixture name must be lowercase letters, digits and dashes`.
- **Given** an existing fixture dir and no `--force` **When** `run` is called **Then** it fails with `fixture <name> exists; pass --force to replace it` and changes nothing.

## Files
- `xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs`: create (code and `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`)

## Tests
In `xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs::tests` (temp dirs via `std::env::temp_dir()` plus a unique subdirectory, since xtask has no `tempfile` dependency; remove it at the end):
- `never_copies_environ_or_maps`, `cmdline_is_scrubbed`, `users_and_hostname_scrubbed`, `serial_files_redacted`, `pid_limit_is_lowest_50`, `symlinks_recreated`, `unreadable_file_is_skipped` (skips itself when running as root), `bad_name_rejected`, `existing_fixture_needs_force`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the two CLI messages above, verbatim; other errors are `anyhow` context strings naming the relative path.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A (developer tool)
- Privacy: this bead is the privacy gate for every committed fixture. Never copy `environ`, `maps` or fd targets; scrub users, hostname, serials, MACs and command lines.

## Notes
- Large file: write `capture_fixture.rs`, commit it, then build and test (CLAUDE.md large-file rule). Fix-ups go in a follow-up commit.
- This bead does not touch `xtask/src/main.rs`; E04-006 adds the dispatch arm.

Run `cargo fmt --check` too.

description:

- `crates/tl-history/tests/store_6h.rs`: a deterministic generator (seed 42, `std` only, a small xorshift) that produces 6 h of 1 s sweeps of 2,000 processes with 200 changing per second (values random-walk with steps above the thresholds), 120 system series at 1 Hz, written through `Recorder` into a `Store` in a temp directory, without real time passing (timestamps synthetic).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the 6 h synthetic run **When** it finishes **Then** the store's disk usage is under 64 MB (ADR-012 verification).
- **Given** 100 random seconds in the 6 h (seed 42) **When** the state at each is rebuilt from the store **Then** it equals the generator's recorded state at that second after threshold rounding (the generator keeps the last stored value per field by the same rule).
- **Given** the closed store **When** the last segment's footer is removed and its last block truncated by 3 bytes **Then** reopening recovers every block before the bad CRC.

## Reference

### History format reference (ADR-012, binding unless marked "proposed")

- Store root: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/history/` (ADR-011 paths table). One directory per boot: `history/<boot_id as 16 hex digits>/`, written with `format!("{:016x}", boot_id.0)` (lowercase: proposed, open item E30-OI-3). Directories mode 0700, files mode 0600 (PROC-087), set with `std::os::unix::fs::DirBuilderExt::mode` and `OpenOptionsExt::mode` (no rustix: `tl-history` may depend only on tl-model, zstd, crc32fast, postcard, serde, thiserror; ADR-001).
- Segment file per 10 minutes: `seg-<start boottime seconds, 10 digits zero padded>.tlh`, for example `seg-0000012345.tlh`. `SEGMENT_SECS = 600`.
- Segment header, fixed 64 bytes, little endian, fields packed in this order with no padding (offsets proposed, E30-OI-3): `0..4` magic `b"TLH\x01"`; `4..6` `format_version: u16 = 1`; `6..14` `boot_id: u64`; `14..22` `realtime_offset_ns: i64` (CLOCK_REALTIME minus CLOCK_BOOTTIME at segment start); `22..30` `start_t_ns: u64`; `30..64` zero bytes.
- Body: blocks of 60 s (`BLOCK_SECS = 60`). Each block on disk is `u32 LE compressed length | u32 LE crc32 (crc32fast) of the compressed bytes | zstd level 3 frame` of a postcard-encoded `Block`.
- Footer, written when a segment closes (layout proposed, E30-OI-3): postcard `Vec<FooterEntry { start_t_ns: u64, offset: u64 }>` (offset = byte offset of the block's length field from file start), then `u32 LE footer length | u32 LE crc32 of the footer bytes | magic b"TLHF"`. A file whose last 4 bytes are not `TLHF`, or whose footer CRC fails, is read by scanning blocks from byte 64 until the first short read or bad CRC (crash recovery).
- Types (ADR-012 text, with the additions proposed in E30-OI-2 marked `// OI-2`):

```rust
pub type MetaId = u32;
pub struct Block {
    pub start_t_ns: u64,
    pub gap_before: bool,                        // OI-2: first block after a suspend, resume or engine epoch change
    pub mem_total_kib: u64,                      // OI-2: MemTotal at block start, for "1.22 / 62.70 GiB"
    pub catalog: Option<Vec<HistDevice>>,        // OI-2: present in the first block of a segment and when the catalog changed
    pub new_meta: Vec<(MetaId, HistMeta)>,       // comm, display name, exe basename, app id; no cmdline
    pub keyframe: Vec<HistProcess>,              // every live process at block start
    pub deltas: Vec<SweepDelta>,                 // one per process sweep in the block
    pub system: Vec<(SeriesId, Vec<(u32 /*ms offset*/, f32)>)>,  // 1 Hz system series
}
pub struct HistMeta { pub comm: Arc<str>, pub name: Arc<str>, pub exe_basename: Option<Arc<str>>, pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>,
                      pub exe_path: Option<Arc<str>>, pub user: Arc<str>, pub uid: u32, pub system: bool } // last four: OI-2
pub struct HistDevice { pub idx: DeviceIdx, pub kind: u8, pub parent: Option<DeviceIdx>, pub name: Arc<str> } // OI-2
// kind: 0 CpuPackage, 1 CpuLogical, 2 Memory, 3 Gpu, 4 Disk, 5 Net, 6 Sensor, 7 Fan, 8 Battery (DeviceIdentity order)
pub struct HistProcess { pub key: ProcessKey, pub meta: MetaId, pub ppid: u32,
                         pub cpu_permille: u16, pub mem_anon_kib: u32, pub io_r_kibps: u32, pub io_w_kibps: u32,
                         pub net_kibps: u32, pub gpu_pct: u8 }
pub struct SweepDelta { pub dt_ms: u32, pub changed: Vec<(u32 /*keyframe or new index*/, FieldPatch)>,
                        pub started: Vec<HistProcess>, pub exited: Vec<u32> }
pub struct FieldPatch { pub ppid: Option<u32>, pub cpu_permille: Option<u16>, pub mem_anon_kib: Option<u32>,
                        pub io_r_kibps: Option<u32>, pub io_w_kibps: Option<u32>, pub net_kibps: Option<u32>,
                        pub gpu_pct: Option<u8> }        // representation proposed, E30-OI-3
```

- Indexes in `changed` and `exited`: index into the block's process list, where the keyframe occupies `0..keyframe.len()` and every `started` entry appends the next index in order (proposed reading of "keyframe or new index", E30-OI-3). `dt_ms` is milliseconds from `Block.start_t_ns`.
- `FieldPatch` thresholds (binding): a field is written only when it changed against the last stored value by CPU ≥ 1 permille, memory ≥ 256 KiB, a rate (`io_r_kibps`, `io_w_kibps`, `net_kibps`) ≥ 1 KiB/s or to or from zero; `ppid` and `gpu_pct` on any change (proposed). Stored values compare against the last stored value, not the last sampled one, so small drifts accumulate until they cross the threshold.
- Conversion from `ProcessRecord` (ADR-003): `cpu_permille = (cpu_pct * 10.0).round()` clamped to `0..=1000`; `mem_anon_kib = rss_anon_bytes / 1024` (RssAnon, D-004); `io_r_kibps = io_read_bps / 1024` rounded; `io_w_kibps = io_write_bps / 1024` rounded; `net_kibps = (net_rx_bps + net_tx_bps) / 1024` rounded; `gpu_pct = gpu_util_pct.round()` clamped to `0..=100`. A field whose `FieldValidity` is not `Valid` is stored as 0 (history never shows validity glyphs; proposed, E30-OI-3).
- System series: stored at 1 Hz; a series sampled faster (CPU at 10 Hz) is reduced to the per-second maximum (bucket = whole boottime second). A point with value `f32::NAN` marks a gap (proposed, E30-OI-3).
- `MetaId` scope (proposed, E30-OI-3): ids are assigned from 0 per segment (store) or per window lifetime (rolling window); `new_meta` of block k holds every id first referenced in block k. A reader of block k loads `new_meta` of blocks `0..=k` of the same segment.
- Command lines are never stored (ADR-015).

description:
## Context


title: E30-008 History store: boot dirs, rotation, 2 s load, deleted keys
description:
## Context
`Store` manages the on-disk history for the current boot: the directory per boot, segment rotation every 10 minutes, loading what is in retention at start within a 2 s budget, the per-boot deleted-keys list, and block lookup for queries (ADR-012, PROC-087, PROC-088, R-103). It does blocking file I/O; the engine calls it only on the blocking pool. Sources: ADR-011 (paths), ADR-012, PROC-087, PROC-088, R-025, R-103.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-history/src/store.rs`:

```rust
pub enum LoadProblem { OpenFailed, EmptyOrTruncated, VersionMismatch, NoInRange, Stale, TimedOut }
pub struct LoadReport { pub problem: Option<LoadProblem>, pub segments: usize, pub span: Option<(TimeNs, TimeNs)> }
pub struct StoreConfig { pub root: PathBuf, pub boot: BootId, pub retention_ns: u64, pub max_disk_bytes: u64,
                        pub load_existing: bool }   // false when history.persist = false: load nothing at start (PROC-087)
pub struct Store { /* config, open writer, per-segment readers and index, deleted keys */ }
impl Store {
    /// Creates root/<boot> (0700) if needed, opens every segment of this boot and of other boots inside retention,
    /// stops when `deadline` (a std::time::Instant) passes.
    pub fn open(cfg: StoreConfig, now_t_ns: TimeNs, deadline: Instant) -> (Store, LoadReport);
    pub fn append(&mut self, b: Block, realtime_offset_ns: i64) -> Result<(), HistoryError>; // encodes, rotates at SEGMENT_SECS
    pub fn close(&mut self) -> Result<(), HistoryError>;
    pub fn span(&self) -> Option<(TimeNs, TimeNs)>;
    /// Decoded blocks overlapping [from, to] in time order, plus the metas needed to resolve them.
    pub fn blocks(&self, from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs) -> Result<(Vec<Arc<Block>>, MetaTable), HistoryError>;
    pub fn delete_keys(&mut self, keys: &[ProcessKey]) -> Result<(), HistoryError>;
    pub fn deleted(&self) -> &DeletedKeys;
    pub fn disk_bytes(&self) -> u64;
    pub fn realtime_offset_ns(&self) -> i64;
}
```
- Rotation: a new segment starts when the next block's `start_t_ns` is at or past `segment start + SEGMENT_SECS`; the old segment is closed with its footer; `reset_meta_scope` is the caller's job (the recorder, E30-011) and the store exposes `fn will_rotate(&self, next_start: TimeNs) -> bool` so the recorder knows.
- Deleted keys file (name proposed, E30-OI-3): `root/<boot>/deleted-keys.bin`, mode 0600, postcard `Vec<ProcessKey>`, rewritten with write-to-temp, fsync, rename on each `delete_keys`. Keys of other boots go into that boot's own file.
- Load problems, mapped from what `open` finds (texts are shown by the UI, E30-026):
  - root or boot directory cannot be created or read: `OpenFailed` ("Could not open process history store.");
  - segments exist but none yields a block: `EmptyOrTruncated` ("Process history store is empty or truncated.");
  - any segment header with `Version(_)`: that segment is skipped and the problem is `VersionMismatch` ("Process history store version/layout mismatch; starting fresh.");
  - segments exist but all are older than retention: `NoInRange` ("No in-range process history in store.");
  - the newest block is older than retention minus 60 s while inside retention for another boot only: `Stale` ("Process history store is stale.");
  - the deadline passed: `TimedOut` ("Process history load timed out; starting fresh."), and the store starts empty for reading (it still writes).
- Block cache: keep at most 16 decoded blocks (`Arc<Block>`, LRU) to bound RAM (16 MB history budget, ADR-012).
- `lib.rs`: add `pub mod store;`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** an empty root **When** `open` runs **Then** the boot directory exists with mode 0700, `problem` is `None` and `span` is `None`.
- **Given** 25 minutes of appended blocks **When** the directory is listed **Then** there are 3 segment files and the first two have footers.
- **Given** a store reopened after 25 minutes of blocks **When** `blocks(from, to)` covers minute 12 to 14 **Then** it returns exactly the 3 blocks overlapping that range in time order.
- **Given** a segment with header version 2 **When** `open` runs **Then** that segment is ignored and `problem` is `VersionMismatch`.
- **Given** a root path that is a regular file **When** `open` runs **Then** `problem` is `OpenFailed`.
- **Given** `load_existing = false` and segments on disk **When** `open` runs **Then** `span` is `None`, `problem` is `None` and the old files are left for retention to remove.
- **Given** a deadline already in the past **When** `open` runs on a store with segments **Then** `problem` is `TimedOut` and `span` is `None`.
- **Given** `delete_keys([k])` **When** the store is reopened **Then** `deleted().contains(&k)` and the segment files are byte-identical to before (segments are not rewritten, R-103).

## Files
- `crates/tl-history/src/store.rs`: create, with unit tests
- `crates/tl-history/src/lib.rs`: module line

## Tests

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `HistoryError` from append and close; `LoadProblem` from open (never an `Err`).
- Validity: N/A

- Performance: open within 2 s for 12 h of segments; the engine enforces the 2 s budget through `deadline`. RAM: indexes plus at most 16 cached blocks.
- Privacy: no command lines; the deleted-keys file holds only `ProcessKey`s.

## Context
Retention keeps the store inside `history.retention_h` and `history.max_disk_mb`: segments older than retention are deleted, the oldest go first when over the disk cap, directories of other boots older than retention are deleted at start, and with `history.persist = false` every segment is deleted at shutdown (ADR-012, PROC-087, R-025). Sources: ADR-012, PROC-086, PROC-087, R-025, canonical table (a) `[history]`.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-history/src/retention.rs`:

```rust

pub fn enforce(store: &mut Store, now_t_ns: TimeNs) -> Result<RetentionReport, HistoryError>;
/// At start: deletes boot directories other than the current one whose newest segment ends before now - retention,
/// using the segment header realtime_offset_ns to compare across boots in CLOCK_REALTIME.
pub fn prune_other_boots(root: &Path, current: BootId, now_realtime_ns: i64, retention_ns: u64) -> Result<RetentionReport, HistoryError>;
/// persist = false at shutdown: closes and deletes every segment and the deleted-keys file of the current boot.
```

title: E30-010 RollingWindow: 10-minute in-RAM history
description:
## Context
`RollingWindow` is the in-RAM history used while recording is off and the Processes tab is open: the open block plus the newest 10 closed blocks, each zstd-compressed when it closes, nothing written to disk (ADR-012 rolling window, D-010, R-103). It implements the tl-model `RecordSink` trait so the engine can feed it like the recorder. Sources: ADR-012, D-010, PROC-086, R-103.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-history/src/rolling.rs`:

```rust
pub const ROLLING_CLOSED_BLOCKS: usize = 10;
pub struct RollingWindow { builder: BlockBuilder, closed: VecDeque<EncodedBlock>, metas: MetaTable, deleted: DeletedKeys, /* .. */ }
impl RollingWindow {
    pub fn new(boot: BootId) -> Self;
    pub fn mark_gap(&mut self, t_ns: TimeNs);
    pub fn set_mem_total_kib(&mut self, kib: u64);
    pub fn span(&self) -> Option<(TimeNs, TimeNs)>;
    /// Decoded closed blocks overlapping [from, to] plus a snapshot Block of the open block.
    pub fn blocks(&self, from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs) -> Result<(Vec<Arc<Block>>, &MetaTable), HistoryError>;
    pub fn delete_keys(&mut self, keys: &[ProcessKey]);
    pub fn deleted(&self) -> &DeletedKeys;
    pub fn ram_bytes(&self) -> usize;
}
impl RecordSink for RollingWindow { /* forwards to the builder; on a closed block: encode_block, push back,
    pop front while len > ROLLING_CLOSED_BLOCKS, absorb the dropped block's new_meta into `metas` first */ }
```
- `MetaId` scope is the window's lifetime (never reset); metas of dropped blocks stay in `metas` while any kept block or the open block references them, and are pruned when a dropped block was the last reference (prune pass on each drop).
- Deleted keys live in RAM only and die with the window.
- `BlockBuilder` needs a way to expose the open block for queries: add `pub fn open_snapshot(&self) -> Option<Block>` to `block.rs` (clones the open keyframe and deltas).
- `crates/tl-history/tests/rolling_window.rs`.
- `lib.rs`: add `pub mod rolling;`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 15 minutes of synthetic 1 s sweeps (ADR-012 verification) **When** the window's `span` is read **Then** it covers at most the newest 11 minutes (10 closed blocks plus the open one) and at least the newest 10 minutes.
- **Given** 2,000 processes changing every second for 15 minutes **When** `ram_bytes` is read **Then** it is under 16 MiB (16 MB budget, ADR-012).
- **Given** a full window **When** a new block closes **Then** the oldest closed block is dropped and the count stays 10.
- **Given** a process that started before the oldest kept block and is still alive **When** a query resolves its meta **Then** the name resolves (meta kept after its first block dropped).
- **Given** `delete_keys([k])` **When** blocks are queried **Then** callers filtering with `deleted()` never see `k`.
- **Given** the window **When** any method runs **Then** no file is created (the test runs with a read-only current directory and checks no error).

## Files
- `crates/tl-history/src/rolling.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-history/src/block.rs`: add `open_snapshot`
- `crates/tl-history/tests/rolling_window.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-history/src/lib.rs`: module line

## Tests
- `tests/rolling_window.rs::keeps_newest_10_minutes_after_15`, `ram_under_16_mib_2000_changing`, `drops_oldest_on_close`, `meta_survives_block_drop`, `deleted_keys_in_ram`, `writes_nothing_to_disk`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `encode_block` errors are counted and the block is dropped (no panic).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: RAM under 16 MB worst case (2,000 processes changing every second); compression once per 60 s.

title: E30-011 Recorder RecordSink for the store
description:
## Context
`Recorder` is the store-side `RecordSink`: it builds blocks from sweeps and samples and hands each closed block, with its segment rotation flag, to the engine, which writes it on the blocking pool (ADR-012, ADR-004 rule: no blocking I/O on the reducer). It never touches the disk itself. Sources: ADR-012, ADR-004, PROC-086.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-history/src/recorder.rs`:

```rust
pub struct ClosedBlock { pub block: Block, pub realtime_offset_ns: i64 }
pub struct Recorder { builder: BlockBuilder, out: VecDeque<ClosedBlock>, max_queued: usize /* = 4 */, dropped: u64 }
impl Recorder {
    pub fn new(boot: BootId) -> Self;
    pub fn mark_gap(&mut self, t_ns: TimeNs);
    pub fn set_mem_total_kib(&mut self, kib: u64);
    /// Called by the engine when the store says the next block starts a new segment.
    pub fn reset_meta_scope(&mut self);
    pub fn take_closed(&mut self) -> Option<ClosedBlock>;
    pub fn flush(&mut self) -> Option<ClosedBlock>;
    pub fn open_snapshot(&self) -> Option<Block>;   // for queries that reach into the last 60 s
    pub fn dropped_blocks(&self) -> u64;
}
impl RecordSink for Recorder { /* forwards to BlockBuilder; closed blocks go to `out`; when out.len() == 4 the oldest is
    dropped and `dropped` increments (the writer is stuck) */ }
```
- `realtime_offset_ns` is computed by the caller and set with `pub fn set_realtime_offset_ns(&mut self, v: i64)` (CLOCK_REALTIME minus CLOCK_BOOTTIME; tl-history has no clock access of its own beyond std, so the engine passes it).
- Segment rotation and meta scope: the engine calls `store.will_rotate(next_start)` when it takes a block and, if true, calls `reset_meta_scope` before the next block opens. To make this exact, `BlockBuilder` resets the scope lazily: `reset_meta_scope` takes effect at the next block start, and that block's `new_meta` re-lists every live process's meta and its `catalog` is `Some`.
- `lib.rs`: add `pub mod recorder;`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 130 s of sweeps **When** `take_closed` is drained **Then** two blocks come out in time order.
- **Given** 5 closed blocks not taken **When** the sixth closes **Then** the queue holds 4 and `dropped_blocks() == 2`.
- **Given** `reset_meta_scope` called mid-block **When** the next block closes **Then** its `new_meta` lists every process alive at its start and its `catalog` is `Some`, while the block that was open at the call is unchanged.
- **Given** `flush` with an open block of 10 s **When** called **Then** it returns that block and a following `flush` returns `None`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-history/src/recorder.rs`: create, with unit tests
- `crates/tl-history/src/block.rs`: lazy scope reset in `BlockBuilder`
- `crates/tl-history/src/lib.rs`: module line

## Tests
- `recorder::tests::closed_blocks_in_order`, `queue_bounded_drops_oldest`, `meta_scope_reset_at_next_block`, `flush_returns_open_block_once`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A (no I/O).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: queue bounded to 4 blocks (at most about 8 MB worst case).
- Privacy: N/A

## Reference

### History format reference (ADR-012, binding unless marked "proposed")

- Store root: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/history/` (ADR-011 paths table). One directory per boot: `history/<boot_id as 16 hex digits>/`, written with `format!("{:016x}", boot_id.0)` (lowercase: proposed, open item E30-OI-3).     pub start_t_ns: u64,

```rust
    pub mem_total_kib: u64,                      // OI-2: MemTotal at block start, for "1.22 / 62.70 GiB"
    pub catalog: Option<Vec<HistDevice>>,        // OI-2: present in the first block of a segment and when the catalog changed
    pub new_meta: Vec<(MetaId, HistMeta)>,       // comm, display name, exe basename, app id; no cmdline
    pub keyframe: Vec<HistProcess>,              // every live process at block start
    pub deltas: Vec<SweepDelta>,                 // one per process sweep in the block
    pub system: Vec<(SeriesId, Vec<(u32 /*ms offset*/, f32)>)>,  // 1 Hz system series
}
pub struct HistMeta { pub comm: Arc<str>, pub name: Arc<str>, pub exe_basename: Option<Arc<str>>, pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>,
                      pub exe_path: Option<Arc<str>>, pub user: Arc<str>, pub uid: u32, pub system: bool } // last four: OI-2
pub struct HistDevice { pub idx: DeviceIdx, pub kind: u8, pub parent: Option<DeviceIdx>, pub name: Arc<str> } // OI-2
// kind: 0 CpuPackage, 1 CpuLogical, 2 Memory, 3 Gpu, 4 Disk, 5 Net, 6 Sensor, 7 Fan, 8 Battery (DeviceIdentity order)

                         pub cpu_permille: u16, pub mem_anon_kib: u32, pub io_r_kibps: u32, pub io_w_kibps: u32,
                         pub net_kibps: u32, pub gpu_pct: u8 }
pub struct SweepDelta { pub dt_ms: u32, pub changed: Vec<(u32 /*keyframe or new index*/, FieldPatch)>,
                        pub started: Vec<HistProcess>, pub exited: Vec<u32> }
pub struct FieldPatch { pub ppid: Option<u32>, pub cpu_permille: Option<u16>, pub mem_anon_kib: Option<u32>,
                        pub io_r_kibps: Option<u32>, pub io_w_kibps: Option<u32>, pub net_kibps: Option<u32>,
```

- Indexes in `changed` and `exited`: index into the block's process list, where the keyframe occupies `0..keyframe.len()` and every `started` entry appends the next index in order (proposed reading of "keyframe or new index", E30-OI-3). `dt_ms` is milliseconds from `Block.start_t_ns`.

- `MetaId` scope (proposed, E30-OI-3): ids are assigned from 0 per segment (store) or per window lifetime (rolling window); `new_meta` of block k holds every id first referenced in block k. A reader of block k loads `new_meta` of blocks `0..=k` of the same segment.
- Command lines are never stored (ADR-015).

title: E30-012 HistorySink and history worker messages in tl-engine
description:
## Context
The reducer calls a `RecordSink` on every process sweep, system sample and device catalog change (ADR-012). Disk and compression work must not run on the reducer, so the sink in tl-engine is a thin forwarder: it pushes each event into the `HistoryRecorder` worker's channel with `try_send` and never blocks. This bead adds the `tl-history` dependency to tl-engine and creates `workers/history.rs` with the message type, the per-generation sender slot and the sink. Sources: ADR-012, ADR-004 (worker list row `HistoryRecorder`, factory contract: never move an `mpsc::Receiver` into a restartable worker), ADR-001 (tl-engine row includes tl-history from P3), ADR-005.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-engine/Cargo.toml` (E08-owned, chain edit): one dependency line for `tl-history` in the same form as the other workspace path dependencies there. This is the only change to that file.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs` (E08-owned, chain edit): one line `pub(crate) mod history;`.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/history.rs`:

```rust
pub(crate) enum HistoryMsg {
    SessionStart { epoch: u32, t_ns: TimeNs },
    System { t_ns: TimeNs, series: Box<[(SeriesId, Sample)]> },
    Sweep { t_ns: TimeNs, records: Arc<[ProcessRecord]> },
    Catalog(DeviceCatalog),                     // DeviceCatalog { version, entries: Arc<[..]> }: cheap clone
    Query { id: u64, range: HistoryRange, what: HistoryWhat },
    Delete { keys: Arc<[ProcessKey]> },
}
/// Each worker generation creates a fresh mpsc::channel(512) and stores its Sender here; the sink reads it.
pub(crate) type HistorySlot = Arc<arc_swap::ArcSwapOption<mpsc::Sender<HistoryMsg>>>;

impl HistorySink {
    pub(crate) fn new(slot: HistorySlot) -> Self;
    /// For Command::HistoryQuery and Command::HistoryDelete routed by the reducer (E30-A2).
    pub(crate) fn command(&mut self, msg: HistoryMsg);
    pub(crate) fn dropped(&self) -> u64;
}
impl RecordSink for HistorySink { /* each callback builds one HistoryMsg and calls try_send on the slot's sender;
    no sender, Full or Closed: dropped += 1 and return */ }
```

- Accessibility: N/A

title: E30-013 HistoryRecorder worker loop and rolling-window mode
description:
## Context
The `HistoryRecorder` worker task (ADR-004 worker list) owns the history state and switches between three modes from demand and settings: recording to the store when `history.enabled` is true; the 10-minute `RollingWindow` when recording is off and the Processes tab is open (`Demand.process_table`); nothing otherwise (ADR-012, D-010, PROC-086). This bead writes the worker loop, the mode switching and the rolling-window path; E30-014 adds the store path. Sources: ADR-004 (supervision, factory contract, D-Bus-free worker loop rules), ADR-012 (rolling window rules), D-010, PROC-086, R-103.

## Deliverable
- In `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/history.rs`:

```rust
pub(crate) struct HistoryWorkerConfig { pub boot: BootId, pub history_dir: Option<PathBuf> }  // dir: E30-OI-4
pub(crate) enum Mode { Off, Rolling(RollingWindow), Recording(RecordingState /* E30-014 */) }
pub(crate) async fn run_history(cx: Cx, io: WorkerIo, slot: HistorySlot, cfg: HistoryWorkerConfig) -> Outcome<(), WorkerError>;
```
- Each generation: create `mpsc::channel::<HistoryMsg>(512)`, store the sender in `slot`, and clear the slot (`store(None)`) before returning on any path.
- Loop: `time::timeout(cx.now(), 500 ms, rx.recv(&cx))`, then `cx.checkpoint()`; on checkpoint error flush (E30-014 handles the store part) and return `Outcome::Ok(())`. Each turn re-reads `io.demand.borrow_and_clone()` and `io.settings.borrow_and_clone()` (never hold a `Ref`, bead c11v6v) and computes the wanted mode: `Recording` if `settings.history.enabled`, else `Rolling` if `demand.process_table`, else `Off`.

title: E30-014 HistoryRecorder store mode: load, write, retention, shutdown
description:
## Context
The store path of the `HistoryRecorder` worker: when recording is on it loads the store within 2 s, writes every closed block on the blocking pool, enforces retention and the disk cap after each block, applies settings changes, and on shutdown closes the store or, with `history.persist = false`, deletes the segments (ADR-012, PROC-086, PROC-087, R-025). Sources: ADR-012, ADR-004, ADR-008 ("recording on" schedule column is the sources' job, not this worker's), PROC-087, canonical table (a) `[history]`.

## Deliverable
- In `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/history.rs`:

```rust
pub(crate) struct RecordingState { recorder: Recorder, store: Option<Store>, store_state: HistoryStoreState, persist: bool }
```
- Entering Recording: `history_dir = None` gives `store_state = Problem(OpenFailed)` and recording runs RAM-only (queries see the open block only). Otherwise one `spawn_blocking` job runs `retention::prune_other_boots(root, boot, now_realtime, retention)` then `Store::open(cfg, now, Instant::now() + 2 s)` with `load_existing = settings.history.persist`; `store_state` is `Loading` until it returns, then `Ready` or `Problem(p)` mapped one-to-one from `LoadProblem`. The job is joined with `time::timeout(cx.now(), 2500 ms, ..)`; on timeout `store_state = Problem(TimedOut)`, the result is discarded when it arrives late, and a fresh `Store::open` with `load_existing = false` is used.
- Writing: after each batch, `while let Some(cb) = recorder.take_closed()`: if `store.will_rotate(cb.block.start_t_ns)` call `recorder.reset_meta_scope()`; then one `spawn_blocking` job does `store.append(cb.block, cb.realtime_offset_ns)` followed by `retention::enforce(&mut store, now)`. A write error sets `store_state = Problem(OpenFailed)` (proposed, E30-OI-4), keeps recording in RAM and retries opening the store after 60 s.
- Settings changes: `retention_h` and `max_disk_mb` call `store.set_limits` (applied at the next `enforce`); `persist` is read at shutdown.
- Leaving Recording or cancellation: `recorder.flush()`, append that block, `store.close()`; if `persist == false`, `retention::purge_current_boot(store)` instead. Cancellation work is bounded: the shutdown drain is 1000 ms (ADR-004 shutdown step 2), so use `cx.masked(..)` only around the final append and close, and skip the purge if more than 800 ms passed since the cancel was seen (log at warn).
- Retention values: `retention_ns = retention_h * 3_600_000_000_000`, `max_disk_bytes = max_disk_mb * 1_048_576`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** recording on with a temp `history_dir` **When** 3 minutes of synthetic sweeps run in LabRuntime **Then** `history/<boot hex>/seg-*.tlh` exists with 3 blocks after shutdown.
- **Given** a store directory whose segments have header version 2 **When** recording turns on **Then** `store_state = Problem(VersionMismatch)` and new blocks are still written.
- **Given** a load job that does not finish within 2.5 s of virtual time **When** the timeout fires **Then** `store_state = Problem(TimedOut)` and recording continues into a fresh store.
- **Given** `persist = false` **When** the engine shuts down **Then** the current boot directory has no `seg-*.tlh`.
- **Given** `max_disk_mb` lowered while recording **When** the next block is written **Then** `enforce` deletes oldest segments down to the new cap.
- **Given** `history_dir = None` **When** recording turns on **Then** no file is touched and `store_state = Problem(OpenFailed)`.

```rust
    pub cpu_pct: f32, pub mem_anon_bytes: u64, pub disk_bps: f32, pub net_bps: f32, pub gpu_pct: f32,
    pub peak: Option<HistoryPeaks>,          // Some only for a Span range

pub struct HistoryTotals { pub cpu_pct: f32, pub mem_used_bytes: u64, pub mem_total_bytes: u64 }
pub struct HistoryTopRow { pub key: ProcessKey, pub name: Arc<str>, pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>, pub value: f32 }
pub struct HistoryTop { pub query_id: u64, pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub metric: HistoryMetric, pub cpu_total_pct: f32,
                        pub mem_total_bytes: u64, pub rows: Arc<[HistoryTopRow]> }
pub struct HistoryView {
    pub header: ComponentHeader,
    pub query_id: u64,                       // id of the Frame query this answers
    pub source: HistorySource,
    pub store_state: HistoryStoreState,
    pub span: Option<(TimeNs, TimeNs)>,      // oldest and newest retained frame
    pub gaps: Arc<[(TimeNs, TimeNs)]>,       // inside the requested view
    pub frame_t: Option<TimeNs>,             // the second the rows describe (None for a Span)
    pub range: HistoryRange,
    pub process_count: u32,                  // processes alive at frame_t
```

Values: rates in bytes per second, memory in bytes, CPU in percent of the whole machine (0..=100), GPU in percent. Every point list holds at most 1,024 points (ADR-012), decimated min/max per bucket as ADR-009 (absolute bucket boundaries: bucket `i` covers `[floor(t / w) * w, +w)` with `w = ceil((view.1 - view.0) / 1024)` rounded up to whole seconds).

title: E30-015 HistoryQuery and HistoryDelete answers in history_query.rs
description:
## Context
`history_query.rs` answers `Command::HistoryQuery` and `Command::HistoryDelete` from whichever history is active: the store when recording is on, the rolling window when it is off (ADR-012 "Reading", PROC-088 to PROC-090, R-103). It builds the `HistoryView` snapshot component (at most 1,024 points per series, min/max decimation) and sends it to the reducer. Sources: ADR-012, ADR-003 (`Snapshot.history`, bit `HISTORY`), ADR-005 (commands), PROC-088, PROC-089, PROC-090, PROC-091, UI-PRC-030 to UI-PRC-037, R-063, R-103.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-engine/src/history_query.rs` and its `mod history_query;` line in `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs` (E08-owned, chain edit, one line):

```rust
pub(crate) enum QuerySource<'a> { None, Rolling(&'a RollingWindow), Store { store: &'a Store, open: Option<Block> } }
pub(crate) struct QueryCtx { pub boot: BootId, pub now_t_ns: TimeNs, pub store_state: HistoryStoreState,
                             pub realtime_offset_ns: i64, pub version: u64 }
pub(crate) fn answer_frame(src: QuerySource, ctx: &QueryCtx, id: u64, range: &HistoryRange, what: &HistoryWhat /* Frame */) -> HistoryView;
pub(crate) fn answer_top(src: QuerySource, ctx: &QueryCtx, id: u64, t: TimeNs, metric: HistoryMetric, n: u8) -> HistoryTop;
```
- Range resolution: `Live` = the newest sweep second; `At(t)` = `t` snapped down to the whole second and clamped into `span`; `Span { from, to }` = averages and peaks over the range via `read::range_stats`.
- Rows: every process alive at `frame_t` (or seen in the span), minus deleted keys; `name`, `comm`, `user`, `exe` (full path), `app_id`, `system` from `HistMeta`; `present = true`; `previous_boot = key.boot_id != ctx.boot`. Then one row per key in `what.keys` that is not alive at `frame_t`: `present = false`, numeric fields 0 (the UI shows `-`). Rows are unsorted (the UI sorts).
- `process_count` = processes alive at `frame_t`.
- `totals` at `frame_t`: CPU from the CpuPackage `CPU_TOTAL`, memory used from `MEM_USED` and total from `Block.mem_total_kib`; for a Span, the averages over the span (proposed, E30-OI-5).
- `series`: first the system total of `what.metric` over `what.view`, then one per key in `what.keys` (at most 8), each from `read::decimate` (≤ 1,024 points). `stack` from `read::stack` over the same view. `overview` over the whole `span` only when `what.overview`. `gaps`: NaN buckets and blocks with `gap_before` inside the view, as `(start, end)` pairs.
- `HistoryTop`: `read::top_at` at `t` snapped to the second, `n` rows, with `cpu_total_pct` and `mem_total_bytes` at `t`.
- Delete: `Store::delete_keys` or `RollingWindow::delete_keys`, then re-answer the last Frame query so the rows disappear with the next `HistoryView` (UI-PRC-037).
- The worker (E30-013) runs both functions inside its `spawn_blocking` batch job, keeps the last Frame view and the last `HistoryTop`, merges them (`view.top = Some(top)`), bumps `header.version` on every answer, and sends `EngineMsg::Source(SourceUpdate::History(Arc<HistoryView>))` (variant name: E30-OI-4).
- No data yet (no sweep stored): `rows` empty, `span = None`, `frame_t = None`; the UI shows "Collecting first history snapshot..." (PROC-091).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a rolling window with 5 minutes of sweeps **When** a Live Frame query for CPU runs **Then** `source = RollingWindow`, `frame_t` is the newest second and `rows.len()` equals the processes alive then.
- **Given** a selected key that exited 2 minutes ago **When** `At(now - 30 s)` is queried with that key **Then** its row has `present = false` and is last.
- **Given** a key whose `boot_id` differs from the current boot **When** queried **Then** its row has `previous_boot = true`.
- **Given** a 6 h store **When** a Frame query with the whole span as view runs **Then** every series has at most 1,024 points.
- **Given** a Span of 2 min 42 s **When** queried **Then** each row's `peak` is `Some` and `frame_t` is `None`.
- **Given** `HistoryDelete { keys: [k] }` **When** the next view is published **Then** no row, series or top entry has key `k`.
- **Given** a TopAt query for Memory at t **When** answered **Then** `rows` holds at most 3 entries sorted by memory descending and `mem_total_bytes` is set.
- **Given** an empty window **When** queried **Then** `rows` is empty and `span` is `None`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/history_query.rs`: create, with unit tests on synthetic `RollingWindow` data
- `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs`: one `mod` line (chain edit, E08)

## Tests
- `history_query::tests::live_frame_from_window`, `absent_selected_key_listed_last`, `previous_boot_marked`, `series_capped_1024`, `span_has_peaks`, `deleted_keys_gone`, `top_at_memory_sorted`, `empty_window_no_rows`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: a store read error answers with the data that could be read and `store_state = Problem(EmptyOrTruncated)` (proposed, E30-OI-4).
- Validity: N/A (history rows carry no validity; absent rows use `present = false`).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: a TopAt answer within 50 ms (PROC-090); a Frame answer for a 10-minute view within 50 ms on 2,000 processes; measured in E30-A1 and here with a release-only assertion.
- Privacy: no command line exists in the history data.

## Notes
- The view type fields come from the E30-OI-1 proposal (Reference). Follow the leader's final text if it differs.
- Large-file rule: this bead creates a large file. Write it, commit it, then build and test. Fix-ups go in a follow-up commit, never an amend.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...` (for example `... cargo test -p tl-history`).
- Commit with a pathspec of your files only: `git add <files> && git commit -m "..." -- <files>`. Never a bare `git commit`, never change branch or history.

## Reference

### History format reference (ADR-012, binding unless marked "proposed")

- Store root: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/history/` (ADR-011 paths table). One directory per boot: `history/<boot_id as 16 hex digits>/`, written with `format!("{:016x}", boot_id.0)` (lowercase: proposed, open item E30-OI-3). Directories mode 0700, files mode 0600 (PROC-087), set with `std::os::unix::fs::DirBuilderExt::mode` and `OpenOptionsExt::mode` (no rustix: `tl-history` may depend only on tl-model, zstd, crc32fast, postcard, serde, thiserror; ADR-001).
- Segment file per 10 minutes: `seg-<start boottime seconds, 10 digits zero padded>.tlh`, for example `seg-0000012345.tlh`. `SEGMENT_SECS = 600`.
- Segment header, fixed 64 bytes, little endian, fields packed in this order with no padding (offsets proposed, E30-OI-3): `0..4` magic `b"TLH\x01"`; `4..6` `format_version: u16 = 1`; `6..14` `boot_id: u64`; `14..22` `realtime_offset_ns: i64` (CLOCK_REALTIME minus CLOCK_BOOTTIME at segment start); `22..30` `start_t_ns: u64`; `30..64` zero bytes.
- Body: blocks of 60 s (`BLOCK_SECS = 60`). Each block on disk is `u32 LE compressed length | u32 LE crc32 (crc32fast) of the compressed bytes | zstd level 3 frame` of a postcard-encoded `Block`.
- Footer, written when a segment closes (layout proposed, E30-OI-3): postcard `Vec<FooterEntry { start_t_ns: u64, offset: u64 }>` (offset = byte offset of the block's length field from file start), then `u32 LE footer length | u32 LE crc32 of the footer bytes | magic b"TLHF"`. A file whose last 4 bytes are not `TLHF`, or whose footer CRC fails, is read by scanning blocks from byte 64 until the first short read or bad CRC (crash recovery).
- Types (ADR-012 text, with the additions proposed in E30-OI-2 marked `// OI-2`):

```rust
pub type MetaId = u32;
pub struct Block {
    pub start_t_ns: u64,
    pub gap_before: bool,                        // OI-2: first block after a suspend, resume or engine epoch change
    pub mem_total_kib: u64,                      // OI-2: MemTotal at block start, for "1.22 / 62.70 GiB"
    pub catalog: Option<Vec<HistDevice>>,        // OI-2: present in the first block of a segment and when the catalog changed
    pub new_meta: Vec<(MetaId, HistMeta)>,       // comm, display name, exe basename, app id; no cmdline
    pub keyframe: Vec<HistProcess>,              // every live process at block start
    pub deltas: Vec<SweepDelta>,                 // one per process sweep in the block
    pub system: Vec<(SeriesId, Vec<(u32 /*ms offset*/, f32)>)>,  // 1 Hz system series
}
pub struct HistMeta { pub comm: Arc<str>, pub name: Arc<str>, pub exe_basename: Option<Arc<str>>, pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>,
                      pub exe_path: Option<Arc<str>>, pub user: Arc<str>, pub uid: u32, pub system: bool } // last four: OI-2
pub struct HistDevice { pub idx: DeviceIdx, pub kind: u8, pub parent: Option<DeviceIdx>, pub name: Arc<str> } // OI-2
// kind: 0 CpuPackage, 1 CpuLogical, 2 Memory, 3 Gpu, 4 Disk, 5 Net, 6 Sensor, 7 Fan, 8 Battery (DeviceIdentity order)
pub struct HistProcess { pub key: ProcessKey, pub meta: MetaId, pub ppid: u32,
                         pub cpu_permille: u16, pub mem_anon_kib: u32, pub io_r_kibps: u32, pub io_w_kibps: u32,
                         pub net_kibps: u32, pub gpu_pct: u8 }
pub struct SweepDelta { pub dt_ms: u32, pub changed: Vec<(u32 /*keyframe or new index*/, FieldPatch)>,
                        pub started: Vec<HistProcess>, pub exited: Vec<u32> }
pub struct FieldPatch { pub ppid: Option<u32>, pub cpu_permille: Option<u16>, pub mem_anon_kib: Option<u32>,
                        pub io_r_kibps: Option<u32>, pub io_w_kibps: Option<u32>, pub net_kibps: Option<u32>,
                        pub gpu_pct: Option<u8> }        // representation proposed, E30-OI-3
```

- Indexes in `changed` and `exited`: index into the block's process list, where the keyframe occupies `0..keyframe.len()` and every `started` entry appends the next index in order (proposed reading of "keyframe or new index", E30-OI-3). `dt_ms` is milliseconds from `Block.start_t_ns`.
- `FieldPatch` thresholds (binding): a field is written only when it changed against the last stored value by CPU ≥ 1 permille, memory ≥ 256 KiB, a rate (`io_r_kibps`, `io_w_kibps`, `net_kibps`) ≥ 1 KiB/s or to or from zero; `ppid` and `gpu_pct` on any change (proposed). Stored values compare against the last stored value, not the last sampled one, so small drifts accumulate until they cross the threshold.
- Conversion from `ProcessRecord` (ADR-003): `cpu_permille = (cpu_pct * 10.0).round()` clamped to `0..=1000`; `mem_anon_kib = rss_anon_bytes / 1024` (RssAnon, D-004); `io_r_kibps = io_read_bps / 1024` rounded; `io_w_kibps = io_write_bps / 1024` rounded; `net_kibps = (net_rx_bps + net_tx_bps) / 1024` rounded; `gpu_pct = gpu_util_pct.round()` clamped to `0..=100`. A field whose `FieldValidity` is not `Valid` is stored as 0 (history never shows validity glyphs; proposed, E30-OI-3).
- System series: stored at 1 Hz; a series sampled faster (CPU at 10 Hz) is reduced to the per-second maximum (bucket = whole boottime second). A point with value `f32::NAN` marks a gap (proposed, E30-OI-3).
- `MetaId` scope (proposed, E30-OI-3): ids are assigned from 0 per segment (store) or per window lifetime (rolling window); `new_meta` of block k holds every id first referenced in block k. A reader of block k loads `new_meta` of blocks `0..=k` of the same segment.
- Command lines are never stored (ADR-015).

title: E30-016 History mode page: layout, header text, state
description:
## Context
Creates the History mode page entity that replaces the live process table while `history_mode` is on: layout, header line text, the state the strip, minimap, chips and table share, and the snapshot subscription (UI-PRC-030). Later beads fill each part. Sources: UI-PRC-030, UI-PRC-036 (states), PROC-088, PROC-091, D-010, R-023, R-063, ADR-009 (entity structure: nothing notifies in render).

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/mod.rs`:

```rust

    pub(crate) state: HistoryUiState,
    pub(crate) view: Option<Arc<HistoryView>>,   // last installed Snapshot.history
    /* child entities added by later beads: table, scrubber, minimap, legend */
}
pub struct HistoryUiState {
    pub metric: HistoryMetric,                   // default Cpu
    pub scrub: Option<TimeNs>,                   // None = live
    pub range: Option<(TimeNs, TimeNs)>,
    pub view_range: (TimeNs, TimeNs),            // strip window, default last 10 min or the whole span when shorter

    pub off_toast_shown: bool,                   // session only
}
pub fn header_text(view: Option<&HistoryView>, s: &HistoryUiState, out: &mut String);
```
- Layout (logical px, tokens from `UiMetrics` and `TlTheme`): header line height 32, horizontal padding `sp5` (12), `t_base` `text_primary`; under it the recording-off banner slot (28, E30-026); timeline strip slot 120 high; `sp2` (4) gap; minimap slot 24 high; `sp4` (8) gap; the table fills the rest. Strip and minimap span the tab content width minus `sp5` margins.
- Header texts (exact; R-063, PROC-088, PROC-091):
  - no frame yet (`view` is None or `frame_t` is None and `span` is None): "Collecting first history snapshot..."
  - live: "History - Drag scrubber below to view timeline"
  - scrub point: "History Snapshot: <N> processes - <M> min <S> sec ago"; under a minute "History Snapshot: <N> processes - <S> sec ago"; at or over an hour "History Snapshot: <N> processes - <H> h <M> min ago". `<N>` is `process_count` grouped with a thin space (table (d)); the age is `now - scrub` in whole seconds.
  - range: "History Range: <HH:MM:SS> - <HH:MM:SS> (<M> min <S> sec), averages", times in local time with the table (d) `HH:MM:SS` formatter in `tl_model::units` (the one the Start time column uses) applied to `t + realtime_offset_ns`; the duration uses the same min/sec/h rules without "ago".
  - store loading: the strip area shows "Loading history…" centred in `text_secondary` and the table is empty.
- Subscribes to `SnapshotHub` `SnapshotChanged` and calls `cx.notify()` only when `mask` contains `ComponentMask::HISTORY` (ADR-005 hub rule).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** no `HistoryView` **When** the page renders **Then** the header reads "Collecting first history snapshot...".
- **Given** a view with 213 processes and a scrub 252 s ago **When** rendered **Then** the header reads "History Snapshot: 213 processes - 4 min 12 sec ago".
- **Given** a scrub 45 s ago **When** rendered **Then** it reads "History Snapshot: 213 processes - 45 sec ago".
- **Given** a scrub 3,900 s ago **When** rendered **Then** it reads "History Snapshot: 213 processes - 1 h 5 min ago".
- **Given** a range 12:01:30 to 12:04:12 local **When** rendered **Then** it reads "History Range: 12:01:30 - 12:04:12 (2 min 42 sec), averages".
- **Given** a snapshot change whose mask lacks `HISTORY` **When** installed **Then** the page's render counter (feature `test-hooks`) does not increase.

title: E30-A2 Recorder and query
description:
## Context
Anchor E30-A2: history is wired into the running engine. The reducer gets the `HistorySink` as its `RecordSink` (it is `None` in P1 and P2, ADR-012), forwards `Command::HistoryQuery` and `Command::HistoryDelete` to it, and stores the worker's `HistoryView` in `Snapshot.history` with the `HISTORY` component bit; the session spawns the `HistoryRecorder` worker like every other worker. These are edits to E09-owned files that 00-epics.md section 2 does not list as chain edits, so this bead waits for the leader to settle E30-OI-4. Sources: ADR-012 (hook), ADR-004 (session, worker list), ADR-005 (commands), ADR-003 (`Snapshot.history`).

## Deliverable
Chain edits, each the only change this bead makes to that file (exact placement follows what E09-A1 wrote; if a needed hook point does not exist, stop and report to the leader):
- `crates/tl-engine/src/session.rs` (E09): at session start, create `let slot: HistorySlot = Arc::new(ArcSwapOption::empty());`, build `HistorySink::new(slot.clone())`, send `HistoryMsg::SessionStart { epoch, t_ns: now_boot_ns() }` through it, install it with the reducer's record-sink setter (`Some(Box::new(sink))`), and spawn the `HistoryRecorder` worker through the same `SourceController` and one-child `ManagedSupervisor` path as the other workers with factory `move |cx, _gen| run_history(cx, io.clone(), slot.clone(), cfg.clone())` and `SourceId::HistoryRecorder`.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs` (E09): the `Command::HistoryQuery { id, range, what }` arm calls `sink.command(HistoryMsg::Query { id, range, what })`; the `Command::HistoryDelete { keys }` arm calls `sink.command(HistoryMsg::Delete { keys })`; the `SourceUpdate::History(view)` arm replaces `snapshot.history` with `view` (a new `Arc`, so the UI's `ComponentMask::HISTORY` bit is set).
- `HistoryWorkerConfig.history_dir` comes from `EngineConfig` (E30-OI-4: field `history_dir: Option<PathBuf>`, set by tl-app to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/history`).
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_history.rs`: end-to-end cases through `Engine::start` with fake sources (E08 `tests/fake_sources.rs` style).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** an engine with a fake Processes source and `Demand.process_table = true` **When** the UI-side client sends `HistoryQuery { id: 7, range: Live, what: Frame { metric: Cpu, .. } }` **Then** a published snapshot carries `history.query_id == 7` with `source = RollingWindow`.
- **Given** that snapshot **When** the next snapshot after another query is installed **Then** its `history` `Arc` differs and its `header.version` increased.
- **Given** an engine session panic **When** the session restarts with epoch 2 **Then** the history worker receives `SessionStart { epoch: 2, .. }` and the next block has `gap_before = true`.
- **Given** P3 code with history settings at defaults (`enabled = false`) and the Processes tab not demanded **When** the engine runs 60 s **Then** the history worker holds no window and allocates nothing beyond its channel (checked with the sink's dropped counter staying 0 and a `ram_bytes` probe returning 0).
- **Given** `HistoryDelete` for a key **When** the next view arrives **Then** that key is absent.

- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs`: chain edit (E09)
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_history.rs`: add the end-to-end cases

- Validity: `Snapshot.history.header.validity` is `Valid` once a view was answered, `WarmingUp` before.
- Accessibility: N/A

## Notes

## Reference

### History format reference (ADR-012, binding unless marked "proposed")

- Store root: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/history/` (ADR-011 paths table). One directory per boot: `history/<boot_id as 16 hex digits>/`, written with `format!("{:016x}", boot_id.0)` (lowercase: proposed, open item E30-OI-3). Directories mode 0700, files mode 0600 (PROC-087), set with `std::os::unix::fs::DirBuilderExt::mode` and `OpenOptionsExt::mode` (no rustix: `tl-history` may depend only on tl-model, zstd, crc32fast, postcard, serde, thiserror; ADR-001).
- Segment file per 10 minutes: `seg-<start boottime seconds, 10 digits zero padded>.tlh`, for example `seg-0000012345.tlh`. `SEGMENT_SECS = 600`.
- Segment header, fixed 64 bytes, little endian, fields packed in this order with no padding (offsets proposed, E30-OI-3): `0..4` magic `b"TLH\x01"`; `4..6` `format_version: u16 = 1`; `6..14` `boot_id: u64`; `14..22` `realtime_offset_ns: i64` (CLOCK_REALTIME minus CLOCK_BOOTTIME at segment start); `22..30` `start_t_ns: u64`; `30..64` zero bytes.
- Body: blocks of 60 s (`BLOCK_SECS = 60`). Each block on disk is `u32 LE compressed length | u32 LE crc32 (crc32fast) of the compressed bytes | zstd level 3 frame` of a postcard-encoded `Block`.
- Footer, written when a segment closes (layout proposed, E30-OI-3): postcard `Vec<FooterEntry { start_t_ns: u64, offset: u64 }>` (offset = byte offset of the block's length field from file start), then `u32 LE footer length | u32 LE crc32 of the footer bytes | magic b"TLHF"`. A file whose last 4 bytes are not `TLHF`, or whose footer CRC fails, is read by scanning blocks from byte 64 until the first short read or bad CRC (crash recovery).
- Types (ADR-012 text, with the additions proposed in E30-OI-2 marked `// OI-2`):

```rust

    pub start_t_ns: u64,
    pub gap_before: bool,                        // OI-2: first block after a suspend, resume or engine epoch change
    pub mem_total_kib: u64,                      // OI-2: MemTotal at block start, for "1.22 / 62.70 GiB"
    pub catalog: Option<Vec<HistDevice>>,        // OI-2: present in the first block of a segment and when the catalog changed
    pub new_meta: Vec<(MetaId, HistMeta)>,       // comm, display name, exe basename, app id; no cmdline
    pub keyframe: Vec<HistProcess>,              // every live process at block start
    pub deltas: Vec<SweepDelta>,                 // one per process sweep in the block
    pub system: Vec<(SeriesId, Vec<(u32 /*ms offset*/, f32)>)>,  // 1 Hz system series
}
pub struct HistMeta { pub comm: Arc<str>, pub name: Arc<str>, pub exe_basename: Option<Arc<str>>, pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>,
                      pub exe_path: Option<Arc<str>>, pub user: Arc<str>, pub uid: u32, pub system: bool } // last four: OI-2
pub struct HistDevice { pub idx: DeviceIdx, pub kind: u8, pub parent: Option<DeviceIdx>, pub name: Arc<str> } // OI-2
// kind: 0 CpuPackage, 1 CpuLogical, 2 Memory, 3 Gpu, 4 Disk, 5 Net, 6 Sensor, 7 Fan, 8 Battery (DeviceIdentity order)
pub struct HistProcess { pub key: ProcessKey, pub meta: MetaId, pub ppid: u32,
                         pub cpu_permille: u16, pub mem_anon_kib: u32, pub io_r_kibps: u32, pub io_w_kibps: u32,
                         pub net_kibps: u32, pub gpu_pct: u8 }
pub struct SweepDelta { pub dt_ms: u32, pub changed: Vec<(u32 /*keyframe or new index*/, FieldPatch)>,
                        pub started: Vec<HistProcess>, pub exited: Vec<u32> }
pub struct FieldPatch { pub ppid: Option<u32>, pub cpu_permille: Option<u16>, pub mem_anon_kib: Option<u32>,
                        pub io_r_kibps: Option<u32>, pub io_w_kibps: Option<u32>, pub net_kibps: Option<u32>,
                        pub gpu_pct: Option<u8> }        // representation proposed, E30-OI-3
```

- Indexes in `changed` and `exited`: index into the block's process list, where the keyframe occupies `0..keyframe.len()` and every `started` entry appends the next index in order (proposed reading of "keyframe or new index", E30-OI-3). `dt_ms` is milliseconds from `Block.start_t_ns`.
- `FieldPatch` thresholds (binding): a field is written only when it changed against the last stored value by CPU ≥ 1 permille, memory ≥ 256 KiB, a rate (`io_r_kibps`, `io_w_kibps`, `net_kibps`) ≥ 1 KiB/s or to or from zero; `ppid` and `gpu_pct` on any change (proposed). Stored values compare against the last stored value, not the last sampled one, so small drifts accumulate until they cross the threshold.
- Conversion from `ProcessRecord` (ADR-003): `cpu_permille = (cpu_pct * 10.0).round()` clamped to `0..=1000`; `mem_anon_kib = rss_anon_bytes / 1024` (RssAnon, D-004); `io_r_kibps = io_read_bps / 1024` rounded; `io_w_kibps = io_write_bps / 1024` rounded; `net_kibps = (net_rx_bps + net_tx_bps) / 1024` rounded; `gpu_pct = gpu_util_pct.round()` clamped to `0..=100`. A field whose `FieldValidity` is not `Valid` is stored as 0 (history never shows validity glyphs; proposed, E30-OI-3).
- System series: stored at 1 Hz; a series sampled faster (CPU at 10 Hz) is reduced to the per-second maximum (bucket = whole boottime second). A point with value `f32::NAN` marks a gap (proposed, E30-OI-3).
- `MetaId` scope (proposed, E30-OI-3): ids are assigned from 0 per segment (store) or per window lifetime (rolling window); `new_meta` of block k holds every id first referenced in block k. A reader of block k loads `new_meta` of blocks `0..=k` of the same segment.
- Command lines are never stored (ADR-015).

title: E30-017 History query controller with one query in flight
description:
## Context
History mode asks the engine for data with `Command::HistoryQuery { id, range, what }` on mode entry, on every scrub change, on range change and every second while live, with at most one Frame query in flight (UI-PRC-030). The minimap's overview is asked once per minute and on mode entry (UI-PRC-033). This bead adds that query controller to the page. Sources: UI-PRC-030, UI-PRC-033, ADR-005 (`EngineClient::send`, `CommandError::Busy`), ADR-012.

## Deliverable
- In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/mod.rs`:

```rust
pub(crate) struct QueryController {
    next_id: u64,                    // starts at 1
    in_flight: Option<u64>,          // id of the Frame query sent and not yet answered
    pending: Option<(HistoryRange, HistoryWhat)>,  // latest wanted query while one is in flight
    last_overview_ns: Option<TimeNs>,
}
impl QueryController {
    pub fn want(&mut self, range: HistoryRange, what: HistoryWhat, client: &dyn EngineClient);
    pub fn on_view(&mut self, view: &HistoryView, client: &dyn EngineClient);  // clears in_flight when view.query_id matches, sends pending
}
```
- Rules: `want` sends at once when nothing is in flight; otherwise it replaces `pending` (a new scrub while a query is pending replaces the pending request). `on_view` with `query_id == in_flight` sends `pending` if any. If no answer arrives within 1,000 ms, `in_flight` is cleared and the pending or latest query is resent (proposed, E30-OI-6).
- `what` is `HistoryWhat::Frame { metric: state.metric, view: state.view_range, keys: state.selected[..min(8)], overview }` where `overview = true` on mode entry and when 60 s passed since the last overview.
- Range: `Live` while `scrub` and `range` are None; `At(scrub)`; `Span { from, to }` when a range is set.
- A 1 s GPUI timer (`cx.spawn` with `Timer::after(1 s)`) sends a Live query while live and History mode is on; it stops when the page is dropped or the mode turns off. No timer runs while scrubbed.
- `CommandError::Busy` from `send`: keep the query as pending and retry on the next timer tick.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a query in flight **When** three scrub changes arrive **Then** no new command is sent and `pending` holds the third.
- **Given** that state **When** the matching view arrives **Then** exactly one command is sent, carrying the third scrub time.
- **Given** a view with a different `query_id` **When** it arrives **Then** `in_flight` is unchanged.
- **Given** live mode **When** 5 s pass with answers arriving **Then** 5 Live queries were sent.
- **Given** mode entry **When** the first query is sent **Then** `overview = true`; the next one within 60 s has `overview = false`.
- **Given** a Busy error **When** the next tick comes **Then** the query is sent again.

## Files

## Cross-cutting

- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: at most one Frame query in flight; the hover card's TopAt queries have their own controller (E30-023).

title: E30-018 History actions and History key context bindings
description:
## Context
Declares the History mode Actions and binds their keys in the `History` key context: Left/Right step 1 s, Shift+Left/Right step 1 min, Home oldest, End live, Esc live when a scrub point is set, 1..5 select a metric (table (b), UI-PRC-030, UI-PRC-032, UI-PRC-035). Actions live in the one `tasklens` namespace (R-128). Sources: RECONCILIATION table (b) rows "History scrubber", "History" and "History (scrub point set)", R-128, UI-PRC-030 to UI-PRC-037, APP-031.

## Deliverable

```rust
actions!(tasklens, [HistoryStepBack, HistoryStepForward, HistoryStepBackMinute, HistoryStepForwardMinute,
                    HistoryOldest, HistoryLive, HistoryMetricCpu, HistoryMetricMemory, HistoryMetricDisk,
                    HistoryMetricNetwork, HistoryMetricGpu, DeleteFromHistory, HistoryShowInLiveTable]);
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Action)] #[action(namespace = tasklens)] pub struct HistoryScrub { pub t: TimeNs }
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Action)] #[action(namespace = tasklens)] pub struct HistorySetRange { pub from: TimeNs, pub to: TimeNs }
```
