title: E30-020 History table menu, jump and Delete from history
description:
## Context
The History table's row menu, double-click and Enter behaviour, and "Delete from history" (UI-PRC-031, UI-PRC-037). Deleting sends `Command::HistoryDelete` with no confirmation; the engine adds the keys to the per-boot deleted list and the rows disappear with the next `HistoryView` (R-103). Show in live table jumps through `select_by_key` (UI-PRC-022), which leaves History mode. Sources: UI-PRC-031, UI-PRC-037, UI-PRC-022, PROC-070, PROC-088, R-103.

## Deliverable
- In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/table.rs`:
  - Right-click menu (`TlMenu`), in order: "Copy", "Copy details", "Copy all metrics", "Copy rows as table", separator, "Show in live table" (disabled when no selected row is live), separator, "Delete from history" (icon Lucide `trash-2` 14 px, text in `status.danger`).
  - Copy texts (PROC-070 formats, applied to the fields history has; the field set is E30-OI-6): "Copy" copies the right-clicked cell's displayed text, one line per selected row in view order, toast "Selected process values copied." for several rows or "Copied to clipboard" for one. "Copy rows as table" copies TSV of the visible columns with a header line, toast "Copied to clipboard". "Copy details" and "Copy all metrics" per E30-OI-6.
  - Double-click or Enter on a row: if the key is in the current live `ProcessTableView`, call `ProcessesPage::select_by_key(key, JumpSource::History)` (E22-A3; leaves History mode); else toast "Process not running".
  - `DeleteFromHistory`: sends `Command::HistoryDelete { keys }` for every selected row; toast "History entry deleted" for one key, "<N> history entries deleted" for more; removes the keys from `HistoryUiState.selected` so their series and chips go at once.
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` (chain edit): keys `history-menu-show-live` "Show in live table", `history-menu-delete` "Delete from history", `history-toast-deleted` "History entry deleted", `history-toast-deleted-n` "{ $count } history entries deleted", `history-toast-not-running` "Process not running".

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** one selected row **When** "Delete from history" is clicked **Then** `HistoryDelete { keys: [k] }` is sent, no dialog opens and the toast reads "History entry deleted".
- **Given** three selected rows **When** deleted **Then** one command carries three keys and the toast reads "3 history entries deleted".
- **Given** a deleted selected key **When** the command is sent **Then** its chip and series are gone before the next view arrives.
- **Given** a row whose key is live **When** double-clicked **Then** `select_by_key` is called and History mode turns off.
- **Given** a row whose key is not live **When** Enter is pressed **Then** the toast reads "Process not running" and the mode stays.
- **Given** the menu **When** opened on a non-live row **Then** "Show in live table" is disabled.

title: E30-021 Timeline scrubber element: paint and geometry cache
description:
## Context
The timeline strip is a custom GPUI `Element` (`HistoryScrubber`), 120 px high, drawing the stacked metric graph, selected process lines, gaps, the handle, a range fill and time labels (UI-PRC-032). This bead draws it and caches its geometry; E30-022 adds pointer and keyboard interaction. Sources: UI-PRC-032, UI-PRC-035 (colours), PROC-089, ADR-009 (chart element pattern, `ChartGeometryKey`, cached `ShapedLine`), ADR-014.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/scrubber.rs`: `pub struct HistoryScrubber` implementing `Element`:
  - `request_layout`: fixed height 120, full width. `prepaint`: one hitbox over the whole element. `paint`: as below.
  - Plot area y 0..100, background `list_bg`. Grid as the ADR-009 chart: hairline `graph.grid`, vertical lines every `visible_range / 10`, horizontal at 25, 50 and 75%.
  - Stacked area of `HistoryView.stack` (top-3 plus other, E30-OI-5) and the system-total line from `series[0]`, in the active metric's `graph.*_fill` and `graph.*_line` colours (CPU `cpu_*`, Memory `mem_*`, Disk `disk_*`, Network `net_*`, GPU `gpu_*`).
  - One 1 px line, no fill, per selected-process series (`series[1..]`), colour k = the `accent` hue rotated by `k × 45°` with the same saturation and lightness, assigned in selection order (UI-PRC-035).
  - Gaps (`HistoryView.gaps`): a hatched band in `divider` at 30% alpha.

Label text: offsets from now under an hour "-M:SS" (for example "-8:20"), at or over an hour "-H:MM:SS" (for example "-1:02:03"), "now" at the right edge. Labels that would overlap the previous label are dropped (keep every second label until none overlap).

title: E30-022 Timeline scrubber interaction and focus
description:
## Context
Pointer and keyboard interaction for the timeline strip: click or drag to scrub, wheel zoom around the cursor, pan, Shift+drag range selection with resizable bounds, double-click to return to live, and a focus ring when the strip has focus (UI-PRC-032, PROC-089). Sources: UI-PRC-032, PROC-089, table (b), UI-PRC-030 (query coalescing while dragging).

## Deliverable
- In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/scrubber.rs` (pointer events registered with `window.on_mouse_event` in `paint`, as ADR-009 charts do):
  - Left click or drag in the plot: dispatch `HistoryScrub { t }` with `t` snapped to whole seconds. While dragging the handle the grip grows to 12 × 12 and the cursor is `ew-resize`.
  - Wheel (no modifier): zoom around the cursor time by a factor 1.25 per notch (in: span / 1.25, out: span × 1.25), the cursor's time stays under the cursor, span clamped to 60 s..retained span (whole span when shorter than 60 s).
  - Shift+wheel or middle-button drag: pan; cursor `grabbing` while dragging; the view range is clamped inside `span`.
  - Shift+left drag: range selection, dispatch `HistorySetRange { from, to }` (from < to, snapped to seconds). Dragging a bound grip resizes that bound. A click without Shift clears the range.
  - Double-click: dispatch `HistoryLive`.
  - Hover: sets the hover x for the hairline and the top-3 card (E30-023); hidden while dragging and after a wheel event until the pointer moves.
  - Focus: click gives focus; the strip is in the Tab order after the header controls; focused draws a 1 px `accent` inset ring.
- `HistoryPage` handles `HistoryScrub` (set `scrub`, clear nothing else), `HistorySetRange` (set `range`), and updates `view_range` from zoom and pan; each change calls the query controller (E30-017), which coalesces while dragging.
- Pure helpers with unit tests: `fn zoom(view: (TimeNs, TimeNs), cursor: TimeNs, notches: f32, span: (TimeNs, TimeNs)) -> (TimeNs, TimeNs)`, `fn pan(view, delta_ns: i64, span) -> (TimeNs, TimeNs)`, `fn x_to_t(x: f32, width: f32, view) -> TimeNs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a 10-minute view and the cursor at its middle **When** zooming in one notch **Then** the span is 480 s and the cursor time is unchanged.
- **Given** a 70 s view **When** zooming in 3 notches **Then** the span is 60 s (clamped).
- **Given** a view at the newest edge **When** panning forward **Then** the view does not move past `span.1`.
- **Given** a click at x = 25% of the width **When** handled **Then** `HistoryScrub` carries the second at 25% of the view.
- **Given** Shift+drag from 20% to 40% **When** released **Then** `HistorySetRange` carries those seconds and the header shows the range text.
- **Given** a double-click **When** handled **Then** the page is live.
- **Given** the strip focused **When** rendered **Then** the focus ring is drawn.

- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/mod.rs`: handlers
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_history.rs`: add tests

title: E30-023 History top-3 hover card
description:
## Context
Hovering the timeline shows a card with the time and the top 3 processes for the active metric at that second (PROC-090, UI-PRC-034, R-063). The engine rebuilds the sweep at that second and ranks it (50 ms budget); the UI debounces pointer moves by 32 ms and keeps one TopAt query in flight. Sources: UI-PRC-034, PROC-090, R-063, table (d) formats.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/hover.rs`:
  - `TopController`: on hover at second `t`, waits 32 ms without a new pointer move, then sends `Command::HistoryQuery { id, range: At(t), what: TopAt { t, metric, n: 3 } }`; at most one in flight, a newer request replaces the pending one (same rule as E30-017).
  - The card renders as a deferred overlay (`defer_draw`) from cached `ShapedLine`s, styled like `TlTooltip`: `menu_bg`, 1 px `divider`, `r_sm`, padding `sp4`, `t_sm`, width 260. Anchor: 12 px right of the hover hairline and 8 px below the strip top; flips to the left of the hairline when it would cross the right edge.
  - Lines: first "<HH:MM:SS>  (<offset>)" with the time in `t_sm` semibold `text_primary` and the offset in `text_secondary`, offset as a short age "-4m 12s" (table (d) short-age form with a leading minus); second "CPU total <value>" in `text_secondary` (CPU total at t, one decimal percent); a divider; then up to 3 rows 20 px high: rank, 16 px icon, "<name> (<pid>)", value right-aligned with tabular numbers.
  - Value formats per metric (R-063): "CPU: 12.3%", "Memory: 1.22 / 62.70 GiB" (process RssAnon over `mem_total_bytes`, IEC two decimals), "Disk: 4.2 MiB/s", "Network: 12.0 Mbps" (in the chosen `units.network` unit), "GPU: 41.0%". Fewer than 3 processes: fewer rows.
  - While waiting: the previous card stays; after 150 ms without an answer for the current second the rows read "…".
  - Shown while the pointer is over the plot and not dragging; hidden on leave, on drag start and on wheel. A click sets the scrub time (E30-022).
- `mod.rs`: `pub mod hover;`.
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` (chain edit): `history-top-cpu-total` "CPU total { $value }", `history-top-cpu` "CPU: { $value }", `history-top-memory` "Memory: { $used } / { $total }", `history-top-disk` "Disk: { $value }", `history-top-network` "Network: { $value }", `history-top-gpu` "GPU: { $value }".

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a TopAt answer for CPU with values 12.3, 6.1, 2.0 **When** the card renders **Then** the rows read "CPU: 12.3%", "CPU: 6.1%", "CPU: 2.0%" in rank order.
- **Given** Memory with 1,310,000,000 bytes and total 67,320,000,000 **When** rendered **Then** the value reads "Memory: 1.22 / 62.70 GiB".
- **Given** `units.network = "bits"` and 1,500,000 B/s **When** rendered **Then** the value reads "Network: 12.0 Mbps".
- **Given** pointer moves every 10 ms for 100 ms **When** they stop **Then** exactly one TopAt query is sent 32 ms after the last move.
- **Given** the hairline 100 px from the right edge **When** the card would overflow **Then** it is placed left of the hairline.
- **Given** no answer for 150 ms **When** rendered **Then** the rows read "…".

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/hover.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/mod.rs`: wire it
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append keys (chain edit, E16)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_history.rs`: add tests

## Tests
- `tests/ui_history.rs::top3_card_formats_per_metric`, `top3_query_debounced_and_coalesced`, `top3_card_flips_at_right_edge`, `top3_stale_rows_after_150ms`.

## Cross-cutting

- Validity: N/A

- Performance: at most one query per 32 ms; the card re-shapes only when its text changes.

title: E30-024 History minimap
description:
## Context
The minimap under the strip shows the whole retained span of the active metric's system total with a viewport box marking the strip's visible range; dragging the box pans the strip and dragging an edge zooms (UI-PRC-033, PROC-089). Sources: UI-PRC-033, PROC-089, UI-PRC-036 (recording-off span).

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/minimap.rs`: custom `Element`, 24 high, full width, `list_bg`, 1 px `divider` top border.
  - One area path of `HistoryView.overview` (the active metric's `graph.*` fill at 50% alpha, no line), cached by the overview's identity and the size.
  - Viewport box over `view_range`: 1 px `accent` border, `accent` at 15% fill, 4 px edge grips; hover: border 2 px. The scrub time as a 1 px `accent` tick.
  - Interaction: drag the box to pan (cursor `grab`, `grabbing` while dragging); drag an edge to zoom (`ew-resize`), span clamped to 60 s..retained span; click outside the box centres it there; wheel zooms like the strip (factor 1.25 per notch, E30-022 `zoom`).
  - Recording off: the span is the 10-minute window, so the box fills the whole map when the strip shows everything.
- `mod.rs`: `pub mod minimap;` and place it in the 24 px slot.

description:
## Context
The Live button, the recording-off banner and toast, the store-loading state and the store load-problem toasts of History mode (UI-PRC-036, PROC-086, PROC-087, D-010). With recording off, History mode shows the 10-minute RAM window and tells the user once per session, with a button to turn recording on. Sources: UI-PRC-036, UI-SHL-023 (toast with Enable), PROC-086, PROC-087, D-003, D-010.

## Deliverable
- In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/mod.rs`:
  - Live button: `TlButton` small (24 high) "Live" in the header line, left of the chips. While live: `primary` filled, no hover change, tooltip "Showing live data". While scrubbed or a range is set: `default` style with a 6 px `status.success` dot before the label and tooltip "Return to live (double-click the timeline or press End)"; click dispatches `HistoryLive`.
  - Recording-off banner (when `history.enabled = false` and not dismissed this session): one line under the header, 28 high, `status.info` at 15% fill, `t_sm` text "History recording is off. Showing the last 10 minutes kept in memory.", a small `TlButton` "Enable" at the right that sets `history.enabled = true` through `TlSettings::update` (the engine switches to the store), and an × that sets `banner_hidden = true` for the session.
  - Recording-off toast: on entering History mode with `history.enabled = false`, once per session (`off_toast_shown`), an Info toast "History recording is off" with one action button "Enable" (same effect); autohide off because it has an action button; it closes on Enable or its close button.
  - Store loading: while `store_state == Loading` the strip shows "Loading history…" centred in `text_secondary` and the table is empty.
  - Load problems: when `store_state` becomes `Problem(p)`, show once per session per problem a Warning toast with the PROC-087 text: `OpenFailed` "Could not open process history store.", `EmptyOrTruncated` "Process history store is empty or truncated.", `VersionMismatch` "Process history store version/layout mismatch; starting fresh.", `NoInRange` "No in-range process history in store.", `Stale` "Process history store is stale.", `TimedOut` "Process history load timed out; starting fresh.".
  - Recording off: the minimap span covers only the 10-minute window and strip labels never exceed "-10:00" (follows from the span; asserted in a test).
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` (chain edit): `history-live` "Live", `history-live-tip-on` "Showing live data", `history-live-tip-off` "Return to live (double-click the timeline or press End)", `history-off-banner` "History recording is off. Showing the last 10 minutes kept in memory.", `history-off-toast` "History recording is off", `history-enable` "Enable", and the six `history-load-*` texts above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Given** a scrub point **When** rendered **Then** the button shows the green dot and clicking it returns to live.
- **Given** recording off **When** History mode is entered twice in one session **Then** the toast "History recording is off" with one "Enable" button shows only the first time.
- **Given** the banner **When** × is clicked **Then** it stays hidden for the session, also after leaving and re-entering History mode.
- **Given** Enable in the banner **When** clicked **Then** `history.enabled` is true and the banner disappears.
- **Given** `store_state = Problem(Stale)` in two views **When** both are installed **Then** one toast "Process history store is stale." appears.
- **Given** recording off with 10 minutes of data **When** the strip labels render **Then** none is beyond "-10:00".

description:
## Context
Anchor E30-A3: History mode works inside the Processes tab. This bead mounts `HistoryPage` in place of the live table while `state.toml [processes] history_mode` is true, handles the toggle, and adds the end-to-end UI tests. The mount and toggle handling are the chain edit 00-epics.md section 2 gives E30 in `pages/processes/mod.rs`. Sources: UI-PRC-030, UI-SHL-023, PROC-088, D-010, R-023, UI-SHL-140 area of shell.md (Ctrl pause freezes the history table), ADR-009.

## Deliverable

  - When `UiState.processes.history_mode` is true, the tab content renders the `HistoryPage` entity (created on first entry, dropped when the mode turns off) instead of the live table; the live table entity is kept, not rebuilt.
  - A handler for `ToggleHistoryMode` (the Action E20 declares in `crates/tl-ui/src/actions.rs`; the window-level part that selects the Processes tab is E20's, UI-SHL-023): flips `history_mode` through `TlSettings::update` (persisted in `state.toml`), and on turning on with `history.enabled = false` triggers the once-per-session recording-off toast (E30-026).
  - While History mode is shown, the page's demand keeps `Demand.process_table = true`, so the engine keeps the rolling window (D-010).
  - While Ctrl is held (Ctrl pause), the history table renders from the paused snapshot like the live table (shell.md: pages that freeze include the history table).
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_history.rs`: end-to-end cases with the fake engine (E16 `testing/fake_engine.rs`), which records commands and returns scripted `HistoryView`s.

- **Given** recording off **When** History mode turns on **Then** the toast "History recording is off" appears once and `Demand.process_table` stays true.
- **Given** `history_mode = true` in `state.toml` at start **When** the window opens **Then** History mode shows at once.
- **Given** Ctrl held **When** a new `HistoryView` arrives **Then** the history table does not change until Ctrl is released.
- **Given** the full History mode **When** a scripted session scrubs, selects a range, picks Memory, selects two rows and deletes one **Then** the commands sent are, in order: Live Frame, At Frame, Span Frame, Span Frame with Memory, Span Frame with two keys, HistoryDelete with one key.

title: E30-001 tl-history crate skeleton, HistoryError and workspace members line
description:
## Context
Creates the P3 crate `tl-history`, which holds the history segment format, the store and the in-RAM rolling window (ADR-012, ADR-001 layout). This bead adds the crate skeleton, its error type and its `members` line in the root `Cargo.toml`. The members line is a chain edit to an E02-owned file (00-epics.md section 2: "a P3 crate adds its `members` line"). Sources: ADR-001, ADR-002, ADR-012, ADR-015 (thiserror enums), R-072.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-history/Cargo.toml`: `name = "tl-history"`, `edition.workspace = true`, `version.workspace = true`, `[lints] workspace = true`. Dependencies, all `workspace = true`: `tl-model`, `zstd`, `crc32fast`, `postcard`, `serde` (features `derive`, `rc` if the workspace pin does not already have them; do not change the root pin), `thiserror`. Dev-dependencies: `proptest` and `tempfile` if they are workspace pins; if a pin is missing, stop and report it to the leader rather than adding one.
- `crates/tl-history/src/lib.rs`: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, module list `pub mod error;` only (later beads add `format`, `block`, `segment`, `store`, `rolling`, `recorder`, `read`, `retention`), and `pub use error::HistoryError;`.
- `crates/tl-history/src/error.rs`:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum HistoryError {
    #[error("i/o error at {path}: {source}")] Io { path: std::path::PathBuf, #[source] source: std::io::Error },
    #[error("bad segment header")] BadHeader,
    #[error("unsupported format version {0}")] Version(u16),
    #[error("block crc mismatch at offset {0}")] Crc(u64),
    #[error("block truncated at offset {0}")] Truncated(u64),
    #[error("zstd: {0}")] Zstd(std::io::Error),
    #[error("postcard: {0}")] Decode(#[from] postcard::Error),
    #[error("load budget exceeded")] Timeout,
}
```

- **Given** the new crate **When** `cargo xtask check-deps` runs **Then** it passes: `tl-history` depends only on its ADR-001 row (tl-model, zstd, crc32fast, postcard, serde, thiserror) and has no asupersync in its closure.

title: E30-002 History format types and segment header codec
description:
## Context
Defines the on-disk and in-RAM history types and the segment header codec in `tl-history/src/format.rs` (ADR-012 "Format"). Everything else in the crate builds on these types. The ADR fixes the field lists; the byte offsets, the footer layout and the `FieldPatch` shape are proposals waiting on open items E30-OI-2 and E30-OI-3 (see Reference). Sources: ADR-012, ADR-003 (ids, `ProcessKey`, `SeriesId`, `DeviceIdx`, `ProcessRecord`), PROC-086, PROC-087, D-004, R-005, R-025.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-history/src/format.rs` with, all `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]`:
  - constants `MAGIC: [u8; 4] = *b"TLH\x01"`, `FOOTER_MAGIC: [u8; 4] = *b"TLHF"`, `FORMAT_VERSION: u16 = 1`, `HEADER_LEN: usize = 64`, `BLOCK_SECS: u64 = 60`, `SEGMENT_SECS: u64 = 600`, `ZSTD_LEVEL: i32 = 3`, `CPU_THRESHOLD_PERMILLE: u16 = 1`, `MEM_THRESHOLD_KIB: u32 = 256`, `RATE_THRESHOLD_KIBPS: u32 = 1`.
  - `MetaId`, `Block`, `HistMeta`, `HistDevice`, `HistProcess`, `SweepDelta`, `FieldPatch` exactly as in the Reference.
  - `FooterEntry { start_t_ns: u64, offset: u64 }`.
  - `SegmentHeader { boot_id: BootId, realtime_offset_ns: i64, start_t_ns: u64 }` with `fn encode(&self) -> [u8; 64]` and `fn decode(b: &[u8]) -> Result<SegmentHeader, HistoryError>` (wrong magic or length gives `BadHeader`, a version other than 1 gives `Version(v)`, non-zero reserved bytes are ignored).
  - `pub fn segment_file_name(start_t_ns: u64) -> String` giving `seg-{:010}.tlh` of `start_t_ns / 1_000_000_000`, and `pub fn boot_dir_name(boot: BootId) -> String` giving `{:016x}`.
  - `pub fn hist_process(rec: &ProcessRecord, meta: MetaId) -> HistProcess` with the conversion rules in the Reference.
  - `impl FieldPatch { pub fn diff(stored: &HistProcess, cur: &HistProcess) -> Option<FieldPatch>; pub fn apply(&self, p: &mut HistProcess); }`: `diff` returns `None` when no field crosses its threshold.
- `lib.rs`: add `pub mod format;`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a header with boot id `0x0123456789abcdef`, offset `-5`, start `42` **When** encoded and decoded **Then** the decoded header equals the input and bytes 30..64 are zero.
- **Given** 64 bytes starting `TLH\x02` **When** decoded **Then** the result is `Err(HistoryError::BadHeader)`.
- **Given** a valid header with version bytes `2, 0` **When** decoded **Then** the result is `Err(HistoryError::Version(2))`.
- **Given** `start_t_ns = 12_345_000_000_000` **When** `segment_file_name` runs **Then** it returns `seg-0000012345.tlh`.
- **Given** stored CPU 100 permille and current 100 permille with memory up 255 KiB **When** `diff` runs **Then** it returns `None`.
- **Given** stored memory 1000 KiB and current 1256 KiB **When** `diff` runs **Then** the patch has `mem_anon_kib: Some(1256)` and every other field `None`.

title: E30-003 Block frame codec with CRC and zstd
description:
## Context
The block frame codec: one 60 s `Block` becomes `u32 LE length | u32 LE crc32 | zstd level 3 frame` of postcard bytes, and back (ADR-012). Segments and the rolling window both use it. Decoding must never panic on bad input, because a crashed segment is read up to the first bad CRC. Sources: ADR-012, ADR-013 (proptest: arbitrary bytes never panic), PROC-087.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-history/src/block.rs`:
  - `pub struct EncodedBlock { pub start_t_ns: u64, pub bytes: Vec<u8> }` where `bytes` is the full frame including the 8-byte prefix.
  - `pub fn encode_block(b: &Block) -> Result<EncodedBlock, HistoryError>`: `postcard::to_stdvec`, then `zstd::bulk::compress(.., ZSTD_LEVEL)`, then prefix length and `crc32fast::hash` of the compressed bytes.
  - `pub fn decode_block(frame: &[u8], offset: u64) -> Result<(Block, usize), HistoryError>`: reads the prefix, returns `Truncated(offset)` when fewer bytes than the length remain, `Crc(offset)` on mismatch, `Zstd` on decompression error and `Decode` on postcard error; returns the block and the number of bytes consumed. Decompression uses `zstd::bulk::decompress` with a capacity limit of 64 MiB (`MAX_BLOCK_RAW = 64 << 20`); a frame claiming more is `Zstd`.

- `lib.rs`: add `pub mod block;`.

- **Given** a block with 3 metas, 50 keyframe processes, 60 deltas and 2 system series **When** encoded and decoded **Then** the decoded block equals the original and `consumed == bytes.len()`.
- **Given** an encoded block with one compressed byte flipped **When** decoded at offset 64 **Then** the result is `Err(Crc(64))`.
- **Given** an encoded block cut 1 byte short **When** decoded **Then** the result is `Err(Truncated(offset))`.
- **Given** any byte vector up to 4 KiB (proptest) **When** `decode_block` runs **Then** it returns `Ok` or `Err` and never panics.

title: E30-004 BlockBuilder: keyframes, deltas, 1 Hz system series
description:
## Context
`BlockBuilder` turns the stream of process sweeps and system samples that the reducer's `RecordSink` sees into 60 s `Block`s: a keyframe of every live process at block start, one `SweepDelta` per later sweep with only the changes beyond the thresholds, and 1 Hz system series (ADR-012). The store recorder and the rolling window share it. Sources: ADR-012 (format, thresholds, 1 Hz rule), ADR-003 (`ProcessRecord`, `Sample`, `SampleFlags::GAP_BEFORE`, `DeviceCatalog`), PROC-086 (gaps for suspend, resume and epoch changes).

## Deliverable
- In `crates/tl-history/src/block.rs`, after the codec:

```rust
pub struct BlockBuilder { /* private */ }
impl BlockBuilder {
    pub fn new(boot: BootId) -> Self;
    /// MetaId counter restarts at 0 (store: new segment).
    pub fn reset_meta_scope(&mut self);
    pub fn on_device_catalog(&mut self, catalog: &DeviceCatalog);
    pub fn set_mem_total_kib(&mut self, kib: u64);
    /// Returns a closed block when this call crossed the block boundary.
    pub fn on_process_sweep(&mut self, t_ns: TimeNs, records: &[ProcessRecord]) -> Option<Block>;
    pub fn on_system_sample(&mut self, t_ns: TimeNs, series: &[(SeriesId, Sample)]) -> Option<Block>;
    /// Gap: suspend, resume or engine epoch change. Closes the open block.
    pub fn mark_gap(&mut self, t_ns: TimeNs) -> Option<Block>;
    /// Closes the open block now (shutdown, mode switch).
    pub fn flush(&mut self) -> Option<Block>;
    pub fn open_bytes_estimate(&self) -> usize;
}
```

Rules:
- A block covers `[start, start + 60 s)` where `start` is the boottime of the first sweep or sample in it. The first event at or after `start + 60 s` closes the block and opens the next, whose first sweep becomes its keyframe.
- Keyframe: every record of the first sweep, converted with `format::hist_process`. Later sweeps: records whose `ProcessKey` is new go to `started` (appending indexes); keys that disappeared go to `exited` by index; others go to `changed` only when `FieldPatch::diff` against the last stored value returns `Some`. `dt_ms = (t_ns - start) / 1_000_000`.
- Records with `ProcFlags::EXITED` are treated as gone (not stored).
- Metadata: a `ProcessKey` gets a `MetaId` the first time it is seen in the current scope; `new_meta` of the block holds those first sightings. `HistMeta` fields: `comm`, `name`, `exe_basename` (last path component of `meta.exe`), `app_id`, `exe_path = meta.exe`, `user`, `uid`, `system = matches!(group kind, System)` taken from `ProcFlags::KERNEL_THREAD | OTHER_USER` or the System group (use the flag test `KERNEL_THREAD || OTHER_USER` if the group kind is not reachable from the record; OI-2). Never `cmdline`.
- System series: per `SeriesId`, one point per boottime second, value = max of the samples in that second; a sample without `SampleFlags::VALID` or with `GAP_BEFORE` writes a `f32::NAN` point for its second.
- `catalog` is `Some` in the first block after `reset_meta_scope` and in the first block after `on_device_catalog` saw a new `version`; `None` otherwise. `HistDevice.kind` follows the `DeviceIdentity` variant order (0 CpuPackage .. 8 Battery).
- `mark_gap` closes the open block (returns it) and sets `gap_before = true` on the next block.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 70 one-second sweeps of the same 10 processes with constant values **When** fed in order **Then** exactly one block is returned (at sweep 61) with 10 keyframe entries, 59 deltas and every delta's `changed`, `started` and `exited` empty.
- **Given** a sweep where one process's CPU goes from 10.0% to 10.05% **When** the next sweep is added **Then** no patch is written for it (0.5 permille is under the threshold).
- **Given** a new key in sweep 3 and a vanished key in sweep 4 **When** the block closes **Then** delta 2 has one `started` entry with index 10 and delta 3 has `exited = [index of the vanished key]`.
- **Given** 10 CPU samples in one second with values 1..=10 **When** the block closes **Then** the CPU series holds one point with value 10.0 for that second.
- **Given** a sample with `GAP_BEFORE` **When** the block closes **Then** that second's point is NaN.
- **Given** an open block **When** `mark_gap` is called **Then** it returns the block and the next returned block has `gap_before = true`.
- **Given** the first block after `reset_meta_scope` **When** it closes **Then** `catalog` is `Some` and later blocks with the same catalog version have `None`.

## Tests
- `block::tests::steady_state_has_empty_deltas`, `sub_threshold_change_not_stored`, `started_and_exited_indexes`, `system_series_per_second_max`, `gap_sample_writes_nan`, `mark_gap_closes_and_flags_next`, `catalog_only_when_changed`, `meta_assigned_once_per_scope`, `no_cmdline_in_meta`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A (no I/O).
- Validity: invalid fields convert to 0 (format rules).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the builder keeps a `HashMap<ProcessKey, (u32 index, HistProcess)>` of last stored values; per sweep it allocates only the delta vectors. 2,000 records per sweep must convert in under 1 ms in release (checked in E30-A1's bench-style test).
- Privacy: `cmdline` is never read.

description:
## Context

This is the core of every history query, from the store and from the rolling window. Sources: ADR-012, PROC-088, PROC-090, UI-PRC-031.

## Deliverable

```rust

impl MetaTable { pub fn absorb(&mut self, b: &Block); pub fn get(&self, id: MetaId) -> Option<&HistMeta>; }

pub struct Frame { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub procs: Vec<HistProcess> }   // state at one second

pub fn state_at(b: &Block, t_ns: TimeNs) -> Option<Frame>;

pub fn for_each_state(b: &Block, f: impl FnMut(&Frame));
```

description:
## Context
The rest of the read side: min/max decimation of system and process series to at most 1,024 points, the top-K processes at one second for the hover card, system totals at a second, and the deleted-keys filter (ADR-012 reading rules, PROC-089, PROC-090, R-103). Sources: ADR-012, ADR-009 (decimation with absolute buckets), PROC-088 to PROC-090, R-063, R-103.

## Deliverable
- In `crates/tl-history/src/read.rs`:

```rust

pub enum Metric { Cpu, Memory, Disk, Network, Gpu }   // mirrors tl_model::command::HistoryMetric
pub struct Point { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub min: f32, pub max: f32 }
/// Bucket width w = max(1 s, ceil((to - from) / MAX_POINTS)) rounded up to whole seconds; bucket i covers
/// [floor(t / w) * w, +w) in absolute boottime, so two calls 100 ms apart give the same boundaries.
pub fn bucket_width_ns(from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs) -> u64;
pub fn decimate(points: impl Iterator<Item = (TimeNs, f32)>, from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs) -> Vec<Point>;
/// Per-second value of one process for one metric, from blocks overlapping [from, to].
pub fn process_series<'a>(blocks: impl Iterator<Item = &'a Block>, key: ProcessKey, m: Metric, from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs) -> Vec<Point>;
/// System total of a metric per second from the stored 1 Hz series and the block catalog:
/// Cpu = CPU_TOTAL of the CpuPackage device; Memory = MEM_USED; Disk = sum of DISK_READ + DISK_WRITE over Disk devices
/// with parent None; Network = sum of NET_RX + NET_TX over Net devices; Gpu = max GPU_UTIL over Gpu devices.
pub fn system_series<'a>(blocks: impl Iterator<Item = &'a Block>, m: Metric, from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs) -> Vec<Point>;
/// Per bucket: the three largest per-process values of the metric and the sum of the rest (E30-OI-5).
pub fn stack<'a>(blocks: impl Iterator<Item = &'a Block>, m: Metric, from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs) -> Vec<(TimeNs, [f32; 3], f32)>;
/// Top n processes at second t, ranked by the metric descending, ties by ProcessKey ascending.
pub fn top_at(frame: &Frame, m: Metric, n: usize) -> Vec<(ProcessKey, MetaId, f32)>;
pub struct DeletedKeys(std::collections::HashSet<ProcessKey>);
impl DeletedKeys { pub fn contains(&self, k: &ProcessKey) -> bool; pub fn insert_all(&mut self, ks: &[ProcessKey]); }
```
- NaN points are gaps: `decimate` never folds a NaN into min or max; a bucket with only NaN is emitted as `min = max = NaN` so the UI draws a gap.
- Every function that returns rows skips keys in `DeletedKeys` (callers pass the set).
- Process metric values: Cpu in percent, Memory in bytes, Disk and Network in bytes per second, Gpu in percent (same conversions as E30-005).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 6 h of 1 Hz points **When** decimated over the whole span **Then** at most 1,024 points come back and each holds the min and max of its bucket.
- **Given** a single spike sample of 100 among zeros **When** decimated **Then** the bucket containing it has `max = 100` (ADR-009: the max spike survives).
- **Given** two calls with `from` 100 ms apart and the same width **When** bucket boundaries are compared **Then** they are identical.
- **Given** a bucket containing only NaN points **When** decimated **Then** that point is NaN.
- **Given** a frame with CPU values 5, 30, 12, 30 for keys k1..k4 (k2 < k4) **When** `top_at(.., Cpu, 3)` runs **Then** it returns k2, k4, k3 in that order.
- **Given** a deleted key **When** `top_at` or `range_stats` callers filter with `DeletedKeys` **Then** the key never appears.
- **Given** a catalog with one CpuPackage and 4 CpuLogical devices **When** `system_series(Cpu)` runs **Then** only the CpuPackage `CPU_TOTAL` points are used.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: NaN marks a gap; nothing else.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: decimation is one pass with no per-point allocation; output `Vec` reserved to `MAX_POINTS`.
- Privacy: N/A

title: E08-A1 Runtime, supervision, Source loop
description:
## Context
Anchor E08-A1 "Runtime, supervision, `Source` loop". ## Deliverable

```rust

pub mod dbus; pub mod workers;
// chain-edit lines added by later beads: session, reducer, bridge (E09); actions (E11); gpu (E13); launcher, opener (E14); helper (E29); history_query (E30)
```

title: E08: demand-driven rate LabRuntime tests (lab_demand.rs)
description:
## Context
ADR-008's schedule is driven by `Demand`: a CPU chart at 10 Hz when `cpu_fast`, 1 Hz when visible, off when hidden with recording off, and "hidden with recording off produces zero `sample()` calls over 60 virtual seconds". This bead proves the loop and a real `period()` table follow the schedule within one `IDLE_RECHECK`. title: E08: zbus connection helper with executor tick and timeouts (dbus/mod.rs)
description:
## Context
D-Bus workers (logind, systemd, KWin, udisks, UPower, NetworkManager, the openers) share one connection recipe: a `zbus::Connection` with `internal_executor(false)` driven by a child task that ticks its executor under a 500 ms timeout, every call wrapped in `time::timeout` (2 s for reads) and followed by a checkpoint, proxies that never outlive their generation. zbus futures do not see `Cx` cancellation, so the timeouts are the only cancellation point. Sources: ADR-004 (D-Bus workers), ADR-006 (action deadlines, used by E11), API notes section 9, ADR-001 (`zbus` allowed in `tl-engine`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/dbus/mod.rs`:

```rust
pub const READ_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
pub const EXECUTOR_TICK: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);
pub const CONNECT_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum DbusError { #[error("connect: {0}")] Connect(Arc<str>), #[error("timeout after {0:?}")] Timeout(Duration), #[error("{name}: {message}")] Call { name: Arc<str>, message: Arc<str> }, #[error("closed")] Closed }
impl From<DbusError> for WorkerError;   // → WorkerError::Dbus(text)

pub enum Bus { Session, System }
pub struct DbusConn { conn: zbus::Connection, _tick: TaskHandle<()> }   // dropping it ends the tick task
pub async fn connect(cx: &Cx, bus: Bus) -> Result<DbusConn, DbusError>;
impl DbusConn {
    pub fn raw(&self) -> &zbus::Connection;
    /// `time::timeout(cx.now(), d, fut)` then `cx.checkpoint()`; Elapsed → DbusError::Timeout(d)
    pub async fn call<T>(&self, cx: &Cx, d: Duration, fut: impl Future<Output = zbus::Result<T>>) -> Result<T, DbusError>;
    pub async fn read<T>(&self, cx: &Cx, fut: impl Future<Output = zbus::Result<T>>) -> Result<T, DbusError>;   // call with READ_TIMEOUT
    /// Next item of a signal stream with a timeout; Ok(None) on timeout so callers can loop and checkpoint.
    pub async fn next_signal<S: Stream + Unpin>(&self, cx: &Cx, s: &mut S, d: Duration) -> Result<Option<S::Item>, DbusError>;
}
pub fn error_name(e: &zbus::Error) -> Option<&str>;   // "org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.AccessDenied" and friends, for E11 mapping
```

`connect` builds `zbus::connection::Builder::session()` or `::system()` with `.internal_executor(false)`, awaits `.build()` under `CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, then spawns the tick task with `cx.spawn(|cx| async move { loop { let _ = time::timeout(cx.now(), EXECUTOR_TICK, conn.executor().tick()).await; if cx.checkpoint().is_err() { break; } } })`. The `zbus` dependency uses `default-features = false, features = ["async-io"]` (workspace pin, E02).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `call` with a future that never resolves and `d = 10 ms` **When** awaited in a LabRuntime task **Then** it returns `Err(DbusError::Timeout(10 ms))` after exactly 10 ms of virtual time.
- **Given** `call` after the `Cx` was cancelled **When** the inner future resolves **Then** `call` returns `Err(DbusError::Closed)` (checkpoint failed).
- **Given** a `zbus::Error::MethodError` with name `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.AccessDenied` **When** `error_name` is called **Then** it returns that string.
- **Given** a real session bus (`#[ignore]` test) **When** `connect(Session)` is awaited **Then** `raw().unique_name()` is `Some` and dropping `DbusConn` ends the tick task within 500 ms.

- `crates/tl-engine/Cargo.toml`: `zbus` is already listed by E08-A1

## Tests

- `dbus/mod.rs::tests::call_after_cancel_is_closed`
- `dbus/mod.rs::tests::error_name_extracts_dbus_name`
- `dbus/mod.rs::tests::real_session_connect` (`#[ignore]`, owner machine)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: every D-Bus failure becomes `DbusError`; workers map it to `Validity::Failed` plus `last_error` unless the bus itself is gone (then `WorkerError::Dbus` restarts the generation).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one executor tick task per connection; at most 5 connections (session, system, plus the KWin and systemd pairs share these two).
- Privacy: log D-Bus error names, never message bodies that carry unit or window names above `debug`.

zbus 5 with `async-io` starts its own reactor thread; its futures wake through the std `Waker` and run beside asupersync's reactor (API notes section 9, inferred and to be confirmed by the first real test here). `time::timeout` `time/timeout_future.rs:344`. title: E08-A2 D-Bus helper and logind worker
description:
## Context
Anchor E08-A2 "D-Bus helper and logind worker". The `Logind` worker is the first event-driven worker and the pattern for every D-Bus worker: it subscribes to `PrepareForSleep` on `org.freedesktop.login1.Manager` and sends `SourceUpdate::Sleep { entering }` so the reducer can pause rates and mark gaps (ADR-008 suspend signal 1). It is always on, in `EngineMode::Full` only (the low-memory process has no graphs to gap). Sources: ADR-004 (`Logind` worker row, D-Bus workers), ADR-008 (suspend and resume), E08-009.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/workers/logind.rs`:

```rust
pub const BUS_NAME: &str = "org.freedesktop.login1";
pub const PATH: &str = "/org/freedesktop/login1";
pub const INTERFACE: &str = "org.freedesktop.login1.Manager";
pub const SIGNAL: &str = "PrepareForSleep";
pub fn spec() -> WorkerSpec;   // id: SourceId::Logind, name "logind", modes &[EngineMode::Full]
pub fn factory(_cfg: Arc<EngineConfig>, io: WorkerIo) -> WorkerFactory;
async fn run(cx: Cx, io: WorkerIo) -> Outcome<(), WorkerError>;
```

`run`: `connect(&cx, Bus::System)`, build a `zbus::Proxy` for the interface, `receive_signal(SIGNAL)` → stream; send `Health { Running }`; loop `{ match conn.next_signal(&cx, &mut stream, READ_TIMEOUT).await { Ok(Some(msg)) => { let entering: bool = msg.body().deserialize()?; io.updates.send(&cx, EngineMsg::Source(SourceUpdate::Sleep { entering, t_ns: now_boot_ns() })).await; } Ok(None) => { if cx.checkpoint().is_err() { return Outcome::Ok(()) } } Err(e) => return Outcome::Err(e.into()) } }`. A missing logind (connect error or `NameHasNoOwner`) sends `Health { state: Failed, last_error: "logind not available" }` and returns `Outcome::Err(WorkerError::Dbus(..))`, so the supervisor retries with backoff and the 60 s disable takes over. No tab lists `Logind` as a surface, so the Collector Health chip never shows it (UI-SHL collector health).

`workers/mod.rs::all_workers()` gets the logind entry (this bead, as the owner).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake stream that yields `true` then `false` **When** `run` consumes it under a LabRuntime `Cx` **Then** the channel receives `Sleep { entering: true }` then `Sleep { entering: false }` in that order with increasing `t_ns`.
- **Given** the stream yields nothing for 10 s **When** the `Cx` is cancelled **Then** `run` returns `Outcome::Ok(())` within one `READ_TIMEOUT` (2 s) of the cancel.
- **Given** a real system bus (`#[ignore]`) **When** the worker connects **Then** `Health { Running }` is sent within 5 s and the proxy's `PreparingForSleep` property reads `false`.
- **Given** `workers_for(EngineMode::LowMemory)` **When** called **Then** `Logind` is not in it; `workers_for(Full)` contains it once.

- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs`: add `pub mod logind;` and the `WorkerSpec` entry

## Tests

- `workers/logind.rs::tests::cancel_ends_within_read_timeout`
- `workers/logind.rs::tests::real_logind_connect` (`#[ignore]`)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: bus loss → `WorkerError::Dbus` → restart with backoff; health `Failed` text "logind not available".
- Validity: N/A (no values)
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one wake per 2 s while idle (the signal timeout loop).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
Depends on E08-A1 and E08-009. The signal body is a single boolean `b`. zbus: `Proxy::new(&conn, BUS_NAME, PATH, INTERFACE)`, `proxy.receive_signal("PrepareForSleep").await` gives a `SignalStream`. title: E08: build_runtime with the ADR-004 RuntimeBuilder settings
description:
## Context
ADR-004 fixes how the asupersync runtime is built: 1 worker thread, a blocking pool of 1 to 4 threads, thread name prefix `tl-engine`, global queue limit 256. The blocking pool is off by default in asupersync 0.5.0 and must be set, or `Cx::spawn_blocking` runs inline on the async worker (API notes section 2). Sources: ADR-004 (runtime construction, banned APIs), `docs/research/claude-asupersync-apis.md` sections 1, 2, 4.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/runtime.rs`:

```rust
pub const WORKER_THREADS: usize = 1;
pub const BLOCKING_THREADS_MIN: usize = 1;
pub const BLOCKING_THREADS_MAX: usize = 4;
pub const GLOBAL_QUEUE_LIMIT: usize = 256;
pub const THREAD_NAME_PREFIX: &str = "tl-engine";

pub(crate) fn build_runtime() -> Result<asupersync::runtime::Runtime, asupersync::Error> {
    RuntimeBuilder::new()
        .worker_threads(WORKER_THREADS)
        .blocking_threads(BLOCKING_THREADS_MIN, BLOCKING_THREADS_MAX)
        .thread_name_prefix(THREAD_NAME_PREFIX)
        .global_queue_limit(GLOBAL_QUEUE_LIMIT)
        .build()
}
```

The function is `pub(crate)`; no asupersync type leaves the crate (ADR-001 rule 2). `current_thread()` is never called. A doc comment lists the banned asupersync APIs from ADR-004 so readers of this file see them.

`crates/tl-engine/Cargo.toml` gains `asupersync = { workspace = true }` (the workspace pin is `=0.5.0`, `default-features = false`, `features = ["proc-macros"]`) and under `[dev-dependencies]` `asupersync = { workspace = true, features = ["proc-macros", "test-internals"] }`.

- **Given** `build_runtime()` **When** called **Then** it returns `Ok` and `rt.handle()` can `spawn_checked` a task that completes.
- **Given** a task that calls `Cx::spawn_blocking(|_| std::thread::current().name().map(str::to_owned))` **When** joined **Then** the thread name starts with `tl-engine` and is not the async worker's thread.
- **Given** `cargo tree -p tl-engine -e features -i asupersync` **When** run without `--all-targets` **Then** neither `nightly-outcome-try` nor `test-internals` is listed.

title: E08: EngineMsg, SourceUpdate (every variant) and WorkerError (update.rs)
description:
## Context
Every worker talks to the reducer with one message type, and every later epic (E09 to E14, E29, E30, E32) compiles against it, so the full variant set is written now and never grows (`00-epics.md` section 2: "`SourceUpdate` carries every variant up front"). The payloads are built from `tl-model` types so the reducer can publish them without copying. Device-bound samples are keyed by `DeviceIdentity`, because `DeviceIdx` is assigned by the reducer's catalog (ADR-003). Sources: ADR-004 (`EngineMsg`, worker list), ADR-003 (component types), ADR-005 (`Command`), ADR-007 (GPU messages), ADR-008 (suspend signals), ADR-015 (`WorkerError`), R-119, R-137.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/update.rs`:

```rust
pub enum EngineMsg {
    Source(SourceUpdate),
    Command(Command),                      // tl_model::command::Command
    ActionFinished { id: ActionId },
    Tick,                                  // housekeeping, sent every 1 s by the session (stale marking, linger expiry)
}

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum WorkerError {
    #[error("collect: {0}")] Collect(#[from] tl_collect::CollectError),
    #[error("d-bus: {0}")] Dbus(Arc<str>),
    #[error("probe: {0}")] Probe(Arc<str>),
    #[error("timeout after {0:?}")] Timeout(Duration),
    #[error("channel closed")] Closed,
    #[error("{0}")] Other(Arc<str>),
}

pub enum SourceUpdate {
    Health { id: SourceId, state: SourceState, last_error: Option<Arc<str>>, t_ns: TimeNs },
    ResumeDetected { id: SourceId, t_ns: TimeNs },        // ADR-008 clock check: Δboot − Δmono > 250 ms
    Sleep { entering: bool, t_ns: TimeNs },               // Logind PrepareForSleep
    Cpu(CpuSample),                                       // E12 Cpu
    Memory(MemorySample),                                 // E12 Memory
    Disks(DiskSample),                                    // E12 Disk
    Nets(NetSample),                                      // E12 Net
    Sensors(SensorSample),                                // E12 Sensors
    Devices(DeviceList),                                  // E12 enumerate (every 5 s)
    Gpu(GpuSample),                                       // E13 GpuNvidia, E12 GpuDrm
    GpuInfo(GpuInfoUpdate),                               // static per-device info
    GpuApiVersions(tl_model::gpu_proto::ApiVersions),     // E13, once at start
    Processes(ProcessSweep),                              // E10 Processes, E32 lowmem
    Details(DetailsUpdate),                               // E10 ProcessDetail and handle search
    Connections(ConnectionsUpdate),                       // E14 Connections
    ConnectionsDestroySupport(bool),                      // E11 SockDestroy answer (sets destroy_supported)
    Services(ServicesUpdate),                             // E14 SystemdSystem / SystemdUser
    Startup(StartupUpdate),                               // E14 Startup
    Inventory(Box<InventorySnapshot>),                    // E12 Inventory (header rewritten by the reducer)
    Windows(Box<WindowsSnapshot>),                        // E14 KWin
    History(Arc<HistoryView>),                            // E30 answer to HistoryQuery
}

pub struct CpuSample { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub totals: CpuTotals, pub irq_pct: f32 /* Δ(irq+softirq)/Δtotal, for the Interrupts row */,
    pub per_cpu: Vec<CpuCoreSample>, pub freq_mhz: Option<u32>, pub temp_c: Option<f32>, pub temp_validity: Validity,
    pub topology: Option<Arc<CpuTopology>> /* Some on first sample and on hotplug */, pub validity: Validity }
pub struct CpuCoreSample { pub cpu: u16, pub pct: f32, pub kernel_pct: f32, pub freq_mhz: Option<u32>, pub validity: Validity }
pub struct MemorySample { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub totals: MemoryTotals, pub zram: Vec<ZramStat>, pub validity: Validity }
pub struct ZramStat { pub name: Arc<str>, pub disksize: u64, pub orig_bytes: u64, pub compr_bytes: u64, pub mem_used_total: u64, pub read_bps: f32, pub write_bps: f32 }
pub struct DiskSample { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub disks: Vec<(DeviceIdentity, DiskTotals)> }

pub struct DeviceList { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub kinds: DeviceKinds, pub entries: Vec<DeviceDesc> }   // complete list for `kinds`; the reducer diffs

pub struct ProcessSweep { pub observed_start: TimeNs, pub observed_end: TimeNs, pub records: Vec<ProcessRecord> /* sorted by key; NEW and EXITED are set by the reducer */,
    pub app_stats: Vec<CgroupStats>, pub unit_stats: Vec<CgroupStats>, pub system_threads: u32, pub file_nr: Option<u64>, pub online_cpus: u16 }
```

- **Given** the crate **When** compiled **Then** every variant above exists with these payload names and no variant is `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- **Given** `size_of::<EngineMsg>()` **When** measured **Then** it is at most 256 bytes (large payloads are boxed or in `Vec`/`Arc`).
- **Given** `SourceUpdate::Cpu(..)` **When** `source_of` is called **Then** it returns `Some(SourceId::Cpu)`; for `Sleep` it returns `None`.
- **Given** a later epic needs a new variant **When** it opens a bead **Then** it depends on E08-A1 and asks the leader; it does not edit this file (owner only).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `WorkerError` is the restart signal (`Outcome::Err`); expected conditions (EACCES, missing device, unsupported) are reported as `Validity` inside the payload, never as `WorkerError` (ADR-004).
- Validity: every payload carries `Validity` per device or field; missing is never zero.

title: E08: Source trait, WorkerIo, WorkerControl and the sampling loop (source.rs)
description:
## Context
Every periodic worker shares one loop: absolute deadlines from asupersync `interval` with `MissedTickBehavior::Skip`, a fresh `Sleep` each turn, a checkpoint, one `spawn_blocking` job per sample, `IDLE_RECHECK` when the source is off, and the `Late` rule. Workers receive demand and settings through `watch` receivers cloned per generation, and reducer-to-worker control (baseline resets after resume, `RefreshNow`, forwarded commands) through one more `watch` (B3 open item 1). Sources: ADR-004 (worker factory contract, sampling worker loop, `Source` trait), ADR-008 (tick semantics, schedule, hidden detection, suspend signal 1), API notes sections 3 to 5 (`watch` borrow rule, `Sleep` per turn, interval is synchronous).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/source.rs`:

```rust
pub const IDLE_RECHECK: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);
pub const LATE_FRACTION: f64 = 0.8;      // job longer than 0.8 × period
pub const LATE_COUNT: u32 = 3;           // ... for 3 consecutive jobs → SourceState::Late

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct WorkerIo {
    pub updates: mpsc::Sender<EngineMsg>,            // asupersync mpsc, capacity 256, shared with the UI command path
    pub demand: watch::Receiver<Demand>,
    pub settings: watch::Receiver<EngineSettings>,
    pub control: watch::Receiver<WorkerControl>,
}
#[derive(Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct WorkerControl {
    pub reset_generation: u64,                       // bumped on resume and on Command::ResetBaselines
    pub commands: Arc<[QueuedCommand]>,              // newest 64 forwarded commands, ascending seq
}
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct QueuedCommand { pub seq: u64, pub target: SourceId, pub command: WorkerCommand }
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub enum WorkerCommand {
    RefreshNow, Reprobe,
    KWin(KWinCommand),
    DetailRefresh { target: DetailTarget, tab: DetailTab }, ComputeHashes(ProcessKey), VerifyPackage(ProcessKey),
    StringScan { scan: ScanId, key: ProcessKey, opts: StringScanOpts }, CancelStringScan(ScanId),
    HandleSearch { search: SearchId, pattern: Arc<str>, include_maps: bool, privileged: bool }, CancelHandleSearch(SearchId),
    HistoryQuery { id: u64, range: HistoryRange, what: HistoryWhat }, HistoryDelete { keys: Arc<[ProcessKey]> },
    SetupStatus, RunSetup { step: SetupStep },
}

pub trait Source: Send + 'static {
    fn id(&self) -> SourceId;
    fn period(&self, demand: &Demand, settings: &EngineSettings) -> Option<Duration>;   // None = off
    fn sample(self) -> (Self, SourceUpdate) where Self: Sized;                           // blocking pool
    fn reset_baselines(&mut self) {}                                                     // reset_generation rose
    fn command(&mut self, cmd: &WorkerCommand) -> bool { false }                         // true = sample at once
}

pub async fn run<S: Source>(cx: Cx, io: WorkerIo, src: S) -> Outcome<(), WorkerError>;
```

`run` behaviour, in order each turn:
1. `period = src.period(&io.demand.borrow_and_clone(), &io.settings.borrow_and_clone())`; if it changed, rebuild `iv = interval(cx.now(), period.unwrap_or(IDLE_RECHECK))` with `set_missed_tick_behavior(Skip)`; a change from one `Some` to another `Some` also calls `src.reset_baselines()` (ADR-008: first sample after a rate change is `WarmingUp`, `GAP_BEFORE` on the ring is the reducer's job).
2. `sleep_until(iv.deadline()).await` (a new `Sleep` each turn); `if cx.checkpoint().is_err() { return Outcome::Ok(()) }`; `iv.tick(cx.now())`.
3. Read `io.control.borrow_and_clone()`: if `reset_generation` rose, `src.reset_baselines()`; for each `QueuedCommand` with `target == src.id()` and `seq > last_seq`: `RefreshNow` forces a sample this turn, anything else goes to `src.command(..)` and forces a sample if it returns true.
4. If `period` is `None` and no forced sample: continue (no I/O).
5. `let job = cx.spawn_blocking(move |_| src.sample())?; let (s, update) = job.join(&cx).await?; src = s;` measure the job duration with `cx.now()`; after `LATE_COUNT` consecutive jobs longer than `LATE_FRACTION × period` send `SourceUpdate::Health { state: Late, .. }` once; when a job is on time again send `Health { state: Running }` once.
6. `io.updates.send(&cx, EngineMsg::Source(update)).await` mapped to `WorkerError::Closed` on error.

Never hold a `watch` `Ref` across another channel call (`borrow_and_clone()` only). A worker never starts a second job while one runs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a source with period 100 ms **When** the loop runs 1 s of virtual time **Then** `sample()` is called 10 times at 100 ms steps from the first deadline (absolute deadlines, no drift).
- **Given** a sample that takes 250 ms with period 100 ms **When** the loop runs **Then** no catch-up burst happens (next sample at the next future deadline) and after 3 such jobs one `Health { state: Late }` is sent.
- **Given** `period()` returns `None` **When** 60 s pass **Then** `sample()` is never called and the loop woke 120 times (`IDLE_RECHECK`).
- **Given** `reset_generation` rises **When** the next turn starts **Then** `reset_baselines()` is called exactly once before `sample()`.
- **Given** a `QueuedCommand { target: this, command: RefreshNow }` **When** the source is off **Then** exactly one `sample()` runs at once.
- **Given** the `Cx` is cancelled **When** the loop reaches its checkpoint **Then** it returns `Outcome::Ok(())` and never calls `sample()` again.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/source.rs`: create

## Tests
- Covered by `tests/lab_source_loop.rs` (E08-007) and `tests/lab_demand.rs` (E08-008); this bead adds `source.rs::tests::worker_control_default_is_empty` only.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `spawn_blocking` or `send` failure returns `Outcome::Err(WorkerError)` so the supervisor restarts the worker; a cancelled `Cx` returns `Ok`.
- Validity: N/A here (payload-level).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: an off source costs two wakeups per second and no I/O; the loop allocates only when the period changes.
- Privacy: `WorkerCommand::StringScan` and `HandleSearch` carry patterns; never log them.

## Notes
asupersync 0.5.0: `time::interval(now, period)` is synchronous (`time/interval.rs:430`); `sleep_until` `time/sleep.rs:1145` returns early on user or shutdown cancel; `Cx::checkpoint` `cx/cx.rs:2508`; `Cx::spawn_blocking` `cx.rs:4661`, joined with `TaskHandle::join(&mut self, &cx)`; `watch::Receiver::borrow_and_clone` (API notes section 5, bead `c11v6v`). The fourth `WorkerIo` field and `WorkerCommand` are B3 open item 1. Event-driven D-Bus workers do not use `run`; they take `WorkerIo` directly (E08-010 shows the pattern). Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E08: per-worker ManagedSupervisor with backoff and budget (supervise.rs)
description:
## Context
Each worker gets its own one-child `ManagedSupervisor` so a crash-looping source cannot spend another source's restart budget (ADR-004, API notes section 3). The policy is fixed: one-for-one, `Transient`, exponential backoff 500 ms doubling to 30 s, 5 restarts per 60 s, escalation `Stop`. Sources: ADR-004 (per-worker supervisor), ADR-013 (LabRuntime cases), API notes section 3 and 7.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/supervise.rs`:

```rust
pub const MAX_RESTARTS: u32 = 5;
pub const RESTART_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);
pub const BACKOFF_INITIAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);
pub const BACKOFF_MAX: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
pub const BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER: f64 = 2.0;

/// Any `Fn(Cx, ManagedGeneration) -> Fut` with `Fut: Future<Output = Outcome<(), WorkerError>> + Send`.
pub type WorkerFactory = Arc<dyn ManagedChildFactory<WorkerError>>;

pub fn build_supervisor(name: &str, factory: WorkerFactory) -> Result<ManagedSupervisor<WorkerError>, SuperviseError>;
pub async fn run_supervised(cx: &Cx, name: &str, factory: WorkerFactory) -> Result<ManagedSupervisorReport<WorkerError>, SuperviseError>;  // spawn + join
pub fn budget_exhausted(report: &ManagedSupervisorReport<WorkerError>) -> bool;  // true when the child is down because the 5-in-60 s budget was spent

fn legacy_unreachable(_: &Scope<'static, FailFast>, _: &mut RuntimeState, _: &Cx) -> Result<TaskId, SpawnError> { unreachable!("managed mode never calls the legacy start") }

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum SuperviseError { #[error("compile: {0}")] Compile(Arc<str>), #[error("bind: {0}")] Bind(Arc<str>), #[error("spawn: {0}")] Spawn(Arc<str>) }
```

`build_supervisor` is exactly the ADR-004 block: `SupervisorBuilder::new(name).with_restart_policy(OneForOne).child(ChildSpec::new(name, legacy_unreachable)).compile()`, then `SupervisionConfig::new(5, 60 s).with_restart_policy(OneForOne).with_backoff(Exponential { initial: 500 ms, max: 30 s, multiplier: 2.0 }).with_escalation(EscalationPolicy::Stop)`, then `bind_managed(vec![ManagedChildBinding::new(name, ManagedRestartMode::Transient, factory)], config)`. `ChildSpec::depends_on` is never used (bead `bi2462.99`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a factory whose generations 1 to 4 return `Outcome::Err` and generation 5 blocks until cancelled **When** run in `LabRuntime` with auto-advance **Then** generation start times are at 0, 0.5, 1.5, 3.5, 7.5 s of virtual time (backoff 0.5, 1, 2, 4 s).
- **Given** a factory that always returns `Err` **When** run **Then** exactly 6 generations start (1 + 5 restarts) and `budget_exhausted(&report)` is true.
- **Given** a factory whose generation 1 panics **When** run **Then** generation 2 starts after 500 ms (`Transient` restarts on panic).
- **Given** a factory that returns `Outcome::Ok(())` after a user cancel **When** the handle is aborted **Then** no generation starts after the abort and the report shows no restart batch after it.
- **Given** any of the above **When** the test ends **Then** `run_until_quiescent_with_report().lab_test_passed()` is true.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/supervise.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_supervise.rs`: create

## Tests
- `lab_supervise.rs::restart_backoff_timings`: the 0, 0.5, 1.5, 3.5, 7.5 s schedule.
- `lab_supervise.rs::budget_exhausted_after_five`: 6 starts then stop; `budget_exhausted` true.
- `lab_supervise.rs::panic_restarts_like_err`: panic → restart.
- `lab_supervise.rs::no_restart_after_cancel`: abort stops generations.
- `lab_supervise.rs::explore_restart` with `#[explore_seeds(seeds = 0..16, workers = 2, chaos)]`: the first two cases hold under chaos.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `SuperviseError` wraps the three asupersync error types as text; it never leaves the crate.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one supervisor task per worker, about 20 tasks total.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
asupersync 0.5.0 `src/supervision.rs`: `ChildSpec::new` L654, `compile` L970, `SupervisionConfig` L429, `BackoffStrategy` L324, `EscalationPolicy` L407, `ManagedRestartMode` L1811, `ManagedChildFactory` L1854, `bind_managed` L2054, `ManagedSupervisor::spawn` L3084, `ManagedSupervisorHandle::join` L3032. The intensity tracker is shared per supervisor (main `supervision.rs:3006-3040`), which is why each worker gets its own. Restart test pattern: main `supervision.rs:3376-3395`, `3606-3651`; `tests/supervision_regression.rs:197-204` for the legacy stub. Lab driving: `LabConfig::new(seed).max_steps(1_000_000)`, `lab.state.create_root_region(Budget::INFINITE)`, `create_task`, `run_with_auto_advance()`. Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E08: SourceController with the 60 s disable (controller.rs)
description:
## Context
A `SourceController` wraps one worker's supervisor for the life of a session. When the restart budget is spent it publishes `SourceState::Disabled { until }`, sleeps 60 s, binds a fresh supervisor and tries again: "five failures in a minute, then off for a minute" (ADR-004). It also publishes `Running` when a generation starts and `Failed` with the last error when one dies, so the Collector Health items ("<Source> paused after errors", "<Source> unavailable", UI-SHL collector health) have data. Sources: ADR-004 (task tree, per-worker supervisor), ADR-013, UI-SHL collector health texts, ADR-015 (log targets).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/controller.rs`:

```rust
pub const DISABLE_FOR: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);

pub struct SourceController { id: SourceId, name: &'static str, factory: WorkerFactory, updates: mpsc::Sender<EngineMsg> }
impl SourceController {
    pub fn new(id: SourceId, factory: WorkerFactory, updates: mpsc::Sender<EngineMsg>) -> Self;
    /// Runs until `cx` is cancelled. Spawn with `cx.spawn(|cx| ctl.run(cx))` from the session.
    pub async fn run(self, cx: Cx);
}
```

`run` loop: send `Health { Running }`; `run_supervised(&cx, name, factory.clone()).await`; if `cx.is_cancel_requested()` return; if `budget_exhausted(&report)`: send `Health { state: Disabled { until: now_boot_ns() + 60 s }, last_error: <last Err text or "panic"> }`, `time::sleep(cx.now(), DISABLE_FOR).await`, checkpoint, loop; otherwise (supervisor ended for another reason) log at `warn` on target `tasklens::source::<name>` and loop at once. Sends use `updates.send(&cx, ..).await`; a `Closed` error ends the loop. The worker's own `Late` and `Running` health messages come from `source::run` (E08-004); the controller does not duplicate them.

`SourceState` values used: `Running`, `Late`, `Disabled { until: TimeNs }`, `Failed` (defined in `tl-model/src/health.rs`, E03-A1; use its exact spelling).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a factory that always fails **When** the controller runs 130 s of virtual time **Then** the health messages are `Running`, then `Disabled { until = t0 + 60 s }` at about 7.5 s (after 5 backoffs: 0.5 + 1 + 2 + 4 = 7.5 s), then `Running` at about 67.5 s, then `Disabled` again at about 75 s.
- **Given** a factory that fails 3 times then runs **When** 60 s pass **Then** no `Disabled` message is sent.
- **Given** the controller's `Cx` is cancelled while a worker generation is running **When** the cancel propagates **Then** the generation returns `Ok` and `run` returns without sending `Disabled`.
- **Given** the `updates` receiver is dropped **When** the controller tries to send **Then** `run` returns.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/controller.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_supervise.rs`: add the controller cases

## Tests
- `lab_supervise.rs::controller_disables_for_60s_then_retries`: the message timeline above.
- `lab_supervise.rs::controller_no_disable_under_budget`: 3 failures, no `Disabled`.
- `lab_supervise.rs::controller_stops_on_cancel`: cancel ends the loop.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the last `WorkerError` text goes into `last_error` (shown in the health tooltip); a panic gives `"panic"`.
- Validity: while `Disabled`, the reducer marks the source's values `Failed` with `last_error` (E09-004).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: idle cost is one sleeping task per source.
- Privacy: `last_error` must not contain process text; `WorkerError::Collect` from `tl-collect` carries paths of `/proc` files only.

## Notes
`time::sleep(now, d)` `time/sleep.rs:1124` returns early on shutdown cancellation, so the 60 s sleep ends promptly at shutdown. `ManagedSupervisorReport` fields: child outcome, `started`, `restart_batches`, `escalations` (`supervision.rs` L1997). Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E08: fake sources and Source-loop LabRuntime tests
description:
## Context
The `Source` loop (E08-004) and the supervisors need scripted fake sources so the LabRuntime tests are deterministic: ok, err, panic, slow, and a sample counter the tests can read. The same file serves E09 and E10 tests through `#[path]` inclusion. Sources: ADR-013 (fake sources with scripted results; required cases), ADR-004 (loop rules).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/tests/fake_sources.rs` (included by other test files with `#[path = "fake_sources.rs"] mod fake_sources;`):

```rust
pub enum Step { Ok, Err(&'static str), Panic, Slow(Duration) }
pub struct FakeSource {
    pub id: SourceId,
    pub script: Vec<Step>,            // consumed in order; the last step repeats
    pub period_on: Option<Duration>,  // returned by period() when `on(demand, settings)` is true
    pub on: fn(&Demand, &EngineSettings) -> bool,
    pub log: Arc<Mutex<Vec<(TimeNs, &'static str)>>>,   // ("sample", t) and ("reset", t) entries
}
impl Source for FakeSource { /* sample() pushes ("sample", now), sleeps virtual time for Slow, panics for Panic, returns SourceUpdate::Health{Running} for Ok */ }
pub fn lab() -> LabRuntime;                                  // LabConfig::new(42).max_steps(1_000_000)
pub fn channels() -> (mpsc::Sender<EngineMsg>, mpsc::Receiver<EngineMsg>, watch::Sender<Demand>, watch::Sender<EngineSettings>, watch::Sender<WorkerControl>);
pub fn io(..) -> WorkerIo;                                    // clones receivers from the senders above
pub fn demand_with(f: impl FnOnce(&mut Demand)) -> Demand;
pub fn drain(rx: &mut mpsc::Receiver<EngineMsg>) -> Vec<EngineMsg>;   // try_recv until empty
```

`crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_source_loop.rs` tests the loop in E08-004 with these fakes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `FakeSource` with `period_on = 100 ms` and script `[Ok]` **When** `source::run` runs 1 s **Then** the log has 10 `sample` entries at 100 ms spacing starting at the first interval deadline.
- **Given** script `[Slow(250 ms)]` and period 100 ms **When** run 2 s **Then** samples start only at future deadlines (no two samples closer than 100 ms, no burst after a slow job) and a `Health { Late }` message appears after the third slow job, followed by no second `Late` until a `Running` has been sent.
- **Given** script `[Err("boom")]` **When** `sample` runs **Then** `source::run` returns `Outcome::Err(WorkerError::Other("boom"))`.
- **Given** script `[Panic]` under a supervisor **When** run **Then** generation 2 starts after 500 ms.
- **Given** the demand watch is updated so `on` flips to false **When** the next wake happens **Then** no further `sample` entries appear and wakes continue every 500 ms (checked by a `Slow(0)` counter: the loop re-reads demand at most 500 ms after the change).
- **Given** every test **When** it ends **Then** `run_until_quiescent_with_report().lab_test_passed()` holds.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/fake_sources.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_source_loop.rs`: create

## Tests
- `lab_source_loop.rs::absolute_deadlines_no_drift`
- `lab_source_loop.rs::slow_job_skips_ticks_and_reports_late`
- `lab_source_loop.rs::err_returns_outcome_err`
- `lab_source_loop.rs::panic_under_supervisor_restarts`
- `lab_source_loop.rs::demand_change_seen_within_idle_recheck`
- `lab_source_loop.rs::reset_generation_calls_reset_once`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A (test support)
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
`Cx::spawn_blocking` runs inline in the lab, so `Slow` must advance virtual time with `time::sleep` inside the blocking closure's `Cx` (the closure receives a `Cx`); do not use `std::thread::sleep`. `Cx::for_testing` needs `test-internals` and is allowed only in tests. title: E09: suspend and resume handling (reducer/suspend.rs, lab_suspend.rs)
description:
## Context
Suspend is detected two ways, whichever comes first: logind `PrepareForSleep(true)` pauses rate publication and `PrepareForSleep(false)` resets baselines, re-enumerates devices and marks `GAP_BEFORE` on every series; or a worker's clock check (`Δboot − Δmono > 250 ms`) reports `ResumeDetected`. After resume the GPU probe is not restarted. Sources: ADR-008 (suspend and resume), ADR-003 (`GAP_BEFORE`), PERF-022, R-051, ADR-013 (lab suspend case), E08-003 (`Sleep`, `ResumeDetected`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/suspend.rs`:

```rust
pub struct SuspendState { pub sleeping: bool, pub slept_at_ns: Option<TimeNs>, pub resumed_at_ns: Option<TimeNs>, pub resume_count: u32 }
impl SuspendState {
    pub fn on_sleep(&mut self, entering: bool, t_ns: TimeNs) -> Transition;      // Entering | Resumed | None
    pub fn on_clock_resume(&mut self, id: SourceId, t_ns: TimeNs) -> Transition; // Resumed once per 2 s window, then None (several workers report the same resume)
    pub fn drop_rates(&self) -> bool;   // true while sleeping: rate samples are appended as gaps
}
pub enum Transition { Entering, Resumed, None }
```

Reducer effects (wired in `apply.rs`): `Entering` → `sleeping = true` (rate samples become gaps until resume); `Resumed` → `series.mark_gap_all()`, `bump_reset_generation()`, `forward(Disk, RefreshNow)`, `forward(Net, RefreshNow)`, `forward(Sensors, RefreshNow)` (re-enumeration), `sleeping = false`. `GpuNvidia` gets no command.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `Sleep { entering: true }` then two CPU samples **When** applied **Then** both samples are gap samples (`VALID` clear).
- **Given** `Sleep { entering: false }` **When** applied **Then** `reset_generation` rose by 1, the next sample of every series has `GAP_BEFORE`, and `RefreshNow` was forwarded to `Disk`, `Net` and `Sensors` but not to `GpuNvidia`.
- **Given** `ResumeDetected` from `Cpu` and 50 ms later from `Memory` **When** applied **Then** the reset generation rose once, not twice.
- **Given** `ResumeDetected` with no earlier `Sleep` **When** applied **Then** the effects are the same as a logind resume.
- **Given** a sample pair with a 5 s boottime gap and a 10 ms monotonic gap (reported as `ResumeDetected` by the worker) **When** applied **Then** the series shows a gap and no rate spike (the first post-resume sample is `WarmingUp`, a gap).

title: E09: table builder flat mode, sort, tie-break, filter (reducer/table.rs)
description:
## Context
The engine builds the process table rows; the UI never sorts or filters (ADR-009). This bead builds the flat mode (`TableMode::Flat`): filter, sort with the `ProcessKey` tie-break, non-sortable columns, and the row list with `query_generation`. Tree and grouped modes extend it (E09-010, E09-011). Sources: ADR-009 (`TableQuery`, `TableRow`, `ProcessTableView`, filter rule), PROC-014 (modes), PROC-044 (filter matching), PROC-047 (sorting; non-sortable columns), R-007 (column ids), R-011 (default PID ascending), R-043, ADR-003 (`ProcessKey` ordering).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs` (part 1):

```rust
pub struct TableInput<'a> { pub records: &'a [ProcessRecord], pub app_stats: &'a [CgroupStats], pub unit_stats: &'a [CgroupStats], pub system: &'a SystemSnapshot, pub devices: &'a DeviceCatalog, pub settings: &'a EngineSettings, pub unit_names: &'a FxHashMap<UnitRef, Arc<str>> /* Description, E09-025; empty in P1 */ }
pub fn build(input: &TableInput<'_>, query: &TableQuery) -> ProcessTableView;
pub const NOT_SORTABLE: &[&str] = &["pss", "uss", "cycles", "cycles_delta", "ctx_switches", "ctx_switches_delta"];   // sorting on these falls back to PID ascending
pub enum SortKey { Int(i128), Float(f32), Text(Arc<str>), Absent }   // Absent sorts last in both directions
pub fn sort_key(r: &ProcessRecord, col: ColumnId) -> SortKey;
pub struct Filter { terms: Vec<Term> }   // Term { lower: String, digits: bool }
impl Filter { pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Self; pub fn matches(&self, r: &ProcessRecord, extra: &[&str]) -> bool; pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool; }
```

Rules:
- `Filter::parse` splits on spaces, lowercases; every term must match: substring of `meta.search_lower`, or of any string in `extra` (group name, unit name), or, when the term is all digits, `key.pid.to_string().starts_with(term)`.
- `sort_key` maps each `ColumnId` to the field it displays: `pid` → `Int(pid)`, `name` → `Text(meta.name)`, `cpu` and `cpu_relative` → `Float(cpu_pct × factor)`, `memory` → `Int(rss_anon_bytes)`, `ws_total` → `Int(rss_bytes)`, `swap`, `disk_read`/`disk_write`/`disk` (rates), `network` (`net_rx + net_tx`), `gpu`, `gpu_mem_dedicated`, `threads`, `nice`/`priority`, `state`, `ppid`, `user` → `Text(meta.user)`, `description`, `cmdline`, `image`/`exe`, `cgroup`, `unit`, `app_id`, `start_time` → `Int(start_ticks)`. A `ColumnId` whose data is not in `ProcessRecord` returns `Absent` (listed in the bead's doc comment; see B3 open item 6). A field whose `FieldValidity` is not `Valid` or `Stale` is `Absent`.
- Order: `sort.ascending` on the key, ties by `ProcessKey` ascending; `Absent` last. Sorting on a `NOT_SORTABLE` id uses `pid` ascending.
- Flat rows: `TableRow { node: Process(key), depth: 0, expanded: false, has_children: false, record: Some(i), group: None, descendants: 0, subtree: None }` for every record that passes the filter; `groups` empty; `query_generation = query.generation`; `totals` from E09-013 (`TableTotals::default()` until then).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** records with PIDs 3, 1, 2 and `sort = pid asc` **When** built **Then** rows are 1, 2, 3; with `desc` 3, 2, 1.
- **Given** two records with equal `cpu_pct` **When** sorted by `cpu` **Then** they are ordered by `ProcessKey` ascending whatever the direction.
- **Given** filter `"fire 12"` and a record named "Firefox" with PID 1234 **When** built **Then** it matches; PID 2123 does not (prefix rule).
- **Given** filter `"root"` **When** built **Then** records whose `search_lower` contains "root" match (user field is part of it).
- **Given** `sort.column = pss` **When** built **Then** the order equals `pid` ascending.
- **Given** a record whose `cpu` validity is `WarmingUp` **When** sorted by `cpu desc` **Then** it is last.
- **Given** `generation = 42` **When** built **Then** `view.query_generation == 42`.

## Cross-cutting

- Validity: `Absent` keeps missing values out of the numeric order; the UI shows the glyph.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one `Vec<(SortKey, u32)>` of n entries per build, sorted with `sort_unstable_by`; 2,000 rows build in under 1 ms on the owner machine (measured in E09-014 with a debug assertion only).
- Privacy: N/A
