title: E09: table builder tree mode, forest, PID +N, include children
description:
## Context
Tree mode shows the ppid forest: a row is a root when its parent is not shown (filtered, hidden or exited); siblings sort under their parent; `expanded` comes from the query; a collapsed parent's PID cell shows "PID +N" with N = total descendants; reparenting moves a process at the next sweep. Include children (filter) shows every descendant of each match. Sources: PROC-014 (Tree View), PROC-018 (+N), PROC-045 (include children), ADR-009 (missing parent → root; UI owns expansion), E09-009.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs`:

```rust
pub struct Forest { pub children: Vec<SmallVec<[u32; 4]>>, pub parent: Vec<Option<u32>>, pub roots: Vec<u32> }   // indexes into the visible record list
pub fn forest(records: &[ProcessRecord], visible: &[bool]) -> Forest;   // parent = index of the record with key.pid == ppid among *visible* records, else None (root)
pub fn descendants_count(f: &Forest, i: u32) -> u32;
pub fn flatten_tree(f: &Forest, order: &dyn Fn(&[u32]) -> Vec<u32>, expanded: &FxHashSet<NodeId>, out: &mut Vec<TableRow>, depth: u8);
```

Rules:
- Visibility: a record is visible when it passes the filter, or (`query.include_children`) when any ancestor passes. With an empty filter every record is visible.
- The parent link uses `ppid` matched against visible records' `pid`; PID 0 and PID 2 handling: kernel threads have ppid 2 and show under `kthreadd` in tree mode (the "Kernel threads" fold is grouped mode only, E09-011).
- `has_children = !children.is_empty()`, `expanded = expanded.contains(&Process(key))`, `descendants = descendants_count`, `depth` increases by 1 per level and saturates at 255.
- Siblings at every level are ordered by the E09-009 sort.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** A(1) → B(2) → C(3) all visible and `expanded = {A, B}` **When** built in Tree mode **Then** rows are A d0, B d1, C d2 with `has_children` true, true, false.
- **Given** the same with `expanded = {A}` **When** built **Then** rows are A d0, B d1 and B has `descendants == 1`; A has `descendants == 2`.
- **Given** filter matches only C **When** built **Then** C is a root at depth 0.
- **Given** filter matches only A and `include_children = true` **When** built **Then** A, B, C all appear (B and C by inheritance).
- **Given** B exits (still lingering with `EXITED`) **When** built **Then** B stays in place and C stays under B; after B is dropped C becomes a root.
- **Given** two roots with `cpu` 10 and 20, sort `cpu desc` **When** built **Then** the 20 root comes first and each root's children are sorted the same way among themselves.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs`: extend

## Tests

- `lab_table.rs::collapsed_parent_descendant_count`
- `lab_table.rs::filtered_child_becomes_root`
- `lab_table.rs::include_children_pulls_descendants`
- `lab_table.rs::exited_parent_keeps_place_then_child_reroots`
- `lab_table.rs::siblings_sorted_under_parent`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: a ppid cycle (impossible in Linux but possible in a fixture) must not loop: `descendants_count` uses an explicit stack with a visited bitset.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: O(n) forest build with one `FxHashMap<u32 /*pid*/, u32>`; no recursion deeper than the stack-based walk.

title: E09: table builder grouped mode, app and unit rows, Kernel threads row
description:
## Context
Task Manager Grouping shows three fixed groups ("Apps (N)", "Background processes (N)", "System processes (N)") whatever the sort, app rows with their primary processes' subtrees, unit rows for systemd units with more than one process, the "Kernel threads (N)" row collapsed by default, and (from P2) the two pseudo rows. Group and app rows aggregate each process once. Sources: PROC-004 (classes and order), PROC-008 (app row contents and children), PROC-009 (unit rows, Kernel threads row), PROC-012 (pseudo rows, P2 in E09-023), ADR-009 (no double counting), R-137 (cgroup stats), D-011, E08-003 (`CgroupStats`).

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs`:

```rust
pub const GROUP_ORDER: [GroupKind; 3] = [GroupKind::App-class, GroupKind::Background, GroupKind::System];   // see classification below
pub fn group_class(r: &ProcessRecord) -> GroupClass;   // Apps | Background | System, from r.group (GroupKind::App → Apps; Background → Background; System and Ungrouped → System; KERNEL_THREAD → System)
pub fn aggregate(records: &[ProcessRecord], members: &[u32], stats: Option<&CgroupStats>) -> GroupRow;   // Σ cpu, io, net, gpu, threads; memory = stats.anon_bytes when Some, else Σ rss_anon; count = members.len(); FieldValidity worst-of
pub fn build_grouped(input: &TableInput<'_>, query: &TableQuery, filter: &Filter) -> (Vec<TableRow>, Vec<GroupRow>);
```

Rules:
- Group header rows: `NodeId::Group(GroupKey)` for the three fixed groups; `has_children = count > 0`; `expanded` from the query (default handling is the UI's; the engine treats a missing entry as collapsed); the count N is the number of processes in the group after filtering (pseudo rows excluded, PROC-012).
- Apps: one row per `GroupKind::App { app_id }` (key = that `GroupKey`), `record: None`, `group: Some(i)` into `groups`; children are the app's primary processes (members whose ppid is not a member) each with its subtree (E09-010 forest restricted to the members), sorted by the query; the app row sorts among app rows by the same column on the aggregated value; memory from `app_stats` (`anon_bytes`, R-137), Disk from members or from the cgroup `io.stat` rate when any member's Disk is `Restricted` (PROC-008, R-103).
- Background and System: processes of the class; those sharing a systemd unit with more than one process fold under a unit row (`GroupKind::Unit(UnitRef)`, name = `unit_names[unit]` else the unit name, aggregated like an app row with `unit_stats` when present); a unit with one process shows the process directly.
- Kernel threads (`KERNEL_THREAD`) fold under one System row `GroupKind::KernelThreads` named "Kernel threads", count N, placed after the sorted System members; pseudo rows follow it (E09-023). The row is expanded only when the query lists it.
- Filter: a term matching a group name ("apps", "background processes", "system processes") or an app or unit name matches every member of it; group headers always stay with their filtered counts.
- No double counting: a process contributes to exactly one app or unit row and to exactly one group header.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 2 app processes, 3 background, 4 system with sort `cpu desc` **When** built **Then** the rows start with "Apps" and the order of headers is Apps, Background, System whatever the sort.
- **Given** an app with primary P (cpu 10) and child C (cpu 5) **When** built with the app expanded **Then** the app `GroupRow.cpu_pct == 15`, rows are App, P d1, C d2, and the Apps header count is 2.
- **Given** `app_stats` with `anon_bytes = 1 GiB` for that app and members whose RssAnon sum is 1.5 GiB **When** built **Then** the app row memory is 1 GiB.
- **Given** 3 processes of unit `pipewire.service` **When** built **Then** one unit row "pipewire.service" with count 3 appears in Background and the processes are its children; a unit with 1 process shows no unit row.
- **Given** 50 kernel threads **When** built **Then** one "Kernel threads" row with count 50 sits after the other System rows and is collapsed unless in `expanded`.
- **Given** filter `"apps"` **When** built **Then** every app member matches and Background and System headers show count 0.
- **Given** the full fixture **When** the group counts are summed **Then** they equal the number of non-pseudo records that pass the filter (each counted once).

## Files

## Tests

- `lab_table.rs::app_row_aggregates_once`
- `lab_table.rs::app_memory_from_cgroup_anon`
- `lab_table.rs::unit_rows_fold_multi_process_units`
- `lab_table.rs::kernel_threads_row_last_in_system`
- `lab_table.rs::group_name_filter_matches_members`
- `lab_table.rs::counts_sum_to_visible_records`

## Cross-cutting

- Validity: `GroupRow` validity per field is the worst of its members (`Restricted` beats `Valid`); memory from the cgroup carries the `CgroupStats.validity`.
- Accessibility: N/A

title: E09: hide system processes in the table builder
description:
## Context
"Hide system processes" is an `EngineSettings` flag that removes the System group, pseudo rows and desktop-infrastructure Background rows, with a fixed exception list; it applies in every mode. Sources: PROC-046 (scope, exception list), R-031, ADR-011 (`hide_system` in `EngineSettings`), PROC-012 (pseudo rows hidden too), E09-011.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs`:

```rust
pub const INFRA_SLICES: [&str; 2] = ["session.slice", "background.slice"];
pub const HIDE_SYSTEM_EXCEPTIONS: [&str; 3] = ["plasma-plasmashell.service", "plasma-kwin_wayland.service", "org.gnome.Shell@wayland.service"];
/// true when the record is hidden by `settings.hide_system`
pub fn hidden_by_hide_system(r: &ProcessRecord, class: GroupClass) -> bool;
```

Rules (PROC-046): hidden when `class == System` (kernel threads, the Kernel threads row, other users, system units), when the row is a pseudo row, or when `class == Background` and the cgroup path contains `/session.slice/` or `/background.slice/` or ends in `/init.scope` under `user@<uid>.service` (`systemd --user`), unless the unit name is in `HIDE_SYSTEM_EXCEPTIONS`; everything in `app.slice` stays. title: E09: two-line header totals (TableTotals)
description:
## Context
The two-line header shows system totals under the column names: CPU and kernel from `/proc/stat`, Memory and Swap percent, Disk highest busy percent, Network as percent of summed link speed or a rate, GPU highest utilization and per-adapter GPU N, VRAM used over total, Threads, Handles from `/proc/sys/fs/file-nr`. The engine fills `ProcessTableView.totals` at every table build from the latest system snapshot. Sources: PROC-038, ADR-008 (CPU and memory math), ADR-003 (`TableTotals`), E08-003 (`ProcessSweep.system_threads`, `file_nr`).

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs`:

```rust
pub fn totals(system: &SystemSnapshot, devices: &DeviceCatalog, sweep: &SweepTotals) -> TableTotals;
pub struct SweepTotals { pub system_threads: u32, pub file_nr: Option<u64> }
```

Each total is a value plus `Validity`:
- `cpu_pct`, `kernel_pct`: from the CPU package totals (`Valid` after two samples, else `WarmingUp`).
- `mem_pct = (MemTotal − MemAvailable) / MemTotal × 100`; `swap_pct = SwapUsed / SwapTotal × 100` (`Unsupported` when `SwapTotal == 0`).
- `disk_busy_pct`: max `DISK_ACTIVE` over present physical disks (parent == None; `loop`, `ram`, `zram`, `fd` excluded by E04's classification); `Missing` when no disk.
- `net`: `Pct(f32)` = Σ(rx + tx) over physical interfaces / Σ link speed when every present physical interface reports a speed, else `Rate { rx_bps, tx_bps }`.
- `gpu_pct`: max over present GPUs; `gpu_n: [Option<f32>; 16]` by PCI bus address ascending; `vram_pct = Σ used / Σ total`; `Unsupported` with no GPU.
- `threads = system_threads`; `handles = file_nr` field 1 (`Unsupported` when `None`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** MemTotal 32 GiB, MemAvailable 8 GiB **When** computed **Then** `mem_pct == 75.0`.
- **Given** SwapTotal 0 **When** computed **Then** `swap_pct` validity is `Unsupported`.
- **Given** disks `sda` busy 40, `nvme0n1` busy 70, `sda1` (child) busy 90 **When** computed **Then** `disk_busy_pct == 70`.
- **Given** two interfaces with speeds 1 Gbit/s and 2.5 Gbit/s and rates summing to 350 Mbit/s **When** computed **Then** `net == Pct(10.0)`; with one speed unknown **Then** `Rate`.
- **Given** two GPUs at bus `0000:2d:00.0` (util 80) and `0000:01:00.0` (util 20) **When** computed **Then** `gpu_pct == 80`, `gpu_n[0] == Some(20)`, `gpu_n[1] == Some(80)`.
- **Given** `file_nr = None` **When** computed **Then** `handles` is `Unsupported`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs`: extend

## Tests
- `lab_table.rs::totals_memory_and_swap`
- `lab_table.rs::totals_disk_max_physical_only`
- `lab_table.rs::totals_net_pct_or_rate`
- `lab_table.rs::totals_gpu_order_by_pci`
- `lab_table.rs::totals_handles_unsupported_without_file_nr`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: every total carries its own `Validity`; the UI renders `n/a` for `Unsupported`.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: O(devices) per build.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
Depends on E09-009. `TableTotals` field names are B3 open item 5 (recommendation in the plan file). Who reads `/proc/sys/fs/file-nr` is B3 open item 7 (recommendation: the E05 sweep fills `ProcessSweep.file_nr`). Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

description:
## Context

title: E09: engine_root and engine_session with epochs and catch_unwind (session.rs)
description:
## Context
`engine_root` owns the UI-facing endpoints for the life of the process and runs sessions in a loop: each session builds its channels, spawns one `SourceController` per worker, runs the reducer inline under `catch_unwind`, and owns every handle so an unwind aborts every child. A reducer panic or `InvariantViolation` restarts with a new epoch after 1 s; more than 3 restarts in 60 s stops restarting and publishes an all-`Failed` health snapshot while the root stays alive. The session also runs the 1 s `Tick` task. Sources: ADR-004 (task tree, session restart rule), ADR-005 (channels), ADR-013 (session restart test), API notes section 2 and 3, E08-A1 (`workers_for`), E09-001.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/session.rs`:

```rust
pub const RESTART_DELAY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);
pub const MAX_RESTARTS: u32 = 3;
pub const RESTART_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);
pub const TICK: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);

pub struct RootEndpoints {
    pub msgs: mpsc::Receiver<EngineMsg>,                 // UI commands and worker updates share it (capacity 256)
    pub msgs_tx: mpsc::Sender<EngineMsg>,                // cloned into every worker's WorkerIo
    pub demand: watch::Receiver<Demand>, pub settings: watch::Receiver<EngineSettings>,
    pub control: watch::Sender<WorkerControl>,
    pub publisher: Publisher, pub events_tx: async_channel::Sender<ActionEvent>,
    pub config: Arc<EngineConfig>, pub boot_id: BootId, pub hooks: EngineHooks,
}
pub async fn engine_root(cx: Cx, mut ep: RootEndpoints);
async fn engine_session(cx: &Cx, ep: &mut RootEndpoints, epoch: u32) -> Result<(), SessionEnd>;   // Ok on cancel; Err on panic or invariant
enum SessionEnd { Panic, Invariant(&'static str) }
```

`engine_session`: `let mut reducer = Reducer::new(epoch, ep.boot_id, ep.control.clone(), ep.events_tx.clone())`; install `hooks.action_gate` and `hooks.record_sink` when present; for every `WorkerSpec` in `workers_for(config.mode)`: build `WorkerIo { updates: msgs_tx.clone(), demand: demand.clone(), settings: settings.clone(), control: control.subscribe() }`, `SourceController::new(id, (spec.factory)(config.clone(), io), msgs_tx.clone())`, `handles.push(cx.spawn(|cx| ctl.run(cx))?)`; spawn the tick task (`loop { sleep(cx.now(), TICK).await; checkpoint; msgs_tx.send(&cx, EngineMsg::Tick).await }`); then `reducer.run(cx, &mut ep.msgs, &mut ep.publisher).await` inline, wrapped in `futures_lite::FutureExt::catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(..))`. Dropping `handles` (a `Vec<TaskHandle>`) on return or unwind aborts every controller.

`engine_root`: `epoch = 1`; loop `{ match engine_session(..).await { Ok(()) => return, Err(end) => { tracing::error!(target: "tasklens::engine", ?end, epoch, "session ended"); restarts.push(now); if restarts in the last 60 s > 3 { publisher.publish(snapshot with health = HealthState::all_failed(epoch, "engine restarted too often")); park until cancel (loop sleep 60 s + checkpoint); return } sleep 1 s; epoch += 1 } } }`. The new session starts with empty rings so every series gets `GAP_BEFORE` on its first sample (rings are new, `pending_gap = true` in `SeriesStore::new`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake worker set and a reducer that panics on the 5th message **When** run in LabRuntime **Then** a new session starts after 1 s with `epoch == 2`, the same `msgs` receiver still delivers, and the first sample of every series in epoch 2 carries `GAP_BEFORE`.
- **Given** a reducer that panics at once in every session **When** run **Then** sessions 1 to 4 start (3 restarts), then the published snapshot has every `SourceHealth.state == Failed` with `last_error == "engine restarted too often"`, and the root task is still alive (not finished) 120 s later.
- **Given** a running session **When** the root `Cx` is cancelled **Then** every controller task ends, `engine_root` returns, and no `sample()` runs afterwards.
- **Given** 10 s of virtual time **When** nothing else happens **Then** exactly 10 `Tick` messages reached the reducer.
- **Given** the sequence from epoch 1 ended at 500 **When** epoch 2 publishes **Then** the sequence continues from 501 (strictly increasing per process: the sequence counter lives in `RootEndpoints`, not in the reducer).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/session.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_session.rs`: create (E09-017 adds the chaos run)

## Tests
- `lab_session.rs::reducer_panic_restarts_with_new_epoch`
- `lab_session.rs::four_restarts_publish_all_failed_and_stay_alive`
- `lab_session.rs::cancel_stops_everything`
- `lab_session.rs::tick_every_second`
- `lab_session.rs::sequence_continues_across_epochs`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: panic text is logged at `error` on `tasklens::engine` with the epoch; no payload content.
- Validity: after the final failure every source is `Failed`.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: a session restart costs one full re-warm of every source (visible gaps).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
Depends on E09-001, E09-007, E08-A1. `Reducer::sequence` is set from `ep.next_sequence` at session start and written back after each publish. `catch_unwind` needs `panic = "unwind"` (ADR-002). API notes: `cx.spawn` `cx.rs:4420`; `try_spawn_with_cx` is used by `Engine::start` (E09-019) to spawn `engine_root`. Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E09-A2 Shutdown
description:
## Context
Anchor E09-A2 "Shutdown". `EngineHandle::shutdown(self, total)` runs the five ADR-004 steps after GPUI has stopped: drop the UI-side senders, `drain_root_region(1000 ms)`, drop every `RuntimeHandle` clone, `shutdown_timeout(500 ms)`, and report; `tl-app` calls `std::process::exit(0)` when the report says a step timed out. Sources: ADR-004 (shutdown), ADR-010 (called on the main thread after GPUI stops), ADR-013 (real-system test: shutdown within 1.5 s under load; lab case: drain is `Quiescent`), API notes section 8, E33-A1 (caller).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/bridge.rs` (part 3):

```rust
pub const DRAIN_BUDGET: Duration = Duration::from_millis(1000);
pub const TEARDOWN_BUDGET: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ShutdownReport { pub drained: bool /* RootDrainOutcome::Quiescent */, pub torn_down: bool /* shutdown_timeout returned true */, pub elapsed: Duration }
impl ShutdownReport { pub fn clean(&self) -> bool { self.drained && self.torn_down } }
impl EngineHandle {
    /// Consumes the handle. `total` is advisory; the two budgets above are the real bounds (1.5 s together).
    pub fn shutdown(self, total: Duration) -> ShutdownReport;
}
```

Steps inside: set `stopped`; take `demand_tx`, `settings_tx`, `msgs_tx`, `events` out of `Inner` and drop them (step 1); `rt.drain_root_region(DRAIN_BUDGET)` (step 2); drop `rt_handle` and every clone (the `Inner` is the last owner; other `EngineHandle` clones must already be dropped by the caller, documented) (step 3); `rt.shutdown_timeout(TEARDOWN_BUDGET)` (step 4); on `!clean()` log `warn` on `tasklens::engine` with both flags (step 5). After `shutdown`, no `TaskHandle` is awaited from any thread (bead `bi2462.91`).

`crates/tl-engine/tests/real_shutdown.rs` (`#[ignore]`, owner machine): start the engine with the real worker set registered so far, `set_demand` with every surface visible, wait 3 s, `shutdown`; assert `clean()` and `elapsed < 1.5 s`; repeat 5 times in one process.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the fake worker set on the real runtime **When** `shutdown(2 s)` is called **Then** `drained && torn_down` and `elapsed < 1.5 s`.
- **Given** a fake worker whose `sample()` blocks for 3 s inside `spawn_blocking` **When** `shutdown` is called **Then** it returns within 1.6 s with `torn_down == false` and the report logged (the blocking job is not interrupted; the process exits anyway).
- **Given** the lab **When** the root `Cx` receives shutdown cancellation **Then** `drain` is `Quiescent` (ADR-013 "shutdown drain is Quiescent").
- **Given** another `EngineHandle` clone is still alive **When** `shutdown` runs **Then** `torn_down == false` (documented behaviour; the test proves the rule from API notes section 8).

title: E09: EngineHandle implementing EngineClient and EngineHooks (bridge.rs part 1)
description:
## Context
`EngineHandle` is the UI's only view of the engine: it implements `tl_model::client::EngineClient` with an `ArcSwap` load, the one-token wake, the action-event channel, the demand and settings `watch` senders and the command queue. No public item names an asupersync type (ADR-001 rule 2, D-001). Sources: ADR-005 (client trait, channels, `CommandError`), ADR-004 (shutdown steps belong to E09-A2), ADR-001, API notes section 5 (no-`Cx` sender operations), R-136.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/bridge.rs` (part 1):

```rust
pub struct EngineHandle { inner: Arc<Inner> }
struct Inner {
    latest: Arc<ArcSwap<Snapshot>>, wake_rx: async_channel::Receiver<()>, events_rx: async_channel::Receiver<ActionEvent>,
    demand_tx: watch::Sender<Demand>, settings_tx: watch::Sender<EngineSettings>, msgs_tx: mpsc::Sender<EngineMsg>,
    last_demand: Mutex<Demand>, journal: Option<JournalSpawner>,
    rt: Mutex<Option<asupersync::runtime::Runtime>>, rt_handle: Mutex<Option<RuntimeHandle>>, stopped: AtomicBool,
}
pub type JournalSpawner = Arc<dyn Fn(JournalQuery) -> JournalHandle + Send + Sync>;   // installed by E14-A4 through EngineHooks

impl EngineClient for EngineHandle {
    fn latest(&self) -> Arc<Snapshot> { self.inner.latest.load_full() }
    fn wake(&self) -> async_channel::Receiver<()> { self.inner.wake_rx.clone() }
    fn action_events(&self) -> async_channel::Receiver<ActionEvent> { self.inner.events_rx.clone() }
    fn set_demand(&self, d: Demand) { if *last != d { last = d.clone(); demand_tx.send(d) } }      // watch::Sender::send needs no Cx; never blocks
    fn set_settings(&self, s: EngineSettings) { settings_tx.send(s) }
    fn send(&self, cmd: Command) -> Result<(), CommandError> {
        if stopped { return Err(CommandError::EngineStopped) }
        msgs_tx.try_send(EngineMsg::Command(cmd)).map_err(|e| match e { SendError::Full(_) => CommandError::Busy, SendError::Closed(_) => CommandError::EngineStopped })
    }
    fn journal(&self, q: JournalQuery) -> JournalHandle { match &journal { Some(f) => f(q), None => JournalHandle::closed(JournalError::NotFound) } }
}
pub struct EngineHooks { pub action_gate: Option<Arc<dyn Fn() -> Box<dyn ActionGate> + Send + Sync>>, pub record_sink: Option<Arc<dyn Fn(&EngineConfig) -> Box<dyn RecordSink> + Send + Sync>>, pub journal: Option<JournalSpawner> }
impl Default for EngineHooks { fn default() -> Self { crate::default_hooks() } }   // lib.rs: filled by chain edits (E11-A1 action gate, E14-A4 journal, E30-A2 record sink)
```

`EngineHandle: Send + Sync + Clone`. `JournalHandle::closed(err)` is a `tl-model` constructor that yields one `JournalEvent::Error(err)` then ends; if E03-A2 did not add it, build the handle from its public parts here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a handle whose command queue holds 256 unread messages **When** `send` is called **Then** it returns `Err(CommandError::Busy)` and does not block.
- **Given** `set_demand(d)` twice with equal `d` **When** the worker side counts `changed()` wakes **Then** it saw one change.
- **Given** `stopped` is set **When** `send` is called **Then** `Err(EngineStopped)`.
- **Given** no journal spawner **When** `journal(q)` is called **Then** the first event on `events()` is `JournalEvent::Error(JournalError::NotFound)` and the channel then closes.
- **Given** `cargo doc --no-deps -p tl-engine` **When** the public signatures of `bridge.rs` are read **Then** none names an asupersync type (`EngineHooks` uses `tl-model` and `tl-engine` traits only).

title: E09: Engine::start (bridge.rs part 2)
description:
## Context
`Engine::start` builds the runtime, the channels and the UI-side endpoints, reads the boot id, and spawns `engine_root` with `try_spawn_with_cx` so shutdown cancellation reaches it. It is the only constructor `tl-app` calls (ADR-001 public API). Sources: ADR-004 (runtime construction, task tree), ADR-005 (channel capacities: wake 1, events 256, commands 256), ADR-003 (`BootId` from `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`), API notes section 2, E08-002, E09-016, E09-018.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/bridge.rs` (part 2):

```rust
pub struct Engine;
impl Engine {
    pub fn start(config: EngineConfig, hooks: EngineHooks) -> Result<EngineHandle, EngineError>;
}
```

Steps: `let rt = runtime::build_runtime().map_err(|e| EngineError::Runtime(e.to_string().into()))?`; `boot_id = tl_model::time::read_boot_id(&config.sys_root)` (or the E03 name); channels: `async_channel::bounded::<()>(1)`, `async_channel::bounded::<ActionEvent>(256)`, `mpsc::channel::<EngineMsg>(256)`, `watch::channel(Demand::default())`, `watch::channel(EngineSettings::default())`, `watch::channel(WorkerControl::default())`; `latest = Arc::new(ArcSwap::from_pointee(Snapshot::empty(boot_id)))` (sequence 0, every component empty with `WarmingUp`, `windows` `Unsupported`); build `RootEndpoints`; `rt.handle().try_spawn_with_cx(move |cx| session::engine_root(cx, ep)).map_err(..Spawn)?`; return the handle holding `rt`, one `RuntimeHandle` clone and the UI endpoints. `Snapshot::empty` lives in `tl-model` if E03-A2 provides it, else a private helper here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `Engine::start(config, EngineHooks::default())` with a fixture `SysRoot` **When** called **Then** it returns within 100 ms, `latest().sequence == 0`, `latest().boot_id` equals the fixture's boot id, and `latest().windows.header.validity == Unsupported`.
- **Given** the handle **When** `wake().recv()` is awaited on a plain executor **Then** it resolves after the first publish and `latest().sequence >= 1`.
- **Given** two `Engine::start` calls in one process (tests) **When** both run **Then** they do not share state (no globals).
- **Given** `set_settings` with `interval_ms = 250` **When** a fake `Processes` worker is registered **Then** its `period()` sees 250 ms within 500 ms.

title: E09: bridge tests: 10,000 publishes, never blocks, Busy (lab_bridge.rs)
description:
## Context
ADR-005 verification: a fake publisher thread does 10,000 publishes and the UI-side loop, run on a plain executor, ends on the final sequence and never sees a sequence go backwards; publishes never block when the wake receiver is never read; memory stays bounded. Sources: ADR-005 (verification), ADR-013, E09-018, E09-019.

## Deliverable

- `ten_thousand_publishes_monotonic`: a `std::thread` publishes 10,000 snapshots through a `Publisher` (sequence 1..=10,000) while a `futures_lite::future::block_on` loop does `wake.recv().await` then `latest()` and asserts `seq > last`; at the end `last == 10_000`.

title: E09: 1 Hz series tier with per-second max
description:
## Context
From P2 every series has a second, 1 Hz ring of 602 samples (10 min + 2) whose values are the per-second maximum of the fast tier, the same rule ADR-012 uses for history; it serves the 5 and 10 minute ranges. Sources: ADR-003 (two tiers), PERF-016, PERF-017, R-016, ADR-012 (per-second max), E09-002.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/series.rs`:

```rust
pub const SLOW_CAPACITY: u32 = 602;
pub const SLOW_PERIOD_NS: u64 = 1_000_000_000;
struct Entry { /* existing */ slow: SeriesRing, bucket_start_ns: TimeNs, bucket_max: Option<f32>, bucket_flags: SampleFlags }
```

`append` also folds into the slow tier: the bucket is `t_ns / 1e9`; within a bucket keep `max(value)` over `VALID` samples and OR the flags; when a sample falls in a later bucket, push `Sample { t_ns: bucket_start_ns, value: max, flags }` to `slow` (a bucket with no valid sample pushes a gap sample); a gap in the fast tier (`GAP_BEFORE`) sets `GAP_BEFORE` on the next slow sample. `publish` emits both tiers: the slow view is published in `SeriesSet.slow` (see B3 open item 5 for the field; recommendation: `SeriesSet { header, series, slow: Arc<[Arc<SeriesView>]> }`, same ordering and `Arc` reuse rule), with `period_ns = 1e9`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 10 Hz samples 1..=10 within one second **When** the next second's first sample arrives **Then** the slow tier holds one sample with value 10 and `t_ns` at the bucket start.
- **Given** 700 s of 1 Hz input **When** published **Then** the slow view holds 602 samples and the fast view 62.
- **Given** a second with no valid sample **When** folded **Then** the slow sample for it is a gap (`VALID` clear).
- **Given** `mark_gap_all` **When** the next bucket closes **Then** that slow sample has `GAP_BEFORE`.
- **Given** no new sample for a series **When** published twice **Then** the slow `Arc<SeriesView>` is pointer-equal across the two sets.

title: E09: pseudo rows Interrupts and Memory compression (zram)
description:
## Context
Two pseudo-process rows stand for kernel work no process owns: "Interrupts" (CPU = irq + softirq share, every other column `n/a`, always present) and "Memory compression (zram)" (Memory = Σ `mem_used_total`, Disk = Σ zram read and write rates, CPU `n/a`, present only when a zram device has `disksize > 0`). They sit in System processes after "Kernel threads (N)", are top-level rows in Tree and List, are excluded from the "N Processes" count, and are hidden by Hide system processes. Sources: PROC-012, R-032, U-21 (`CONFIG_IRQ_TIME_ACCOUNTING`, E05 records), E08-003 (`CpuSample.irq_pct`, `MemorySample.zram`), E09-011.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs` and `apply.rs`:

```rust
pub struct PseudoInput { pub irq_pct: Option<f32> /* None when irq time is not accounted (U-21) */, pub zram: Vec<ZramStat> }
pub fn pseudo_rows(input: &PseudoInput) -> Vec<GroupRow>;   // GroupKind::Pseudo(PseudoRow::Interrupts) always; Pseudo(PseudoRow::Zram) when any zram.disksize > 0
```

Row values: Interrupts `cpu_pct = irq_pct` (`Unsupported` with the tooltip text carried in `GroupRow.note: Option<Arc<str>>` = "Interrupt time is included in task time on this kernel" when `None`), every other field `Unsupported`, name "Interrupts", user "root", count 0. Zram: `rss_anon_bytes = Σ mem_used_total`, `io_read_bps = Σ read_bps`, `io_write_bps = Σ write_bps`, `cpu_pct` `Unsupported`, `note` = "Original <orig> · Compressed <compr> · Ratio <orig/compr:.2>" formatted with `tl_model::units`, name "Memory compression (zram)". Placement: Grouped → after the Kernel threads row in System; Tree and Flat → top-level rows sorted like any other (sort key from the row's value, `Absent` for `Unsupported`). `hide_system` hides both. The group count N excludes them. The reducer keeps the latest `irq_pct` and `zram` from `Cpu` and `Memory` samples for the next table build.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `irq_pct = Some(1.5)` and one zram device with `disksize > 0` **When** built in Grouped mode **Then** the last two System rows are "Interrupts" then "Memory compression (zram)" and the System header count excludes them.
- **Given** no zram device or all `disksize == 0` **When** built **Then** only "Interrupts" appears.
- **Given** `irq_pct = None` **When** built **Then** the Interrupts row CPU is `Unsupported` with the kernel note.
- **Given** Flat mode sorted by `cpu desc` with Interrupts at 1.5 and processes at 1.0 and 2.0 **When** built **Then** the order is 2.0, Interrupts, 1.0.
- **Given** `hide_system = true` **When** built **Then** neither pseudo row appears.
- **Given** filter `"zram"` **When** built **Then** the zram row matches by name.

## Files

- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs`: keep `irq_pct` and `zram` from the samples
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_table.rs`: add the cases

title: E09: subtree totals on parent processes
description:
## Context
With `processes.subtree_totals = true` (Settings > Processes > "Show subtree totals on parent processes", default off, part of `EngineSettings`), process rows that have children show the sum over their subtree for CPU, Disk, Network, GPU, Threads, Handles and Memory (Σ RssAnon), with a "Σ" prefix drawn by the UI. Each process counts once. App and unit rows always aggregate (E09-011). Sources: PROC-019, R-005, ADR-011 (`EngineSettings`), E09-010.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs`:

```rust
pub fn subtree_totals(f: &Forest, records: &[ProcessRecord], visible: &[u32]) -> Vec<GroupRow>;   // one per row with children, computed bottom-up in one pass
```

When `settings.subtree_totals` is true, every `TableRow` whose `has_children` is true gets `subtree: Some(i)` into `ProcessTableView.subtree` (the `Vec<GroupRow>` above; field per B3 open item 5); when false, `subtree` is `None` everywhere and the vector is empty. A collapsed parent in Tree mode always gets its subtree sum (ADR-009: "the collapsed parent shows its subtree sum in secondary text"), independent of the setting.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** A → B → C with cpu 1, 2, 3 and the setting on **When** built with A and B expanded **Then** A's subtree row has `cpu_pct == 6`, B's `3`, C has `subtree == None`.
- **Given** the setting off and A expanded **When** built **Then** A has `subtree == None`; with A collapsed **Then** A has a subtree row (`cpu_pct == 6`).
- **Given** memory 100, 200, 300 MiB **When** built **Then** A's subtree `rss_anon_bytes == 600 MiB`.
- **Given** a filtered-out middle node B with `include_children = false` **When** built **Then** C is a root and A's subtree sum excludes B and C (sums are over visible descendants).

title: E09: unit row names from systemd Description
description:
## Context

title: E09: DetailsSnapshot assembly with Arc reuse and demand retain
description:
## Context
`Snapshot.details` (bit `DETAILS`) holds the Properties payloads per target and tab, the affinity masks for `affinity_targets` and the handle-search state. Unchanged payloads reuse their `Arc`; a window re-renders only when its own tab's `Arc` changed. The `ProcessDetail` worker (E10) sends `DetailsUpdate`s; the reducer assembles the component. Sources: ADR-003 (`DetailsSnapshot`, `TargetDetail`), UI-PWN-002, ADR-008 (`details`, `affinity_targets`), E08-003 (`DetailsUpdate`), R-119.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/mod.rs` and `apply.rs`:

```rust
pub struct DetailsState { targets: FxHashMap<DetailTarget, TargetDetail>, affinity: FxHashMap<ProcessKey, AffinityInfo>, handle_search: Option<Arc<HandleSearchState>>, dirty: bool }
impl DetailsState {
    pub fn apply_tab(&mut self, target: DetailTarget, tab: DetailTab, payload: Arc<TabPayload>, validity: Validity);   // replaces that tab's Arc, bumps its version
    pub fn apply_affinity(&mut self, entries: Vec<(ProcessKey, AffinityInfo)>);
    pub fn apply_handle_search(&mut self, state: Arc<HandleSearchState>);
    pub fn retain(&mut self, demand: &Demand);   // drop targets not in demand.details and keys not in affinity_targets (called on every demand change seen by the reducer through a `Demand` snapshot in `Tick`)
    pub fn publish(&mut self) -> Option<Arc<DetailsSnapshot>>;
}
```

`Tick` reads `demand.borrow_and_clone()` (the reducer holds a `watch::Receiver<Demand>` too) and calls `retain` so closed windows free their payloads within 1 s.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `apply_tab(Process(A), General, p1)` then `apply_tab(Process(A), Threads, p2)` **When** published twice **Then** the General `Arc` is pointer-equal across both snapshots and `targets[A].threads.version == 1`.
- **Given** a demand without target A **When** `Tick` runs **Then** the next snapshot has no entry for A.
- **Given** `apply_affinity` for keys A and B **When** published **Then** `affinity` has both; after demand lists only A, `retain` drops B.
- **Given** `apply_handle_search` with progress 42 **When** published **Then** `handle_search.progress == 42`; a later `None`-clearing (search ended and cleared by E10) removes it.

title: E09: P2 components (connections, services, startup, inventory, windows) and sys_table calls
description:
## Context
The P2 workers publish whole components: `Connections`, `Services`, `Startup`, `Inventory`, `Windows`, plus `GpuInfo` and `GpuApiVersions` into inventory and device names. For the three system tables the reducer calls `sys_table::build` whenever the component or its `SysTableQuery` changes and stores the rows and `query_generation` in the component. Sources: ADR-003 (component fields: `rows`, `query_generation`, `counts`, `managers`, `details`, `destroy_supported`), ADR-005 (`SetSysTableQuery`), UI-SYS-002, E08-003, E09-015, R-119.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs` (arm bodies) and `mod.rs`:
- `Connections(u)` → new `ConnectionsSnapshot { header, records: u.records.into(), counts: computed (total, tcp, udp, established, listening), destroy_supported: kept, rows, query_generation }`, then `rebuild_sys(Connections)`.
- `ConnectionsDestroySupport(b)` → `destroy_supported = Some(b)`, component replaced.
- `Services(u)` → per-manager merge: the component keeps units of both managers; `managers[u.manager] = u.state`; `details` map replaced by `u.details`; `counts` recomputed; `backend`; then `rebuild_sys(Services)`; also feeds `unit_names` (E09-025).
- `Startup(u)` → `entries`, `counts { total, enabled, disabled }`, `rebuild_sys(Startup)`.
- `Inventory(b)` → header rewritten (version, observed, validity from the box), component replaced. `GpuApiVersions` → merged into the inventory's graphics section fields (`vulkan_version`, `opengl_version` per PCI bus id). `GpuInfo` → `devices.ensure` with the display name and the caps map used by E09-006.
- `Windows(b)` → component replaced with validity `Valid`.
- `Command::SetSysTableQuery(q)` → `sys_queries[q.table] = Some(q)`, `rebuild_sys(q.table)`.
- `rebuild_sys(table)`: `sys_table::build(&SysTableInput { .. }, query)` with `query = sys_queries[table].clone().unwrap_or(SysTableQuery { table, generation: 0, sort: default_sort(table), filter: "", expanded: [], services: None })`; stores `rows` and `query_generation`; marks the component bit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a `Connections` update with 3 TCP (2 established, 1 listening) and 1 UDP record **When** applied **Then** `counts == { total: 4, tcp: 3, udp: 1, established: 2, listening: 1 }`.
- **Given** `SetSysTableQuery { table: Services, generation: 5 }` **When** applied **Then** `services.query_generation == 5` and `SERVICES` was marked even with an empty stub result.
- **Given** `Services` updates from `User` then `System` **When** applied **Then** the component holds both managers' units and `managers` shows both states.
- **Given** `ConnectionsDestroySupport(false)` **When** applied **Then** `destroy_supported == Some(false)` and it survives the next `Connections` update.
- **Given** `GpuApiVersions` with one device **When** applied after `Inventory` **Then** the inventory graphics section shows the Vulkan and OpenGL versions; applied before `Inventory` **Then** they are kept and merged when `Inventory` arrives.

title: E09: Reducer state, loop, publish and the RecordSink hook (reducer/mod.rs)
E09: HistoryView component and the remaining RecordSink calls
description:
## Context
In P3 the history recorder (or the 10-minute rolling window while recording is off) is a `RecordSink` installed through `EngineHooks.record_sink`, and `HistoryQuery` answers arrive as `SourceUpdate::History(Arc<HistoryView>)` for the `Snapshot.history` component (bit `HISTORY`). The reducer already calls the sink (E09-001, E09-005); this bead wires the remaining calls and the component. - `on_device_catalog(&DeviceCatalog)` is called whenever `devices.publish()` returns `Some`.

title: E09: SeriesStore fast tier with gaps and Arc reuse (reducer/series.rs)
description:
## Context
Every graph series is a `SeriesRing` owned by the reducer and published as an immutable `SeriesView`. The fast tier has capacity `ceil(60 s / period) + 2` (602 at 10 Hz, 62 at 1 Hz); a rate change keeps the ring and marks `GAP_BEFORE` on the first sample; unchanged series reuse their `Arc` in `SeriesSet`. Sources: ADR-003 (series, tiers, `SeriesSet`), ADR-008 (stale threshold, `GAP_BEFORE` on resume and rate change, counter rules), PERF-017, PERF-022, R-016, R-051.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/series.rs`:

```rust
pub struct SeriesStore { rings: FxHashMap<SeriesId, Entry>, pending_gap: bool /* set by suspend, applied to every series' next sample */ }
struct Entry { ring: SeriesRing, period_ns: u64, view: Option<Arc<SeriesView>> /* cached until the next append */, gap_next: bool }
impl SeriesStore {
    pub fn fast_capacity(period_ns: u64) -> u32;   // ceil(60e9 / period_ns) + 2
    /// Appends; creates the ring on first use; a period change sets gap_next; `valid == false` appends a gap sample (VALID clear).
    pub fn append(&mut self, id: SeriesId, t_ns: TimeNs, value: f32, period_ns: u64, flags: SampleFlags);
    pub fn append_gap(&mut self, id: SeriesId, t_ns: TimeNs);
    pub fn mark_gap_all(&mut self);                 // next sample of every series gets GAP_BEFORE
    pub fn mark_stale(&mut self, now_ns: TimeNs);   // STALE flag bookkeeping: a series whose last t is older than max(3 × period, 1.5 s)
    pub fn changed(&self) -> SmallVec<[SeriesId; 64]>;
    pub fn publish(&mut self) -> Arc<SeriesSet>;    // sorted by SeriesId; unchanged entries reuse `view`
}
```

Value conversion: callers pass `f32` graph values; counters stay `u64` upstream (ADR-003). `Sample { t_ns, value, flags }` is 16 bytes. The 1 Hz tier is E09-022 (P2) and must not change these signatures.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** period 100 ms **When** `fast_capacity` is called **Then** it returns 602; for 1 s it returns 62.
- **Given** 700 appends at 100 ms **When** `publish` runs **Then** the view holds the newest 602 in chronological order.
- **Given** a series at 100 ms **When** the next append passes period 1 s **Then** that sample carries `GAP_BEFORE` and the ring keeps its older samples.
- **Given** two series and an append to one **When** `publish` runs twice **Then** the untouched series' `Arc<SeriesView>` is pointer-equal across the two sets and the touched one is not.
- **Given** `mark_gap_all` then one append per series **When** published **Then** every series' newest sample has `GAP_BEFORE`.
- **Given** a 1 s series whose last sample is 4 s old **When** `mark_stale(now)` runs **Then** `changed()` names it and its view is rebuilt with `STALE` on the newest sample; a 10 Hz series 1.4 s old is not stale (threshold `max(0.3 s, 1.5 s)`).

- `series.rs::tests::rate_change_marks_gap_before`

- `series.rs::tests::gap_all_then_append`
- `series.rs::tests::stale_threshold`

- Validity: a gap sample has `VALID` clear; stale samples carry `STALE` (the chart draws at 50% alpha then a gap).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: about 1.5 MB for 80 series; `publish` allocates one `Arc<[Sample]>` per changed series only.

title: E09: device catalog with generations (reducer/devices.rs)
description:
## Context
The reducer owns the device catalog: every `DeviceIdentity` gets a stable `DeviceIdx` for the session; a device that disappears keeps its index with `present = false`; one that returns with the same identity keeps the index and gets `generation + 1`; counters are never subtracted across generations. The CPU package and each logical CPU are devices too. Sources: ADR-003 (device identity, catalog), ADR-008 (CPU hotplug, enumeration every 5 s), PERF-005 (hotplug and stable keys), E08-003 `DeviceList`.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/devices.rs`:

```rust
pub struct Catalog { entries: Vec<DeviceEntry>, by_identity: FxHashMap<DeviceIdentity, DeviceIdx>, version: u64, dirty: bool }
impl Catalog {
    pub fn new() -> Self;   // entry 0 = CpuPackage, present = true, display "CPU"
    pub fn idx(&self, id: &DeviceIdentity) -> Option<DeviceIdx>;
    pub fn ensure(&mut self, id: &DeviceIdentity, display_name: &str, parent: Option<&DeviceIdentity>) -> (DeviceIdx, bool /* new or regenerated */);
    /// Apply a full list for `kinds`: new identities are added, missing ones become present=false, returning ones bump generation.
    pub fn apply_list(&mut self, list: &DeviceList) -> Vec<(DeviceIdx, DeviceChange)>;   // Added | Removed | Returned
    pub fn set_cpus(&mut self, online: &CpuSet) -> bool;   // CpuLogical devices; offline → present=false; returns changed
    pub fn generation(&self, idx: DeviceIdx) -> u32;
    pub fn publish(&mut self) -> Option<Arc<DeviceCatalog>>;   // Some when changed since the last publish
}
pub enum DeviceChange { Added, Removed, Returned }
```

`DeviceIdx` is `u16`; more than 65,535 devices is an `InvariantViolation`. Kinds in `DeviceList.kinds` decide which identity variants a list is complete for (`DISKS` → `Disk`, `NETS` → `Net`, `SENSORS` → `Sensor`, `FANS` → `Fan`, `GPUS` → `Gpu`, `BATTERIES` → `Battery`, `CPUS` → `CpuLogical`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a list with disk `sda` **When** applied, then a list without it, then with it again **Then** `sda` keeps its `DeviceIdx`, `present` goes true, false, true and `generation` goes 0, 0, 1.
- **Given** a `DISKS` list **When** applied **Then** `Net` entries are untouched.
- **Given** `set_cpus` with CPUs 0 to 31 then 0 to 30 **When** applied **Then** CPU 31 is `present = false` and the catalog version rose.
- **Given** no change **When** `publish` is called **Then** it returns `None` and the previous `Arc<DeviceCatalog>` stays valid.
- **Given** a partition `sda1` with parent `sda` **When** applied **Then** `entries[sda1].parent == Some(idx(sda))`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/devices.rs`: create

## Tests
- `devices.rs::tests::returning_device_keeps_idx_and_bumps_generation`
- `devices.rs::tests::list_scoped_by_kinds`
- `devices.rs::tests::cpu_hotplug_marks_missing`
- `devices.rs::tests::publish_none_when_unchanged`
- `devices.rs::tests::partition_parent_link`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: index overflow → `InvariantViolation("device index overflow")`.
- Validity: a `present = false` device's series get `Missing` at the next sample (E09-007 uses `generation` and `present`).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: `apply_list` is O(n) with one hash lookup per entry; runs every 5 s.
- Privacy: display names are device model strings; no serials beyond `wwn_or_serial` in the identity (never logged above `debug`).

title: E09: health state and stale marking (reducer/health.rs)
description:
## Context
`Snapshot.health` carries one `SourceHealth` per `SourceId` so the Collector Health chip can show "<Source> data stale", "<Source> unavailable" and "<Source> paused after errors" with the `last_error` tooltip. Workers send `Health` updates (`Running`, `Late`, `Failed`, `Disabled { until }`); the reducer adds `Stale` from timestamps on `Tick`. Sources: ADR-004 (controller health), ADR-008 (stale threshold), ADR-015 (errors appear as `Validity::Failed` plus `last_error`), UI-SHL collector health, E08-003, E08-006.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/health.rs`:

```rust
pub struct HealthState { by_id: FxHashMap<SourceId, Entry>, dirty: bool }
struct Entry { state: SourceState, last_error: Option<Arc<str>>, last_ok_ns: Option<TimeNs>, period_ns: Option<u64>, stale: bool }
impl HealthState {
    pub fn apply(&mut self, id: SourceId, state: SourceState, last_error: Option<Arc<str>>, t_ns: TimeNs);
    pub fn sample_ok(&mut self, id: SourceId, t_ns: TimeNs, period_ns: u64);   // called by apply.rs for every data update
    pub fn tick(&mut self, now_ns: TimeNs) -> bool;   // stale = now - last_ok > max(3 × period, 1.5 s) for Running sources; returns changed
    pub fn is_down(&self, id: SourceId) -> bool;      // Failed or Disabled
    pub fn publish(&mut self) -> Option<Arc<HealthSnapshot>>;
    pub fn all_failed(epoch: u32, reason: &str) -> Arc<HealthSnapshot>;   // used by the session after 3 restarts in 60 s
}
```

`SourceHealth` (tl-model `health.rs`) is filled as: `state`, `last_error`, `last_ok_ns`, `stale`. The display names table ("CPU", "Memory", "Disks", "Network", "GPU", "Sensors", "Processes", "Services", "Startup", "Connections", "Inventory", "KWin") is UI-side; the engine sends only `SourceId`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `apply(Cpu, Running)` and `sample_ok(Cpu, t, 100 ms)` **When** `tick(t + 1.4 s)` **Then** not stale; **When** `tick(t + 1.6 s)` **Then** stale and `tick` returned true.
- **Given** a 1 s source **When** `tick(t + 2.9 s)` **Then** not stale; at `t + 3.1 s` stale.
- **Given** `apply(Cpu, Disabled { until })` **When** `is_down(Cpu)` **Then** true; `apply(Cpu, Running)` clears it and `stale` resets.
- **Given** `all_failed(3, "engine restarted too often")` **When** read **Then** every `SourceId` is `Failed` with that `last_error`.
- **Given** two consecutive `tick`s with no change **When** `publish` is called **Then** the second returns `None`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `last_error` text comes from workers; it is shown in a tooltip, so keep it one line.
- Validity: a down source's component gets `Validity::Failed` in its header (E09-007).

title: E09: process cache with linger, NEW and EXITED (reducer/processes.rs)
description:
## Context
The reducer keeps the process metadata cache: live records plus at most 256 exited ones kept for the linger time (`2 × processes.interval_ms` clamped to 1..=3 s), sets `NEW` and `EXITED`, keeps records sorted by `ProcessKey`, and builds `ProcessSnapshot` with `coverage`. It also feeds `RecordSink::on_process_sweep`. Sources: ADR-004 (bounded reducer state, linger), ADR-003 (`ProcFlags`, `ProcessSnapshot`, `Coverage`), ADR-008 (coverage of PSS), PROC-043, R-041, ADR-012 (hook), E08-003 `ProcessSweep`.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/processes.rs`:

```rust
pub const MAX_EXITED: usize = 256;
pub fn linger_ns(interval_ms: u32) -> u64;   // clamp(2 × interval_ms, 1000, 3000) × 1e6

pub struct ProcessState {
    live: FxHashMap<ProcessKey, Live>,           // Live { record: ProcessRecord, first_seen_ns }
    exited: VecDeque<(ProcessKey, TimeNs /* exit seen */, ProcessRecord)>,
    app_stats: Vec<CgroupStats>, unit_stats: Vec<CgroupStats>,
    system_threads: u32, file_nr: Option<u64>, online_cpus: u16,
    last_sweep_ns: TimeNs, dirty: bool,
}
impl ProcessState {
    /// Diff the sweep against `live`: new keys get NEW (first_seen = observed_end); missing keys move to `exited` with EXITED; cap 256 (drop oldest).
    pub fn apply_sweep(&mut self, sweep: ProcessSweep, now_ns: TimeNs, interval_ms: u32, sink: Option<&mut dyn RecordSink>);
    /// Called on Tick: clears NEW after linger, drops exited after linger; returns changed.
    pub fn expire(&mut self, now_ns: TimeNs, interval_ms: u32) -> bool;
    pub fn flags(&self, key: &ProcessKey) -> Option<ProcFlags>;
    pub fn live_keys(&self) -> &FxHashMap<ProcessKey, ProcFlags>;          // for admission (E11)
    pub fn exited_within_linger(&self) -> FxHashSet<ProcessKey>;
    pub fn records_sorted(&self) -> Vec<ProcessRecord>;                    // live plus exited, by ProcessKey
    pub fn publish(&mut self, coverage: Coverage, observed: (TimeNs, TimeNs)) -> Option<Arc<ProcessSnapshot>>;
}
```

`apply_sweep` keeps the sweep's record for a key seen before (counters already rate-converted by `tl-collect`), copies the flags `KERNEL_THREAD`, `OTHER_USER`, `IS_SELF`, `PROTECTED` from the sweep, and owns `NEW` and `EXITED` itself. An exited record keeps its last values; the table shows it greyed (UI). `on_process_sweep(t_ns = observed_end, &Arc<[ProcessRecord]>)` is called once per sweep when a sink is installed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** sweep 1 with keys A, B **When** applied at t0 **Then** both have `NEW`; **When** `expire(t0 + linger + 1 ms)` **Then** neither has `NEW`.
- **Given** sweep 2 without B at t1 **When** applied **Then** B is in `exited` with `EXITED`, `records_sorted` still contains B, and `exited_within_linger` contains B; after `expire(t1 + linger + 1 ms)` B is gone.
- **Given** 300 processes exit in one sweep **When** applied **Then** `exited.len() == 256` and the 44 oldest by exit time were dropped.
- **Given** `interval_ms = 250` **When** `linger_ns` is called **Then** 1,000,000,000; for 1000 → 2,000,000,000; for 5000 → 3,000,000,000.
- **Given** a key that exited and a new process reuses its PID with a different `start_ticks` **When** the next sweep arrives **Then** both records exist (different keys) and only the new one has `NEW`.
- **Given** a sweep identical to the previous one **When** `publish` is called **Then** it still returns `Some` (values are the same but the observation window moved; `header.version` rises).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/processes.rs`: create

## Tests
- `processes.rs::tests::new_flag_lifecycle`
- `processes.rs::tests::exited_lingers_then_drops`
- `processes.rs::tests::exited_cap_256`
- `processes.rs::tests::linger_clamp`
- `processes.rs::tests::pid_reuse_is_a_new_key`
- `processes.rs::tests::sink_called_once_per_sweep`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: records carry `FieldValidity` from the sweep unchanged; the reducer never turns a missing value into zero.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the diff is O(n) with hash lookups; `records_sorted` allocates one `Vec` per sweep (about 2,000 × 160 B).
- Privacy: never log `ProcessMeta` text; debug logs carry counts only.

title: E09: GPU pid mapping and PSS coverage in process records
description:
## Context
Two workers enrich process records after the sweep: the GPU probe reports per-pid samples that the reducer maps to `ProcessKey` through the current table (a pid not in the table is dropped; utilization is never divided among processes), and the `ProcessDetail` worker reports PSS and USS for `detail_keys` only. `ProcessSnapshot.coverage` tells the UI which keys have PSS so others show `WarmingUp`. Sources: ADR-007 (pid mapping), ADR-008 (PSS coverage, "Only measured for visible rows"), PROC-033, PROC-030 (`pss`, `uss` columns), E08-003 (`GpuSample.processes`, `DetailsUpdate::Pss`).

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/processes.rs`:

```rust
impl ProcessState {
    /// pid → key through `live`; sums over devices per pid; sets gpu_util_pct = max over devices of max(sm, enc, dec), gpu_mem_bytes = Σ mem_used; validity Valid, or Unsupported when the device has `supports_process_util == false`.
    pub fn apply_gpu_processes(&mut self, samples: &[GpuProcessSample], device_caps: &FxHashMap<[u8; 16], bool>) -> u32 /* matched */;
    /// For each entry: set pss_bytes, uss_bytes, swap_bytes and the Pss/Uss validity; keys not in `live` are ignored; records the key in `coverage.pss`.
    pub fn apply_pss(&mut self, entries: &[PssEntry]);
    pub fn coverage(&self) -> Coverage;   // pss keys (sorted), gpu_process: bool (any GPU sample this interval)
    pub fn clear_pss_outside(&mut self, keep: &[ProcessKey]);   // when detail_keys shrink, PSS of dropped keys becomes WarmingUp
}
```

A process with GPU support but no sample this interval keeps `gpu_util_pct = 0` with validity `Valid` only when some device reported `supports_process_util == true` (PROC-033: "0%" only then; otherwise `Unsupported`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** two GPU samples for pid 100 on two devices (sm 30 and 60, mem 1 GiB and 2 GiB) and pid 100 live **When** applied **Then** `gpu_util_pct == 60`, `gpu_mem_bytes == 3 GiB`, validity `Valid`, return value 1.
- **Given** a sample for pid 999 not live **When** applied **Then** it is dropped and no record changes.
- **Given** `device_caps` all false **When** applied with no samples **Then** every live record's GPU validity is `Unsupported`.
- **Given** `apply_pss` for key A only **When** `coverage()` is read **Then** `pss` contains A and not B, and B's Pss validity is `WarmingUp`.
- **Given** `clear_pss_outside(&[B])` after A had PSS **When** read **Then** A's Pss validity is back to `WarmingUp` and `coverage.pss` is empty.

title: E09: apply.rs dispatch for every EngineMsg and Command
description:
## Context
`apply.rs` is the one `match` over `EngineMsg`: every `SourceUpdate` variant and every `Command` variant has an arm from the start (owner only, up front). At this anchor the P0 arms do the work (health, CPU and system samples into series and devices, process sweeps, table query, reset baselines, control forwarding); later E09 beads replace the bodies of the P1 to P3 arms, which until then only log at `debug`. Sources: ADR-004 (reducer owns everything; `EngineMsg`), ADR-005 (`Command` list, demand and settings paths), ADR-008 (suspend, reset baselines, series period), E08-003, E08-004 (`WorkerControl`), R-119, R-134.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs`:

```rust
impl Reducer {
    pub fn apply(&mut self, cx: &Cx, msg: EngineMsg, settings: &EngineSettings);
    fn apply_source(&mut self, cx: &Cx, up: SourceUpdate, settings: &EngineSettings);
    fn apply_command(&mut self, cx: &Cx, cmd: Command);
    fn forward(&mut self, target: SourceId, command: WorkerCommand);   // appends a QueuedCommand (seq += 1, keep newest 64) and sends the watch
    fn bump_reset_generation(&mut self);
}
```

Arm table (P0 bodies):
- `Health { id, state, last_error, t_ns }` → `health.apply`; `Disabled`/`Failed` also sets the component header validity of that source's component to `Failed`.
- `Cpu(s)` → series `CPU_TOTAL`, `CPU_KERNEL`, `CPU_FREQ`, `CPU_TEMP` on the `CpuPackage` device and `CPU_TOTAL`, `CPU_KERNEL`, `CPU_FREQ` per `CpuLogical` (period from the sample spacing or `settings`; a `WarmingUp` sample appends a gap); `topology: Some` → `devices.set_cpus` and `system.cpu_topology`; `irq_pct` stored for the Interrupts row (E09-023); `system` component replaced; `health.sample_ok`.
- `Memory(s)` → `MEM_USED`, `MEM_COMMIT`, `SWAP_USED`, `MEM_CACHED` on the `Memory` device; zram stats stored (E09-023); `system` replaced.
- `Disks(s)`, `Nets(s)`, `Sensors(s)` → `devices.ensure` per identity, then `DISK_ACTIVE`, `DISK_READ`, `DISK_WRITE`, `DISK_LATENCY`; `NET_RX`, `NET_TX`; `FAN_RPM`, `SENSOR_TEMP`, `BATTERY_PCT` per device; a device with `present == false` gets `Missing` (gap). `system` totals replaced.
- `Devices(list)` → `devices.apply_list`; `Returned` devices get `mark_gap` on their series.
- `Gpu(s)` → `GPU_UTIL`, `GPU_MEM`, `GPU_ENC`, `GPU_DEC`, `GPU_TEMP`, `GPU_POWER`, `GPU_CLOCK` per GPU device; `processes: Some` → `processes.apply_gpu_processes` (E09-006, P1 arm). `GpuInfo` → display names and caps; `GpuApiVersions` → inventory fields (E09-027).
- `Processes(sweep)` → `processes.apply_sweep` with the sink, then `table::rebuild` (E09-009..) with `self.query` and `settings`; marks `PROCESSES` and `TABLE`.
- `Details(..)` → E09-006 (`Pss`) and E09-026 (`Tab`, `Affinity`, `HandleSearch`).
- `Connections`, `ConnectionsDestroySupport`, `Services`, `Startup`, `Inventory`, `Windows` → E09-027. `History` → E09-028.
- `Sleep { entering }`, `ResumeDetected` → `suspend` (E09-008; at P0 the arm records the flag and calls `series.mark_gap_all()` on resume plus `bump_reset_generation()`).
- `Command::SetTableQuery(q)` → store, rebuild the table, mark `TABLE` (even when rows are equal, `query_generation` must echo). `SetSysTableQuery(q)` → store in `sys_queries[table]` and rebuild that table (E09-027).
- `Command::Action(req)` → `action_gate.submit(..)` with `AdmissionView`; no gate → one `ActionEvent { id, target: None, state: Rejected(Unsupported) }` through `events_tx.try_send`.
- `RefreshNow(id)` → `forward(id, RefreshNow)`; `ResetBaselines` → `bump_reset_generation` and `series.mark_gap_all`; `ReprobeSource(id)` → `forward(id, Reprobe)`; `KWin(c)` → `forward(KWin, KWin(c))`; `DetailRefresh`, `ComputeHashes`, `VerifyPackage`, `StringScan`, `CancelStringScan`, `HandleSearch`, `CancelHandleSearch` → `forward(ProcessDetail, ..)`; `HistoryQuery`, `HistoryDelete` → `forward(HistoryRecorder, ..)`; `SetupStatus`, `RunSetup` → forwarded to the helper session's `SourceId` (E29 names it; until then `debug` log).
- `ActionFinished { id }` → `action_gate.finished(id)` → `forward(source, RefreshNow)` when `Some`.
- `Tick` → `health.tick`, `series.mark_stale`, `processes.expire`; marks `HEALTH`, `SERIES`, `PROCESSES` and `TABLE` when anything changed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `Cpu` samples at 100 ms with `totals.cpu_pct = 50` **When** applied **Then** `CPU_TOTAL` on `CpuPackage` has one new sample per update with value 50 and the `SeriesSet` version rose once per update.
- **Given** a `Disks` sample for an identity not in the catalog **When** applied **Then** the device is added and its `DISK_READ` series exists.
- **Given** `Command::SetTableQuery` with `generation = 7` and unchanged rows **When** applied **Then** the published `table.query_generation == 7` and `TABLE` was marked.
- **Given** `Command::RefreshNow(SourceId::Startup)` **When** applied **Then** the control watch holds a `QueuedCommand { target: Startup, command: RefreshNow }` with `seq` one higher than before.
- **Given** 70 forwarded commands **When** read **Then** the queue holds the newest 64 in ascending `seq`.
- **Given** `Command::Action` with no gate **When** applied **Then** one `Rejected(Unsupported)` event with `target: None` is on `events_tx`.
- **Given** `ResumeDetected` **When** applied **Then** `reset_generation` rose by 1 and the next sample of every series carries `GAP_BEFORE`.
- **Given** a message of every `SourceUpdate` variant and every `Command` variant **When** applied at this anchor **Then** nothing panics (P1 to P3 arms log and return).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_reducer.rs`: add the cases

## Tests
- `lab_reducer.rs::cpu_update_appends_series`
- `lab_reducer.rs::unknown_disk_identity_is_added`
- `lab_reducer.rs::set_table_query_echoes_generation`
- `lab_reducer.rs::refresh_now_is_forwarded`
- `lab_reducer.rs::forward_queue_keeps_newest_64`
- `lab_reducer.rs::action_without_gate_is_rejected_unsupported`
- `lab_reducer.rs::resume_bumps_reset_and_gaps`
- `lab_reducer.rs::every_variant_applies_without_panic`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: an unknown `DeviceIdx` or a series append on a missing device is an `InvariantViolation`.
- Validity: a sample whose validity is not `Valid` becomes a gap sample; `Stale` is added on `Tick`.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no allocation per sample beyond the ring append; the table rebuild is the expensive step and runs only on sweep or query change.
- Privacy: forwarded `StringScan` and `HandleSearch` patterns are never logged.

## Notes
Depends on E09-001 to E09-005. The period passed to `series.append` is `settings.interval_ms` for process-derived series and the spacing of the last two samples for system series (first sample uses the worker's nominal period: 100 ms when `cpu_fast`, else 1 s). Large-file rule: commit before building. Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: Startup Apps: delete confirmation window and delete flow
description:
## Context
"Delete entry…" on the Startup Apps tab opens a modal confirmation window and, on "Delete", sends `ActionKind::StartupDelete`. Only entries the user owns can be deleted (user XDG entries, user systemd units not owned by a package, Plasma scripts). Sources: UI-SYS-047, UI-SYS-044, UI-SYS-007, SYS-024, APP-045, UI-FND-021 (`TlDialog::confirm`, focus on Cancel for destructive actions), ADR-005, R-119.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/windows/confirm_startup_delete.rs`:
- `pub fn open_startup_delete(parent: WindowHandle<..>, entries: SmallVec<[StartupEntryView; 4]>, skipped: usize, on_delete: impl Fn(&mut Window, &mut App) + 'static, cx: &mut App) -> WindowHandle<..>` where `StartupEntryView { name: SharedString, source_path: SharedString, kind: StartupKind }` holds only the deletable entries.
- `TlDialog::confirm` window, modal to the main window, title "tasklens Delete Startup Entry", width 440, height fits content. Icon `triangle-alert` 20 px in `status.warning`.
- One entry: heading "Delete startup entry" (`t_md` semibold); text "Permanently remove this startup entry?" (`t_base`); type line (`t_base` `text_secondary`): user XDG entry "The autostart file will be deleted. The app stays installed."; user systemd unit "The unit will be disabled and its unit file deleted."; Plasma pre-startup or logout script "The script file will be deleted."; then the entry name (`t_base` medium); then the source path (`t_sm` `text_secondary`, selectable).
- Several entries: heading "Delete startup entries"; text "Permanently remove these <n> startup entries?"; then up to 5 names (`t_base` medium), then "and <m> more" when there are more than 5; when `skipped > 0` a line "<skipped> entries cannot be deleted and are skipped." (`t_base` `text_secondary`). No type line and no paths in this form.
- Footer: "Cancel" (`TlButton::Secondary`) then "Delete" (`TlButton::Danger`). Focus starts on "Cancel". Enter triggers the focused button; Esc cancels.
- While deleting: both buttons disabled, "Delete" shows a 14 px `TlSpinner` (static under reduced motion). The window closes when the request's final event arrives.

`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/startup/flows.rs`: `StartupDelete` handler:
- Targets from `menu_targets` or the selection; keep those with `can_delete`; `skipped` = the rest. No deletable target: Warning toast "This startup entry cannot be deleted" (E28-012 rule), no window.
- Opens the dialog; on "Delete" submits `SysActions::submit(ActionKind::StartupDelete, ActionKindTag::StartupDelete, targets, texts)` with: pending none (open item B8-E28-10), done_one "Startup entry deleted.", done_many "{ $n } startup entries deleted", partial_many "{ $ok } of { $n } startup entries deleted. { $failed } failed.", failed_prefix "Failed to delete startup entry", unknown "Outcome unknown", busy "A startup action is already in progress.", no failed button, progress_cap true. Result toasts show in the main window.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** one user XDG entry "Discord" at "~/.config/autostart/discord.desktop" **When** Delete entry… is chosen **Then** a window titled "tasklens Delete Startup Entry" shows the heading, text, "The autostart file will be deleted. The app stays installed.", "Discord" and the path, and focus is on "Cancel".
- **Given** the dialog **When** Enter is pressed without moving focus **Then** the dialog closes and no request is sent.
- **Given** the dialog **When** Tab then Enter **Then** a `StartupDelete` request is sent, both buttons are disabled and "Delete" shows the spinner; on `Succeeded` the window closes and "Startup entry deleted." shows in the main window.
- **Given** a user systemd unit **When** the dialog opens **Then** the type line is "The unit will be disabled and its unit file deleted.".
- **Given** 7 entries selected, 2 of them system entries **When** Delete entry… is chosen **Then** the heading is "Delete startup entries", the text "Permanently remove these 5 startup entries?", five names, no "and … more" line, and "2 entries cannot be deleted and are skipped.".
- **Given** 8 deletable entries **When** the dialog opens **Then** five names and "and 3 more" are listed.
- **Given** Esc in the dialog **When** pressed **Then** it closes and nothing is sent.

## Files

title: Startup Apps: copy commands and Open file location
description:
## Context
Copy commands and "Open file location" for the Startup Apps tab: the "Copy row" text block, "Copy rows as table", "Copy" (cell), "Copy command", and showing the entry's source file in the file manager. The shared mechanics are E27's `sys_copy.rs`; this bead supplies the startup source and the two startup-only commands. Sources: UI-SYS-048, UI-SYS-006, UI-SYS-044, SYS-025, R-012, R-134 (`ActionKind::ShowInFileManager`), APP-044, ADR-015 (exports).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/startup/copy.rs` (new; `mod copy;` in `mod.rs`):
- `impl SysCopySource for StartupPage` with `RowId = StartupRef`:
  - `copy_rows`: selected refs in view order.
  - `write_block`, exactly these eight lines (no trailing newline):
    ```
    Name: <name>
    Publisher: <publisher>
    Status: <status label>
    Startup impact: <impact word>
    Type: <type words>
    Location: <full directory path>
    Command: <command>
    Resolved path: <absolute binary path, or "Not found">
    ```
    Location prints the full path (no `~`), so the copy works in a shell. Empty publisher prints "Publisher: " with nothing after the space.
  - `visible_columns` and `write_cell`: the cell text as shown (Location with `~`), validity glyph cells empty.
  - `copy_texts`: `row_ok` "Copied to clipboard", `row_failed` "Failed to copy to clipboard", `nothing_selected` "Select a startup row first.".
- Handlers on `StartupPage`: `CopyCell { col }` → `copy_cell` with the cell captured at menu open; `CopyDetails` (Ctrl+C) → `copy_row`; `CopyRowsAsTable` (Ctrl+Shift+C) → `copy_rows_as_table`.
- `StartupCopyCommand` (one target): writes the Command value to the clipboard; Success toast "Startup command copied.".
- `StartupOpenFileLocation` (one target): when the entry's source file no longer exists (entry `file_exists == false`), Warning toast "Startup file location unavailable." and nothing is sent. Otherwise submit `ActionRequest { kind: ActionKind::ShowInFileManager { path: source_path, properties: false }, targets: [] }` through `ActionTracker` (E16-A3); Info toast "Opening file location" with `ToastKey(id.0)`; on `Failed` or `OutcomeUnknown` the same key becomes the Error toast "Failed to open file location".

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the entry fixture "Discord" **When** `CopyDetails` runs **Then** the clipboard equals the golden `tests/golden/startup_copy_block.txt` and the toast is "Copied to clipboard".
- **Given** two selected entries **When** `CopyDetails` runs **Then** the two blocks are joined by one blank line in view order.
- **Given** nothing selected **When** Ctrl+C is pressed **Then** the toast "Select a startup row first." shows and the clipboard is unchanged.
- **Given** a location under $HOME **When** copied as a block **Then** the Location line has the full path; **When** copied as a table **Then** the Location cell has `~`.
- **Given** one entry **When** "Copy command" runs **Then** the clipboard holds its command and the toast is "Startup command copied.".
- **Given** an entry whose source file is gone **When** "Open file location" runs **Then** the toast "Startup file location unavailable." shows and no request is sent.
- **Given** an existing file **When** "Open file location" runs and the engine answers `Failed` **Then** the toast changes in place from "Opening file location" to "Failed to open file location".

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/startup/copy.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/startup/mod.rs`: change (`mod copy;`, handler registration)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_startup.rs`: add tests; `crates/tl-ui/tests/golden/startup_copy_block.txt`: create
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append `startup-copy-*`, `startup-open-location-*` keys

## Tests

- `ui_startup::startup_copy_multi_blank_line`.
- `ui_startup::startup_copy_nothing_selected_toast`.
- `ui_startup::startup_copy_location_full_vs_tilde`.
- `ui_startup::startup_copy_command_toast`.
- `ui_startup::open_location_missing_file_toast`.
- `ui_startup::open_location_failure_replaces_toast`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: "Failed to copy to clipboard", "Startup file location unavailable.", "Failed to open file location".
- Validity: glyph cells copy as empty fields in TSV.
- Accessibility: Ctrl+C and Ctrl+Shift+C work without the pointer; "Copy" (cell) needs the pointer.
- Performance: one `String` per command, `capacity = rows × 256`.
- Privacy: commands are copied only on the user's explicit command (ADR-015); nothing is logged.

title: Startup Apps: Startup Properties window
description:
## Context
The read-only Startup Properties window, opened by Properties (Enter, Alt+Enter, Ctrl+I, double-click) on a startup row. One window per entry, at most 10, each line with its own copy button. Sources: UI-SYS-050, SYS-026, APP-045, UI-FND-021 (`TlSecondaryWindow`, `WindowRegistry`, `WindowKey::StartupProperties(StartupRef)`), UI-FND-025, docs/ui/INDEX.md window keys.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/windows/startup_properties.rs`:
- `pub fn open_startup_properties(r: StartupRef, hub: &Entity<SnapshotHub>, cx: &mut App)`: if `WindowRegistry` holds `WindowKey::StartupProperties(r)`, activate that window; else if 10 startup properties windows are open, push the Warning toast "Too many startup properties windows are already open" in the main window and open nothing; else open a `TlSecondaryWindow` (Properties kind, not modal) titled "Startup properties: <Name>", default size 620 × 520, minimum 480 × 360.
- `StartupPropertiesView` (Entity): subscribes to `SnapshotHub`; on STARTUP changes it looks up its entry by `StartupRef` and notifies only when the entry `Arc` differs by pointer. Content: `TlKeyValueGrid` inline layout in a vertical scroll region, padding `sp6`, `.label_width(220)`; each line ends with a copy button (`TlButton::Icon`, icon `copy` 14 px in a 20 × 20 hit area at the line's right end, `text_secondary` at 60% alpha, full alpha on row hover or focus; accessible name "Copy <label>"). Footer 48 px high with one `TlButton::Secondary` "Close".
- Lines, in order (labels exact):

  | Label | Value |
  |---|---|
  | "Name" | name |
  | "Publisher" | publisher, or "Not reported" (Unsupported-no-value word) |
  | "Status / Enabled / State code" | "<status label> / <Yes or No> / <ActiveState (SubState)>", for example "Enabled / Yes / active (running)"; State code "-" when there is no generated unit |
  | "Startup impact" | "<High, Medium or Low> (<activation_ms> ms)", for example "Low (212 ms)"; "None" and "Not measured" without ms |
  | "Type / Source / Scope" | "<type words> / <source word> / <user or system>", for example "Autostart (user) / XDG autostart / user"; source words "XDG autostart", "systemd user unit", "Plasma pre-startup script", "Plasma logout script" |
  | "Location" | directory (full path) |
  | "Source path" | file path |
  | "Resolved path" | binary found on PATH, or "Not found" |
  | "Command" | command; wraps to several lines |
  | "Can run / Can toggle / Can delete / File exists" | four "Yes"/"No" words joined with " / ", for example "Yes / Yes / No / Yes" |
  | "OnlyShowIn" | list joined with ", "; line shown only when set |
  | "NotShowIn" | list; only when set |
  | "TryExec" | value; only when set |
