title: Startup Apps: Enable, Disable and Run now flows
description:
## Context
The Enable, Disable and Run now flows of the Startup Apps tab: target selection, the action requests through E27's `SysActions`, the result toasts (with the 4-or-more summary rule) and the "Updating…" status while an enable or disable is pending. Sources: UI-SYS-045, UI-SYS-046, UI-SYS-007, UI-SYS-042 (pending state), SYS-022, SYS-023, ADR-005 (`ActionKind::StartupEnable`, `StartupDisable`, `StartupRunNow`, `ActionTarget::Startup`), ADR-006 (2 s budget), R-114, R-119.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/startup/flows.rs` (new; `mod flows;` in `mod.rs`):
- Handlers on `StartupPage` for `StartupEnable`, `StartupDisable`, `StartupRunNow`, using the targets from `menu_targets` or the selection (E28-012).
- Enable: targets = entries whose status is not Enabled and whose `can_toggle` is true; Disable: entries whose status is Enabled and `can_toggle` is true. Targets whose state would not change are skipped. An empty target list does nothing (no request, no toast).
- Run now: targets = entries with `can_run`, whatever the status.
- Each submits through `SysActions::submit(kind, tag, targets, texts, ..)` with `targets` as `ActionTarget::Startup(StartupRef)` and these exact `ActionTexts` (Fluent args `$n`, `$ok`, `$failed`):

  | Field | Enable | Disable | Run now |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | kind, tag | `StartupEnable` | `StartupDisable` | `StartupRunNow` |
  | pending_one, pending_many | none (no pending toast; see Notes) | none | none |
  | done_one | "Startup entry enabled." | "Startup entry disabled." | "Startup entry launched." |
  | done_many | "{ $n } startup entries enabled" | "{ $n } startup entries disabled" | "{ $n } startup entries launched" |
  | partial_many | "{ $ok } of { $n } startup entries enabled. { $failed } failed." | "{ $ok } of { $n } startup entries disabled. { $failed } failed." | "{ $ok } of { $n } startup entries launched. { $failed } failed." |
  | failed_prefix | "Failed to update startup entry" | "Failed to update startup entry" | "Failed to launch startup entry" |
  | unknown | "Outcome unknown" | "Outcome unknown" | "Outcome unknown" |
  | busy | "A startup action is already in progress." | same | same |
  | failed_button | none | none | none |
  | progress_cap | true | true | true |

  Failure text is `failure_text(failed_prefix, err)`, for example "Failed to update startup entry: not authorized". Run now when the entry is already running as its autostart unit shows the Info toast "Already running" instead of the success text (how the engine reports this: open item B8-E28-9).
- No confirmation for any of the three. Changes apply at next login; running programs are not stopped; no toast text says so.
- Pending display: `StartupPage` subscribes to `SysActionsEvent::PendingChanged` and notifies; `StartupDelegate` draws the Status cell of a target whose `pending_tag` is `StartupEnable` or `StartupDisable` as a filled `status.info` dot with the label "Updating…" until the final event. Run now changes no row.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** one Disabled entry **When** `StartupEnable` runs and the fake engine answers `Succeeded` **Then** one request with kind `StartupEnable` and one target was sent, the Status cell showed "Updating…" until the event, and the toast "Startup entry enabled." shows.
- **Given** two Disabled and one Enabled entries selected **When** `StartupDisable` runs **Then** the request has exactly one target (the Enabled one).
- **Given** only already-disabled entries selected **When** `StartupDisable` runs **Then** no request is sent and no toast shows.
- **Given** 4 Disabled entries **When** Enable runs and 3 succeed, 1 fails **Then** one summary toast "3 of 4 startup entries enabled. 1 failed." with a "Details" button shows.
- **Given** a failure `ActionError::PermissionDenied` **When** the event arrives **Then** the Error toast reads "Failed to update startup entry: not authorized" (E27 `failure_text`).
- **Given** a Masked entry **When** Run now runs **Then** a `StartupRunNow` request is sent for it (status does not matter).
- **Given** the engine reports the already-running case **When** Run now finishes **Then** the Info toast "Already running" shows.
- **Given** an Enable pending on entry A **When** Enable is chosen again for A **Then** the Warning toast "A startup action is already in progress." shows and no request is sent.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/startup/flows.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/startup/delegate.rs`: change ("Updating…" status cell)
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/startup/mod.rs`: change (`mod flows;`, handler registration, `PendingChanged` subscription)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_startup.rs`: add tests; `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append `startup-action-*` keys

## Tests
- `ui_startup::startup_enable_toast`.
- `ui_startup::startup_disable_skips_already_disabled`.
- `ui_startup::startup_toggle_empty_is_noop`.
- `ui_startup::startup_enable_summary_at_4`.
- `ui_startup::startup_updating_status_while_pending`.
- `ui_startup::run_now_any_status`.
- `ui_startup::run_now_already_running_toast`.
- `ui_startup::startup_busy_toast`.
- `ui_startup::startup_enable_targets_only_captured_refs` (security regression).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: "Failed to update startup entry: <error>", "Failed to launch startup entry: <error>", "Outcome unknown", "A startup action is already in progress.".
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: every flow is reachable from the menu with the keyboard (Shift+F10).
- Performance: one request per command; pending changes repaint only the affected rows.
- Privacy: action logs (engine) record kind and target only; the UI logs nothing.

## Notes
- `SysActions` (E27-A1) always pushes a Progress toast today; these flows need none (UI-SYS-045, UI-SYS-046). Open item B8-E28-10 asks the leader to let an empty `pending_one` skip the Progress toast; implement after that is settled.
- The "busy" and "unknown" texts and the Run now and Disable summary strings follow the UI-SYS-007 pattern and are listed in open item B8-E28-10 for confirmation.
- Security: the request carries only `StartupRef` targets; the engine validates them (ADR-006). Regression test `startup_enable_targets_only_captured_refs` asserts no other ref is sent.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`. title: E03 tl-model: every data contract
description: Epic E03 (model). Phases: P1 (P0 anchors). Estimated beads: 30. Scope, sources and file ownership: docs/plan/00-epics.md sections 1 and 2, key E03.

title: E03-A1 Core types compile with size tests
description:
## Context
Capstone of the first half of tl-model: it proves the core types compile and locks the numbers that history files depend on. ADR-003 verification asks for `size_of::<Sample>() == 16`, `size_of::<ProcessKey>() == 24`, `size_of::<ProcessRecord>() <= 160`, and a test that serializes every `MetricId` constant and compares against a checked-in list so changing a number fails the test. ADR-012 constraint 2 extends the freeze to `ColumnId` numbers and strings. This anchor is P0: the phase-0 spike (E01) and every later crate build on these types. Sources: ADR-003 "Verification", ADR-012 "Constraints on P1 code", R-007, 00-epics anchor row E03-A1.

## Deliverable
1. `crates/tl-model/tests/sizes.rs`:
   - `sample_is_16_bytes`: `assert_eq!(size_of::<tl_model::series::Sample>(), 16)`.
   - `process_key_is_24_bytes`: `assert_eq!(size_of::<tl_model::ids::ProcessKey>(), 24)`.
   - `process_record_at_most_160`: `assert!(size_of::<tl_model::process::ProcessRecord>() <= 160)`, with the actual size in the failure message.
   - `field_validity_is_13_bytes`: `assert_eq!(size_of::<tl_model::validity::FieldValidity>(), 13)`.
   - `validity_is_1_byte`: `assert_eq!(size_of::<tl_model::validity::Validity>(), 1)`.
   - `cpuset_is_128_bytes`: `assert_eq!(size_of::<tl_model::system::CpuSet>(), 128)`.
2. `crates/tl-model/tests/frozen/metric_ids.txt`: 24 lines `NAME=number`, in the order of `MetricId::ALL`:
   `CPU_TOTAL=1`, `CPU_KERNEL=2`, `CPU_FREQ=3`, `CPU_TEMP=4`, `MEM_USED=10`, `MEM_COMMIT=11`, `SWAP_USED=12`, `MEM_CACHED=13`, `DISK_ACTIVE=20`, `DISK_READ=21`, `DISK_WRITE=22`, `DISK_LATENCY=23`, `NET_RX=30`, `NET_TX=31`, `GPU_UTIL=40`, `GPU_MEM=41`, `GPU_ENC=42`, `GPU_DEC=43`, `GPU_TEMP=44`, `GPU_POWER=45`, `GPU_CLOCK=46`, `FAN_RPM=50`, `SENSOR_TEMP=51`, `BATTERY_PCT=60`.
3. `crates/tl-model/tests/frozen/column_ids.txt`: 121 lines `number string`, generated once from `ColumnId::ALL` (1 `name` to 121 `container`, the list in bead E03-005) and committed.
4. `crates/tl-model/tests/frozen/validity.txt`: 7 lines `Name=number` (`Valid=0` to `Failed=6`) and `crates/tl-model/tests/frozen/process_fields.txt`: 13 lines `Name=index` (`Cpu=0` to `Threads=12`).
5. `crates/tl-model/tests/frozen_ids.rs`:
   - `metric_ids_frozen`: builds `NAME=number` lines from `MetricId::ALL`, serializes each id with `postcard::to_allocvec` and checks the bytes decode back to the same number (the "serializes every constant" part of ADR-003), then compares the text with `include_str!("frozen/metric_ids.txt")` line by line.
   - `column_ids_frozen`: builds `number string` lines from `ColumnId::ALL` and compares with `include_str!("frozen/column_ids.txt")`.
   - `validity_numbers_frozen` and `process_fields_frozen`: same pattern with the two small files.
   - On mismatch every test prints the first differing line and the message "Frozen ids changed. History files and settings depend on these numbers. Add new ids at the end; never renumber."
   - No update mode: the files are edited by hand only when an id is added at the end.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the finished first half of tl-model **When** `cargo test -p tl-model` runs **Then** every test in `sizes.rs`, `frozen_ids.rs`, `units_format.rs` and the unit tests of E03-002 to E03-013 pass.
- **Given** `MetricId::CPU_FREQ` changed from 3 to 5 in a scratch edit **When** `metric_ids_frozen` runs **Then** it fails with the frozen-ids message.
- **Given** a `ColumnId` variant renamed from `"memory"` to `"mem"` in a scratch edit **When** `column_ids_frozen` runs **Then** it fails.
- **Given** a new field added to `ProcessRecord` that pushes it past 160 bytes **When** `process_record_at_most_160` runs **Then** it fails and prints the size.
- **Given** the workspace **When** `cargo clippy -p tl-model --all-targets -- -D warnings` runs **Then** it passes.

- `crates/tl-model/tests/frozen_ids.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-model/tests/frozen/{metric_ids,column_ids,validity,process_fields}.txt`: create

## Tests

## Cross-cutting

- Validity: freezes the `Validity` numbers stored in history.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A

## Notes
- Generate `column_ids.txt` once by a throwaway test print, check it against the E03-005 list by eye, then commit; the test never writes files.
- The scratch edits in the acceptance criteria are checks the implementer runs and reverts; they are not committed.

title: E03-008 process.rs: ProcessMeta, ProcessRecord, flags, groups, coverage
description:
## Context
The per-process record the sweep fills and the table shows. Numeric fields are fixed-size and text lives in a shared `ProcessMeta` behind an `Arc`, so a 10 Hz CPU publish costs no process copying (ADR-003, ADR-012 constraint 3). Each numeric field has its own validity (`FieldValidity`). The default Memory column is RssAnon (D-004, R-005). Groups classify processes into Apps, Background and System (PROC-004). Sources: ADR-003 "Process record and metadata" and "Groups", ADR-008 (coverage, linger time), ADR-009 (`TableRow.group`), D-004, R-005, R-043, PROC-004, PROC-008, PROC-012, PROC-030.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-model/src/process.rs` (uses `ids::{ProcessKey, GroupKey}`, `validity::FieldValidity`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ProcessMeta {
    pub comm: Arc<str>,                // /proc/<pid>/comm, sanitized
    pub name: Arc<str>,                // display name: desktop entry Name, else exe basename, else comm
    pub exe: Option<Arc<str>>,         // readlink /proc/<pid>/exe; None if restricted
    pub cmdline: Option<Arc<str>>,     // bounded to 32 KiB, NULs to spaces, sanitized (ADR-015)
    pub user: Arc<str>,                // user name for uid
    pub cgroup: Option<Arc<str>>,      // cgroup v2 path relative to /sys/fs/cgroup
    pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>,      // from the app scope or desktop entry
    pub icon: Option<Arc<str>>,        // resolved icon file path
    pub description: Option<Arc<str>>, // desktop entry Comment or GenericName
    pub search_lower: Arc<str>,        // lowercase filter text: display name, image name, cmdline, user,
                                       // description, app name, unit name (R-043)
}

#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum ProcState { Running, Sleeping, DiskSleep, Stopped, Zombie, Idle, Other }

impl ProcState {
    /// From /proc/<pid>/stat field 3: b'R' Running, b'S' Sleeping, b'D' DiskSleep,
    /// b'T' and b't' Stopped, b'Z' Zombie, b'I' Idle, any other byte Other.
    pub const fn from_stat_char(c: u8) -> ProcState;
}

bitflags::bitflags! {
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct ProcFlags: u16 {
        const NEW = 1;           // appeared within the linger time: 2 × processes.interval_ms, clamped to 1..=3 s
        const EXITED = 2;        // exited within the linger time; kept for highlight, then removed
        const KERNEL_THREAD = 4;
        const OTHER_USER = 8;
        const IS_SELF = 16;      // tasklens or its probe
        const PROTECTED = 32;    // see ADR-006
    }
}

/// Linger time for NEW and EXITED: 2 × interval, clamped to 1_000..=3_000 ms.
pub const fn linger_ms(processes_interval_ms: u32) -> u32;

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ProcessRecord {
    pub key: ProcessKey,
    pub ppid: u32,
    pub uid: u32,
    pub meta: Arc<ProcessMeta>,
    pub group: GroupKey,
    pub state: ProcState,
    pub flags: ProcFlags,
    pub nice: i8,
    pub threads: u32,
    pub cpu_pct: f32,          // percent of whole machine capacity, 0..=100
    pub rss_anon_bytes: u64,   // RssAnon from /proc/<pid>/status; the default Memory column (D-004)
    pub rss_bytes: u64,        // VmRSS; the "Working set total" column
    pub pss_bytes: u64,        // only for demanded keys (ADR-008)
    pub uss_bytes: u64,
    pub swap_bytes: u64,
    pub io_read_bps: f32,
    pub io_write_bps: f32,
    pub net_rx_bps: f32,       // attributed TCP only (ADR-016)
    pub net_tx_bps: f32,
    pub gpu_util_pct: f32,
    pub gpu_mem_bytes: u64,
    pub validity: FieldValidity,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum GroupKind {
    App { app_id: Arc<str> },   // cgroup app-*.scope or app-*.service under user@<uid>.service/app.slice
    Background,                 // processes of the current uid not in an app scope
    System,                     // other uids, system.slice, init.scope, kernel threads
    Ungrouped,                  // cgroup unreadable
}

/// Aggregated values of one group row. Each member process is counted once (no double
/// counting of descendants, ADR-009). Field meanings match ProcessRecord.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct GroupRow {
    pub key: GroupKey,
    pub kind: GroupKind,
    pub name: Arc<str>,            // display name of the row
    pub icon: Option<Arc<str>>,    // resolved icon file path
    pub members: u32,              // member processes after filtering
    pub cpu_pct: f32,
    pub rss_anon_bytes: u64,       // App rows: cgroup memory.stat `anon` (R-005)
    pub rss_bytes: u64,
    pub pss_bytes: u64,
    pub uss_bytes: u64,
    pub swap_bytes: u64,
    pub io_read_bps: f32,
    pub io_write_bps: f32,
    pub net_rx_bps: f32,
    pub net_tx_bps: f32,
    pub gpu_util_pct: f32,
    pub gpu_mem_bytes: u64,
    pub threads: u32,
    pub validity: FieldValidity,
}

/// Which expensive fields cover which keys (ADR-008). Keys not listed show WarmingUp for PSS and USS.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Coverage {
    pub pss_uss: Arc<[ProcessKey]>, // sorted ascending, so the UI can binary_search
}
impl Coverage {
    pub fn has_pss_uss(&self, key: &ProcessKey) -> bool; // binary search
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** each byte `R S D T t Z I X` **When** `ProcState::from_stat_char` runs **Then** the results are Running, Sleeping, DiskSleep, Stopped, Stopped, Zombie, Idle, Other.
- **Given** `linger_ms(250)`, `linger_ms(1000)`, `linger_ms(2000)` and `linger_ms(10000)` **When** called **Then** they return 1000, 2000, 3000 and 3000.
- **Given** the `ProcFlags` constants **When** their bits are read **Then** they are NEW 1, EXITED 2, KERNEL_THREAD 4, OTHER_USER 8, IS_SELF 16, PROTECTED 32.
- **Given** a `Coverage` with keys sorted **When** `has_pss_uss` asks for a listed and an unlisted key **Then** it returns true and false.
- **Given** a `ProcessRecord` **When** cloned **Then** `Arc::ptr_eq(&a.meta, &b.meta)` is true (metadata is shared, not copied).

## Tests

  - `record_clone_shares_meta`
- `size_of::<ProcessRecord>() <= 160` is in `tests/sizes.rs` (E03-A1). By field sizes the record is 141 bytes before padding, 144 after.

- Errors: N/A

- Accessibility: N/A

- Privacy: `cmdline`, `exe`, `cgroup` and `search_lower` may hold user data. Never derive `Display` for these types and never log `ProcessMeta` at any level (ADR-015 never-logged list); `Debug` is for tests only.

title: E03-009 system.rs: CPU, memory, disk, net, GPU and sensor totals, CpuSet, topology
description:
## Context
Machine-wide live values that the Performance pages, sidebar cards, status chip and Information tab read from `SystemSnapshot` (ADR-003: "SystemSnapshot carries, besides the totals of system.rs, cpu_topology"). Graph history is in series (`series.rs`); these structs hold the current values and the counters the stats grids show. CPU topology feeds the Set Affinity dialog (UI-PWN-021) and the per-core grid marks (PERF-031). Sources: ADR-003 "Per-component fields", ADR-005 (`CpuSet`), ADR-008 (CPU and memory math), PERF-031, PERF-033, PERF-038 to PERF-043, PERF-049, PERF-056, PERF-063 to PERF-068, PERF-076, PERF-077.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-model/src/system.rs` (uses `ids::DeviceIdx`, `validity::Validity`, `time::TimeNs`):

```rust
/// A value with its validity. Never read `value` unless `validity == Valid` or `Stale`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Default)]
pub struct Metric<T: Copy + Default> { pub value: T, pub validity: Validity }
impl<T: Copy + Default> Metric<T> {
    pub fn valid(v: T) -> Self;          // validity Valid
    pub fn with(validity: Validity) -> Self; // value T::default()
}

/// CPU affinity mask, up to 1024 CPUs (ADR-005).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CpuSet(pub [u64; 16]);
impl CpuSet {
    pub const MAX_CPUS: u16 = 1024;
    pub const fn empty() -> CpuSet;
    pub fn insert(&mut self, cpu: u16);   // ignores cpu >= 1024
    pub fn remove(&mut self, cpu: u16);
    pub fn contains(&self, cpu: u16) -> bool;
    pub fn count(&self) -> u32;           // popcount
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool;
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = u16> + '_; // ascending
    pub fn intersection(&self, other: &CpuSet) -> CpuSet;
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum CoreKind { Performance, Efficiency, Standard }

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CoreInfo {
    pub id: u16,                         // core index in the order of (package, core_id)
    pub logical: SmallVec<[u16; 2]>,     // logical CPU ids of this core (SMT siblings)
    pub l3_group: u16,                   // index of the L3 domain (shared_cpu_list of the L3 cache)
    pub kind: CoreKind,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct CpuTopology {
    pub online: CpuSet,
    pub cores: Arc<[CoreInfo]>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
pub struct CpuTotals {
    pub util_pct: Metric<f32>,        // 100 × Δbusy / Δtotal (ADR-008); also series CPU_TOTAL
    pub kernel_pct: Metric<f32>,      // 100 × Δ(system + irq + softirq) / Δtotal; series CPU_KERNEL
    pub iowait_pct: Metric<f32>,      // iowait share, reported in CPU details (ADR-008)
    pub freq_mhz: Metric<u32>,        // mean of cpuinfo_avg_freq over policies (PERF-033, PERF-040)
    pub freq_fastest_mhz: Metric<u32>,// fastest core, for the Speed tooltip (PERF-033)
    pub base_mhz: Metric<u32>,        // base_frequency, else acpi_cppc nominal_freq, else bios_limit
    pub temp_c: Metric<f32>,          // Tctl or Package id 0 (PERF-039)
    pub package_power_w: Metric<f32>, // RAPL intel-rapl:0 (PERF-038, P2)
    pub core_power_w: Metric<f32>,    // RAPL intel-rapl:0:0, for the tooltip (PERF-038, P2)
    pub processes: Metric<u32>,       // numeric /proc entries (PERF-033)
    pub threads: Metric<u32>,         // sum from the sweep, else /proc/stat fallback (PERF-033)
    pub handles: Metric<u64>,         // /proc/sys/fs/file-nr field 1 (PERF-033)
    pub load_avg: Metric<[f32; 3]>,   // /proc/loadavg 1, 5, 15 min
    pub sockets: Metric<u16>,         // distinct physical_package_id
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
pub struct MemoryTotals {             // all bytes, from /proc/meminfo unless noted (PERF-041 to PERF-043)
    pub validity: Validity,           // of the meminfo read as a whole
    pub total: u64, pub available: u64, pub used: u64, // used = MemTotal - MemAvailable (MemFree when Available > Total)
    pub free: u64, pub cached: u64, pub dirty: u64, pub writeback: u64,
    pub committed: u64, pub commit_limit: u64,          // Committed_AS, CommitLimit
    pub slab_reclaimable: u64, pub slab_unreclaimable: u64,
    pub swap_total: u64, pub swap_free: u64,
    pub huge_pages_total: u64, pub huge_pages_free: u64, pub huge_page_size: u64,
    pub zswap: u64, pub zswapped: u64,
    pub zram: Metric<ZramTotals>,     // summed over zram devices; Unsupported when none
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct ZramTotals { pub orig_data: u64, pub compr_data: u64, pub mem_used: u64 } // mm_stat fields 1, 2, 3

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct DiskTotals {               // one per disk device (PERF-049)
    pub device: DeviceIdx,
    pub active_pct: Metric<f32>,
    pub read_bps: Metric<f64>, pub write_bps: Metric<f64>, // bytes per second
    pub response_ms: Metric<f32>,     // Δticks / Δops over reads, writes, discards, flushes
    pub read_total: u64, pub written_total: u64,           // bytes since boot (sectors × 512)
    pub capacity: u64,                // /sys/block/<d>/size × 512
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct NetTotals {                // one per interface (PERF-056)
    pub device: DeviceIdx,
    pub rx_bps: Metric<f64>, pub tx_bps: Metric<f64>,     // bytes per second
    pub rx_total: u64, pub tx_total: u64,                 // bytes since boot
    pub link_speed_mbps: Metric<u32>,                     // sysfs speed; -1 gives Unsupported ("Not reported")
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct GpuTotals {                // one per GPU (PERF-063 to PERF-068)
    pub device: DeviceIdx,
    pub util_pct: Metric<f32>, pub mem_util_pct: Metric<f32>,
    pub mem_used: Metric<u64>, pub mem_total: Metric<u64>,
    pub shared_used: Metric<u64>, pub shared_total: Metric<u64>,
    pub enc_pct: Metric<f32>, pub dec_pct: Metric<f32>,
    pub temp_c: Metric<f32>, pub power_w: Metric<f32>, pub power_limit_w: Metric<f32>,
    pub clock_gfx_mhz: Metric<u32>, pub clock_mem_mhz: Metric<u32>,
    pub fan_pct: Metric<f32>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub enum SensorKind { Temperature, Fan }

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct SensorReading {            // one per hwmon temperature or fan device (PERF-076)
    pub device: DeviceIdx,
    pub kind: SensorKind,
    pub value: Metric<f32>,           // °C for Temperature, RPM for Fan
    pub pwm_pct: Metric<f32>,         // Fan only: pwmN / 255 × 100; Unsupported for Temperature
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** an empty `CpuSet` **When** cpus 0, 63, 64 and 1023 are inserted **Then** `count()` is 4, `contains(64)` is true and `iter()` yields 0, 63, 64, 1023.
- **Given** `insert(1024)` **When** called **Then** the set is unchanged.
- **Given** two sets {0,1,2} and {1,2,3} **When** `intersection` runs **Then** the result is {1,2}.
- **Given** `Metric::<f32>::with(Validity::Restricted)` **When** read **Then** `value == 0.0` and `validity == Restricted`.
- **Given** `Metric::<u64>::default()` **When** read **Then** `validity == WarmingUp` (the `Validity` default).
- **Given** a `CpuTopology::default()` **When** read **Then** `online` is empty and `cores` is empty.

## Files
- `crates/tl-model/src/system.rs`: fill the placeholder

## Tests
- `system.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`:
  - `cpuset_insert_contains_iter`
  - `cpuset_ignores_out_of_range`
  - `cpuset_intersection`
  - `metric_with_validity`
  - `metric_default_warming_up`
  - `proptest cpuset_matches_btreeset`: random inserts and removes of 0..1100 match a `BTreeSet<u16>` model filtered to < 1024.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: every live field is a `Metric` or carries a `validity` field; a missing value is never a bare zero.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: all totals are `Copy` and fixed-size. Per-device lists live in `SystemSnapshot` as `Arc<[DiskTotals]>` and so on (snapshot.rs, E03-A2 half).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- ADR-003 names these types but does not list their fields. The fields above are derived row by row from the PERF entries in Context (each comment names its source). The leader confirms the list (open item in docs/plan/b1-infra.md). Static rows (cache sizes, governor, DIMMs, WWN, Wi-Fi, battery properties) are not totals and are not here; they belong to inventory and device detail payloads.
- `CpuSet` is written once here; `actions.rs` (`ActionKind::SetAffinity(CpuSet)`) and `details.rs` (`AffinityInfo`) use it from this module.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`

title: E03-010 devices.rs: DeviceIdentity, DeviceEntry, DeviceCatalog, NetKind
description:
## Context
Every device (CPU, memory, GPU, disk, network interface, sensor, fan, battery) has an identity and a session index. A device that disappears keeps its index with `present = false`; one that comes back with the same identity gets the same index and `generation + 1`, and counters are never subtracted across generations (ADR-003, PERF-005). The engine reducer (E09) owns the catalog; this bead defines the types. Network interfaces are classified for sidebar visibility (ADR-016 sources table, PERF-054). Sources: ADR-003 "Device identity", ADR-016 (network row), PERF-004, PERF-005, PERF-054, R-052.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-model/src/devices.rs` (uses `ids::DeviceIdx`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum DeviceIdentity {
    CpuPackage,                                   // the whole machine's CPU
    CpuLogical { id: u16 },
    Memory,
    Gpu { uuid: [u8; 16], pci_bus_id: Arc<str> }, // NVML UUID, or DRM PCI slot for non-NVIDIA
    Disk { major: u32, minor: u32, name: Arc<str>, wwn_or_serial: Option<Arc<str>> },
    Net { netns_ino: u64, ifindex: u32, name: Arc<str> },
    Sensor { chip: Arc<str>, label: Arc<str> },   // hwmon name plus label
    Fan { chip: Arc<str>, index: u16 },
    Battery { native_path: Arc<str> },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub enum DeviceKind { Cpu, CpuLogical, Memory, Gpu, Disk, Net, Sensor, Fan, Battery }

impl DeviceIdentity {
    pub fn kind(&self) -> DeviceKind;   // CpuPackage -> Cpu, others by variant name
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct DeviceEntry {
    pub idx: DeviceIdx,
    pub identity: DeviceIdentity,
    pub generation: u32,
    pub display_name: Arc<str>,
    pub present: bool,
    pub parent: Option<DeviceIdx>,  // partitions and device-mapper children point to their disk
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct DeviceCatalog { pub version: u64, pub entries: Arc<[DeviceEntry]> }

impl DeviceCatalog {
    /// entries[idx.0], or None when out of range. Entries are stored in idx order: entries[i].idx == DeviceIdx(i).
    pub fn get(&self, idx: DeviceIdx) -> Option<&DeviceEntry>;
    /// Linear search by identity (the catalog is small: tens of entries).
    pub fn find(&self, identity: &DeviceIdentity) -> Option<&DeviceEntry>;
    /// Present entries of one kind, in idx order.
    pub fn present_of(&self, kind: DeviceKind) -> impl Iterator<Item = &DeviceEntry> + '_;
}

/// Network interface class for sidebar visibility (ADR-016, PERF-054).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum NetKind { Wired, Wireless, VpnTunnel, Virtual, Other }
```

Classification rules that tl-collect (E04) applies and the UI relies on, recorded here as doc comments on `NetKind`: `lo` is never shown; `tailscale0` is `VpnTunnel` and shown; `docker0`, `veth*`, `br-*`, `virbr*`, `vnet*` are `Virtual` and hidden by default; settings `performance.show_network_{wired,wireless,vpn,virtual,other}` where only `virtual` defaults to false.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a catalog with entries for idx 0, 1, 2 **When** `get(DeviceIdx(1))` runs **Then** it returns the idx-1 entry; `get(DeviceIdx(3))` returns `None`.
- **Given** a catalog holding `Net { netns_ino: 1, ifindex: 2, name: "eno1" }` **When** `find` is called with an equal identity **Then** it returns that entry; with ifindex 3 it returns `None`.
- **Given** a catalog with two disks, one `present = false` **When** `present_of(DeviceKind::Disk)` runs **Then** it yields only the present disk.
- **Given** each `DeviceIdentity` variant **When** `kind()` runs **Then** it returns the matching `DeviceKind` (`CpuPackage` gives `Cpu`).

## Files
- `crates/tl-model/src/devices.rs`: fill the placeholder

## Tests
- `devices.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`:
  - `catalog_get_by_idx`
  - `catalog_find_by_identity`
  - `catalog_present_of_kind`
  - `identity_kind_mapping`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: a device with `present = false` shows `Missing` for its live values.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the catalog is replaced as a whole `Arc` only when it changes (`version` bumps); lookups do not allocate.
- Privacy: disk `wwn_or_serial` is a hardware serial. Never log it; copy commands may include it only where the spec says so (PERF-011).

## Notes
- `DeviceKind` is a helper the B1 writer added so pages can filter the catalog; it adds no data. `DeviceIdentity` is exactly ADR-003.
- ADR-003's `DeviceEntry` has no `NetKind` field, and PERF-005's persistent key strings (`cpu`, `memory`, `gpu:<uuid>`, `disk:<wwn or serial>`, `net:<ifname>`, `fan:<hwmon name>:<device path>:<n>`, `bat:<native path>`) need data the identity does not hold (fan device path, disk by-path name). Where the kind and the persistent key are carried is an open item in docs/plan/b1-infra.md; do not add fields in this bead.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`

title: E03-011 health.rs: SourceId, SourceState, SourceHealth, HealthSnapshot
description:
## Context
Every engine worker is one supervised source with a `SourceId` (ADR-004 worker list). Its health is published in `Snapshot.health` so the status chip can show "GPU data stale", "<Source> unavailable" or "<Source> paused after errors" (UI-SHL-051, APP-029), empty states can show the last error (UI-SYS empty states), and the shield can show the helper state (UI-SHL-011, UI-FND-028). Collection errors become `Validity::Failed` plus `SourceHealth.last_error`, never a toast (ADR-015). Sources: ADR-004 (worker list, `Disabled { until }`, `Late` rule), ADR-008 (stale threshold), ADR-003 (`ManagerState`), UI-SHL-051, UI-FND-028, APP-029.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-model/src/health.rs` (uses `time::TimeNs`):

```rust
/// One per supervised worker (ADR-004 worker list). Order and numbers are frozen.
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum SourceId {
    Cpu = 0, Memory = 1, Disk = 2, Net = 3, GpuNvidia = 4, GpuDrm = 5, Sensors = 6,
    Processes = 7, ProcessDetail = 8, Connections = 9, SystemdSystem = 10, SystemdUser = 11,
    Logind = 12, Startup = 13, Inventory = 14, KWin = 15, Udisks = 16, UPower = 17,
    NetworkManager = 18, HistoryRecorder = 19, Journal = 20,
}
impl SourceId {
    pub const COUNT: usize = 21;
    pub const ALL: [SourceId; 21];          // in number order
    pub const fn index(self) -> usize;       // the discriminant
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug, Default)]
pub enum SourceState {
    #[default]
    Off,                          // not demanded; the worker sleeps (IDLE_RECHECK)
    Running,                      // producing fresh data
    Late,                         // 3 consecutive jobs longer than 0.8 × period (ADR-004)
    Stale,                        // last fresh data older than max(3 × period, 1.5 s) (ADR-008)
    Failed,                       // last attempt failed; last_error says why
    Disabled { until: TimeNs },   // restart budget spent (5 in 60 s); off for 60 s (ADR-004)
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct SourceHealth {
    pub state: SourceState,
    pub last_ok_ns: Option<TimeNs>,   // CLOCK_BOOTTIME of the last fresh update, for "No new data for 12 s"
    pub last_error: Option<Arc<str>>, // short, sanitized error text for tooltips and empty states
}

/// Privileged helper state for the shield (UI-FND-028, ADR-006). P3; Missing before then.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug, Default)]
pub enum HelperState { #[default] Missing, Locked, Starting, Unlocked }

/// systemd manager connection state for the Services tab (ADR-003 ServicesSnapshot.managers).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug, Default)]
pub enum ManagerState { Connected, #[default] Unavailable, Reconnecting }

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct HealthSnapshot {
    pub version: u64,                          // bumps when any state or the helper state changes
    pub sources: [SourceHealth; SourceId::COUNT],
    pub helper: HelperState,
}
impl HealthSnapshot {
    pub fn get(&self, id: SourceId) -> &SourceHealth;   // &self.sources[id.index()]
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `SourceId::ALL` **When** iterated **Then** it has 21 entries and `index()` equals the position for each.
- **Given** `SourceState::default()` **When** read **Then** it is `Off`.
- **Given** a `HealthSnapshot` whose `sources[SourceId::GpuNvidia.index()]` is `Stale` **When** `get(SourceId::GpuNvidia)` runs **Then** it returns that entry.
- **Given** a `HealthSnapshot` **When** its fields are listed **Then** they are exactly `version`, `sources`, `helper`.
- **Given** `HelperState::default()` and `ManagerState::default()` **When** read **Then** they are `Missing` and `Unavailable`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-model/src/health.rs`: fill the placeholder

## Tests
- `health.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`:
  - `source_id_all_and_index`
  - `source_id_numbers_frozen`: asserts each discriminant listed above.
  - `defaults`
  - `health_get_by_id`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `last_error` is display text, set by the engine from `WorkerError` (E08). It must be one line, at most 200 characters, with control characters removed (ADR-015 sanitize rules apply in the engine before it is stored).
- Validity: `SourceState` explains why values show `Stale` or `Failed`.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: `HealthSnapshot` is replaced as a whole `Arc` only when a state changes.
- Privacy: `last_error` must never contain a command line, environment value or file content (ADR-015).

## Notes
- `HealthSnapshot` carries a plain `version` instead of a `ComponentHeader`: `ComponentHeader` lives in `snapshot.rs` (E03-A2 half), which depends on this half, so using it here would make a dependency cycle. Health has no observed time range of its own; the UI only needs the version to detect a change. Recorded as an open item for the leader.
- The source display names ("CPU", "Memory", "Disks", "Network", "GPU", "Sensors", "Processes", "Services", "Startup", "Connections", "Inventory", "KWin") and the chip texts are UI strings (E20, UI-SHL-051), not part of this type.
- `SourceState` variants are not listed in one place in the docs; the six above collect every state ADR-004, ADR-008 and UI-SHL-051 name (open item for confirmation). The `last_error` 200-character limit is also a B1 proposal.
- ADR-004's worker list has no entry for the public IP fetch (E12) or the low-memory stripped sweep (E32). The recommendation is that the low-memory source reports as `Processes` and the public IP fetch is not a supervised source (open item).
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`

title: E03-012 units.rs: percent, sizes and rates
E03-013 units.rs: counts, times, frequencies, power, caches, addresses
E03-050 snapshot.rs: component header, mask, series, process, system and windows components
description:
## Context
Fills the first part of `tl-model/src/snapshot.rs`: the component header, the component mask the UI hub computes, and the four simple components (series, processes, system, windows). Every other component file and the `Snapshot` struct itself (bead E03-064) build on `ComponentHeader`. Sources: ADR-003 "Snapshot" and "Per-component fields the UI reads", ADR-005 (hub mask), R-046 and PROC-052 (window list fields), R-119.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-model/src/snapshot.rs` (the placeholder file created by E03-001; do not edit `lib.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug, Default)]
pub struct ComponentHeader {
    pub version: u64,          // bumps when the component content changes
    pub observed_start: TimeNs,
    pub observed_end: TimeNs,
    pub validity: Validity,    // Default: Validity::WarmingUp
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Default)]
pub struct ComponentMask(pub u16); // one bit per Snapshot component, computed by the UI
impl ComponentMask {
    pub const SYSTEM: Self = Self(1 << 0);
    pub const SERIES: Self = Self(1 << 1);
    pub const PROCESSES: Self = Self(1 << 2);
    pub const TABLE: Self = Self(1 << 3);
    pub const CONNECTIONS: Self = Self(1 << 4);
    pub const SERVICES: Self = Self(1 << 5);
    pub const STARTUP: Self = Self(1 << 6);
    pub const INVENTORY: Self = Self(1 << 7);
    pub const DEVICES: Self = Self(1 << 8);
    pub const HEALTH: Self = Self(1 << 9);
    pub const WINDOWS: Self = Self(1 << 10);
    pub const DETAILS: Self = Self(1 << 11);
    pub const HISTORY: Self = Self(1 << 12);
    pub const ALL: Self = Self(0x1FFF);
    pub const NONE: Self = Self(0);
    pub const fn contains(self, other: Self) -> bool;   // (self.0 & other.0) == other.0
    pub const fn intersects(self, other: Self) -> bool; // (self.0 & other.0) != 0
    pub const fn union(self, other: Self) -> Self;
}
// also impl BitOr and BitOrAssign for ComponentMask

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct SeriesSet {
    pub header: ComponentHeader,
    pub series: Arc<[Arc<SeriesView>]>, // sorted by SeriesId; unchanged series reuse their Arc
}
impl SeriesSet { pub fn get(&self, id: SeriesId) -> Option<&Arc<SeriesView>>; } // binary search

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct ProcessSnapshot {
    pub header: ComponentHeader,
    pub records: Arc<[ProcessRecord]>, // sorted by ProcessKey
    pub coverage: Coverage,            // from process.rs (E03-A1 half)
}
impl ProcessSnapshot { pub fn get(&self, key: ProcessKey) -> Option<&ProcessRecord>; } // binary search

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct SystemSnapshot {
    pub header: ComponentHeader,
    pub cpu: CpuTotals,
    pub memory: MemoryTotals,
    pub disks: Arc<[(DeviceIdx, DiskTotals)]>,     // sorted by DeviceIdx
    pub nets: Arc<[(DeviceIdx, NetTotals)]>,
    pub gpus: Arc<[(DeviceIdx, GpuTotals)]>,
    pub sensors: Arc<[(DeviceIdx, SensorReading)]>,
    pub cpu_topology: Arc<CpuTopology>,            // read at start and on CPU hotplug
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug, Default)]
pub struct FrameGeometry { pub x: i32, pub y: i32, pub width: i32, pub height: i32 } // logical px

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct WindowEntry {
    pub internal_id: Arc<str>,       // KWin internalId, a braced UUID, as given
    pub pid: u32,
    pub caption: Arc<str>,
    pub resource_class: Arc<str>,
    pub desktop_file_name: Arc<str>,
    pub minimized: bool,
    pub maximized: bool,
    pub keep_above: bool,
    pub frame_geometry: FrameGeometry,
    pub window_type: i32,            // KWin windowType value as reported
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct WindowsSnapshot {
    pub header: ComponentHeader,     // validity Unsupported when the KWin bridge is not available
    pub windows: Arc<[WindowEntry]>, // sorted by (pid, internal_id)
}
impl WindowsSnapshot { pub fn for_pid(&self, pid: u32) -> &[WindowEntry]; } // binary-search range
```

`Default` derives must give `validity = Validity::WarmingUp` (the `Validity` default) and empty slices (`Arc::from([])`). The types use `Arc` from `std::sync`. `CpuTotals`, `MemoryTotals`, `DiskTotals`, `NetTotals`, `GpuTotals`, `SensorReading`, `CpuTopology` come from `system.rs`; `SeriesView` from `series.rs`; `ProcessRecord`, `Coverage` from `process.rs`; `ProcessKey`, `SeriesId`, `DeviceIdx` from `ids.rs`; `TimeNs` from `time.rs`. If any of those does not implement `Default`, implement `Default` for the snapshot type by hand with the same rule. No serde on these types: snapshots never leave the process.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `ComponentMask::SYSTEM | ComponentMask::SERIES` **When** `contains(ComponentMask::SERIES)` is called **Then** it returns true, and `contains(ComponentMask::TABLE)` returns false.
- **Given** the thirteen bit constants **When** they are ORed together **Then** the result equals `ComponentMask::ALL` and no two constants share a bit.
- **Given** a `SeriesSet` with three views sorted by `SeriesId` **When** `get` is called with the second id **Then** it returns that view, and an absent id returns `None`.
- **Given** a `ProcessSnapshot` with records sorted by key **When** `get` is called with a key that is not present **Then** it returns `None`.
- **Given** a `WindowsSnapshot` with two windows for pid 10 and one for pid 12 **When** `for_pid(10)` is called **Then** it returns exactly the two pid-10 entries, and `for_pid(11)` returns an empty slice.
- **Given** `ComponentHeader::default()` **When** it is read **Then** `version == 0` and `validity == Validity::WarmingUp`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-model/src/snapshot.rs`: fill the placeholder with the types above (the `Snapshot` struct and the services, startup, connections and inventory components are added by E03-054, E03-055, E03-056 and E03-064).

## Tests
- `snapshot.rs` unit tests (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests`):
  - `mask_bits_distinct_and_all`: every constant has one bit, pairwise distinct, OR equals `ALL`.
  - `mask_contains_intersects`: the first criterion plus `intersects`.
  - `series_set_get_binary_search`: present and absent ids.
  - `process_snapshot_get`: present and absent keys.
  - `windows_for_pid_range`: the window criterion.
  - `header_default_warming_up`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: every header can carry any of the seven `Validity` states; `WindowsSnapshot` uses `Unsupported` without the bridge.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: lookups are binary searches over sorted slices; no hashing, no allocation.
- Privacy: window captions are untrusted text from other programs; they are displayed through the UI's untrusted-text path and never logged by this crate.

## Notes
- ADR-003 defines `ComponentMask(pub u16)` and the bit names; the bit positions follow the order in which ADR-003 lists them. The mask is computed by the UI and never stored, so the numbers are not part of any file format.
- The `SystemSnapshot` field layout (one field per `system.rs` totals type, per-device totals keyed by `DeviceIdx`) and `WindowEntry` field types are derived from ADR-003 and PROC-052; see open item "SystemSnapshot and WindowEntry layout" in `docs/plan/b1-infra.md`. If the leader changes them, update this bead before it starts.
- Depends on E03-A1 for every type from the core files.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo test -p tl-model`.

title: E03-051 table.rs: process TableQuery, TableRow, ProcessTableView and header totals
description:
## Context
Fills the process-table half of `tl-model/src/table.rs`: the query the UI sends with `Command::SetTableQuery`, and the engine-built view the process table renders. The engine sorts, filters, groups and flattens; the UI never does (ADR-009). Sources: ADR-009 "Process tree-table", ADR-003, ADR-011 (sort in `state.toml`), PROC-022, PROC-038 (header totals), R-010, R-011, R-043.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-model/src/table.rs` (placeholder from E03-001):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum TableMode { #[default] Grouped, Tree, Flat }   // settings value "grouped" | "tree" | "flat"

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub struct SortSpec { pub column: ColumnId, pub ascending: bool } // tie-break is always ProcessKey (engine)

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub struct TableQuery {
    pub generation: u64,
    pub mode: TableMode,          // Grouped | Tree | Flat
    pub sort: SortSpec,           // column + Asc/Desc; tie-break ProcessKey
    pub filter: Arc<str>,         // lowercase; matches display name, image name, cmdline, user,
                                  // description, app name, unit name, group names; numeric input
                                  // also matches PID by prefix
    pub expanded: Arc<[NodeId]>,  // UI owns expansion state
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub struct TableRow {
    pub node: NodeId, pub depth: u8, pub expanded: bool, pub has_children: bool,
    pub record: Option<u32>,      // index into ProcessSnapshot.records
    pub group: Option<u32>,       // index into ProcessTableView.groups
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub struct Total<T> { pub value: T, pub validity: Validity }   // Default: value default, WarmingUp

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub struct TableTotals {          // the two-line header numbers (PROC-038)
    pub cpu_pct: Total<f32>,          // /proc/stat total, ADR-008 math
    pub memory_pct: Total<f32>,       // (MemTotal - MemAvailable) / MemTotal
    pub swap_pct: Total<f32>,         // swap used %
    pub disk_busy_pct: Total<f32>,    // highest busy % among physical disks
    pub network_bps: Total<f64>,      // total physical-interface throughput, bytes per second
    pub network_link_bps: Option<f64>,// summed link speed in bytes per second; None = unknown (UI shows the rate)
    pub gpu_pct: Total<f32>,          // highest utilisation among GPUs; Unsupported with no GPU
    pub gpu_adapter_pct: [Total<f32>; 16], // columns gpu_0 .. gpu_15
    pub vram_pct: Total<f32>,         // used / total over all GPUs
    pub threads: Total<u64>,          // system thread count
    pub handles: Total<u64>,          // /proc/sys/fs/file-nr field 1
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ProcessTableView {
    pub header: ComponentHeader,
    pub query_generation: u64,
    pub rows: Arc<[TableRow]>,
    pub groups: Arc<[GroupRow]>,  // aggregated values, no double counting of descendants
    pub totals: TableTotals,
}
```

`Default` for `TableQuery`: generation 0, `TableMode::Grouped`, sort `{ column: ColumnId` for `"pid"`, `ascending: true }` (state.toml `[sort.processes] column = "pid", ascending = true`), empty filter, empty `expanded`. `Default` for `TableTotals`: every `Total` WarmingUp, `network_link_bps: None`. `Default` for `ProcessTableView`: default header, generation 0, empty slices, default totals. `NodeId` and `ColumnId` come from `ids.rs`, `GroupRow` from `process.rs`, `ComponentHeader` from `snapshot.rs` (E03-050). Use the `ColumnId` constructor that E03-A1 provides for `"pid"` (for example `ColumnId::from_str("pid")` or its named constant).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `TableQuery::default()` **When** it is read **Then** mode is `Grouped`, sort column is the `pid` id, `ascending` is true and `filter` is empty.
- **Given** `TableMode::Tree` **When** it is serialized with serde to a string value **Then** the value is `"tree"`, and `"flat"` deserializes to `TableMode::Flat`.
- **Given** `TableTotals::default()` **When** each total is read **Then** every validity is `WarmingUp` and `network_link_bps` is `None`.
- **Given** two `TableQuery` values that differ only in `generation` **When** they are compared **Then** they are not equal.

## Files
- `crates/tl-model/src/table.rs`: the types above. The system-table half (`SysTable`, `SysTableQuery`, `ServiceFilter`, `SysNodeId`, `SysRow`, `UnitRef`, `Manager`, `StartupRef`) is added by E03-052.

## Tests
- `table.rs` unit tests:
  - `table_query_default_matches_state_toml`: first criterion.
  - `table_mode_serde_lowercase`: second criterion (use `serde` with a small test serializer, for example `postcard` round trip plus `serde::de::value` for the string form; do not add a `toml` dependency).
  - `table_totals_default_warming_up`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: every total carries its own `Validity`; GPU totals are `Unsupported` without a GPU (shown `n/a`), `WarmingUp` before the second sample (shown `…`).
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: `TableRow` is `Copy` and small; `rows` and `groups` are shared `Arc` slices so a snapshot that does not change the table reuses them.
- Privacy: `filter` holds user text; never log it above debug level.

## Notes
- PROC-038 gives Network as "% of the summed link speed; a rate when the link speed is unknown". The view carries the rate and the summed link speed so the UI formats either form in the `units.network` unit; this split is derived (see open item "TableTotals field layout").
- Depends on E03-050 (`ComponentHeader`) and E03-A1 (`NodeId`, `ColumnId`, `GroupRow`, `Validity`).
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo test -p tl-model`.

title: E03-052 table.rs: system-table query, rows, UnitRef, StartupRef and ServiceFilter
description:
## Context
Adds the system-table half of `tl-model/src/table.rs`: one query type for the Services, Startup Apps and Connections tables, the row type the engine flattens into, and the identity types for units and startup entries. The engine sorts, filters and flattens these tables like the process table (UI-SYS-002). Sources: ADR-003 (table.rs code block), UI-SYS-002, UI-SYS-011 (filter strip), SYS-001 to SYS-004, SYS-019, SYS-020, R-082, canonical table (a) `[services]`.

## Deliverable
Append to `crates/tl-model/src/table.rs`:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Manager { System, User }

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct UnitRef { pub manager: Manager, pub name: Arc<str> } // `foo.service` may exist in both managers

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum StartupSource { AutostartUser, AutostartSystem, UserUnit, PlasmaEnv, PlasmaShutdown }
// serde names: "autostartuser", ... are never written to disk; they exist for postcard only

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct StartupRef { pub source: StartupSource, pub id: Arc<str> }
// id: the .desktop file name for autostart entries, the unit id for user units,
// the script file name for Plasma scripts. Stable across rescans (selection is kept by StartupRef, R-082).

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum UnitType { Service, Socket, Timer, Mount, Automount, Path, Target, Swap, Slice, Scope }
impl UnitType {
    pub fn from_unit_name(name: &str) -> Option<UnitType>; // suffix after the last '.'
    pub const DEFAULT_SHOWN: [UnitType; 4] = [Service, Socket, Timer, Mount];
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum ServiceStateFilter { Running, Failed, Stopped, Disabled }

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub struct ServiceFilter {
    pub states: SmallVec<[ServiceStateFilter; 4]>, // OR; empty = all states
    pub unit_types: SmallVec<[UnitType; 10]>,      // never empty (UI keeps one selected)
    pub system: bool,                              // show System group; default true
    pub user: bool,                                // show User group; default true
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub enum SysTable { Services, Startup, Connections }

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub enum SysNodeId {
    ServiceGroup(Manager),             // "System services (N)" / "User services (N)"
    Unit(UnitRef),
    UnitProcess(UnitRef, ProcessKey),  // child process row under a unit
    Startup(StartupRef),
    Conn(u64),                         // socket cookie
}

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub struct SysTableQuery {
    pub table: SysTable,
    pub generation: u64,
    pub sort: SortSpec,                // column id + ascending
    pub filter: Arc<str>,              // lowercase text filter from the FilterBox
    pub expanded: Arc<[SysNodeId]>,    // UI-owned expansion
    pub services: Option<ServiceFilter>, // Some only for SysTable::Services
}

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub struct SysRow {
    pub node: SysNodeId, pub depth: u8, pub expanded: bool,
    pub has_children: bool,
    pub record: Option<u32>,           // index into the component's records/units/entries
}
```

`ServiceFilter::default()`: `states` empty, `unit_types` = `UnitType::DEFAULT_SHOWN`, `system: true`, `user: true`. `UnitType::from_unit_name("sshd.service")` is `Some(Service)`; `"foo.device"` is `None` (device units are always hidden, SYS-002); a name without a dot is `None`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `ServiceFilter::default()` **When** it is read **Then** `unit_types` is `[Service, Socket, Timer, Mount]`, `states` is empty, and `system` and `user` are true.
- **Given** the names `sshd.service`, `dbus.socket`, `fstrim.timer`, `home.mount`, `proc-sys-fs-binfmt_misc.automount`, `cups.path`, `graphical.target`, `dev-zram0.swap`, `user.slice`, `session-2.scope` **When** `from_unit_name` is called **Then** each maps to its `UnitType`.
- **Given** `foo.device`, `noext` and `` (empty) **When** `from_unit_name` is called **Then** each returns `None`.
- **Given** two `UnitRef`s with the same name and different managers **When** they are compared **Then** they are not equal.
- **Given** `UnitType::Automount` **When** serialized to a string value **Then** it is `"automount"` (matches `services.unit_types` in table (a)).

## Files
- `crates/tl-model/src/table.rs`: append the types above.

## Tests
- `table.rs` unit tests:
  - `service_filter_default_matches_table_a`.
  - `unit_type_from_name_all_ten`.
  - `unit_type_from_name_rejects_device_and_bare`.
  - `unit_ref_manager_distinguishes`.
  - `unit_type_and_state_filter_serde_lowercase`: string forms for every variant of `UnitType` and `ServiceStateFilter`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: `SysNodeId` clones are cheap (`Arc<str>` names).
- Privacy: unit and entry names are not secret; filter text is user input and is never logged above debug level.

## Notes
- **`SysNodeId` location.** ADR-003's code block puts `SysNodeId` in `table.rs`; `docs/plan/00-epics.md` section 2 lists it under `ids.rs`. It needs `UnitRef` and `StartupRef`, which live in `table.rs`, so this bead defines it in `table.rs` (ADR-003 has precedence). The E03-A1 half must not define it in `ids.rs`. Open item "SysNodeId location".
- **`StartupRef` fields** are not fixed by any doc (ADR-003 and UI-SYS name the type only). The `{ source, id }` form above is the recommendation in open item "StartupRef identity"; confirm before starting.
- `smallvec` is in tl-model's allowed row (ADR-001).
- Depends on E03-051 (same file, `SortSpec`) and E03-A1 (`ProcessKey`).
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo test -p tl-model`.

title: E03-053 actions.rs: action requests, targets, kinds, states, events and ActionError
description:
## Context
Fills `tl-model/src/actions.rs`: every type of an action request, its targets and its results. The UI builds `ActionRequest`s with identities captured at menu-open time; the engine admits them and reports ordered `ActionEvent`s; `tl-ui/src/action_tracker.rs::message(&ActionError)` turns errors into text. Sources: ADR-005 "Action request and result types", ADR-006 (action kinds, thread target, cgroup ref, deadlines are the engine's), ADR-015 (`ActionError` variants), R-035 to R-040, R-092, R-093, R-097, R-117, R-119, R-134, SYS-013, SYS-031, D-009, canonical table (a) `processes.dump_type`.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-model/src/actions.rs` (placeholder from E03-001):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ActionId(pub u64);  // allocated by the UI: AtomicU64 starting at 1

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ActionRequest {
    pub id: ActionId,
    pub kind: ActionKind,
    pub targets: SmallVec<[ActionTarget; 1]>,  // max 256, captured at menu-open time; empty for OpenUri, ShowInFileManager, Launch
    pub privileged: bool,                       // user chose "Retry as administrator" (P3)
}

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub struct CgroupRef {
    pub rel_path: Arc<str>,  // relative to /sys/fs/cgroup
    pub cgroup_id: u64,      // inode of the cgroup directory when captured
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Family { Inet, Inet6 }          // AF_INET, AF_INET6
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Proto { Tcp, Udp }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct FourTuple { pub local: std::net::SocketAddr, pub remote: std::net::SocketAddr }

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub enum ActionTarget {
    Process(ProcessKey),
    Thread { process: ProcessKey, tid: u32 },  // P2: Threads tab (allowed kinds: Signal, SetNice, SetSched, SetAffinity)
    Cgroup(CgroupRef),                         // app cgroups under app.slice
    Unit(UnitRef),                             // services; freeze, thaw and kill of units outside app.slice
    Startup(StartupRef),
    Socket { cookie: u64, family: Family, proto: Proto, four_tuple: FourTuple }, // P3: SockDestroy
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Signal { Term, Kill, Hup, Int, Quit, Stop, Cont, Usr1, Usr2, Other(u8) } // Other: any other number, incl. SIGRTMIN..=SIGRTMAX
impl Signal {
    /// Linux signal number: Term 15, Kill 9, Hup 1, Int 2, Quit 3, Stop 19, Cont 18, Usr1 10, Usr2 12, Other(n) n.
    pub const fn number(self) -> i32;
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum SchedPolicy { Other, Batch, Idle, Fifo, Rr }   // rt_prio 1..=99 for Fifo and Rr, else 0

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum IoPriority { None, Realtime(u8), BestEffort(u8), Idle } // levels 0..=7; None = IOPRIO_CLASS_NONE, "Default (follows nice)"

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum DumpMode { #[default] Mini, Full }   // setting processes.dump_type = "mini" | "full"

/// P3: only the keys the user changed, plus the keys already in the tasklens drop-in (SYS-013).
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug, Default)]
pub struct RecoveryEdit {
    pub restart: Option<Arc<str>>,               // Restart= word: no, on-success, on-failure, on-abnormal, on-watchdog, on-abort, always
    pub restart_usec: Option<u64>,               // RestartSec in microseconds
    pub restart_steps: Option<u32>,              // RestartSteps=
    pub restart_max_delay_usec: Option<u64>,     // RestartMaxDelaySec in microseconds
    pub start_limit_burst: Option<u32>,          // StartLimitBurst=
    pub start_limit_interval_usec: Option<u64>,  // StartLimitIntervalSec in microseconds
    pub start_limit_action: Option<Arc<str>>,    // StartLimitAction= word
    pub failure_action: Option<Arc<str>>,        // FailureAction= word
    pub on_failure: Option<Arc<[Arc<str>]>>,     // OnFailure= unit names
}

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum LaunchWhat { Command(Arc<str>), DesktopEntry(Arc<str>), Unit(UnitRef) }
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub struct LaunchSpec { pub what: LaunchWhat, pub as_admin: bool, pub cwd: Option<Arc<str>> }

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub enum ActionKind {
    Signal(Signal),            // End Task = Signal(Term), End Process = Signal(Kill)
    KillTree,                  // SIGSTOP every target, then SIGKILL every target
    Suspend, Resume,           // SIGSTOP / SIGCONT on one process
    SetNice(i8),               // -20..=19
    SetSched { policy: SchedPolicy, rt_prio: u8 },  // P2
    SetAffinity(CpuSet),
    SetIoPriority(IoPriority),
    FreezeGroup, ThawGroup, KillGroup,
    Dump { mode: DumpMode, path: Arc<str> },   // P2; the UI picks the path (R-119)
    UnitStart, UnitStop, UnitRestart, UnitReload, UnitResetFailed,
    UnitEnable, UnitDisable, UnitMask, UnitUnmask,
    UnitWriteRecovery(RecoveryEdit),           // P3
    UnitRemoveRecovery,                        // P3: deletes the tasklens drop-in
    StartupEnable, StartupDisable, StartupRunNow, StartupDelete,
    SockDestroy,                               // P3: target ActionTarget::Socket
    OpenUri(Arc<str>),                         // portal OpenURI, else xdg-open
    ShowInFileManager { path: Arc<str>, properties: bool }, // FileManager1 ShowItems / ShowItemProperties
    Launch(LaunchSpec),                        // Run dialog, Startup "Run now"
}
impl ActionKind {
    /// True for OpenUri, ShowInFileManager and Launch: targets is empty and admission skips the target checks (R-134).
    pub fn is_targetless(&self) -> bool;
}

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum ActionError {
    PermissionDenied,
    NoSuchProcess,
    Partial { done: u16, total: u16 },
    UnitJob(Arc<str>),        // JobRemoved result other than "done"
    Os(i32),                  // errno
    Internal(Arc<str>),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub enum RejectReason { Busy, TooManyTargets, IdentityChanged, KernelThread, Protected, NotOwner, Unsupported }

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum ActionState {
    Rejected(RejectReason),    // never started, nothing changed
    Started,                   // admitted and running
    Succeeded,
    Failed(ActionError),       // the OS or service reported failure; nothing changed
    OutcomeUnknown(Arc<str>),  // timed out or target vanished after the effect may have happened
}
impl ActionState {
    pub fn is_final(&self) -> bool;  // every state except Started
    /// Summary rule (ADR-005): Succeeded only if every target succeeded; otherwise the worst state in the
    /// order Failed, OutcomeUnknown, Rejected. Returns the first state of the worst class found.
    pub fn summarize<'a>(per_target: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a ActionState>) -> ActionState;
}

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub struct ActionEvent {
    pub id: ActionId,
    pub target: Option<u16>,   // index into the request's targets; None for the whole request
    pub state: ActionState,
}

pub const MAX_ACTION_TARGETS: usize = 256;   // ADR-005, ADR-006 admission
pub const MAX_ACTIONS_IN_FLIGHT: usize = 16;
```

`CpuSet` comes from `system.rs`, `ProcessKey` from `ids.rs`, `UnitRef` and `StartupRef` from `table.rs` (E03-052). `summarize` over an empty iterator returns `Succeeded` (a targetless kind has no per-target events; the engine sends the summary from the one job's result).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** each named `Signal` variant **When** `number()` is called **Then** it returns 15, 9, 1, 2, 3, 19, 18, 10, 12 in variant order, and `Other(34)` returns 34.
- **Given** per-target states `[Succeeded, Succeeded]` **When** `summarize` runs **Then** the result is `Succeeded`.
- **Given** `[Succeeded, Rejected(IdentityChanged), OutcomeUnknown("x")]` **When** `summarize` runs **Then** the result is `OutcomeUnknown("x")`.
- **Given** `[Rejected(Protected), Failed(PermissionDenied), OutcomeUnknown("x")]` **When** `summarize` runs **Then** the result is `Failed(PermissionDenied)`.
- **Given** `[Rejected(KernelThread)]` **When** `summarize` runs **Then** the result is `Rejected(KernelThread)`.
- **Given** `ActionKind::OpenUri`, `ShowInFileManager` and `Launch` **When** `is_targetless` is called **Then** it is true; for `Signal(Term)` and `UnitStart` it is false.
- **Given** `ActionState::Started` **When** `is_final` is called **Then** it is false; every other variant gives true.
- **Given** `DumpMode::Full` **When** serialized to a string value **Then** it is `"full"`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-model/src/actions.rs`: the types, constants and the three methods above.

## Tests
- `actions.rs` unit tests: `signal_numbers_linux`, `summarize_all_succeeded`, `summarize_failed_beats_unknown_and_rejected`, `summarize_unknown_beats_rejected`, `summarize_single_rejected`, `summarize_empty_is_succeeded`, `targetless_kinds`, `state_is_final`, `dump_mode_serde_lowercase`.
- `tests/proto_roundtrip.rs` (E03-070) round-trips the serde types of this file through postcard.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `ActionError` variants exactly as ADR-015; no `Display` text here (the UI's `message()` owns wording).
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: `ActionRequest.targets` is a `SmallVec` with one inline target; no allocation for single-target actions.
- Privacy: `OpenUri`, `Launch` command text and dump paths are user data; they must not be logged above debug level (ADR-015 never-logged list covers command lines).
- Security: the targets carry full identities (`ProcessKey` with boot id and start ticks, `CgroupRef` with inode) so the engine and helper can revalidate; never add a PID-only target.

## Notes
- `FourTuple` as two `std::net::SocketAddr` values (scope id in `SocketAddrV6`) is derived: ADR-005 names the type without fields. Open item "FourTuple, Family, Proto fields".
- `RecoveryEdit` fields are derived one-to-one from the SYS-013 key list (`Restart*`, `StartLimit*`, `FailureAction`, `OnFailure`) and the R-004 helper key limit. Open item "RecoveryEdit fields".
- `MAX_ACTION_TARGETS` and `MAX_ACTIONS_IN_FLIGHT` restate ADR-005 and ADR-006 numbers so the UI and engine share one constant.
- serde derives are only on `Copy` types: workspace `serde` has only the `derive` feature (ADR-002), so `Arc<str>` fields are not serializable. The helper protocol (E03-070) defines its own owned-string types.
- Depends on E03-052 (`UnitRef`, `StartupRef`) and E03-A1 (`ProcessKey`, `CpuSet`).
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo test -p tl-model`.

title: E03-A2 Contracts compile
description:
## Context
Anchor E03-A2, the capstone of the `tl-model` contracts. When it closes, every contract file (`snapshot.rs`, `table.rs`, `details.rs`, `demand.rs`, `actions.rs`, `command.rs`, `settings.rs`, `wire.rs`, `gpu_proto.rs`, `helper_proto.rs`, `journal.rs`, `history.rs`, `client.rs`) is filled and compiles, and the settings defaults are proven equal to canonical table (a). The engine, UI and app epics depend on this anchor, so it is phase P0 (needed by the phase-0 spike through E08-A1, E09-A1, E16-A1). Sources: ADR-003, ADR-005, ADR-011 "Verification", canonical table (a), `docs/plan/00-epics.md` section 3 (E03-A2 row).

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-model/tests/settings_defaults.rs`: the test file below. It embeds the two TOML blocks of canonical table (a) (the `settings.toml` block and the `state.toml` block, copied verbatim from `docs/RECONCILIATION.md` section "(a) Settings schema", with the commented example entries of `[fans]`, `[[minigraphs]]`, `[[detached_windows]]` and `[[tray_graphs]]` left as comments) as `const SETTINGS_TOML: &str` and `const STATE_TOML: &str`.
- Add `toml = { workspace = true }` under `[dev-dependencies]` of `crates/tl-model/Cargo.toml` (test only; `toml` is not a normal dependency of tl-model).
- No change to any `src/` file unless a test here finds a default that differs from table (a); then fix that default in `settings.rs` in this bead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `SETTINGS_TOML` **When** parsed with `toml::from_str::<Settings>` **Then** the result equals `Settings::default()`.
- **Given** `STATE_TOML` **When** parsed with `toml::from_str::<UiState>` **Then** the result equals `UiState::default()` except the column tables of history, services, startup and connections (table (a) shows only `[columns.processes]`; the test overwrites those four with their defaults before comparing).
- **Given** an empty string **When** parsed as `Settings` and as `UiState` **Then** both equal their defaults (every struct is `#[serde(default)]`).
- **Given** a `settings.toml` text with an unknown key `[general] foo = 1` and an unknown section `[bogus]` **When** parsed **Then** parsing succeeds and the known values are the defaults (unknown keys are ignored, ADR-011 load step 5).
- **Given** `toml::to_string(&Settings::default())` **When** parsed back **Then** it equals `Settings::default()` (save and load round trip).
- **Given** the crate **When** `cargo test -p tl-model` runs **Then** every test of E03-050 to E03-071 and this file passes, and `cargo build -p tl-model` has no warnings under the workspace lints.

## Files

- `crates/tl-model/Cargo.toml`: one `[dev-dependencies]` line.
- `crates/tl-model/src/settings.rs`: only to fix a default that differs from table (a).

## Tests

## Cross-cutting

- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: N/A.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- Unknown-key tolerance requires that no struct uses `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`.
- This anchor closes the E03 contract half. Later changes to these files need a new bead that depends on this anchor (00-epics section 2 "Up front" rule).
