title: E21-004 Settings menu with every P1 item
description:
## Context
Adds the Settings menu with every P1 item: refresh rate, network unit, the motion checks, Close with Esc, Default tab, Language and "Reset Settings to Defaults". Later beads add the P2, P3 and P4 rows (E21-010, E21-011, E21-033, E21-040, E21-042). Sources: UI-SHL-040, UI-SHL-031, UI-SHL-131, APP-022, APP-043, R-015, R-017, R-024, R-081, R-132.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/window/menus_settings.rs` (create): `pub fn build(window, cx, return_focus) -> Entity<PopupMenu>` with `TlMenu` header rows for the groups. P1 items, in order:

| Group header | Label | Kind | Key / Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monitoring | Refresh | submenu, radio: "0.25s", "0.5s", "1.0s", "2.0s", "5.0s", "10.0s" | `SetSetting { ProcessesIntervalMs, Int(250 / 500 / 1000 / 2000 / 5000 / 10000) }` |
| | Network transfer unit | submenu, radio: "Bits per second", "Bytes per second" | `SetSetting { UnitsNetwork, Str("bits" / "bytes") }` |
| | Auto-scale network transfer rates | check | `ToggleSetting(UnitsNetworkAutoScale)` |
| Motion & interaction | Animations | check | `ToggleSetting(MotionAnimations)` |
| | Smooth Graphs | check | `ToggleSetting(MotionSmoothGraphs)` |
| | Smooth Scroll | check | `ToggleSetting(MotionSmoothScroll)` |
| | Close with Esc | check | `ToggleSetting(WindowCloseWithEsc)` |
| Window & startup | Default tab | submenu, radio | `SetSetting { GeneralStartTab, Str(..) }` |
| Language | Language: | submenu, radio | `SetSetting { GeneralLanguage, Str(..) }` |
| (none) | separator | | |
| | Reset Settings to Defaults | item | `ResetSettings` (E21-005) |

- Refresh labels are exactly "0.25s", "0.5s", "1.0s", "2.0s", "5.0s", "10.0s"; the radio mark is on the item equal to `processes.interval_ms`; when the stored value is not one of the six (a hand-edited file, clamped to 250..=10000), no item is marked.
- Default tab items: one per tab built in the current phase, in tab order, with the tab labels "Processes", "Performance", "Services", "Startup Apps", "Connections", "Information", then "Last used"; values `processes`, `performance`, `services`, `startup`, `connections`, `information`, `last_used`. In P1 that is "Processes", "Performance", "Last used".
- Language items: "System default" (`system`), then each locale shipped in this build by its own name. This round ships English only (R-132), so the submenu has "System default" and "English (United States)" (`en-US`). Choosing one dispatches `SetSetting { GeneralLanguage, .. }`; the live switch itself (bundle reload, `strings_version`) is E16's `i18n.rs` reacting to the setting.
- Rows in a group appear only when their feature exists; a group header appears only when at least one row under it exists.
- `menubar.rs`: replace the `MenuId::Settings` arm with `menus_settings::build`.
- Chain edit `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`: `pub mod menus_settings;`.
- String keys appended (`shell-menu-settings-*`): "Monitoring", "Refresh", the six refresh labels, "Network transfer unit", "Bits per second", "Bytes per second", "Auto-scale network transfer rates", "Motion & interaction", "Animations", "Smooth Graphs", "Smooth Scroll", "Close with Esc", "Window & startup", "Default tab", "Last used", "Language", "Language:", "System default", "English (United States)", "Reset Settings to Defaults". Tab labels reuse the tab strip's keys (E20).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `processes.interval_ms = 1000` **When** Settings > Refresh opens **Then** the mark is on "1.0s".
- **Given** the Refresh submenu is open **When** "2.0s" is chosen **Then** `processes.interval_ms = 2000` and the fake engine receives `EngineSettings.interval_ms = 2000`.
- **Given** `units.network = "bits"` **When** "Bytes per second" is chosen **Then** `units.network = "bytes"`.
- **Given** `motion.animations = true` **When** "Animations" is activated **Then** the key becomes false.
- **Given** P1 tabs Processes and Performance **When** Default tab opens **Then** it lists exactly "Processes", "Performance", "Last used".
- **Given** the Language submenu **When** it opens **Then** it lists "System default" and "English (United States)" with the mark on the current `general.language`.
- **Given** the menu **When** "Reset Settings to Defaults" is activated **Then** `ResetSettings` is dispatched.
- **Given** Alt+S **When** pressed **Then** the Settings menu opens with the first enabled item highlighted.

## Files

- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/menubar.rs`: change the `MenuId::Settings` arm.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`, `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: chain edits.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_menus.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_menus.rs`:
- `settings_menu_refresh_radio`: choosing "2.0s" writes 2000 and the fake engine receives `EngineSettings.interval_ms = 2000`.
- `settings_menu_refresh_labels`: the six labels exactly as written.
- `settings_menu_p1_rows`: group headers and rows in the order above, no P2+ rows.
- `default_tab_lists_built_tabs`: P1 build lists Processes, Performance, Last used.
- `language_submenu_p1`: two items, mark on the current value.
- `reset_item_dispatches`: dispatches `ResetSettings`.

## Notes

title: E21-006 Crash Report window
description:
## Context
Builds the "tasklens Crash Report" window shown once after a crash: it tells the user tasklens closed unexpectedly and offers "Open log folder", "Copy report" and "Close". tl-app's panic hook (E33) writes the report files; this bead only shows the newest unseen one. Sources: UI-SHL-093, APP-055, R-049, ADR-015, UI-FND-021, UI-SHL-090.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/window/crash_report.rs` (create):
- `pub struct CrashReportWindow { report_text: Arc<str> }` (Entity), opened with `TlSecondaryWindow::open` (E16-A2): title "tasklens Crash Report", kind Tool window (`WindowKind::Floating`), size 480 × 220, not resizable, `WindowKey::CrashReport`.
- Content (padding 16): Lucide `triangle-alert` 24 px in `status.warning`; line 1 "tasklens closed unexpectedly last time." in `t_base` `text_primary`; line 2 "If tasklens crashed without a report, run coredumpctl info tasklens in a terminal." in `t_sm` `text_secondary`. Footer, right-aligned, gap `sp4`: "Open log folder" (Secondary), "Copy report" (Secondary), "Close" (Primary, default, Enter).
- "Copy report": `cx.write_to_clipboard(ClipboardItem::new_string(report_text))`, Success toast "Copied to clipboard" in this window.
- "Open log folder": sends `Command::Action(ActionRequest { kind: ActionKind::OpenUri("file://<logs dir>"), targets: [], .. })` where `<logs dir>` is `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/logs`; failure shows the action's failure toast through `ActionTracker` (E16-A3) as "Failed to open file location" (APP-044 shared text).
- "Close", Esc and Ctrl+W close the window.
- `pub fn show_pending(window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App)`: called after the main window's first frame (E20's startup steps call it; see Notes). It shows the window when a pending report exists and the main window is visible, then marks the report seen. When tasklens started hidden to the tray, it does nothing and runs again the next time the main window is shown.
- Seen rule: a report `crash-<t>.txt` without a matching `crash-<t>.seen` in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/crash/` is pending; on show the `.seen` marker is written. Only the newest pending report is shown, once.
- String keys appended (`shell-crash-*`): window title, the two lines, "Open log folder", "Copy report", "Close", plus `shell-toast-copied` "Copied to clipboard" if E16 has not added it.
- Chain edit `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`: `pub mod crash_report;`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a pending report with text "panic at x" **When** `show_pending` runs with the main window visible **Then** one "tasklens Crash Report" window opens and the report is marked seen.
- **Given** the report was marked seen **When** `show_pending` runs again **Then** no window opens.
- **Given** tasklens started hidden to the tray **When** `show_pending` runs **Then** no window opens and the report stays pending.
- **Given** the window is open **When** "Copy report" is clicked **Then** the clipboard holds "panic at x" and the toast "Copied to clipboard" shows in this window.
- **Given** the window is open **When** "Open log folder" is clicked **Then** the fake engine receives one `ActionKind::OpenUri` whose URI ends in `/tasklens/logs`.
- **Given** the window is open **When** Enter is pressed **Then** the window closes.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/crash_report.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`, `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: chain edits.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell_windows.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell_windows.rs`:
- `crash_report_shown_once`: pending report: window opens, mark-seen called once; second call opens nothing.
- `crash_report_deferred_while_hidden`.
- `crash_report_copy`: clipboard text equals the report, toast text.
- `crash_report_open_logs`: fake engine receives `OpenUri` for the logs dir.
- `crash_report_enter_closes`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: "Open log folder" failure uses the action failure toast "Failed to open file location".
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: focus starts on "Close"; Tab order Open log folder, Copy report, Close, then the pin.
- Performance: N/A.
- Privacy: the report text is shown and copied only on user request; nothing from it is logged.

## Notes
- GAP (open item 1 in the B7 plan, E21 section): tl-ui does no file I/O itself (ADR-011) and does not know the XDG directories; how tl-app hands over the pending report (text plus a mark-seen call) and the logs directory is not decided. The leader's recommendation is an `AppEnv` Global passed into `TasklensUi::init` and filled by E33 (fields used here: `logs_dir: Arc<Path>`, `pending_crash: Option<PendingCrash { text: Arc<str>, mark_seen: Box<dyn FnOnce() + Send> }>`). Implement against what the leader settles.
- Who calls `show_pending`: E20's startup sequence steps 8 to 11 (UI-SHL-110, "queued toasts after the first frame"). If E20's bead does not call it, the leader adds that edge.
- `ActionKind::OpenUri` and empty `targets`: R-134.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E21-007 Collector Health window
description:
## Context
Builds the "tasklens Collector Health" window: one row per engine source with its state, data age, restart count and last error. It opens from a health item in the status chip (P1, E20) and later from Debug > Collector health (E21-038). It replaces TaskSlinger's debug window and has no setting (R-071). Sources: UI-SHL-099, UI-SHL-051, APP-026, APP-029, R-071, ADR-003 (`HealthSnapshot`), ADR-004 (restart budget).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/window/collector_health.rs` (create):
- `pub fn init(cx: &mut App)`: registers the global handler for `OpenCollectorHealth` (Action declared by E20-A1 so the status chip can dispatch it; see Notes). Handler: `WindowRegistry` refocus if open, else open. Called from `TasklensUi::init` (one line in `app.rs`).
- `pub struct CollectorHealthWindow { rows: Vec<HealthRow>, _hub_sub: Subscription, _tick: Task<()> }` opened with `TlSecondaryWindow::open`: title "tasklens Collector Health", Tool window, default size 720 × 360, `WindowKey::CollectorHealth`.
- A fixed-column table (plain flex rows, row height from `UiMetrics.row_height`, header row with `header` background):

| Column | Width | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Source | 140 | source display name |
| State | 100 | "Running" `status.success`; "Stale" `status.warning`; "Disabled" `status.warning`; "Failed" `status.danger` |
| Last data | 100 | age of the last data as a table (d) short age plus " ago" ("3s ago", "12m 5s ago") |
| Restarts | 80, right-aligned, tabular figures | restart count |
| Last error | fills the rest, truncated at the end with "…" | `last_error`, full text in a `TlTooltip` |

- Rows are in `SourceId` declaration order. Source display names: CPU, Memory, Disks, Network, GPU, Sensors, Processes, Services, Startup, Connections, Inventory, KWin (UI-SHL-051); see Notes for the other sources.
- Re-render on `SnapshotChanged` with `ComponentMask::HEALTH` and once per second (a 1 s timer task that lives only while the window is open) for the ages.
- Esc and Ctrl+W close.
- String keys appended (`shell-health-*`): title, the five column headings, the four state words, " ago".
- Chain edit `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`: `pub mod collector_health;`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the window is closed **When** `OpenCollectorHealth` is dispatched twice **Then** exactly one "tasklens Collector Health" window exists and it is focused.
- **Given** a health snapshot with CPU Running, GPU Failed ("probe version mismatch"), Disk Stale **When** the window renders **Then** it shows three rows in `SourceId` order with "Failed" in `status.danger` and the error text truncated with its full text in the tooltip.
- **Given** a source whose last data is 3 s old **When** one second passes with no new snapshot **Then** its Last data cell changes from "3s ago" to "4s ago".
- **Given** a source with 5 restarts and state Disabled **When** rendered **Then** Restarts shows "5" right-aligned and State "Disabled" in `status.warning`.
- **Given** the window is open **When** Esc is pressed **Then** it closes and its timer task stops.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/collector_health.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`, `crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs`, `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: chain edits.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell_windows.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell_windows.rs`:
- `collector_health_refocus`: two dispatches leave one window.
- `collector_health_rows_and_colours`: fake health snapshot as above; row order, state words and colours.
- `collector_health_age_ticks`: advance the test clock 1 s: age text updates without a snapshot.
- `collector_health_timer_stops_on_close`: after close no further renders are scheduled.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A (it displays errors; it creates none).
- Validity: the State column shows `SourceState` only. A source with no data yet shows the WarmingUp glyph "…" (U+2026, `text_secondary`, ADR-003 table) in Last data.
- Accessibility: Esc closes; the table is read-only text; tooltips carry the full error.
- Performance: at most one render per second plus one per HEALTH change; rows reuse a `Vec` and `String` buffers.
- Privacy: `last_error` strings come from the engine, which never puts command lines or paths of other users' processes in them (ADR-015); show them as untrusted text (E15 `text/untrusted.rs`).

## Notes
- `OpenCollectorHealth` must be declared in E20-A1 `actions.rs`, because the status chip (E20) dispatches it and E20 cannot depend on E21. Proposed to the leader (edge 2).
- `HealthSnapshot`, `SourceHealth`, `SourceState`, `SourceId` come from tl-model `health.rs` (E03-A1); use its exact field names for state, last-data time, restart count and `last_error`.
- GAP: display names for `SourceId` values not in the UI-SHL-051 list (for example the logind, udisks, UPower and NetworkManager workers) are not decided; open item 6 in the B7 plan. Until settled, use the list above and the leader's answer for the rest.
- Short age format: `tl-model::units` (table d).
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E33 tl-app binary: args, paths, settings store, logging, crash, single instance, notifications; PKGBUILD, desktop file, assets
description: Epic E33 (app-packaging). Phases: P1 to P4 (P0 anchor). Estimated beads: 30. Scope, sources and file ownership: docs/plan/00-epics.md sections 1 and 2, key E33.

title: E33-A1 Binary starts
description:
## Context
Anchor bead E33-A1. The `tasklens` binary runs the UI-SHL-110 startup sequence steps 1 to 3 and 7 to 10 with default settings: panic hook, logging, arguments, the NVIDIA X11 environment rule, engine start, the GPUI application and the main window. Single instance (step 4) and settings loading (step 5) come in E33-A2. The phase-0 spike (E01) and E32 chain-edit their argument arms into this `main.rs`. Sources: UI-SHL-110, ADR-010 (Backend, Close behaviour), ADR-001 rule 4 (`unsafe` allowed in `tl-app/src/main.rs` only), ADR-015, APP-052, U-2.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`, with `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` at file level (ADR-001 rule 4) and a `// SAFETY:` comment on every `unsafe` block:
```rust
fn main() -> std::process::ExitCode
```
in this order:
1. `paths::Paths::from_env()`; on error print it to stderr and exit 1. `crash::install_hook(paths.crash_dir(), recent_cell.clone(), noop)`. Then `logging::init(&paths.logs_dir())` and fill `recent_cell`. The `LogGuard` is a local of `main`, dropped last.
2. `let args = args::parse();` (clap exits 2 on unknown arguments, UI-SHL-110 step 2). `debug = args.debug || std::env::var_os("TASKLENS_DEBUG").is_some_and(|v| v == "1")`.
3. NVIDIA X11 rule (ADR-010), before any thread starts: if `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is unset or empty, and `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` exists, and `__NV_FORCE_ENABLE_X11_EGL_PLATFORM` is unset, then `unsafe { std::env::set_var("__NV_FORCE_ENABLE_X11_EGL_PLATFORM", "1") }`. Log `info!(target: "tasklens::engine", "NVIDIA on X11: set __NV_FORCE_ENABLE_X11_EGL_PLATFORM=1")` when it is set. No other environment changes in P0 to P3 (`ZED_DEVICE_ID` is never set, R-070).
4. (E33-A2 inserts single instance here.)
5. (E33-A2 inserts settings, state and themes loading here.) In this bead use `Settings::default()` and `UiState::default()` from `tl-model`.
7. Start the engine: `tl_engine::Engine::start(config)` with the `EngineConfig` that E08-A1 defines, `mode = EngineMode::Full`, and the `EngineSettings` derived from `Settings` (ADR-011 Ownership: `processes.interval_ms`, `units.network`, `performance.show_network_*`, `history.*`, `processes.subtree_totals`, `processes.hide_system`). Do not wait for any collector. On error: `error!` with the message, print "tasklens could not start the engine: <error>" to stderr, exit 1.
8 to 10. Hand control to tl-ui: call the tl-ui run entry point that E16-A1 provides (open item E33-OI-1; recommended form `tl_ui::run(UiLaunch { client: Arc<dyn EngineClient>, settings, state, start_tab: args.tab.map(TabArg::to_model), select_pid: args.select_pid, debug, start_minimized: args.start_minimized, app_requests: None, persist: None, queued_toasts: Vec::new() })`). tl-ui performs step 8 (fonts, kit init, assets, theme, keys, globals), step 9 (main window on `--tab` or `general.start_tab`) and step 10 (first frame without waiting). `main.rs` never names a GPUI type, because gpui-kit is not in tl-app's allowed row (ADR-001).
- After the run entry returns: in this bead, log `info!(target: "tasklens::engine", "ui stopped")` and return `ExitCode::SUCCESS`, letting the engine drop. E33-011 adds the 1500 ms shutdown.
- Argument arms owned elsewhere: leave clearly marked insertion points as comments `// E01: --bench and --gallery arms go here (before step 7)` and `// E32: --low-memory and --watch-memory arms go here (before step 4)`. `--watch-memory` starts no GPUI (UI-SHL-110). In this bead those flags are accepted by clap and ignored.
- `--start-minimized`, `--select-pid` and `--tab` are only passed through to tl-ui here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a Wayland session **When** `tasklens` runs **Then** the main window opens on the Processes tab with default settings and the log file shows the engine start.
- **Given** `tasklens --tab performance` **When** it runs **Then** the main window opens on the Performance tab.
- **Given** `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset, `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` present and `__NV_FORCE_ENABLE_X11_EGL_PLATFORM` unset **When** `main` reaches step 3 **Then** the variable is `1` for the rest of the process.
- **Given** `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0` **When** `main` reaches step 3 **Then** `__NV_FORCE_ENABLE_X11_EGL_PLATFORM` is not set.
- **Given** `__NV_FORCE_ENABLE_X11_EGL_PLATFORM=0` set by the user **When** `main` reaches step 3 **Then** it stays `0`.
- **Given** `tasklens --bogus` **When** it runs **Then** it exits 2 and opens no window.
- **Given** a panic injected before step 7 (test build) **When** it happens **Then** a crash report exists under `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/crash/`.
- **Given** the user closes the main window **When** tl-ui quits **Then** the process exits 0.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: write steps 1 to 3 and 7 to 10 as above (large file rule does not apply; it stays under 200 lines).
- The X11 rule is a pure function inside `main.rs`, `fn nvidia_x11_rule(wayland: Option<OsString>, nvidia_present: bool, current: Option<OsString>) -> bool`, so it is testable; the `set_var` call stays in `main`.

## Tests
- `main.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: `x11_rule_sets_when_x11_nvidia_unset` (`nvidia_x11_rule(None, true, None) == true`), `x11_rule_skips_on_wayland`, `x11_rule_skips_without_nvidia`, `x11_rule_respects_user_value`, `x11_rule_empty_wayland_counts_as_unset`, `debug_from_env` (a pure helper `fn debug_enabled(flag: bool, env: Option<OsString>) -> bool`: `TASKLENS_DEBUG=1` gives true, `TASKLENS_DEBUG=0` gives false).
- Manual (record in the commit message): start on the owner machine, window opens, close quits.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: engine start failure text above, exit 1; paths error, exit 1.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: steps 1 to 9 fit the ADR-014 first-frame gate (200 ms warm, 500 ms cold); nothing here blocks on I/O except creating the log and crash directories.
- Privacy: do not log arguments or environment values except the X11 rule line.

## Notes
- Blocked on E33-OI-1 for the exact tl-ui entry point; if E16-A1 lands with a different signature, adapt to it, never add gpui-kit to tl-app.
- U-2 (whether `Application::run` returns on Linux) is handled in E33-011.
- `std::env::set_var` is `unsafe` in edition 2024; it is sound here because no other thread exists yet.
Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`. One commit for this bead, with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`. Read CLAUDE.md first.

title: E33-007 migrations.rs: schema migration chain for both TOML files
description:
## Context
ADR-011 load step 3: a file with a `schema_version` lower than the current one runs `fn migrate_vN_to_vN1(t: &mut toml::Table)` in order before deserializing. The current version is 1 and a missing version counts as 1, so the chain is empty today; this bead builds the mechanism and its tests so later schema changes only add a function. Sources: ADR-011 (Load step 3), APP-033, canonical table (a) (`schema_version = 1`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/migrations.rs`:
```rust
pub type Migration = fn(&mut toml::Table);
/// MIGRATIONS[i] migrates version i+1 to i+2. Empty while SCHEMA_VERSION is 1.
pub const MIGRATIONS: &[Migration] = &[];
pub fn version_of(t: &toml::Table) -> u32;          // schema_version as integer; missing or not an integer >= 1 gives 1
pub fn migrate(t: &mut toml::Table, from: u32) -> u32; // runs MIGRATIONS[from-1 ..] in order, sets t["schema_version"] = SCHEMA_VERSION, returns the new version
```
- `SCHEMA_VERSION` comes from `tl_model::settings::SCHEMA_VERSION` (value 1).
- `version_of`: `schema_version = 0`, negative, or a non-integer value is logged at `warn!` and treated as 1.
- `migrate` with `from >= SCHEMA_VERSION` does nothing except leave the table as is and return `from`.
- Each migration logs `info!` "settings migrated from v{N} to v{N+1}".
- The test module defines a private test-only chain to prove ordering (the public `MIGRATIONS` stays empty).
Add `mod migrations;` to `main.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a table without `schema_version` **When** `version_of` runs **Then** it returns 1.
- **Given** `schema_version = "x"` **When** `version_of` runs **Then** it returns 1 and logs a warning.
- **Given** `schema_version = 1` and the empty chain **When** `migrate(t, 1)` runs **Then** the table is unchanged and 1 is returned.
- **Given** a test chain of two migrations that each append to a list **When** a v1 table is migrated to v3 by the test helper **Then** both ran in order and `schema_version` is 3.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/migrations.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: add `mod migrations;`.

## Tests
- `migrations.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: `missing_version_is_1`, `bad_version_is_1`, `current_version_untouched`, `chain_runs_in_order` (uses `fn migrate_with(t, from, chain: &[Migration], to: u32)`, the private core that `migrate` calls with `MIGRATIONS` and `SCHEMA_VERSION`).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: none surfaced.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: never log table contents.

## Notes
- Small bead; keep `migrate` and `migrate_with` pure so E33-006 can test through it.
Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`. title: E33-008 settings_store.rs save half, atomic.rs re-export and the persist callback
description:
## Context
ADR-011 Save: settings and state are saved 500 ms after the last change and once on exit, through the atomic write in `tl-ops/src/fs.rs` (R-130), re-exported by `tl-app/src/atomic.rs`. tl-ui holds settings and state in GPUI Globals and calls a persist callback that tl-app gives it. A file loaded as newer (read-only) is never written. Sources: ADR-011 (Save, Ownership), APP-033, R-018, R-130, UI-SHL conventions (`TlSettings::update` calls the persist callback).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/atomic.rs`:
```rust
pub use tl_ops::fs::write_atomic;   // write <name>.tmp-<pid>, fsync file, rename, fsync dir (E07-A3)
```
`crates/tl-app/src/settings_store.rs` (save half):
```rust
pub const SAVE_DEBOUNCE: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);
pub struct Store { /* paths, read_only flags, last written bytes per file, pending (Settings, UiState), saver thread handle */ }
impl Store {
    pub fn new(paths: &Paths, settings_ro: bool, state_ro: bool, initial: (Settings, UiState)) -> Store;
    pub fn persist_callback(&self) -> Box<dyn Fn(&Settings, &UiState) + Send + Sync>; // the ADR-011 callback type
    pub fn flush(&self);       // write any pending change now; called on exit
}
fn serialize_settings(s: &Settings) -> String;   // toml::to_string_pretty, schema_version first
fn serialize_state(s: &UiState) -> String;
```
- The callback clones its arguments into the pending slot (a `Mutex<Option<(Settings, UiState)>>`) and wakes the saver thread. The saver thread (named `tasklens-save`, `std::thread`) waits until 500 ms pass with no new call, then for each file: serialize, compare with the last bytes written or loaded; if different and the file is not read-only, call `write_atomic(path, bytes, 0o600)`; on success remember the bytes. Ensure the parent directory with `paths::ensure_dir` first.
- A write error logs `warn!` "Could not save {file name}: {error}" and keeps the pending state, so the next change or `flush` retries.
- `flush` takes the pending value and writes it synchronously on the calling thread, then stops the saver thread. Calls after `flush` are ignored.
- Read-only file: never written, by callback or flush (ADR-011 step 3).
- Saved files start with `schema_version = 1`. Unknown keys from the loaded file are not written back (ADR-011 step 5).
- Only `settings.toml` and `state.toml` are handled here. Theme file writes (`themes.json`) go through the request type in open item E33-OI-4.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** three callback calls 100 ms apart **When** 500 ms pass after the last **Then** `settings.toml` is written once with the last value.
- **Given** a callback call that changes only `UiState` **When** the save runs **Then** only `state.toml` is written.
- **Given** a settings file loaded as newer (read-only) **When** callbacks and `flush` run **Then** `settings.toml` keeps its original bytes.
- **Given** a pending change **When** `flush` runs **Then** the file is written before `flush` returns.
- **Given** an unwritable config dir **When** the save runs **Then** a warning is logged and no panic happens.
- **Given** a crash simulated between the temp write and the rename (test hook in `write_atomic` from E07-A3, or a leftover `settings.toml.tmp-<pid>` file) **When** the store loads again **Then** either the old or the new file is intact.
- **Given** a loaded file with an unknown key **When** any change is saved **Then** the new file does not contain that key.
- **Given** a save **When** the file is inspected **Then** its mode is 0600 and its first line is `schema_version = 1`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/atomic.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/settings_store.rs`: add the save half.
- `crates/tl-app/tests/settings_store.rs`: add save tests.

## Tests
`tests/settings_store.rs`: `debounce_writes_once`, `only_changed_file_written`, `read_only_never_written`, `flush_writes_now`, `write_error_logged_and_retried`, `crash_between_write_and_rename_leaves_intact_file`, `unknown_keys_absent_after_save`, `saved_file_mode_and_header`. Debounce tests use real time with margins (wait 800 ms); keep total under 5 s.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the warning above; no toast (ADR-015: only user-started actions toast).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A

title: E33-009 single_instance.rs: org.freedesktop.Application on the session bus
description:
## Context
tasklens runs once per session. Before GPUI starts, tl-app takes the bus name `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens` with a blocking zbus connection. A second copy forwards its arguments to the first and exits 0. The first copy serves `org.freedesktop.Application` and passes requests to the GPUI main thread as `AppRequest` values. The D-Bus methods accept input from any session client, so parameters are validated. Sources: ADR-010 (Single instance), APP-011, R-047, R-001, R-136, table (c), UI-SHL-112, U-6.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/single_instance.rs`:
```rust
pub const BUS_NAME: &str = "io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens";
pub const OBJECT_PATH: &str = "/io/github/oysteinkrog/Tasklens";
pub enum Outcome {
    Primary { conn: zbus::blocking::Connection, requests: async_channel::Receiver<AppRequest> },
    Forwarded,          // caller exits 0
    NoBus,              // caller runs without single instance
}
pub struct Forward { pub tab: Option<Tab>, pub select_pid: Option<u32> }
pub fn acquire(forward: &Forward, activation_token: Option<String>) -> Outcome;
struct AppIface { tx: async_channel::Sender<AppRequest> }   // #[zbus::interface(name = "org.freedesktop.Application")]
```
Behaviour (ADR-010):
1. `zbus::blocking::Connection::session()`. Error: `warn!` "Session bus unavailable; running without single instance" and return `NoBus`. No lock-file fallback.
2. `request_name_with_flags(BUS_NAME, RequestNameFlags::DoNotQueue)`. Reply `Exists` or a `NameTaken` error means another copy runs:
   - Call `org.freedesktop.Application.Activate(platform_data)` on `OBJECT_PATH` with `platform_data = {"activation-token": <XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN>}` when the env var is set, else an empty dict.
   - Then, if `forward.tab` is set, `ActivateAction("tab", [<tab name string>], platform_data)`; if `forward.select_pid` is set, `ActivateAction("select-pid", [<uint32>], platform_data)`. Tab names: `processes`, `performance`, `services`, `startup`, `connections`, `information`.
   - `--start-minimized` is not forwarded (APP-011).
   - Each call uses a 2 s timeout; a failure is logged at `warn!` and the copy still exits 0. Return `Forwarded`.
3. Name owned: serve `AppIface` at `OBJECT_PATH` on the same connection (zbus internal executor thread, ADR-002 executor rule), with an `async_channel::bounded(4)` channel:
   - `Activate(platform_data: a{sv})`: read `activation-token` if it is a string of at most 256 bytes; send `AppRequest::Activate { token }`.
   - `Open(uris: as, platform_data: a{sv})`: return the D-Bus error `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.NotSupported` with message "tasklens does not open files".
   - `ActivateAction(name: s, parameter: av, platform_data: a{sv})`: `quit` with no parameter sends `AppRequest::Quit`; `tab` with exactly one string that is one of the six tab names sends `AppRequest::Activate { token }` then `AppRequest::SelectTab(tab)`; `select-pid` with exactly one `u32` greater than 0 sends `Activate` then `AppRequest::SelectPid(pid)`. Any other name, parameter count or type returns `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.InvalidArgs` with message "unknown action or bad parameter" and sends nothing.
   - Sending uses `try_send`; a full channel drops the request with `debug!` (the UI is busy; four requests are queued).
   - Return `Primary { conn, requests }`; `main` keeps `conn` alive until exit.
- Logs record method names only, never `platform_data` contents.
`crates/tl-app/tests/real_single_instance.rs` (`#[ignore]`, owner machine):
- `second_instance_forwards_and_exits`: start the built `tasklens` binary (test build path from `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_tasklens")`), wait for the bus name, start a second copy with `--tab services`, assert it exits 0 within 1 s, and that the first logs the received `Activate` (ADR-010 Verification).
Add `mod single_instance;` to `main.rs` (the call is wired in E33-A2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** no other copy **When** `acquire` runs **Then** it returns `Primary` and the name is owned.
- **Given** a primary copy **When** a second calls `acquire` with `tab = services` **Then** the primary receives `Activate` then `SelectTab(Services)`, and the second gets `Forwarded`.
- **Given** a primary copy **When** a client calls `ActivateAction("select-pid", [0])` **Then** it gets `InvalidArgs` and nothing is sent.
- **Given** a primary copy **When** a client calls `ActivateAction("tab", ["nowhere"])` **Then** it gets `InvalidArgs`.
- **Given** a primary copy **When** a client calls `Open(["file:///x"], {})` **Then** it gets `NotSupported`.
- **Given** a primary copy **When** a client calls `ActivateAction("quit", [])` **Then** `AppRequest::Quit` is received.
- **Given** an activation token of 300 bytes **When** `Activate` is called **Then** `AppRequest::Activate { token: None }` is sent.
- **Given** five rapid `Activate` calls and no receiver progress **When** they arrive **Then** four are queued and the fifth is dropped without error to the caller.
- **Given** no session bus (`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/nonexistent`) **When** `acquire` runs **Then** it returns `NoBus`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/single_instance.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: add `mod single_instance;`.
- `crates/tl-app/tests/real_single_instance.rs`: create.

## Tests
- `single_instance.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (pure parameter validation, no bus): `parse_tab_action`, `parse_select_pid_action`, `reject_zero_pid`, `reject_wrong_type`, `reject_unknown_action`, `token_length_limit`. Put the validation in `fn parse_action(name: &str, params: &[OwnedValue]) -> Result<Vec<AppRequest>, ActionErr>` so it is testable.
- `tests/real_single_instance.rs::second_instance_forwards_and_exits` (`#[ignore]`), `tests/real_single_instance.rs::interface_methods` (`#[ignore]`: owns a private test name `io.github.oysteinkrog.TasklensTest` through a `name` parameter on an internal `acquire_named` function, then calls each method with `busctl`-equivalent zbus proxy calls and checks the replies listed above).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the D-Bus error names and messages above; warnings for no bus and forward failures.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: runs once before GPUI; the bus calls are bounded by the 2 s timeout.
- Privacy: never log `platform_data` or tokens.

## Notes
- Security: every D-Bus input is untrusted. Validate before sending; the regression tests are the reject cases above.
- On Wayland, activation may only flash the taskbar entry; that is accepted (U-6).
- `async_channel` dependency: open item E33-OI-3.

title: E33-010 notify.rs: desktop notifications through org.freedesktop.Notifications
description:
## Context
Some failures happen when no GPUI window can show a toast: a panic on the main thread, a renderer that cannot start, a lost graphics device. tl-app sends these as desktop notifications through `org.freedesktop.Notifications.Notify` on its own blocking zbus connection, which works without a window. Sources: UI-SHL-114, APP-055, ADR-015 (Crash handling), R-049.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/notify.rs`:
```rust
pub enum Fatal { Crashed, RendererFailed, DeviceLost }
impl Fatal { pub fn text(self) -> &'static str; }
pub fn send(kind: Fatal);   // blocking, best effort, at most 1 s
```
- Texts, exact (UI-SHL-114):
  - `Crashed`: "tasklens stopped after an unrecoverable error."
  - `RendererFailed`: "tasklens could not start the renderer"
  - `DeviceLost`: "tasklens lost the graphics device and must restart"
- Call: `org.freedesktop.Notifications` at `/org/freedesktop/Notifications`, method `Notify(app_name: s = "tasklens", replaces_id: u = 0, app_icon: s = "io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens", summary: s = <text>, body: s = "", actions: as = [], hints: a{sv} = {"desktop-entry": "io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens", "urgency": byte 2}, expire_timeout: i = -1)`.
- Opens a fresh `zbus::blocking::Connection::session()` per call (it runs rarely, possibly from a panic hook). Every error is logged at `warn!` and swallowed. The method call uses a 1 s timeout.
- Must be safe to call from the panic hook: no panics, no locks shared with the GPUI thread.
Add `mod notify;` to `main.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `Fatal::Crashed` **When** `text()` is read **Then** it is "tasklens stopped after an unrecoverable error."
- **Given** `Fatal::RendererFailed` **When** `text()` is read **Then** it is "tasklens could not start the renderer".
- **Given** `Fatal::DeviceLost` **When** `text()` is read **Then** it is "tasklens lost the graphics device and must restart".
- **Given** no session bus **When** `send` runs **Then** it returns within 1 s without panicking.
- **Given** a running notification server **When** `send(Fatal::Crashed)` runs **Then** a notification with that summary appears.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/notify.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: add `mod notify;`.

## Tests
- `notify.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: `texts_exact` (all three), `no_bus_is_silent` (sets `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/nonexistent` in a child process via `std::process::Command` on the test binary with a filter, or tests the inner `fn send_on(conn_result)` with an `Err`), `hints_fields` (the hint map built by `fn hints() -> HashMap<&str, Value>` has `desktop-entry` and `urgency` 2).
- Manual on the owner machine: a notification appears.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: swallowed and logged.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: off the hot path.
- Privacy: no process data in notifications.

## Notes
- Urgency 2 is "critical" in the freedesktop spec; the docs call these fatal errors, so critical is the matching level (inferred, not stated in the docs; see open item E33-OI-7).

title: E33-011 main.rs: engine shutdown in 1500 ms after the UI stops (U-2)
description:
## Context
After GPUI stops, `main` calls `EngineHandle::shutdown(Duration::from_millis(1500))`, then flushes logs, then exits (ADR-010 Close behaviour). Whether `Application::run` returns on Linux after `cx.quit()` is unverified (U-2), so the same steps also run from the quit hook if it does not. If the engine shutdown reports a timeout, `tl-app` exits at once without running destructors (ADR-004 Shutdown step 5). Sources: ADR-010 (Close behaviour), ADR-004 (Shutdown), APP-047, U-2, ADR-010 Verification ("process exits within 2 s and tl-gpu-probe is gone").

## Deliverable
Changes to `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`:
```rust
fn finish(engine: tl_engine::EngineHandle, store: &settings_store::Store, log: logging::LogGuard) -> !;
```
- Order: (1) `store.flush()`; (2) `let report = engine.shutdown(Duration::from_millis(1500));` (3) if the report says the drain or runtime shutdown timed out (field names from E09-A2's `ShutdownReport`), log `warn!(target: "tasklens::engine", "engine shutdown timed out")`, drop `log` to flush the file, and call `std::process::exit(0)`; (4) otherwise drop `log` and `std::process::exit(0)`.
- U-2 handling: the engine handle and store live in an `Arc<Mutex<Option<ExitParts>>>` shared with the quit hook that the tl-ui entry accepts (`on_quit: Box<dyn FnOnce() + Send>`, part of E33-OI-1). Whichever runs first (the return of the tl-ui entry, or the quit hook) takes the parts and calls `finish`; the other finds `None` and does nothing.
- Log once at `info!(target: "tasklens::engine")` which path ran: "shutdown after run returned" or "shutdown from quit hook". Record the result for U-2 in the commit message.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** tasklens with all sources running **When** the main window closes (no tray) **Then** the process exits within 2 s and no `tl-gpu-probe` process remains.
- **Given** a shutdown report with a timeout **When** `finish` runs **Then** the warning is logged and the exit code is 0.
- **Given** both the quit hook and the run return happen **When** they race **Then** `finish` runs exactly once.
- **Given** a pending settings change **When** tasklens quits **Then** the change is on disk.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: `finish`, the shared exit parts, the two call sites.

## Tests
- `main.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests::finish_runs_once`: a pure `ExitOnce` helper (`fn take(&self) -> Option<T>`) returns `Some` once and `None` after, from two threads.
- Manual on the owner machine (record in the commit message): close the window, measure exit time with `time`, check `pgrep tl-gpu-probe` is empty, record which path ran (U-2).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: timeout warning only.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: exit within 2 s total.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Do not call `std::process::exit` before the log guard is dropped; the non-blocking writer loses lines otherwise.
- Blocked on E33-OI-1 for the quit hook field.

title: E33-012 main.rs: renderer start failure notice and exit 1; device-loss relaunch once
description:
## Context
If GPUI cannot start its renderer, tasklens prints "tasklens could not start the renderer" to stderr, sends the same desktop notification and exits 1. If the graphics device is lost and GPUI cannot recover, tasklens sends "tasklens lost the graphics device and must restart" and relaunches itself once. Sources: APP-055, UI-SHL-114, ADR-015 (Crash handling), R-049.

## Deliverable
Changes to `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`:
- The tl-ui entry returns a result that distinguishes a renderer start failure and a device loss (exact form per open item E33-OI-1; recommended `enum UiExit { Quit, RendererFailed(String), DeviceLost }`).
- `RendererFailed(msg)`: `error!(target: "tasklens::ui", "renderer start failed: {msg}")`, `eprintln!("tasklens could not start the renderer")`, `notify::send(Fatal::RendererFailed)`, then the normal `finish` steps with exit code 1 instead of 0.
- `DeviceLost`: `notify::send(Fatal::DeviceLost)`, then `finish`, then relaunch: `std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe())` with the same arguments minus `--start-minimized`, and the environment variable `TASKLENS_RELAUNCHED=1`. If `TASKLENS_RELAUNCHED=1` is already set in this process, do not relaunch again (one automatic relaunch, ADR-015). `TASKLENS_RELAUNCHED` is not in table (c); see open item E33-OI-8.
- The relaunch spawns and does not wait; the parent then exits 0.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a tl-ui entry that returns `RendererFailed` (test build) **When** `main` handles it **Then** stderr has "tasklens could not start the renderer", the notification is sent and the exit code is 1.
- **Given** `DeviceLost` and no `TASKLENS_RELAUNCHED` **When** `main` handles it **Then** a new tasklens process starts with `TASKLENS_RELAUNCHED=1`.
- **Given** `DeviceLost` and `TASKLENS_RELAUNCHED=1` **When** `main` handles it **Then** no new process starts.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: the two arms and a pure helper `fn relaunch_args(args: &[OsString]) -> Vec<OsString>` (drops `--start-minimized` and argv[0]).

- Accessibility: N/A

title: E33-014 autostart.rs: Start at login entry written or removed from settings
description:
## Context
"Start at login" (`startup.start_at_login`) writes an XDG autostart entry; turning it off deletes it. "Start minimized" (`startup.start_minimized`) adds `--start-minimized` to it. The entry then shows in the Startup Apps tab like any other. tl-app learns of setting changes through the persist callback, the only channel from tl-ui to tl-app (ADR-011 Ownership). Sources: APP-048, table (c) (autostart path), canonical table (a) `[startup]`, ADR-011 (write_atomic), R-130.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/autostart.rs`:
```rust
pub fn entry_text(start_minimized: bool) -> String;
pub fn apply(path: &Path, start_at_login: bool, start_minimized: bool) -> io::Result<Change>;
pub enum Change { Written, Removed, Unchanged }
```
- Path: `paths.autostart_file()` = `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autostart/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop` (directory created with `create_dir_all` if missing; the `autostart` directory is shared with other apps, so do not chmod it).
- `entry_text`, exact:
  ```
  [Desktop Entry]
  Type=Application
  Name=tasklens
  Exec=tasklens
  Icon=io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens
  X-KDE-autostart-phase=2
  ```
  with `Exec=tasklens --start-minimized` when `start_minimized` is true. `Exec` and `X-KDE-autostart-phase=2` come from APP-048; `Type`, `Name` and `Icon` follow the desktop file (E33-013, open item E33-OI-9).
- `apply`: `start_at_login = true` writes the text with `write_atomic(path, bytes, 0o644)` only when the file is missing or its content differs (`Unchanged` otherwise). `false` removes the file if it exists (`Removed`), else `Unchanged`.
- Wiring in `settings_store.rs`: the saver thread, after writing `settings.toml`, compares the new `startup.start_at_login` and `startup.start_minimized` with the values it last applied and calls `autostart::apply` when either changed. Errors log `warn!` "Could not update the autostart entry: {error}". At start, `apply` is not called (a missing file with the setting on is left alone until the user changes it; the Startup Apps tab shows the real state).
- Read-only settings (newer file) do not block `apply`; the autostart entry is not the settings file.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the setting turned on **When** the save runs **Then** the autostart file exists with `Exec=tasklens` and `X-KDE-autostart-phase=2`.
- **Given** both settings on **When** the save runs **Then** `Exec=tasklens --start-minimized`.
- **Given** the setting turned off **When** the save runs **Then** the file is gone.
- **Given** an unchanged setting **When** other settings change **Then** the autostart file is not rewritten (mtime unchanged).
- **Given** an unwritable autostart directory **When** the save runs **Then** a warning is logged and `settings.toml` is still saved.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/autostart.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/settings_store.rs`: call `apply` on change.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: add `mod autostart;`.

## Tests

- `tests/settings_store.rs::autostart_follows_setting`: toggling through the persist callback writes and removes the entry.

- Validity: N/A

title: E33-016 rendering_env.rs: rendering.gpu sets ZED_DEVICE_ID or software rendering
description:
## Context
In P4 the setting `rendering.gpu` picks the GPU GPUI renders on. It acts before GPUI starts, by setting environment variables, and a `ZED_DEVICE_ID` already set by the user always wins. Before P4 tasklens never sets `ZED_DEVICE_ID`. Changing the setting needs a restart (the Settings window shows "Restart tasklens to use the new GPU", E21). Sources: APP-046, R-070, ADR-010 (GPU selection), canonical table (a) `[rendering] gpu = "auto"  # auto | software | pci:<bus id>`, UI-SHL-110 step 3.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/rendering_env.rs`:
```rust
pub fn env_for(gpu: &str, user_zed_device_id: Option<&OsStr>, read_device_id: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<u16>) -> Vec<(&'static str, String)>;
pub fn pci_device_id(bus_id: &str) -> Option<u16>;  // reads /sys/bus/pci/devices/<bus id>/device, e.g. "0x2684"
```
- `"auto"`: no variables.
- `"pci:<bus id>"`: if `user_zed_device_id` is set, no variables (user wins, R-070). Else read the device id and return `[("ZED_DEVICE_ID", format!("0x{:04x}", id))]`. If the bus id has characters outside `[0-9a-fA-F:.]` or the device file is missing, return no variables and log `warn!` "Rendering GPU {bus id} not found; using the default".
- `"software"`: `[("WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME", "llvmpipe"), ("VK_ICD_FILENAMES", <lavapipe ICD path>)]`; the path is open item E33-OI-11 (recommended `/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/lvp_icd.x86_64.json`, the Arch `vulkan-swrast` path). Applies even when the user set `ZED_DEVICE_ID` (only `ZED_DEVICE_ID` itself is protected by R-070).
- Any other value: no variables, `warn!` "Unknown rendering.gpu value; using the default".
- In `main.rs` step 3 (after the X11 rule, before any thread starts): compute with the loaded settings and set each pair with `unsafe { std::env::set_var }`, which is allowed only in `main.rs` (ADR-001 rule 4). This needs `settings.toml` loaded before step 3: move the settings load (not the state load) ahead of the environment step; single instance (step 4) does not depend on the order.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `gpu = "auto"` **When** `env_for` runs **Then** it returns no variables.
- **Given** `gpu = "pci:0000:01:00.0"` and device id 0x2684 **When** `env_for` runs **Then** it returns `ZED_DEVICE_ID=0x2684`.
- **Given** the same and a user `ZED_DEVICE_ID=0x1234` **When** `env_for` runs **Then** it returns no variables.
- **Given** `gpu = "pci:../../etc"` **When** `env_for` runs **Then** it returns no variables and logs the warning.
- **Given** `gpu = "software"` **When** `env_for` runs **Then** it returns `WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME=llvmpipe` and `VK_ICD_FILENAMES`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/rendering_env.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: `mod rendering_env;`, the step 3 call, settings load order.

## Tests
- `rendering_env.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: `auto_none`, `pci_sets_device_id`, `user_value_wins`, `bad_bus_id_rejected`, `software_sets_both`, `unknown_value_none`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: warnings above; the app always starts.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one small sysfs read at start.
- Privacy: N/A

title: E33-A2 Settings store
description:
## Context
Anchor bead E33-A2. `main.rs` gains UI-SHL-110 steps 4 and 5: single instance before anything else that is slow, then loading `settings.toml`, `state.toml` and `themes.json`, building the store and its persist callback, and handing the settings, the queued notices and the `AppRequest` receiver to tl-ui. It also wires the main-thread panic notification. After this bead, settings persist between runs. Sources: UI-SHL-110 steps 4, 5 and 11, UI-SHL-112, ADR-010 (Single instance), ADR-011 (Load, Save, Ownership), APP-011, APP-033, APP-055, R-047, R-136.

## Deliverable
Changes to `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs` only:
- Step 1: `crash::install_hook(..., on_main_thread_panic = main_panic_notify)` where `fn main_panic_notify() { notify::send(notify::Fatal::Crashed) }`.
- Step 4 (after the X11 rule, before loading files): `let forward = Forward { tab: args.tab.map(TabArg::to_model), select_pid: args.select_pid };` and `match single_instance::acquire(&forward, std::env::var("XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN").ok())`:
  - `Forwarded`: `info!` "another tasklens is running; forwarded" and return `ExitCode::SUCCESS` (exit 0).
  - `NoBus`: continue with `app_requests = None`.
  - `Primary { conn, requests }`: keep `conn` alive as a local until the end of `main`; `app_requests = Some(requests)`.
- Step 5: `let now = unix seconds; let s = settings_store::load_settings(&paths.settings_file(), now); let st = settings_store::load_state(&paths.state_file(), now);` Build `Store::new(&paths, s.read_only, st.read_only, (s.value.clone(), st.value.clone()))`. Collect `queued_toasts: Vec<String>` from both `notices` (`toast_text()`), in the order settings then state. `themes.json` is read as raw bytes (`Option<Vec<u8>>`, `None` if missing) and passed to tl-ui, which parses it (UI-FND-042); see open item E33-OI-4 for the write path.
- Step 7: the engine starts with `EngineSettings` derived from the loaded `Settings`.
- Steps 8 to 10: pass to the tl-ui entry (E33-OI-1): `settings = s.value`, `state = st.value`, `persist = Some(store.persist_callback())`, `app_requests`, `queued_toasts`, `themes_json`. tl-ui shows the queued toasts after the first frame (UI-SHL-110 step 11).
- After the tl-ui entry returns: `store.flush()` before anything else on exit (ADR-011 "plus on exit").

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a running tasklens **When** `tasklens --tab services` is started **Then** the second process exits 0 within 1 s and the first shows its window on the Services tab.
- **Given** no session bus **When** tasklens starts **Then** it logs "Session bus unavailable; running without single instance" and opens its window.
- **Given** the user changes the refresh interval and quits within 200 ms **When** tasklens starts again **Then** the new interval is loaded (flush on exit).
- **Given** a corrupt `settings.toml` **When** tasklens starts **Then** the window opens with defaults and, after the first frame, the toast "Settings file was unreadable and has been reset. The old file was kept as settings.toml.corrupt-<t>" shows.
- **Given** a newer `state.toml` **When** tasklens runs and the window is resized **Then** `state.toml` is not modified.
- **Given** a panic on the main thread **When** the hook runs **Then** the notification "tasklens stopped after an unrecoverable error." is sent and a crash report is written.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: steps 4 and 5, flush on exit, panic notify wiring.

## Tests
- `tests/real_single_instance.rs::second_instance_forwards_and_exits` (from E33-009) now passes end to end (`#[ignore]`, owner machine).
- `main.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests::queued_toast_order`: a pure helper `fn queued_toasts(s: &[LoadNotice], st: &[LoadNotice]) -> Vec<String>` returns settings notices before state notices.
- Manual: restart keeps settings; corrupt file toast appears after the first frame.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as in E33-006 and E33-009.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: single instance and both loads fit in the 200 ms warm first-frame budget (ADR-014); the bus round trip is about 1 ms.
- Privacy: never log settings contents.

title: E33-017 kglobalaccel.rs: Open with Ctrl+Esc through KDE kglobalaccel (verify U-16)
description:
## Context
Settings > Startup and window > "Open with Ctrl+Esc" makes KDE's Ctrl+Esc open tasklens instead of Plasma System Monitor; off restores the KDE default. There is no settings key: the check state is read from kglobalaccel. Whether `setForeignShortcutKeys` sticks for a `.desktop` launch component that is not running is unverified (U-16); the fallback edits `kglobalshortcutsrc`. Sources: APP-051, R-080, U-16.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/kglobalaccel.rs` (blocking zbus on the session bus, service `org.kde.kglobalaccel`, object `/kglobalaccel`):
```rust
pub fn is_enabled() -> Result<bool, KgaError>;     // tasklens _launch currently bound to Ctrl+Esc
pub fn set_enabled(on: bool) -> Result<Applied, KgaError>;
pub enum Applied { Live, NeedsRelogin }
```
- On: register component `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop` action `_launch` with key Ctrl+Esc and set `org.kde.plasma-systemmonitor.desktop` `_launch` to no key, using `setForeignShortcutKeys`.
- Off: set tasklens `_launch` to no key and restore `org.kde.plasma-systemmonitor.desktop` `_launch` to Ctrl+Esc.
- U-16 check inside `set_enabled`: after the call, read the shortcut back; if it did not stick, write `~/.config/kglobalshortcutsrc` group `[services][io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop]` key `_launch=Ctrl+Esc` (or remove the key when off) and return `NeedsRelogin`; the UI then asks the user to log out and back in (R-080; the UI text is E21's).
- Errors: no bus or no kglobalaccel gives `KgaError::Unavailable`; the UI hides or disables the item.
- How the Settings window (tl-ui) reaches this module is open item E33-OI-12.
- The exact kglobalaccel method signatures (`setForeignShortcutKeys(as actionId, a(ai) keys)` in Plasma 6, key encoding of Ctrl+Esc as a Qt key code) must be read from the KDE `kglobalaccel` sources before coding; record the file and line in the commit message.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** Plasma 6 and the option turned on **When** Ctrl+Esc is pressed **Then** tasklens opens.
- **Given** the option turned off **When** Ctrl+Esc is pressed **Then** Plasma System Monitor opens.
- **Given** `setForeignShortcutKeys` did not stick **When** `set_enabled(true)` returns **Then** it is `NeedsRelogin` and `kglobalshortcutsrc` has the `_launch=Ctrl+Esc` line under `[services][io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop]`.
- **Given** no kglobalaccel service **When** `is_enabled` runs **Then** it returns `Unavailable`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/kglobalaccel.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: `mod kglobalaccel;`.

## Tests
- `kglobalaccel.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: `rc_fallback_writes_line` and `rc_fallback_removes_line` (pure function over the INI text; keeps every other line and group unchanged).
- Manual on Plasma 6, recorded for U-16 in the commit message: on, press Ctrl+Esc, off, press again; also with tasklens not running.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `Unavailable`; logged at `warn!`.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: Ctrl+Esc is a global shortcut; no in-app focus impact.
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Write `kglobalshortcutsrc` with `write_atomic` and keep the user's other shortcuts byte for byte.

title: E33-018 import_ts.rs: import TaskSlinger UserSettings.ini into settings
description:
## Context
Settings > Advanced > "Import from TaskSlinger…" lets the owner bring over TaskSlinger settings from `UserSettings.ini` (TaskSlinger runs under Wine). This bead is the settings half: parse the INI and map its keys onto `Settings` and `UiState` with the APP-032 origin table. The themes half (`themes.json`) is E17's. The INI comes from a file the user picks, so it is untrusted input. Sources: APP-034, APP-032 (origin table), ADR-011.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/import_ts.rs`:
```rust
pub struct ImportResult { pub settings: Settings, pub state: UiState, pub imported: usize, pub skipped: Vec<String> }
pub fn parse_ini(text: &str) -> Vec<(String /*section*/, String /*key*/, String /*value*/)>;
pub fn import(text: &str, base: (&Settings, &UiState)) -> ImportResult;
```
- `parse_ini`: `[Section]` headers, `key=value` lines, `;` and `#` comments, trims whitespace, accepts CRLF, ignores lines without `=`. Input above 1 MiB is rejected before parsing ("File is too large to be a TaskSlinger settings file"). Invalid UTF-8 is decoded with `from_utf8_lossy`.
- Mapping: one row per APP-032 origin with a TaskSlinger source, for example `DefaultTab` to `general.start_tab`, `UIScale` to `appearance.ui_scale_pct`, `RowHeightPct` to `appearance.row_height_pct`, `AnimationsEnabled` to `motion.animations`, `SmoothGraphs` to `motion.smooth_graphs`, `RefreshIntervalMs` to `processes.interval_ms`, `HighlightNewExitedProcesses` to `processes.highlight_new_exited`, `HideMicrosoftProcesses` to `processes.hide_system`, `CloseToTray`, `MinimizeToTray`, `AlwaysShowTrayIcon` to `tray.*`, `StartWithWindows` and `StartMinimized` to `startup.*`, `Window.Width`, `Window.Height`, `Window.Maximized` to state `[window]`, and every other TS row of the APP-032 table. The INI section names and value encodings (for example whether `DefaultTab` is a number or a name, and the `UIScale` format) are not in the docs: open item E33-OI-13. Until resolved, implement only keys whose value is a plain `true`/`false` or a decimal integer in the target range, and add the rest when the leader supplies the encodings.
- Values are clamped with the same clamp as loading (E33-006). A key that is unknown, unparseable or out of the mapping goes to `skipped` with its `section.key` name.
- `imported` counts mapped keys. The UI toast "Imported N settings and M themes" (APP-034) is built by the caller with N = `imported` and M from the theme half.
- The file chooser portal call and the trigger from the Settings window are not decided: open item E33-OI-12.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** an INI with `AnimationsEnabled=false` **When** imported **Then** `motion.animations == false` and `imported == 1`.
- **Given** `RefreshIntervalMs=50` **When** imported **Then** `processes.interval_ms == 250` (clamped).
- **Given** `Window.X=100` **When** imported **Then** it is in `skipped` (position is not restored, APP-032).
- **Given** a 2 MiB file **When** imported **Then** it is rejected with "File is too large to be a TaskSlinger settings file".
- **Given** binary garbage **When** imported **Then** the result has `imported == 0` and no panic.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/import_ts.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: `mod import_ts;`.

## Tests
- `import_ts.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: `parse_sections_and_comments`, `crlf_accepted`, `bool_key_mapped`, `int_key_clamped`, `position_skipped`, `too_large_rejected`, plus a proptest `never_panics_on_arbitrary_bytes` (proptest is a workspace dev-dependency; add it to tl-app `[dev-dependencies]`).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the size error text above.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: do not log INI values; log only skipped key names at `debug!`.

## Notes
- Security: untrusted input; the size cap and the fuzz-style proptest are the regression tests.

title: E33-019 --app-id: separate instance and settings directory for development builds
description:
## Context
`--app-id <reverse-dns id>` runs a separate instance with its own settings directory, for development builds next to an installed tasklens (APP-052, taken from Mission Center). title: E33-A3 Packaging
description:
## Context
Anchor bead E33-A3. An Arch `PKGBUILD` builds the workspace in release mode and installs the binaries, the desktop file and the app icon to the paths in table (c). Later phases add their own install lines through E33 beads (E33-015 for P3). `tasklens --version` proves the installed binary runs. Sources: table (c) (Binaries and scripts, Identity), ADR-002 (Build and run packages, profiles, release without `bench`), APP-050 (pacman installs binary, desktop file, icon, policy), APP-052 (`--version`).

## Deliverable
`packaging/PKGBUILD`:
- `pkgname=tasklens`, `arch=('x86_64')`.
- `makedepends=('base-devel' 'clang' 'pkgconf' 'rustup')`, with the toolchain from `rust-toolchain.toml` (E02).
- `depends=('wayland' 'libxkbcommon' 'libxkbcommon-x11' 'libxcb' 'fontconfig' 'vulkan-icd-loader')` (ADR-002). `nvidia-utils` goes in `optdepends=('nvidia-utils: NVIDIA GPU monitoring')` because tl-gpu-probe loads NVML at run time and handles its absence (ADR-007); see open item E33-OI-10.
- `build()`: `cargo build --release --locked --workspace` from the repo root; no `--features bench` (ADR-002).
- `check()`: `cargo test --release --locked --workspace` (no `--ignored`).
- `package()` installs:
  - `target/release/tasklens` to `$pkgdir/usr/bin/tasklens`, mode 0755.
  - `target/release/tl-gpu-probe` to `$pkgdir/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-gpu-probe`, mode 0755.
  - `packaging/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop` to `$pkgdir/usr/share/applications/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop`, mode 0644.
  - `assets/icons/tasklens.svg` (E15) to `$pkgdir/usr/share/icons/hicolor/scalable/apps/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.svg`, mode 0644 (icon path per open item E33-OI-9).
- `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `url`, `license` and `source` are not decided in the docs (open item E33-OI-10). Until decided, use `pkgver=0.1.0`, `pkgrel=1`, and a local source (`source=()`, build from `$startdir/..`), which matches the localbuilds style of building from a checkout.
- Release builds use the workspace `release` profile unchanged (`panic = "unwind"`, `lto = "fat"`, `debug = "line-tables-only"`, `strip = "none"`); set `options=('!strip')` so makepkg does not strip the line tables needed for crash backtraces.

- **Given** a clean checkout **When** `makepkg -f` runs in `packaging/` **Then** a package builds and `namcap` reports no errors.
- **Given** the installed package **When** `tasklens --version` runs **Then** it prints `tasklens 0.1.0` and exits 0.
- **Given** the installed package **When** the file list is checked **Then** it contains exactly `/usr/bin/tasklens`, `/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-gpu-probe`, the desktop file and the icon.
- **Given** the built `tasklens` **When** `strings` is searched for `bench` scene names **Then** the bench module is absent (built without `bench`).

title: E33-001 tl-app Cargo.toml dependencies, bench feature and build.rs git hash
description:
## Context
E02-A1 creates `crates/tl-app` as a skeleton with an empty `main.rs`. This bead gives the crate its real manifest: the binary name `tasklens`, the workspace dependencies ADR-001 allows for `tl-app`, the `bench` feature (ADR-002), and a `build.rs` that records the git short hash for the crash report (ADR-015) and the About window (APP-053). Sources: ADR-001 (allowed row), ADR-002 (pins, `bench` feature), ADR-015, APP-053, R-130.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/Cargo.toml`:
- `[package] name = "tasklens"`, `edition` and `rust-version` inherited from the workspace as E02-A1 set them, `build = "build.rs"`.
- `[[bin]] name = "tasklens"`, `path = "src/main.rs"`.
- `[lints] workspace = true`.
- `[dependencies]` (all `{ workspace = true }` or path deps): `tl-model`, `tl-engine`, `tl-ui`, `tl-ops` (for `write_atomic`, R-130), `zbus`, `toml`, `serde`, `anyhow`, `tracing`, `tracing-subscriber`, `tracing-appender`, `rustix`. Plus the argument parser and the channel crate named by the leader's answer to open items E33-OI-2 and E33-OI-3 (recommended: `clap` with `derive`, and `async-channel`). Nothing else: `xtask check-deps` (E02-A2) fails on any dependency outside the tl-app row.
- `[dev-dependencies]`: `tempfile = { workspace = true }`.
- `[features] bench = ["tl-ui/bench"]` (ADR-002). Release builds do not enable it.
`crates/tl-app/build.rs`:
- Runs `git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD` in `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`; on success emits `cargo:rustc-env=TASKLENS_GIT_SHA=<hash>`, on any failure (no git, not a checkout, as in a PKGBUILD tarball build) emits `TASKLENS_GIT_SHA=unknown`.
- Emits `cargo:rerun-if-changed=../../.git/HEAD` and `cargo:rerun-if-changed=../../.git/refs` only when those paths exist.
- Uses only `std` (no build-dependencies).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a git checkout **When** the crate builds **Then** `env!("TASKLENS_GIT_SHA")` is a 12-character hex string.
- **Given** a source tree without `.git` **When** the crate builds **Then** the build succeeds and `TASKLENS_GIT_SHA` is `unknown`.
- **Given** the finished manifest **When** `cargo xtask check-deps` runs (once E02-A2 exists) **Then** it reports no violation for `tasklens`.
- **Given** `cargo build -p tasklens --features bench` **When** it runs **Then** `tl-ui/bench` is enabled.

- `crates/tl-app/build.rs`: create.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: build.rs never fails the build.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: the git hash is not sensitive.

## Notes
- E33-OI-2 (argument parser not in ADR-001 or ADR-002) and E33-OI-3 (`async-channel` not in the tl-app row) must be resolved before this bead starts; add exactly what the leader decides.

title: E33-002 paths.rs: XDG path resolution with fallbacks and 0700/0600 modes
description:
## Context
Every tasklens file lives under one of three XDG roots (ADR-011, table (c)). `paths.rs` resolves them by hand (no `directories` crate, ADR-002) and creates directories with mode 0700. Logging, crash reports, the settings store and the autostart writer all take their paths from here. Sources: ADR-011 (paths table), table (c) XDG paths, R-018, APP-033.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/paths.rs`:
```rust
pub struct Paths {
    pub config_dir: PathBuf,   // $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tasklens
    pub state_dir: PathBuf,    // $XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens
    pub cache_dir: PathBuf,    // $XDG_CACHE_HOME/tasklens
    pub home: PathBuf,
}
impl Paths {
    pub fn from_env() -> anyhow::Result<Paths>;          // reads the process environment
    pub fn from_vars(get: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<OsString>) -> anyhow::Result<Paths>; // testable core
    pub fn settings_file(&self) -> PathBuf;   // config_dir/settings.toml
    pub fn themes_file(&self) -> PathBuf;     // config_dir/themes.json
    pub fn state_file(&self) -> PathBuf;      // state_dir/state.toml
    pub fn logs_dir(&self) -> PathBuf;        // state_dir/logs
    pub fn crash_dir(&self) -> PathBuf;       // state_dir/crash
    pub fn history_dir(&self) -> PathBuf;     // state_dir/history
    pub fn dumps_dir(&self) -> PathBuf;       // state_dir/dumps
    pub fn run_history_file(&self) -> PathBuf;// state_dir/run-history.json
    pub fn icon_cache_file(&self) -> PathBuf; // cache_dir/icons.toml
    pub fn autostart_file(&self) -> PathBuf;  // $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autostart/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop
}
pub fn ensure_dir(path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<()>; // create_dir_all, then chmod 0700 on each directory it created
pub const FILE_MODE: u32 = 0o600;
pub const DIR_MODE: u32 = 0o700;
```
Rules (ADR-011): for each of `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, a value that is unset, empty or not absolute falls back to `$HOME/.config`, `$HOME/.local/state`, `$HOME/.cache`. `HOME` unset, empty or not absolute is an error: "HOME is not set to an absolute path". `autostart_file` uses the same resolved `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` root (not the `tasklens` subdirectory). `ensure_dir` does not change the mode of a directory that already existed.
Add `mod paths;` to `main.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/x/cfg` **When** `from_vars` runs **Then** `settings_file()` is `/x/cfg/tasklens/settings.toml`.
- **Given** `XDG_STATE_HOME` unset and `HOME=/home/u` **When** `from_vars` runs **Then** `state_file()` is `/home/u/.local/state/tasklens/state.toml`.
- **Given** `XDG_CACHE_HOME=""` **When** `from_vars` runs **Then** `icon_cache_file()` is `$HOME/.cache/tasklens/icons.toml`.
- **Given** `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=relative/dir` **When** `from_vars` runs **Then** the default `$HOME/.config` is used.
- **Given** `HOME` unset **When** `from_vars` runs **Then** it returns the error "HOME is not set to an absolute path".
- **Given** a missing nested directory **When** `ensure_dir` runs **Then** every created directory has mode 0700.
- **Given** an existing directory with mode 0755 **When** `ensure_dir` runs **Then** its mode stays 0755.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/paths.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: add `mod paths;`.
- `crates/tl-app/tests/paths.rs`: create. Because tl-app is a binary crate, the test file includes the module with `#[path = "../src/paths.rs"] mod paths;`.

## Tests
- `tests/paths.rs::config_home_set`, `state_home_default`, `cache_home_empty_falls_back`, `relative_xdg_ignored`, `home_missing_is_error`, `autostart_path`, `ensure_dir_creates_0700` (in a `tempfile::TempDir`), `ensure_dir_keeps_existing_mode`, `all_file_names` (asserts every getter's file name: `settings.toml`, `themes.json`, `state.toml`, `logs`, `crash`, `history`, `dumps`, `run-history.json`, `icons.toml`, `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop`).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: only the HOME error above; I/O errors from `ensure_dir` are returned as is.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: called once at start; no caching needed.
- Privacy: paths are not logged above `debug`.

## Notes
- `--app-id` (P4) may later change the `tasklens` subdirectory name; that is E33-019 and open item E33-OI-6. Do not add it here.
- Use `std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt` for modes (no `unsafe`).
Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`. title: E33-003 args.rs: clap declaration of every command-line argument
description:
## Context
All command-line arguments are declared once, up front, in `args.rs` (00-epics section 2). Later beads add only the `main.rs` arms that act on them (E01 for `--bench` and `--gallery`, E32 for `--low-memory` and `--watch-memory`). Sources: APP-052, table (c) argument list, R-138 item 15 (`--gallery`), UI-SHL-110 step 2, APP-011 (forwarded arguments).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/args.rs` with clap derive (see open item E33-OI-2 for the crate):
```rust
#[derive(clap::Parser, Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
#[command(name = "tasklens", version, about = "Task manager for Linux")]
pub struct Args {
    #[arg(long)] pub start_minimized: bool,
    #[arg(long)] pub low_memory: bool,
    #[arg(long)] pub watch_memory: bool,
    #[arg(long, value_enum)] pub tab: Option<TabArg>,
    #[arg(long, value_name = "PID")] pub select_pid: Option<u32>,
    #[arg(long)] pub debug: bool,
    #[arg(long)] pub force_full_memory_mode: bool,
    #[arg(long, value_name = "ID")] pub app_id: Option<String>,
    #[cfg(feature = "bench")] #[arg(long, value_name = "SCENE")] pub bench: Option<BenchScene>,
    #[cfg(feature = "bench")] #[arg(long, requires = "bench", value_name = "SECONDS")] pub duration: Option<u32>,
    #[cfg(feature = "bench")] #[arg(long, requires = "bench", value_name = "SECONDS")] pub warmup: Option<u32>,
    #[cfg(feature = "bench")] #[arg(long, requires = "bench", value_name = "PATH")] pub json: Option<PathBuf>,
    #[cfg(feature = "bench")] #[arg(long, conflicts_with = "bench")] pub gallery: bool,
}
#[derive(clap::ValueEnum, Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TabArg { Processes, Performance, Services, Startup, Connections, Information }
#[cfg(feature = "bench")]
#[derive(clap::ValueEnum, Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BenchScene { PerfCpu, Table2000, Bridge, Static, HistoryScrub }  // CLI names perf-cpu, table-2000, bridge, static, history-scrub
impl TabArg { pub fn to_model(self) -> tl_model::command::Tab; }   // Tab is the enum used by AppRequest::SelectTab (R-136)
pub fn parse() -> Args;   // Args::parse(): clap prints usage and exits 2 on an unknown argument, 0 for --help and --version
```
- `--version` prints `tasklens <CARGO_PKG_VERSION>` (clap default format) and exits 0.
- `--tab` values are exactly `processes`, `performance`, `services`, `startup`, `connections`, `information`.
- Defaults for `--duration`, `--warmup` and the `--json` form belong to the E01 bead that handles `--bench` (ADR-014); this bead only declares them as optional.
- Without the `bench` feature, `--bench` and `--gallery` are unknown arguments (exit 2).
- Help text per argument (clap `help`): `--start-minimized` "Start hidden to the tray, or minimized when the tray is off"; `--low-memory` "Open the low-memory rescue window"; `--watch-memory` "Run the low-memory watcher (no window)"; `--tab` "Open on this tab"; `--select-pid` "Open Processes and select this process"; `--debug` "Show the Debug menu"; `--force-full-memory-mode` "Test option: ignore low-memory mode"; `--app-id` "Run a separate instance with its own settings (development builds)"; `--bench` "Run a benchmark scene"; `--gallery` "Open the component gallery". These strings are not in the docs; see open item E33-OI-7.
- Environment variables are not parsed here (`TASKLENS_DEBUG` is read in `main.rs`, E33-A1).
Add `mod args;` to `main.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `tasklens --tab services --select-pid 1234` **When** parsed **Then** `tab == Some(TabArg::Services)` and `select_pid == Some(1234)`.
- **Given** `tasklens --frobnicate` **When** parsed **Then** usage is printed to stderr and the exit code is 2.
- **Given** `tasklens --tab nowhere` **When** parsed **Then** the exit code is 2.
- **Given** `tasklens --select-pid -5` **When** parsed **Then** the exit code is 2.
- **Given** `tasklens --version` **When** run **Then** stdout is `tasklens <version>` and the exit code is 0.
- **Given** a build without `bench` **When** `tasklens --bench perf-cpu` is parsed **Then** the exit code is 2.
- **Given** a `bench` build **When** `tasklens --bench table-2000 --duration 30` is parsed **Then** `bench == Some(BenchScene::Table2000)` and `duration == Some(30)`.
- **Given** a `bench` build **When** `tasklens --duration 30` is parsed without `--bench` **Then** the exit code is 2.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/args.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: add `mod args;`.

## Tests
- `args.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` using `Args::try_parse_from`: `tab_and_pid`, `unknown_argument_is_error` (asserts `ErrorKind::UnknownArgument` and `exit_code() == 2`), `bad_tab_value`, `negative_pid_rejected`, `version_flag` (asserts `ErrorKind::DisplayVersion`), `all_bools_default_false`, `tab_maps_to_model` (each `TabArg` maps to the matching `tl_model::command::Tab`), and under `#[cfg(feature = "bench")]`: `bench_scene_names` (all five CLI names parse), `duration_requires_bench`, `gallery_conflicts_with_bench`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: clap's own messages; exit code 2 for usage errors (UI-SHL-110 step 2).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: arguments are not logged above `debug`.
