title: E33-004 logging.rs: tracing subscriber, daily log file, 200-line ring
description:
## Context
Logging is set up in `main` right after the panic hook (UI-SHL-110 step 1). It follows ADR-015 exactly: `tracing-subscriber` with `EnvFilter` from `TASKLENS_LOG`, a daily rotating file kept 7 days, stderr only when it is a terminal. The crash report needs the last 200 log lines, so the subscriber also keeps them in memory. Sources: ADR-015 (Logging), APP-054, R-048, R-049.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/logging.rs`:
```rust
pub const DEFAULT_FILTER: &str = "info,wgpu=warn,wgpu_core=warn,wgpu_hal=warn,naga=warn,zbus=warn";
pub const RING_LINES: usize = 200;
pub struct LogGuard { _file: tracing_appender::non_blocking::WorkerGuard }  // held in main, dropped last
#[derive(Clone)] pub struct RecentLines(Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<String>>>);
impl RecentLines { pub fn snapshot(&self) -> Vec<String>; }   // oldest first, at most 200
pub fn init(logs_dir: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<(LogGuard, RecentLines)>;
pub fn build_filter(var: Option<&str>) -> EnvFilter;  // TASKLENS_LOG value or DEFAULT_FILTER
```
- Filter: `TASKLENS_LOG` if set and parseable, else `DEFAULT_FILTER`. An unparseable `TASKLENS_LOG` falls back to the default and logs one `warn!` "TASKLENS_LOG is invalid; using the default filter". `RUST_LOG` is never read (do not call `EnvFilter::from_default_env`).
- File output: `tracing_appender::rolling::RollingFileAppender::builder().rotation(Rotation::DAILY).filename_prefix("tasklens").filename_suffix("log").max_log_files(7).build(logs_dir)`, wrapped in `tracing_appender::non_blocking`. `logs_dir` is created with `paths::ensure_dir` (0700). Files are created by the appender; after `init`, chmod the current file to 0600 if it exists.
- stderr output: a second `fmt` layer, added only when `std::io::IsTerminal::is_terminal(&std::io::stderr())` is true, with ANSI colours.
- Ring layer: a `tracing_subscriber::Layer` that formats each event the same way as the file layer (one line, no ANSI) and pushes it into `RecentLines`, dropping the oldest beyond 200. It sees only events that passed the filter.
- If `logs_dir` cannot be created, logging continues to stderr and the ring only, and `init` logs `warn!` "Log folder is not writable; logging to stderr only". `init` fails only if a global subscriber was already set.
- Targets used across tasklens (documented in a module comment, not enforced here): `tasklens::engine`, `tasklens::source::<name>`, `tasklens::action`, `tasklens::ui`, `tasklens::frame`, `tasklens::probe`, `tasklens::perf`.
Add `mod logging;` to `main.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `TASKLENS_LOG` unset **When** `build_filter(None)` runs **Then** the filter string equals `DEFAULT_FILTER`.
- **Given** `TASKLENS_LOG=debug` **When** `build_filter(Some("debug"))` runs **Then** debug events pass.
- **Given** `RUST_LOG=trace` and `TASKLENS_LOG` unset **When** `init` runs **Then** trace events are filtered out.
- **Given** 250 events logged **When** `snapshot()` is read **Then** it holds 200 lines, the oldest being event 51.
- **Given** a temp logs dir **When** one event is logged and the guard dropped **Then** a file named `tasklens.<yyyy-mm-dd>.log` exists in it and contains the event.
- **Given** a logs dir path that cannot be created **When** `init` runs **Then** it returns `Ok` and later events still reach the ring.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/logging.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: add `mod logging;`.

## Tests
- `logging.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: `default_filter_string`, `tasklens_log_used`, `invalid_tasklens_log_falls_back`, `ring_keeps_last_200` (uses the ring layer with a local subscriber via `tracing::subscriber::with_default`), `ring_skips_filtered_events`, `file_written_with_prefix_and_suffix` (tempfile dir, local subscriber, drop guard, assert one file whose name starts with `tasklens.` and ends with `.log`).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as above; never panics.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the ring layer formats into a reused `String` per event and allocates one `String` per kept line; no logging in per-frame or per-process loops above `trace` (ADR-015) is a rule for callers.
- Privacy: ADR-015 never-logged list applies to every caller: command lines, environment, working directories, open file paths, executable paths of other users' processes, window titles, user names other than the current user. This module adds no fields of its own.

## Notes
- Tests that install a global subscriber must not run in the same process as others; use `with_default` for unit tests.
Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`. title: E33-005 crash.rs: panic hook writes crash-<unix seconds>.txt, keeps newest 20
description:
## Context
The panic hook is the first thing `main` installs (UI-SHL-110 step 1). It writes one report file per panic with version, thread, message, location, backtrace and the last 200 log lines, then calls the default hook (ADR-015, R-049). The report never contains process metadata or settings. Sources: ADR-015 (Crash handling), APP-055, R-049, UI-SHL-093 (report files read later by the Crash Report window).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/crash.rs`:
```rust
pub const KEEP_REPORTS: usize = 20;
pub fn install_hook(crash_dir: PathBuf, recent: Arc<OnceLock<RecentLines>>, on_main_thread_panic: fn());
pub fn write_report(crash_dir: &Path, info: &PanicHookInfo<'_>, recent: &[String], now_unix: u64) -> io::Result<PathBuf>;
pub fn format_report(info_text: &ReportFields, recent: &[String]) -> String;
pub struct ReportFields<'a> { pub version: &'a str, pub git_sha: &'a str, pub thread: &'a str, pub message: &'a str, pub location: &'a str, pub backtrace: &'a str }
pub fn prune(crash_dir: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;   // keep the newest 20 crash-*.txt by the number in the name; remove older ones and their crash-<t>.seen markers
```
- File: `<crash_dir>/crash-<unix seconds>.txt`, mode 0600, directory created 0700 with `paths::ensure_dir`. If that name exists (two panics in one second), append `-1`, `-2` before `.txt`.
- Content, in this order, one field per line, then sections:
  ```
  tasklens <CARGO_PKG_VERSION> (<TASKLENS_GIT_SHA>)
  thread: <name or "unnamed">
  message: <panic payload as &str or String, else "Box<dyn Any>">
  location: <file>:<line>:<column>

  backtrace:
  <std::backtrace::Backtrace::force_capture()>

  last log lines:
  <up to 200 lines, oldest first>
  ```
- No process metadata, no settings contents, no command lines or environment (ADR-015).
- `install_hook` takes the previous hook with `std::panic::take_hook()`, installs a new one that writes the report (errors are ignored), calls `prune`, then, if the panicking thread is the main thread (`std::thread::current().name() == Some("main")`), calls `on_main_thread_panic`, and finally calls the previous hook. The hook must not panic; wrap the body in `std::panic::catch_unwind` with `AssertUnwindSafe`.
- `recent` is a `OnceLock` because the hook is installed before logging; it is filled right after `logging::init`. Before that, the "last log lines" section is empty.
- `on_main_thread_panic` is the desktop notification hook added by E33-012; in this bead `main.rs` passes a no-op `fn noop() {}`.
Add `mod crash;` to `main.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a panic with message "boom" on a thread named "worker" **When** the hook runs **Then** a file `crash-<t>.txt` exists with lines `thread: worker` and `message: boom` and a `backtrace:` section.
- **Given** 3 recent log lines **When** a report is written **Then** the `last log lines:` section holds those 3 lines in order.
- **Given** 25 report files with different times and 25 `.seen` markers **When** `prune` runs **Then** the 20 newest reports remain and the 5 oldest reports and their `.seen` markers are gone.
- **Given** two reports in the same second **When** both are written **Then** the second is named `crash-<t>-1.txt`.
- **Given** an unwritable crash dir **When** the hook runs **Then** the default hook still runs and the process behaves as without the hook.
- **Given** any report **When** its text is searched for the test process's command line and for `HOME=` **Then** neither appears.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/crash.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: add `mod crash;`.
- `crates/tl-app/tests/crash_report.rs`: create; includes `#[path = "../src/crash.rs"] mod crash;` plus the modules it needs (`paths`, `logging` types) the same way.

## Tests
- `tests/crash_report.rs::report_fields_in_order` (calls `format_report` and checks line order), `report_file_written` (tempfile dir; spawns a named thread that panics with `std::panic::set_hook` from `install_hook`, joins it, reads the file), `same_second_suffix`, `prune_keeps_newest_20`, `prune_removes_seen_markers`, `no_cmdline_or_env_in_report`, `unwritable_dir_falls_through` (dir path under a read-only tempdir).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: hook I/O errors are swallowed; nothing is shown to the user from this module.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: runs only on panic.
- Privacy: content restricted as above; this is a regression requirement of ADR-015.

## Notes
- `PanicHookInfo` is the stable name since Rust 1.81 (`std::panic::PanicHookInfo`).
- Tests that set the global panic hook must restore it (`take_hook` before, `set_hook` back after).
Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`. title: E33-006 settings_store.rs: load settings.toml and state.toml (corrupt, newer, clamp)
description:
## Context
UI-SHL-110 step 5 loads `settings.toml` and `state.toml` before the engine starts. ADR-011 fixes the load steps for each file: missing file gives defaults, a parse error renames the file and warns, a missing `schema_version` counts as 1, a lower one migrates, a higher one is read-only, out-of-range values clamp, unknown keys are dropped. The toasts are queued and shown after the first frame (UI-SHL-110 step 11). Sources: ADR-011 (Load), APP-033, R-018, canonical table (a), UI-SHL-110 steps 5 and 11.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/settings_store.rs` (load half; E33-008 adds the save half):
```rust
pub enum FileKind { Settings, State }
pub struct Loaded<T> { pub value: T, pub read_only: bool, pub notices: Vec<LoadNotice> }
pub enum LoadNotice {
    Corrupt { kept_as: String },  // file name only, e.g. "settings.toml.corrupt-1759500000"
    Newer,
}
impl LoadNotice { pub fn toast_text(&self) -> String; }
pub fn load_settings(path: &Path, now_unix: u64) -> Loaded<tl_model::settings::Settings>;
pub fn load_state(path: &Path, now_unix: u64) -> Loaded<tl_model::settings::UiState>;
fn load_table(path: &Path, now_unix: u64) -> LoadStep;  // shared core
```
Steps, the same for each file (ADR-011):
1. File missing (`ErrorKind::NotFound`): defaults, `read_only = false`, no notice, nothing written.
2. Read and parse to `toml::Table`. Read or parse error: rename the file to `<name>.corrupt-<unix seconds>` in the same directory (for example `settings.toml.corrupt-1759500000`), use defaults, push `LoadNotice::Corrupt { kept_as }`. Toast text: `Settings file was unreadable and has been reset. The old file was kept as {name}` with `{name}` replaced by `kept_as`. If the rename fails, log `warn!` and still use defaults; the notice is still pushed with the intended name.
3. `schema_version` missing: treat as 1. Lower than `tl_model::settings::SCHEMA_VERSION`: call `migrations::migrate(&mut table, from)` (E33-007), then deserialize. Higher: deserialize what is understood, `read_only = true`, push `LoadNotice::Newer` with toast text `Settings were written by a newer tasklens; changes will not be saved`.
4. Deserialize with `toml::Table::try_into::<T>()`; all structs are `#[serde(default)]` (E03), so missing keys take defaults. A type error in one value must not reset the whole file: deserialize section by section (each top-level table into its section struct), and a section that fails takes its default with a `warn!` naming the section.
5. Clamp out-of-range values with the clamp function E03-A2 provides on `Settings` and `UiState` (ranges from canonical table (a)); each clamped key is logged at `info!` with key name, old and new value.
6. Unknown keys are ignored (serde default behaviour, no `deny_unknown_fields`); they are not preserved on save. Unknown column ids are dropped with a log line by the `ColumnId::from_str` path in E03; this module only keeps the order of the known ones.
- The two files have independent `read_only` flags.
- Logs never include file contents.
Add `mod settings_store;` to `main.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** no settings file **When** `load_settings` runs **Then** the value equals `Settings::default()`, there are no notices and no file is created.
- **Given** a file with `[general` (broken TOML) **When** `load_settings` runs at unix time 1759500000 **Then** the file is renamed to `settings.toml.corrupt-1759500000`, defaults load and the notice text is "Settings file was unreadable and has been reset. The old file was kept as settings.toml.corrupt-1759500000".
- **Given** a file without `schema_version` and `[processes] interval_ms = 2000` **When** loaded **Then** `interval_ms == 2000`.
- **Given** `schema_version = 2` (newer) **When** loaded **Then** `read_only == true`, known keys are read and the notice text is "Settings were written by a newer tasklens; changes will not be saved".
- **Given** `[appearance] ui_scale_pct = 500` **When** loaded **Then** the value is 200 and an info line names `appearance.ui_scale_pct`.
- **Given** `[processes] interval_ms = "fast"` **When** loaded **Then** the `processes` section takes its defaults and the other sections keep their file values.
- **Given** an unknown key `[general] colour = 3` **When** loaded **Then** loading succeeds.
- **Given** `state.toml` with `[columns.processes] visible = ["name", "bogus", "pid"]` **When** loaded **Then** visible is `["name", "pid"]`.

- `crates/tl-app/tests/settings_store.rs`: create; includes the modules with `#[path]` as in `tests/paths.rs`.

title: E24: CPU Details grid, P1 rows 1 to 9 and 11 to 14 (pages/performance/cpu_details.rs)
description:
## Context
The CPU page's Details grid shows 12 live values at 1 Hz and the static core counts and caches. This bead writes the P1 rows with their exact labels, formats and tooltips; the P2 rows are E24-020. Sources: PERF-033 to PERF-036, PERF-039, PERF-040, UI-PRF-024 (row table), table (d), ADR-014 fixture ("a stats block with 12 values updated at 1 Hz").

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/cpu_details.rs`:

```rust
pub fn cpu_details_model() -> KeyValueModel;   // rows in grid order with the P1 labels
pub fn update_live(model: &mut KeyValueModel, sys: &SystemSnapshot, now_boot_ns: u64) -> bool;   // rows 1 to 9, 11, 12; returns true when any text changed
pub fn update_static(model: &mut KeyValueModel, sys: &SystemSnapshot, catalog: &DeviceCatalog) -> bool;  // rows 13, 14, 19 to 21
```

P1 rows, labels, formats, tooltips (grid order; values are examples):

| # | Label | Value | Tooltip and rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Utilization` | `18.6%` | |
| 2 | `Kernel time` | `2.3%` | |
| 3 | `Speed` | `4631 MHz` | tooltip `Fastest core: 5050 MHz`; BogoMIPS-only source: value `4200 MHz (?)`, tooltip `Reported by the kernel at boot; the current clock is not available` |
| 4 | `Processes` | `295` | count format |
| 5 | `Threads` | `5 596` | thin-space grouping |
| 6 | `Handles` | `253 248` | tooltip `Open file descriptors, system-wide` |
| 7 | `Up time` | `2 days, 2h 38m 15s` | uptime format (table (d)); tooltip `Boot time 2026-10-01 07:12:33` (local time `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`) |
| 8 | `Base speed` | `4200 MHz` | |

| 12 | `Load average` | `1.24 0.98 0.87` | two decimals each, single spaces; tooltip `1, 5 and 15 minutes` |
| 13 | `Cores` | `8` | static |
| 14 | `Logical processors` | `16` | static |
| 19 | `L1 cache` | `512 KiB` | cache format; tooltip `16 × 32 KiB data + 16 × 32 KiB instruction` |
| 20 | `L2 cache` | `8 MiB` | tooltip `8 × 1 MiB` |
| 21 | `L3 cache` | `96 MiB` | tooltip `98 304 KiB · 1 × 96 MiB`; `L4 {size}` appended to the tooltip when present |

title: E24: CpuPage entity: header toggles, Overall and Per core modes, kernel toggle, demand, bench layout (pages/performance/cpu.rs)
description:
## Context
The CPU page is the phase-0 scene: the overall chart or the per-core grid, the kernel toggle, the Details grid, and the demand that switches the engine to 10 Hz per-core sampling. This bead writes the P1 page (Overall and Per core); overlaid, stacked, marks and the secondary graph are P2 beads. Sources: PERF-027, PERF-028, PERF-029, PERF-033, UI-PRF-023 (anatomy, buttons, data binding, build), UI-PRF-053 (`bench_show_both`), ADR-008 (`cpu: PerCore`, `cpu_fast`), ADR-014, table (a) `cpu_graph_mode`, `cpu_kernel`, R-126 (`cpu_fast` stays on with smooth off).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/cpu.rs`:

```rust
pub struct CpuPage {
    key: DeviceKey, row: DeviceRow,
    overall: Entity<ChartView>, grid: CpuGrid,
    overlaid: Option<Entity<ChartView>>, stacked: Option<Entity<ChartView>>,   // E24-018
    secondary: Option<Entity<ChartView>>,                                      // E24-021
    details: KeyValueModel, mode: CpuGraphMode, kernel: bool,
    pub bench_show_both: bool,            // bench-only (UI-PRF-053): overall chart above the grid
    mode_button_focus: FocusHandle, kernel_button_focus: FocusHandle,
    hub, demand, #[cfg(..)] pub render_count: Cell<u32>,
}
impl CpuPage { pub fn new(key, row, hub, demand, cx) -> Self; }
impl DevicePage for CpuPage { .. }
impl Render for CpuPage { .. }   // renders DevicePageFrame { page: self, .. }
```

Behaviour:
- Overall chart: `ChartSpec { series: [total: fill cpu_fill, line cpu_line; kernel: no fill, line kernel_line, present when kernel], y: Fixed 0..100, range from performance.graph_range_s, smooth from motion.smooth_graphs, background: Window, grid lines on }`, `ChartLabels { heading: Some("Utilization"), value_fmt: Percent, value_align: Right, range_word: "Utilization", legend: [("Total", Solid), ("Kernel", Dashed)] when kernel else [("Total", Solid)], show_axis_max: false }`, height `GRAPH_H_OVERALL` 300.
- `graphs()`: `mode == Overall` → the overall chart; `PerCore` → the grid (`CpuGrid`, height from `grid_height`); `bench_show_both` → overall chart, `sp4`, grid. The two P2 modes render the overall chart until E24-018 lands.

title: E24: sidebar hotplug: insert and remove animations, re-plug gap, saved slot
description:
## Context
Disks and network interfaces appear and disappear while tasklens runs. A new card slides in at its saved place, a removed card collapses, the selection moves to the next card, and a re-plugged device is a new card whose graph starts with a gap. Sources: PERF-005, UI-PRF-012 (hotplug add, remove, re-plug), UI-FND-003 (motion tokens), ADR-009 (page entities dropped).

## Deliverable
In `pages/performance/sidebar.rs`:
- `CardState.anim: CardAnim { Steady, Inserting { started: Instant }, Removing { started: Instant } }`.
- On `DEVICES`: a row that is new (key not in `cards`) gets `Inserting`; a card whose row is gone or became hidden gets `Removing` and keeps rendering until the animation ends (`m_base` 200 ms, `ease_out_cubic`), then is dropped together with its page entity (the sidebar emits `SidebarEvent::Removed(key)`; `PerformancePage` removes `pages[key]`).
- Insert: the card wrapper animates height 0 → 80 and opacity 0 → 1 through `with_animation(ElementId, Animation::new(m_base).with_easing(ease_out_cubic), |div, t| div.h(px(80 × t)).opacity(t))`; cards below move with the flex layout. Remove: opacity 1 → 0 and height 80 → 0. Reduced motion (`cx.reduce_motion()`) or `motion.animations == false`: no animation, the state changes at once.
- Selection: when the selected card starts `Removing`, `selection_after_removal` picks the next visible card and `select` runs at once (not after the animation).

title: E24: edit mode drag reorder within a group, drop indicator, Alt+Up and Alt+Down, device_order persistence
description:
## Context
In edit mode a card can be dragged by its handle to another slot inside its group; a 3 px accent line marks the drop position; Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the focused row by one slot. The result is `performance.device_order`. Sources: PERF-003, UI-PRF-013 (drag, drop indicator, keyboard reorder, data binding), PERF-005 (saved place).

## Deliverable
In `sidebar.rs`:
- `drag: Option<DragState { key: DeviceKey, group: DeviceKind, over: Option<usize> /* drop index inside the group */ }>`.
- Handle `on_drag(DraggedCard { key }, |drag, _, w, cx| ghost view)`: the ghost is the card at opacity 0.8 following the pointer; the original row renders at opacity 0.3.
- Card rows `on_drag_move::<DraggedCard>`: compute the drop index from the pointer y against each row's midpoint, only among rows of the same group (a drop into another group is ignored and shows no indicator); the indicator is a 3 px `accent` line across the sidebar width at the drop position between two cards.
- `on_drop::<DraggedCard>` → `PerfMoveDevice { key, before: Option<DeviceKey> }` (`before = None` = end of the group).
- `PerfMoveDevice` handler: builds the new `device_order` as the full current sidebar order with the moved key placed before `before` (or last in its group) and writes `performance.device_order` (every present device key, so later re-plugs keep their slot; PERF-005).
- `PerfMoveFocusedDevice { delta }` (Alt+Up −1, Alt+Down +1): moves `edit_focus_row` one slot within its group; no-op at the group's ends.
- Numbering (`Disk N`, `GPU N`, `Fan N`) re-computes from the new order (`type_number`).

- **Given** disks `[X, Y, Z]` **When** `PerfMoveDevice { key: Z, before: Some(X) }` is handled **Then** `device_order` lists `Z, X, Y` in the disk positions and the cards read `Disk 0` = Z, `Disk 1` = X (`drag_shifts_cards` for the sidebar).
- **Given** a drag of a disk over the Fans group **When** `on_drag_move` runs **Then** no indicator is shown and a drop does nothing (`reorder_within_group_only`).
- **Given** `edit_focus_row = Y` **When** Alt+Up is pressed **Then** the order is `Y, X, Z`; Alt+Up again is a no-op.
- **Given** the drop indicator between X and Y **When** rendered **Then** a 3 px accent quad spans the sidebar width at that boundary.
- **Given** a re-plugged device whose key is in `device_order` **When** it returns **Then** it takes its saved slot (E24-010 covers the insert; this test asserts the order after a move then remove then re-add).

title: E24: Graph summary mode: SummaryView tiles, key context, Esc and Ctrl+M, title suffix (pages/performance/summary.rs)
description:
## Context
Ctrl+M replaces the whole window content with a tiled grid of every visible device's main graph. Esc or Ctrl+M returns; tab switching is blocked while it is on. Sources: PERF-010, UI-PRF-016 (anatomy, states, interaction, build), UI-SHL-001 (`MainWindow::render` hook `summary_view()`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/summary.rs`:

```rust
pub struct SummaryView { tiles: Vec<Tile { key: DeviceKey, heading: SharedString, line1: SharedString, chart: Entity<ChartView> }>, selected_on_entry: Option<DeviceKey>, focus: FocusHandle /* key_context "PerformanceSummary" */, .. }
pub fn tile_grid(n: usize, w: Pixels, h: Pixels) -> TileLayout { cols, rows, tile_w, tile_h, scrolls: bool }
    // cols = ceil(sqrt(n)), rows = ceil(n / cols); tile_w = (W − 2 sp6 − (cols − 1) sp4) / cols, tile_h likewise over H; minimum tile 200 × 120: while tile_w < 200 and cols > 1, cols −= 1; if tile_h < 120 the grid scrolls vertically with tile_h = 120
```

Behaviour:
- `PerfToggleSummaryMode` on `PerformancePage`: on → create `SummaryView` with one tile per visible device in sidebar order (a fresh `ChartView` per tile with the card's series and scale, `background: Window`); off → drop it. `PerformancePage::summary_view(&self) -> Option<AnyView>`; `MainWindow::render` (E20-A1) asks the Performance page for it before rendering the tab strip and renders it instead of tab strip plus page when `Some` (chain edit in `window/main.rs`: one `if let Some(v) = perf.summary_view()` branch; the title bar stays with its caption buttons and its menus hidden).
- Tile: bg `window_bg` padding `sp6`, gap `sp4`; label row: heading `t_md` 500 left (plus ` · {line1}` in `text_secondary` when the tile is ≥ 280 px wide), value `t_md` 400 `tnum` right; the chart fills the rest; legend shown when tile width ≥ 200; range label when tile height ≥ 160; a 2 px `accent` line under the label row on the tile of `selected_on_entry`.
- Entering: sidebar and page fade out over `m_fast`, tiles fade in over `m_base`; reduced motion instant. Window title gets the suffix ` · Graph Summary` (`window.set_window_title("tasklens · Graph Summary")`), restored on exit.
- Keys in `PerformanceSummary` (bound by E24-002): Esc and Ctrl+M → off; tab keys swallowed. Click on a tile → off, then `PerfSelectDevice { key }`. Right-click on a tile → `page_menu` for that device's page (created on demand through `build_page` if not visited). Double-click → `PerfShowMiniWindow`. Window resize re-tiles (layout computed in render from the bounds).
- Demand unchanged (the sidebar still contributes while hidden under the summary; the sidebar entity is kept).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 9 visible devices in a 1600 × 1000 window **When** summary mode opens **Then** 9 tiles in 3 × 3 (`summary_tile_grid_for_9`) and `tiles` follow the sidebar order (`summary_tiles_all_visible_devices`).
- **Given** summary mode on **When** `ctrl-2` is pressed **Then** the active tab is still Performance (`summary_blocks_tab_switch`).
- **Given** memory selected on entry **When** Esc is pressed **Then** summary is off and memory is still selected (`summary_esc_returns_to_selected_device`); the window title is `tasklens` again.
- **Given** a click on the GPU tile **When** handled **Then** summary is off and `gpu` is selected.
- **Given** a 500 × 300 window and 9 devices **When** `tile_grid` runs **Then** `cols == 2` (200 px minimum) and `scrolls == true`.
- **Given** reduce motion on **When** entering **Then** no animation frames are requested by the fade.

title: E24: CPU "All cores overlaid" and "All cores stacked" modes with cross-fade and the kernel button rule
description:
## Context
The two Mission Center modes draw every core in one 300 px chart: overlaid lines at `max(1/n, 0.08)` alpha, or stacked filled bands with a `Stacked(n)` axis ("1600%"). The kernel toggle is disabled in these modes and a mode change cross-fades. Sources: PERF-027, PERF-029, PERF-030, UI-PRF-023 (modes, animation, button states), UI-PRF-006 `Stacked`.

## Deliverable
In `cpu.rs`:
- `overlaid: Option<Entity<ChartView>>` created on first use: `ChartSpec { series: one per logical CPU with fill None, line cpu_line.alpha(max(1/n, 0.08)), y: Fixed 0..100, stack: false }`, labels heading `Utilization`, no legend, `show_axis_max: false`.
- `stacked`: `series` one per CPU with `fill = Some(cpu_fill.alpha(0.85 … stepped: band k uses lightness offset k/n × 0.15 of cpu_fill)` and `line = cpu_line`, `y: Stacked(n)`, `stack: true`, `show_axis_max: true` (axis text `1600%` from E19-004).
- `CPU_EXTRA_MODES_ENABLED = true`; the mode menu items are enabled.
- Kernel button: disabled (opacity 0.5, tooltip kept) in `AllCoresOverlaid` and `AllCoresStacked`; its label is unchanged.
- Demand: `cpu: PerCore` in both modes.
- Mode change: cross-fade `m_base` between the old and new graph area (both rendered during the fade, old opacity 1 → 0, new 0 → 1 with `with_animation`); the graph area height animates between 300 and the grid height over the same duration; reduced motion or `motion.animations == false`: instant.
- CPU hotplug (`DEVICES` with a changed topology) rebuilds both specs.

- **Given** 16 CPUs and `PerfSetCpuGraphMode { AllCoresOverlaid }` **When** rendered **Then** the overlaid chart has 16 series, each with alpha `0.08` (`max(1/16, 0.08)`), no fill, and the kernel button is disabled (`cpu_kernel_disabled_in_overlaid`).

title: E24: CPU secondary graph: Power draw, Clock speed, Temperature, fallback rule and the menu
description:
## Context
Under the CPU graph area sits one 120 px chart chosen from the page menu: power (default), clock, temperature or none. When power is not available the chart falls back to temperature, then clock, without changing the saved choice. Sources: PERF-032, PERF-038 to PERF-040, UI-PRF-025 (table, states, interaction), table (a) `cpu_secondary_graph`.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Power | `Power draw` | package W filled (`cpu_fill`/`cpu_line`), core W dashed `cpu_line` | `StickyUp { hw_max: None }` | Watts |
| Clock | `Clock speed` | average MHz filled, maximum-core MHz dashed | `StickyUp { hw_max: cpuinfo_max_freq }` | Mhz |
| Temperature | `Temperature` | main sensor °C | `StickyTemp` | Celsius |
| None | absent | | | |

- Demand: `sensors = true` while the effective choice is Temperature (the CPU worker owns RAPL and clocks).
- Series: `cpu.power_pkg`, `cpu.power_core`, `cpu.clock_avg` (`CPU_FREQ`), `cpu.clock_max`, `cpu.temp` (`CPU_TEMP`) at 1 Hz; the constants without an ADR-003 id are plan open item 1.

title: E24: Details value selection fallback: click selects, Ctrl+C copies the value, Esc clears, "Copy value" context item (U-46)
description:
## Context
PERF-012 wants selectable Details values, but gpui-pre 0.3.7 has no text selection on arbitrary elements. tasklens ships a fallback: clicking a value selects it visually, Ctrl+C copies that value, Esc clears, and a right-click offers "Copy value". The bead also records U-46. Sources: PERF-012, UI-PRF-020 (interaction), R-126, U-46.

## Deliverable
- `details.rs`: `KeyValueModel.selected: Option<&'static str>` (label of the selected row); `render_details` draws the selected value with bg `row_selected` and text `text_selected_primary`; click on a value sets `selected` and notifies; click elsewhere on the page or Esc clears it.
- `mod.rs`: `PerfCopyDeviceInfo` copies the selected value only when `selected.is_some()` (no toast); `PerfCopyValue` (from the context item) copies the clicked value. Esc in the `Performance` context clears the selection before the global Esc chain (bind `escape` → `PerfClearValueSelection`, a unit action added to `actions.rs`, on the page root only while a selection exists, so the global chain runs otherwise).
- Context menu on a value: `Copy value` → `PerfCopyValue` (the item is added at the top of the page menu when the right-click landed on a value, through `PageMenuCtx.clicked_value: Option<&'static str>`).
- U-46 check: before coding, the implementer greps gpui-pre 0.3.7 for a text-selection API on `div` or `Label` (`selectable`, `text_selection`, `InteractiveText` selection); if one exists and works in a `TestAppContext`, use it instead of the fallback and record the finding in the closing comment and in `docs/RECONCILIATION.md`'s unverified list entry U-46 (one line, the only doc edit this bead makes).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a click on the `Speed` value **When** handled **Then** that value renders with `row_selected` bg and `PerfCopyDeviceInfo` copies `4631 MHz` without a toast.
- **Given** a selection **When** Esc is pressed **Then** the selection is cleared and the filter box (none on Performance) is untouched; a second Esc runs the global chain.
- **Given** a right-click on a value **When** the menu builds **Then** the first item is `Copy value` and it copies the value.
- **Given** no selection **When** `PerfCopyDeviceInfo` dispatches **Then** the whole page text is copied (E24-016 behaviour unchanged).

title: E24: DeviceKey, DeviceKind, sidebar order and visibility rules, PerformancePage skeleton (pages/performance/mod.rs)
description:
## Context
The Performance tab identifies devices by persistent string keys (`cpu`, `gpu:<uuid>`, `disk:<wwn>` …) in settings and state, orders them by `performance.device_order` then by type, and shows or hides them by per-device overrides and per-type defaults. This bead writes those pure rules and the `PerformancePage` entity skeleton every later E24 bead fills. Sources: PERF-002, PERF-004, PERF-005 (key forms), PERF-008 (type order), UI-PRF-010 (entity fields), UI-PRF-012 (order, visibility, selection rules), canonical table (a) `[performance]` keys, ADR-003 `DeviceIdentity`.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/mod.rs` and the line `pub mod performance;` in `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/mod.rs` (chain edit, E16-A1).

```rust
pub mod page; pub mod sidebar; pub mod card; pub mod summary; pub mod menu; pub mod actions; pub mod details; pub mod cpu; pub mod cpu_grid; pub mod cpu_details;  // empty modules with a `//! filled by <plan key>` line until their beads run

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct DeviceKey(pub Arc<str>);
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
pub enum DeviceKind { Cpu, Memory, Gpu, Disk, Net, Fan, Battery, AggregateDisk, AggregateGpu }
impl DeviceKey {
    pub fn from_identity(id: &DeviceIdentity) -> Option<DeviceKey>;  // None for CpuLogical and Sensor (not cards)
    pub fn kind(&self) -> DeviceKind;      // from the prefix
    pub const CPU: &'static str = "cpu"; pub const MEMORY: &'static str = "memory";
    pub const AGGREGATE_DISK: &'static str = "aggregate:disk"; pub const AGGREGATE_GPU: &'static str = "aggregate:gpu";
}
```

Key forms (PERF-005): `CpuPackage` → `cpu`; `Memory` → `memory`; `Gpu { uuid, pci_bus_id }` → `gpu:GPU-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` (lower-case hex of the 16 bytes in 8-4-4-4-12 groups) when `uuid != [0; 16]`, else `gpu:pci:<pci_bus_id>`; `Disk { wwn_or_serial: Some(s), .. }` → `disk:<s>`; `Disk { wwn_or_serial: None, name, .. }` → `disk:<name>` (plan open item 6 records that the by-path fallback is not available from `DeviceIdentity`); `Net { name, .. }` → `net:<name>`; `Fan { chip, index }` → `fan:<chip>:<index>` (open item 6: the device path is not in the identity); `Battery { native_path }` → `bat:<native_path>`.

```rust
pub struct PerformanceSettingsView<'a> { pub order: &'a [DeviceKey], pub overrides: &'a HashMap<DeviceKey, Override /* Show | Hide */>, pub show_disks: bool, pub show_gpus: bool, pub show_fans: bool, pub show_batteries: bool, pub show_network_wired: bool, pub show_network_wireless: bool, pub show_network_vpn: bool, pub show_network_virtual: bool, pub show_network_other: bool }
pub struct DeviceRow { pub key: DeviceKey, pub kind: DeviceKind, pub idx: DeviceIdx, pub generation: u32, pub net_class: Option<NetClass> }
pub fn sidebar_order(catalog: &DeviceCatalog, settings: &PerformanceSettingsView, out: &mut Vec<DeviceRow>);
    // present devices only; keys in `order` first, in that order; the rest by kind order Cpu, Memory, Gpu, Disk, Net, Fan, Battery, AggregateDisk, AggregateGpu; within a kind by DeviceCatalog order; `lo` never included
pub fn is_visible(row: &DeviceRow, settings: &PerformanceSettingsView) -> bool;
    // override Show → true, Hide → false; else Cpu and Memory → true; Disk → show_disks; Gpu → show_gpus; Fan → show_fans; Battery → show_batteries; Net → by NetClass (Wired → show_network_wired, Wireless → show_network_wireless, VpnOrTunnel → show_network_vpn, Virtual → show_network_virtual, Other → show_network_other); aggregates → false
pub fn visible_rows<'a>(rows: &'a [DeviceRow], settings: &PerformanceSettingsView) -> impl Iterator<Item = &'a DeviceRow>;
pub fn selection_after_removal(visible: &[DeviceRow], removed_at: usize) -> Option<DeviceKey>;  // next below, else the one above, else None
pub fn initial_selection(visible: &[DeviceRow], saved: Option<&DeviceKey>) -> Option<DeviceKey>; // saved if visible, else the first visible
pub fn type_number(rows: &[DeviceRow], key: &DeviceKey) -> u16;   // index among visible rows of the same kind, counting from 0 ("Disk 0", "GPU 0")

pub struct PerformancePage {
    pub(crate) sidebar: Entity<sidebar::DeviceSidebar>,     // E24-004
    pub(crate) pages: FxHashMap<DeviceKey, AnyView>,         // created on first visit, kept (ADR-009)
    pub(crate) selected: Option<DeviceKey>,
    pub(crate) summary: Option<Entity<summary::SummaryView>>,// E24-015
    pub(crate) sidebar_visible: bool,                        // not persisted (R-090)
    pub(crate) focus: FocusHandle,                           // key_context "Performance"
    #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-hooks"))] pub render_count: Cell<u32>,
}
```

`NetClass` is the PERF-054 type class of an interface as the engine reports it in the device catalog (`DeviceEntry` carries `NetKind` from `tl_model::devices`, E03-A1; map `NetKind::{Ethernet, Usb} → Wired`, `WiFi → Wireless`, `Tunnel | Vpn → VpnOrTunnel`, `Virtual | Bridge → Virtual`, `Cellular | Other → Other`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `DeviceIdentity::Gpu { uuid: [0x12, 0x34, ..], pci_bus_id }` **When** `from_identity` runs **Then** the key is `gpu:GPU-1234…` in 8-4-4-4-12 form; with a zero uuid it is `gpu:pci:0000:2d:00.0`.
- **Given** a catalog with `cpu, memory, gpu A, disk X, disk Y, net enp38s0, net lo, net tailscale0` and `order = [net:enp38s0, disk:Y]` **When** `sidebar_order` runs **Then** the rows are `net:enp38s0, disk:Y, cpu, memory, gpu A, disk X, net:tailscale0` and `lo` is absent (`order_saved_then_type_default`).
- **Given** `show_network_virtual = false` and a `docker0` row of class Virtual **When** `is_visible` runs **Then** false; with override Show, true.
- **Given** override `Hide` on `cpu` **When** `is_visible` runs **Then** false.
- **Given** visible rows `[a, b, c]` and `removed_at = 1` **When** `selection_after_removal` runs **Then** `c`; with `removed_at = 2`, `b`; with one row removed at 0, `None`.
- **Given** saved `disk:Y` hidden **When** `initial_selection` runs **Then** the first visible row's key.
- **Given** visible rows `disk:X, disk:Y` in that order **When** `type_number(.., disk:Y)` runs **Then** 1.
- **Given** an entry with `present == false` **When** `sidebar_order` runs **Then** it is not in the output.

- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/mod.rs`: add `pub mod performance;` (chain edit)

## Tests

- `pages::performance::tests::order_saved_then_type_default`
- `pages::performance::tests::visibility_overrides_and_type_defaults`

- `pages::performance::tests::initial_selection_falls_back_to_first`
- `pages::performance::tests::type_number_counts_visible_of_kind`

- Errors: N/A
- Validity: `present == false` entries are never rows; a returning device gets a new row with `generation + 1` (PERF-005).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: `sidebar_order` runs on `DEVICES` changes only (every 5 s rescan at most); 9 to 15 rows.

`DeviceIdentity`, `DeviceEntry`, `DeviceCatalog`, `DeviceIdx`, `NetKind` are `tl_model::devices` (ADR-003, E03-A1); `Settings.performance` fields are `tl_model::settings` (E03-A2, table (a)). `schemars::JsonSchema` is required by gpui-kit's `#[derive(Action)]` for data-carrying actions (E24-002 carries `DeviceKey`); if gpui-pre 0.3.7's `Action` derive does not need it, drop the derive. title: E24: every Perf* action, bind_keys_performance and the app.rs registration (pages/performance/actions.rs)
description:
## Context
Every menu item, button and key on the Performance tab dispatches one GPUI Action in the `tasklens` namespace with a `Perf` prefix. This bead declares all of them up front, for E24 and for the E25 device pages, so no later bead edits this file, and binds the table (b) keys in the `Performance` context. ```

pub struct CardLines { pub heading: SharedString, pub line1: SharedString, pub line2: SharedString, pub line2_accent: bool, pub tooltip: Option<SharedString>, pub disconnected: bool }

|---|---|---|---|---|

| Memory | `Memory` | `34.68 GiB / 63.16 GiB` | `Commit 69.0%` | false |

| Disk | `Disk {n}` | `NVMe - /` (kind, ` - `, primary mount; no mount: kind only) | model; from P2 `{model} · 41 °C` when the temperature is Valid | false |
| Net | the interface name | type word (`Ethernet`, `Wi-Fi`, `Virtual`, `USB network`, `Bridge`, `Cellular`, `Tunnel`, `VPN`, `Other`) | connected: `↓ 1.2 Mbps ↑ 0.3 Mbps` when both rates are non-zero, else the total rate `0.01 Mbps` (table (d) network format, `network_unit`, `auto_scale`); not connected: the state word (`Disconnected`, `Testing`, `Dormant`, `Not present`, `Lower layer down`, `Unknown`) | true when connected |
| Fan | `Fan {n}` or the fan label when set | label, else chip name | `1200 RPM · 45 °C` (`45 °C` part omitted without a paired sensor) | false |
| Battery | kind word (`Battery`, `Mouse`, `UPS`, …) | vendor and model | `85.0% · Discharging` | false |
| AggregateDisk | `Aggregate storage` | `{k} disks` | `Multiple` when kinds differ, else the kind | false |
| AggregateGpu | `Aggregate graphics` | `{k} adapters` | `Multiple` when vendors differ, else the vendor | false |

`tooltip`: the full model when `line1` would truncate (the owner decides truncation from width; the card always sets the tooltip to the full line1 and `TlTooltip` shows it on hover of the text column); network cards append the NetworkManager connection name on a second line when known. `disconnected = true` for a Net card whose state is not Connected.

Card rendering (sizes × `ui_scale`): `h_flex` width × 80, bg `list_bg`, 1 px `divider` border, radius `r_md`; left inset `sp5` (12); the chart box 116 × 56 (`ChartSpec.background = List`, `ChartLabels { heading: None, value_align: Left, legend: empty, show_axis_max: false }`, grid on, outline on); `sp4` gap; text column `v_flex` vertically centred, lines 18 / 16 / 16 px high: heading `t_md` 500 `text_primary`, line1 and line2 `t_sm` 400 `text_secondary` (line2 in `accent` when `line2_accent`), each `overflow_hidden` + `text_ellipsis` + `whitespace_nowrap`. States: hover bg `row_hover`; pressed bg `row_selected` at alpha 0.6; selected: a 2 px `accent` outline quad drawn inside the card bounds (`div().absolute().inset_0().border_2().border_color(accent).rounded(r_md)`); focused and selected: a second outline 1 px `accent` at alpha 0.5, 2 px outside; `disconnected`: whole card `opacity(0.6)`; edit mode: no selected border, `hidden_in_edit` → opacity 0.6. Click → `PerfSelectDevice { key }` (not in edit mode when the click lands on the switch; E24-013). Double-click: nothing. `cursor` default.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a CPU entry with model "AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D 8-Core Processor", clock 4631 MHz and temperature 52 °C **When** `card_lines` runs **Then** heading `CPU`, line1 the model, line2 `4631 MHz · 52 °C` (`card_lines_cpu`).
- **Given** a Net entry with rx 1.2 Mbps and tx 0.3 Mbps, bits, auto-scale off **When** `card_lines` runs **Then** line2 `↓ 1.2 Mbps ↑ 0.3 Mbps` and `line2_accent == true` (`card_lines_network_both_directions`).
- **Given** rx 1.2 Mbps and tx 0 **When** `card_lines` runs **Then** line2 `1.2 Mbps` (`card_lines_network_one_direction`).
- **Given** a Net entry with operstate down **When** rendered **Then** the card has opacity 0.6 and line2 is `Disconnected` in `text_secondary` (`card_disconnected_opacity`).
- **Given** a Disk entry with temperature `Validity::Restricted` **When** `card_lines` runs **Then** line2 is `{model} · ` followed by the lock glyph text placeholder handled by the renderer: the line is split into `model` text and a `TlValidityGlyph` for the temperature (`card_value_glyph_for_restricted`).
- **Given** `selected == true, focused == false` **When** rendered **Then** one 2 px accent outline and no 1 px outer ring; with `focused == true` both.
- **Given** the same inputs twice **When** `card_lines` runs **Then** the returned `SharedString`s compare equal and the caller's cache keeps the first allocation (test asserts `Arc::ptr_eq` after the caller's compare-and-keep step).

title: E24: DeviceSidebar entity: cards, charts, selection, keys, scroll, demand (pages/performance/sidebar.rs)
description:
## Context
The sidebar lists one card per visible device, keeps one `ChartView` per card, owns the roving selection and its keys, scrolls the selected card into view, and tells the demand aggregator which sources it needs. Hotplug animations and edit mode are later beads. Sources: UI-PRF-010 (sidebar part, focus), UI-PRF-011 (data binding, build), UI-PRF-012 (selection, keys, demand), PERF-001, PERF-007, ADR-008 `Demand`, ADR-009 (cached entities, notify rules).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/sidebar.rs`:

```rust
pub struct CardState { pub row: DeviceRow, pub chart: Entity<ChartView>, pub lines: CardLines, pub line_bits: [u64; 3] /* value bits of the last format per line */ }
pub struct DeviceSidebar {
    pub(crate) cards: IndexMap<DeviceKey, CardState>,   // in sidebar order
    pub(crate) rows: Vec<DeviceRow>,                     // from sidebar_order (all present devices, hidden included)
    pub(crate) selected: Option<DeviceKey>,
    pub(crate) focus: FocusHandle,                      // key_context "Performance", tab_stop true (the one Tab stop of the list)
    pub(crate) scroll: ScrollHandle,
    pub(crate) edit_mode: bool,                         // E24-013
    pub(crate) hub: Entity<SnapshotHub>, pub(crate) demand: Entity<DemandAggregator>,
    #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-hooks"))] pub render_count: Cell<u32>,
}
pub enum SidebarEvent { Selected(DeviceKey), Removed(DeviceKey) }   // EventEmitter; PerformancePage listens
impl DeviceSidebar {
    pub fn new(hub, demand, cx) -> Self;    // subscribes to the hub (DEVICES, SYSTEM, SERIES) and observes TlSettings (performance section)
    pub fn select(&mut self, key: DeviceKey, cx);         // sets selected, scrolls into view (ScrollHandle::scroll_to_item Nearest), emits Selected, notifies
    pub fn visible_keys(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &DeviceKey>;
    pub fn heading_for(&self, key: &DeviceKey) -> Option<&CardLines>;
}
```

Behaviour:
- On `DEVICES` or a `performance` settings change: recompute `rows = sidebar_order(..)`; for a new visible row create `CardState` with a `ChartView` (`ChartSpec` per kind: Cpu `[total filled cpu_fill/cpu_line, kernel line kernel_line when cpu_kernel]` `Fixed 0..100`; Memory `[used filled mem, committed dashed mem_line]` `FixedTotal(MemTotal)`; Gpu `[3D/Compute engine]` `Fixed`; Disk `[active time]` `Fixed`; Net `[rx filled net, tx dashed tinted]` `AutoRate { iec: unit == Bytes }` or `LinkSpeed` when `network_dynamic_scale == false` and the speed is known; Fan `[rpm]` `StickyUp { hw_max: fan_max }`; Battery `[percent]` `Fixed` for peripherals, `[power]` `Symmetric` for system batteries; `range_ns = performance.graph_range_s`, `smooth = motion.smooth_graphs`, `background = List`, `grid.lines = true`); drop the state of a row that is gone (E24-010 adds the animation); keep the order of `cards` equal to `rows`. Series ids: `SeriesId { device: row.idx, metric }` with the `MetricId` constants from E03-A1 (`CPU_TOTAL`, `CPU_KERNEL`, `MEM_USED`, `MEM_COMMIT`, `GPU_UTIL`, `DISK_ACTIVE`, `NET_RX`, `NET_TX`, `FAN_RPM`, `BATTERY_PCT`; battery power per plan open item 1).
- On `SYSTEM` and on `SERIES` for a card's ids: re-run `card_lines` for that card, compare each line's value bits (`line_bits`) and keep the old `SharedString` when unchanged; `cx.notify()` only when some line changed.
- Selection: `initial_selection(visible, state.performance.selected_device)` at construction; `select` writes `state.performance.selected_device` through `TlSettings::update` (debounced persist, ADR-011); when the selected card disappears or becomes hidden, `selection_after_removal` picks the next and `select` runs.
- Actions on the focus element: `PerfSelectDevice`, `PerfSelectVisibleDevice { index }` (the Nth visible, hidden cards not counted), `PerfSelectPrevDevice`, `PerfSelectNextDevice`, `PerfSelectFirstDevice`, `PerfSelectLastDevice`. Up at the first card and Down at the last do nothing.
- Demand: after each `rows` change, give the aggregator this surface's part: `cpu: Total` always (the CPU card), `memory` always, `disks` when any Disk card is visible, `nets` when any Net card, `gpus` when any Gpu card, `sensors` when any Fan or Battery card; `cpu_fast` is not set by the sidebar.
- Render: `v_flex` with `sp4` padding, `sp4` gaps, `overflow_y_scroll` with the kit scrollbar in `ScrollbarMode::Scrolling`, one `DeviceCard` per visible row (`selected`, `focused = focus.is_focused(window)`), `.track_focus(&focus)`, `.key_context("Performance")`, `.cached(StyleRefinement::default().size_full())` applied by the parent. Right-click on a card is wired by E24-011.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a `FakeEngine` catalog with 9 devices (CPU, Memory, GPU, 4 disks, 2 nets) **When** the sidebar renders **Then** 9 cards exist in type order and `cards.len() == 9`.
- **Given** `selected_device = "disk:X"` saved and visible **When** constructed **Then** `selected == disk:X`; when it is hidden by `show_disks = false`, the first visible key is selected.
- **Given** `show_disks = false` and 4 disks **When** `PerfSelectVisibleDevice { index: 2 }` dispatches **Then** the third visible card (GPU → the third of CPU, Memory, GPU, nets) is selected (`f3_selects_third_visible_card_skipping_hidden`).
- **Given** the first card selected **When** `PerfSelectPrevDevice` dispatches **Then** the selection is unchanged.
- **Given** a snapshot that changes only memory series **When** installed **Then** the Memory card's lines re-format and the CPU card's `lines` are pointer-equal to before; `render_count` increased by 1.
- **Given** a snapshot that changes nothing the sidebar draws (a process sweep) **When** installed **Then** `render_count` is unchanged.
- **Given** visible card kinds CPU, Memory, Disk **When** demand is read from the aggregator **Then** `disks == true`, `nets == false`, `gpus == false`, `cpu == Total`.
- **Given** `select(key)` **When** called **Then** `UiState.performance.selected_device == key` after the debounce and `SidebarEvent::Selected(key)` was emitted once.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/sidebar.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_sidebar.rs`: change

## Tests
- `ui_sidebar.rs::sidebar_nine_cards_in_type_order`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::saved_selection_or_first_visible`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::f3_selects_third_visible_card_skipping_hidden`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::prev_at_first_is_noop`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::only_changed_card_reformats`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::unrelated_snapshot_does_not_rerender`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::demand_follows_visible_kinds`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::select_persists_and_emits`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: cards show glyphs per E24-003; a device whose main series is absent shows `WarmingUp`.
- Accessibility: one Tab stop (the list) with roving selection; F1..F8, Up, Down, Home, End; the selected card draws the focus ring when the list is focused.
- Performance: 9 cards at 1 Hz (CPU at 10 Hz when `cpu_fast` is set by the CPU page); line text re-shapes only when its bits change; the sidebar entity is cached by the page and re-renders on card text changes, not on every series tick (the charts re-render themselves).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
`SnapshotHub`, `DemandAggregator` (register one surface, update its `Demand` contribution; API names per E16-A1), `TlSettings` (E20-A2 `settings_global.rs`; before it lands, read `Settings` from the E16-A1 global the hub provides and note the swap) and `FakeEngine` are other batches' anchors. `IndexMap` needs `indexmap` in tl-ui's row: it is not there (ADR-001), so use a `Vec<CardState>` plus `FxHashMap<DeviceKey, usize>` instead and keep the field name `cards`. `ScrollHandle::scroll_to_item` is gpui-pre `src/elements/div.rs`. Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E24: Details grid model: KvRow, fallback words, tooltips, change-only formatting (pages/performance/details.rs)
description:
## Context
Every device page ends with a three-column "Details" grid of label-over-value pairs. The page keeps a `KeyValueModel` and re-formats a value only when its bits change; validity maps to the PERF-013 words with their tooltips; some rows hide when missing. Sources: PERF-012, PERF-013, R-050, UI-PRF-021, UI-FND-025 (`TlKeyValueGrid`, `TlValue`), table (d).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/details.rs`:

```rust
pub struct KvRow { pub label: &'static str /* Fluent key */, pub value: SharedString, pub validity: Validity, pub tooltip: Option<SharedString>, pub action: Option<Box<dyn Action>>, pub link: bool, pub bits: u64 }
pub struct KeyValueModel { pub rows: Vec<KvRow>, scratch: String }
pub enum Fallback { NeedsSetup, NotSupported, NotReported, Unavailable, Unknown }
impl KeyValueModel {
    pub fn set_valid(&mut self, label: &'static str, bits: u64, write: impl FnOnce(&mut String)) -> bool;  // formats only when bits differ from the row's; returns true when the text changed
    pub fn set_text(&mut self, label: &'static str, text: &str) -> bool;
    pub fn set_fallback(&mut self, label: &'static str, validity: Validity, fallback: Fallback, reason: Option<&str>) -> bool;
    pub fn set_stale(&mut self, label: &'static str, age_ns: u64) -> bool;     // keeps the last value, validity Stale, tooltip "Last updated {age} ago"
    pub fn set_tooltip(&mut self, label: &'static str, text: Option<SharedString>);
    pub fn hide(&mut self, label: &'static str); pub fn show(&mut self, label: &'static str);   // hidden rows are skipped by the grid (PERF-013 hidden-when-missing list)
    pub fn to_kv_rows(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = TlKvRow<'_>>;   // for TlKeyValueGrid
    pub fn copy_into(&self, out: &mut String);   // "    Label: value" per visible row, PERF-011 (E24-016 uses it)
}
pub fn fallback_word(v: Validity, f: Fallback) -> (&'static str, Option<&'static str> /* tooltip */);
```

Word and tooltip table (`text_secondary` for every non-valid word):

| Validity | Word | Tooltip |
|---|---|---|
| WarmingUp | `Collecting…` | none |
| Stale | the last value | `Last updated {age} ago` (short age, table (d)) |
| Restricted | `Restricted` | `Needs administrator access.` (from P3 `Needs administrator access. Click the shield to grant it.`; the string is one Fluent key `validity-restricted-tooltip` owned by E15-A2, read here) |
| Unsupported + NeedsSetup | `Needs setup` | `Needs setup. Open Additional Setup…`; `link = true`, `action = OpenAdditionalSetup { focus_row }` (shell action) |
| Unsupported + NotSupported | `Not supported` | `Not available on this device` |
| Unsupported + NotReported | `Not reported` | none |
| Failed | `Unavailable` | `Could not read: {reason}` |
| Unknown (enum or status unknown) | `Unknown` | none |

Grid rendering helper: `pub fn render_details(model: &KeyValueModel, m: &UiMetrics, theme: &TlTheme, cx) -> impl IntoElement` builds `TlKeyValueGrid` in stacked layout with `.columns(3)`, `.row_height(46 × ui_scale)` (`kv_row_h`), `.column_gap(sp6)` (`kv_col_gap`), label `t_sm` `text_secondary`, value `t_base` `text_primary` `tnum`; link values in `accent`; a value with a tooltip or action gets a dotted underline on hover; rows fill left to right, top to bottom in model order.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a row with `bits = 0x1` **When** `set_valid(label, 0x1, ..)` is called **Then** the closure does not run and it returns false; with `0x2` it runs and returns true.
- **Given** `set_fallback(label, Unsupported, NeedsSetup, None)` **When** read **Then** `value == "Needs setup"`, `link == true`, the action is `OpenAdditionalSetup` and the tooltip is `Needs setup. Open Additional Setup…` (`kv_grid_fallback_words_per_validity` covers every row of the table).
- **Given** `set_stale(label, 125_000_000_000)` **When** read **Then** the value text is unchanged and the tooltip is `Last updated 2m 5s ago`.
- **Given** `hide("Serial")` **When** `to_kv_rows` iterates **Then** the row is absent and `copy_into` omits it (`kv_grid_hidden_rows_rule`).
- **Given** 14 rows **When** rendered at 1000 px width **Then** the grid has 5 rows of 3 columns, pitch 46 px (`render_details` test through element bounds).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/details.rs`: create
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append `perf-fallback-collecting = Collecting…`, `perf-fallback-restricted = Restricted`, `perf-fallback-needs-setup = Needs setup`, `perf-fallback-needs-setup-tooltip = Needs setup. Open Additional Setup…`, `perf-fallback-not-supported = Not supported`, `perf-fallback-not-supported-tooltip = Not available on this device`, `perf-fallback-not-reported = Not reported`, `perf-fallback-unavailable = Unavailable`, `perf-fallback-could-not-read = Could not read: {$reason}`, `perf-fallback-unknown = Unknown`, `perf-last-updated = Last updated {$age} ago`, `perf-details-heading = Details` (chain edit)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_performance.rs`: change

## Tests
- `details::tests::set_valid_formats_only_on_bits_change`
- `ui_performance.rs::kv_grid_fallback_words_per_validity`
- `ui_performance.rs::kv_grid_stale_keeps_value`
- `ui_performance.rs::kv_grid_hidden_rows_rule`
- `ui_performance.rs::details_grid_three_columns_46px`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `Failed` rows carry `Could not read: {reason}` from `SourceHealth.last_error` passed by the page.
- Validity: the full PERF-013 table.
- Accessibility: label and value are adjacent text; link rows are reachable through the page's focus order (E24-022 adds the selection fallback and context menu).
- Performance: 12 to 30 rows; a value re-formats only on bits change; the grid lives inside the page's `.cached()` Details block.
- Privacy: `copy_into` is the only path to the clipboard and prints exactly the visible rows (D-007 is enforced by never reading serials, E25).

## Notes
`TlKeyValueGrid`, `TlKvRow`, `TlValue` are E15-A2 (UI-FND-025); pass `.row_height(px(46.) × ui_scale)` because the Performance file owns `kv_row_h = 46` (UI-FND-025's 56 is its default). `OpenAdditionalSetup { focus_row: Option<SetupRow> }` is the shell's action (UI-PRF-052); `SetupRow` is `tl_model::command::SetupStep`'s UI twin declared by E29 (`window/setup.rs`), so until E29 lands pass `focus_row: None` through the unit form `OpenAdditionalSetup` declared by E20-A1. Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E24: DevicePage trait and DevicePageFrame: header, toggles, graph area, Details, blocks, page builder (pages/performance/page.rs)
description:
## Context
Every device page has the same frame: a header row with the type word, the model and the page toggles, the graph area, the "Details" heading, the grid and page blocks, inside a scrolling area with `page_pad`. This bead writes the trait pages implement and the frame that renders them, plus the builder that maps a device kind to its page entity (CPU here, the other arms are E25 chain edits). Sources: PERF-008 (page headers), PERF-012, PERF-014, UI-PRF-020 (anatomy, header strings, toggles, states, build), UI-PRF-010 (page column), R-058 (double-click opens the mini window).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/page.rs`:

```rust
pub trait DevicePage: 'static {
    fn key(&self) -> &DeviceKey;
    fn header(&self) -> (SharedString, SharedString);          // (type word, model text)
    fn toggles(&self, w: &mut Window, cx: &mut App) -> SmallVec<[AnyElement; 2]>;
    fn graphs(&self, w: &mut Window, cx: &mut App) -> AnyElement;
    fn details(&self) -> &KeyValueModel;
    fn blocks(&self, w: &mut Window, cx: &mut App) -> SmallVec<[AnyElement; 3]>;
    fn menu_items(&self, menu: TlMenu, w: &mut Window, cx: &mut App) -> TlMenu;   // page-specific items for UI-PRF-015 slot 5
    fn copy_text(&self, out: &mut String);                      // E24-016 and E25 fill it
    fn focus_order(&self) -> SmallVec<[FocusHandle; 4]>;        // header toggles then block controls (UI-SHL-121)
}
pub struct DevicePageFrame<'a> { pub page: &'a dyn DevicePage, pub m: &'a UiMetrics, pub theme: &'a TlTheme }
impl RenderOnce for DevicePageFrame<'_> { .. }
pub fn header_text(kind: DeviceKind, number: u16, entry: &DeviceEntry, system: &SystemSnapshot) -> (SharedString, SharedString);
pub fn build_page(key: &DeviceKey, row: &DeviceRow, hub, demand, cx) -> AnyView;   // match row.kind { Cpu => cx.new(CpuPage::new).into(), _ => placeholder }  (E25 adds one arm per kind; the placeholder renders the frame with an empty graph area and an empty model, and never panics)
pub const PAGE_PAD: f32 = 16.; pub const PAGE_HEADER_H: f32 = 36.; pub const DETAILS_GAP: f32 = 24.; pub const PAGE_MIN_W: f32 = 400.;
pub const GRAPH_H_SINGLE: f32 = 240.; pub const GRAPH_H_STACKED: f32 = 150.; pub const GRAPH_H_OVERALL: f32 = 300.; pub const SECONDARY_GRAPH_H: f32 = 120.;
```

Header strings (PERF-008, UI-PRF-020): Cpu → (`Processor`, model or `Unknown processor`); Memory → (`Memory`, ``); Gpu → (`Graphics adapter`, name or `Unknown GPU`); Disk → (`Disk {n}`, `{model} ({kernel name})` with the kernel name in `text_secondary`: the second string carries a `\u{1}` separator the frame splits on); Net → (`{ifname}`, adapter name or `Unknown adapter`); Fan → (`Fan {n}`, chip); Battery → (kind word, `{vendor} {model}`); AggregateDisk → (`Aggregate storage`, `{k} disks`); AggregateGpu → (`Aggregate graphics`, `{k} adapters`).

Frame layout (× `ui_scale`): `v_flex().size_full().min_w(400).overflow_y_scroll()` with the kit scrollbar (`Scrolling`), padding `page_pad` 16; header row 36 high: type word `t_lg` 500 `text_primary`, `sp4`, model `t_lg` 400 `text_secondary` one line with ellipsis and a `TlTooltip::text(full)` when truncated; toggles right-aligned, `sp4` apart, each a `TlButton` sm (24 high, min width 122); `sp4`; the graph area `div().id("perf-graph-area").on_click(|ev| if ev.click_count() == 2 { dispatch PerfShowMiniWindow })` holding `page.graphs(..)`; `details_gap` 24; `Details` `t_md` 500 in a 24 px row; `sp4`; `render_details(page.details())` (E24-005) inside a `div().cached(..)` block that re-renders when the page notifies; `sp6`; `page.blocks(..)` each separated by `sp6`; bottom padding `page_pad`. title: E24: CPU per-core grid wrapper: cell specs from topology, headings, tooltips, offline cells (pages/performance/cpu_grid.rs)
description:
## Context
The per-core grid is a `ChartGridView` whose cells come from the CPU topology: one cell per logical CPU titled "CPU N", a kernel overlay per cell when the toggle is on, the "Total"/"Kernel" legend in cell 0, a tooltip "Core C, thread T, 4200 MHz" on each heading, and "Offline" for CPUs that are off. Sources: PERF-028, PERF-029, PERF-031 (marks are E24-019), UI-PRF-002, UI-PRF-023 (per-core cell), ADR-003 `CpuTopology`, ADR-014 fixture.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/cpu_grid.rs`:

```rust
pub struct CpuGrid { pub view: Entity<ChartGridView>, cores: Arc<CpuTopology>, kernel: bool, scratch: String }
impl CpuGrid {
    pub fn new(hub, topology: Arc<CpuTopology>, logical_devices: &[DeviceIdx] /* DeviceIdx per logical CPU id, from the catalog's CpuLogical entries */, kernel: bool, range_ns: u64, smooth: bool, theme: &TlTheme, cx) -> Self;
    pub fn set_kernel(&mut self, on: bool, cx);          // rebuilds the ChartGridSpec with or without overlay series
    pub fn set_topology(&mut self, topology, logical_devices, cx);   // CPU hotplug: offline cells, new cells
    pub fn update_clocks(&mut self, per_cpu_mhz: &[(u16, f32, Validity)], cx);  // refreshes heading tooltips at 1 Hz, re-formatting only changed values
    pub fn set_range(&mut self, range_ns, cx); pub fn set_smooth(&mut self, smooth, cx);
}
pub fn cell_specs(topology: &CpuTopology, logical_devices: &[DeviceIdx], kernel: bool, out: &mut Vec<GridCellSpec>);
pub fn heading_tooltip(core: u16, thread: u16, mhz: Option<u32>, out: &mut String);   // "Core 3, thread 1, 4200 MHz"; without a clock "Core 3, thread 1"
```

Rules:
- One cell per logical CPU id in ascending id order; `heading = "CPU {id}"`; `fill_series = SeriesId { device: logical_devices[id], metric: CPU_TOTAL }`; `overlay_series = Some(SeriesId { .., CPU_KERNEL })` when `kernel`; `offline = !topology.online.contains(id)`; `tooltip` from `heading_tooltip(core_id, thread index within the core's `logical` list, mhz)`.
- `ChartGridSpec { fill: theme.graph.cpu_fill, line: theme.graph.cpu_line, overlay_line: theme.graph.kernel_line, y: Fixed 0..100, cell_min_w: 120, cell_h: 112, gap: sp4 (8), legend: [("Total", Solid), ("Kernel", Dashed)] when kernel else [("Total", Solid)], value_fmt: Percent, hover: false (E19-015 turns it on in P2) }`.
- The value label per cell is the newest total percent (`6.1%`), formatted by the grid element (E19-010).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a topology with 16 logical CPUs, all online **When** `cell_specs` runs with `kernel = true` **Then** 16 specs, headings `CPU 0`..`CPU 15`, every `overlay_series.is_some()`, cell 0's legend has two entries (`cpu_grid_16_cores_6_cols` also asserts `grid_layout(16, 1000, 120, 8).cols == 6`).
- **Given** `kernel = false` **When** `set_kernel(false)` runs **Then** every `overlay_series` is `None` and the legend has one entry.
- **Given** CPU 5 offline **When** `cell_specs` runs **Then** spec 5 has `offline == true`.
- **Given** core 3 with logical CPUs `[3, 11]` and 4200 MHz on CPU 11 **When** `heading_tooltip` runs for CPU 11 **Then** `Core 3, thread 1, 4200 MHz`.
- **Given** `update_clocks` twice with the same values **When** run **Then** no tooltip `SharedString` is re-allocated the second time (bits compare).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/cpu_grid.rs`: create
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append `perf-cpu-cell = CPU {$n}`, `perf-cpu-cell-tooltip = Core {$core}, thread {$thread}, {$mhz} MHz`, `perf-cpu-cell-tooltip-noclock = Core {$core}, thread {$thread}`, `perf-cpu-offline = Offline`, `perf-legend-total = Total`, `perf-legend-kernel = Kernel` (chain edit)

- `ui_cpu_page.rs::cpu_grid_offline_cell`

- Validity: an offline CPU is an `offline` cell; a per-CPU clock that is not Valid drops the MHz part of the tooltip.
- Accessibility: headings and values are text; the tooltip repeats the core identity.
- Performance: this is the 32-cell `perf-cpu` case; the grid view is one element with 3 paths (E19-010). ADR-014 gate p50 ≤ 1.0 ms applies through E24-A1.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
`CpuTopology { online: CpuSet, cores: Arc<[CoreInfo { id, logical: SmallVec<[u16; 2]>, l3_group, kind }]> }` is `tl_model::system` (ADR-003 "Per-component fields"); per-CPU clocks come from `SystemSnapshot` (E03-A2; field names per E03). pub struct BootSettings { pub settings: Settings, pub state: UiState,
                          pub persist: Option<Box<dyn Fn(&Settings, &UiState)>>,
                          pub persist_themes: Option<Box<dyn Fn(PersistTheme)>>,

impl Global for BootSettings {}
pub struct AppRequestHandler(pub Box<dyn Fn(AppRequest, &mut App)>);
impl Global for AppRequestHandler {}                         // default handler: debug!(target: "tasklens::ui", ?req, "app request")

title: E16-007 TlDialog confirmation windows
description:
## Context
Builds `TlDialog`, the confirmation window body and footer every "are you sure" prompt uses, opened as a modal `TlSecondaryWindow` of kind Confirmation. It fixes the one focus and Enter rule for every confirmation (R-104). Spec phase P1; priority 0 because it sits in the E16-A2 group that E18-A2 (P0) needs. Sources: UI-FND-021 (confirmation body), R-104, UI-SHL-091, APP-045 (title "tasklens", modal to parent), R-083.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/components/dialog.rs` (add `pub mod dialog;` to `components/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub enum DialogIcon { Warning, Info, None }
pub struct TlDialog { text: SharedString, heading: Option<SharedString>, icon: DialogIcon,
                      action_label: SharedString, destructive: bool, extra: Option<AnyElement>,
                      checkbox: Option<(SharedString, bool)>, title: SharedString }
impl TlDialog {
    pub fn confirm(text: impl Into<SharedString>, action_label: impl Into<SharedString>) -> Self; // title "tasklens", icon Info, not destructive
    pub fn destructive(self) -> Self;            // Danger action button, icon Warning, focus on Cancel
    pub fn heading(self, text: impl Into<SharedString>) -> Self;
    pub fn title(self, title: impl Into<SharedString>) -> Self;   // default "tasklens" (APP-045, R-083)
    pub fn extra(self, el: impl IntoElement) -> Self;             // owner lines under the text (entry name, path, target list)
    pub fn checkbox(self, label: impl Into<SharedString>, initial: bool) -> Self; // "Do not ask again" where a spec allows; none in P1
    pub fn open(self, parent: &mut Window, cx: &mut App,
                on_result: impl FnOnce(DialogResult, &mut Window, &mut App) + 'static) -> gpui::Result<()>;
}
pub enum DialogResult { Confirmed { checkbox: bool }, Cancelled }
```
Layout (width 420, height content-sized 140 to 320, min 360 × 120, not resizable): padding `sp6` (16). Left a leading icon `i_lg` 20: Warning = Lucide `triangle-alert` in `status.warning` (destructive actions), Info = `info` in `status.info`. Right of it, gap `sp5`: optional heading `t_md` 500 `text_primary`, one line; then the text `t_base` `text_primary`, wrapping, at most 6 lines; then the owner's extra element (`t_base` or `t_sm`); then the optional `TlCheckbox`. Footer right-aligned, gap `sp4`, buttons md (28 high, min width 72): Cancel (`TlButton::Secondary`, label "Cancel") left of the action button (`Primary`, or `Danger` when destructive). Button labels name the result ("End tree", "Delete", "Reset"), never "Yes".
Behaviour (R-104, one rule for every confirmation):
- Focus on open: Cancel when destructive; the action button otherwise.
- Enter activates the focused button (bound on the dialog window root; not while a multi-line input has focus). So a stray Enter in a destructive confirmation cancels; the destructive button needs Tab then Enter, or a click.
- Esc always cancels. Closing the window by its X cancels.
- Tab order: content (checkbox if any), Cancel, action, then the pin.
- The window is modal to `parent` (GPUI `WindowKind::Dialog`, xdg_dialog_v1); the parent's content gets `derived.overlay` and ignores input until the dialog closes.
- `on_result` is called exactly once.
In-window kit `Dialog` is used only for sub-prompts inside a secondary window; it reuses this body and footer through `TlDialog::render_body` (pub fn returning the body element).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a destructive confirmation **When** it opens **Then** Cancel has focus.
- **Given** a destructive confirmation just opened **When** Enter is pressed **Then** `on_result` receives `Cancelled`.
- **Given** a destructive confirmation **When** Tab then Enter is pressed **Then** `on_result` receives `Confirmed`.
- **Given** a non-destructive confirmation just opened **When** Enter is pressed **Then** `on_result` receives `Confirmed`.
- **Given** any confirmation **When** Esc is pressed **Then** `on_result` receives `Cancelled` and the window closes.
- **Given** a heading set **When** it renders **Then** the heading line uses `t_md` 500 above the text.
- **Given** a long text **When** it renders **Then** it wraps to at most 6 lines and the window height stays between 140 and 320.
- **Given** the dialog is open **When** the parent window receives a click **Then** the parent ignores it.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/components/dialog.rs`: create, with tests.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/components/mod.rs`: add `pub mod dialog;`.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_dialogs.rs`: add the tests below.

## Tests

- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::confirm_enter_runs_focused_button_escape_cancels` (both kinds)
- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::tab_then_enter_confirms_destructive`
- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::result_called_once_on_window_close`
- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::parent_blocked_while_open`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: if the window cannot open, `open` returns `Err` and `on_result` is not called; the owner treats that as Cancelled and logs.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: the warning icon is always paired with text; buttons are keyboard reachable; focus rule above.
- Performance: one small view per confirmation.
- Privacy: owner texts may name a process; nothing is logged.

- "Toast": one static toast card per kind (Info "Process suspended.", Success "Process terminated", Warning "Outcome unknown", Error "Could not end task.", Progress "Writing core…"), one with an action button "Retry as administrator", one coalesced "Copied to clipboard (×5)", one 3-line cut text. Cards are rendered through the same card element `ToastQueue` uses (static, no timers).
- "Dialog": a destructive confirmation body with heading "End kwin_wayland?" and text "Ending kwin_wayland will end your desktop session. End it anyway?" (buttons Cancel, End; Cancel focused) and a non-destructive sample "Apply these changes?" with buttons Cancel and Apply (Apply focused), rendered with `TlDialog::render_body`.
- "Window frame": the 34 px title bar at 480 wide with title "tasklens Settings": pin off, pin on, pin disabled ("Not supported by this desktop"), active and inactive, and the server-decorations 24 px pin.
- "Menu": a menu with check items and shortcuts (End Task / Delete, End Process / Shift+Delete), a separator, a disabled item, a submenu parent with chevron, a header row, a painted theme item, an empty menu ("No items"), rendered open with one item highlighted.
