title: Dump confirmation, progress and result toasts (windows/notices.rs)
description:
## Context
Dump file creation flow in the UI (P3): large-dump confirmation, the output path, the progress toast fed by stat-ing the file every 500 ms, and the result toasts with "Open folder". Sources: UI-PWN-034, UI-PWN-035, PROC-075, R-004, R-119 (UI picks the path, progress by file size), ADR-005 (`ActionKind::Dump { mode, path }`), canonical table (a) `processes.dump_type = "mini"`, table (c) dumps path.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/notices.rs`:
- `pub fn start_dump(key: ProcessKey, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App)`:
  1. If the record's VmRSS is over 2 GiB (2,147,483,648 bytes): E22's confirmation row "Create dump file, VmRSS > 2 GiB" (title "Create a large dump?", text "<name> uses 3.4 GiB. The process pauses while the core is written and the file will be about that size. Continue?", buttons "Create dump" (Primary) and "Cancel"). Cancel sends nothing.
  2. Path: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/dumps/{name}_{pid}_{yyyymmdd_hhmmss}.core` (local time; `{name}` the display name, see the Notes for characters that cannot appear in a file name); mode from `processes.dump_type` (`mini` -> `DumpMode::Mini`, `full` -> `DumpMode::Full`).
  3. Send `Command::Action(ActionRequest { kind: ActionKind::Dump { mode, path }, targets: [Process(key)], privileged: false })`.
  4. Progress toast: Info, top centre of the window that started it, no autohide while running, key `DumpToast(action_id)`, text "Writing core…" until the first size read, then "Writing core… 1.2 GiB" (table d memory size). A `DumpProgress` task stats the path with `std::fs::metadata(path).len()` on the background executor every 500 ms while the action is pending; cancelled when the action ends.
  5. Result, replacing the toast in place (same key): success: Success toast "Dump created: {path}" with `$HOME` shown as `~`, path middle-ellipsized at the toast width, action button "Open folder" (kit turns autohide off for action toasts, so it stays until closed or replaced); clicking the path text copies the full path (toast "Copied to clipboard"). "Open folder" (`OpenDumpFolder`) sends `ActionKind::ShowInFileManager { path, properties: false }` (FileManager1 `ShowItems` with the file selected), toast "Opening file location". Failure: Error toast "Could not create dump file." with the error text on a second line, 8 s. Rejected for privileges (EPERM or the engine's privilege error): Warning toast "Creating a dump needs administrator rights" (the "Retry as administrator" button comes from the action tracker in P3).
- `pub struct DumpToast(pub u64)`.
- Strings `pwn-notices-dump-*` in `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** VmRSS 1 GiB **When** `start_dump` runs **Then** no confirmation opens and a `Dump` action with the computed path is sent.
- **Given** VmRSS 3.4 GiB **Then** the confirmation "Create a large dump?" opens first; Cancel sends nothing.
- **Given** the dump running and the file growing to 1.2 GiB **When** 500 ms pass **Then** the same toast key now reads "Writing core… 1.20 GiB" (table d format).
- **Given** success with path `/home/u/.local/state/tasklens/dumps/x_1_20261003_101500.core` and `$HOME=/home/u` **Then** the toast reads "Dump created: ~/.local/state/tasklens/dumps/x_1_20261003_101500.core" with "Open folder".
- **Given** failure "gcore exited 1" **Then** the toast reads "Could not create dump file." and "gcore exited 1".
- **Given** `processes.dump_type = "full"` **Then** the request mode is `Full`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/notices.rs`: extend.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs`: tests.
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: chain-edit keys.

## Tests
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::dump_confirm_only_over_2gib`
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::dump_progress_toast_updates_in_place`
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::dump_success_toast_text_and_button`
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::dump_failure_toast_text`
- `windows::notices::tests::dump_path_format`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: failure and privilege toasts above.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: the toast text carries the size; it is the only progress indicator.
- Performance: one `stat` every 500 ms off the UI thread during a dump.
- Privacy: core files hold process memory; the path is shown, contents never read by the UI.

## Notes
- Security: dumps need CAP_SYS_PTRACE through the helper (engine side); the UI never runs gcore.
- The exact size text uses the table (d) memory formatter (two decimals at GiB); the example "1.2 GiB" in UI-PWN-034 is illustrative.
- Open item (leader): no doc says how `{name}` is made safe for a file name (a display name can contain `/`). Recommendation: replace `/` and control characters with `_` and cut to 64 bytes. Ask before coding the path builder.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_dialogs_process`.

title: Regression test: process window confirmations use UI-PRC-014 texts
description:

title: Process window Actions and key bindings (windows/actions.rs)
description:
## Context
Declares every GPUI Action that the process windows (Properties, App Properties, Set Affinity, Custom priority, Send Signal, Run, Handle Search, dump and VirusTotal notices) use, and binds their keys per context. One namespace, `tasklens` (R-128, R-133). Sources: UI-PWN conventions ("Actions"), table (b) rows for PropsWindow, KvGrid, AffinityDialog, PriorityDialog, SignalDialog, RunDialog, HandleSearch (R-120), UI-PRC-013 and UI-PRC-020 action names, D-008.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/windows/actions.rs` with:
- Naming rule (written as a module doc comment): an Action named in the UI docs keeps that name; an Action the docs do not name gets the R-133 prefix (`Props`, `Affinity`, `Priority`, `Signal`, `Run`, `HandleSearch`).
- Unit Actions via `actions!(tasklens, [...])`:
  `SetAffinity`, `OpenCustomPriority`, `SignalOpenRealtime`, `OpenVirusTotal`, `CreateDump` (row-menu items E23 adds; they carry nothing and read the captured row-menu targets, UI-PRC-013),
  `PropsNextTab`, `PropsPrevTab`, `PropsRefreshNow`, `PropsFocusFilter`, `PropsCloseWindow`, `PropsCopyAllFields`, `PropsCopyValue`, `PropsActivateField`, `PropsFieldMenu`, `PropsFieldUp`, `PropsFieldDown`, `PropsFieldLeft`, `PropsFieldRight`, `PropsFieldHome`, `PropsFieldEnd`, `PropsToggleRevealEnv`, `PropsVerifyPackage`, `PropsStartStringScan`, `PropsCancelStringScan`, `PropsEscape`,
  `AffinityApply`, `AffinityReset`, `AffinityToggle`, `AffinityToggleGroup`, `AffinityMoveLeft`, `AffinityMoveRight`, `AffinityMoveUp`, `AffinityMoveDown`, `AffinityHome`, `AffinityEnd`,
  `PriorityApply`, `PrioritySliderStep { delta: i8 }` (data action, see below),
  `SignalSendRealtime`,
  `RunCommand`, `RunCommandElevated`, `ClearRunHistory`, `BrowseRunTarget`, `RunHistoryUp`, `RunHistoryDown`,
  `StartHandleSearch`, `StopHandleSearch`, `ClearHandleSearch`, `HandleSearchAll`, `HandleSearchEndTask`, `HandleSearchEndProcess`, `HandleSearchGoToProcess`, `HandleSearchCopyPaths`, `HandleSearchCopyRows`,
  `OpenDumpFolder`.
- Data Actions (`#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Deserialize, JsonSchema, Action)] #[action(namespace = tasklens)]`): `PropsSelectTab(pub u8)` (1..=7), `SendSignal { pub signo: i32 }`, `SetThreadNice(pub i8)`, `SetThreadSched { pub policy: SchedPolicyWire, pub rt_prio: u8 }` where `SchedPolicyWire` is a serde mirror of `tl_model::actions::SchedPolicy` (`other`, `batch`, `idle`, `fifo`, `rr`), `SignalThread { pub signo: i32 }`, `PrioritySliderStep { pub delta: i8 }`.
- `pub fn bind_keys_process_windows(cx: &mut App)` with `cx.bind_keys([...])`:
  - `PropsWindow`: `alt-1`..`alt-7` -> `PropsSelectTab(1..7)`; `ctrl-tab`, `ctrl-pagedown` -> `PropsNextTab`; `ctrl-shift-tab`, `ctrl-pageup` -> `PropsPrevTab`; `ctrl-f` -> `PropsFocusFilter`; `f5` -> `PropsRefreshNow`; `ctrl-w` -> `PropsCloseWindow`; `escape` -> `PropsEscape`.
  - `PropsWindow > KvGrid`: `up`/`down`/`left`/`right`/`home`/`end` -> `PropsFieldUp/Down/Left/Right/Home/End`; `enter` -> `PropsActivateField`; `ctrl-c` -> `PropsCopyValue`; `shift-f10`, `menu` -> `PropsFieldMenu`.
  - `AffinityDialog`: `left`/`right`/`up`/`down`/`home`/`end` -> the `Affinity*` moves; `space` -> `AffinityToggle`; `shift-space` -> `AffinityToggleGroup`; `enter` -> `AffinityApply`.
  - `PriorityDialog`: `pageup` -> `PrioritySliderStep { delta: 5 }`, `pagedown` -> `PrioritySliderStep { delta: -5 }`; `enter` -> `PriorityApply`.
  - `SignalDialog`: `enter` -> `SignalSendRealtime`.
  - `RunDialog`: `up` -> `RunHistoryUp`, `down` -> `RunHistoryDown`, `enter` -> `RunCommand`, `shift-enter` -> `RunCommandElevated`.
  - `HandleSearch`: `enter` -> `StartHandleSearch`; `escape` -> `StopHandleSearch` (the handler stops a running search, else closes the window when idle, UI-PWN-030).
  - `HandleSearch > Table`: `delete`, `ctrl-e` -> `HandleSearchEndTask`; `shift-delete`, `ctrl-x` -> `HandleSearchEndProcess`; `enter` -> `HandleSearchGoToProcess`; `ctrl-c` -> `HandleSearchCopyPaths`; `ctrl-shift-c` -> `HandleSearchCopyRows`.
  - Slider Left/Right/Home/End and stepper Up/Down in PriorityDialog and SignalDialog are the foundation components' own keys (TlSlider, TlStepper); not bound here.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/mod.rs`: add `pub mod actions;` (chain edit, one line).
- `crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs`: add the call `crate::windows::actions::bind_keys_process_windows(cx);` in `TasklensUi::init` next to the other `bind_keys_*` calls (chain edit, one line).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `TasklensUi::init` ran in a `TestAppContext` **When** the keymap is queried for `alt-3` in context `PropsWindow` **Then** it resolves to `PropsSelectTab(3)`.
- **Given** the keymap **When** `shift-enter` is queried in `RunDialog` **Then** it resolves to `RunCommandElevated`.
- **Given** the keymap **When** `ctrl-x` is queried in `HandleSearch > Table` **Then** it resolves to `HandleSearchEndProcess`.
- **Given** the keymap **When** `escape` is queried in `HandleSearch` **Then** it resolves to `StopHandleSearch`.
- **Given** `SendSignal { signo: 10 }` serialized to JSON **When** deserialized **Then** it equals the original.

## Tests

- `windows::actions::tests::run_dialog_keys_bound` (up, down, enter, shift-enter).
- `windows::actions::tests::handle_search_table_keys_bound` (delete, ctrl-e, shift-delete, ctrl-x, enter, ctrl-c, ctrl-shift-c).
- `windows::actions::tests::data_actions_roundtrip` (`SendSignal`, `SetThreadNice`, `SetThreadSched`, `PropsSelectTab`).

## Notes

title: Process window frame specs, titles and Esc order (windows/frame.rs)
description:
## Context
Fixes the frame values every process window passes to the foundation's `TlSecondaryWindow` (UI-FND-021): kind, title, default and minimum size, resizable flag, plus the Esc order shared by these windows. Sources: UI-PWN-001, UI-FND-021, R-073, R-127, APP-045, D-006.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/windows/frame.rs`:
- `pub enum PwnWindow { ProcessProperties, AppProperties, SetAffinity, SetPriority, RealtimeSignal, Run, HandleSearch }`.
- `pub struct PwnFrameSpec { pub kind: TlWindowKind, pub default_size: Size<Pixels>, pub min_size: Size<Pixels>, pub resizable: bool, pub modal: bool }` and `pub const fn spec(w: PwnWindow) -> PwnFrameSpec` with exactly these logical sizes (multiplied by `ui_scale_pct / 100` through `UiMetrics` at open time):

| Window | Kind | Default | Minimum | Resizable | Modal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ProcessProperties | Properties (`Floating`) | 900 x 640 | 640 x 400 | yes | no |
| AppProperties | Properties (`Floating`) | 720 x 560 | 640 x 400 | yes | no |
| SetAffinity | Dialog | 640 x content (height 360..=640) | same | no | yes, to parent |
| SetPriority | Dialog | 440 x content | same | no | yes, to parent |
| RealtimeSignal | Dialog | 360 x content | same | no | yes, to parent |
| Run | Run row of UI-FND-021 (`Floating`) | 480 x 248 | 480 x 248 | no | no |
| HandleSearch | Tool (`Floating`) | 860 x 560 | 560 x 360 | yes | no |

- Titles as functions returning `SharedString`: `props_title(name, pid, exited)` -> `Process Properties - {name} - PID {pid}` plus ` (not running)` when exited; `app_props_title(name, exited)` -> `App Properties - {name}` plus ` (not running)`; constants `TITLE_SET_AFFINITY = "tasklens Set Affinity"`, `TITLE_SET_PRIORITY = "tasklens Set Priority"`, `TITLE_SEND_SIGNAL = "tasklens Send Signal"`, `TITLE_RUN = "tasklens Run"`, `TITLE_HANDLE_SEARCH = "tasklens Handle Search"`.
- `pub fn open_pwn<V: Render>(cx: &mut App, w: PwnWindow, title: SharedString, parent: Option<AnyWindowHandle>, build: impl FnOnce(&mut Window, &mut App) -> Entity<V>) -> Result<WindowHandle<Root>>` that calls `TlSecondaryWindow::open` with the spec; modal dialogs pass the parent. Properties windows open centred on the main window's output (`Bounds::centered(None, size, cx)`); position is never saved (ADR-010).
- Esc order helper: `pub enum EscStep { ClosePopup, CancelScan, ClearFilter, CloseWindow }` and `pub fn esc_step(popup_open: bool, scan_running: bool, filter_focused_non_empty: bool) -> EscStep` returning the first true in that order, else `CloseWindow` (UI-PWN-001: popup or menu, then running scan or search, then focused non-empty filter, then close; Cancel for modals).
- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/mod.rs`: `pub mod frame;` (chain edit, one line).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `spec(PwnWindow::Run)` **When** read **Then** default and minimum are both 480 x 248 and resizable is false.
- **Given** a `TestAppContext` **When** each `PwnWindow` is opened through `open_pwn` with a dummy view **Then** the window's default and minimum sizes equal the table at `ui_scale_pct = 100`.
- **Given** `ui_scale_pct = 125` **When** ProcessProperties opens **Then** its default size is 1125 x 800.
- **Given** popup closed, scan running, filter non-empty and focused **When** `esc_step` runs **Then** it returns `CancelScan`; with scan stopped it returns `ClearFilter`; with filter empty it returns `CloseWindow`.
- **Given** `props_title("firefox", 4321, true)` **Then** the text is `Process Properties - firefox - PID 4321 (not running)`.

## Files

- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/mod.rs`: one `mod` line.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_props.rs`: create with the size test.

## Tests

- `windows::frame::tests::pwn_esc_order_scan_then_filter_then_close`: the three Esc steps in order (UI-PWN-001 test, done on the helper; the Strings tab bead repeats it end to end).
- `windows::frame::tests::titles_format`.

## Cross-cutting

- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: the window title names the target, so the compositor window list identifies it.
- Performance: frame is static; no work per frame.

- `TlSecondaryWindow::open(cx, kind, title, size, build_content)` is in `components/window_frame.rs` (E16-A2). The pin and caption buttons come from it; this bead never respecifies the frame.

title: Set Affinity dialog for one process (windows/affinity.rs)
description:
## Context
The Set Affinity dialog for one process target (P1). It shows the CPU topology as core tiles grouped by L3 cache, keeps a CPU list field in sync, and sends one `SetAffinity` action. Several targets, thread targets and mixed marks come in a later bead. Sources: UI-PWN-021, PROC-067 (P1 one target), R-039, UI-PRC-021, ADR-003 (`SystemSnapshot.cpu_topology`), ADR-008 (`Demand.affinity_targets`), R-119.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/windows/affinity.rs`:
- `pub struct AffinityDialog` (Entity): `targets: SmallVec<[ActionTarget; 1]>` (captured at menu open, max 256), `initial: Vec<CpuSet>` (one per target, filled from `DetailsSnapshot.affinity`), `state: CpuTriState` (`[u8; 1024]`, values `OFF = 0`, `ON = 1`, `MIXED = 2`), `list_input: Entity<InputState>`, `loading: bool`, `_subs: Vec<Subscription>`.
- `pub fn open(targets: SmallVec<[ActionTarget; 1]>, subtitle: SharedString, parent: AnyWindowHandle, cx: &mut App)` opening `PwnWindow::SetAffinity` (E23-002) modal to `parent`, title "tasklens Set Affinity", width 640, height from content 360..=640 (the group area scrolls beyond that), key context `AffinityDialog`.
- On open it adds the target keys to `Demand.affinity_targets` through the `DemandAggregator` and removes them in `on_release`.
- Layout, top to bottom (padding `sp6`):
  - Subtitle row 24 high, `t_sm` `text_secondary`: `{name} (PID {pid})`; while loading it ends with " - reading current affinity…".
  - Row 32 high: `TlCheckbox` "All processors" (checked when every allowed CPU is checked, indeterminate when some are); right side label "CPU list" `t_sm` `text_secondary` and `TlTextInput` sm, width 200, placeholder "0-7,16-23".
  - 1 px `divider`.
  - Per L3 group: header 24 high with a group `TlCheckbox` (indeterminate when partly checked) and label `t_base` medium `text_primary`: `CCD {n}: CPU {list}`; Intel hybrid: `P-cores: CPU {list}` and `E-cores: CPU {list}` with the app SVG icons `cpu-pcore` / `cpu-ecore` 12 px `text_secondary` before the label; machine without L3 data: one group `CPUs: {list}`.
  - Core tiles 72 x 52, gap 4, background `list_bg`, radius `r_sm`, padding `sp2`, 8 per row in core order, wrapping. Each tile: two stacked 24 px rows, a `TlCheckbox` labelled `CPU {n}` (`t_sm`, tabular figures) for the first logical CPU, its SMT sibling below; a core without SMT has one row and an empty lower half. Hybrid tiles show the P or E icon (10 px) before the label. Tile tooltip `Core {k}: CPU {a} and CPU {b}`.
  - Validation line 20 high, only when nothing is checked: Lucide `circle-alert` 14 px `status.danger` and "At least one CPU must stay enabled" `t_sm` `status.danger`.
  - Footer 52 high, top border 1 px `divider`, padding `sp6`, right-aligned `TlButton` "Cancel" (Secondary) then "OK" (Primary), gap `sp4`.
- CPU states: outside `AffinityInfo.cpuset_limit`: disabled, unchecked, tooltip "Not allowed by the process's cpuset"; not in `cpu_topology.online`: disabled, tooltip "CPU is offline"; while loading: every checkbox disabled.
- List field sync: every checkbox change rewrites the field to the canonical list (ascending, ranges merged, e.g. `0-7,16-23`); a valid field edit updates the grid on each Change event; invalid text (not comma-separated CPU numbers and `a-b` ranges, or a CPU not allowed) sets the input border `status.danger`, shows "Use CPU numbers and ranges, for example 0-7,16-23" under it in `t_xs` `status.danger`, disables OK and leaves the grid at its last valid state.
- `pub fn parse_cpu_list(text: &str, max_cpu: u16) -> Result<CpuSet, ()>` and `pub fn format_cpu_list(set: &CpuSet, out: &mut String)`.
- Group checkbox click: checks the whole group, or unchecks it when fully checked.
- Keyboard (`AffinityDialog`): Tab order All processors, CPU list, grid (one focus stop), Cancel, OK. In the grid Left/Right move between CPUs in the same tile row and across tiles; Up/Down switch the tile's two rows, then tile rows and groups; Home/End first and last CPU; Space toggles (`AffinityToggle`); Shift+Space toggles the group (`AffinityToggleGroup`); Enter runs OK when enabled (`AffinityApply`); Esc and Cancel close without action.
- OK: sends one `Command::Action(ActionRequest { id: next ActionId, kind: ActionKind::SetAffinity(mask), targets, privileged: false })`, registers it with `ActionTracker` with the toast texts "Affinity updated" (success) and "Could not update selected process affinity." (failure, PROC-058 forms for EPERM: "Permission denied"), and closes the dialog at once. Toasts show in the parent window. A target that exited is rejected by engine revalidation (identity toast from PROC-058).
- Validation text is also the OK tooltip while OK is disabled.
- Strings appended to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` with keys `pwn-affinity-*` (title, subtitle loading suffix, All processors, CPU list, placeholder, group labels, validation, invalid-list helper, cpuset and offline tooltips, OK, Cancel, toasts).
- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/mod.rs`: `pub mod affinity;`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake topology with two L3 groups (CPUs 0-7,16-23 and 8-15,24-31, SMT pairs n and n+16) **When** the dialog opens for one target **Then** it shows two groups "CCD 0: CPU 0-7,16-23" and "CCD 1: CPU 8-15,24-31" with 8 tiles each, CPU 0 above CPU 16 in the first tile.
- **Given** the target mask 0-3 **When** the affinity payload arrives **Then** CPUs 0-3 are checked, the field reads `0-3` and "All processors" is indeterminate.
- **Given** the dialog **When** CPU 5 is checked **Then** the field reads `0-3,5`.
- **Given** the field text `0-1,4` **When** typed **Then** exactly CPUs 0, 1, 4 are checked.
- **Given** the field text `0-x` **When** typed **Then** OK is disabled, the helper text shows and the grid is unchanged.
- **Given** every CPU unchecked **When** rendered **Then** the validation line shows and OK is disabled with that tooltip.
- **Given** a cpuset limit 0-7 **When** rendered **Then** CPU 8 is disabled and unchecked with tooltip "Not allowed by the process's cpuset".
- **Given** CPU 31 offline **Then** it is disabled with tooltip "CPU is offline".
- **Given** a valid selection **When** Enter is pressed **Then** one `ActionRequest` with `SetAffinity` and the captured target is sent and the dialog closes.
- **Given** the dialog is open **When** Esc is pressed **Then** it closes and nothing is sent.
- **Given** the dialog opens and closes **Then** `Demand.affinity_targets` contains the key while open and not after.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/affinity.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/mod.rs`, `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: chain-edit lines.

## Tests
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::affinity_grid_groups_by_l3`
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::affinity_list_field_sync_both_ways`
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::affinity_ok_disabled_when_empty_and_message`
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::affinity_cpuset_limited_cpus_disabled`
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::affinity_invalid_list_text`
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::affinity_demand_registered_and_removed`
- `windows::affinity::tests::parse_and_format_cpu_list` (proptest: `format(parse(format(s))) == format(s)` for random sets up to 1024 CPUs; rejects `""`, `"a"`, `"3-1"`, `"0,,1"`).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: invalid list text (above); engine failures as PROC-058 toasts in the parent window.
- Validity: loading state until `DetailsSnapshot.affinity` has the key (at most one 1 Hz read, ADR-008).
- Accessibility: every checkbox has its label as accessible name; full keyboard model above; validation text doubles as OK tooltip.
- Performance: at most 1,024 checkboxes; rebuild the grid only on state change; 32 CPUs render about 70 elements.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Mixed CPUs use `TlCheckbox`'s indeterminate state (UI-FND-011); kit `Checkbox::indeterminate` at `gpui-component/crates/base/src/checkbox.rs:106`.
- `InputState::text()` at `gpui-component/crates/base/src/input/base/state.rs:1272` (read with `text()`, not `value()`).

- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_dialogs_process`.

title: Set Affinity with several targets, mixed marks and thread targets
description:
## Context
Extends the Set Affinity dialog to several targets with mixed marks, to thread targets, and to app rows (P2). Sources: UI-PWN-022, UI-PWN-021 (subtitles, thread toasts), PROC-069, PROC-067, PROC-079, R-097, R-039.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/affinity.rs`:
- Subtitle forms: one process `firefox (PID 4321)`; several processes `4 processes`; one thread `Thread 4325 of firefox (PID 4321)`; several threads `3 threads of firefox (PID 4321)`; app row `Firefox (34 processes)`.
- Targets may be `ActionTarget::Thread { process, tid }` (opened from the Threads tab, E23-017). For thread targets the initial mask comes from the Threads payload `ThreadRow.cpus` of each tid (the caller passes `initial` masks); cpuset limit from the process's `AffinityInfo`.
- Initial marks with several targets: a CPU is ON when every target has it, MIXED when only some do, OFF when none.
- Click cycle: MIXED -> ON, ON -> OFF, OFF -> ON. Only "Reset" returns CPUs to MIXED.
- Footer gains, at its left end and only with several targets, `TlButton` Ghost sm "Reset" with Lucide `rotate-ccw` 12 px (`AffinityReset`), which restores the initial state of every CPU.
- The CPU list field shows only ON CPUs; while any CPU is MIXED, the helper "Mixed CPUs keep each process's current setting" shows under the field in `t_xs` `text_secondary`. A MIXED checkbox has the tooltip "Set for some of the selected processes".
- "Nothing checked" with several targets means no ON and no MIXED CPU.
- `fn resulting_masks(&self) -> SmallVec<[(CpuSet, SmallVec<[ActionTarget; 4]>); 4]>`: per target, ON set, OFF cleared, MIXED kept from that target's current mask; targets with equal result masks grouped.
- OK sends one `ActionRequest` per group; the `ActionTracker` joins them under one toast id (the first request's `ActionId`), so one toast shows. Toast texts: one process "Affinity updated"; several "Selected process affinity updated."; failure "Could not update selected process affinity."; partial "Affinity updated for 3 of 4 processes. 1 failed: permission denied" (the "Retry as administrator" button appears from P3 through the tracker); threads "Thread affinity updated".
- The P1 rule "hidden on multi-select" in the row menu is lifted: chain edit `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/menu.rs` so item 7 is built on multi-select with the same label (UI-PRC-013 "M: same (P2)").
- New strings appended under `pwn-affinity-*` in `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 3 targets with masks {0,1}, {0,2}, {0} **When** opened **Then** CPU 0 is ON, CPUs 1 and 2 are MIXED, the rest OFF.
- **Given** CPU 1 MIXED **When** clicked **Then** it becomes ON; clicked again OFF; again ON.
- **Given** changed marks **When** Reset is clicked **Then** every CPU returns to its initial state including MIXED.
- **Given** one target **When** rendered **Then** no Reset button shows.
- **Given** 3 targets whose result masks are A, A, B **When** OK **Then** 2 requests are sent and the tracker shows 1 toast id.
- **Given** a MIXED CPU **When** the field renders **Then** it lists only ON CPUs and the mixed helper text shows.
- **Given** 2 thread targets of PID 4321 **When** opened **Then** the subtitle reads `2 threads of firefox (PID 4321)` and OK sends `Thread` targets; success toast "Thread affinity updated".
- **Given** two process rows selected **When** the row menu opens **Then** "Set Affinity…" is built.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/affinity.rs`: extend.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/menu.rs`: lift the multi-select rule for item 7 (chain edit).
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs`: tests.

## Tests

- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::affinity_mixed_click_sets_all`

title: Custom priority dialog and Realtime confirmation (windows/priority.rs)
description:
## Context
The Custom priority dialog "tasklens Set Priority" with policy, nice and realtime priority, and its use of the Realtime confirmation. Sources: UI-PWN-023, UI-PWN-024, PROC-066 (P2 Custom, Realtime, Idle), PROC-069, PROC-079, R-038, UI-PRC-014 row "Set Priority > Realtime".

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/windows/priority.rs`:
- `pub struct PriorityDialog` (Entity): `targets`, `policy: Entity<SelectState<..>>`, `nice: Entity<SliderState>`, realtime `TlStepper` state, `initial: (SchedPolicy, i8, u8)`.
- `pub fn open(targets: SmallVec<[ActionTarget; 1]>, subtitle: SharedString, initial: (SchedPolicy, i8, u8), parent: AnyWindowHandle, cx: &mut App)` opening `PwnWindow::SetPriority`: modal, title "tasklens Set Priority", width 440, not resizable, key context `PriorityDialog`.
- Layout: subtitle row 24 (`t_sm` `text_secondary`, same forms as Set Affinity: `firefox (PID 4321)`, `4 processes`, `Thread 4325 of firefox (PID 4321)`, `Firefox (34 processes)`); labels column 128 wide `t_base` `text_secondary`; controls width 260; rows 32:
  - "Policy": `TlSelect` items "Normal (SCHED_OTHER)", "Batch (SCHED_BATCH)", "Idle (SCHED_IDLE)", "Realtime FIFO (SCHED_FIFO)", "Realtime round-robin (SCHED_RR)". For app rows the select has tooltip "Applies to the app's current processes".
  - "Nice": `TlSlider` -20..=19 step 1, current value as text right of it (`t_base`, tabular, width 28, right-aligned); an 18 px row below with "-20 (highest)" and "19 (lowest)" in `t_xs` `text_secondary`. Slider tooltip "With autogroup on, nice only orders processes within the same session.".
  - "Realtime priority": `TlStepper` 1..=99, width 72.
  - Warning line, FIFO and RR only: Lucide `triangle-alert` 14 px `status.warning`, "Realtime priority can freeze the desktop if the process spins." `t_sm` `text_primary`; second line "Child processes start at normal priority." `t_xs` `text_secondary`.
  - Footer 52: "Cancel" (Secondary) and "Set priority" (Primary).
- Enable rules: Normal and Batch: Nice on, Realtime priority off. Idle: Nice and Realtime priority off, Nice tooltip "Not used by this policy". FIFO and RR: Nice off (same tooltip), Realtime priority on, warning line shown.
- Initial values from the caller (the right-clicked target's General payload, thread row, or `ProcessRecord.nice` with policy Other).
- Keys (`PriorityDialog`): Tab order Policy, Nice, Realtime priority, Cancel, Set priority; Left/Right slider 1, PgUp/PgDn 5 (`PrioritySliderStep`), Home/End -20 and 19; Up/Down step the stepper; Enter "Set priority" (`PriorityApply`); Esc cancels.
- "Set priority" dispatch:
  - Normal or Batch, same policy as initial: one request `SetNice(n)`.
  - Normal or Batch, different policy: `SetSched { policy, rt_prio: 0 }`, and when its final event is `Succeeded`, `SetNice(n)`; both under one toast id.
  - Idle: `SetSched { policy: Idle, rt_prio: 0 }`.
  - FIFO or RR: first `pages::processes::confirm::confirm(ConfirmKind::Realtime, targets, window, cx)` (UI-PRC-014 row: title "Set realtime priority?", text "Realtime priority can freeze the desktop if the process spins. Set it anyway?", buttons "Set realtime" (danger) and "Cancel"); on confirm `SetSched { policy, rt_prio }`; on cancel nothing is sent and the dialog stays open.
  - The dialog closes when the request is sent (after the confirmation for realtime).
- Toasts: one target "Priority updated"; several targets the PROC-069 forms ("Priority updated for 3 of 4 processes. 1 failed: permission denied"); thread targets "Thread priority updated". EPERM is not blocked in the dialog; the engine's failure gives the PROC-058 toast "Permission denied".
- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/mod.rs`: `pub mod priority;`; strings `pwn-priority-*` appended to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** policy Idle selected **When** rendered **Then** Nice and Realtime priority are disabled and Nice has tooltip "Not used by this policy".
- **Given** policy FIFO **When** rendered **Then** Realtime priority is enabled and the warning lines show.
- **Given** initial Normal nice 0 **When** nice set to 5 and "Set priority" pressed **Then** exactly one request `SetNice(5)` is sent.
- **Given** initial Normal **When** Batch with nice 3 is applied **Then** `SetSched { Batch, 0 }` is sent, and after its `Succeeded` event `SetNice(3)` is sent, both under one toast id.
- **Given** RR priority 10 **When** "Set priority" pressed **Then** the Realtime confirmation opens first and nothing is sent yet; Confirm sends `SetSched { Rr, 10 }`.
- **Given** the Realtime confirmation **When** Cancel **Then** nothing is sent.
- **Given** the slider focused at 0 **When** PgUp **Then** the value is 5.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/priority.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs`: tests.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/mod.rs`, `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: chain-edit lines.

## Tests
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::priority_dialog_enables_fields_by_policy`
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::priority_dialog_dispatch_same_policy_nice_only`
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::priority_dialog_policy_change_then_nice`
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::priority_dialog_realtime_confirms_first`
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::realtime_from_custom_dialog_confirms_first`
- `tests/ui_dialogs_process.rs::realtime_cancel_sends_nothing`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: PROC-058 failure forms; nothing validated client-side beyond ranges.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: slider accessible name "Nice value", stepper "Realtime priority"; disabled reasons in tooltips.
- Performance: static dialog.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Security: changes scheduling of user processes; realtime always confirms first (regression tests above).
- `SliderState` at `gpui-component/crates/base/src/slider.rs:170`.
- `ConfirmKind::Realtime` and `confirm(..)` are E22's `pages/processes/confirm.rs` (E22-A2).
- The menu item "Custom…" and its handler are E23-007; the Realtime menu item itself is E22's (UI-PRC-020).

title: E27-A1 System table frame
Services: ServicesDelegate skeleton, row kinds, columns, sort and column persistence
description:
## Context
The Services table is a `TlTreeTable` driven by a `ServicesDelegate` over `Snapshot.services`: two manager group rows, unit rows, and child process rows under expanded units. The engine sorts, filters and flattens (`ServicesSnapshot.rows: Arc<[SysRow]>`); the delegate maps rows to kinds, owns expansion, defines the 19 columns and persists sort and columns. This bead writes the delegate skeleton and the column model; cells come in the next two beads. Sources: UI-SYS-002 (delegate table), UI-SYS-013, UI-SYS-014 (expand persistence), SYS-003, SYS-017, R-011, R-075, APP-018, ADR-008 (`service_cgroup_stats`), R-119, canonical table (a) `[sort.services]`, `[columns.services]`, `[services] group_expanded`.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/delegate.rs` and `pub mod delegate;` in `pages/services/mod.rs`.

```rust
pub struct ServicesDelegate {
    snap: Arc<ServicesSnapshot>,          // last accepted
    processes: Arc<ProcessSnapshot>,      // for child rows (UnitProcess)
    rows: Arc<[SysRow]>,                  // = snap.rows
    row_index: FxHashMap<SysNodeId, usize>, // rebuilt in install()
    expanded: FxHashSet<SysNodeId>,       // UI-owned; groups seeded from UiState services.group_expanded
    layout: ColumnLayout,                 // E18
    sort: SortSpec,
    backend: ServiceBackend,              // Systemd | OpenRc, from snap.backend
}
impl TreeTableDelegate for ServicesDelegate { type RowId = SysNodeId; ... }
impl SysDelegate for ServicesDelegate { ... mask() = ComponentMask::SERVICES | ComponentMask::PROCESSES ... }
pub fn services_columns() -> &'static [ColumnDef];
pub fn cgroup_stats_wanted(layout: &ColumnLayout) -> bool;
```

Row mapping:
- `row_kind`: `SysNodeId::ServiceGroup(_)` -> `RowKind::GroupHeader`; `Unit(_)` -> `RowKind::Unit`; `UnitProcess(..)` -> `RowKind::Process`.
- `row_depth`: `SysRow.depth` (groups 0, units 1, child processes 2).
- `row_expandable`: group -> `Some(expanded)`, except `None` when that manager's `ManagerState.state` is `Unavailable`; unit -> `Some(expanded)` when `SysRow.has_children`, else `None`; child -> `None`.
- `selectable`: true for `Unit` and `UnitProcess`, false for group rows (UI-SYS-002). Group rows still take keyboard focus.
- `header_lines`: `HeaderLines::One`. `header_total`: always false. `columns_fixed`: false.
- `on_toggle_expand(id)`: flip `id` in `expanded`, send `SysQuery::set_expanded` with the set as `Arc<[SysNodeId]>`; for a group id also write `UiState` `[services] group_expanded = { system, user }` (save debounced by the store).
- `on_sort(col)`: direction rule of `TlTreeTable` (same column toggles, new column starts ascending), send `SysQuery::set_sort`, write `UiState` `[sort.services] column, ascending`. Default sort `name` ascending (R-011). The engine keeps groups grouped and sorts child rows by PID ascending always.
- `on_columns_changed(layout)`: write `UiState` `[columns.services]` (order, visible, widths) through the E18 column persistence by id, then update `Demand.service_cgroup_stats = cgroup_stats_wanted(layout)` through `DemandAggregator`.
- `cgroup_stats_wanted`: true when any of `cpu`, `memory`, `disk`, `tasks` is visible.
- `install(snap)`: replace `snap`, `rows`, `processes`, rebuild `row_index`, set `backend`.

Columns (`services_columns()`, in this order; `ColumnId` strings are the spec ids):

| Id | Header label | Default width | Min width | Align | Visible by default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | "Name" | 250 | 120 | left | yes |
| `display_name` | "Display name" | 300 | 60 | left | yes |
| `status` | "Status" | 100 | 80 | left | yes |
| `startup_type` | "Startup type" | 120 | 80 | left | yes |
| `pid` | "PID" | 80 | template "999999" | right | yes |
| `user` | "User" | 200 | 60 | left | yes |
| `path` | "Path" | 260 | 60 | left | yes |
| `manager` | "Manager" | 80 | 60 | left | no |
| `unit_type` | "Unit type" | 90 | 60 | left | no |
| `sub_state` | "Sub state" | 100 | 60 | left | no |
| `load_state` | "Load state" | 100 | 60 | left | no |
| `cpu` | "CPU" | 63 | template "100.0%" | right | no |
| `memory` | "Memory" | 92 | template "999.99 MiB" | right | no |
| `disk` | "Disk" | 82 | template "xxx MiB/s" | right | no |
| `tasks` | "Tasks" | 72 | template "999999" | right | no |
| `active_since` | "Active since" | 150 | template "9999-99-99 99:99:99" | left | no |
| `unit_file` | "Unit file" | 300 | 60 | left | no |
| `triggered_by` | "Triggered by" | 200 | 60 | left | no |
| `description` | "Description" | 300 | 60 | left | no |

`ColumnSpec` kinds: `pid` and `tasks` are integer/count (`tnum`), `cpu` percent, `memory` memory size, `disk` rate; all others text. Heat colouring applies to `cpu`, `memory`, `disk` when `appearance.heat_coloring` is on (process references, ADR-009); `tasks` is never tinted. `tables.dim_zero_values` and `tables.column_separators` apply (R-075). The column picker lists these columns without headings; View > Columns acts on this table while the Services tab is active (APP-018, E21's menu).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the default layout **When** `services_columns()` is read **Then** the seven visible columns and their widths are Name 250, Display name 300, Status 100, Startup type 120, PID 80, User 200, Path 260.
- **Given** a snapshot with a group, a unit with children and a child **When** `row_kind` is asked per row **Then** it returns GroupHeader, Unit, Process.
- **Given** the user manager is `Unavailable` **When** `row_expandable` is asked for its group row **Then** it returns None.
- **Given** a group row **When** `selectable` is asked **Then** it returns false.
- **Given** the Memory column is made visible **When** `on_columns_changed` runs **Then** the next `Demand` has `service_cgroup_stats = true`; hiding CPU, Memory, Disk and Tasks again sets it false.
- **Given** the user clicks the Status header **When** `on_sort` runs **Then** one `SetSysTableQuery` with sort `status` ascending is sent and `[sort.services]` is written.
- **Given** the user collapses the System group **When** `on_toggle_expand` runs **Then** `UiState.services.group_expanded.system` is false and one query with the reduced `expanded` set is sent.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/delegate.rs`: create `ServicesDelegate` (trait impls with cell bodies left as `CellOut::empty()` for this bead), `services_columns`, `cgroup_stats_wanted`
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/mod.rs`: add `pub mod delegate;`
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_services.rs`: add the tests below

## Tests
- `ui_services::services_default_columns_and_widths`.
- `ui_services::services_row_kinds_and_selectable`.
- `ui_services::services_cgroup_demand_follows_columns`.
- `ui_services::services_sort_persists_and_sends_query`.
- `ui_services::group_expand_state_persisted`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: resource columns carry `Validity` from the snapshot (drawn in the cells bead).
- Accessibility: header cells use the label as accessible name; sort tooltip "Sorted ascending" / "Sorted descending" comes from E18.
- Performance: no sort, filter or allocation per frame; `row_index` rebuilt once per accepted snapshot (about 300 rows).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- `ServicesSnapshot`, `SysRow`, `SysNodeId`, `UnitRef`, `Manager`, `ManagerState`, `ServiceBackend` (`backend: Systemd | OpenRc`) are `tl-model` types (E03-A2, ARCHITECTURE ADR-003 "per-component fields"). If `ColumnId` has no constants for the Services column strings, stop and report (open item B8-E27-5); do not add them to `tl-model` from this bead.
- `UiState` writes go through the state store hooks E20-A2 exposes (`settings_global.rs`).
- Large-file rule: `delegate.rs` grows over three beads; commit before building or testing.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`, for example `... cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_services`.

title: Services: group and unit row cells, icons, status overlay, tooltips
description:
## Context
This bead fills the Services delegate's cell output for the two manager group rows and for unit rows: labels with counts, the unavailable and reconnecting group states, unit icons, status cells with the pending overlay, startup-type colours, blank PID at 0, tooltips and accessible names. Sources: UI-SYS-014, UI-SYS-015, UI-SYS-003, UI-SYS-018 (overlay labels), SYS-001, SYS-003, SYS-005, D-011, R-050, table (d).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/delegate.rs`, fill `cell`, `name_cell`, `row_flags` and `row_tooltip` for `ServiceGroup` and `Unit` rows, and add:

```rust
pub fn unit_icon(kind: UnitKind) -> IconName;
pub fn startup_type_tone(t: StartupType) -> LabelTone;    // sys_status::LabelTone
pub fn service_sys_status(s: ServiceStatus) -> SysStatus; // sys_status::SysStatus
pub fn overlay_label(tag: ActionKindTag) -> Option<SharedString>;
pub fn group_label(manager: Manager, n: u32, state: ManagerState, out: &mut String);
pub fn unit_accessible_name(unit: &UnitRecord, out: &mut String);
```

Group rows (shared group row painter of E18/E22: chevron 16, label `t_md` 600 `text_primary`, `header` band across the full row, no cells, 1 px `divider` top line except on the first row):
- Text "System services (N)" or "User services (N)"; N counts unit rows after all filters (`ServicesSnapshot.counts` per manager, as the engine computes), thin-space (U+2009) grouped.
- Manager `Unavailable`: "System services" (or "User services"), then `sp3`, a `circle-alert` icon 14 px in `status.warning`, then "System manager not available" (or "User manager not available") in `text_secondary`. No count, no chevron.
- Manager `Reconnecting`: label plus " (reconnecting…)" in `text_secondary`; the unit rows under it get the `STALE` flag (all text `text_secondary`).
- A group with zero unit rows after filtering is not in `rows` (the engine hides it); the delegate does nothing extra.
- Accessible name: "System services, 214 units, expanded" (or "collapsed").

Unit rows (depth 1):

| Column | Content | Style |
|---|---|---|
| name | chevron (only when `has_children`), unit icon 16, unit id | `text_primary` `t_base`, ellipsis at end |
| display_name | `description`; empty shows nothing | `text_primary` |
| status | `status_cell(status_look(service_sys_status(status)), ..)`; while an action is pending on this unit, the label is `overlay_label(tag)` with a filled `status.info` dot and `text_primary` | |
| startup_type | word | tone from `startup_type_tone` |
| pid | `main_pid`, right, `tnum`; blank when 0 | |
| user | owner name | ellipsis |
| path | path per SYS-003 for the unit type | ellipsis at end; full value in the cell tooltip |
| manager | "System" or "User" | |
| unit_type | "Service", "Socket", "Timer", "Mount", "Automount", "Path", "Target", "Swap", "Slice", "Scope" | |
| sub_state, load_state | raw systemd words | |
| cpu, memory, disk, tasks | `units.rs` formats: `%.1f%%` ("0%" at measured zero), IEC two decimals, MiB/s one decimal, thin-space count | `…` while warming up, `-` for units without a cgroup (validity glyphs from E18 `cells.rs`) |
| active_since | `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` local | |
| unit_file | `fragment_path` | |
| triggered_by | unit ids joined by ", " | |
| description | `description` | |

- `unit_icon` (Lucide): service `cog`, socket `plug`, timer `clock`, mount and automount `hard-drive`, path `folder-open`, target `circle-dot`, swap `memory-stick`, slice and scope `box`. Colour `text_secondary`; on a selected row `text_selected_secondary`.
- `startup_type_tone`: Enabled, Enabled (runtime), Static, Indirect, Generated, Transient, Alias, Linked -> Primary; Disabled and "-" -> Secondary; Masked -> Warning.
- `service_sys_status`: Running, Active, Starting, Stopping, Reloading, Stopped, Failed, Maintenance map one to one onto `SysStatus`.
- `overlay_label`: Start "Starting…", Stop "Stopping…", Restart "Restarting…", Reload "Reloading…"; ResetFailed and SetStartup -> None (no overlay).
- Status cell tooltip: "<ActiveState> (<SubState>)", for example "active (running)".
- Name cell tooltip (600 ms): three lines "<Description>", "<FragmentPath>", "Manager: System" (or "Manager: User").
- Row accessible name: "<id>, <Status>, <Startup type>".
- States: default `list_bg`/`row_alt`; hover `row_hover`; selected `row_selected` with `text_selected_primary`; failed units keep the danger status label when selected.
- Text: strings from the snapshot are `Arc<str>` wrapped in `SharedString` without copying; numbers go through `CellTextCache` keyed by `(SysNodeId, ColumnId)`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a socket unit **When** its name cell renders **Then** the icon is `plug` at 16 px in `text_secondary`.
- **Given** a unit with `main_pid = 0` **When** the PID cell renders **Then** it is empty.
- **Given** a Masked unit **When** the Startup type cell renders **Then** "Masked" is drawn in `status.warning`.
- **Given** a Start pending on a stopped unit **When** its row renders **Then** the Status cell shows a filled `status.info` dot and "Starting…".
- **Given** the user manager `Unavailable` **When** its group row renders **Then** it reads "User services" with the warning icon and "User manager not available", and has no chevron.
- **Given** the system manager `Reconnecting` **When** rows render **Then** the group label ends with " (reconnecting…)" and its unit rows draw all text in `text_secondary`.
- **Given** a Failed unit selected **When** it renders **Then** the Status label stays `status.danger`.
- **Given** a unit with no cgroup and the CPU column visible **When** the CPU cell renders **Then** it shows `-`.

## Files

- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_services.rs`: add the tests below
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append every string above (keys `services-sys014-<slug>`, `services-sys015-<slug>`, `services-sys018-<slug>`)

## Tests

- `ui_services::unit_row_pid_blank_when_zero`.
- `ui_services::unit_row_masked_warning_color`.
- `ui_services::unit_row_pending_overlay_label`.
- `ui_services::group_row_unavailable_label`.
- `ui_services::group_row_reconnecting_stale_units`.
- `ui_services::unit_row_tooltips_and_accessible_name`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A (manager failures show in the group row)
- Validity: resource cells show `…` (WarmingUp), `-` (no cgroup), stale at 60% opacity (E18 rule); Reconnecting marks rows stale.
- Accessibility: group and row accessible names as above; chevron tooltip "Expand" / "Collapse" (E18).
- Performance: no allocation for unchanged cells; strings are shared `Arc<str>`.
- Privacy: user names of other users are shown but never logged.

title: Services: child process rows and process demand
description:
## Context
An expanded unit row lists the processes in its cgroup subtree as child rows (depth 2), drawn with the process table's cells mapped onto the Services columns. While any unit is expanded on a visible Services tab, the page asks the engine for the process sweep and the visible child keys. Sources: UI-SYS-016, SYS-001 (cgroup subtree), SYS-006, PROC-057 (menu reuse), UI-PRC-002, UI-PRC-004, D-004 (Memory is RssAnon), ADR-008 (`process_table`, `detail_keys`).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/delegate.rs`, fill `cell`, `name_cell`, `row_flags` and `row_tooltip` for `SysNodeId::UnitProcess(unit, key)` rows, and add:

```rust
/// Services column -> what the child row shows.
pub fn child_column(col: ColumnId) -> ChildCell;
pub enum ChildCell { Name, Description, Pid, User, ExePath, Cpu, Memory, Disk, Threads, Empty }
/// Demand contribution of the Services page.
pub fn child_demand(expanded_units: usize, visible_child_keys: &[ProcessKey]) -> (bool, SmallVec<[ProcessKey; 64]>);
```

Column mapping (exact):

| Services column | Child row content |
|---|---|
| name | process icon 16 and display name (processes naming, PROC-007) |
| display_name | process Description |
| status | empty |
| startup_type | empty |
| pid | PID |
| user | process user |
| path | exe path |
| cpu | process CPU |
| memory | process Memory (RssAnon, D-004) |
| disk | process Disk |
| tasks | process Threads |
| every other column | empty |

- The record is found by `ProcessKey` in `Snapshot.processes.records` (sorted by `ProcessKey`, binary search). Paint delegates to the process table's `ProcessRowCells` (E22-A1) with the column mapping above, so formats, validity glyphs (`…`, lock), heat tint, and the new and exited highlight match the Processes tab.
- A key no longer in the process snapshot draws the row as exited (E22 rule) until the next services update removes it after its linger time.
- Processes in nested cgroups appear flat under the unit, sorted by PID ascending (the engine's row order; the delegate does not sort).
- `child_demand`: returns `(true, keys)` when at least one unit row is expanded, with `keys` = the visible child keys reported by `on_visible_range` (max 512, E18), else `(false, empty)`. The page sends `Demand.process_table = first` and adds `keys` to `Demand.detail_keys` through `DemandAggregator`; both clear when no unit is expanded.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** an expanded unit with child pid 812 **When** the child row renders **Then** the Status and Startup type cells are empty and the PID cell shows 812.
- **Given** the Memory column visible **When** a child row renders **Then** the cell shows the process RssAnon formatted IEC two decimals.
- **Given** no unit is expanded **When** demand is computed **Then** `process_table` is false and no child keys are added.
- **Given** one unit expanded with 3 visible child rows **When** demand is computed **Then** `process_table` is true and `detail_keys` contains those 3 keys.
- **Given** a child whose process exited **When** the row renders before the next services update **Then** it uses the exited style.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/delegate.rs`: change, child rows and `child_demand`
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_services.rs`: add the tests below

## Tests
- `ui_services::child_rows_column_mapping`.
- `ui_services::expanding_unit_enables_process_demand`.
- `ui_services::collapsing_last_unit_clears_process_demand`.
- `ui_services::child_row_exited_style`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: as process rows (E22): `…` warming up, lock for restricted fields.
- Accessibility: as process rows.
- Performance: the process sweep runs only while a unit is expanded on a visible Services tab; lookup is a binary search per visible child row.
- Privacy: exe paths of other users' processes are shown, never logged (ADR-015).

## Notes
- `ProcessRowCells` is the name in UI-SYS-016 and `docs/ui/INDEX.md` for the shared process cell painter; use the name and signature E22-A1 delivers.
- The child-row context menu and Ctrl+E handling are in the Services menu and page beads.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`, for example `... cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_services`.

title: Services: filter strip and Unit types dropdown
description:
## Context
Above the Services table sits a 28 px filter strip: four state toggles, the "Unit types" dropdown, two manager toggles and "Remove filters". Each change sends the query at once; state and unit-type choices persist in `settings.toml`. This bead writes the strip, its state and the dropdown in `pages/services/filter_strip.rs`. Sources: UI-SYS-011, UI-SYS-012, SYS-002, SYS-004, R-019, canonical table (a) `[services] unit_types`, `filter_states`, UI-FND-010 (`Segment` look), UI-FND-022 (`TlMenu`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/filter_strip.rs` and `pub mod filter_strip;` in `pages/services/mod.rs`.

```rust
pub struct ServiceFilterState {
    pub states: SmallVec<[StateFilterArg; 4]>,   // none on = all states
    pub unit_types: SmallVec<[UnitTypeArg; 10]>, // from settings services.unit_types
    pub system: bool,                            // session only, default true
    pub user: bool,                              // session only, default true
}
impl ServiceFilterState {
    pub fn from_settings(s: &ServicesSettings) -> Self;
    pub fn is_default(&self) -> bool;           // states empty, types = the default four, system && user
    pub fn to_filter(&self) -> ServiceFilter;   // tl_model::table::ServiceFilter { states, unit_types, system, user }
    pub fn toggle_state(&mut self, s: StateFilterArg);
    pub fn toggle_manager(&mut self, m: ManagerArg);
    /// Returns false (and changes nothing) when it would uncheck the last checked type.
    pub fn toggle_unit_type(&mut self, k: UnitTypeArg) -> bool;
    pub fn reset_unit_types(&mut self);
    pub fn remove_filters(&mut self);           // states off, default four types, system and user on; text filter untouched
}
pub fn render_strip(state: &ServiceFilterState, disabled: bool, menu_open: bool, openrc: bool,
                    window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App) -> AnyElement;
pub fn unit_types_menu(state: &ServiceFilterState, menu: PopupMenu, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<PopupMenu>) -> PopupMenu;
```

Defaults (canonical table a): `unit_types = ["service", "socket", "timer", "mount"]`, `filter_states = []`.

Strip anatomy (height 28, `toolbar` background, padding x `sp4`, gap `sp3`, 1 px `divider` bottom border; groups separated by a 1 x 16 `divider` rule with `sp3` on both sides; controls 24 high, 2 px above and below):

| Part | Widget | Text | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| State toggles | `TlButton::Segment` x 4, height 24, padding x `sp5`, `r_sm`, label `t_sm` | "Running", "Failed", "Stopped", "Disabled" | multi-select; none on = all states |
| Unit types | `TlButton::Ghost` sm with `chevron-down` `i_xs` caret | "Unit types", plus " (N)" when not all ten types are on, N = number of checked types | opens the dropdown; shows pressed while the menu is open |
| Manager toggles | `TlButton::Segment` x 2 | "System", "User" | both on by default |
| Remove filters | `TlButton::Ghost` sm, icon `funnel-x` `i_sm` | "Remove filters" | disabled when `is_default()`; tooltip "Show all units" |

`Segment` look (UI-FND-010): off = `toolbar` fill with 1 px `divider` border; on = `accent` at alpha 0.25 with 1 px `accent` border; hover `tab_hover`; keyboard focus ring. Each toggle sets the kit button's toggled state so it reads as a toggle.

Dropdown (`TlMenu`, min width 180, anchored below the button): check items "Services", "Sockets", "Timers", "Mounts", "Automounts", "Paths", "Targets", "Swaps", "Slices", "Scopes", a separator, "Reset to default". Clicking an item toggles it and keeps the menu open (item `on_click` plus `PopupMenu::rebuild`, `gpui-component/crates/component/src/menu/popup_menu.rs:753`); Esc or a click outside closes it; Up/Down move; Space or Enter toggles. Unchecking the last checked item is refused: it stays checked and a Warning toast "At least one unit type must stay selected" shows.

Behaviour:
- Handlers (wired by the Services page): `ServicesToggleStateFilter`, `ServicesToggleManagerFilter`, `ServicesToggleUnitType`, `ServicesResetUnitTypes`, `ServicesRemoveFilters`. Each mutates the state, sends `SysQuery::set_services_filter(state.to_filter())` at once (no debounce), and for states and unit types writes `settings.toml` `services.filter_states` / `services.unit_types` through the settings global (debounced save, ADR-011). System and User are never persisted.
- State toggles combine with OR; the result combines with the text filter using AND; child rows inherit their unit's state (all engine-side, SYS-004).
- Both System and User off is allowed; the table then shows the "No matches" empty state.
- `disabled = true` (while the skeleton shows) disables every control.
- `openrc = true` (P4) hides the Unit types button and the System and User toggles (used by the OpenRC bead).
- Tab order: state toggles left to right, Unit types, System, User, Remove filters. No key bindings.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** Running and Failed on and the text "ssh" **When** the strip sends its query **Then** the fake engine receives `ServiceFilter { states: [Running, Failed], .. }` and filter "ssh" in the same `SysTableQuery`.
- **Given** only "Services" is checked **When** the user unchecks it **Then** it stays checked, no query is sent, and the toast "At least one unit type must stay selected" shows.
- **Given** the dropdown is open **When** the user clicks "Timers" **Then** the menu stays open and "Timers" toggles.
- **Given** a non-default strip and the text filter "ssh" **When** "Remove filters" is pressed **Then** states are off, unit types are the default four, System and User are on, and the text filter is still "ssh".
- **Given** six unit types checked **When** the strip renders **Then** the button reads "Unit types (6)".
- **Given** the strip at its defaults **When** it renders **Then** "Remove filters" is disabled.
- **Given** the user toggles "Failed" **When** the settings store saves **Then** `services.filter_states = ["failed"]`; toggling "User" off writes nothing.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/filter_strip.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/mod.rs`: add `pub mod filter_strip;`
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_services.rs`: add the tests below
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append every string above (keys `services-sys011-<slug>`, `services-sys012-<slug>`)

## Tests
- `ui_services::strip_state_or_text_and`.
- `ui_services::remove_filters_restores_defaults`.
- `ui_services::strip_persists_states_and_types`.
- `ui_services::unit_types_last_item_refused`.
- `ui_services::unit_types_menu_stays_open_on_toggle`.
- `ui_services::unit_types_count_suffix`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the refusal toast only.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: each chip is a toggle named by its label; the Unit types button shows pressed while its menu is open; full keyboard path through Tab and the menu keys.
- Performance: a click sends one command; no UI filtering; the menu is built on open only.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- `StateFilterArg`, `ManagerArg`, `UnitTypeArg` and the strip actions are in `pages/services/actions.rs` (E27 actions bead).
- `TlButton`, `TlMenu`, `ToastQueue` come from E15-A1, E16-A3, E16-A2.
- Strings: slug = first five words lowercased, non-alphanumeric runs replaced by `-`.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`, for example `... cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_services`.

title: Services: Copy row block and copy source
description:
## Context
"Copy row" (Ctrl+C) on a unit row copies a fixed seven-line block; "Copy rows as table" copies TSV; child process rows copy the process "Copy details" block. This bead implements the Services side of the shared copy commands in `pages/services/copy.rs`. Sources: UI-SYS-020, UI-SYS-006, SYS-009, R-012, ADR-015 (exports and copy).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/copy.rs` and `pub mod copy;` in `pages/services/mod.rs`.

```rust
pub fn block_service(unit: &UnitRecord, out: &mut String);
pub fn services_copy_texts() -> CopyTexts;  // sys_copy::CopyTexts
impl SysCopySource for ServicesDelegate { type RowId = SysNodeId; ... }
```

`block_service` writes exactly (no trailing newline):

```
Name: <id>
Display name: <Description>
Status: <Status>
Start type: <Startup type>
PID: <MainPID>
User: <User>
Binary: <ExecStart[0].path>
```

- `<Status>` is the status label ("Running", "Failed", …); `<Startup type>` the startup word; `<MainPID>` decimal.
- Empty values print nothing after "Label: " (so "PID: " when MainPID is 0, "Binary: " when no ExecStart).
- `services_copy_texts()`: `row_ok` "Service details copied.", `row_failed` "Could not copy service details.", `nothing_selected` "Select a service row first.".
- `SysCopySource for ServicesDelegate`:
  - `copy_rows`: selected ids in view order without `ServiceGroup` ids.
  - `write_block`: `Unit` -> `block_service`; `UnitProcess(_, key)` -> the process "Copy details" block from E22 (the function E22-A2 exposes for the Processes "Copy details" command).
  - `visible_columns`, `write_cell`: the visible Services columns and the cell text as shown; validity glyph cells write nothing; child rows write their mapped values (E27 child-row bead).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** sshd.service, "OpenSSH Daemon", Running, Enabled, 812, root, /usr/bin/sshd **When** `block_service` runs **Then** the output equals the seven lines above with those values, "Binary: /usr/bin/sshd" last.
- **Given** a unit with MainPID 0 **When** `block_service` runs **Then** the fifth line is "PID: " with nothing after the space.
- **Given** a selection of the System group row and two unit rows **When** Ctrl+C runs **Then** two blocks separated by one blank line are copied and the toast reads "Service details copied.".
- **Given** a selected child process row **When** Ctrl+C runs **Then** the process "Copy details" block is copied.
- **Given** no selection **When** Ctrl+C runs **Then** the toast reads "Select a service row first.".

## Files

- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/mod.rs`: add `pub mod copy;`
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_services.rs`: add the tests below

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: "Could not copy service details." (through `sys_copy`, open item B8-E27-2 on detection).
- Validity: glyph cells copy as empty TSV fields.
- Accessibility: Ctrl+C and Ctrl+Shift+C from the keyboard.

- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`, for example `... cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_services`.

title: Services: Start, Stop, Restart, Reload and Reset failed flows
description:
## Context
Start, Stop, Restart, Reload and Reset failed state run without confirmation, show a toast replaced in place, and overlay the row's Status cell while pending; failures carry a "View logs" button that opens Service Properties on the Logs tab. This bead writes those flows in `pages/services/flows.rs` on top of `SysActions` (E27-A1). Sources: UI-SYS-018, UI-SYS-007, SYS-005, SYS-006, ADR-005 (`UnitStart`, `UnitStop`, `UnitRestart`, `UnitReload`, `UnitResetFailed`), R-114, R-117.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/flows.rs` and `pub mod flows;` in `pages/services/mod.rs`.

```rust
pub enum UnitVerb { Start, Stop, Restart, Reload, ResetFailed }
pub fn unit_action_kind(v: UnitVerb) -> ActionKind;   // UnitStart, UnitStop, UnitRestart, UnitReload, UnitResetFailed
pub fn unit_action_tag(v: UnitVerb) -> ActionKindTag; // Start, Stop, Restart, Reload, ResetFailed
pub fn unit_action_texts(v: UnitVerb) -> ActionTexts;
/// Submits one request for the captured unit targets (group rows and child rows already removed).
pub fn run_unit_verb(v: UnitVerb, units: &[UnitRef], actions: &Entity<SysActions>,
                     window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App);
```

Texts (exact; `progress_cap = false` and `failed_suffix = true` for all five; service jobs have no client-side timeout):

| Verb | pending_one | done_one | failed_prefix | Button on failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Start | "Starting service..." | "Service started" | "Failed to start service" | "View logs" |
| Stop | "Stopping service..." | "Service stopped" | "Failed to stop service" | "View logs" |
| Restart | "Restarting service..." | "Service restarted" | "Failed to restart service" | "View logs" |
| Reload | "Reloading service..." | "Service reloaded" | "Failed to reload service" | "View logs" |
| ResetFailed | "Clearing failed state..." | "Failed state cleared" | "Failed to clear failed state" | none |

Shared for all five: `unknown` "Service action finished." (Warning; the engine resyncs), `busy` "A service action is already in progress.". Summary texts for 4 or more targets (R-114): Start `pending_many` "Starting { $n } services...", `done_many` "{ $n } services started", `partial_many` "{ $ok } of { $n } services started. { $failed } failed."; Stop "Stopping { $n } services...", "{ $n } services stopped", "{ $ok } of { $n } services stopped. { $failed } failed."; Restart "Restarting { $n } services...", "{ $n } services restarted", "{ $ok } of { $n } services restarted. { $failed } failed."; Reload "Reloading { $n } services...", "{ $n } services reloaded", "{ $ok } of { $n } services reloaded. { $failed } failed."; ResetFailed "Clearing failed state of { $n } services...", "Failed state cleared for { $n } services", "Failed state cleared for { $ok } of { $n } services. { $failed } failed.".

- The failure text is `failure_text(prefix, err)` (E27-A1): "<prefix>: <result>" where result is the systemd job word, the D-Bus error text, or "not authorized".
- "View logs" dispatches `ServicePropertiesWindow::open(unit, ServicePropsTab::Logs)` for the failed target (E27-A3 API); the toast lasts 15 s.
- The request is `ActionRequest { kind: unit_action_kind(v), targets: units.map(ActionTarget::Unit), privileged: false }` through `SysActions::submit`. No confirmation dialog for any verb.
- While pending, the Status cell overlay ("Starting…", "Stopping…", "Restarting…", "Reloading…") comes from the delegate (E27 cells bead) via `SysActions::pending_tag`. Reset failed has no overlay.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a stopped unit **When** Start runs and the fake engine emits `Started` then `Succeeded` **Then** the toast goes "Starting service..." (Progress) then "Service started" (Success) under one key.
- **Given** a Start that fails with job result `failed` **When** the final event arrives **Then** the toast reads "Failed to start service: failed" with a "View logs" button, lasting 15 s, and pressing it opens Service Properties on Logs for that unit.
- **Given** a Reset failed **When** it succeeds **Then** the toast reads "Failed state cleared" and no overlay was drawn.
- **Given** a Start already pending on the unit **When** Start runs again **Then** the toast "A service action is already in progress." shows and no request is sent.
- **Given** `OutcomeUnknown` **When** it arrives **Then** a Warning toast "Service action finished." shows.
- **Given** 5 units **When** Stop runs and all succeed **Then** one toast "Stopping 5 services..." becomes "5 services stopped".

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/flows.rs`: create

- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_services.rs`: add the tests below

title: Services: startup type flow, file openers and Jump to process
description:
## Context
The rest of the Services row commands: change the startup type (Enabled, Disabled, Masked), File properties, Open file location, Open unit file, and Jump to process. Startup changes go through systemd unit-file calls; the three openers go through the engine's opener actions (R-134); Jump to process uses the Processes tab's jump entry point. This bead adds them to `pages/services/flows.rs`. Sources: UI-SYS-019, UI-SYS-017 (interaction rows), UI-SYS-021 (outbound jump), SYS-007, SYS-008, SYS-010, PROC-071, R-134, R-114, ADR-005 (`UnitEnable`, `UnitDisable`, `UnitMask`, `UnitUnmask`, `ShowInFileManager`, `OpenUri`).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/flows.rs`, add:

```rust
/// Request kind for a startup change, or None when the choice equals the current value.
pub fn startup_change_kind(current: StartupType, choice: StartupChoice) -> Option<ActionKind>;
pub fn run_set_startup(choice: StartupChoice, units: &[(UnitRef, StartupType)], actions: &Entity<SysActions>,
                       window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App);
pub fn run_file_properties(unit: &UnitRecord, actions: &Entity<SysActions>, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App);
pub fn run_open_file_location(unit: &UnitRecord, actions: &Entity<SysActions>, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App);
pub fn run_open_unit_file(unit: &UnitRecord, actions: &Entity<SysActions>, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App);
pub fn run_jump_to_process(unit: &UnitRecord, snap: &Snapshot, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App);
pub fn file_uri(path: &str) -> String;   // "file://" + RFC 3986 percent-encoding of every byte outside unreserved and '/'
```

Startup type (UI-SYS-019):
- `startup_change_kind`: current Enabled or "Enabled (runtime)" counts as Enabled. Same value -> None (nothing sent). Choice Enabled -> `UnitEnable`; Disabled -> `UnitDisable`; Masked -> `UnitMask`. Leaving Masked for Enabled or Disabled sends `UnitEnable` or `UnitDisable`; the engine unmasks first as part of that request (open item B8-E27-7 confirms this split with E11).
- Multi-select: one request per distinct resulting kind, each with all its units as targets (units whose value already equals the choice are left out).
- Texts: `pending_one` "Changing startup type...", `done_one` "Startup type changed", `failed_prefix` "Failed to change startup type", `failed_suffix = true` (so ": <error>" is appended), `unknown` "Service action finished.", `busy` "A service action is already in progress.", `progress_cap = false`, no button. Summary for 4 or more targets: "Changing startup type of { $n } services...", "Startup type changed for { $n } services", "Startup type changed for { $ok } of { $n } services. { $failed } failed." (open item B8-E27-6). Tag `ActionKindTag::SetStartup`. Polkit may prompt twice for system units; the toast stays pending through both.

File properties: `ShowInFileManager { path: exec_start_path, properties: true }`, else the unit file path when there is no ExecStart. Texts: `pending_one` empty (no pending toast), `done_one` "Opened service file properties.", `failed_prefix` "Could not open service file properties.", `failed_suffix = false`. Neither path known -> Warning toast "Service image unavailable", nothing sent.

Open file location: `ShowInFileManager { path: exec_start_path, properties: false }`. Texts: `pending_one` empty, `done_one` "Opening service file location.", `failed_prefix` "Could not open service file location.", `failed_suffix = false`. No ExecStart -> Warning toast "Service image unavailable", nothing sent.

Open unit file: `OpenUri(file_uri(fragment_path))`. Texts: `pending_one` empty, `done_one` empty (no success toast: when `done_one` is empty `SysActions` removes the toast silently on success), `failed_prefix` "Could not open the unit file", `failed_suffix = false`. Empty `FragmentPath` -> nothing (the menu item is disabled).

Jump to process (outbound, UI-SYS-021): one unit. `main_pid == 0` -> Info toast "Service not running", nothing else. Otherwise find the `ProcessKey` whose pid equals `main_pid` in `snap.processes.records`, and call the Processes jump entry point (E22-A3, `select_by_key(key, source)`) with caller texts: success "Switched to service process."; hidden by filter or Hide system processes: "Service process not visible in the current process view." with the "Show" button (E22 shows it); key missing: E22's "Process not found in current view".

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a Masked unit **When** the user chooses Enabled **Then** one request with kind `UnitEnable` and that unit is sent.
- **Given** an Enabled (runtime) unit **When** the user chooses Enabled **Then** nothing is sent.
- **Given** a failure "Access denied" on enable **When** the final event arrives **Then** the toast reads "Failed to change startup type: not authorized".
- **Given** a unit with ExecStart `/usr/bin/sshd` **When** File properties runs **Then** the request is `ShowInFileManager { path: "/usr/bin/sshd", properties: true }` and no toast shows before the result.
- **Given** a unit with no ExecStart **When** Open file location runs **Then** the Warning toast "Service image unavailable" shows and nothing is sent.
- **Given** `FragmentPath = /usr/lib/systemd/system/a b.service` **When** Open unit file runs **Then** the request is `OpenUri("file:///usr/lib/systemd/system/a%20b.service")` and success shows no toast.
- **Given** MainPID 0 **When** Jump to process runs **Then** the toast reads "Service not running" and the tab does not change.
- **Given** MainPID 812 present in the process snapshot **When** Jump to process runs **Then** the jump entry point is called with that key and the toast reads "Switched to service process.".

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/flows.rs`: change, add the functions above
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_services.rs`: add the tests below
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append every string above (keys `services-sys019-<slug>`, `services-sys017-<slug>`, `services-sys021-<slug>`)

- `ui_services::startup_same_value_sends_nothing`.
- `ui_services::open_unit_file_uri_encoding`.
- `ui_services::file_properties_falls_back_to_unit_file`.
- `ui_services::jump_to_process_main_pid_zero_toast`.
- `ui_services::jump_to_process_calls_entry_point`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: per the texts above.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: every command is reachable from the context menu with the keyboard (Shift+F10).
- Performance: one request per command.
- Privacy: paths are passed to the engine only; never logged (ADR-015).
