title: System tables: status cell looks and painter (sys_status.rs)
description:
## Context
The Services, Startup Apps and Connections tables draw a status cell: a small dot plus a text label, or (Connections) coloured text only. This bead writes the shared look tables and the one cell painter in `pages/sys_status.rs`, so all three tables colour states the same way and never by colour alone. Sources: UI-SYS-003, SYS-003, SYS-020, SYS-029, R-050, APP-058, 00-epics section 2 (`pages/sys_status.rs` owned by E27).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/sys_status.rs`:

```rust
/// One label colour role; resolved against TlTheme at paint time.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum LabelTone { Primary, Secondary, Danger, Warning, Info, Success }

/// Dot shape and colour role. `None` draws no dot (Connections).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum DotStyle { Filled(LabelTone), Ring(LabelTone), None }

/// The UI-side status words of the three tables. Pages map their model enums onto these.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub enum SysStatus {
    // Services (SYS-003 labels)
    Running, Active, Starting, Stopping, Reloading, Stopped, Failed, Maintenance,
    // Startup Apps (SYS-020)
    Enabled, Disabled, Masked, NotInThisDesktop, MissingProgram,
}

/// Connections State column classes (SYS-029). Labels are the page's (E28); only colour lives here.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum ConnStateClass { Listening, Established, Transitional, TimeWaitOrClosed, Unknown, Udp }

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub struct StatusLook { pub dot: DotStyle, pub label: LabelTone }

pub fn status_look(s: SysStatus) -> StatusLook;
pub fn status_label(s: SysStatus) -> SharedString;          // interned once per language, see Strings
pub fn conn_state_tone(c: ConnStateClass) -> LabelTone;
pub fn tone_color(t: LabelTone, theme: &TlTheme, selected: bool) -> Hsla;

/// The status cell: dot 8 x 8, gap sp3 (6 px), label t_base with ellipsis.
pub fn status_cell(look: StatusLook, label: SharedString, selected: bool, stale: bool,
                   theme: &TlTheme, metrics: &UiMetrics) -> impl IntoElement;
```

`status_look` table (exact):

| SysStatus | dot | label |
|---|---|---|
| Running | Filled(Success) | Primary |
| Active | Ring(Success) | Primary |
| Starting, Stopping, Reloading | Filled(Info) | Primary |
| Stopped | Ring(Secondary) | Secondary |
| Failed | Filled(Danger) | Danger |
| Maintenance | Filled(Warning) | Primary |
| Enabled | Filled(Success) | Primary |
| Disabled | Ring(Secondary) | Secondary |
| Masked | Filled(Warning) | Primary |
| NotInThisDesktop | Ring(Secondary) | Secondary |
| MissingProgram | Filled(Warning) | Primary |

The dot tone `Success` means `status.success`; `Success` is never used as a label tone.

`status_label` strings (exact): "Running", "Active", "Starting", "Stopping", "Reloading", "Stopped", "Failed", "Maintenance", "Enabled", "Disabled", "Masked", "Not in this desktop", "Missing program".

`conn_state_tone`: Listening -> Info; Established -> Primary; Transitional (SYN-SENT, SYN-RECEIVED, FIN-WAIT-1, FIN-WAIT-2, CLOSE-WAIT, CLOSING, LAST-ACK) -> Primary; TimeWaitOrClosed -> Secondary; Unknown -> Warning; Udp (UNCONNECTED and CONNECTED) -> Secondary.

`tone_color(t, theme, selected)`: Primary -> `text_primary` (selected: `text_selected_primary`); Secondary -> `text_secondary` (selected: `text_selected_secondary`); Danger -> `status.danger` in both cases (a failure stays visible on a selected row); Warning -> `status.warning`; Info -> `status.info`; Success -> `status.success`. Dots keep their colour on a selected row.

`status_cell` geometry: an `h_flex` with `items_center`, `gap(sp3)`; dot is a `div().size(px(8) * scale).rounded_full()` with `bg(color)` for `Filled` or `border(px(1.5) * scale).border_color(color)` for `Ring`; label `t_base`, `text_ellipsis`, `whitespace_nowrap`, `overflow_hidden`. `DotStyle::None` draws no dot and no gap. Stale (`stale = true`): label colour is `text_secondary` whatever the tone, and the dot colour is drawn at 50% alpha.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** each `SysStatus` value **When** `status_look` is called **Then** it returns the dot and label tones of the table above.
- **Given** `SysStatus::Failed` and `selected = true` **When** `tone_color(look.label, ..)` is called **Then** it returns `status.danger`, not `text_selected_primary`.
- **Given** `SysStatus::Running` and `selected = true` **When** the label colour is resolved **Then** it is `text_selected_primary` and the dot is still `status.success`.
- **Given** `stale = true` **When** `status_cell` renders `Running` **Then** the label uses `text_secondary` and the dot alpha is half the theme colour's alpha.
- **Given** `DotStyle::None` **When** `status_cell` renders **Then** the element has no dot child and the label starts at the cell's left padding.
- **Given** each `ConnStateClass` **When** `conn_state_tone` is called **Then** it returns the tone listed above.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/sys_status.rs`: create the types and functions above
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_sys_table.rs`: create (E27 owns it); add the tests below
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append the 13 status labels (chain edit allowed by 00-epics, see Notes)

## Tests
- `ui_sys_table::status_cell_colors_per_state`: for every `SysStatus`, `status_look` matches the table, and `tone_color` with the Default Dark theme maps each tone to the named token.
- `ui_sys_table::status_cell_selected_keeps_danger`: `Failed` selected resolves to `status.danger`; `Running` selected resolves to `text_selected_primary`.
- `ui_sys_table::status_cell_stale_dims`: `TestAppContext` render of `status_cell(.., stale: true, ..)`; the label colour is `text_secondary` and the dot alpha is halved.
- `ui_sys_table::conn_state_tones`: one assertion per `ConnStateClass`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: stale only (dimmed). Other validity glyphs are drawn by `table/cells.rs` (E18), not here.
- Accessibility: the label always shows; colour is a second cue only (APP-058).
- Performance: no allocation per frame; `status_label` returns cached `SharedString`s interned once per language (keep them in a `OnceCell` keyed by the `strings_version` from `i18n.rs`).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Strings: append each label to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` with keys `sys-sys003-<slug>` where the slug is the label lowercased with spaces replaced by `-` (for example `sys-sys003-not-in-this-desktop = Not in this desktop`). Read them with `tr(key)` from `i18n.rs` (E16-A1). The `.ftl` append is the chain edit 00-epics section 2 allows "in the bead that uses them".
- UI-SYS-003 names `table/cells.rs` for the painter; 00-epics section 2 moves system-table status cells to `pages/sys_status.rs` (E27). Follow 00-epics; never edit `table/cells.rs`.
- Colour tokens are `TlTheme` fields (E17-A1); `UiMetrics` gives `sp3` and the scale.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`, for example `... cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_sys_table`.

title: System tables: SysQuery and SysPageState (query generation, demand, first visit)
System tables: skeleton and empty or error body states
description:
## Context
Before the first data of a session a system table shows skeleton rows under a live header; afterwards an empty or failed table shows a centred empty state. This bead writes the body-state decision and its rendering in `pages/sys_table.rs`, shared by Services, Startup Apps and Connections. Sources: UI-SYS-004, UI-SYS-005, UI-FND-024, UI-FND-029, UI-SHL-111, R-060, APP-059, SYS-001, SYS-016, SYS-027, SYS-028, SYS-036, U-48.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/sys_table.rs`, add:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum SysBody {
    Skeleton,                        // first data not seen yet in this session
    Rows,                            // draw the TlTreeTable body
    NoMatches,                       // rows empty and a filter is active
    NoEntries,                       // rows empty, no filter, source fine
    FailedFirst { error: SharedString }, // source Failed before first data
    ManagerMissing,                  // Services only: both systemd managers Unavailable
}

pub struct SysBodyInput<'a> {
    pub tab: Tab,
    pub first_data_seen: bool,
    pub rows_len: usize,
    pub filter_active: bool,              // text filter non-empty, or (Services) strip not at defaults
    pub source: Option<&'a SourceHealth>, // health of the page's source; Services passes the worse of the two
    pub managers_unavailable: bool,       // Services only
}

pub fn sys_body(input: &SysBodyInput) -> SysBody;
pub fn render_skeleton(columns: &[Pixels], viewport_h: Pixels, metrics: &UiMetrics) -> AnyElement;
pub fn render_empty(body: &SysBody, tab: Tab, clear_action: Box<dyn Action>, cx: &App) -> AnyElement;
```

`sys_body` order of rules (first match wins):
1. `source` state `Failed` and `!first_data_seen` -> `FailedFirst { error: last_error }` (one line).
2. `!first_data_seen` -> `Skeleton`.
3. `tab == Services && managers_unavailable` -> `ManagerMissing`.
4. `rows_len == 0 && filter_active` -> `NoMatches`.
5. `rows_len == 0` -> `NoEntries` (Services never returns this: with no filter and managers reachable it returns `Rows`).
6. otherwise `Rows`.
A `Failed` source after first data keeps `Rows` (the status chip shows the health item; no empty state).

`render_skeleton`: `TlSkeletonRows { rows: min(floor(viewport_h / row_h), 12), columns }` (UI-FND-024: bar height 10, `r_sm`, widths `[0.6, 0.45, 0.8, 0.5, 0.7]` of each column width, inset `sp4`, alternating `list_bg` / `row_alt`). It is drawn in place of the `uniform_list`, never inside it.

`render_empty` uses `TlEmptyState` (icon `i_lg`, heading `t_md` semibold, text `t_base` `text_secondary` max width 420, optional `TlButton::Secondary` sm), with these exact values:

| SysBody, tab | Icon | Heading | Text | Button |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ManagerMissing (Services) | `server` | "systemd not found" | "tasklens lists services from systemd. Neither the system manager nor the user manager answered." | "Retry" -> `RefreshCurrentTab` |
| NoMatches, Services | `funnel-x` | "No matches" | "No services match the current filters." | "Clear filters" -> `clear_action` |
| NoMatches, Startup | `funnel-x` | "No matches" | "No startup entries match the filter." | "Clear filter" -> `clear_action` |
| NoMatches, Connections | `funnel-x` | "No matches" | "No connections match the filter." | "Clear filter" -> `clear_action` |
| NoEntries, Startup | `app-window` | "No startup entries" | "Nothing starts automatically when you log in." | none |
| NoEntries, Connections | `network` | "No connections" | none | none |
| FailedFirst, Services | `circle-alert` in `status.warning` | "Could not load services" | the error | "Retry" -> `RefreshCurrentTab` |
| FailedFirst, Startup | same | "Could not load startup entries" | the error | "Retry" -> `RefreshCurrentTab` |
| FailedFirst, Connections | same | "Could not load connections" | the error | "Retry" -> `RefreshCurrentTab` |

The "Clear filters" / "Clear filter" button action is passed in, so this file does not depend on the Services actions: Services passes `ServicesClearAllFilters`, Startup Apps and Connections pass `ClearFilter`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `first_data_seen = false` and a healthy source **When** `sys_body` runs **Then** it returns `Skeleton`.
- **Given** `first_data_seen = false` and the source `Failed` with `last_error = "bus timeout"` **When** `sys_body` runs **Then** it returns `FailedFirst { error: "bus timeout" }`.
- **Given** `first_data_seen = true`, `rows_len = 0`, a non-empty text filter on Startup **When** the body renders **Then** it shows "No matches", "No startup entries match the filter." and a "Clear filter" button that dispatches `ClearFilter`.
- **Given** Services with both managers `Unavailable` **When** the body renders **Then** it shows "systemd not found" with a "Retry" button that dispatches `RefreshCurrentTab`.
- **Given** `first_data_seen = true` and the source turns `Failed` **When** `sys_body` runs **Then** it returns `Rows`.
- **Given** a viewport of 1000 px and `row_h = 28` **When** `render_skeleton` runs **Then** it draws 12 rows.
- **Given** the skeleton showed, data arrived, the tab was left and re-entered **When** the body is computed **Then** it is never `Skeleton` again in the session.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/sys_table.rs`: add `SysBody`, `SysBodyInput`, `sys_body`, `render_skeleton`, `render_empty`
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_sys_table.rs`: add the tests below
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append the strings of the table (keys `sys-sys005-<slug>`, see Notes)

## Tests
- `ui_sys_table::sys_body_rules_order`: one case per rule above, including Failed-after-data -> `Rows`.
- `ui_sys_table::skeleton_shows_once_per_session`: fake engine with an empty `WarmingUp` component, then rows, then empty again; the page body is `Skeleton` only in the first state.
- `ui_sys_table::skeleton_row_count_capped_at_12`.
- `ui_sys_table::empty_state_strings_per_tab`: render each table row of `render_empty` and compare heading, text and button label.
- `ui_sys_table::services_systemd_missing_state`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `SourceHealth.last_error` shown as one line with ellipsis; never a toast (ADR-015).
- Validity: `WarmingUp` before first data drives the skeleton; `Failed` drives `FailedFirst`.
- Accessibility: the heading is the region's accessible name; Tab reaches the button; Enter or Space presses it. While the skeleton shows, keys and clicks on the body do nothing; the header stays live.
- Performance: the kit `Skeleton` requests frames while visible (2 s pulse; U-48 says it stops once removed). Twelve rows by up to 7 bars is at most 84 quads. Reduced motion: static at opacity 0.7 (UI-FND-024).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Strings: append to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` with keys `sys-sys005-<slug>`, slug = first five words of the English text lowercased, every run of non-alphanumeric characters replaced by one `-`, trimmed of `-`. Read with `tr(key)`.
- `TlSkeletonRows` and `TlEmptyState` come from E15-A2 (`components/skeleton.rs`, `components/empty.rs`).
- `RefreshCurrentTab` and `ClearFilter` are shell actions (E20-A1, `actions.rs`).
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`, for example `... cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_sys_table`.

title: System tables: shared copy commands (sys_copy.rs)
System tables: action toasts, pending map and summary toast (SysActions)
description:
## Context
Service, startup and connection actions show progress as a toast that is replaced in place, as a pending overlay on the row, and as a disabled menu item while the same action on the same target is pending. With 4 or more targets one summary toast replaces the per-target toasts. This bead writes that shared action-tracking layer for the system tables in `pages/sys_table.rs`, on top of E16's `ActionTracker` and `ToastQueue`. Sources: UI-SYS-007, R-114, R-117, U-39, ADR-005 (action events, event order, `ActionTracker`), ADR-015 (`ActionError`, `message`), SYS-005 to SYS-007, SYS-022 to SYS-024, SYS-031, APP-044.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/sys_table.rs`, add:

```rust
/// Toast texts for one action kind on one table. Fluent args: $n total, $ok succeeded, $failed failed.
pub struct ActionTexts {
    pub pending_one: SharedString,   // e.g. "Starting service..."
    pub pending_many: SharedString,  // e.g. "Starting { $n } services..."
    pub done_one: SharedString,      // e.g. "Service started"
    pub done_many: SharedString,     // e.g. "{ $n } services started"
    pub partial_many: SharedString,  // e.g. "{ $ok } of { $n } services started. { $failed } failed."
    pub failed_prefix: SharedString, // e.g. "Failed to start service"
    pub failed_suffix: bool,         // true: "<prefix>: <result>"; false: the prefix alone (opener toasts)
    pub unknown: SharedString,       // e.g. "Service action finished."
    pub busy: SharedString,          // e.g. "A service action is already in progress."
    pub failed_button: Option<(SharedString, Box<dyn Fn(&ActionTarget) -> Box<dyn Action>>)>, // "View logs"
    pub progress_cap: bool,          // false for service jobs (no 120 s Progress cap), true otherwise
}

/// One per system-table page. Emits SysActionsEvent.
pub struct SysActions {
    pending: FxHashMap<ActionTarget, (ActionId, ActionKindTag)>,
    requests: FxHashMap<ActionId, Tracked>, // targets, texts, per-target finals, summary flag
}
pub enum SysActionsEvent { PendingChanged { target: ActionTarget } }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub enum ActionKindTag { Start, Stop, Restart, Reload, ResetFailed, SetStartup, StartupEnable,
                         StartupDisable, StartupRunNow, StartupDelete, CloseTcp, Other }

impl SysActions {
    pub fn new(tracker: &Entity<ActionTracker>, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> Self; // subscribes to the tracker's events for request ids it submitted
    /// Builds ActionRequest { id: next id, kind, targets, privileged: false }, submits through
    /// ActionTracker, marks every target pending, pushes the pending toast(s). Returns None and
    /// pushes `texts.busy` as a Warning toast when any target is already pending with the same tag.
    pub fn submit(&mut self, kind: ActionKind, tag: ActionKindTag, targets: SmallVec<[ActionTarget; 1]>,
                  texts: ActionTexts, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> Option<ActionId>;
    pub fn is_pending(&self, target: &ActionTarget, tag: ActionKindTag) -> bool;
    pub fn pending_tag(&self, target: &ActionTarget) -> Option<ActionKindTag>; // for the row overlay
}
pub fn failure_text(prefix: &str, err: &ActionError) -> SharedString;
```

Toast lifecycle per request (exact):

| State | Toast kind (UI-FND-020 durations) | Text |
|---|---|---|
| request sent, no event yet | Progress (spinner; static under reduced motion) | `pending_one`, or `pending_many` with 4+ targets; when `pending_one` is empty no toast is pushed until the final event (opener actions) |
| `Started` | Progress, unchanged | unchanged |
| `Succeeded` | Success, 5 s | `done_one`; when `done_one` is empty the toast (if any) is removed and nothing shows |
| `Failed(e)` | Error, 8 s; 15 s when `failed_button` is set | `failure_text(failed_prefix, e)` when `failed_suffix`, else `failed_prefix`; plus the button |
| `OutcomeUnknown(_)` | Warning, 5 s | `unknown` |
| `Rejected(Busy)` | Warning, 5 s | `busy` |
| other `Rejected(r)` | Error, 8 s | `<failed_prefix>: <text>` where `<text>` is the text E16-A3's tracker gives for `r` |

Keys and target counts:
- 0 targets (`OpenUri`, `ShowInFileManager`, `Launch`, R-134) and 1 target: one toast, `ToastKey(id.0)`.
- 2 or 3 targets: one toast per target, key `ToastKey(fxhash((id.0, target_index)))` using `rustc_hash::FxHasher` over the tuple; each follows the table with the per-target final event.
- 4 or more targets: one summary toast `ToastKey(id.0)`. Pending text `pending_many` ($n = targets). On the final event with `target: None`: all succeeded -> Success `done_many`; otherwise Warning `partial_many` ($ok, $n, $failed) with a "Details" button. "Details" opens a `TlDialog` window titled "tasklens" that lists one line per failed target: "<target label>: <failure text>", with one button "Close" (open item B8-E27-4).
- `progress_cap = false` pushes the Progress toast with the queue's no-cap option so it stays until the final event (service jobs have no client-side timeout, SYS-005). Every other kind keeps the 120 s cap of UI-FND-020.

`failure_text(prefix, err)`:
- `ActionError::PermissionDenied` -> "<prefix>: not authorized".
- `ActionError::UnitJob(s)`: if `s` is `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.InteractiveAuthorizationRequired` -> "<prefix>: no authentication agent is running"; if `s` is `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.AccessDenied` -> "<prefix>: not authorized"; else "<prefix>: <s>" (the systemd job result word `failed`, `timeout`, `canceled`, `dependency`, `skipped`, `invalid`, or the D-Bus error text).
- any other variant -> "<prefix>: <message(err)>" using `action_tracker::message` (E16-A3).
- A dismissed polkit prompt cannot be told from a denial on systemd D-Bus calls (R-117, U-39), so both read "not authorized" here. pkexec paths (P3) use their own texts.

Pending map: a target is pending from `submit` until its final event (per-target event, or the summary event for targets with no per-target event). On every change emit `SysActionsEvent::PendingChanged { target }` so the page notifies only the affected row.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** one Start on `sshd.service` **When** the fake engine emits `Started` then `Succeeded` **Then** exactly one toast exists throughout, keyed `ToastKey(id.0)`, ending as Success "Service started".
- **Given** a Start on `sshd.service` is pending **When** a second Start on the same unit is submitted **Then** `submit` returns None, no request reaches the engine, and a Warning toast "A service action is already in progress." shows.
- **Given** 6 targets **When** `submit` runs **Then** one Progress toast "Starting 6 services..." shows and no per-target toast is pushed.
- **Given** 6 targets where 2 fail **When** the summary event arrives **Then** the toast becomes Warning "4 of 6 services started. 2 failed." with a "Details" button whose dialog lists the 2 failed units.
- **Given** 3 targets **When** the request is sent **Then** three toasts with distinct keys show.
- **Given** `Failed(UnitJob("org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.InteractiveAuthorizationRequired"))` with prefix "Failed to start service" **When** the toast updates **Then** it reads "Failed to start service: no authentication agent is running".
- **Given** a service job with `progress_cap = false` **When** 130 s pass with no final event **Then** the toast is still Progress.
- **Given** an `OpenUri` request (no targets) with empty `pending_one` **When** it is submitted **Then** no toast shows until the final event.
- **Given** a pending target **When** its final event arrives **Then** `PendingChanged { target }` is emitted and `is_pending` turns false.

## Files

title: E06-007 Other network namespaces list
description:
## Context
Lists the network namespaces other than tasklens's own, with a display name, for the Connections tab's "Namespaces: All" mode (P4). The dump inside each namespace runs in tl-helper (`NetnsSockDiagDump { netns_ino }`, E29); this bead only finds the namespaces and their names on the host side. Sources: SYS-037, R-004 (helper allowlist), ADR-016.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/net/netns.rs` (add `pub mod netns;` to `net/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct NetnsInfo {
    pub ino: u64,                       // inode of the net namespace
    pub name: std::sync::Arc<str>,      // display name, rules below
    pub member_pid: u32,                // lowest readable pid in it
    pub member_count: u32,
}
/// Every net namespace seen through /proc/<pid>/ns/net, except tasklens's own (/proc/self/ns/net).
/// Sorted by name, then ino.
pub fn list_netns(root: &SysRoot, run_netns: &std::path::Path) -> Result<Vec<NetnsInfo>, CollectError>;
```

Rules:
- For each numeric `/proc/<pid>`: `readlinkat(pid_dirfd, "ns/net")` gives `net:[<ino>]`. `EACCES`, `EPERM`, `ENOENT` skip the pid.
- Name, first match wins: (1) a file in `run_netns` (normally `/run/netns`) whose `stat` inode equals `ino`: its file name; (2) the last path component of the member pid's cgroup v2 path from `/proc/<member_pid>/cgroup` (the `0::` line), for example `docker-3f2a.scope`; (3) `net:[<ino>]`.
- The host namespace (inode of `<root.proc>/self/ns/net`) is never listed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fixture with pids 10 and 11 in `net:[4026531840]` (host, same as `self`), pid 20 in `net:[4026532001]` and a `run_netns/blue` file whose inode is 4026532001 **When** `list_netns` runs **Then** it returns one entry with name `blue`, `member_pid == 20`, `member_count == 1`.
- **Given** pid 30 in `net:[4026532002]` with cgroup line `0::/system.slice/docker-3f2a.scope` and no run_netns match **When** listed **Then** the name is `docker-3f2a.scope`.
- **Given** a namespace with no run_netns match and no readable cgroup **When** listed **Then** the name is `net:[4026532003]`.

Inode matching for `run_netns` uses a test-only name lookup `fn ino_of(path) -> u64` that the fixture overrides with a `run_netns/.inodes` file (`blue 4026532001`); the real path uses `stat`.

title: E06-008 Desktop Entry parser for autostart files
description:
## Context
Parses XDG autostart `.desktop` files for the Startup Apps tab. Autostart files are untrusted input (any program can drop one in `~/.config/autostart`), so the parser is bounded, never panics and sanitizes every string it keeps. Writing overrides is E07 (`tl-ops/src/fs.rs`); this bead only reads. Sources: SYS-019, SYS-020, SYS-026, ADR-016 ("Startup apps"), ADR-015 (untrusted text).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/startup/autostart.rs` (add `pub mod autostart;` to `startup/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct DesktopEntry {
    pub name: Option<std::sync::Arc<str>>,      // Name, localised (rules below)
    pub exec: Option<std::sync::Arc<str>>,      // Exec, unescaped
    pub try_exec: Option<std::sync::Arc<str>>,  // TryExec
    pub icon: Option<std::sync::Arc<str>>,      // Icon (name or path, resolved later)
    pub path: Option<std::sync::Arc<str>>,      // Path (working directory)
    pub entry_type: Option<std::sync::Arc<str>>,// Type
    pub hidden: bool,                           // Hidden=true
    pub gnome_autostart_enabled: Option<bool>,  // X-GNOME-Autostart-enabled
    pub only_show_in: smallvec::SmallVec<[std::sync::Arc<str>; 2]>, // OnlyShowIn, split on ';', empties dropped
    pub not_show_in: smallvec::SmallVec<[std::sync::Arc<str>; 2]>,  // NotShowIn
    pub kde_autostart_phase: Option<std::sync::Arc<str>>, // X-KDE-autostart-phase
    pub tasklens_override: bool,                // X-Tasklens-Override=true
}

pub const MAX_DESKTOP_FILE: usize = 64 * 1024;

/// Parses the `[Desktop Entry]` group of `bytes`. `locales` is the caller's match list, most
/// specific first, for example ["de_DE@euro", "de_DE", "de@euro", "de"].
pub fn parse_desktop_entry(bytes: &[u8], locales: &[&str]) -> DesktopEntry;

/// Builds the match list from a POSIX locale string such as "de_DE.UTF-8@euro" (encoding dropped).
pub fn locale_match_list(locale: &str) -> smallvec::SmallVec<[String; 4]>;
```

Parsing rules (Desktop Entry Specification 1.5):
- Only keys inside the `[Desktop Entry]` group count; parsing stops at the next `[group]` header. Lines starting with `#` and blank lines are skipped. A line without `=` is skipped.
- Key and value are trimmed of spaces around `=`. Value escapes: `\s` space, `\n` newline, `\t` tab, `\r` CR, `\\` backslash; for list keys `\;` is a literal `;`. An unknown escape keeps both characters.
- Booleans: exactly `true` or `false`; anything else is treated as absent.
- `Name[<locale>]` picks the first entry of `locales` that has a key; else plain `Name`.
- Bytes are decoded with `String::from_utf8_lossy` and passed through the control-character and bidi filter from `crate::sanitize` (E05-A1) before they become `Arc<str>`.
- Input longer than `MAX_DESKTOP_FILE` is cut at that length before parsing (the caller reads at most that many bytes).
- Duplicate keys: the first one wins.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `[Desktop Entry]\nName=Foo\nName[de]=Fuh\nExec=foo --bar\nHidden=true\nOnlyShowIn=KDE;GNOME;\n` and locales `["de"]` **When** parsed **Then** name is "Fuh", exec "foo --bar", hidden true, only_show_in ["KDE", "GNOME"].
- **Given** `Exec=foo\sbar\\\\x` **When** parsed **Then** exec is `foo bar\x`.
- **Given** a file with `[Desktop Action new]` before `[Desktop Entry]` **When** parsed **Then** keys from the action group are ignored.
- **Given** `Hidden=yes` **When** parsed **Then** hidden is false.
- **Given** a Name containing U+202E and a 0x07 byte **When** parsed **Then** the stored name has no U+202E and the BEL is U+FFFD.
- **Given** `X-Tasklens-Override=true` **When** parsed **Then** `tasklens_override` is true.
- **Given** "de_DE.UTF-8@euro" **When** `locale_match_list` runs **Then** it returns ["de_DE@euro", "de_DE", "de@euro", "de"].

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/startup/autostart.rs`: create (parser, unit tests)
- `crates/tl-collect/src/startup/mod.rs`: add `pub mod autostart;`
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/prop_netsys.rs`: startup section, add `prop_desktop_entry_never_panics`

## Tests
- `startup::autostart::tests::{basic_keys_and_locale, escapes, ignores_other_groups, bool_strict, sanitized_strings, tasklens_override_key, locale_list}`: criteria 1 to 7.
- `tests/prop_netsys.rs::prop_desktop_entry_never_panics`: arbitrary bytes up to 128 KiB never panic.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A (the parser is total).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one pass over the bytes with `memchr` for line ends.
- Privacy: never log `Exec` values above `trace`.

title: E06-009 Autostart scan, precedence and status
description:
## Context
Scans the XDG autostart directories, applies the XDG override precedence and computes each entry's status, producing raw startup rows for the engine's `Startup` worker (E14). It also defines the shared raw types that the unit and Plasma script readers fill. Sources: SYS-019 (sources, precedence, effective disable rules), SYS-020 (Status and Type values), SYS-024 (system entries cannot be deleted), SYS-026 (Properties lines), ADR-016, ADR-011 (env var fallback rule).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-collect/src/startup/mod.rs` (types shared by every startup reader):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug, Hash)]
pub enum StartupKindRaw { AutostartUser, AutostartSystem, AutostartSystemOverridden, UserUnit, PlasmaPreStartup, PlasmaLogout }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug, Hash)]
pub enum StartupStatusRaw { Enabled, Disabled, Masked, NotInThisDesktop, MissingProgram }

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct StartupRaw {
    pub kind: StartupKindRaw,
    pub file_name: Arc<str>,            // "org.kde.foo.desktop", "foo.service", "env.sh"
    pub source_path: Arc<str>,          // absolute path of the file this row was read from (row identity)
    pub location: Arc<str>,             // its directory
    pub name: Arc<str>,                 // desktop Name, else file name without extension
    pub icon: Option<Arc<str>>,
    pub command: Arc<str>,              // Exec, ExecStart or the script path
    pub resolved_path: Option<Arc<str>>,// absolute path of the command's program found on PATH
    pub status: StartupStatusRaw,
    pub try_exec: Option<Arc<str>>,
    pub only_show_in: SmallVec<[Arc<str>; 2]>,
    pub not_show_in: SmallVec<[Arc<str>; 2]>,
    pub kde_autostart_phase: Option<Arc<str>>,
    pub generated_unit: Option<Arc<str>>, // filled by E06-A2 for desktop entries
    pub overrides: Option<Arc<str>>,      // user row: the system path it shadows
    pub overridden_by_user: bool,         // system row shadowed by a user file
    pub tasklens_override: bool,
    pub unit_file_state: Option<Arc<str>>,// user units only (E06-010)
    pub can_toggle: bool, pub can_delete: bool, pub can_run: bool, pub file_exists: bool,
}
```

In `crates/tl-collect/src/startup/autostart.rs`:

```rust
pub struct StartupEnv {
    pub config_home: PathBuf,        // $XDG_CONFIG_HOME, else $HOME/.config
    pub config_dirs: Vec<PathBuf>,   // $XDG_CONFIG_DIRS split on ':', else ["/etc/xdg"]
    pub current_desktop: Vec<String>,// $XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP split on ':'
    pub path_dirs: Vec<PathBuf>,     // $PATH split on ':'
    pub locales: SmallVec<[String; 4]>, // locale_match_list of $LC_ALL, else $LC_MESSAGES, else $LANG
}
impl StartupEnv { pub fn from_env() -> Self; }
pub fn scan_autostart(env: &StartupEnv, out: &mut Vec<StartupRaw>) -> Result<(), CollectError>;
pub fn find_on_path(program: &str, path_dirs: &[PathBuf]) -> Option<PathBuf>;
```

Rules:
- Env fallback (ADR-011): an env var that is unset, empty or not absolute (for path entries: each entry) uses the default. Relative entries inside `XDG_CONFIG_DIRS` and `PATH` are dropped.
- Directories: user `config_home/autostart`, then each `config_dirs[i]/autostart` in order. A missing directory is skipped. Files: names ending in `.desktop`, regular files after following symlinks, read at most `MAX_DESKTOP_FILE` bytes, parsed with `parse_desktop_entry` (E06-008).
- Precedence by file name: the user file is effective and the first system dir's file beats later ones. The winning system file shadowed by a user file is emitted once more as `AutostartSystemOverridden` with `overridden_by_user = true`; the user row gets `overrides = Some(<that system path>)`. System files shadowed by an earlier system dir are dropped.
- Status, first rule that matches: `OnlyShowIn` non-empty and no element in `current_desktop`, or any `NotShowIn` element in `current_desktop` (case-sensitive): `NotInThisDesktop`; `TryExec` set and not found (absolute: exists and has an execute bit; else `find_on_path`): `MissingProgram`; `Hidden=true` or `X-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=false`: `Disabled`; else `Enabled`.
- `resolved_path`: the first word of `Exec` (shell-style quotes `"..."` removed), absolute if it already is, else `find_on_path`.
- Flags: `can_toggle` = status not `NotInThisDesktop` or `MissingProgram`, and kind not `AutostartSystemOverridden`; `can_delete` = kind `AutostartUser`; `can_run = true`; `file_exists = true`.
- Rows are appended in this order: user rows sorted by file name, then system rows sorted by file name.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `user/autostart/a.desktop` and `/etc/xdg/autostart/a.desktop` **When** scanned **Then** there are two rows: `AutostartUser` with `overrides = Some("/etc/xdg/autostart/a.desktop")` and `AutostartSystemOverridden` with `overridden_by_user = true`.
- **Given** `config_dirs = [d1, d2]` both with `b.desktop` and no user file **When** scanned **Then** one `AutostartSystem` row from `d1`.
- **Given** `OnlyShowIn=GNOME;` and `current_desktop = ["KDE"]` **When** scanned **Then** status is `NotInThisDesktop` and `can_toggle` is false.
- **Given** `TryExec=/nonexistent/bin` **When** scanned **Then** status is `MissingProgram`.
- **Given** `Hidden=true` **When** scanned **Then** status is `Disabled` and `can_toggle` is true.
- **Given** `X-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=false` **When** scanned **Then** status is `Disabled`.
- **Given** `XDG_CONFIG_DIRS="relative:/etc/xdg"` **When** `from_env` runs **Then** `config_dirs == ["/etc/xdg"]`.
- **Given** a system entry **When** scanned **Then** `can_delete` is false; a user entry has `can_delete` true.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/startup/mod.rs`: add the types
- `crates/tl-collect/src/startup/autostart.rs`: add `StartupEnv`, `scan_autostart`, `find_on_path`, unit tests
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/autostart-kde/{home/.config/autostart,etc/xdg/autostart,etc/xdg2/autostart}/*.desktop`: create the files the tests need (E06-A2 extends this fixture)

## Tests
- `startup::autostart::tests::{user_overrides_system, earlier_config_dir_wins, only_show_in_excludes, try_exec_missing, hidden_disables, gnome_enabled_false_disables, env_fallback_drops_relative, delete_only_user}`: criteria 1 to 8, against the fixture.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: only an unreadable `config_home` that exists but cannot be listed returns the I/O error variant; missing directories are skipped.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: scan runs on page open, `RefreshNow` and watch events only (ADR-008).
- Privacy: no command text in logs above `trace`.

## Notes
- The engine maps `StartupRaw` to the `tl-model` startup entry type (E14); `source_path` is the row identity.

title: E06-010 systemd user unit startup rows and unit-name escaping
description:
## Context
Turns the user manager's unit files into startup rows (source 3 of SYS-019) and provides the systemd unit-name escaping that links a desktop entry to its generated `app-<escaped id>@autostart.service`. The D-Bus calls (`ListUnitFilesByPatterns`, `ListUnitsByPatterns`, `UnitFilesChanged`) are E14's; this bead parses the unit files the engine names and is pure apart from reading those files. Sources: SYS-019, SYS-020, SYS-022 (units toggle through the manager), SYS-024 (package-owned units cannot be deleted), UI-SYS-044 (Masked cannot be toggled).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/startup/user_units.rs` (add `pub mod user_units;` to `startup/mod.rs`):

```rust
/// One entry of ListUnitFilesByPatterns on the user manager.
pub struct UnitFileListing<'a> { pub path: &'a str, pub state: &'a str }

/// Reads each listed unit file and appends a `UserUnit` row for every unit whose [Install]
/// WantedBy= names default.target, graphical-session.target or a target matching plasma-*.target.
pub fn scan_user_units(units: &[UnitFileListing<'_>], env: &StartupEnv, out: &mut Vec<StartupRaw>);

/// systemd unit-name escaping (systemd `unit_name_escape`).
pub fn systemd_escape(s: &str, out: &mut String);
/// "app-" + systemd_escape(desktop id without ".desktop") + "@autostart.service"
pub fn autostart_unit_name(desktop_file_name: &str) -> String;
pub fn is_generated_autostart_unit(unit_name: &str) -> bool; // "app-" prefix and "@autostart.service" suffix
```

Unit file parsing (only what the rows need):
- Sections `[Unit]`, `[Service]`, `[Install]`; `#` and `;` comments; line continuation with a trailing `\`. Keys repeat: `WantedBy=` values are space-separated and accumulate; an empty `WantedBy=` resets the list.
- `[Service] ExecStart=`: the first non-empty value; leading prefix characters `@`, `-`, `:`, `+`, `!` are removed for `command` and `resolved_path`. `[Service] Type=` is kept for impact (E06-012) as `service_type`.
- Read at most 64 KiB per file; untrusted text goes through the `crate::sanitize` filter (E05-A1).

Row values: `kind = UserUnit`; `file_name` and `name` = unit name (file name of `path`); `source_path = path`; `location` = its directory; `command` = ExecStart or ""; `unit_file_state = Some(state)`.
- Status: state `enabled` or `enabled-runtime`: `Enabled`; `masked` or `masked-runtime`: `Masked`; any other: `Disabled`.
- `can_toggle` = status not `Masked`; `can_delete` = `path` starts with `<env.config_home>/systemd/user/`; `can_run = true`; `file_exists = true`.
- Units with `is_generated_autostart_unit` are never emitted (they are linked to their desktop entry instead).
- A listed path that cannot be read is emitted with `command = ""` and `file_exists = false`.

Escaping (`unit_name_escape`): every byte outside `[A-Za-z0-9:_.]` becomes `\xNN` with lowercase hex, `/` becomes `-`, and a leading `.` becomes `\x2e`. So `-` itself is written `\x2d`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `foo.service` with `[Install]\nWantedBy=graphical-session.target` and state `enabled` **When** scanned **Then** one row, `Enabled`, name `foo.service`.
- **Given** `bar.service` with `WantedBy=multi-user.target` **When** scanned **Then** no row.
- **Given** `baz.service` with `WantedBy=plasma-workspace.target` and state `masked` **When** scanned **Then** status `Masked` and `can_toggle` false.
- **Given** `WantedBy=a.target` then `WantedBy=` then `WantedBy=default.target` **When** parsed **Then** the list is `[default.target]`.
- **Given** `ExecStart=-/usr/bin/foo --x` **When** scanned **Then** `command` is `/usr/bin/foo --x`.
- **Given** path `/usr/lib/systemd/user/foo.service` **When** scanned **Then** `can_delete` is false; `<config_home>/systemd/user/foo.service` gives true.
- **Given** desktop id `org.kde.kalendarac.desktop` **When** `autostart_unit_name` runs **Then** it returns `app-org.kde.kalendarac@autostart.service`; `my-app.desktop` gives `app-my\x2dapp@autostart.service`.
- **Given** `app-org.kde.foo@autostart.service` in the listing **When** scanned **Then** no row.

title: E06-012 Startup impact classification
description:
## Context
Classifies startup impact from systemd activation timing, the data `systemd-analyze --user blame` uses. The engine reads the unit properties over D-Bus (E14); this bead is the pure computation so it is tested without a bus. Sources: SYS-021, UI-SYS-043 (`impact_detail` fields).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/startup/impact.rs` (add `pub mod impact;` to `startup/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum ImpactRaw { High, Medium, Low, None, NotMeasured }

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug, Default)]
pub struct ImpactDetailRaw {
    pub activation_ms: u64,   // ActiveEnter - InactiveExit
    pub start_offset_ms: u64, // InactiveExit - Manager UserspaceTimestampMonotonic
    pub cpu_ns: Option<u64>,  // CPUUsageNSec; u64::MAX on the bus means not available -> None
    pub fork_exec_only: bool, // service Type= simple or exec (or unset, which is simple)
}

pub struct UnitTiming {
    pub inactive_exit_mono_us: u64,   // InactiveExitTimestampMonotonic
    pub active_enter_mono_us: u64,    // ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic
    pub userspace_mono_us: u64,       // Manager UserspaceTimestampMonotonic (user manager)
    pub cpu_usage_ns: u64,            // CPUUsageNSec
    pub service_type: Option<std::sync::Arc<str>>,
}

pub fn classify(enabled: bool, timing: Option<&UnitTiming>) -> (ImpactRaw, Option<ImpactDetailRaw>);
```

Rules:
- `enabled == false`: `(None, None)`.
- `timing == None`, or `inactive_exit_mono_us == 0`, or `active_enter_mono_us == 0`, or `active_enter < inactive_exit`: `(NotMeasured, None)`.
- `activation_ms = (active_enter - inactive_exit) / 1000` (integer division). High when `activation_ms >= 1000`, Medium when `300..=999`, Low when `< 300`.
- `start_offset_ms = inactive_exit.saturating_sub(userspace) / 1000`.
- `fork_exec_only = matches!(service_type, None | Some("simple") | Some("exec"))`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** enabled and activation 999 ms **When** classified **Then** Medium; 1000 ms gives High; 299 ms gives Low; 300 ms gives Medium.
- **Given** disabled **When** classified **Then** `None` impact and no detail.
- **Given** enabled and `active_enter_mono_us == 0` **When** classified **Then** NotMeasured.
- **Given** `userspace = 5_000_000`, `inactive_exit = 8_200_000` **When** classified **Then** `start_offset_ms == 3200`.
- **Given** `cpu_usage_ns == u64::MAX` **When** classified **Then** `cpu_ns == None`.
- **Given** `service_type = Some("oneshot")` **When** classified **Then** `fork_exec_only == false`.

- `crates/tl-collect/src/startup/mod.rs`: add `pub mod impact;`

title: E06-013 inotify watch for startup directories
E06-014 /proc/cpuinfo parser
description:
## Context
Parses `/proc/cpuinfo` for the Information tab's Processor section and for the CPU page's Virtualization and Microcode rows. Cores, logical processors, base and max speed come from E04's topology and cpufreq readers; this bead covers only `/proc/cpuinfo`. Sources: PERF-096, PERF-035 (Microcode), PERF-037 (cpuinfo flags), ADR-016 ("Information").

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/inventory/cpuinfo.rs` (add `pub mod cpuinfo;` to `inventory/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct CpuInfo {
    pub model_name: Option<Arc<str>>,   // "model name"
    pub vendor_id: Option<Arc<str>>,    // "vendor_id", e.g. "AuthenticAMD"
    pub family: Option<u32>,            // "cpu family"
    pub model: Option<u32>,             // "model"
    pub stepping: Option<u32>,          // "stepping"
    pub microcode: Option<Arc<str>>,    // "microcode", e.g. "0xa201016"
    pub mhz: Option<f32>,               // "cpu MHz" of the first block (speed fallback, PERF-033)
    pub bogomips_only: bool,            // no "cpu MHz" line anywhere but "bogomips" present
    pub logical_count: u32,             // number of "processor" lines
    pub flags: CpuFlags,
}
bitflags::bitflags! {
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub struct CpuFlags: u16 {
        const SVM = 1; const VMX = 2; const HYPERVISOR = 4; const SME = 8;
        const USER_SHSTK = 16; const AVX512F = 32;
    }
}
pub fn parse_cpuinfo(bytes: &[u8], out: &mut CpuInfo);
/// "Family 25 Model 97 Stepping 2"; None when any of the three is missing.
pub fn identifier(info: &CpuInfo, out: &mut String) -> bool;
```

Rules:
- Lines are `key<tabs or spaces>: value`. Keys are trimmed. Fields are taken from the first block (up to the first blank line) except `processor` (counted over the whole file) and `flags` (from the first block).
- `flags` is split on spaces; the six names above set the bits (`svm`, `vmx`, `hypervisor`, `sme`, `user_shstk`, `avx512f`).
- Numbers that do not parse leave the field `None`. Strings are trimmed and passed through the `crate::sanitize` control-character filter (E05-A1).
- `parse_cpuinfo` resets `out` first and never panics.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the `owner-desktop` style text with two blocks for an AMD CPU (vendor `AuthenticAMD`, family 25, model 97, stepping 2, microcode `0xa601206`, flags containing `svm` and `avx512f`) **When** parsed **Then** the fields match, `logical_count == 2`, flags `SVM | AVX512F`.
- **Given** that result **When** `identifier` runs **Then** it writes "Family 25 Model 97 Stepping 2".
- **Given** a file with `bogomips` and no `cpu MHz` (ARM style) **When** parsed **Then** `mhz == None` and `bogomips_only == true`.
- **Given** `cpu family : abc` **When** parsed **Then** `family == None`.

title: E06-015 Virtualization and security feature readers
description:
## Context
Reads the CPU page's Virtualization, Hypervisor and Security features sources and the CPU vulnerability summary. Some of these files may not be readable without root (U-27); a source that cannot be read is left out of the list and named so the tooltip can say so. "Running in VM" comes from systemd over D-Bus and is E12's. Sources: PERF-037, PERF-101 (Secure Boot), U-27, R-056.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-collect/src/inventory/cpuinfo.rs`:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum Virtualization { EnabledKvm, SupportedNoKvm, NotSupported }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum Lockdown { None, Integrity, Confidentiality }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug, Default)]
pub struct VulnCounts { pub mitigated: u16, pub vulnerable: u16, pub not_affected: u16, pub unknown: u16 }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum SecuritySource { SecureBoot, KernelLockdown, MemoryEncryption, IommuSysfs, Vulnerabilities }

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct SecurityInfo {
    pub virtualization: Virtualization,
    pub hypervisor: Option<Arc<str>>,         // /sys/hypervisor/type, or "unknown" when only the flag is set; None when no flag
    pub secure_boot: Option<bool>,
    pub lockdown: Option<Lockdown>,
    pub memory_encryption: Option<bool>,
    pub user_shadow_stack: bool,
    pub iommu: Option<bool>,
    pub vulns: Option<VulnCounts>,
    pub unreadable: SmallVec<[SecuritySource; 4]>, // sources that gave EACCES or EPERM
}
pub struct SecurityPaths<'a> { pub sys: &'a Path, pub proc: &'a Path, pub dev: &'a Path }
pub fn read_security(cpu: &CpuInfo, p: &SecurityPaths<'_>) -> SecurityInfo;
pub const EFI_GLOBAL_GUID: &str = "8be4df61-93ca-11d2-aa0d-00e098032b8c";
```

Rules (paths relative to the roots in `SecurityPaths`):
- Virtualization: flag `SVM` or `VMX` and `<dev>/kvm` exists: `EnabledKvm`; flag set, no `/dev/kvm`: `SupportedNoKvm`; no flag: `NotSupported`.
- Hypervisor: flag `HYPERVISOR` set: contents of `<sys>/hypervisor/type` trimmed, else `"unknown"`; flag not set: `None`.
- Secure Boot: read `<sys>/firmware/efi/efivars/SecureBoot-<EFI_GLOBAL_GUID>`; byte at index 4 (after the 4-byte attributes) `1` gives `Some(true)`, `0` gives `Some(false)`; missing file or shorter than 5 bytes gives `None`; EACCES or EPERM gives `None` and pushes `SecureBoot`.
- Kernel lockdown: `<sys>/kernel/security/lockdown`, the bracketed word: `none`, `integrity`, `confidentiality`. Missing: `None`. EACCES or EPERM: `None` and pushes `KernelLockdown`.
- Memory encryption: flag `SME` set and `<proc>/cmdline` contains the word `mem_encrypt=on`: `Some(true)`; flag set otherwise: `Some(false)`; no flag: `None`. An unreadable cmdline pushes `MemoryEncryption`.
- User shadow stack: flag `USER_SHSTK`.
- IOMMU: `<sys>/class/iommu` exists and has at least one entry: `Some(true)`; exists and empty: `Some(false)`; missing: `Some(false)`; unreadable: `None` and pushes `IommuSysfs`.
- Vulnerabilities: each file in `<sys>/devices/system/cpu/vulnerabilities/`: text starting with `Not affected` counts not_affected, `Mitigation` mitigated, `Vulnerable` vulnerable, anything else unknown. Directory missing: `None`; any file unreadable pushes `Vulnerabilities` once and that file counts as unknown.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** flags `SVM` and a fixture `dev/kvm` file **When** read **Then** `EnabledKvm`; without `dev/kvm` **Then** `SupportedNoKvm`.
- **Given** a SecureBoot efivar file with bytes `07 00 00 00 01` **When** read **Then** `secure_boot == Some(true)`.
- **Given** lockdown text `none [integrity] confidentiality` **When** read **Then** `Some(Integrity)`.
- **Given** vulnerability files `Mitigation: X`, `Not affected`, `Vulnerable`, `KVM: Mitigation: Y` **When** read **Then** counts mitigated 1, not_affected 1, vulnerable 1, unknown 1.
- **Given** `class/iommu` with two entries **When** read **Then** `iommu == Some(true)`.
- **Given** the real owner machine as uid 1000 **When** `read_security` runs **Then** the test prints `unreadable` and every field, and the bead's close note records which of lockdown, efivars and iommu were readable (settles U-27).

- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/dmi-desktop/{sys,dev,proc}/...`: add the files the tests need (`sys/firmware/efi/efivars/SecureBoot-<guid>`, `sys/kernel/security/lockdown`, `sys/class/iommu/ivhd0`, `sys/devices/system/cpu/vulnerabilities/*`, `dev/kvm`, `proc/cmdline`)

title: E06-016 DMI fields and firmware type
description:
## Context
Reads the world-readable DMI fields and the firmware type for the Information tab's BIOS/Firmware, Motherboard and System sections. Root-only fields are shown as `Restricted`, never as empty or zero. The shield does not change them: the helper allowlist has no DMI read. Memory module serials are a separate file (E06-018) and are never read. Sources: PERF-101, PERF-102, ADR-016 ("Information", "Restricted, not zero"), D-007.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/inventory/dmi.rs` (add `pub mod dmi;` to `inventory/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum Field { Value(Arc<str>), Restricted, Missing }

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum FirmwareType { Uefi, LegacyBios }

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct DmiInfo {
    pub firmware: FirmwareType,     // <sys>/firmware/efi exists -> Uefi
    pub bios_vendor: Field, pub bios_version: Field, pub bios_date: Field, pub bios_release: Field,
    pub board_vendor: Field, pub board_name: Field, pub board_version: Field, pub board_serial: Field,
    pub sys_vendor: Field, pub product_name: Field,
    pub chassis_type: Option<u8>,   // SMBIOS chassis type code from chassis_type; the UI maps it to text
}
pub fn read_dmi(sys: &Path) -> DmiInfo;
```

Rules:
- Files are read from `<sys>/class/dmi/id/<name>` for exactly these names: `bios_vendor`, `bios_version`, `bios_date`, `bios_release`, `board_vendor`, `board_name`, `board_version`, `board_serial`, `sys_vendor`, `product_name`, `chassis_type`. No other file in that directory is opened (in particular not `product_serial`, `product_uuid` or `chassis_serial`).
- Each read is capped at 256 bytes. The value is trimmed; an empty value or `ENOENT` gives `Missing`. Vendor placeholder texts such as "Default string" are shown as read. `EACCES` or `EPERM` gives `Restricted`. Any other error gives `Missing`.
- Values pass through the `crate::sanitize` control-character filter (E05-A1).
- `chassis_type` parses as a decimal `u8`; otherwise `None`.
- `pub fn classify_errno(e: rustix::io::Errno) -> Field` holds the error mapping so it is unit-tested without root.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the `dmi-desktop` fixture with `bios_vendor` = "American Megatrends International, LLC.", `board_name` = "ROG STRIX X570-E GAMING", `chassis_type` = "3" and no `board_serial` file **When** read **Then** those values are `Value`, `chassis_type == Some(3)`, `board_serial == Missing`, `firmware == Uefi` (fixture has `sys/firmware/efi/`).
- **Given** `bios_release` containing only a newline **When** read **Then** it is `Missing`.
- **Given** `Errno::ACCESS` or `Errno::PERM` **When** `classify_errno` runs **Then** it returns `Restricted`.
- **Given** the fixture also contains `product_serial` with the text `SERIAL-MUST-NOT-APPEAR` **When** `read_dmi` runs **Then** `format!("{:?}", info)` does not contain that text.
- **Given** the real machine as uid 1000 **When** `read_dmi` runs **Then** `board_serial == Restricted` (mode 0400, verified in PERF-102).

## Files

title: E06-A2 Startup entries
description:
## Context
Anchor E06-A2 "Startup entries". It closes the startup set (`startup/{autostart,user_units,plasma_scripts,watch,impact}.rs`, E06-008 to E06-013) with one entry point the `Startup` worker (E14) calls, the `autostart-kde` fixture, the fixture snapshot test and the startup proptests. After it closes, the startup API is frozen. Sources: SYS-019 to SYS-021, SYS-024, SYS-026, R-082, ADR-016, ADR-013.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-collect/src/startup/mod.rs`:

```rust
pub use autostart::{StartupEnv, DesktopEntry, parse_desktop_entry, locale_match_list, find_on_path, MAX_DESKTOP_FILE};
pub use user_units::{UnitFileListing, systemd_escape, autostart_unit_name, is_generated_autostart_unit};
```

title: E06-017 OS release, kernel, install date and package manager
description:
## Context
Reads the Information tab's Operating System section: `/etc/os-release`, kernel release and version, architecture, install date, package manager version and machine ID, plus the NIS domain for the System section. Hostnames, user, desktop and session come from D-Bus and the environment in the engine (E12). Sources: PERF-095, PERF-097 (Domain), ADR-016 ("Information").

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/inventory/os_release.rs` (add `pub mod os_release;` to `inventory/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct OsRelease {
    pub pretty_name: Option<Arc<str>>, pub name: Option<Arc<str>>, pub id: Option<Arc<str>>,
    pub version_id: Option<Arc<str>>,  // None means the UI shows "Rolling"
    pub build_id: Option<Arc<str>>,    // None means "Not reported"
    pub logo: Option<Arc<str>>,        // icon name, looked up in the icon theme by the UI
}
pub fn parse_os_release(bytes: &[u8]) -> OsRelease;
/// <etc>/os-release, else <usr_lib>/os-release.
pub fn read_os_release(etc: &Path, usr_lib: &Path) -> Option<OsRelease>;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct KernelInfo { pub release: Arc<str>, pub version: Arc<str>, pub machine: Arc<str>, pub nis_domain: Option<Arc<str>> }
pub fn read_kernel() -> KernelInfo;              // rustix::system::uname()

pub fn read_machine_id(etc: &Path) -> Option<Arc<str>>; // first 32 hex chars of <etc>/machine-id

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum InstallDateSource { RootBirthTime, PacmanLog }
/// Unix seconds and the source used.
pub fn read_install_date(root: &Path, pacman_log: &Path) -> Option<(i64, InstallDateSource)>;

/// "pacman 7.0.0", "dpkg 1.21.22" or "rpm 4.19.1": the first of the three programs found in `path_dirs`.
pub fn package_manager_version(path_dirs: &[PathBuf]) -> Option<Arc<str>>;
```

Rules:
- os-release syntax (freedesktop os-release): `KEY=value` per line, `#` comments. Values may be in double or single quotes; inside double quotes `\"`, `\\`, `` \` ``, `\$` are unescaped. Unquoted values are taken as is. Unknown keys ignored. Values pass the `crate::sanitize` filter (E05-A1). Read at most 64 KiB.
- `nis_domain`: `uname().domainname()`; empty or `(none)` gives `None`.
- `machine` is the raw `uname` machine string (`x86_64`); the UI writes "x86_64 (64-bit)".
- Install date: `statx(root, "", AT_EMPTY_PATH, STATX_BTIME)`; if the returned mask has `STATX_BTIME` and `stx_btime.tv_sec > 0`, use it (`RootBirthTime`). Else read the first line of `pacman_log` (at most 4 KiB); it must start with `[YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HHMM]` or `-HHMM`; convert to Unix seconds with the offset (`PacmanLog`). Any other first-line form gives `None`.
- Package manager: look for `pacman`, `dpkg-query`, `rpm` in that order in `path_dirs`; run the first one found with `--version` through `std::process::Command` with stdin, stderr null and a 2 s limit (poll `try_wait` every 10 ms, then `kill` and `wait`). Parse: pacman, the token after `Pacman v` (`7.0.0`); dpkg-query, the token after `version ` (`1.21.22`); rpm, the token after `RPM version ` (`4.19.1`). Output form `"<pacman|dpkg|rpm> <version>"`. No match or timeout gives `None`. Run once per inventory read.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `PRETTY_NAME="CachyOS Linux"\nID=cachyos\nBUILD_ID=rolling\nLOGO=cachyos\n` **When** parsed **Then** pretty_name "CachyOS Linux", id "cachyos", build_id "rolling", logo "cachyos", version_id `None`.
- **Given** `NAME="A \"quoted\" \\ name"` **When** parsed **Then** name is `A "quoted" \ name`.
- **Given** no `<etc>/os-release` but `<usr_lib>/os-release` **When** `read_os_release` runs **Then** it reads the second.
- **Given** a fake `pacman` script in a temp `path_dirs` that prints ` .--.                  Pacman v7.0.0 - libalpm v15.0.0` **When** `package_manager_version` runs **Then** it returns "pacman 7.0.0".
- **Given** a fake `pacman` that sleeps 5 s **When** run **Then** the call returns `None` within 3 s.
- **Given** a pacman.log first line `[2024-05-01T10:22:33+0200] [PACMAN] Running 'pacman -S'` and a root without birth time support **When** `read_install_date` runs with the birth time path forced off (test hook) **Then** it returns `(1714551753, PacmanLog)`.
- **Given** a machine-id file `0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\n` **When** read **Then** that 32-char string.

## Files

- `crates/tl-collect/src/inventory/mod.rs`: add `pub mod os_release;`
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/dmi-desktop/{etc/os-release,etc/machine-id,var/log/pacman.log}`: create

- `tests/prop_netsys.rs` inventory section: `prop_os_release_never_panics`.

- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the child process runs once per inventory read, on the blocking pool (E12).
- Privacy: the machine ID is shown only on the Information tab; never log it.

## Notes
- `rustix::fs::statx` with `StatxFlags::BTIME`; `rustix::system::uname`.

title: E06-018 Memory modules from udev without serials
description:
## Context
Reads the memory module (DIMM) details that systemd's `dmi_memory_id` stores as udev properties, for the Memory page and the Information tab. Serial numbers are never read, stored, shown or copied (D-007, R-030), so the parser skips the `SERIAL_NUMBER` key before it allocates anything. No root and no `dmidecode` are needed. Sources: PERF-046, PERF-099, D-007, R-030.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/inventory/modules.rs` (add `pub mod modules;` to `inventory/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct MemoryModule {
    pub index: u32,                     // n in MEMORY_DEVICE_<n>_*, SMBIOS order
    pub size_bytes: u64,                // SIZE
    pub locator: Option<Arc<str>>,      // LOCATOR, e.g. "DIMM 0"
    pub bank_locator: Option<Arc<str>>, // BANK_LOCATOR, e.g. "P0 CHANNEL A"
    pub speed_mts: Option<u32>,         // SPEED_MTS
    pub configured_speed_mts: Option<u32>, // CONFIGURED_SPEED_MTS
    pub mem_type: Option<Arc<str>>,     // TYPE as reported (DDR4, DDR5, LPDDR5, ...)
    pub form_factor: Option<Arc<str>>,  // FORM_FACTOR
    pub manufacturer: Option<Arc<str>>, // MANUFACTURER
    pub part_number: Option<Arc<str>>,  // PART_NUMBER, trimmed
    pub rank: Option<u32>,              // RANK
    pub configured_voltage_mv: Option<u32>, // CONFIGURED_VOLTAGE (millivolts)
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum ModulesInfo {
    Modules { slots_total: Option<u32>, modules: Vec<MemoryModule> }, // slots_total = MEMORY_ARRAY_NUM_DEVICES
    NotReported,                                                       // no MEMORY_DEVICE_ keys at all
}
pub const UDEV_DMI_DATA: &str = "/run/udev/data/+dmi:id";
pub fn parse_udev_dmi(bytes: &[u8]) -> ModulesInfo;
pub fn read_modules(udev_dmi: &Path) -> ModulesInfo; // missing or unreadable file -> NotReported
```

Rules:
- Only lines starting with `E:` are read; the rest (`I:`, `G:`, `Q:`, `V:`) are skipped. The text after `E:` is `KEY=value`.
- Keys used: `MEMORY_ARRAY_NUM_DEVICES` and `MEMORY_DEVICE_<n>_{SIZE,PRESENT,LOCATOR,BANK_LOCATOR,SPEED_MTS,CONFIGURED_SPEED_MTS,TYPE,FORM_FACTOR,MANUFACTURER,PART_NUMBER,RANK,CONFIGURED_VOLTAGE}`. Any key ending in `_SERIAL_NUMBER` (and every other key) is skipped before its value is copied. `MEMORY_ARRAY_*` keys other than `NUM_DEVICES` are ignored.
- A module is kept only if it has `SIZE` > 0 and no `PRESENT=0`. Empty slots are left out. Modules are sorted by `index`.
- Strings are trimmed and pass the `crate::sanitize` filter (E05-A1). Numbers that do not parse leave the field `None` (a bad `SIZE` drops the module).
- Read at most 64 KiB.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** udev data with `MEMORY_ARRAY_NUM_DEVICES=4`, devices 0 and 2 populated (16 GiB DDR4 3200, Kingston, part `KHX3200C18D4/16G`, locator `DIMM 0`, bank `P0 CHANNEL A`, voltage 1350) and devices 1 and 3 with `PRESENT=0` **When** parsed **Then** `Modules { slots_total: Some(4), modules }` with two modules, indexes 0 and 2, `size_bytes == 17179869184`, `configured_voltage_mv == Some(1350)`.
- **Given** the same data with `E:MEMORY_DEVICE_0_SERIAL_NUMBER=SERIAL-MUST-NOT-APPEAR` **When** parsed **Then** `format!("{:?}", result)` does not contain `SERIAL-MUST-NOT-APPEAR`.
- **Given** udev data with no `MEMORY_DEVICE_` keys **When** parsed **Then** `NotReported`.
- **Given** a missing file **When** `read_modules` runs **Then** `NotReported`.
- **Given** `E:MEMORY_DEVICE_0_SIZE=abc` **When** parsed **Then** device 0 is dropped.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/inventory/modules.rs`: create with unit tests
- `crates/tl-collect/src/inventory/mod.rs`: add `pub mod modules;`
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/dmi-desktop/run/udev/data/+dmi:id`: create with the first criterion's data plus the serial line

- `tests/prop_netsys.rs` inventory section: `prop_udev_dmi_never_panics`.

title: E06-019 Display connectors from sysfs and EDID
description:
## Context
Lists the display connectors of each DRM card from sysfs and reads the monitor name from EDID, for the GPU page's Displays list and Information > Graphics > Resolution. This bead covers the sysfs path, which PERF-072 names as the fallback. The KMS ioctl path (current mode, refresh, `max bpc`) needs `unsafe` or a new crate and is an open item; KScreen data (`kscreen-doctor -j`) is an engine concern. Sources: PERF-072, PERF-073, R-057, U-26.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/inventory/displays.rs` (add `pub mod displays;` to `inventory/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum ConnectorType { Unknown, Vga, DviI, DviD, DviA, Composite, SVideo, Lvds, Component, Din,
    DisplayPort, Hdmi, Tv, Edp, Virtual, Dsi, Dpi, Writeback, Spi, Usb }

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct ConnectorInfo {
    pub card: u32,                     // N of cardN
    pub sysfs_name: Arc<str>,          // "card1-DP-2"
    pub connector_type: ConnectorType,
    pub connected: bool,               // status == "connected"
    pub enabled: Option<bool>,         // "enabled" file: enabled/disabled; None when absent
    pub monitor_name: Option<Arc<str>>,// EDID descriptor 0xFC
    pub modes: SmallVec<[(u32, u32); 4]>, // "modes" lines "WxH" in file order; first is the preferred mode
}
/// Every connector directory <sys>/class/drm/card<N>-<NAME> for one card, sorted by sysfs name.
pub fn read_connectors(sys: &Path, card: u32) -> Vec<ConnectorInfo>;
pub fn connector_type_from_sysfs(name_after_card: &str) -> ConnectorType;
pub fn edid_monitor_name(edid: &[u8]) -> Option<Arc<str>>;
```

Rules:
- Connector type from the sysfs name prefix (after `cardN-`, before the last `-<index>`), using the kernel names: `VGA`, `DVI-I`, `DVI-D`, `DVI-A`, `Composite`, `SVIDEO`, `LVDS`, `Component`, `DIN`, `DP` (DisplayPort), `HDMI-A` and `HDMI-B` (both `Hdmi`), `TV`, `eDP`, `Virtual`, `DSI`, `DPI`, `Writeback`, `SPI`, `USB`; anything else `Unknown`.
- `status` file: `connected` gives true; anything else false. Files are read with a 4 KiB cap except `edid` (cap 32 KiB).
- EDID: needs at least 128 bytes and the header `00 FF FF FF FF FF FF 00`; otherwise `None`. Look at the four 18-byte descriptors at offsets 54, 72, 90, 108; a display descriptor has bytes 0, 1 and 2 equal to 0 and byte 3 the tag. Tag `0xFC` gives the name from bytes 5..18, cut at the first `0x0A`, trailing spaces removed. Keep only bytes 0x20 to 0x7E. An empty result gives `None`. The checksum is not enforced.
- Only connected connectors with `enabled != Some(false)` are listed by the UI; this reader returns all connectors so the engine can apply KScreen's view (PERF-072: disconnected and disabled connectors are not listed).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fixture `sys/class/drm/card1-DP-2/{status,enabled,modes,edid}` with `connected`, `enabled`, `3840x2160\n1920x1080\n` and an EDID whose 0xFC descriptor holds `LG ULTRAGEAR\n   ` **When** `read_connectors(sys, 1)` runs **Then** one entry: type `DisplayPort`, connected, enabled `Some(true)`, monitor "LG ULTRAGEAR", modes `[(3840, 2160), (1920, 1080)]`.
- **Given** `card1-HDMI-A-1` with status `disconnected` and an empty `edid` **When** read **Then** connected false and monitor `None`.
- **Given** EDID bytes with a bad header **When** `edid_monitor_name` runs **Then** `None`.
- **Given** an EDID name containing byte 0x1B **When** parsed **Then** that byte is dropped.
- **Given** the name `Writeback-1` **When** typed **Then** `Writeback`; `XYZ-1` gives `Unknown`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/inventory/displays.rs`: create with unit tests
- `crates/tl-collect/src/inventory/mod.rs`: add `pub mod displays;`
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_inventory.rs`: add `real_connectors_listed`
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/dmi-desktop/sys/class/drm/{card1-DP-2,card1-HDMI-A-1}/*`: create (the EDID is a hand-built 128-byte file committed as binary)

## Tests

- `tests/prop_netsys.rs` inventory section: `prop_edid_never_panics`.
- `tests/fixture_inventory.rs::real_connectors_listed` (`#[ignore]`): prints every connector of every card (U-26).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: none returned; unreadable files leave fields empty.
- Validity: missing refresh, bit depth and orientation show "Not reported" until the KMS and KScreen open items are settled.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: read on GPU page open and on KScreen change (engine).
- Privacy: EDID serial fields are not parsed or kept.

title: E06-020 DRM card discovery and PCIe link
description:
## Context
Finds the DRM GPUs in sysfs and reads the vendor-neutral facts the GPU pages and the `GpuDrm` worker (E12) need: vendor, PCI slot (matched to NVML's bus id for NVIDIA), driver, hwmon directory and the PCIe link. AMD and Intel are read in-process; NVIDIA metrics stay in `tl-gpu-probe`. Sources: PERF-062 (discovery), PERF-070 (PCIe link fallback), PERF-069 (hwmon path), ADR-016.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-collect/src/gpu_drm/mod.rs`:

```rust
pub const VENDOR_NVIDIA: u16 = 0x10de;
pub const VENDOR_AMD: u16 = 0x1002;
pub const VENDOR_INTEL: u16 = 0x8086;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct DrmCard {
    pub card: u32,                       // N of /sys/class/drm/cardN
    pub vendor: u16,                     // device/vendor
    pub device_id: u16,                  // device/device
    pub pci_slot: Arc<str>,              // PCI_SLOT_NAME from device/uevent, e.g. "0000:2d:00.0"
    pub driver: Option<Arc<str>>,        // basename of the device/driver symlink: "amdgpu", "i915", "xe", "nvidia"
    pub hwmon: Option<PathBuf>,          // first device/hwmon/hwmon* directory
}
/// cardN directories only (names "card" + digits), vendors NVIDIA, AMD and Intel, sorted by N.
pub fn discover_cards(sys: &Path) -> Vec<DrmCard>;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct PcieLink { pub cur_gen: Option<u8>, pub cur_width: Option<u8>, pub max_gen: Option<u8>, pub max_width: Option<u8> }
pub fn read_pcie_link(sys: &Path, card: &DrmCard) -> PcieLink;
pub fn gts_to_gen(gts: f32) -> Option<u8>;
```

Rules:
- `vendor` and `device` files hold `0x` hex; other vendors are skipped. Connector directories such as `card1-DP-2` are not cards.
- `pci_slot`: the `PCI_SLOT_NAME=` line of `device/uevent`; a card without it is skipped.
- PCIe: `device/current_link_speed`, `device/max_link_speed` hold text like `16.0 GT/s PCIe`; take the number before ` GT/s`. `gts_to_gen`: 2.5 to 1, 5 to 2, 8 to 3, 16 to 4, 32 to 5, 64 to 6 (compare with a 0.1 tolerance); other values `None`. `device/current_link_width` and `max_link_width` are decimal.
- Card N's NVIDIA match with NVML is by `pci_slot` compared case-insensitively against NVML's bus id with the domain cut to 4 hex digits (NVML `00000000:2D:00.0` matches `0000:2d:00.0`); provide `pub fn same_pci_slot(sysfs: &str, nvml: &str) -> bool`.

- **Given** `current_link_speed` `16.0 GT/s PCIe`, width `16`, max `32.0 GT/s PCIe`, width `16` **When** read **Then** `PcieLink { cur_gen: Some(4), cur_width: Some(16), max_gen: Some(5), max_width: Some(16) }`.
- **Given** `same_pci_slot("0000:2d:00.0", "00000000:2D:00.0")` **When** compared **Then** true.
- **Given** a card with vendor `0x1af4` **When** discovered **Then** it is skipped.

title: E06-021 DRM fdinfo client parser and engine busy
description:
## Context
Parses DRM fdinfo (`/proc/<pid>/fdinfo/<fd>` of fds open on `/dev/dri/*`) to get per-client engine busy time and memory for AMD (Compute, DMA, JPEG engines; encode and decode fallback) and Intel (all engines). Only processes tasklens can read are covered, and the result says so ("Own processes only"). Sources: PERF-074, PERF-075, PERF-064 (Intel memory keys), PERF-065 (AMD enc/dec fallback), ADR-016.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/gpu_drm/fdinfo.rs` (add `pub mod fdinfo;` to `gpu_drm/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct DrmClient {
    pub pid: u32,
    pub driver: Arc<str>,                  // drm-driver
    pub pdev: Arc<str>,                    // drm-pdev, e.g. "0000:03:00.0"
    pub client_id: u64,                    // drm-client-id
    pub engine_ns: SmallVec<[(Arc<str>, u64); 8]>,   // drm-engine-<name>: <n> ns
    pub cycles: SmallVec<[(Arc<str>, u64); 8]>,      // drm-cycles-<name>
    pub total_cycles: SmallVec<[(Arc<str>, u64); 8]>,// drm-total-cycles-<name>
    pub resident_bytes: SmallVec<[(Arc<str>, u64); 4]>, // drm-resident-<region>: <n> KiB|MiB|B
    pub total_bytes: SmallVec<[(Arc<str>, u64); 4]>,    // drm-total-<region>
}
/// Parses one fdinfo file. None when there is no drm-driver line or no drm-client-id.
pub fn parse_fdinfo(pid: u32, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<DrmClient>;

pub struct FdinfoScan { pub clients: Vec<DrmClient>, pub partial: bool, pub t_ns: tl_model::TimeNs }
/// Walks <proc>/<pid>/fd, keeps fds whose link target starts with "/dev/dri/", reads their fdinfo.
/// Clients are de-duplicated by (pdev, client_id); the first one wins.
pub fn scan(root: &SysRoot, out: &mut FdinfoScan);

/// Busy percent per engine name for one pdev between two scans: sum over clients of
/// delta(engine_ns) / delta(t_ns) * 100, clamped to 0..=100. Clients present in only one scan add nothing.
pub fn engine_busy(prev: &FdinfoScan, cur: &FdinfoScan, pdev: &str, out: &mut SmallVec<[(Arc<str>, f32); 8]>);
/// Same for xe cycles: delta(cycles) / delta(total_cycles) * 100 per engine, summed over clients, clamped.
pub fn engine_busy_cycles(prev: &FdinfoScan, cur: &FdinfoScan, pdev: &str, out: &mut SmallVec<[(Arc<str>, f32); 8]>);
```

Rules:
- Lines are `key:<whitespace>value`. Engine values end in ` ns`. Memory values end in ` KiB`, ` MiB` or nothing (bytes); convert to bytes.
- `scan` sets `partial = true` when any `/proc/<pid>/fd` or fdinfo read gives `EACCES` or `EPERM`. Gone pids are skipped silently.
- Counters that went backwards add nothing (reset rule, ADR-008). `t_ns` is `now_boot_ns()` read before the walk.
- `scan` reuses `out.clients` capacity; engine and region names are interned per scan (one `Arc<str>` per distinct name).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** fdinfo text with `drm-driver: amdgpu`, `drm-pdev: 0000:03:00.0`, `drm-client-id: 12`, `drm-engine-gfx: 5000000 ns`, `drm-engine-compute: 1000000 ns`, `drm-resident-vram: 2048 KiB` **When** parsed **Then** the client holds those values with `resident vram == 2097152`.
- **Given** text without `drm-driver` **When** parsed **Then** `None`.
- **Given** two scans 1 s apart where client 12's `compute` rises by 250000000 ns **When** `engine_busy` runs **Then** `compute == 25.0`.
- **Given** two fds of one process with the same client id **When** scanned **Then** one client.
- **Given** a fixture proc tree where one pid's `fdinfo` cannot be read (simulated by a test hook returning EACCES) **When** scanned **Then** `partial == true`.
- **Given** xe text with `drm-cycles-rcs: 600` then `900` and `drm-total-cycles-rcs: 1000` then `2000` **When** `engine_busy_cycles` runs **Then** `rcs == 30.0`.

- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/drm-basic/proc/<pid>/{fd,fdinfo}/*`: create (fd symlinks to `/dev/dri/renderD128`)

title: E06-022 AMD GPU sysfs, hwmon and gpu_metrics readers
description:
## Context
Reads AMD GPU metrics from sysfs and hwmon for the GPU pages: utilization, memory, clocks, power, temperatures and fan. The `GpuDrm` worker (E12) samples it at 1 Hz and adds the fdinfo engines (E06-021). Not testable on the owner machine (NVIDIA only), so fixtures carry the tests. Sources: PERF-074, PERF-064, PERF-065, PERF-066, PERF-067, PERF-068, PERF-069.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/gpu_drm/amdgpu.rs` (add `pub mod amdgpu;` to `gpu_drm/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct AmdSample {
    pub gpu_busy_pct: Option<u8>,      // device/gpu_busy_percent
    pub mem_busy_pct: Option<u8>,      // device/mem_busy_percent
    pub vram_used: Option<u64>, pub vram_total: Option<u64>, // device/mem_info_vram_{used,total}, bytes
    pub gtt_used: Option<u64>,  pub gtt_total: Option<u64>,  // device/mem_info_gtt_{used,total}
    pub sclk_mhz: Option<u32>, pub mclk_mhz: Option<u32>,    // hwmon freq1_input, freq2_input (Hz / 1_000_000)
    pub sclk_max_mhz: Option<u32>, pub mclk_max_mhz: Option<u32>, // last line of device/pp_dpm_sclk, pp_dpm_mclk
    pub power_uw: Option<u64>,         // hwmon power1_input, else power1_average
    pub power_cap_uw: Option<u64>,     // hwmon power1_cap
    pub temps: SmallVec<[(AmdTemp, i32); 3]>, // millidegrees C, from temp1/2/3_input with temp*_label
    pub fan_rpm: Option<u32>,          // hwmon fan1_input
    pub fan_pwm: Option<u8>,           // hwmon pwm1, 0..=255
    pub metrics: Option<GpuMetrics>,   // device/gpu_metrics
}
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AmdTemp { Edge, Junction, Mem }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct GpuMetrics {
    pub format_revision: u8, pub content_revision: u8,
    pub average_gfx_activity: Option<u16>, pub average_umc_activity: Option<u16>,
    pub vcn_activity: SmallVec<[u16; 4]>,
    pub temperature_edge: Option<u16>, pub temperature_hotspot: Option<u16>, pub temperature_mem: Option<u16>,
}
pub fn read_amd(card: &DrmCard, sys: &Path, out: &mut AmdSample);
pub fn parse_gpu_metrics(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<GpuMetrics>;
pub fn parse_dpm_max_mhz(text: &[u8]) -> Option<u32>; // "2: 2500Mhz *" -> 2500
/// Main temperature: Junction when present, else Edge (PERF-068). Source text per PERF-069:
/// "hwmon amdgpu: junction", "hwmon amdgpu: edge" or "hwmon amdgpu: mem".
pub fn main_temp(s: &AmdSample) -> Option<(AmdTemp, i32)>;
pub fn temp_source_text(t: AmdTemp) -> &'static str;
```

Rules:
- Paths are `<sys>/class/drm/card<N>/device/...` and the card's `hwmon` directory (E06-020). Temperature labels come from `temp*_label` (`edge`, `junction`, `mem`); a sensor without a known label is ignored.
- `gpu_metrics`: header bytes 0..4 are `structure_size: u16 LE`, `format_revision: u8`, `content_revision: u8`. Parse format 1 content 0 to 3 and format 2 content 0 to 4 with the field offsets of the kernel structs `gpu_metrics_v1_0` to `gpu_metrics_v1_3` and `gpu_metrics_v2_0` to `gpu_metrics_v2_4` in `drivers/gpu/drm/amd/include/kgd_pp_interface.h`; copy the offsets into constants with a comment naming the struct. A field equal to `0xFFFF` is `None`. Any other revision, or a buffer shorter than `structure_size`, gives `None`.
- Every file read is capped at 4 KiB (`gpu_metrics` 4 KiB too); unreadable or unparsable files leave the field `None`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the `drm-amd` fixture (gpu_busy_percent `37`, mem_info_vram_used `3006477107`, total `17095983104`, hwmon freq1_input `1905000000`, pp_dpm_sclk ending `2: 2500Mhz *`, power1_average `31900000`, power1_cap `300000000`, temp1 edge 52000, temp2 junction 61000) **When** `read_amd` runs **Then** the sample holds those values, `sclk_mhz == Some(1905)`, `sclk_max_mhz == Some(2500)`.
- **Given** that sample **When** `main_temp` runs **Then** `(Junction, 61000)` and `temp_source_text(Junction) == "hwmon amdgpu: junction"`.
- **Given** no `power1_input` but `power1_average` **When** read **Then** `power_uw` is the average.
- **Given** a `gpu_metrics` blob with format 9 **When** parsed **Then** `None`.
- **Given** a hand-built v1_3 blob with `average_gfx_activity = 4200` and `temperature_hotspot = 0xFFFF` **When** parsed **Then** `Some(4200)` and `None`.

- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/drm-amd/sys/class/drm/card0/device/**`: create

## Tests
