title: E06-023 Intel GPU readers for i915 and xe
description:
## Context
Reads Intel GPU (i915 and xe) clocks, power, temperature and memory, and maps fdinfo engines, for the GPU pages in P3. Engines use the fdinfo fallback of PERF-075; the i915 PMU path needs `perf_event_open`, which has no safe wrapper in the allowed crates, and is an open item. Not testable on the owner machine. Sources: PERF-075, PERF-064, PERF-066, PERF-067, PERF-068, PERF-069.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/gpu_drm/intel.rs` (add `pub mod intel;` to `gpu_drm/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum IntelDriver { I915, Xe }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct IntelSample {
    pub act_freq_mhz: Option<u32>, pub max_freq_mhz: Option<u32>,
    pub energy_uj: Option<u64>,       // hwmon energy1_input, the engine computes power from the delta
    pub power_max_uw: Option<u64>,    // hwmon power1_max
    pub temp_mc: Option<i32>,         // hwmon temp1_input (dGPU only)
}
pub fn read_intel(card: &DrmCard, sys: &Path, drv: IntelDriver, out: &mut IntelSample);
/// Engine display names for fdinfo engine keys (PERF-075).
pub fn i915_engine_name(key: &str) -> Option<&'static str>; // render, copy, video, video-enhance, compute
/// Memory from fdinfo: (local resident, local total) summed over clients for pdev; system resident for iGPU.
pub fn fdinfo_memory(scan: &FdinfoScan, pdev: &str) -> (Option<u64>, Option<u64>, Option<u64>);
pub fn temp_source_text(drv: IntelDriver) -> &'static str; // "hwmon i915" or "hwmon xe: pkg"
```

Rules:
- Clocks: i915 `<sys>/class/drm/card<N>/gt_act_freq_mhz` and `gt_max_freq_mhz`; xe `<card>/device/tile0/gt0/freq0/act_freq` and `max_freq`.
- Power: hwmon `energy1_input` (microjoules) and `power1_max` (microwatts) from the card's hwmon directory.
- Temperature: hwmon `temp1_input` when present (dGPU); none on an iGPU.
- Memory: sum of `drm-resident-local0` and `drm-total-local0` over clients for the card's pdev; iGPU "Shared" from summed `drm-resident-system0`.
- Engines: i915 keys `render`, `copy`, `video`, `video-enhance`, `compute` through `engine_busy` (ns); xe through `engine_busy_cycles`.
- Driver from `DrmCard::driver` (`i915` or `xe`); other Intel drivers are not read.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** an i915 fixture with `gt_act_freq_mhz` `1300` and `gt_max_freq_mhz` `2200` **When** read **Then** `act_freq_mhz == Some(1300)`, `max_freq_mhz == Some(2200)`.
- **Given** an xe fixture with `device/tile0/gt0/freq0/act_freq` `900` **When** read **Then** `act_freq_mhz == Some(900)`.
- **Given** an fdinfo scan with two clients on pdev P with `drm-resident-local0` 1024 KiB and 2048 KiB **When** `fdinfo_memory` runs **Then** local resident is 3145728.
- **Given** keys `render` and `foo` **When** `i915_engine_name` runs **Then** `Some("render")` and `None`.
- **Given** `IntelDriver::Xe` **When** `temp_source_text` runs **Then** "hwmon xe: pkg".

title: E06-A3 Inventory readers
description:
## Context
Anchor E06-A3 "Inventory readers". It closes the inventory set (`inventory/{cpuinfo,dmi,os_release,displays,modules}.rs`, E06-014 to E06-019) behind one entry point for the `Inventory` worker (E12), and it also closes the P2 AMD DRM readers (`gpu_drm/{mod,fdinfo,amdgpu}.rs`, E06-020 to E06-022), because E12's `GpuDrm` worker depends on this anchor only (00-epics.md section 4). Memory module serials are never read (D-007). Sources: PERF-094 to PERF-104, PERF-046, PERF-072, PERF-074, ADR-016, D-007, R-030.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-collect/src/inventory/mod.rs`:

```rust
pub use cpuinfo::{CpuInfo, CpuFlags, parse_cpuinfo, identifier, SecurityInfo, Virtualization, Lockdown, VulnCounts, SecuritySource, SecurityPaths, read_security};
pub use dmi::{DmiInfo, Field, FirmwareType, read_dmi};
pub use os_release::{OsRelease, KernelInfo, InstallDateSource, read_os_release, read_kernel, read_machine_id, read_install_date, package_manager_version};
pub use modules::{MemoryModule, ModulesInfo, read_modules};
pub use displays::{ConnectorType, ConnectorInfo, read_connectors, edid_monitor_name};

pub struct InventoryPaths {
    pub proc: PathBuf,       // /proc
    pub sys: PathBuf,        // /sys

    pub etc: PathBuf,        // /etc
    pub usr_lib: PathBuf,    // /usr/lib

    pub pacman_log: PathBuf, // /var/log/pacman.log

}
impl InventoryPaths { pub fn system() -> Self; pub fn under(root: &Path) -> Self; } // under(): every path joined below `root`

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct InventoryRaw {
    pub cpu: CpuInfo, pub security: SecurityInfo, pub dmi: DmiInfo,
```

title: E06-002 sock_diag record types and dump parser
description:
## Context
Defines the raw socket record that every Connections and per-process network feature uses, and the parser that turns a `NETLINK_SOCK_DIAG` dump reply into records. Parsing is pure (bytes in, records out), so fixtures and proptests cover it without a kernel. Sources: SYS-028, PROC-032, ADR-016 ("Per-process network", "Connections"), ADR-013 (fixtures, proptests).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/net/sock_diag.rs` (add `pub mod sock_diag;` to `net/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug, Hash)]
pub enum Family { V4, V6 }            // AF_INET = 2, AF_INET6 = 10
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug, Hash)]
pub enum Proto { Tcp, Udp }           // IPPROTO_TCP = 6, IPPROTO_UDP = 17

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug, Default)]
pub struct TcpInfoLite {
    pub bytes_acked: u64,       // tcpi_bytes_acked: bytes sent and acknowledged
    pub bytes_received: u64,    // tcpi_bytes_received
    pub rtt_us: u32,            // tcpi_rtt
    pub rttvar_us: u32,         // tcpi_rttvar
    pub snd_cwnd: u32,          // tcpi_snd_cwnd
    pub total_retrans: u32,     // tcpi_total_retrans
    pub last_data_recv_ms: u32, // tcpi_last_data_recv
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct SockRecord {
    pub family: Family,
    pub proto: Proto,
    pub state: u8,                     // kernel TCP state number (1 ESTABLISHED .. 12 NEW_SYN_RECV); UDP: 7 CLOSE = unconnected, 1 ESTABLISHED = connected
    pub src: std::net::IpAddr,         // id.idiag_src (first 4 bytes for V4)
    pub dst: std::net::IpAddr,         // id.idiag_dst
    pub sport: u16,                    // host byte order
    pub dport: u16,
    pub ifindex: u32,                  // id.idiag_if
    pub cookie: u64,                   // id.idiag_cookie, the two u32 words as (hi << 32) | lo
    pub rqueue: u32,
    pub wqueue: u32,
    pub uid: u32,
    pub inode: u64,                    // 0 for TIME-WAIT and orphaned sockets
    pub tcp_info: Option<TcpInfoLite>, // only for TCP when INET_DIAG_INFO was present
}

/// Appends every record in one or more netlink messages in `buf` to `out`.
/// Returns Ok(true) when an NLMSG_DONE was seen, Ok(false) when more messages are expected.
pub fn parse_dump(buf: &[u8], family: Family, proto: Proto, out: &mut Vec<SockRecord>) -> Result<bool, CollectError>;
```

Rules:
- Walk the buffer by netlink header length (`nlmsg_len`, 4-byte aligned). A header with `nlmsg_len < 16` or past the end of `buf` gives `CollectError::NetlinkMalformed("short netlink header")`.
- `NLMSG_ERROR` (type 2) with a negative error gives `CollectError::SockDiagErrno(-error)`; error 0 is an ACK and is skipped. `NLMSG_DONE` (type 3) ends the dump.
- `SOCK_DIAG_BY_FAMILY` (type 20) messages are parsed as `inet_diag_msg` with `netlink-packet-sock-diag` 0.5 (`SockDiagMessage::InetResponse`), or by hand from the fixed 72-byte `inet_diag_msg` layout when the crate type does not expose a field. Ports are big-endian on the wire.
- `INET_DIAG_INFO` (attribute type 2) holds `struct tcp_info`. Read the fields above at their kernel offsets (`include/uapi/linux/tcp.h`); a payload shorter than the offset of `tcpi_bytes_received` + 8 leaves `tcp_info = None` (old kernel), it is not an error.
- An unknown attribute is skipped. A truncated attribute gives `NetlinkMalformed("truncated attribute")`.
- `parse_dump` never panics on any input and allocates only by pushing to `out`.

Also `pub fn tcp_state_label(state: u8) -> &'static str` with the SYS-029 table: 10 LISTEN "LISTENING", 2 SYN_SENT "SYN-SENT", 3 SYN_RECV and 12 NEW_SYN_RECV "SYN-RECEIVED", 1 "ESTABLISHED", 4 "FIN-WAIT-1", 5 "FIN-WAIT-2", 8 "CLOSE-WAIT", 11 "CLOSING", 9 "LAST-ACK", 6 "TIME-WAIT", 7 "CLOSED", any other "UNKNOWN"; and `pub fn udp_state_label(state: u8) -> &'static str`: 1 "CONNECTED", any other "UNCONNECTED".

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a buffer with one TCP v4 `inet_diag_msg` (src 127.0.0.1:631, dst 0.0.0.0:0, state 10, inode 4242, cookie words lo=7 hi=1) and `NLMSG_DONE` **When** `parse_dump` runs **Then** `out` holds one record with those values, `cookie == (1 << 32) | 7` and the function returns `Ok(true)`.
- **Given** a TCP v6 message with an `INET_DIAG_INFO` attribute whose `tcpi_bytes_acked` is 1000 and `tcpi_bytes_received` is 2000 **When** parsed **Then** `tcp_info` holds those two values.
- **Given** an `INET_DIAG_INFO` payload shorter than the `tcpi_bytes_received` offset **When** parsed **Then** the record is kept with `tcp_info == None`.
- **Given** an `NLMSG_ERROR` with error -13 **When** parsed **Then** the result is `Err(CollectError::SockDiagErrno(13))`.
- **Given** a header whose `nlmsg_len` runs past the buffer **When** parsed **Then** the result is `Err(NetlinkMalformed(..))` and no panic.
- **Given** state 12 **When** `tcp_state_label` runs **Then** it returns "SYN-RECEIVED"; state 99 gives "UNKNOWN".

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/net/sock_diag.rs`: create (types, parser, labels, unit tests)
- `crates/tl-collect/src/net/mod.rs`: add `pub mod sock_diag;`
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/prop_netsys.rs`: in the sockets section, add the proptest below

## Tests
- `net::sock_diag::tests::parse_tcp4_listener`: first criterion.
- `net::sock_diag::tests::parse_tcp6_with_info`: second criterion.
- `net::sock_diag::tests::short_tcp_info_is_none`: third criterion.
- `net::sock_diag::tests::nlmsg_error_maps_errno`: fourth criterion.
- `net::sock_diag::tests::overlong_header_is_malformed`: fifth criterion.
- `net::sock_diag::tests::state_labels_match_sys029`: every row of the label table.
- `tests/prop_netsys.rs::prop_sock_diag_never_panics`: arbitrary bytes up to 64 KiB into `parse_dump` never panic.
Build the test buffers in a helper `fn msg(...) -> Vec<u8>` in the test module, using the crate's `emit` where it exists.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `SockDiagErrno(errno)`, `NetlinkMalformed(reason)`; no user text here.
- Validity: N/A (the engine maps a failed dump to `Validity::Failed`).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no allocation besides pushes to `out`; the caller reuses `out` between dumps.
- Privacy: never log addresses or ports at any level above `trace`.

## Notes
- Kernel layouts: `include/uapi/linux/inet_diag.h` (`inet_diag_sockid`, `inet_diag_msg`), `include/uapi/linux/tcp.h` (`tcp_info`).
- The cookie is stored as two native-endian u32 words, `idiag_cookie[0]` low and `[1]` high.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`, for example `... cargo test -p tl-collect`. title: E06-003 sock_diag netlink dump requests
description:
## Context
Sends the `SOCK_DIAG_BY_FAMILY` dump requests to the kernel and feeds the replies to `parse_dump` (E06-002). The Connections worker (E14) calls it every 2 s while demanded; the per-process TCP column uses the TCP part. Unprivileged dumps work; the `inet_diag` and `udp_diag` modules load on demand. Sources: SYS-028, PROC-032, ADR-016, ADR-008 (connections every 2 s).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-collect/src/net/sock_diag.rs`:

```rust
pub struct SockDiag { sock: netlink_sys::Socket, buf: Vec<u8>, seq: u32 }
impl SockDiag {
    /// Opens a NETLINK_SOCK_DIAG (protocol 4) socket with SOCK_CLOEXEC, bound with port id 0.
    pub fn open() -> Result<Self, CollectError>;
    /// One dump for one family and protocol. Appends to `out`.
    pub fn dump(&mut self, family: Family, proto: Proto, out: &mut Vec<SockRecord>) -> Result<(), CollectError>;
    /// The four dumps TCPv4, TCPv6, UDPv4, UDPv6 in that order. Clears `out` first.
    pub fn dump_all(&mut self, out: &mut Vec<SockRecord>) -> Result<(), CollectError>;
    /// TCP v4 and v6 only, for per-process attribution when the Connections tab is not shown.
    pub fn dump_tcp(&mut self, out: &mut Vec<SockRecord>) -> Result<(), CollectError>;
}
```

Request (`inet_diag_req_v2`): `sdiag_family` = 2 or 10, `sdiag_protocol` = 6 or 17, `idiag_states = 0xFFF` (all states), `idiag_ext = 1 << (INET_DIAG_INFO - 1)` for TCP (INET_DIAG_INFO = 2) and 0 for UDP, zeroed `id` with `idiag_cookie = [!0, !0]` (INET_DIAG_NOCOOKIE). Netlink flags `NLM_F_REQUEST | NLM_F_DUMP` (0x1 | 0x300), type 20, sequence number incremented per request.

Receive loop: `recv` into `buf` (capacity 64 KiB, kept between calls) until `parse_dump` returns `Ok(true)`. A reply whose sequence number differs from the request is skipped. `EINTR` is retried; any other `recv` error is returned. A protocol whose diag module is missing (`ENOENT` or `EINVAL` in `NLMSG_ERROR`) returns `Ok(())` with nothing appended, so UDP missing never hides TCP.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a test process that listens on TCP 127.0.0.1 port P **When** `dump_all` runs **Then** `out` holds a TCP V4 record with `sport == P`, `state == 10` and `inode != 0`.
- **Given** a bound UDP v6 socket on [::1] port Q **When** `dump_all` runs **Then** `out` holds a UDP V6 record with `sport == Q`.
- **Given** an established TCP pair over loopback that has sent 1000 bytes **When** `dump_tcp` runs **Then** the sender's record has `tcp_info.bytes_acked >= 1000`.
- **Given** two calls to `dump_all` **When** the second runs **Then** `out` holds only the second dump (cleared first) and the `buf` capacity is unchanged.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/net/sock_diag.rs`: add `SockDiag`
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_sockets.rs`: create the file with the real-system tests below (E06-A1 adds the fixture tests to the same file)

## Tests
- `tests/fixture_sockets.rs::real_dump_sees_tcp_listener` (`#[ignore]`, real system): first criterion with `std::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0")`.
- `tests/fixture_sockets.rs::real_dump_sees_udp6` (`#[ignore]`): second criterion.
- `tests/fixture_sockets.rs::real_tcp_info_bytes_acked` (`#[ignore]`): third criterion.
- `net::sock_diag::tests::dump_all_clears_out` (`#[ignore]`): fourth criterion.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: socket open failure maps to the I/O variant of `CollectError`; kernel errors to `SockDiagErrno`.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one 64 KiB buffer reused; no per-record allocation besides `out` growth.
- Privacy: no address logging above `trace`.

## Notes
- `netlink-sys` 0.9 with `default-features = false` (ADR-002): `Socket::new(NETLINK_SOCK_DIAG)`, `bind_auto`, `send`, `recv`. Use `netlink-packet-sock-diag` 0.5 `InetRequest` and `NetlinkMessage::finalize` to build the request, or write the 56-byte `inet_diag_req_v2` by hand.

title: E06-004 Socket inode to process map
description:
## Context
Maps socket inodes to the processes that hold them, by walking `/proc/<pid>/fd` symlinks of the form `socket:[<inode>]`. The Connections tab shows the owner from it, and the per-process TCP Network column attributes traffic with it. Other users' fd directories give EACCES; those pids are recorded as restricted so the UI can show the lock glyph, never 0 and never blank. Sources: SYS-030, PROC-032, ADR-016 ("Socket to pid map", "Restricted, not zero"), U-23.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/net/socket_map.rs` (add `pub mod socket_map;` to `net/mod.rs`):

```rust
pub struct SocketMap {
    /// inode -> every process holding an fd to it, sorted by ProcessKey, no duplicates.
    pub owners: rustc_hash::FxHashMap<u64, smallvec::SmallVec<[tl_model::ProcessKey; 1]>>,
    /// pids whose /proc/<pid>/fd could not be read (EACCES or EPERM), with their uid from fstat of /proc/<pid>.
    pub restricted: rustc_hash::FxHashMap<u32, u32>, // pid -> uid
    pub built_ns: tl_model::TimeNs,                   // now_boot_ns() at the start of the walk
    pub elapsed_ns: u64,                              // walk duration, for the U-23 budget
}
impl SocketMap {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    /// Rebuilds in place, reusing the maps' capacity.
    pub fn rebuild(&mut self, root: &SysRoot, boot: tl_model::BootId) -> Result<(), CollectError>;
    pub fn owners_of(&self, inode: u64) -> &[tl_model::ProcessKey]; // empty slice when unknown
}
```

Walk rules:
- Open `<root.proc>` with `O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC`, read entries, keep names that are all digits.
- For each pid: `openat(proc_dirfd, "<pid>", O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC)`; then `openat(pid_dirfd, "fd", O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC)`. `ENOENT` or `ESRCH` (process gone) skips the pid silently. `EACCES` or `EPERM` adds `pid -> st_uid of the pid dir` to `restricted`.
- For each fd entry: `readlinkat(fd_dirfd, name)` into a reused 64-byte buffer. A target that starts with `socket:[` and ends with `]` with digits in between gives the inode. Anything else is ignored.
- Before inserting a pid's inodes, read its `start_ticks` (field 22 of `/proc/<pid>/stat`, parsed from the last `)`) with the reader that E05-A1 delivers in `crate::proc::pid_stat`, using the same `pid_dirfd`. Build `ProcessKey { start_ticks, boot_id: boot, pid }`. If the stat read fails the pid is skipped.
- Every fd is closed in the same walk. Nothing is cached between rebuilds.
- Kernel threads have empty fd dirs and cost one `getdents` each.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the fixture `tests/fixtures/sockets-basic/proc` where pid 100 has fds `3 -> socket:[5001]` and `4 -> /dev/null`, and pid 200 has `5 -> socket:[5001]` **When** `rebuild` runs **Then** `owners_of(5001)` holds the keys for 100 and 200 in `ProcessKey` order and `owners_of(4)` is empty.
- **Given** a pid directory that vanishes between `readdir` and `openat` **When** `rebuild` runs **Then** it returns `Ok` and that pid appears nowhere.
- **Given** a link target `socket:[12x]` or `socket:[]` **When** parsed **Then** it is ignored.
- **Given** the real system as uid 1000 **When** `rebuild` runs **Then** pid 1 is in `restricted` with uid 0 and the test's own TCP listener inode maps to the test's own pid.
- **Given** the real system **When** `rebuild` runs **Then** `elapsed_ns` is recorded; the test prints it, and the bead's close note records the value against the 20 ms target (U-23).

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/net/socket_map.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-collect/src/net/mod.rs`: add `pub mod socket_map;`
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/sockets-basic/proc/{100,200}/{stat,fd/*}`: create (fd entries are committed symlinks with the targets above; stat lines are hand-written with field 22 = 5000 and 6000)

## Tests
- `net::socket_map::tests::fixture_shared_inode`: first criterion against the fixture.
- `net::socket_map::tests::parse_socket_link`: `socket:[5001]` gives 5001; `socket:[12x]`, `socket:[]`, `pipe:[1]`, `/dev/null` give none.
- `net::socket_map::tests::vanished_pid_is_skipped`: a fixture pid dir without `fd` behaves as gone.
- `tests/fixture_sockets.rs::real_socket_map_pid1_restricted` (`#[ignore]`): fourth criterion.
- `tests/fixture_sockets.rs::real_socket_map_timing` (`#[ignore]`): fifth criterion; asserts only that `elapsed_ns > 0`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: only a failure to open `<root.proc>` is returned; per-pid errors are absorbed as above.
- Validity: pids in `restricted` give `Restricted` downstream (E06-005, E06-006); never zero.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: target under 20 ms per rebuild on the owner machine (U-23, unverified). Reuse the maps and the link buffer; no `String` per fd.
- Privacy: never log fd targets or paths. Socket inodes only at `trace`.

## Notes
- `rustix::fs::{openat, readlinkat, Dir, fstat}`; `SysRoot` from E04-A1 (`root.proc`).
- Git stores the fixture symlinks as links; dangling targets such as `socket:[5001]` are fine.

title: E06-005 Per-process TCP attribution
description:
## Context
Turns two TCP dumps plus the socket map into per-process send and receive rates for the process table's Network columns (`network`, `net_send_rate`, `net_recv_rate`). The column is labelled "Network (TCP, attributed)": UDP is not attributed, a socket shared by several processes counts fully for each of them, and the header total includes unattributed traffic. Sources: PROC-032, ADR-016 ("Per-process network"), ADR-008 (counter rules, rates from elapsed time, first sample is WarmingUp).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/net/attribution.rs` (add `pub mod attribution;` to `net/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct NetRate { pub rx_bps: f32, pub tx_bps: f32, pub shared: bool, pub validity: tl_model::Validity }

pub struct TcpAttribution {
    prev: rustc_hash::FxHashMap<u64, (u64, u64)>, // cookie -> (bytes_acked, bytes_received) at prev_ns
    prev_ns: Option<tl_model::TimeNs>,
    pub per_process: rustc_hash::FxHashMap<tl_model::ProcessKey, NetRate>,
    pub restricted_pids: rustc_hash::FxHashMap<u32, u32>, // copied from SocketMap::restricted
    pub total_rx_bps: f32, pub total_tx_bps: f32,             // every TCP socket in the dump
    pub unattributed_rx_bps: f32, pub unattributed_tx_bps: f32, // sockets with inode 0 or no owner
    pub validity: tl_model::Validity,                          // WarmingUp on the first update, else Valid
}
impl TcpAttribution {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    /// `records` from SockDiag::dump_tcp taken at `t_ns` (CLOCK_BOOTTIME read just before the dump).
    pub fn update(&mut self, records: &[SockRecord], map: &SocketMap, t_ns: tl_model::TimeNs);
    /// Drops all baselines (suspend, epoch change, ResetBaselines). The next update is WarmingUp.
    pub fn reset(&mut self);
}
```

Rules for `update`:
- Only `Proto::Tcp` records with `tcp_info: Some(..)` count. Records are matched to the previous update by `cookie`.
- `dt_s = (t_ns - prev_ns) as f64 / 1e9`. Per socket: `tx = (acked - prev_acked) / dt_s`, `rx = (received - prev_received) / dt_s`, in bytes per second, using the rate and reset helpers in `crate::counters` (E04-A1). A counter that went backwards is a reset: that socket adds nothing this interval and gets a new baseline. A cookie with no previous entry adds nothing this interval.
- The first `update` after `new` or `reset` sets `validity = WarmingUp`, fills baselines and leaves `per_process` empty.
- A socket's rate is added in full to every key in `map.owners_of(inode)`; when there are 2 or more owners each gets `shared = true`. Sockets with `inode == 0` or no owners go to `unattributed_*`. All sockets go to `total_*`.
- Every key that owns at least one TCP socket gets an entry (0.0 rates when idle) with `Validity::Valid`. Keys without TCP sockets get no entry; the engine shows 0 for them when their fd dir was readable. `restricted_pids` lets the engine show `Restricted` for those pids instead (never zero).
- Baselines for cookies not seen in this dump are removed, so `prev` never grows past the live socket count.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** two updates 2 s apart where cookie 7 owned by key A goes from acked 1000 to 3000 and received 0 to 4000 **When** the second update runs **Then** A has `tx_bps == 1000.0`, `rx_bps == 2000.0`, `shared == false`, `Valid`.
- **Given** cookie 7 owned by A and B **When** rates are computed **Then** both have the full rate and `shared == true`, and `total_tx_bps` counts it once.
- **Given** the first update after `new` **When** it runs **Then** `validity == WarmingUp` and `per_process` is empty.
- **Given** cookie 7 whose `bytes_acked` drops from 3000 to 100 **When** updated **Then** it adds 0 for this interval, and the next update computes from 100.
- **Given** a TIME-WAIT socket with inode 0 and traffic **When** updated **Then** its rate is in `unattributed_*` and `total_*` and in no process entry.
- **Given** `reset()` **When** the next update runs **Then** it is `WarmingUp` again.
- **Given** a UDP record **When** updated **Then** it is ignored.

title: E06-006 Connection records, owners and address formats
description:
## Context
Builds one connection record per socket for the Connections tab, with the address strings formatted once (ADR-003: "engine-formatted address strings, formatted once per cookie") and the owner resolved from the socket map. Rows keep identity by socket cookie. Sources: SYS-028, SYS-029, SYS-030, ADR-003 (`ConnectionsSnapshot`), canonical table (d) "Addresses".

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/net/connections.rs` (add `pub mod connections;` to `net/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum Owner {
    Kernel,                                                      // inode 0 or state TIME-WAIT (6): PID "-", Process "No owner (kernel)"
    Processes(smallvec::SmallVec<[tl_model::ProcessKey; 1]>),    // one or more owners
    Restricted { uid: u32 },                                     // no owner found and the socket uid's processes were unreadable: PID "?"
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ConnRecord {
    pub cookie: u64,                // row identity
    pub sock: SockRecord,
    pub local: std::sync::Arc<str>,   // formatted local address with port
    pub foreign: std::sync::Arc<str>, // formatted foreign address with port
    pub interface: Option<std::sync::Arc<str>>, // name for sock.ifindex, None when 0 or unknown
    pub owner: Owner,
}

pub struct ConnectionTable {
    pub records: Vec<ConnRecord>,   // sorted by cookie
    pub counts: ConnCounts,
}
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ConnCounts { pub total: u32, pub tcp: u32, pub udp: u32, pub established: u32, pub listening: u32 }

impl ConnectionTable {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    /// Rebuilds from one `dump_all`. Address strings of cookies seen last time with the same
    /// (src, sport, dst, dport, ifindex) are reused (Arc clone), not re-formatted.
    pub fn update(&mut self, socks: &[SockRecord], map: &SocketMap, ifnames: &IfNames);
}

/// ifindex -> interface name, read from /sys/class/net/<name>/ifindex.
pub struct IfNames(pub rustc_hash::FxHashMap<u32, std::sync::Arc<str>>);
impl IfNames { pub fn read(root: &SysRoot) -> Result<Self, CollectError>; }

pub fn format_endpoint(addr: std::net::IpAddr, port: u16, scope: Option<&str>, foreign_unbound: bool, out: &mut String);
```

Formatting rules (`format_endpoint`, table d, SYS-029):
- IPv4: `a.b.c.d:port`.
- IPv6: `[addr]:port`, with `addr` in the `std::net::Ipv6Addr` `Display` form (RFC 5952). An IPv4-mapped address (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) is written in IPv4 form `a.b.c.d:port`.
- Link-local IPv6 (`fe80::/10`) gets `%scope` inside the brackets, where `scope` is the interface name for `ifindex` (`[fe80::1%enp5s0]:22`); when the name is unknown the decimal ifindex is used.
- Port 0 is written `*`: wildcard listeners give `0.0.0.0:*` and `[::]:*`.
- `foreign_unbound = true` (a TCP LISTEN socket, or a UDP socket with state 7 and an all-zero destination) writes `*:*` for the foreign side.

Owner rules:
- `inode == 0` or (`Tcp` and `state == 6`): `Owner::Kernel`.
- `map.owners_of(inode)` not empty: `Owner::Processes`.
- Otherwise, if any pid in `map.restricted` has uid `sock.uid`: `Owner::Restricted { uid }`.
- Otherwise (the owner exited between the dump and the walk): `Owner::Processes` with an empty list, which the UI shows as `-` (Missing).

Counts: `established` and `listening` count TCP rows only (state 1 and 10).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a TCP v4 listener on 0.0.0.0 port 22 **When** formatted **Then** local is `0.0.0.0:22` and foreign is `*:*`.
- **Given** a UDP v6 socket bound to [::] port 0 **When** formatted **Then** local is `[::]:*` and foreign is `*:*`.
- **Given** the v6 address `::ffff:192.168.1.5` port 443 **When** formatted **Then** the result is `192.168.1.5:443`.
- **Given** `fe80::1` port 22 on ifindex 3 named `enp5s0` **When** formatted **Then** the result is `[fe80::1%enp5s0]:22`; with an unknown ifindex 9 it is `[fe80::1%9]:22`.
- **Given** a TIME-WAIT record with inode 4242 **When** the owner is resolved **Then** it is `Owner::Kernel`.
- **Given** a socket with uid 0 and no owners while pid 1 (uid 0) is in `restricted` **When** resolved **Then** it is `Owner::Restricted { uid: 0 }`.
- **Given** two updates where cookie 9 keeps the same endpoints **When** the second runs **Then** `local` is the same `Arc` (pointer-equal) as before.
- **Given** 3 TCP ESTABLISHED, 1 TCP LISTEN and 2 UDP records **When** counted **Then** counts are total 6, tcp 4, udp 2, established 3, listening 1.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/net/connections.rs`: create with unit tests
- `crates/tl-collect/src/net/mod.rs`: add `pub mod connections;`

## Tests
- `net::connections::tests::{tcp4_listener_format, udp6_wildcard_format, v4_mapped_as_v4, link_local_scope_name_and_number}`: criteria 1 to 4.
- `net::connections::tests::time_wait_owner_kernel`: criterion 5.
- `net::connections::tests::restricted_owner_by_uid`: criterion 6.
- `net::connections::tests::address_strings_reused`: criterion 7 (`Arc::ptr_eq`).
- `net::connections::tests::counts_tcp_only_states`: criterion 8.
- `net::connections::tests::ifnames_from_fixture`: `IfNames::read` on `tests/fixtures/sockets-basic/sys/class/net/{lo,enp5s0}/ifindex` (values 1 and 3).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `IfNames::read` returns the I/O error variant when `/sys/class/net` cannot be listed.
- Validity: `Owner::Restricted` shows the restricted glyph with tooltip "Owned by <user from diag uid>. Needs the tasklens helper to identify the process" (UI, SYS-030); empty `Processes` shows `-`.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one `String` scratch buffer reused for formatting; address `Arc<str>` reused per cookie.
- Privacy: never log addresses above `trace`.

## Notes
- State labels come from `tcp_state_label` and `udp_state_label` (E06-002).
- The scope as interface name follows `ss` and `ip`; see open item "IPv6 scope text" in docs/plan/b2-collect-ops.md if the leader changes it.

title: E07-A1 Verified process operations
description:
## Context
Anchor E07-A1: the verified process operations are complete and proven on the real system. This bead closes the set built by E07-001 to E07-007 (`error.rs`, `sys.rs`, `process.rs`) and adds `tests/ops_real.rs`, the real-system integration tests ADR-006 and ADR-013 require. Other epics (E11 actions, E29 helper, E32 low-memory window) depend on this anchor for `open_verified`, signals, nice, sched, affinity, I/O priority, thread targets and the kill tree. Sources: ADR-006 (verification list), ADR-013 (real-system tests: pidfd identity checks, nice and affinity on a child), PROC-001, PROC-060 to PROC-063, PROC-065 to PROC-068, R-037, R-038, R-093, R-097.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ops/src/lib.rs`: confirm the public surface is exactly: `OpsError`, `OpsResult`, and in `process`: `open_verified`, `read_start_ticks`, `signal_number`, `send_signal`, `suspend`, `resume`, `set_nice`, `set_sched`, `set_affinity`, `set_io_priority`, `thread_send_signal`, `thread_set_nice`, `thread_set_sched`, `thread_set_affinity`, `kill_tree`. Add rustdoc on each (one or two lines; the PID-based ones state the before-and-after pidfd rule and that a readable pidfd gives `OutcomeUnknown`).
- `crates/tl-ops/tests/ops_real.rs` with every test `#[ignore]` (owner machine, run with `cargo test -p tl-ops -- --ignored`), each spawning its own children and killing and reaping them in a `Drop` guard:
  - `real_open_verified_true_key_signals`: spawn `sleep 60`, build its key from `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 and the folded boot id (`tl_model::time` helper from E03, or fold `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` as ADR-003 says: first 8 bytes XOR last 8 bytes of the UUID), `send_signal(Term)` succeeds, the child's wait status is signal 15.
  - `real_shifted_start_ticks_is_identity_changed`: same child, key with `start_ticks + 1`: `send_signal(Kill)` returns `IdentityChanged` and the child still runs.
  - `real_set_nice_5_every_tid`: `set_nice(5)` returns `Ok`; every `/proc/<pid>/task/*/stat` field 19 is 5.
  - `real_exited_child_never_succeeds`: spawn `true`, wait for it to exit and reap it, then `set_nice(5)` with its key returns `IdentityChanged` or `OutcomeUnknown`, never `Ok`.
  - `real_set_affinity_cpu0`: `set_affinity({0})` returns `Ok`; `/proc/<pid>/status` `Cpus_allowed_list:` reads `0`.
  - `real_io_priority_idle`: `set_io_priority(Idle)` returns `Ok`; `ionice -p <pid>` (util-linux) prints `idle` (integration tests cannot use `unsafe`, so they never call `libc::syscall` directly).

No signal is ever sent to a root process in this test.

title: E07-007 kill_tree: SIGSTOP all, then SIGKILL all
description:
## Context
"End Process Tree" ends a process and every descendant the UI captured when the menu opened (max 256 keys). To stop any process in the tree from forking a new child between passes, the operation opens a verified pidfd for every target, sends SIGSTOP to all of them, then SIGKILL to all of them, then closes the fds. Sources: ADR-006 (tree operations), R-037, PROC-062, ADR-005 (`ActionKind::KillTree`).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ops/src/process.rs`:
```rust
pub fn kill_tree(keys: &[ProcessKey], boot: BootId) -> Vec<OpsResult>;
pub(crate) fn kill_tree_with(
    keys: &[ProcessKey], boot: BootId,
    send: &mut dyn FnMut(BorrowedFd<'_>, i32) -> Result<(), Errno>,
) -> Vec<OpsResult>;
```
- `kill_tree` calls `kill_tree_with` with `sys::pidfd_send_signal_raw` as `send`.
- `kill_tree_with`:
  1. `keys.len() > 256` returns a `Vec` of `InvalidInput("too many targets")` for every key (the engine already rejects this as `TooManyTargets`; this is a second guard).
  2. Pass 0: `open_verified(key, boot)` for every key, in input order. A key that fails keeps its error (`IdentityChanged` and so on) as its final result and is skipped in later passes.
  3. Pass 1: `send(fd, 19)` (SIGSTOP) for every opened target, in input order. Record the first error per target.
  4. Pass 2: `send(fd, 9)` (SIGKILL) for every opened target, in input order, including targets whose SIGSTOP failed. Record the first error per target.
  5. Drop every pidfd.
  6. Result per target, in input order: the open error if pass 0 failed; else the first signal error mapped through E07-001 (`ESRCH` gives `NoSuchProcess`, `EPERM` gives `PermissionDenied`); else `Ok(())`.
- The returned `Vec` has exactly `keys.len()` entries.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** three live children A, B, C and a recording `send` that calls the real raw send and logs `(pid, sig)` **When** `kill_tree_with([A, B, C])` runs **Then** the log is `(A,19) (B,19) (C,19) (A,9) (B,9) (C,9)`: every SIGSTOP comes before any SIGKILL.
- **Given** a parent `sh -c 'sleep 60 & sleep 60 & wait'` and its two children captured as keys **When** `kill_tree` runs **Then** every result is `Ok` and every one of the three processes is gone (wait status signal 9 for the parent; children no longer in `/proc`).
- **Given** keys [A, X, B] where X has a shifted `start_ticks` **When** `kill_tree` runs **Then** results are `[Ok, Err(IdentityChanged), Ok]` and X's real process still runs.
- **Given** 257 keys **When** `kill_tree_with` runs **Then** every result is `InvalidInput("too many targets")` and `send` is never called.
- **Given** an empty slice **When** `kill_tree` runs **Then** it returns an empty `Vec`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ops/src/process.rs`: add `kill_tree` and `kill_tree_with`, tests

## Tests
- `process.rs::tests::kill_tree_stops_all_before_killing_any` (regression test for R-037 ordering)
- `process.rs::tests::kill_tree_ends_parent_and_children`: finds the two `sleep` children of the `sh` parent by scanning `/proc/*/stat` for ppid; reaps the parent; waits up to 2 s for the children to vanish (they are reparented and reaped by init or the subreaper).
- `process.rs::tests::kill_tree_skips_changed_identity`
- `process.rs::tests::kill_tree_over_256_is_invalid`
- `process.rs::tests::kill_tree_empty`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: per target, `IdentityChanged`, `NoSuchProcess`, `PermissionDenied`, `Os`.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one `Vec` of pidfds (at most 256) and one result `Vec`.
- Privacy: log the target count and per-target pid and result at `debug` only.

## Notes
- `security` bead. Capturing the subtree is the UI's job (UI-PRC, E22) and the confirmation "End N processes in this tree?" is E22's; this function only acts on the keys it gets.
- If a target's SIGSTOP fails with EPERM (another user's process), its SIGKILL is still attempted; it fails the same way and the result is `PermissionDenied`.
- When the test runs under a session with a child subreaper, reparented children go there; the test waits for them to leave `/proc` rather than calling `waitpid` on them.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`, for example `... cargo test -p tl-ops`.
- Read CLAUDE.md first. Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead. `tl-ops` has no async code and no runtime (ADR-001 rule 3). `unsafe` is denied workspace-wide; the only `unsafe` file in this crate is `src/sys.rs` (ADR-001 rule 4).

title: E07-008 cgroup open_validated and validation tests
description:
## Context
Freeze App, Thaw App and Kill App act on an app's cgroup under the user's `app.slice`. Before any write, `open_validated` proves the captured `CgroupRef` still names the same cgroup, that it belongs to the current user, that it is an app scope or service, and that tasklens itself is not inside it. Sources: ADR-006 (cgroup operations, validation steps 1 to 3, `CgroupRef { rel_path: Arc<str>, cgroup_id: u64 }`), PROC-064, R-092 (units outside `app.slice` go through systemd, not here), ADR-013 (unit test list for `open_validated`).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ops/src/cgroup.rs`:
```rust
pub const CGROUP_ROOT: &str = "/sys/fs/cgroup";
pub struct CgroupDir { fd: OwnedFd }          // O_DIRECTORY fd of the validated cgroup
impl CgroupDir { pub fn as_fd(&self) -> BorrowedFd<'_>; }
pub fn open_validated(cg: &CgroupRef, uid: u32) -> OpsResult<CgroupDir>;
pub fn open_validated_at(root: &Path, cg: &CgroupRef, uid: u32, own_cgroup: &str) -> OpsResult<CgroupDir>;
pub fn own_cgroup() -> OpsResult<String>;     // from /proc/self/cgroup
pub(crate) fn check_rel_path(rel: &str, uid: u32) -> OpsResult;
```
- `check_rel_path` (pure, no I/O), each failure returns `NotOwner`:
  - not empty, no leading or trailing `/`, no NUL byte, no `//`, and no component equal to `.` or `..`;
  - starts with the exact prefix `user.slice/user-{uid}.slice/user@{uid}.service/app.slice/`, with `uid` formatted in decimal;
  - has at least one component after the prefix;
  - the last component ends in `.scope` or `.service`.
- `open_validated_at`, in this order:
  1. `check_rel_path(&cg.rel_path, uid)?`.
  2. Open `root` with `O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC | O_RDONLY`.
  3. `openat(root_fd, rel_path, O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC | O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW)`. `ENOENT` gives `IdentityChanged` (the cgroup is gone).
  4. `fstat`: `st_ino != cg.cgroup_id` gives `IdentityChanged`; `st_uid != uid` gives `NotOwner`.
  5. `own_cgroup` equal to `rel_path`, or starting with `rel_path` followed by `/`, gives `Protected`.
  6. Return `CgroupDir`.
- `own_cgroup`: reads `/proc/self/cgroup`, takes the line starting with `0::`, strips `0::/`, returns the rest (empty string for the root cgroup). No such line gives `Unsupported("cgroup v2 not mounted")`.
- `open_validated(cg, uid)` = `open_validated_at(Path::new(CGROUP_ROOT), cg, uid, &own_cgroup()?)`.
- `uid` always comes from the caller, who reads `rustix::process::getuid()` at runtime; `1000` is never written in this file (tests use the real uid).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** uid U and rel path `user.slice/user-U.slice/user@U.service/app.slice/app-org.kde.konsole@1a2b.service` **When** `check_rel_path` runs **Then** it returns `Ok`.
- **Given** `user.slice/user-U.slice/session-2.scope` **When** `check_rel_path` runs **Then** it returns `NotOwner`.
- **Given** `user.slice/user-U.slice/user@U.service/app.slice/../../../system.slice/sshd.service` **When** `check_rel_path` runs **Then** it returns `NotOwner`.
- **Given** the valid prefix for uid U+1 while `uid` is U **When** `check_rel_path` runs **Then** it returns `NotOwner`.
- **Given** a valid prefix ending in `app.slice/foo.slice` **When** `check_rel_path` runs **Then** it returns `NotOwner` (suffix rule).
- **Given** `/user.slice/...` (leading slash), a path with `//`, or a path with a NUL byte **When** `check_rel_path` runs **Then** each returns `NotOwner`.
- **Given** a fake root made in a temp dir with the directory chain for the current uid and a leaf `app-test@1.scope`, and a `CgroupRef` with the leaf's real inode **When** `open_validated_at` runs with an unrelated `own_cgroup` **Then** it returns `Ok`.
- **Given** the same fake root and `cgroup_id` = real inode + 1 **When** `open_validated_at` runs **Then** it returns `IdentityChanged` (regression test: a recreated cgroup with the same name is refused).
- **Given** the same fake root, the valid path built for uid U+1, and directories owned by U **When** `open_validated_at(.., uid = U+1, ..)` runs **Then** it returns `NotOwner` (owner check).
- **Given** the leaf removed after capture **When** `open_validated_at` runs **Then** it returns `IdentityChanged`.
- **Given** `own_cgroup` equal to the leaf path plus `/sub` **When** `open_validated_at` runs **Then** it returns `Protected`.
- **Given** the leaf replaced by a symlink to another directory **When** `open_validated_at` runs **Then** it returns an error (`O_NOFOLLOW`), not `Ok`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ops/src/cgroup.rs`: fill (validation)
- `crates/tl-ops/tests/cgroup_validate.rs`: create, the fake-root tests through the public `open_validated_at`

title: E07-009 cgroup freeze, thaw, kill and the frozen wait
description:
## Context
The three cgroup writes behind Freeze App, Thaw App and Kill App, on a `CgroupDir` that `open_validated` returned. Freeze has a completion wait: the kernel sets `frozen 1` in `cgroup.events` once every task has stopped. Sources: ADR-006 (validation step 4 and 5: `"1"` to `cgroup.freeze` freezes, `"0"` thaws, `"1"` to `cgroup.kill` kills; poll `cgroup.events` for `frozen 1` every 50 ms for up to 2 s, else `OutcomeUnknown("freeze still in progress")`), PROC-064.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ops/src/cgroup.rs`:
```rust
pub const FREEZE_POLL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(50);
pub const FREEZE_WAIT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
pub fn freeze(dir: &CgroupDir) -> OpsResult;                 // writes "1" to cgroup.freeze
pub fn thaw(dir: &CgroupDir) -> OpsResult;                   // writes "0" to cgroup.freeze
pub fn kill(dir: &CgroupDir) -> OpsResult;                   // writes "1" to cgroup.kill
pub fn is_frozen(dir: &CgroupDir) -> OpsResult<bool>;        // reads cgroup.events
pub fn wait_frozen(dir: &CgroupDir, wait: Duration, poll: Duration) -> OpsResult;
pub(crate) fn parse_frozen(events: &[u8]) -> Option<bool>;
pub fn freeze_group(cg: &CgroupRef, uid: u32) -> OpsResult;  // open_validated + freeze + wait_frozen(FREEZE_WAIT, FREEZE_POLL)
pub fn thaw_group(cg: &CgroupRef, uid: u32) -> OpsResult;    // open_validated + thaw
pub fn kill_group(cg: &CgroupRef, uid: u32) -> OpsResult;    // open_validated + kill
```
- Writes: `openat(dir_fd, "cgroup.freeze" | "cgroup.kill", O_WRONLY | O_CLOEXEC)`, one `write` of the 1-byte value, close. A short write gives `Os(libc::EIO)`. `EACCES` or `EPERM` gives `PermissionDenied`. `ENOENT` on `cgroup.kill` gives `Unsupported("cgroup.kill not available")`; on `cgroup.freeze`, `Unsupported("cgroup.freeze not available")`.
- `parse_frozen`: finds the line starting with `frozen ` and returns `Some(true)` for value `1`, `Some(false)` for `0`, `None` if the line is missing or malformed.
- `is_frozen`: `openat(dir_fd, "cgroup.events", O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC)`, read at most 256 bytes, `parse_frozen`; `None` gives `Os(libc::EIO)`.
- `wait_frozen`: checks `is_frozen` immediately, then every `poll` until `wait` has passed (measured with `std::time::Instant`); frozen gives `Ok`; not frozen by the end gives `OutcomeUnknown("freeze still in progress")`. Thread sleep is allowed here: it runs on the engine's blocking pool.
- Thaw and kill do not wait.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** events text `populated 1\nfrozen 1\n` **When** `parse_frozen` runs **Then** it returns `Some(true)`; for `populated 1\nfrozen 0\n` it returns `Some(false)`; for `populated 1\n` it returns `None`.
- **Given** a fake cgroup dir (temp dir with regular files `cgroup.freeze`, `cgroup.kill`, `cgroup.events`) **When** `freeze` runs **Then** `cgroup.freeze` contains `1`; **When** `thaw` runs **Then** it contains `0`; **When** `kill` runs **Then** `cgroup.kill` contains `1`.
- **Given** a fake dir whose `cgroup.events` says `frozen 0` and a test thread that rewrites it to `frozen 1` after 120 ms **When** `wait_frozen(dir, 2 s, 50 ms)` runs **Then** it returns `Ok` in under 300 ms.
- **Given** a fake dir whose `cgroup.events` stays `frozen 0` **When** `wait_frozen(dir, 200 ms, 50 ms)` runs **Then** it returns `OutcomeUnknown("freeze still in progress")` after at least 200 ms.
- **Given** a fake dir with no `cgroup.kill` **When** `kill` runs **Then** it returns `Unsupported("cgroup.kill not available")`.
- **Given** a `CgroupRef` that fails validation **When** `freeze_group` runs **Then** it returns the validation error and writes nothing.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ops/src/cgroup.rs`: add the writes, the wait and the `*_group` entry points
- `crates/tl-ops/tests/cgroup_validate.rs`: add the fake-dir write and wait tests

- `tests/cgroup_validate.rs::wait_frozen_times_out_outcome_unknown`
- `tests/cgroup_validate.rs::kill_without_cgroup_kill_is_unsupported`
- `tests/cgroup_validate.rs::freeze_group_invalid_ref_writes_nothing`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `PermissionDenied`, `Unsupported(..)`, `OutcomeUnknown("freeze still in progress")`, `Os`, plus validation errors.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: at most 41 reads of a 256-byte file per freeze wait; no allocation per poll.
- Privacy: log the cgroup's last component and result at `debug` only.

## Notes
- `security` bead. The 2 s write deadline and the separate 2 s completion wait (ADR-006 deadline table) are both covered: the engine wraps `freeze_group` in its timeout; `wait_frozen` ends by itself after 2 s.

title: E07-010 fs::write_atomic
description:
## Context
One atomic file-write routine for every file tasklens writes in place: `settings.toml`, `state.toml`, `themes.json` (through the `tl-app/src/atomic.rs` re-export) and the XDG autostart overrides (from the engine's Startup worker). A crash or power loss leaves either the old file or the new file, never a partial one. It lives in `tl-ops` because both `tl-app` and `tl-engine` may depend on `tl-ops` (R-130). Priority 1: the P1 settings store (E33-A2) uses it. Sources: ADR-011 (save: write `<name>.tmp-<pid>` in the same directory, `fsync` the file, `rename` over the target, `fsync` the directory; files `0600`), R-130, ADR-016 (autostart writes are atomic).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ops/src/fs.rs`:
```rust
pub const PRIVATE_FILE_MODE: u32 = 0o600;
pub fn write_atomic(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8], mode: u32) -> OpsResult;
pub(crate) fn temp_path(path: &Path) -> OpsResult<PathBuf>;
```
- `temp_path`: `path` must have a parent and a UTF-8-independent file name (use `OsStr`); returns `<parent>/<file name>.tmp-<pid>` where `<pid>` is `std::process::id()`. No file name gives `InvalidInput("path has no file name")`.
- `write_atomic`, in this order:
  1. `let tmp = temp_path(path)?`.
  2. Create `tmp` with `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_CLOEXEC` and `mode`. `EEXIST` (left over by an earlier crashed run with the same pid): unlink `tmp` and retry once; a second `EEXIST` gives `Os(libc::EEXIST)`.
  3. Write all of `bytes` (loop on short writes; `EINTR` retries).
  4. `fsync` the file. Close it.
  5. `rename(tmp, path)`.
  6. Open the parent directory with `O_DIRECTORY | O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC` and `fsync` it.
  7. On any error in steps 3 to 5, unlink `tmp` (ignore that unlink's own error) and return the first error.
- The parent directory must exist; a missing parent gives the mapped `ENOENT` error (`Os(libc::ENOENT)`). Callers create directories (mode `0700`, ADR-011).
- The mode is applied at create time; `fchmod` the temp file to `mode` after creating it so the process umask cannot widen or narrow it.
- `path` that is an existing directory gives the `rename` error (`Os(libc::EISDIR)`), and `tmp` is removed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a temp dir and no target file **When** `write_atomic(dir/"settings.toml", b"a = 1\n", 0o600)` runs **Then** the file contains `a = 1\n`, its mode is `0600`, and no `settings.toml.tmp-*` file remains.
- **Given** an existing target with content `old` **When** `write_atomic` writes `new` **Then** the file contains `new` and its inode differs from the old inode (it was replaced by rename, not rewritten).
- **Given** a stale `settings.toml.tmp-<own pid>` in the dir **When** `write_atomic` runs **Then** it succeeds and the stale file is gone.
- **Given** a parent directory that does not exist **When** `write_atomic` runs **Then** it returns `Os(libc::ENOENT)` and creates nothing.
- **Given** a target path that is a directory **When** `write_atomic` runs **Then** it returns an error and no temp file remains.
- **Given** mode `0o640` **When** `write_atomic` runs **Then** the file mode is exactly `0o640`, whatever the process umask.
- **Given** a 4 MiB payload **When** `write_atomic` runs **Then** the file equals the payload byte for byte.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ops/src/fs.rs`: fill (`write_atomic`), with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`

## Tests

- `fs.rs::tests::write_atomic_replaces_by_rename`
- `fs.rs::tests::write_atomic_removes_stale_temp`
- `fs.rs::tests::write_atomic_missing_parent_is_enoent`
- `fs.rs::tests::write_atomic_onto_directory_cleans_temp`
- `fs.rs::tests::write_atomic_mode_ignores_umask`: umask is process-wide, so instead of changing it the test calls `write_atomic` with mode `0o640` and asserts the mode is exactly `0o640` (the `fchmod` step makes the result independent of the umask, whatever it is).
- `fs.rs::tests::write_atomic_large_payload`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `InvalidInput("path has no file name")`, `PermissionDenied`, `Os(errno)`.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no copy of `bytes`; one temp file per call.
- Privacy: never log `bytes`. Log the file name (not the full path) and the result at `debug`.

## Notes
- `security` bead: the 0600 default protects settings and state from other local users (ADR-011).
- Do not add a `tempfile` dependency; test dirs go under `std::env::temp_dir()` with a unique name and are removed at the end.

title: E07-011 Autostart override write and remove, script toggle, confined delete
description:
## Context
Startup Apps enables and disables entries without ever editing a system file. A system XDG entry is disabled by writing a user override with `Hidden=true`; a user entry is toggled in place; a Plasma script is toggled by its executable bit; Delete removes a user file. The engine's Startup actions (E11) call these functions on the blocking pool under the 2 s startup-entry deadline. Sources: SYS-022, SYS-024, ADR-016 (startup row: user `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autostart` overrides by file name, atomic write), ADR-011 (`write_atomic`), ADR-006 (startup entry write deadline 2 s, engine side), R-130.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ops/src/fs.rs`:
```rust
pub struct StartupRoots {
    pub autostart: PathBuf,        // $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autostart
    pub systemd_user: PathBuf,     // $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user
    pub plasma_env: PathBuf,       // $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/plasma-workspace/env
    pub plasma_shutdown: PathBuf,  // $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/plasma-workspace/shutdown
}
impl StartupRoots { pub fn from_config_home(config_home: &Path) -> Self; }
pub enum EnableOutcome { OverrideDeleted, Rewritten }
pub const MAX_DESKTOP_FILE: u64 = 1024 * 1024;
pub fn autostart_disable_system(system_file: &Path, roots: &StartupRoots) -> OpsResult<PathBuf>;
pub fn autostart_enable_override(user_file: &Path, roots: &StartupRoots) -> OpsResult<EnableOutcome>;
pub fn autostart_set_hidden(user_file: &Path, hidden: bool, roots: &StartupRoots) -> OpsResult;
pub fn script_set_enabled(script: &Path, enabled: bool, roots: &StartupRoots) -> OpsResult;
pub fn delete_startup_file(path: &Path, roots: &StartupRoots) -> OpsResult;
pub(crate) fn desktop_set_key(text: &str, key: &str, value: &str) -> OpsResult<String>;
pub(crate) fn desktop_remove_key(text: &str, key: &str) -> OpsResult<String>;
pub(crate) fn desktop_get_key<'a>(text: &'a str, key: &str) -> Option<&'a str>;
```
- Key editing works only inside the `[Desktop Entry]` group (from the line `[Desktop Entry]` to the next line starting with `[` or the end). A key line is `Key=value` with optional spaces or tabs around `=`; the key part must equal `key` exactly, so `Hidden[de]=` does not match `Hidden`. Comments (`#` lines), blank lines, other groups, unknown keys and line order are kept byte for byte.
  - `desktop_set_key`: replaces the value of the first matching line, removes later duplicates of that key in the group, and if there is no match inserts `key=value` after the last non-blank line of the group. No `[Desktop Entry]` group gives `InvalidInput("no [Desktop Entry] group")`. The result ends in `\n`.
  - `desktop_remove_key`: removes every matching line in the group.
  - `desktop_get_key`: the trimmed value of the first matching line.
- Path confinement (every function, before any I/O): the target's parent must equal the named root exactly (compare `Path` components, no canonicalisation) and the file name must not be `.` or `..`. Autostart functions use `roots.autostart` and require the `.desktop` suffix; `script_set_enabled` accepts `roots.plasma_env` or `roots.plasma_shutdown`; `delete_startup_file` accepts `roots.autostart`, `roots.systemd_user`, `roots.plasma_env` or `roots.plasma_shutdown`. Anything else gives `NotOwner`.
- `autostart_disable_system`: reads `system_file` (at most `MAX_DESKTOP_FILE` bytes, else `InvalidInput("desktop file too large")`; invalid UTF-8 gives `InvalidInput("desktop file is not UTF-8")`); target = `roots.autostart/<system file name>`; if the target already exists, returns `InvalidInput("user entry already exists")` (the caller toggles that user entry with `autostart_set_hidden` instead); creates `roots.autostart` with mode `0700` if missing; text = system text with `Hidden=true` and `X-Tasklens-Override=true` set; `write_atomic(target, text, PRIVATE_FILE_MODE)`; returns the target path.
- `autostart_enable_override`: reads the user file; if `desktop_get_key(.., "X-Tasklens-Override") == Some("true")` it unlinks the file and returns `OverrideDeleted`; otherwise it sets `Hidden=false`, removes `X-GNOME-Autostart-enabled` when its value is `false`, writes with `write_atomic` keeping the file's current mode, and returns `Rewritten`.
- `autostart_set_hidden`: sets `Hidden=true` or `Hidden=false` in place with `write_atomic`, keeping the file's current mode.
- `script_set_enabled`: `enabled` adds `0o100` to the mode; disabled clears `0o111`; uses `fchmodat` on the file; a symlink target gives `NotOwner` (checked with `lstat`).
- `delete_startup_file`: `unlink` (a symlink is unlinked, never followed). `ENOENT` gives `Os(libc::ENOENT)`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a system file `[Desktop Entry]\nName=Foo\n# keep me\nExec=foo\n[Desktop Action new]\nExec=foo --new\n` **When** `autostart_disable_system` runs **Then** the user file equals the system text with `Hidden=true` and `X-Tasklens-Override=true` added after `Exec=foo` inside `[Desktop Entry]`, the comment and the action group unchanged, mode `0600`.
- **Given** a user file with `X-Tasklens-Override=true` **When** `autostart_enable_override` runs **Then** the file is deleted and the result is `OverrideDeleted`.
- **Given** a user file without the marker containing `Hidden=true` and `X-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=false` **When** `autostart_enable_override` runs **Then** the file has `Hidden=false`, no `X-GNOME-Autostart-enabled` line, and the result is `Rewritten`.
- **Given** a user file with `Hidden = false` and `Hidden[de]=x` **When** `autostart_set_hidden(true)` runs **Then** the line becomes `Hidden=true` and `Hidden[de]=x` is unchanged.
- **Given** a target that already exists **When** `autostart_disable_system` runs **Then** it returns `InvalidInput("user entry already exists")` and the file is unchanged.
- **Given** a path `roots.autostart/../evil.desktop` or a file in another directory **When** any function runs **Then** it returns `NotOwner` and touches nothing (regression test for path confinement).
- **Given** a script in `plasma_env` with mode `0o644` **When** `script_set_enabled(true)` runs **Then** the mode is `0o744`; **When** `script_set_enabled(false)` runs **Then** it is `0o644`.
- **Given** a file without `[Desktop Entry]` **When** `desktop_set_key` runs **Then** it returns `InvalidInput("no [Desktop Entry] group")`.
- **Given** a 2 MiB system file **When** `autostart_disable_system` runs **Then** it returns `InvalidInput("desktop file too large")`.
- **Given** a symlink in `roots.autostart` pointing to a file outside **When** `delete_startup_file` runs **Then** the symlink is gone and the outside file still exists.

## Files

- Test inputs are string literals in the test module; no fixture directory

## Tests
- `fs.rs::tests::disable_system_writes_override_keeping_comments_and_groups`

- `fs.rs::tests::enable_rewrites_foreign_override`

- `fs.rs::tests::disable_system_refuses_existing_user_entry`
- `fs.rs::tests::paths_outside_roots_are_not_owner`
- `fs.rs::tests::script_exec_bit_toggle`
- `fs.rs::tests::set_key_without_group_is_invalid`
- `fs.rs::tests::too_large_desktop_file_is_invalid`
- `fs.rs::tests::delete_unlinks_symlink_not_target`
- `fs.rs::tests::set_key_removes_duplicates_and_inserts_at_group_end`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `NotOwner`, `InvalidInput(..)` as listed, `PermissionDenied`, `Os`. Toast text ("Startup entry enabled.", "Startup entry disabled.", "Failed to update startup entry", "Startup entry deleted.", "Failed to delete startup entry") is the UI's.

## Notes

- The enable rule follows SYS-022 (marker `X-Tasklens-Override=true`). ADR-016's wording ("remove an override that differs only in `Hidden`") differs; see open item E07-O2 in docs/plan/b2-collect-ops.md. If the leader picks ADR-016's rule, `autostart_enable_override` changes and nothing else.

title: E07-012 dump.rs: core dump into a passed fd
description:
## Context
"Create dump file" writes a core file of a running process. The engine runs it directly when ptrace rules allow; the P3 helper runs the same code as root and writes to a file descriptor tasklens opened, so the file belongs to the user. The UI picks the output path and shows progress by reading the file size every 500 ms, so the core must be written directly into the final file. Sources: PROC-075, R-004 (`Dump { key, mode, out_fd }`, fixed binary path, writes to the passed fd), ADR-005 (`ActionKind::Dump { mode: DumpMode, path: Arc<str> }`, R-119), UI-PWN-034 (path `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/dumps/{name}_{pid}_{yyyymmdd_hhmmss}.core`, size polled every 500 ms), ADR-006 (helper `Dump`).

**Blocked: do not start until the leader resolves open item E07-O1** (how a fixed-path gdb tool writes into a passed fd). This description uses the recommended answer; if the leader picks another, only the "Run" step changes.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ops/src/dump.rs`:
```rust
pub const GDB_PATH: &str = "/usr/bin/gdb";
pub const GCORE_PATH: &str = "/usr/bin/gcore";
pub const FULL_COREDUMP_FILTER: &str = "0x1ff";
pub fn dump_available() -> bool;                     // GCORE_PATH and GDB_PATH both exist
pub fn dump_to_path(key: ProcessKey, boot: BootId, mode: DumpMode, out: &Path) -> OpsResult;
pub fn dump_to_fd(key: ProcessKey, boot: BootId, mode: DumpMode, out: OwnedFd) -> OpsResult;
pub(crate) fn ptrace_allowed(scope: u8, euid: u32) -> OpsResult;
```
- `ptrace_allowed`: reads nothing; `scope` comes from `/proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope` (missing file = 0). `euid == 0`: `Ok` for scope 0 to 2. `scope == 3`: `Unsupported("ptrace is disabled on this system")`. Non-root with scope 1 or 2: `PermissionDenied` (UI toast "Creating a dump needs administrator rights", PROC-075). Non-root with scope 0: `Ok`.
- `dump_to_path`: `out` must not exist; open it `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_CLOEXEC` with mode `0600` (`EEXIST` gives `Os(libc::EEXIST)`), then `dump_to_fd`; on error, unlink `out`.
- `dump_to_fd`, in this order:
  1. `dump_available()` false gives `Unsupported("gdb is not installed")`.
  2. `ptrace_allowed(scope, geteuid())?`.
  3. `let pidfd = open_verified(key, boot)?`.
  4. `DumpMode::Full`: read `/proc/<pid>/coredump_filter` (keep the text), write `0x1ff`. `DumpMode::Mini`: leave the filter as it is.
  5. Run (recommended answer to E07-O1): `std::process::Command::new(GDB_PATH)` with the arguments `--nx`, `--nh`, `--batch`, `-p`, `<pid>`, `-ex`, `gcore /proc/<tasklens pid>/fd/<n>`, where `<tasklens pid>` is `std::process::id()` and `<n>` is the raw fd number of `out`. gdb opens the file through that `/proc` link of the calling process, which works for root and for the same uid, so `out` does not need to be inherited (it keeps `O_CLOEXEC`). stdin, stdout and stderr are `/dev/null`; the environment is cleared except `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` and `LC_ALL=C`. Wait for exit.
  6. Restore the saved `coredump_filter` if step 4 changed it (also on every error path after step 4).
  7. Non-zero exit gives `Os(libc::EIO)`. Zero exit with `fstat(out).st_size == 0` gives `Os(libc::EIO)`.
- `out` is closed when the function returns.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** scope 1 and euid 1000 **When** `ptrace_allowed` runs **Then** it returns `PermissionDenied`; scope 0 and euid 1000 gives `Ok`; scope 2 and euid 0 gives `Ok`; scope 3 and euid 0 gives `Unsupported`.
- **Given** a path that already exists **When** `dump_to_path` runs **Then** it returns `Os(libc::EEXIST)` and the existing file is unchanged.
- **Given** `/usr/bin/gdb` missing (test injects a missing path through an internal `dump_to_fd_with(gdb: &Path, gcore: &Path, ..)` helper) **When** a dump runs **Then** it returns `Unsupported("gdb is not installed")`.
- **Given** a key with shifted `start_ticks` **When** a dump runs with scope 0 **Then** it returns `IdentityChanged` and no gdb process starts.
- **Given** the owner machine, `ptrace_scope` 1, a normal user **When** `dump_to_path` runs on a child `sleep 60` **Then** it returns `PermissionDenied` and removes the empty output file.
- **Given** `DumpMode::Full` and a gdb run that fails **When** the dump returns **Then** `coredump_filter` holds its old value.
- **Given** root (helper test, owner machine, `#[ignore]`) and a child `sleep 60` **When** `dump_to_path` runs with `Mini` **Then** it returns `Ok`, the file is non-empty, mode `0600`, and `file <path>` reports an ELF core.

title: E07-013 Desktop Entry Exec parser
description:
## Context
Startup "Run now" and launching a desktop entry need the entry's `Exec` key turned into an argument vector exactly as the Desktop Entry Specification says, with no shell in between. This bead writes that parser; E07-014 spawns the result. Sources: SYS-023 (field codes `%f %F %u %U` removed, `%i %c %k` expanded, quoting rules applied), PROC-095 and R-134 (`LaunchWhat::DesktopEntry`), Desktop Entry Specification 1.5 sections "Possible value types" and "The Exec key".

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ops/src/launch.rs`:
```rust
pub struct ExecContext<'a> {
    pub name: &'a str,                 // the entry's Name (already chosen by the caller)
    pub icon: Option<&'a str>,         // the entry's Icon value, raw
    pub desktop_file: Option<&'a str>, // absolute path of the .desktop file
}
pub fn parse_exec(raw: &str, ctx: &ExecContext<'_>) -> OpsResult<Vec<String>>;
pub(crate) fn unescape_string_value(raw: &str) -> String;
```
- Input `raw` is the value exactly as it follows `Exec=` in the file (the desktop-file parsers in tl-collect do not unescape it).
- Step 0: a NUL byte anywhere in `raw` gives `InvalidInput("Exec contains a NUL byte")`.
- Step 1, `unescape_string_value` (spec "string" type): `\s` to space, `\n` to newline, `\t` to tab, `\r` to carriage return, `\\` to `\`; any other `\x` pair is kept as both characters.
- Step 2, split into arguments: arguments are separated by one or more spaces (U+0020) outside quotes. A double-quoted argument starts and ends with `"`; inside it the pairs `\"`, `` \` ``, `\$` and `\\` give `"`, `` ` ``, `$` and `\`. A quote that is never closed gives `InvalidInput("unterminated quote in Exec")`. A `"` in the middle of an unquoted word gives `InvalidInput("quote inside an unquoted Exec argument")` (the spec requires such arguments to be fully quoted).
- Step 3, field codes, applied to unquoted arguments only (the spec forbids field codes inside quotes; a `%` inside a quoted argument is literal):
  - an argument that is exactly `%f`, `%F`, `%u` or `%U` is removed;
  - `%i` as a whole argument becomes the two arguments `--icon` and the icon value, or is removed when `ctx.icon` is `None` or empty;
  - `%c` becomes `ctx.name` (embedded or whole);
  - `%k` becomes `ctx.desktop_file`, or the empty string when `None`;
  - `%%` becomes `%`;
  - the deprecated codes `%d %D %n %N %v %m` are deleted;
  - any other `%` sequence gives `InvalidInput("invalid field code in Exec")`;
  - an unquoted argument that becomes empty is removed.
- Step 4: an empty result gives `InvalidInput("Exec is empty")`.
- The function never runs a shell and never interprets `$`, `;`, `|`, `&` or `` ` ``; they reach the program as literal characters.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `firefox %u` **When** `parse_exec` runs **Then** the result is `["firefox"]`.
- **Given** `"/opt/My App/run" --flag %F` **When** parsed **Then** the result is `["/opt/My App/run", "--flag"]`.
- **Given** the file bytes `app "a \\"b\\" \\$c"` **When** parsed **Then** the second argument is `a "b" $c` (step 1 turns each `\\` into `\`, step 2 then reads `\"` and `\$`).
- **Given** `foo\sbar baz` **When** parsed **Then** the result is `["foo bar", "baz"]`.
- **Given** `app %i --title=%c` with icon `app-icon` and name `My App` **When** parsed **Then** the result is `["app", "--icon", "app-icon", "--title=My App"]`.
- **Given** `app %i` with no icon **When** parsed **Then** the result is `["app"]`.
- **Given** `app %k` with desktop file `/usr/share/applications/app.desktop` **When** parsed **Then** the result is `["app", "/usr/share/applications/app.desktop"]`.
- **Given** `app 100%%` **When** parsed **Then** the result is `["app", "100%"]`.
- **Given** `app "50%"` **When** parsed **Then** the result is `["app", "50%"]` (literal inside quotes).
- **Given** `app %z` **When** parsed **Then** it returns `InvalidInput("invalid field code in Exec")`.
- **Given** `app "unterminated` **When** parsed **Then** it returns `InvalidInput("unterminated quote in Exec")`.
- **Given** `app ab"cd"` **When** parsed **Then** it returns `InvalidInput("quote inside an unquoted Exec argument")`.
- **Given** `%f %U` **When** parsed **Then** it returns `InvalidInput("Exec is empty")`.
- **Given** `sh -c "echo $HOME; ls | wc -l"` **When** parsed **Then** the result is `["sh", "-c", "echo $HOME; ls | wc -l"]` and nothing is expanded (regression test: no shell interpretation in the parser).
- **Given** arbitrary strings up to 4 KiB **When** parsed (proptest) **Then** the function never panics.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ops/src/launch.rs`: fill (`ExecContext`, `parse_exec`, `unescape_string_value`)
- `crates/tl-ops/tests/launch_exec_parse.rs`: create, the cases above through the public `parse_exec`, plus the proptest

## Tests

- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::quoted_path_with_spaces`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::quoted_escapes`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::string_value_escapes`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::icon_and_name_codes`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::icon_code_without_icon_removed`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::desktop_file_code`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::percent_escape`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::percent_literal_inside_quotes`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::invalid_field_code`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::unterminated_quote`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::quote_inside_unquoted_word`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::empty_after_codes`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::no_shell_interpretation`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::prop_never_panics` (proptest, strings up to 4 KiB, 512 cases)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the `InvalidInput` texts above. The UI toast is "Failed to launch startup entry" (SYS-023).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one `Vec<String>`; runs once per launch.
- Privacy: never log `raw` or the result (they are command lines, ADR-015).

title: E07-014 Detached spawn, shell and pkexec argv, child reaping
description:
## Context
The engine's shared launcher (E14, `tl-engine/src/launcher.rs`) starts programs for the Run dialog and for Startup "Run now". It needs a detached spawn (new session, stdio on `/dev/null`, chosen working directory), the argument vectors for a shell command, a script and the administrator form, and a way to reap the child. The D-Bus parts (`StartTransientUnit`, `StartUnit`, portal `OpenURI`) stay in the engine. Sources: SYS-023 (`posix_spawn` with `setsid`, stdio `/dev/null`, cwd from `Path=`; script through `/bin/sh <path>`), PROC-095 (`/bin/sh -c <text>`; "Run as administrator": `pkexec env DISPLAY=… WAYLAND_DISPLAY=… XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=… /bin/sh -c <text>` under `org.freedesktop.policykit.exec`, never `tl-helper`; "Command contains invalid text." for a NUL byte or a control character; "Authentication cancelled" for a cancelled prompt), ADR-006 (Run as administrator), R-134.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ops/src/launch.rs`:
```rust
pub const SH_PATH: &str = "/bin/sh";
pub const PKEXEC_PATH: &str = "/usr/bin/pkexec";
pub const PKEXEC_NOT_AUTHORIZED: i32 = 127;  // pkexec(1): not authorized, or authentication failed
pub const PKEXEC_DISMISSED: i32 = 126;       // pkexec(1): the user dismissed the authentication dialog
pub const ADMIN_ENV_KEYS: [&str; 3] = ["DISPLAY", "WAYLAND_DISPLAY", "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR"];

pub struct Spawned { pub pid: u32, pub pidfd: OwnedFd }
pub enum ExitKind { Exited(i32), Signaled(i32) }

pub fn validate_command_text(text: &str) -> OpsResult;
pub fn shell_argv(text: &str) -> OpsResult<Vec<String>>;
pub fn script_argv(script: &Path) -> OpsResult<Vec<String>>;
pub fn admin_argv(text: &str, env: &[(&str, Option<&str>)]) -> OpsResult<Vec<String>>;
pub fn spawn_detached(argv: &[String], cwd: Option<&Path>) -> OpsResult<Spawned>;
pub fn wait_exit(child: &Spawned) -> OpsResult<ExitKind>;
```
- `validate_command_text`: the text trimmed of ASCII whitespace must not be empty (`InvalidInput("command is empty")`, UI toast "Please enter a command"); it must not contain U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F or U+0080 to U+009F (`InvalidInput("command contains invalid text")`, UI toast "Command contains invalid text.").
- `shell_argv(text)`: validates, returns `["/bin/sh", "-c", text]` with `text` unchanged (not trimmed).
- `script_argv(path)`: path must be absolute and valid UTF-8 (else `InvalidInput("script path is not absolute UTF-8")`), returns `["/bin/sh", path]`.
- `admin_argv(text, env)`: validates `text`; `env` lists each key of `ADMIN_ENV_KEYS` with its current value from the caller (the engine reads its own environment); result is `["/usr/bin/pkexec", "env"]`, then `KEY=value` for each key in `ADMIN_ENV_KEYS` order whose value is `Some` and not empty, then `"/bin/sh", "-c", text`. A value containing a NUL or newline gives `InvalidInput("environment value contains invalid text")`.
- `spawn_detached(argv, cwd)`: `argv` empty gives `InvalidInput("empty argument list")`; any argument containing a NUL byte gives `InvalidInput("argument contains a NUL byte")`; `cwd` that is not an existing directory gives `InvalidInput("working directory does not exist")`. Converts to `CString`s, calls `sys::spawn_setsid(&argv, cwd)` (new session, stdin, stdout and stderr on `/dev/null`, signal mask cleared, default signal dispositions), then `rustix::process::pidfd_open(pid)` (safe: the child stays a zombie until reaped, so the pid cannot be reused before this call). Spawn errors map through E07-001 (`ENOENT` gives `Os(libc::ENOENT)`).
- `wait_exit(child)`: blocking `rustix::process::waitid(WaitId::PidFd(child.pidfd.as_fd()), WaitIdOptions::EXITED)`; returns `Exited(code)` or `Signaled(signo)`. The engine calls this on its blocking pool for every spawned child so no zombie is left (for `pkexec`, it compares the code with `PKEXEC_DISMISSED` to show "Authentication cancelled").

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `"   "` **When** `validate_command_text` runs **Then** it returns `InvalidInput("command is empty")`.
- **Given** `"ls\u{0}x"`, `"ls\nrm"`, `"ls\u{7f}"` or `"ls\u{85}"` **When** `validate_command_text` runs **Then** each returns `InvalidInput("command contains invalid text")` (regression test for PROC-095's invalid-text rule).
- **Given** `"echo hi > /tmp/x"` **When** `shell_argv` runs **Then** the result is `["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo hi > /tmp/x"]`.
- **Given** text `kate` and env `[("DISPLAY", Some(":0")), ("WAYLAND_DISPLAY", Some("wayland-0")), ("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR", Some("/run/user/1000"))]` **When** `admin_argv` runs **Then** the result is `["/usr/bin/pkexec", "env", "DISPLAY=:0", "WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0", "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000", "/bin/sh", "-c", "kate"]`.
- **Given** `DISPLAY` unset (`None`) and the other two set **When** `admin_argv` runs **Then** no `DISPLAY=` argument appears.
- **Given** a relative script path **When** `script_argv` runs **Then** it returns `InvalidInput`.
- **Given** argv `["sleep", "30"]` and cwd `/tmp` **When** `spawn_detached` runs **Then** the child's session id equals its pid (`/proc/<pid>/stat` field 6), its cwd is `/tmp`, its fds 0, 1 and 2 point to `/dev/null`, and `SigIgn:` in `/proc/<pid>/status` is `0000000000000000`.
- **Given** a spawned `sh -c 'exit 3'` **When** `wait_exit` runs **Then** it returns `Exited(3)`; for a child killed with SIGKILL it returns `Signaled(9)`.
- **Given** argv `["tasklens-no-such-binary-xyz"]` **When** `spawn_detached` runs **Then** it returns `Os(libc::ENOENT)`.
- **Given** cwd `/nonexistent` **When** `spawn_detached` runs **Then** it returns `InvalidInput("working directory does not exist")` and nothing is spawned.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ops/src/launch.rs`: add the argv builders, `spawn_detached`, `wait_exit`, tests
- `crates/tl-ops/tests/launch_exec_parse.rs`: add the argv builder cases (pure, no spawning)

## Tests
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::command_text_empty`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::command_text_control_chars_rejected`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::shell_argv_keeps_text`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::admin_argv_full_env`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::admin_argv_skips_unset_env`
- `tests/launch_exec_parse.rs::script_argv_requires_absolute`
- `launch.rs::tests::spawn_detached_new_session_devnull_cwd_default_signals`
- `launch.rs::tests::wait_exit_code_and_signal`
- `launch.rs::tests::spawn_missing_binary_is_enoent`
- `launch.rs::tests::spawn_missing_cwd_is_invalid`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the `InvalidInput` texts above, `Os(errno)`. Toast texts ("Command launched", "Failed to run command", "Authentication cancelled", "Please enter a command", "Command contains invalid text.") are the UI's (E23), mapped by the engine.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one `Vec<CString>` per spawn.
- Privacy: never log the command text, argv, environment values or cwd (ADR-015). Log the pid and the result at `debug` only.

## Notes
- `security` bead. The administrator form uses `pkexec` by absolute path and passes the user's text only as the single argument after `-c`; it never goes through `tl-helper` (ADR-006).
- Whether to keep a variable when it is unset is this bead's choice to omit it; see open item E07-O5 in docs/plan/b2-collect-ops.md.
- The `pkexec` exit codes 126 and 127 are from the pkexec(1) manual page.

- Read CLAUDE.md first. Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead. `tl-ops` has no async code and no runtime (ADR-001 rule 3). `unsafe` is denied workspace-wide; the only `unsafe` file in this crate is `src/sys.rs` (ADR-001 rule 4).
