title: E07-001 tl-ops crate root and OpsError
description:
## Context
Creates the `tl-ops` crate body: dependency features, the module list and the error type every operation returns. `tl-ops` holds every synchronous OS operation (signals, nice, scheduling, affinity, I/O priority, cgroup writes, atomic files, launch, dump). It is shared by the unprivileged engine and the P3 root helper, so both run the same code. Sources: ADR-001 (crate row: deps `tl-model`, `rustix`, `libc`, `thiserror`, `tracing`), ADR-006, ADR-015 (`OpsError` via `thiserror`, `ActionError` variants), ADR-005 (`ActionState`, `RejectReason`), R-130.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ops/Cargo.toml`: `[dependencies]` `tl-model = { path = "../tl-model" }`, `rustix` (workspace pin; features `process`, `thread`, `fs`, `event`, `std`), `libc`, `thiserror`, `tracing` (all `workspace = true`). No other dependency. `[lints] workspace = true`.
- `crates/tl-ops/src/lib.rs`: module list, in this order: `pub mod error; mod sys; pub mod process; pub mod cgroup; pub mod fs; pub mod dump; pub mod launch;` and `pub use error::OpsError;`. Modules other than `error` start as empty files with a one-line `//!` doc comment; later beads fill them. `sys` is private.
- `crates/tl-ops/src/error.rs`:
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum OpsError {
    #[error("process identity changed")]            IdentityChanged,
    #[error("target is not owned by the current user")] NotOwner,
    #[error("target is protected")]                 Protected,
    #[error("not supported: {0}")]                  Unsupported(&'static str),
    #[error("permission denied")]                   PermissionDenied,
    #[error("no such process")]                     NoSuchProcess,
    #[error("partially applied: {done} of {total}")] Partial { done: u16, total: u16 },
    #[error("outcome unknown: {0}")]                OutcomeUnknown(&'static str),
    #[error("invalid input: {0}")]                  InvalidInput(&'static str),
    #[error("OS error {0}")]                        Os(i32),
}
impl From<rustix::io::Errno> for OpsError { .. }
impl From<std::io::Error> for OpsError { .. }
impl OpsError { pub fn to_action_state(&self) -> tl_model::actions::ActionState { .. } }
pub type OpsResult<T = ()> = Result<T, OpsError>;
```
- Errno mapping (both `From` impls): `EPERM` and `EACCES` give `PermissionDenied`; `ESRCH` gives `NoSuchProcess`; any other errno `e` gives `Os(e)`. A `std::io::Error` without a raw OS error gives `Os(libc::EIO)`.
- `to_action_state` mapping: `IdentityChanged` to `Rejected(RejectReason::IdentityChanged)`; `NotOwner` to `Rejected(NotOwner)`; `Protected` to `Rejected(Protected)`; `Unsupported(_)` to `Rejected(Unsupported)`; `PermissionDenied` to `Failed(ActionError::PermissionDenied)`; `NoSuchProcess` to `Failed(ActionError::NoSuchProcess)`; `Partial { done, total }` to `Failed(ActionError::Partial { done, total })`; `OutcomeUnknown(s)` to `OutcomeUnknown(Arc::from(s))`; `InvalidInput(s)` to `Failed(ActionError::Internal(Arc::from(s)))`; `Os(e)` to `Failed(ActionError::Os(e))`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `rustix::io::Errno::PERM` **When** converted to `OpsError` **Then** the result is `PermissionDenied`.
- **Given** `Errno::ACCESS` **When** converted **Then** the result is `PermissionDenied`.
- **Given** `Errno::SRCH` **When** converted **Then** the result is `NoSuchProcess`.
- **Given** `Errno::INVAL` **When** converted **Then** the result is `Os(libc::EINVAL)`.
- **Given** `std::io::Error::new(ErrorKind::Other, "x")` **When** converted **Then** the result is `Os(libc::EIO)`.
- **Given** each `OpsError` variant **When** `to_action_state()` runs **Then** the result is the state in the mapping above.
- **Given** the crate **When** `cargo xtask check-deps` runs **Then** it passes (tl-ops row unchanged).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ops/Cargo.toml`: change (dependencies and features)
- `crates/tl-ops/src/lib.rs`: change (module list)
- `crates/tl-ops/src/error.rs`: create, with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`
- `crates/tl-ops/src/{sys,process,cgroup,fs,dump,launch}.rs`: create as empty modules with a `//!` line

## Tests
- `error.rs::tests::errno_perm_and_acces_map_to_permission_denied`
- `error.rs::tests::errno_srch_maps_to_no_such_process`
- `error.rs::tests::other_errno_maps_to_os`
- `error.rs::tests::io_error_without_errno_maps_to_eio`
- `error.rs::tests::action_state_mapping_covers_every_variant`: one assertion per variant.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: defines them; user text is made in the UI from `ActionError` (ADR-015), never from `OpsError`'s `Display`.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: `OpsError` never carries a path, command line or process name.

## Notes
- Check the rustix version pinned in the workspace `Cargo.toml` (E02) for the exact feature names; `sched_setaffinity` is under `thread` in rustix 1.x and under `process` in 0.38. Enable whichever the pin needs.

title: E07-002 sys.rs unsafe wrappers: ioprio_set, sched_setattr, tgkill, posix_spawnp with setsid
description:
## Context
`src/sys.rs` is the only file in `tl-ops` allowed to contain `unsafe` (ADR-001 rule 4). It wraps the four calls that `rustix` does not offer: `ioprio_set`, `sched_setattr`, `tgkill` and `posix_spawnp` with `POSIX_SPAWN_SETSID`. Every other module calls these safe wrappers. Sources: ADR-001, ADR-006 (ioprio through `libc::syscall(SYS_ioprio_set, ..)` in `sys.rs`; `SCHED_RR` with `SCHED_RESET_ON_FORK`; `tgkill` for thread signals), R-038, R-093, R-097, SYS-023 (`posix_spawn` with `setsid`, stdio `/dev/null`, cwd).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ops/src/sys.rs`, starting with `#![allow(unsafe_code)]`, every `unsafe` block preceded by a `// SAFETY:` comment that names the invariant. All functions are `pub(crate)` and return `Result<_, rustix::io::Errno>` (errno read with `Errno::from_raw_os_error(std::io::Error::last_os_error().raw_os_error())`).

Constants (x86_64 Linux values, written out):
```rust
pub(crate) const IOPRIO_WHO_PROCESS: i32 = 1;
pub(crate) const IOPRIO_CLASS_SHIFT: u16 = 13;
pub(crate) const IOPRIO_CLASS_NONE: u16 = 0;
pub(crate) const IOPRIO_CLASS_RT: u16 = 1;
pub(crate) const IOPRIO_CLASS_BE: u16 = 2;
pub(crate) const IOPRIO_CLASS_IDLE: u16 = 3;
pub(crate) const fn ioprio_value(class: u16, level: u16) -> u16 { (class << IOPRIO_CLASS_SHIFT) | level }
pub(crate) const SCHED_OTHER: u32 = 0;
pub(crate) const SCHED_FIFO: u32 = 1;
pub(crate) const SCHED_RR: u32 = 2;
pub(crate) const SCHED_BATCH: u32 = 3;
pub(crate) const SCHED_IDLE: u32 = 5;
pub(crate) const SCHED_FLAG_RESET_ON_FORK: u64 = 0x01;
pub(crate) const SCHED_ATTR_SIZE_VER0: u32 = 48;
```

Struct (kernel `struct sched_attr`, version 0, 48 bytes):
```rust
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct SchedAttr {
    pub size: u32,           // always SCHED_ATTR_SIZE_VER0
    pub sched_policy: u32,
    pub sched_flags: u64,
    pub sched_nice: i32,
    pub sched_priority: u32,
    pub sched_runtime: u64,  // 0
    pub sched_deadline: u64, // 0
    pub sched_period: u64,   // 0
}
```

Functions:
- `pub(crate) fn ioprio_set_tid(tid: u32, value: u16) -> Result<(), Errno>`: `libc::syscall(libc::SYS_ioprio_set, IOPRIO_WHO_PROCESS, tid as libc::c_int, value as libc::c_int)`.
- `pub(crate) fn sched_setattr_tid(tid: u32, attr: &SchedAttr) -> Result<(), Errno>`: `libc::syscall(libc::SYS_sched_setattr, tid as libc::pid_t, attr as *const SchedAttr, 0u32)`. Debug-asserts `attr.size == SCHED_ATTR_SIZE_VER0`.
- `pub(crate) fn tgkill(pid: u32, tid: u32, sig: i32) -> Result<(), Errno>`: `libc::syscall(libc::SYS_tgkill, pid as libc::pid_t, tid as libc::pid_t, sig)`.
- `pub(crate) fn spawn_setsid(argv: &[CString], cwd: Option<&CStr>) -> Result<u32, Errno>`: `posix_spawnp` of `argv[0]` with argument vector `argv` and the current `environ`. Attributes: flags `POSIX_SPAWN_SETSID | POSIX_SPAWN_SETSIGMASK | POSIX_SPAWN_SETSIGDEF`, an empty signal mask, and `sigfillset` as the default set (so the child does not inherit tasklens's ignored `SIGPIPE` or blocked signals). File actions: `addopen(0, "/dev/null", O_RDONLY, 0)`, `addopen(1, "/dev/null", O_WRONLY, 0)`, `addopen(2, "/dev/null", O_WRONLY, 0)`, and `posix_spawn_file_actions_addchdir_np(cwd)` when `cwd` is `Some`. Destroys the attribute and file-action objects on every path (use a guard struct with `Drop`). `argv` empty returns `Err(Errno::INVAL)` without calling `posix_spawnp`. Returns the child pid. `posix_spawnp` returns the error number directly (not through `errno`); convert that value.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `SchedAttr` **When** `size_of::<SchedAttr>()` is checked **Then** it is 48.
- **Given** class `IOPRIO_CLASS_BE` and level 4 **When** `ioprio_value` runs **Then** it returns `0x4004`.
- **Given** class `IOPRIO_CLASS_IDLE` and level 0 **When** `ioprio_value` runs **Then** it returns `0x6000`.
- **Given** the current thread's own TID **When** `ioprio_set_tid(tid, ioprio_value(IOPRIO_CLASS_BE, 7))` runs **Then** it returns `Ok` and `ioprio_get` through `libc::syscall(SYS_ioprio_get, 1, tid)` reads `0x4007` (test restores the old value).
- **Given** a spawned `sleep 30` child **When** `tgkill(pid, pid, libc::SIGTERM)` runs **Then** it returns `Ok` and the child exits with signal 15.
- **Given** tid 0x7fff_fff0 that does not exist **When** `tgkill` runs **Then** it returns `Err(Errno::SRCH)`.
- **Given** argv `["sleep", "30"]` and cwd `/tmp` **When** `spawn_setsid` runs **Then** the child's `getsid(pid)` equals its pid, `/proc/<pid>/cwd` resolves to `/tmp`, and `/proc/<pid>/fd/0`, `1`, `2` resolve to `/dev/null`.
- **Given** an empty argv **When** `spawn_setsid` runs **Then** it returns `Err(Errno::INVAL)`.
- **Given** argv `["/nonexistent/tasklens-test-binary"]` **When** `spawn_setsid` runs **Then** it returns `Err` (`ENOENT`) and leaves no child.
- **Given** the workspace **When** `rg -n "unsafe" crates/tl-ops/src --glob '!sys.rs'` runs **Then** it prints nothing.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ops/src/sys.rs`: create (filled from the empty module of E07-001), with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`

## Tests
- `sys.rs::tests::sched_attr_is_48_bytes`
- `sys.rs::tests::ioprio_value_encoding`: the two values above plus `ioprio_value(IOPRIO_CLASS_RT, 0) == 0x2000` and `ioprio_value(IOPRIO_CLASS_NONE, 0) == 0`.
- `sys.rs::tests::ioprio_set_own_thread_roundtrip`
- `sys.rs::tests::tgkill_child_terminates`: spawns `sleep 30` with `std::process::Command`, then waits with `Child::wait`.
- `sys.rs::tests::tgkill_missing_tid_is_esrch`
- `sys.rs::tests::spawn_setsid_new_session_devnull_cwd`: reaps the child with `waitpid` after `kill`.
- `sys.rs::tests::spawn_setsid_empty_argv_is_einval`
- `sys.rs::tests::spawn_setsid_missing_binary_fails`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: raw `Errno`; callers convert to `OpsError` (E07-001 mapping).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no allocation except the `CString` pointer array in `spawn_setsid`.
- Privacy: never log `argv` or `cwd` (ADR-015: command lines and working directories are never logged). Log only the errno at `debug`.

## Notes
- `security` bead: this is the crate's `unsafe` boundary. Each `// SAFETY:` comment states why pointers are valid for the call (for example: `attr` points to a live, initialised `SchedAttr` of `size` bytes; `argv` pointers live until `posix_spawnp` returns and the array ends in a null pointer).
- `posix_spawn_file_actions_addchdir_np` needs glibc 2.29 or later; Arch is far newer. It is in the `libc` crate for `target_env = "gnu"`.

title: E07-003 open_verified and pidfd signals
description:
## Context
Every process operation starts by proving the target is still the captured process. `open_verified` opens a pidfd, which pins the process, then re-reads its start time and compares it with the captured `ProcessKey`. Signals then go through `pidfd_send_signal` on that pidfd, so they cannot hit a reused PID. This bead also adds the pidfd poll helper that the PID-based calls use. Sources: ADR-006 (identity revalidation code, signals, suspend and resume), PROC-001, PROC-060, PROC-061, PROC-063, PROC-065, R-035.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ops/src/process.rs`:
```rust
use tl_model::{ids::ProcessKey, time::BootId, actions::Signal};
pub fn open_verified(key: ProcessKey, boot: BootId) -> OpsResult<OwnedFd>;
pub fn read_start_ticks(pid: u32) -> OpsResult<u64>;
pub(crate) fn parse_start_ticks(stat: &[u8]) -> Option<u64>;
pub(crate) fn has_exited(pidfd: &OwnedFd) -> OpsResult<bool>;
pub fn signal_number(sig: Signal) -> OpsResult<i32>;
pub fn send_signal(key: ProcessKey, boot: BootId, sig: Signal) -> OpsResult;
pub fn suspend(key: ProcessKey, boot: BootId) -> OpsResult;  // SIGSTOP
pub fn resume(key: ProcessKey, boot: BootId) -> OpsResult;   // SIGCONT
```
- `open_verified` steps, in this order: (1) `key.boot_id != boot` returns `IdentityChanged`. (2) `key.pid == 0` returns `IdentityChanged`. (3) `rustix::process::pidfd_open(Pid::from_raw(key.pid as i32), PidfdFlags::empty())`; `ESRCH` returns `IdentityChanged`, other errors map through the E07-001 table. (4) `read_start_ticks(key.pid)` after the pidfd is open; `ENOENT` or `ESRCH` returns `IdentityChanged`. (5) value differs from `key.start_ticks` returns `IdentityChanged`. (6) return the pidfd.
- `read_start_ticks`: reads `/proc/<pid>/stat` (at most 4096 bytes, one `read` into a stack buffer) and calls `parse_start_ticks`; `None` returns `Os(libc::EIO)`.
- `parse_start_ticks`: finds the last `)` byte (`memrchr`-style reverse scan), skips the following space, splits the rest on single spaces; the token at index 19 (field 22, `starttime`) parsed as `u64`. Any missing or non-numeric token gives `None`.
- `has_exited`: `rustix::event::poll` on the pidfd with `POLLIN` and timeout 0; returns `true` when `POLLIN` is set.
- `signal_number` (x86_64 numbers): `Term` 15, `Kill` 9, `Hup` 1, `Int` 2, `Quit` 3, `Stop` 19, `Cont` 18, `Usr1` 10, `Usr2` 12, `Other(n)` gives `n` when `1 <= n <= 64`, else `InvalidInput("signal number out of range")`.
- `send_signal`: `open_verified`, then `sys::pidfd_send_signal_raw(pidfd.as_fd(), signal_number(sig)?)`. Add to `sys.rs`: `pub(crate) fn pidfd_send_signal_raw(pidfd: BorrowedFd<'_>, sig: i32) -> Result<(), Errno>` calling `libc::syscall(libc::SYS_pidfd_send_signal, pidfd.as_raw_fd(), sig, std::ptr::null::<libc::siginfo_t>(), 0u32)` with a `// SAFETY:` comment. The raw call is used for every signal so real-time numbers 34..=64 need no special case. Errors map through E07-001 (`ESRCH` after verification is `NoSuchProcess`).
- `suspend` is `send_signal(key, boot, Signal::Stop)`; `resume` is `send_signal(key, boot, Signal::Cont)`.
- The pidfd is closed when the `OwnedFd` drops, at the end of each call.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a `ProcessKey` whose `boot_id` differs from `boot` **When** `open_verified` runs **Then** it returns `IdentityChanged` without opening a pidfd.
- **Given** a live child `sleep 60` with its true key **When** `open_verified` runs **Then** it returns a pidfd.
- **Given** the same child with `start_ticks + 1` **When** `open_verified` runs **Then** it returns `IdentityChanged`.
- **Given** a key for a pid that no longer exists **When** `open_verified` runs **Then** it returns `IdentityChanged`.
- **Given** the stat line `1234 (a b) c) S 1 1234 1234 0 -1 4194304 10 0 0 0 5 6 0 0 20 0 1 0 98765 1000 100` **When** `parse_start_ticks` runs **Then** it returns `Some(98765)`.
- **Given** a stat line cut after field 20 **When** `parse_start_ticks` runs **Then** it returns `None`.
- **Given** a live child **When** `send_signal(key, boot, Signal::Term)` runs **Then** it returns `Ok` and the child's wait status is signal 15.
- **Given** a live child **When** `suspend` runs **Then** `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 3 reads `T`; **When** `resume` runs **Then** it no longer reads `T`.
- **Given** a live child **When** `send_signal` with `Signal::Other(34)` runs **Then** the child's wait status is signal 34.
- **Given** `Signal::Other(0)` or `Signal::Other(65)` **When** `signal_number` runs **Then** it returns `InvalidInput`.
- **Given** a pidfd for a child that has exited (not yet reaped) **When** `has_exited` runs **Then** it returns `true`; for a running child it returns `false`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ops/src/process.rs`: fill (verification, signals), with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`
- `crates/tl-ops/src/sys.rs`: add `pidfd_send_signal_raw`

## Tests
- `process.rs::tests::parse_start_ticks_name_with_spaces_and_parens`
- `process.rs::tests::parse_start_ticks_truncated_is_none`
- `process.rs::tests::parse_start_ticks_non_numeric_is_none`
- `process.rs::tests::boot_mismatch_is_identity_changed`
- `process.rs::tests::open_verified_true_key_opens` (child `sleep 60`, killed and reaped at the end)
- `process.rs::tests::open_verified_shifted_start_ticks_is_identity_changed` (regression test for PID reuse protection)
- `process.rs::tests::open_verified_gone_pid_is_identity_changed`
- `process.rs::tests::signal_numbers_table`: every named variant plus `Other` bounds.
- `process.rs::tests::send_term_ends_child`
- `process.rs::tests::suspend_resume_changes_state`
- `process.rs::tests::realtime_signal_34_delivered`
- `process.rs::tests::has_exited_tracks_child`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `IdentityChanged`, `NoSuchProcess`, `PermissionDenied`, `InvalidInput`, `Os`. The UI's identity text is "The selected process changed; wait for the list to update and try again." (R-035); that text is not in this crate.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no heap allocation per call except the `/proc/<pid>/stat` path string (use a stack `itoa`-style buffer if convenient).
- Privacy: log only pid and result at `debug`; never `comm` above `debug`, never the command line.

## Notes
- `security` bead: this is the PID-reuse guard for every action. Never fall back to `kill(pid)` (ADR-006 rejected alternative).
- Kernel threads and protected targets are refused by the engine's admission (ADR-006), not here.
- Tests spawn children with `std::process::Command` and must always kill and reap them, even on assertion failure (use a guard struct whose `Drop` kills and waits).

title: E07-004 Per-TID loop with the pidfd poll rule, set_nice, set_affinity
description:
## Context
Nice and affinity take a PID, not a pidfd, so they need the ADR-006 before-and-after rule: verify the pidfd, call by PID on every thread, then poll the pidfd with timeout 0. A live process cannot have its PID reused, so a pidfd that is not readable after the loop proves the calls hit the target. This bead writes the shared per-TID loop and the two P1 operations on it. Sources: ADR-006 (PID-based syscalls, `SetNice` on every TID, `SetAffinity`, TIDs re-listed before the loop, vanished TID skipped), PROC-001, PROC-066 (nice classes P1), PROC-067, PROC-069 (partial form), ADR-005 (`CpuSet(pub [u64; 16])`).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ops/src/process.rs`:
```rust
pub(crate) fn list_tids(pid: u32) -> OpsResult<Vec<u32>>;
pub(crate) fn for_each_tid(
    key: ProcessKey, boot: BootId,
    op: &mut dyn FnMut(u32) -> Result<(), rustix::io::Errno>,
) -> OpsResult;
pub fn set_nice(key: ProcessKey, boot: BootId, nice: i8) -> OpsResult;
pub fn set_affinity(key: ProcessKey, boot: BootId, set: &tl_model::system::CpuSet) -> OpsResult;
pub(crate) fn to_rustix_cpuset(set: &CpuSet) -> OpsResult<rustix::thread::CpuSet>;
```
- `list_tids`: reads the directory `/proc/<pid>/task`, parses every entry name as `u32`, skips names that do not parse, returns them sorted ascending. `ENOENT` returns `NoSuchProcess`.
- `for_each_tid`, in this order:
  1. `let pidfd = open_verified(key, boot)?`.
  2. `let tids = list_tids(key.pid)?` (re-listed right before the loop).
  3. For each tid: call `op(tid)`. `ESRCH` means the thread exited mid-loop: skip it and do not count it. Otherwise count it in `total`; `Ok` adds 1 to `done`; the first error is kept in `first_err`.
  4. `if has_exited(&pidfd)? { return Err(OutcomeUnknown("process exited during the change")) }`.
  5. `total == 0` returns `Err(OutcomeUnknown("process exited during the change"))`.
  6. `done == total` returns `Ok(())`.
  7. `done == 0` returns `Err(OpsError::from(first_err))` (for example `PermissionDenied`).
  8. Otherwise `Err(Partial { done, total })` with both values saturated to `u16::MAX`.
- `set_nice`: rejects `nice` outside `-20..=19` with `InvalidInput("nice out of range")`, then `for_each_tid` with `rustix::process::setpriority_process(Some(Pid::from_raw(tid)), nice as i32)`.
- `set_affinity`: `to_rustix_cpuset` (bit `i` of word `w` is CPU `w * 64 + i`; an empty set returns `InvalidInput("empty CPU set")`), then `for_each_tid` with `sched_setaffinity(Some(Pid::from_raw(tid)), &set)`. `EINVAL` (mask outside the cgroup's allowed CPUs) maps to `Os(EINVAL)`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a multi-threaded child (the threaded test child described in Notes) **When** `set_nice(key, boot, 5)` runs **Then** it returns `Ok` and field 19 of `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/stat` is `5` for every TID.
- **Given** a child at nice 5 **When** `set_nice(key, boot, 0)` runs without `CAP_SYS_NICE` **Then** it returns `PermissionDenied` and the nice values stay 5.
- **Given** nice `20` **When** `set_nice` runs **Then** it returns `InvalidInput` and makes no syscall.
- **Given** a child **When** `set_affinity` with the set `{0}` runs **Then** it returns `Ok` and `sched_getaffinity` for every TID gives exactly `{0}`.
- **Given** an empty `CpuSet` **When** `set_affinity` runs **Then** it returns `InvalidInput("empty CPU set")`.
- **Given** an `op` that returns `Ok` for the first TID and `EPERM` for the second of two **When** `for_each_tid` runs on a live child **Then** it returns `Partial { done: 1, total: 2 }`.
- **Given** an `op` that returns `ESRCH` for one of three TIDs and `Ok` for the others **When** `for_each_tid` runs **Then** it returns `Ok` (the vanished thread is not counted).
- **Given** an `op` that kills the target with SIGKILL and then waits until its pidfd is readable **When** `for_each_tid` runs **Then** it returns `OutcomeUnknown("process exited during the change")`, never `Ok`.
- **Given** a key whose `start_ticks` is shifted by one **When** `set_nice` runs **Then** it returns `IdentityChanged` and no TID is touched.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ops/src/process.rs`: add the loop, `set_nice`, `set_affinity`, tests

## Tests
- `process.rs::tests::set_nice_applies_to_every_tid`
- `process.rs::tests::lowering_nice_without_cap_is_permission_denied` (skips with a printed note when the test runs as root)
- `process.rs::tests::nice_out_of_range_is_invalid`
- `process.rs::tests::set_affinity_cpu0_every_tid`
- `process.rs::tests::empty_cpuset_is_invalid`
- `process.rs::tests::for_each_tid_partial`
- `process.rs::tests::for_each_tid_skips_vanished_tid`
- `process.rs::tests::for_each_tid_exit_during_change_is_outcome_unknown` (regression test: a target that exits must never report success)
- `process.rs::tests::set_nice_shifted_key_is_identity_changed`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `IdentityChanged`, `PermissionDenied`, `Partial { done, total }`, `OutcomeUnknown("process exited during the change")`, `InvalidInput`, `Os`. UI text for partial results ("Priority updated for 3 of 4 processes. 1 failed: permission denied") is built in the UI from `Partial` and per-target events (PROC-069), not here.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one `Vec<u32>` per call for the TID list; no other allocation per TID.
- Privacy: log pid, TID count and result at `debug` only.

## Notes
- `security` bead. The pidfd stays open for the whole loop; it is what makes the after-poll meaningful.
- The 2 s per-target deadline is applied by the engine around this blocking call (ADR-006); this crate has no timeouts.
- Threaded test child: spawn `std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe()).args(["--exact", "process::tests::threaded_child_entry", "--nocapture"]).env("TL_OPS_THREADED_CHILD", "1")`. `threaded_child_entry` is a `#[test]` that returns at once unless `TL_OPS_THREADED_CHILD=1`; with it set, it starts 2 extra threads and sleeps 60 s. The libtest harness adds threads of its own, so assert "every TID", never "exactly 3". Kill and reap the child in a `Drop` guard. E07-005 and E07-006 reuse this child.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`, for example `... cargo test -p tl-ops`.
- Read CLAUDE.md first. Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead. `tl-ops` has no async code and no runtime (ADR-001 rule 3). `unsafe` is denied workspace-wide; the only `unsafe` file in this crate is `src/sys.rs` (ADR-001 rule 4).

title: E07-005 set_sched and set_io_priority on every TID
description:
## Context
Adds scheduling policy and I/O priority changes on the per-TID loop from E07-004. `SetSched` serves the Realtime, Idle and Custom priority items; `SetIoPriority` serves the Set I/O Priority submenu, including "Default (follows nice)". Both are P2 features in the UI, but the anchor E07-A1 delivers them with the other process operations, so this bead has priority 1. Sources: ADR-006 (`SetSched` with `sched_setattr` on every TID; `SetIoPriority` through `ioprio_set` in `sys.rs` on every TID), R-038, R-093, PROC-066, PROC-068, ADR-005 (`SchedPolicy { Other, Batch, Idle, Fifo, Rr }`, `rt_prio` 1..=99 for Fifo and Rr else 0; `IoPriority { None, Realtime(u8), BestEffort(u8), Idle }`, levels 0..=7).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ops/src/process.rs`:
```rust
pub fn set_sched(key: ProcessKey, boot: BootId, policy: SchedPolicy, rt_prio: u8) -> OpsResult;
pub fn set_io_priority(key: ProcessKey, boot: BootId, prio: IoPriority) -> OpsResult;
pub(crate) fn sched_attr_for(policy: SchedPolicy, rt_prio: u8, current_nice: i32) -> OpsResult<sys::SchedAttr>;
pub(crate) fn ioprio_for(prio: IoPriority) -> OpsResult<u16>;
```
- `sched_attr_for`:
  - `Fifo` and `Rr`: `rt_prio` must be `1..=99`, else `InvalidInput("rt priority out of range")`. `sched_policy` = `SCHED_FIFO` (1) or `SCHED_RR` (2), `sched_priority` = `rt_prio`, `sched_flags` = `SCHED_FLAG_RESET_ON_FORK` (0x01), `sched_nice` = 0.
  - `Other`, `Batch`, `Idle`: `rt_prio` must be 0, else `InvalidInput("rt priority must be 0")`. `sched_policy` = `SCHED_OTHER` (0), `SCHED_BATCH` (3) or `SCHED_IDLE` (5), `sched_priority` = 0, `sched_flags` = 0, `sched_nice` = `current_nice`.
  - `size` = `SCHED_ATTR_SIZE_VER0` (48); runtime, deadline and period 0.
- `set_sched`: `for_each_tid` with an op that reads the TID's current nice with `rustix::process::getpriority_process(Some(tid))` (so changing the policy does not reset the nice value), builds the attr with `sched_attr_for`, and calls `sys::sched_setattr_tid`. Validation errors from `sched_attr_for` are returned before `open_verified` runs (validate once with `current_nice = 0` first).
- `ioprio_for`: `None` gives `ioprio_value(IOPRIO_CLASS_NONE, 0)` = 0; `Realtime(l)` gives `ioprio_value(IOPRIO_CLASS_RT, l)`; `BestEffort(l)` gives `ioprio_value(IOPRIO_CLASS_BE, l)`; `Idle` gives `ioprio_value(IOPRIO_CLASS_IDLE, 0)`. A level above 7 gives `InvalidInput("I/O priority level out of range")`.
- `set_io_priority`: `ioprio_for` first, then `for_each_tid` with `sys::ioprio_set_tid(tid, value)`.
- The menu values (UI side, for reference only): High = `BestEffort(0)`, Normal = `BestEffort(4)`, Low = `BestEffort(7)`, Idle = `Idle`, Default (follows nice) = `None`; Realtime needs `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` and returns `PermissionDenied` without it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `(Rr, 1)` **When** `sched_attr_for` runs **Then** it returns policy 2, priority 1, flags 0x01, size 48.
- **Given** `(Fifo, 0)` or `(Rr, 100)` **When** `sched_attr_for` runs **Then** it returns `InvalidInput`.
- **Given** `(Batch, 5)` **When** `sched_attr_for` runs **Then** it returns `InvalidInput`.
- **Given** `(Idle, 0)` and current nice 7 **When** `sched_attr_for` runs **Then** it returns policy 5, priority 0, flags 0, nice 7.
- **Given** a threaded child at nice 5 **When** `set_sched(key, boot, Batch, 0)` runs **Then** it returns `Ok`, field 41 (`policy`) of every `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/stat` is 3, and field 19 (nice) is still 5.
- **Given** a threaded child **When** `set_sched(key, boot, Rr, 1)` runs without `CAP_SYS_NICE` **Then** it returns `PermissionDenied` and every TID's policy is unchanged.
- **Given** each `IoPriority` value **When** `ioprio_for` runs **Then** `None` is 0, `BestEffort(4)` is 0x4004, `BestEffort(7)` is 0x4007, `Realtime(0)` is 0x2000, `Idle` is 0x6000.
- **Given** `BestEffort(8)` **When** `ioprio_for` runs **Then** it returns `InvalidInput`.
- **Given** a threaded child **When** `set_io_priority(key, boot, BestEffort(7))` runs **Then** it returns `Ok` and `ioprio_get(IOPRIO_WHO_PROCESS, tid)` reads 0x4007 for every TID.
- **Given** a threaded child **When** `set_io_priority(key, boot, Realtime(0))` runs as a normal user **Then** it returns `PermissionDenied`.
- **Given** a key whose `start_ticks` is shifted by one **When** `set_sched` or `set_io_priority` runs **Then** it returns `IdentityChanged`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ops/src/process.rs`: add `set_sched`, `set_io_priority` and helpers, tests
- `crates/tl-ops/src/sys.rs`: add `pub(crate) fn ioprio_get_tid(tid: u32) -> Result<u16, Errno>` (`libc::syscall(libc::SYS_ioprio_get, IOPRIO_WHO_PROCESS, tid)`) for the tests and for later readers

## Tests

- `process.rs::tests::sched_attr_rejects_bad_rt_prio`
- `process.rs::tests::sched_attr_non_rt_keeps_nice`
- `process.rs::tests::set_sched_batch_keeps_nice_every_tid`
- `process.rs::tests::set_sched_rr_without_cap_is_permission_denied` (skips as root)
- `process.rs::tests::ioprio_for_table`
- `process.rs::tests::ioprio_level_out_of_range_is_invalid`
- `process.rs::tests::set_io_priority_best_effort_7_every_tid`
- `process.rs::tests::set_io_priority_realtime_needs_admin` (skips as root)
- `process.rs::tests::sched_and_ioprio_shifted_key_is_identity_changed`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as E07-004, plus `InvalidInput` for out-of-range values.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one `getpriority` per TID extra for `set_sched`; no allocation per TID.
- Privacy: log pid, policy or I/O class, and result at `debug` only.

- `SCHED_FLAG_RESET_ON_FORK` is set for every Fifo and Rr request, including the Custom dialog (see open item E07-O3 in docs/plan/b2-collect-ops.md; if the leader decides otherwise, only the Realtime menu item would set it and `ActionKind::SetSched` would need a flag).

title: E07-006 Thread targets: signal, nice, sched, affinity on one TID
description:
## Context
The Properties window's Threads tab acts on one thread: priority, scheduling, affinity and signals. The identity rule stays the process's: verify the process pidfd, check the TID still exists under it, act on that TID only, then poll the pidfd. Signals to a thread use `tgkill`, because `pidfd_send_signal` targets the whole process. Sources: R-097, ADR-006 (`ActionTarget::Thread { process, tid }`; allowed kinds `Signal`, `SetNice`, `SetSched`, `SetAffinity`), ADR-005 (`ActionTarget::Thread` is P2), PROC-079 (thread actions).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ops/src/process.rs`:
```rust
pub fn thread_send_signal(process: ProcessKey, boot: BootId, tid: u32, sig: Signal) -> OpsResult;
pub fn thread_set_nice(process: ProcessKey, boot: BootId, tid: u32, nice: i8) -> OpsResult;
pub fn thread_set_sched(process: ProcessKey, boot: BootId, tid: u32, policy: SchedPolicy, rt_prio: u8) -> OpsResult;
pub fn thread_set_affinity(process: ProcessKey, boot: BootId, tid: u32, set: &CpuSet) -> OpsResult;
fn with_verified_thread(process: ProcessKey, boot: BootId, tid: u32,
                        op: &mut dyn FnMut() -> Result<(), Errno>) -> OpsResult;
```
- `with_verified_thread`, in this order: (1) validate arguments (same ranges as E07-004 and E07-005; done by each public function before calling this). (2) `let pidfd = open_verified(process, boot)?`. (3) `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>` must exist (`rustix::fs::statat` or `std::fs::metadata`); missing gives `IdentityChanged`. (4) `op()`; `ESRCH` gives `IdentityChanged` (the thread ended before the call), other errors map through E07-001. (5) `has_exited(&pidfd)?` true gives `OutcomeUnknown("process exited during the change")`. (6) `Ok(())`.
- `thread_send_signal`: op = `sys::tgkill(process.pid, tid, signal_number(sig)?)`.
- `thread_set_nice`: op = `setpriority_process(Some(tid), nice)`.
- `thread_set_sched`: op = `sys::sched_setattr_tid(tid, &sched_attr_for(policy, rt_prio, getpriority_process(Some(tid))?)?)`.
- `thread_set_affinity`: op = `sched_setaffinity(Some(tid), &to_rustix_cpuset(set)?)`.
- There is no thread form of `SetIoPriority`, `KillTree`, `Suspend` or `Resume` (ADR-006 allowed list). The engine rejects those combinations; this crate does not offer them.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a threaded child and one of its non-main TIDs **When** `thread_set_nice(key, boot, tid, 5)` runs **Then** it returns `Ok`, that TID's nice is 5 and the main thread's nice is unchanged.
- **Given** the same **When** `thread_set_affinity` with `{0}` runs **Then** only that TID's affinity is `{0}`.
- **Given** the same **When** `thread_set_sched(.., Batch, 0)` runs **Then** only that TID's policy is 3.
- **Given** a threaded child **When** `thread_send_signal(key, boot, tid, Signal::Stop)` runs **Then** the whole thread group stops (state `T` in `/proc/<pid>/stat`), which is Linux's group-stop rule, and the call returns `Ok`.
- **Given** a TID that is not under `/proc/<pid>/task/` **When** any thread function runs **Then** it returns `IdentityChanged` and no syscall targets that TID.
- **Given** a TID that belongs to a different process (the test's own TID) **When** `thread_set_nice(child_key, boot, own_tid, 5)` runs **Then** it returns `IdentityChanged` and the test thread's nice is unchanged (regression test: a TID is only accepted under its own process).
- **Given** a process key with `start_ticks + 1` **When** any thread function runs **Then** it returns `IdentityChanged`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ops/src/process.rs`: add the thread functions, tests

## Tests
- `process.rs::tests::thread_set_nice_only_that_tid`
- `process.rs::tests::thread_set_affinity_only_that_tid`
- `process.rs::tests::thread_set_sched_only_that_tid`
- `process.rs::tests::thread_signal_stop_stops_group`: sends `Cont` afterwards, then kills the child.
- `process.rs::tests::thread_missing_tid_is_identity_changed`
- `process.rs::tests::thread_foreign_tid_is_identity_changed`
- `process.rs::tests::thread_shifted_key_is_identity_changed`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `IdentityChanged`, `PermissionDenied`, `OutcomeUnknown("process exited during the change")`, `InvalidInput`, `Os`.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no allocation.
- Privacy: log pid, tid and result at `debug` only.

## Notes
- `security` bead. Priority 1 because the anchor E07-A1 delivers thread targets; the UI that uses them is P2.
- Uses the threaded test child from E07-004. Find a non-main TID with `list_tids(pid)` and pick one that differs from `pid`.

title: E17-A1 Theme model
description:
## Context
Anchor E17-A1 "Theme model". Writes `ThemeStore`, the GPUI Global that holds the built-in and user theme definitions, the active `TlTheme` and the optional preview, plus the instant theme switch (`activate` without crossfade) and the one-time install at start. When this bead closes, the whole theme model of E17-A1 is in place: `theme/{mod,palette,derived,builtin,metrics,map,store}.rs` and `assets/themes/builtin.json` with Default Dark and Default Light, U-8 recorded. Spec phase P1 (UI-FND-040 "P1: activate, instant switch"); priority 0 because the phase-0 spike needs it. This anchor closes E17-001, E17-002, E17-003 and E17-004. Sources: UI-FND-040, UI-SHL-080, ADR-009 "Theme switch", APP-035, APP-036, R-017, R-068, R-069, R-138.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/theme/store.rs`:

```rust
pub struct ThemeStore {
    pub builtin: Arc<[ThemeDef]>,       // from builtin::load(); 2 in P1, 12 in P2, in TaskSlinger order
    pub user: Vec<ThemeDef>,            // from themes.json (E17-008); empty until then
    pub active: Arc<TlTheme>,
    pub preview: Option<Arc<TlTheme>>,  // set only by E17-A2; when Some, it is what renders
    pub system_scheme: u8,              // portal color-scheme 0, 1 or 2 (E17-007); 0 until then
    version_counter: u64,               // TlTheme.version source
}
impl gpui::Global for ThemeStore {}

pub enum ActivateSource { User, FollowSystem }
pub enum ThemeEvent { Activated { name: Arc<str> }, Deleted { name: Arc<str> }, Copied { name: Arc<str> }, ImportFailed }
pub enum ThemeError { UnknownTheme(Arc<str>), PreviewActive }

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Deserialize, JsonSchema, Action)]
#[action(namespace = tasklens)]
pub struct ActivateTheme { pub name: SharedString }
```

Functions:
- `pub fn init(cx: &mut App, theme: &ThemeSettings, appearance: &AppearanceSettings, user: Vec<ThemeDef>)`: loads built-ins, builds the store, resolves `theme.active` (unknown name falls back to `theme.dark` and then to "Default Dark", with a `warn!`), installs `ThemeStore` and `UiMetrics` (`metrics::init_metrics`), and runs `map::apply` once inside `Theme::update`. No crossfade at start (UI-SHL-110 step 8). Called by `TasklensUi::init` (E16-A1).
- `pub fn current(cx: &App) -> &Arc<TlTheme>`: returns `preview` when `Some`, else `active`. Views never read `active` directly (UI-FND-043 rule 2).
- `impl ThemeStore { pub fn resolve(&self, name: &str) -> Option<(&ThemeDef, bool /*builtin*/)> }`: user themes first, then built-ins (a user theme may shadow a built-in name; the menu shows both and marks the user one "(custom)", UI-FND-040 step 1).
- `pub fn activate(name: &str, source: ActivateSource, cx: &mut App) -> Result<ThemeEvent, ThemeError>`:
  1. `preview.is_some()` gives `Err(PreviewActive)` (the shell shows "Finish or cancel the theme editor first").
  2. Resolve `name`, else `Err(UnknownTheme)`.
  3. Build `TlTheme::from_def` with the fallback built-in of the same mode (Default Dark or Default Light) and `rebuild_derived(appearance)`; increment `version`.
  4. Replace `active`; call `metrics::bump_style_version(cx)` exactly once; run `map::apply` once with the final theme; call `cx.refresh_windows()`.
  5. Return `Ok(ThemeEvent::Activated { name })`. The caller writes `theme.active` when `source == User` (and turns off sync, UI-SHL-080); with `FollowSystem` it writes nothing. This function does no settings write and pushes no toast.
  `CellTextCache` is not cleared by a theme switch (text colour is not part of its key).

Called by the shell on scale or row-height changes (UI-SHL-130 steps 1 to 3) and on `rounded_corners` or `shadow_intensity_pct` changes (the latter also re-runs `rebuild_derived` on `active`).
- `pub fn names(cx: &App) -> Vec<(Arc<str>, bool /*builtin*/)>` in menu order: built-ins in `TS_THEME_ORDER`, then user themes in file order.

title: E17-008 User themes file: load, repair, copy, delete, save
description:
## Context
Adds the user themes file `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tasklens/themes.json` (P2): lenient loading with per-theme repair, Create copy, Delete with fallback, and saving through the tl-app persist callback. tl-ui does no file I/O itself: tl-app reads the file text and passes it in `UiInit.themes_json`, and writes through `UiInit.persist_themes` (ADR-011). Sources: UI-FND-042, ADR-011 (path, atomic write, corrupt rename pattern), APP-036, R-018, R-079.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/theme/user_store.rs`:
- `pub enum PersistTheme { Save(Vec<ThemeDef>), RenameCorrupt { unix_seconds: u64 } }` (the request type carried by `UiInit.persist_themes`; tl-app performs `write_atomic` or the rename).
- `pub struct LoadOutcome { pub themes: Vec<ThemeDef>, pub corrupt: Option<u64 /*unix seconds*/>, pub repairs: Vec<Repair> }` and `pub enum Repair { MissingSlot { theme: Arc<str>, key: &'static str }, BadColor { theme: Arc<str>, key: String }, Unnamed { index: usize, given: Arc<str> }, Renamed { from: Arc<str>, to: Arc<str> }, Truncated { total: usize } }`.
- `pub fn load_user_themes(text: Option<&str>, builtins: &[ThemeDef], now_unix: u64) -> LoadOutcome`:
  1. `None` (missing file): empty, nothing written until the first copy or import.
  2. Text that is not JSON, or not an object with a `themes` array: `corrupt = Some(now_unix)`, empty list.
  3. Per theme, lenient: a missing slot or bad colour string takes the value from the built-in of the same mode (Default Dark or Default Light; mode from `mode` key or `WINDOW_BG` lightness) and records a `Repair` (logged with `warn!` naming theme and slot); a theme without a name gets "Custom theme N" (N = 1-based index among unnamed); duplicate names get " (2)", " (3)" appended in file order; more than 64 themes keeps the first 64 and records `Truncated { total }`.
  4. Unknown keys go into `ThemeDef.extra` and are written back on save (round trip through `BTreeMap`).
- `pub fn serialize_user_themes(themes: &[ThemeDef]) -> String`: `{"themes":[...]}` pretty-printed with 2-space indent; slot keys upper-case, `name`, `mode` (when set), `accent`, `status` and `graph` (when set) lower-case, then `extra` keys.
- `impl ThemeStore`:
  - `pub fn install_user(&mut self, outcome: LoadOutcome)`; called by `TasklensUi::init` before `activate`.
  - `pub fn copy_theme(name: &str, cx) -> Result<ThemeEvent, ThemeError>`: new name "<name> copy", or "<name> copy 2", "<name> copy 3" and so on (first free); appended to `user`; saved (`PersistTheme::Save`); activated with `ActivateSource::User`; returns `Copied { name }`.
  - `pub fn delete_theme(name: &str, cx) -> Result<ThemeEvent, ThemeError>`: built-ins return `Err(ThemeError::BuiltinCannotBeDeleted)` (new variant; shell toast "Built-in themes cannot be deleted"); removes the user theme; saves; if it was active, activates `theme.dark` or `theme.light` chosen by the deleted theme's mode; returns `Deleted { name }`. The confirmation "Delete this custom theme?" is the shell's (UI-SHL-084).
  - Saving happens after Create copy, Delete, Import (E17-009) and editor Done (E17-A2). Never on activate.
- Persist callback access: a Global `ThemePersist(Box<dyn Fn(PersistTheme)>)` installed by `TasklensUi::init` from `UiInit.persist_themes`; tests install a recording closure.
- At init, when `corrupt` is `Some(t)`: send `PersistTheme::RenameCorrupt { unix_seconds: t }` and queue the Warning toast "Themes file was unreadable and has been reset. The old file was kept as themes.json.corrupt-<unix seconds>" (the toast is pushed by the shell after the first frame with the other queued start-up toasts, UI-SHL-110 step 11; this bead returns the text through `LoadOutcome` helper `pub fn corrupt_toast_text(t: u64) -> SharedString`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** no themes file **When** `load_user_themes(None, ..)` runs **Then** the list is empty, `corrupt` is `None`, and no persist request is sent.
- **Given** text `{"themes":` (truncated) **When** loaded at unix time 1759500000 **Then** the list is empty, `corrupt == Some(1759500000)`, and `corrupt_toast_text` reads "Themes file was unreadable and has been reset. The old file was kept as themes.json.corrupt-1759500000".
- **Given** a light theme missing `HEADER` **When** loaded **Then** its `HEADER` equals Default Light `#DDE1E5` and a `MissingSlot` repair is recorded.
- **Given** a dark theme with an unknown key `"FOO":"x"` and `"accent":"blue"` **When** loaded **Then** `accent` falls back to the same-mode built-in accent, a `BadColor` repair is recorded, and `FOO` is kept in `extra`.
- **Given** two themes both named "Mine" **When** loaded **Then** they are "Mine" and "Mine (2)".
- **Given** 70 themes **When** loaded **Then** 64 are kept and `Truncated { total: 70 }` is recorded.
- **Given** a loaded file with unknown keys **When** serialized again **Then** the unknown keys and values are present unchanged.
- **Given** user themes "Ocean copy" exists **When** `copy_theme("Ocean")` runs **Then** the new theme is "Ocean copy 2", it is active, and one `Save` request with the full list is sent.
- **Given** the active user theme "Ocean copy" with mode light **When** `delete_theme` runs **Then** it is removed, `theme.light` becomes active, and one `Save` is sent.
- **Given** "Default Dark" **When** `delete_theme` runs **Then** it returns `BuiltinCannotBeDeleted` and nothing is saved.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/user_store.rs`: create, with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/mod.rs`: add `pub mod user_store;`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/store.rs`: add `ThemeError::BuiltinCannotBeDeleted` and the `install_user` call path.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_theme.rs`: copy and delete through the store with a recording persist closure.

## Tests
- `theme::user_store::tests::missing_file_empty`.
- `theme::user_store::tests::corrupt_renamed_and_toast`: `corrupt` set, toast text exact, `RenameCorrupt` sent at install.
- `theme::user_store::tests::missing_slot_falls_back`.
- `theme::user_store::tests::unknown_keys_round_trip`.
- `theme::user_store::tests::copy_names_increment`.
- `theme::user_store::tests::duplicate_and_unnamed_names`.
- `theme::user_store::tests::cap_at_64`.
- `ui_theme::delete_active_falls_back_by_mode`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: corrupt file renamed and reset with the Warning toast above; per-theme problems repaired and logged, never a toast.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Privacy: theme names are user data; log them only at `warn!` with the repair, never colours or file paths of other users.
- Performance: load once at start and after writes; under 1 ms for 64 themes.

## Notes
- The persist callback type and `UiInit.themes_json` are the proposed contract of open items 4 and 5 in docs/plan/b5-ui-foundation.md; B1 (E33) must match. If the leader changes the contract, follow the settled form.

title: E17-009 TL1 share codes and theme import
description:
## Context
Adds the tasklens theme share code `TL1.` (encode and decode) and the clipboard import path (P3): "Share theme" shows a `TL1.` code, and "Import theme" accepts a `TL1.` code, raw `themes.json` text (`{"themes":[…]}`) or a single theme object, and adds the themes to the user file. The share and import windows and toasts are E21's; this bead is the codec and the store call. Sources: APP-038, UI-FND-042 (import), UI-FND-043 rule 8 (Share encodes the preview), R-079.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/theme/share_code.rs`:
- `pub const TL1_PREFIX: &str = "TL1.";`
- `pub fn encode_tl1(def: &ThemeDef) -> String`: `"TL1."` + base64url without padding of the UTF-8 JSON object `{"v":1,"name":…,"accent":"#RRGGBB","WINDOW_BG":"#RRGGBB", … all 22 slots}` (APP-038). Keys in this order: `v`, `name`, `accent`, then the 22 slots in `ThemeSlot` order. Colours as upper-case `#RRGGBB`. `mode`, `status`, `graph` and `extra` are not included.
- `pub fn decode_tl1(code: &str) -> Result<ThemeDef, ShareCodeError>`: trims whitespace; requires the prefix; base64url decode (padding optional); JSON object; `v == 1`; then the lenient per-theme parse of E17-008 (missing slots fall back by mode).
- `pub enum ShareCodeError { NotAThemeCode, BadBase64, BadJson, UnsupportedVersion(u64) }`.
- `pub fn import_text(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<ThemeDef>, ShareCodeError>`: trimmed text starting with `TL1.` decodes one theme; text starting with `TS1.` goes to `decode_ts1` (E17-010; until then returns `Err(NotAThemeCode)`); text that parses as a JSON object with a `themes` array imports every entry; a JSON object with `WINDOW_BG` imports one theme; anything else `Err(NotAThemeCode)`.
- base64url: write a small encoder and decoder in this file (RFC 4648 section 5 alphabet). No new crate (the tl-ui row has no base64 crate).

`crates/tl-ui/src/theme/user_store.rs`:
- `impl ThemeStore { pub fn import_themes(defs: Vec<ThemeDef>, cx: &mut App) -> Result<ThemeEvent, ThemeError> }`: appends to `user` with the duplicate-name rule (" (2)", " (3)") and the 64-theme cap (extra themes are dropped and counted); saves once (`PersistTheme::Save`); does not activate. Returns a new `ThemeEvent::Imported { count }` (add the variant). Empty input returns `Ok(ThemeEvent::ImportFailed)`.

The shell (E21) shows "Theme imported" or "Clipboard does not contain a theme code" (APP-038) and "Theme code copied" for Share.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** Default Dark's def **When** `encode_tl1` then `decode_tl1` runs **Then** the 22 slots, `accent` and `name` round-trip exactly.
- **Given** a code **When** encoded **Then** it starts with "TL1." and contains only `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` after the prefix.
- **Given** the decoded JSON of a code **When** inspected **Then** it is `{"v":1,"name":…,"accent":…,` followed by the 22 slot keys.
- **Given** `"TL1.!!!"` **When** decoded **Then** `BadBase64`; a valid base64 of `{"v":2,...}` gives `UnsupportedVersion(2)`.
- **Given** raw text `{"themes":[{...},{...}]}` **When** `import_text` runs **Then** two defs are returned.
- **Given** a single theme object text **When** `import_text` runs **Then** one def is returned.
- **Given** "hello" **When** `import_text` runs **Then** `NotAThemeCode`.
- **Given** an existing user theme "Mine" **When** `import_themes` adds another "Mine" **Then** it is stored as "Mine (2)", one `Save` is sent, and the active theme is unchanged.
- **Given** a live preview **When** Share runs **Then** it encodes `preview_def` (E17-A2), not the saved def.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/share_code.rs`: create, with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/user_store.rs`: `import_themes`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/store.rs`: add `ThemeEvent::Imported { count: usize }`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/mod.rs`: add `pub mod share_code;`.

## Tests
- `theme::share_code::tests::tl1_round_trip`.
- `theme::share_code::tests::tl1_alphabet_and_key_order`.
- `theme::share_code::tests::bad_codes_rejected`.
- `theme::share_code::tests::import_raw_json_list_and_single`.
- `theme::share_code::tests::base64url_rfc4648_vectors` (the RFC 4648 section 10 test vectors in the URL alphabet).
- `theme::user_store::tests::import_renames_duplicates_and_saves_once`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the four `ShareCodeError` variants all map to the shell toast "Clipboard does not contain a theme code".
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one-shot on user action.
- Privacy: clipboard text is user input; never log it, log only the error kind.
- Security: clipboard text is untrusted input. Cap the accepted text at 1 MiB before decoding and the theme count at 64; never panic on any input (a proptest over arbitrary strings asserts no panic).

title: E17-011 Import themes from a TaskSlinger themes.json
description:
## Context
Adds the themes half of "Import from TaskSlinger…" (P4): parsing a TaskSlinger `themes.json` chosen by the user and adding its custom themes to tasklens's user themes. The Settings window entry (Advanced page), the portal file chooser and the toast "Imported N settings and M themes" belong to E21 and the settings half to E33; this bead turns the file text into `ThemeDef`s and adds them. Sources: APP-034, APP-035 (TaskSlinger format is tasklens's base format), UI-FND-042.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/theme/import_ts.rs`:
- `pub struct TsImport { pub themes: Vec<ThemeDef>, pub skipped_builtin_names: usize }`.
- `pub fn parse_taskslinger_themes(text: &str, builtins: &[ThemeDef]) -> Result<TsImport, ShareCodeError>`: parses `{"themes":[…]}` with the lenient per-theme parse of E17-008 (missing slots fall back by mode, unknown keys kept in `extra`). A theme whose name equals one of the 12 names in `TS_THEME_ORDER` and whose 22 slots equal the shipped built-in exactly is skipped and counted (TaskSlinger exports may carry built-ins); others are kept, including user copies with built-in names (they get " (2)" through the import rule).
- `impl ThemeStore { pub fn import_taskslinger(text: &str, cx: &mut App) -> Result<usize /*themes added*/, ShareCodeError> }`: parses, then calls `import_themes` (E17-009) and returns the count for the toast.

- **Given** a TaskSlinger theme without `accent` **When** imported **Then** `accent` falls back to the same-mode built-in accent.
- **Given** text that is not JSON **When** imported **Then** it returns `BadJson` and nothing is saved.
- **Given** a file of 2 MiB **When** imported **Then** it is refused before parsing (1 MiB cap) with `BadJson`.

title: E17-012 Theme render goldens
description:
## Context
Adds headless render goldens for the two P1 themes (ADR-013 case "Default Dark theme", rendered at scale 1.0 and 1.1), so a wrong slot value or a broken kit mapping shows up as a pixel diff in CI. The test renders a fixed swatch view built only from `theme::current()` and the kit `Theme`. Sources: ADR-013 headless screenshot tests, UI-FND-001, UI-FND-002, UI-FND-030 (golden workflow).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/tests/render_theme.rs` (feature `render-tests`):
- A test-local view `ThemeSwatches` that draws, top to bottom at 100% scale: one row per `ThemeSlot` (23 rows, 20 px high) with a 120 × 20 block of the slot colour and the slot label in `text_primary` on `window_bg`; then 13 blocks for the `GraphPalette` fields and 4 for the status colours; then one kit `Button` (primary) and one kit `Input`, which read the kit `Theme` filled by `map::apply`.

title: E17-A2 User themes and follow-system
description:
## Context
Anchor E17-A2 "User themes and follow-system". Writes the theme editor live-preview contract in `theme/preview.rs`: how the Theme Editor window (E21) shows unsaved colours across the whole app and how Done and Cancel end the preview. When this bead closes, E17-A2 is complete: `theme/user_store.rs` (E17-008), follow-system switching (E17-007), the crossfade (E17-006) and `theme/preview.rs`. Spec phase of the preview is P3 (UI-FND-043, with the editor APP-037); it is built in P2 with priority 2 because E21's editor depends on this anchor (open item 1 in docs/plan/b5-ui-foundation.md). This anchor closes E17-006, E17-007 and E17-008. Sources: UI-FND-043, APP-037, R-083, UI-FND-040 rule 2.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/theme/preview.rs`:

```rust
pub struct PreviewToken { id: u64 }        // not Clone; one live preview at a time
impl ThemeStore {
    pub fn begin_preview(base: &ThemeDef, cx: &mut App) -> PreviewToken;
    pub fn set_preview_slot(tok: &PreviewToken, slot: ThemeSlot, c: Hsla, cx: &mut App);
    pub fn set_preview_name(tok: &PreviewToken, name: Arc<str>, cx: &mut App);
    pub fn preview_def(tok: &PreviewToken, cx: &App) -> ThemeDef;          // current edited def (Share encodes this)
    pub fn commit_preview(tok: PreviewToken, cx: &mut App) -> Result<ThemeDef, ThemeError>;  // Done
    pub fn cancel_preview(tok: PreviewToken, cx: &mut App);                // Cancel, or editor window closed by X
    pub fn random_preview(tok: &PreviewToken, seed: u64, cx: &mut App);    // "Random"
    pub fn preview_name(cx: &App) -> Option<Arc<str>>;                     // for the Theme submenu "(editing)" marker
}
```

Rules (UI-FND-043):
1. One preview at a time. `begin_preview` while one is live cancels the first (the shell closes the first editor window) and invalidates its token: later calls with the old token are ignored with a `debug!`.
2. While `preview` is `Some`, `theme::current()` returns it (E17-A1). Views never read `active` directly.
3. `set_preview_slot` and `set_preview_name` record the latest value per slot and apply at most once per frame: the first call in a frame schedules one `window.on_next_frame` through the main window's `AnimationDriver` request (same reserved-id mechanism as E17-006); the callback clones `preview`, changes the recorded fields, runs `rebuild_derived`, replaces `preview` with the new `Arc<TlTheme>`, calls `bump_style_version` once, and refreshes windows. No crossfade during preview.
4. A change of `ThemeSlot::Accent` also runs `map::apply` with the preview theme, so kit `primary` and `ring` and the derived focus ring preview too. Other slot changes do not run `map::apply` per frame; `commit` and `cancel` run it once.
5. The graph palette and status colours are not editable and keep the base theme's values.
6. `random_preview(seed)`: randomizes the 22 slots and `accent` with a deterministic PRNG from `seed` (any small xorshift in this file; no new crate); re-rolls `text_primary` lightness until `text_primary` on `list_bg` is at least 4.5:1. The shell shows the toast "Random theme generated." (APP-037).
7. `commit_preview`: the base must be a user theme (built-ins are refused upstream with "Copy a theme before editing it"; here a built-in base returns `Err(ThemeError::BuiltinCannotBeEdited)`). Writes the def into `user`, replacing the theme with the same original name (a rename via `set_preview_name` replaces it under the new name), saves through `PersistTheme::Save` (E17-008), activates it without crossfade (`ActivateSource::User`), clears `preview`, returns the saved def.
8. `cancel_preview`: clears `preview`, bumps `style_version`, refreshes windows; `active` was never changed, so the app returns to it in one frame.
9. `activate` while previewing is refused with `ThemeError::PreviewActive` (E17-A1); the shell shows "Finish or cancel the theme editor first".
10. `preview_name()` returns the previewed theme name so the Theme submenu can show "<name> (editing)" with the check on it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** Default Dark active and a user theme "Ocean" **When** `begin_preview(Ocean)` runs **Then** `current().name == "Ocean"` and `active` is still Default Dark.
- **Given** a live preview **When** `set_preview_slot(WindowBg, #000000)` is called 50 times within one frame **Then** after the frame `current().window_bg == #000000` and `style_version` rose by exactly 1.
- **Given** a live preview **When** `set_preview_slot(Accent, c)` is applied **Then** kit `primary == c` and `derived.focus_ring == c`.
- **Given** a live preview with edits **When** `cancel_preview` runs **Then** `current()` is the original active theme, `preview` is `None`, and no save request was sent.
- **Given** a live preview of user theme "Ocean" with edits **When** `commit_preview` runs **Then** `user` holds the edited "Ocean", one `Save` request is sent, "Ocean" is active, and `preview` is `None`.
- **Given** a preview based on a built-in **When** `commit_preview` runs **Then** it returns `BuiltinCannotBeEdited` and nothing is saved.
- **Given** a live preview with token A **When** `begin_preview` runs again (token B) **Then** calls with token A change nothing.
- **Given** any seed **When** `random_preview` runs **Then** `text_primary` on `list_bg` has contrast at least 4.5:1 and graph and status colours are unchanged.
- **Given** a live preview **When** `preview_def` is read **Then** it holds the unsaved edits (used by Share, E17-009).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/preview.rs`: create, with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/mod.rs`: add `pub mod preview;`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/store.rs`: add `ThemeError::BuiltinCannotBeEdited`.

## Tests
- `theme::preview::tests::views_read_preview_when_live`.
- `theme::preview::tests::cancel_restores_active`.
- `theme::preview::tests::commit_saves_and_activates`.
- `theme::preview::tests::second_begin_cancels_first`.
- `theme::preview::tests::random_keeps_contrast` (100 seeds).
- `theme::preview::tests::slot_updates_coalesce_per_frame`.
- `theme::preview::tests::accent_edit_updates_kit_tokens`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `BuiltinCannotBeEdited` and `PreviewActive` returned to the shell, which shows "Copy a theme before editing it" and "Finish or cancel the theme editor first".
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: Random keeps the 4.5:1 text floor.
- Performance: one `TlTheme` clone (about 1 KB) per applied frame while dragging in the editor; each applied frame bumps `style_version`, the same cost as one theme-switch frame (UI-FND-043).
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- The editor window itself (slot list, hue strip, colour plane, readouts, buttons) is E21's `window/theme_editor.rs`; it calls only these methods.
- Uses the driver hook from E17-006 for the per-frame coalescing.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo test -p tl-ui theme::preview`.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- crates/tl-ui/src/theme/preview.rs crates/tl-ui/src/theme/mod.rs crates/tl-ui/src/theme/store.rs`.

title: E17-001 TlTheme, GraphPalette, status colours and derived tints
description:
## Context
Creates the theme data types every tasklens view reads: `TlTheme` with TaskSlinger's 22 colour slots, `accent`, the 13-field `GraphPalette`, the four status colours and the derived tints. Nothing renders yet; later beads load the built-in JSON (E17-002), map onto the kit theme (E17-004) and install the store (E17-A1). This bead also adds the `theme` module and the tl-ui crate dependencies, so it is the first tl-ui bead. Spec phase P1 (UI-FND-001); built in the phase-0 slice because anchor E17-A1 (P0) needs it. Sources: ADR-009 "Theme model", UI-FND-001, UI-FND-040 (struct), APP-035, APP-039 (accent list), R-068, R-119 (`chart_bg`), D-005.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/theme/mod.rs`:
- `pub enum ThemeMode { Dark, Light }` (`Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug`, serde lower-case `"dark"` / `"light"`).
- `pub struct StatusColors { pub success: Hsla, pub warning: Hsla, pub danger: Hsla, pub info: Hsla }`.
- `pub struct TlTheme { pub name: Arc<str>, pub mode: ThemeMode, pub version: u64, pub builtin: bool, pub window_bg, titlebar, toolbar, input, input_focus, header, list_bg, row_alt, row_hover, row_selected, divider, menu_bg, menu_hover, tab_bg, tab_hover, scroll_track, scroll_thumb, text_primary, text_secondary, text_selected_primary, text_selected_secondary, value_heat: Hsla (22 slots, this order), pub accent: Hsla, pub graph: GraphPalette, pub status: StatusColors, pub derived: Derived }` (`Clone, Debug`).
- `pub enum ThemeSlot` with 23 variants in this order: `WindowBg, Titlebar, Toolbar, Input, InputFocus, Header, ListBg, RowAlt, RowHover, RowSelected, Divider, MenuBg, MenuHover, TabBg, TabHover, ScrollTrack, ScrollThumb, TextPrimary, TextSecondary, TextSelectedPrimary, TextSelectedSecondary, ValueHeat, Accent`. Methods: `pub const ALL: [ThemeSlot; 23]`; `pub fn json_key(self) -> &'static str` (upper-case TaskSlinger keys `WINDOW_BG`, `TITLEBAR`, `TOOLBAR`, `INPUT`, `INPUT_FOCUS`, `HEADER`, `LIST_BG`, `ROW_ALT`, `ROW_HOVER`, `ROW_SELECTED`, `DIVIDER`, `MENU_BG`, `MENU_HOVER`, `TAB_BG`, `TAB_HOVER`, `SCROLL_TRACK`, `SCROLL_THUMB`, `TEXT_PRIMARY`, `TEXT_SECONDARY`, `TEXT_SELECTED_PRIMARY`, `TEXT_SELECTED_SECONDARY`, `VALUE_HEAT`; `Accent` returns lower-case `accent`); `pub fn label(self) -> &'static str` with the APP-035 labels: Window background, Title bar, Toolbar, Input, Input focus, Header, List background, Alternate row, Row hover, Selected row, Divider, Menu background, Menu hover, Tab background, Tab hover, Scroll track, Scroll thumb, Primary text, Secondary text, Selected primary text, Selected secondary text, Value heat, and "Accent"; `pub fn get(self, t: &TlTheme) -> Hsla`; `pub fn set(self, t: &mut TlTheme, c: Hsla)`.
- `pub struct ThemeDef { pub name: Arc<str>, pub mode: Option<ThemeMode>, pub slots: [Hsla; 22], pub accent: Hsla, pub status: Option<StatusColors>, pub graph: Option<GraphPalette>, pub extra: BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value> }` (the parsed JSON record; `extra` holds unknown keys so a user file round-trips, UI-FND-042). `impl ThemeDef { pub fn effective_mode(&self) -> ThemeMode }`: `mode` if set, else `Dark` when `slots[WindowBg]` HSL lightness `< 0.5`, else `Light` (UI-FND-040).
- `impl TlTheme { pub fn from_def(def: &ThemeDef, fallback: &TlTheme, appearance: &AppearanceSettings, builtin: bool, version: u64) -> TlTheme }`: copies slots and accent; `status` and `graph` from the def, else from `fallback` (the built-in theme of the same mode); then `rebuild_derived`.
- `pub mod palette; pub mod derived;` and `pub use` of `GraphPalette`, `Derived`.

`crates/tl-ui/src/theme/palette.rs`:
- `pub struct GraphPalette { pub cpu_fill, cpu_line, kernel_line, mem_fill, mem_line, gpu_fill, gpu_line, disk_fill, disk_line, net_fill, net_line, grid, chart_bg: Hsla }` (13 fields, `Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq`).
- `pub const GRAPH_COLOR_ACCENT: &str = "accent";`
- `pub const ACCENT_COLORS: [(&str, u32); 17]` in this order (APP-039, stored lower-case in state.toml): Coral `0xFF7F50`, Orange `0xF28C28`, Amber `0xF5B700`, Yellow `0xE8D44D`, Lime `0x9BCB3C`, Green `0x4CAF50`, Mint `0x3EB489`, Teal `0x14A098`, Cyan `0x22B8CF`, Blue `0x3B82F6`, Indigo `0x6366F1`, Violet `0x8B5CF6`, Lavender `0xB4A7F5`, Fuchsia `0xD946EF`, Pink `0xEC4899`, Rose `0xF43F5E`, Slate `0x64748B`. Names in display case ("Coral"); `pub fn accent_color(name_lower: &str) -> Option<Hsla>` matches case-insensitively. These hex values are fallbacks until U-18 replaces them (APP-039).

`crates/tl-ui/src/theme/derived.rs`:
- `pub struct Derived { pub new_row_tint: Hsla, pub exited_row_tint: Hsla, pub focus_ring: Hsla, pub shadow: Hsla, pub overlay: Hsla, pub stale_text: Hsla }`.
- `pub fn rebuild_derived(t: &mut TlTheme, appearance: &AppearanceSettings)` with the UI-FND-001 rules: `new_row_tint` = `status.success` alpha 0.18; `exited_row_tint` = `status.danger` alpha 0.18; `focus_ring` = `accent` alpha 1.0; `shadow` = `#000000` alpha `0.35 × shadow_intensity_pct / 100` (dark) or `0.18 × shadow_intensity_pct / 100` (light); `overlay` = `#000000` alpha 0.4 (dark) or 0.25 (light); `stale_text` = `text_secondary`.
- `pub fn heat(row_bg: Hsla, value_heat: Hsla, value: f32, reference: f32, intensity_pct: u8) -> Hsla`: `t = clamp(value / reference, 0, 1) × intensity_pct / 100`; convert both to sRGB `Rgba`, lerp r, g, b per component by `t` (alpha of `row_bg`), convert back. Two multiplies and three lerps; no allocation. `reference <= 0` returns `row_bg`.
- `pub fn blend_over(base: Hsla, tint: Hsla) -> Hsla` (source-over in sRGB, used for the NEW and EXITED tints over a row background).

Crate wiring (this bead is the first to touch tl-ui):
- `crates/tl-ui/src/lib.rs`: add `pub mod theme;`.
- `crates/tl-ui/Cargo.toml` `[dependencies]`, if missing: `tl-model = { path = "../tl-model" }`, `gpui-kit = { workspace = true }`, `serde = { workspace = true }`, `serde_json = { workspace = true }`, `smallvec = { workspace = true }`, `rustc-hash = { workspace = true }`, `tracing = { workspace = true }` (the ADR-001 tl-ui row).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a theme with `row_bg #191B1D` and `value_heat #3E2A28` **When** `heat(row_bg, value_heat, 0.0, r, 100)` is called **Then** the result equals `row_bg`.
- **Given** the same colours **When** `heat(.., r, r, 100)` is called **Then** the result equals `value_heat` (within 1/255 per channel).
- **Given** intensity 50 and value = reference **When** `heat` is called **Then** each sRGB channel is the midpoint of the two inputs (within 1/255).
- **Given** a value above the reference **When** `heat` is called **Then** the result is clamped to `value_heat` at 100% intensity.
- **Given** `shadow_intensity_pct = 0` **When** `rebuild_derived` runs **Then** `derived.shadow.a == 0.0`.
- **Given** a dark theme and `shadow_intensity_pct = 100` **When** `rebuild_derived` runs **Then** `derived.shadow.a == 0.35`; for a light theme `0.18`.
- **Given** a `ThemeDef` with `mode = None` and `WINDOW_BG #F3F4F6` **When** `effective_mode()` is called **Then** it returns `Light`; with `#191B1D` it returns `Dark`.
- **Given** a `ThemeDef` without `status` and `graph` **When** `TlTheme::from_def` runs with a fallback theme **Then** `status` and `graph` equal the fallback's.
- **Given** `ThemeSlot::ALL` **When** iterated **Then** it has 23 entries, 22 unique upper-case keys plus `accent`, in the APP-035 order.
- **Given** `accent_color("coral")` and `accent_color("Coral")` **When** called **Then** both return `#FF7F50`; `accent_color("magenta")` returns `None`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/mod.rs`: create (types above).
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/palette.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/derived.rs`: create, with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/lib.rs`: add `pub mod theme;`.
- `crates/tl-ui/Cargo.toml`: add the dependencies above if missing.

## Tests
- `theme::derived::tests::heat_endpoints`: `heat(0, r)` equals the row bg; `heat(r, r)` at 100% equals `value_heat`.
- `theme::derived::tests::heat_midpoint_and_clamp`: 50% intensity midpoint; value above reference clamps.
- `theme::derived::tests::shadow_and_overlay_alphas`: dark 0.35 and 0.4, light 0.18 and 0.25, intensity 0 gives alpha 0.
- `theme::tests::mode_inferred_from_window_bg`: lightness rule.
- `theme::tests::slot_keys_and_labels`: 23 slots, key and label tables as above, `get`/`set` round-trip every slot.
- `theme::palette::tests::seventeen_accent_colours`: count 17, order, case-insensitive lookup.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A (pure data).
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A here; the contrast floor test is in E17-002.
- Performance: `heat` is called per heat-coloured cell; it must not allocate and must be at most 2 multiplies and 3 lerps beyond the colour-space conversion. Everything else runs only on theme switch.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- Parse colours elsewhere (E17-002) with `gpui::Rgba::try_from(&str)` then `.into()` to `Hsla` (UI-FND-001 Build line).
- `AppearanceSettings` is the `[appearance]` section type from `tl-model::settings` (E03-A2): `shadow_intensity_pct`, `heat_intensity_pct`, `rounded_corners`, `ui_scale_pct`, `row_height_pct`.
- Asupersync types are banned in tl-ui (D-001, ADR-001 rule 1).
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo test -p tl-ui theme::`.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- crates/tl-ui/src/theme/mod.rs crates/tl-ui/src/theme/palette.rs crates/tl-ui/src/theme/derived.rs crates/tl-ui/src/lib.rs crates/tl-ui/Cargo.toml Cargo.lock`.

description:

- `pub fn parse_hex(s: &str) -> Result<Hsla, ColorParseError>`: accepts `#RRGGBB` and `#RRGGBBAA` only (case-insensitive hex digits); anything else is an error. Used again by the user store.
- `pub enum ThemeParseError { Json(serde_json::Error), NotAnObject, MissingThemesArray, MissingName { index: usize }, MissingSlot { theme: Arc<str>, key: &'static str }, BadColor { theme: Arc<str>, key: String, value: String } }` with `thiserror`-free manual `Display` (thiserror is not in the tl-ui row) naming the theme and key.
- `pub fn parse_theme_object(obj: &BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>, strict: bool) -> Result<ThemeDef, ThemeParseError>`: reads `name`, optional `mode` (`"dark"`/`"light"`), the 22 upper-case slot keys, `accent`, optional `status` object (four keys), optional `graph` object (13 keys); every other key goes into `ThemeDef.extra`. With `strict = true` a missing slot or bad colour is an error (built-ins). The lenient path is the user store's (E17-008), which calls this with `strict = false` and gets back the list of repairs through a separate function there.
- `pub fn load() -> Arc<[ThemeDef]>`: parses `BUILTIN_JSON` into `serde_json::Value`, each theme into `BTreeMap<String, Value>`, then `parse_theme_object(.., strict = true)`. Panics with the `ThemeParseError` text on failure (the file is embedded; the parse test catches it at build time). Runs once at `TasklensUi::init`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the embedded file **When** `load()` runs **Then** it returns 2 themes named "Default Dark" and "Default Light", in that order.
- **Given** each loaded theme **When** its slots are read **Then** all 22 slots plus `accent` hold the values listed above.
- **Given** a JSON theme object missing `HEADER` **When** parsed with `strict = true` **Then** the result is `MissingSlot { key: "HEADER" }` naming the theme.
- **Given** a colour `"#12345"`, `"red"` or `"#GG0000"` **When** `parse_hex` runs **Then** it returns an error; `"#0277A6"` and `"#0277A6CC"` parse.
- **Given** a theme object without a `mode` key and `WINDOW_BG #F3F4F6` **When** parsed **Then** `effective_mode()` is `Light`.
- **Given** a theme object with an unknown key `"FOO":"bar"` **When** parsed **Then** `extra` holds `FOO` with its value.
- **Given** the loaded names **When** compared with `TS_THEME_ORDER` **Then** they appear in the same relative order.
- **Given** each loaded theme **When** every text/background pair below is measured **Then** WCAG contrast is at least 4.5:1, except the selected pairs which are at least 4.4:1. Pairs: `text_primary` on `list_bg`, `window_bg`, `row_alt`, `menu_bg`, `header`; `text_secondary` on `list_bg`, `window_bg`; `text_selected_primary` and `text_selected_secondary` on `row_selected`.

## Files

- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/builtin.rs`: create, with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/mod.rs`: add `pub mod builtin;`.

## Tests

- `theme::builtin::tests::all_slots_present_in_every_theme`: 22 slots plus accent per theme, values equal the tables above.
- `theme::builtin::tests::names_in_ts_order`: loaded names are an ordered subsequence of `TS_THEME_ORDER`.
- `theme::builtin::tests::light_theme_mode_inferred_if_missing`: object without `mode` infers Light from `#F3F4F6`.
- `theme::builtin::tests::strict_rejects_missing_slot_and_bad_colour`.
- `theme::builtin::tests::parse_hex_forms`: the accepted and rejected forms above.
- `theme::builtin::tests::contrast_floor`: the pair list above, with relative luminance per WCAG 2.x.

## Cross-cutting

- Accessibility: the contrast test is the accessibility check for both themes (UI-FND-001).
