title: E17-003 UiMetrics global
description:
## Context
Creates `UiMetrics`, the GPUI Global that holds every size token already multiplied by the UI scale: row height, base text, the two radii, spacing, text and icon sizes, and the batch-wide `style_version`. Every view reads sizes from it; no view multiplies by `ui_scale` by hand. Spec phase P1; built in the phase-0 slice for anchor E17-A1. Sources: ADR-009 "Metrics and scale", UI-FND-003, R-020, R-077, APP-040, UI-SHL-130 (recompute steps).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/theme/metrics.rs`:

```rust
pub struct TextSizes { pub xs: Pixels, pub sm: Pixels, pub base: Pixels, pub md: Pixels, pub lg: Pixels, pub xl: Pixels }
pub struct IconSizes { pub xs: Pixels, pub sm: Pixels, pub md: Pixels, pub lg: Pixels }
pub struct UiMetrics {
    pub ui_scale: f32,            // ui_scale_pct / 100
    pub row_height: Pixels,       // 28 × row_height_pct/100 × ui_scale
    pub base_text: Pixels,        // 13 × ui_scale
    pub radius_small: Pixels,     // 4 × ui_scale, or 0 when rounded_corners = false
    pub radius_card: Pixels,      // 6 × ui_scale, or 0
    pub sp: [Pixels; 9],          // sp[0] = 0; sp[1..=8] = 2 4 6 8 12 16 24 32 × ui_scale
    pub text: TextSizes,          // 11 12 13 14 16 20 × ui_scale
    pub icon: IconSizes,          // 12 14 16 20 × ui_scale
    pub line_height: f32,         // 1.3 for every text size (ratio, not scaled)
    pub style_version: u64,       // bumps on any change here or in the active theme
}
impl gpui::Global for UiMetrics {}
```

Functions:
- `pub fn compute(appearance: &AppearanceSettings, prev_version: u64) -> UiMetrics`: pure; takes `ui_scale_pct`, `row_height_pct`, `rounded_corners` from the `[appearance]` section of table (a) (ranges 75..=200 and 80..=150, already clamped by the settings loader); sets `style_version = prev_version + 1`.
- `impl UiMetrics { pub fn hairline(window: &Window) -> Pixels }`: `px(1.0 / window.scale_factor())` (one physical px).
- `pub fn recompute(appearance: &AppearanceSettings, cx: &mut App) -> bool`: computes new metrics; if any field other than `style_version` changed, installs the global with the bumped version and returns `true`; else leaves the global and returns `false`. A change of `window.scale_factor()` is reported by the caller calling `bump_style_version` (scale factor is not part of `UiMetrics`; chart keys and text caches read it themselves).
- `pub fn bump_style_version(cx: &mut App)`: `style_version += 1` on the installed global. The one function every style-version change goes through (theme switches, preview edits, scale-factor changes).
- `pub fn init_metrics(appearance: &AppearanceSettings, cx: &mut App)`: installs the first value with `style_version = 1`.
- `pub fn metrics(cx: &App) -> &UiMetrics` (shorthand for `cx.global::<UiMetrics>()`).

Rules carried in doc comments: views read `metrics(cx)` once per render into a local; no `px()` arithmetic in element builders beyond `m.sp[n]`. `recompute` does not call `theme::map::apply` and does not touch `CellTextCache`; the theme store (E17-A1) calls `map::apply` after a metrics change, and `CellTextCache` clears itself on a new `style_version` (E18).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `ui_scale_pct = 100, row_height_pct = 100, rounded_corners = true` **When** `compute` runs **Then** `row_height = 28`, `base_text = 13`, `radius_small = 4`, `radius_card = 6`, `sp = [0,2,4,6,8,12,16,24,32]`, text `11,12,13,14,16,20`, icons `12,14,16,20`.
- **Given** `ui_scale_pct = 150, row_height_pct = 120` **When** `compute` runs **Then** `row_height = 50.4`, `base_text = 19.5`, `sp[4] = 12`.
- **Given** `rounded_corners = false` **When** `compute` runs **Then** `radius_small = 0` and `radius_card = 0` at any scale.
- **Given** installed metrics with `style_version = 5` **When** `recompute` runs with unchanged appearance **Then** it returns `false` and `style_version` stays 5.
- **Given** installed metrics with `style_version = 5` **When** `recompute` runs with `ui_scale_pct = 125` **Then** it returns `true` and `style_version = 6`.
- **Given** installed metrics **When** `bump_style_version` is called twice **Then** `style_version` rose by 2.
- **Given** a window with scale factor 1.1 **When** `hairline` is called **Then** it returns `px(1.0 / 1.1)`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/metrics.rs`: create, with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/mod.rs`: add `pub mod metrics;` and `pub use metrics::{UiMetrics, bump_style_version, metrics};`.

## Tests
- `theme::metrics::tests::scale_and_row`: scale 150 and row 120 give `row_height` 50.4, `base_text` 19.5, `sp[4]` 12.
- `theme::metrics::tests::defaults_at_100`: the full token list at 100%.
- `theme::metrics::tests::rounded_off_zeroes_radii`.
- `theme::metrics::tests::recompute_bumps_only_on_change` (`#[gpui_kit::test]`, `TestAppContext`).
- `theme::metrics::tests::bump_style_version_increments`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A (scale changes come from the shell, UI-SHL-130).
- Performance: `compute` runs only on a settings or scale change; views read fields, no per-frame work.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- GPUI applies the compositor scale (1.1 on the owner machine); tasklens multiplies by `ui_scale` once (ADR-009). Nothing in tl-ui reads `window.scale_factor()` except `hairline`, chart geometry keys and text cache invalidation (UI-FND-003 preamble).
- `AppearanceSettings` comes from `tl-model::settings` (E03-A2).
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo test -p tl-ui theme::metrics`.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- crates/tl-ui/src/theme/metrics.rs crates/tl-ui/src/theme/mod.rs`.

description:
## Context
Adds the 200 ms theme crossfade (P2): when animations are on, a theme switch interpolates every colour from the old theme to the new one over `m_base` 200 ms, driven by the window's `AnimationDriver` so there is still exactly one `on_next_frame` per frame. Chart geometry rebuilds twice per animated switch (start and end), not every frame. Sources: UI-FND-040 step 3 and states, APP-035 (200 ms crossfade), R-017, ADR-009 "Theme switch" and "Animation driver", UI-SHL-080, UI-SHL-132.

## Deliverable
Changes in `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/store.rs`:
- `struct Crossfade { from: Arc<TlTheme>, to: Arc<TlTheme>, started: Instant, duration: Duration /*200 ms*/ }` held as `crossfade: Option<Crossfade>` in `ThemeStore`.
- `pub fn lerp_theme(a: &TlTheme, b: &TlTheme, t: f32) -> TlTheme`: linear interpolation in Hsla space for each of the 22 slots, `accent`, the 4 status colours and the 13 graph colours (40 lerps); hue interpolates along the shorter arc; then `rebuild_derived`. Name, mode, version and `builtin` come from `b`.
- `activate` (E17-A1) gains the animated path: when `motion.animations` is true and `cx.reduce_motion()` is false ("animations on", R-017), set `crossfade = Some(..)` with `from = current active (or the current interpolated theme if a crossfade is running)` and `to = new theme`; call `bump_style_version` once at the start; request the next frame through the main window's `AnimationDriver::request(THEME_ANIM_ID)`, where `THEME_ANIM_ID` is a reserved `EntityId` constant used only for the theme.
- `pub fn tick_crossfade(cx: &mut App) -> bool`: called by the driver callback for `THEME_ANIM_ID` (the window's driver calls it instead of `cx.notify` for this id). It computes `t = ease_out_cubic(elapsed / 200 ms)`, replaces `active` with `Arc::new(lerp_theme(from, to, t))`, refreshes windows, and re-requests the next frame while `t < 1`. At `t >= 1`: `active = to`, `crossfade = None`, `bump_style_version` once more, `map::apply` once with the final theme, return `false`. It does not bump `style_version` on intermediate frames.
- `map::apply` is not called on intermediate frames; kit widgets switch at the end.
- A second `activate` during a crossfade restarts from the current interpolated colours (UI-FND-040 states).
- With animations off or reduced motion: the E17-A1 instant path, unchanged (one bump, one apply).

The `AnimationDriver` hook: `anim.rs` (E19-A1) owns the driver. This bead adds no code to `anim.rs`; it registers `tick_crossfade` through the driver's public request API for a non-entity requester if E19-A1 provides one, and otherwise through a callback registration function on the driver. If E19-A1 provides neither, stop and report it as a new open item (do not edit `anim.rs`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** animations on and reduced motion off **When** `activate("Default Light", User)` runs from Default Dark and frames run for 250 ms of test time **Then** `style_version` rose by exactly 2 and the final `active` equals Default Light.
- **Given** a crossfade at 100 ms **When** `active.window_bg` is read **Then** it lies strictly between `#191B1D` and `#F3F4F6` in lightness.
- **Given** a crossfade at 100 ms **When** `activate("Default Dark", User)` runs **Then** the new crossfade starts from the interpolated colours (its `from.window_bg` equals the value at 100 ms, not `#F3F4F6`).
- **Given** `motion.animations = false` **When** `activate` runs **Then** the switch is instant and `style_version` rose by 1 (E17-A1 behaviour).
- **Given** reduced motion on **When** `activate` runs **Then** the switch is instant.
- **Given** a running crossfade **When** frames are drawn **Then** exactly one `on_next_frame` callback is registered per frame by the window (the driver's), never one from the store.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/store.rs`: crossfade state, `lerp_theme`, `tick_crossfade`, animated `activate` path, tests.

## Tests
- `theme::store::tests::crossfade_bumps_style_version_twice` (`TestAppContext`, `advance_clock`).
- `theme::store::tests::crossfade_midpoint_is_between`.
- `theme::store::tests::second_switch_restarts_from_current`.
- `theme::store::tests::animations_off_is_instant_and_single_rebuild` (kept from E17-A1, still passing).
- `theme::store::tests::lerp_theme_endpoints`: `t = 0` equals `a`, `t = 1` equals `b` for all 40 colours.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: reduced motion and `motion.animations = false` make the switch instant (R-017, APP-058).
- Performance: 40 Hsla lerps per frame, 12 frames at 60 Hz; two geometry rebuilds per animated switch (UI-FND-040 Performance). No allocation per frame beyond one `TlTheme` (about 1 KB).
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- Easing `ease_out_cubic` (UI-FND-003 motion).
- GPUI `App::reduce_motion()`: `gpui-pre-0.3.7/src/app.rs:1141`.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo test -p tl-ui theme::store`.

title: E17-007 Follow system light and dark
description:
## Context
Adds follow-system theme switching (P2): when `theme.follow_system` is on, a change of the desktop colour scheme selects `theme.dark` for portal value 0 (no preference) or 1 (prefer dark) and `theme.light` for 2 (prefer light), through the normal `activate` path with the crossfade. The portal value arrives from the engine in the snapshot (`system.color_scheme`). Sources: UI-FND-040 "Follow system", APP-036, UI-SHL-080, R-069, table (a) `[theme]`.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/theme/store.rs`:
- `pub fn scheme_target(theme: &ThemeSettings, scheme: u8) -> &str`: `0 | 1 => theme.dark`, `2 => theme.light`, any other value `=> theme.dark`.
- `pub fn on_system_scheme(scheme: u8, theme: &ThemeSettings, cx: &mut App) -> Option<Result<ThemeEvent, ThemeError>>`: stores `system_scheme = scheme`; if `theme.follow_system` is false or the scheme did not change, returns `None`; else calls `activate(scheme_target(..), ActivateSource::FollowSystem, cx)` and returns its result. `FollowSystem` writes nothing to settings.
- `pub fn on_follow_system_enabled(theme: &ThemeSettings, cx: &mut App) -> Option<Result<ThemeEvent, ThemeError>>`: applies the matching preferred theme at once (UI-SHL-080 "Turning sync on applies the matching preferred theme at once"); returns `None` when it is already active.
- Turning follow-system off keeps the current theme; the shell writes it to `theme.active` (UI-FND-040). No store function needed beyond `current()`.

`crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs` (chain edit inside this batch, after E16-A1): in `TasklensUi::init`, subscribe to `SnapshotHub` events; when the `SYSTEM` bit is in the mask and `snapshot.system.color_scheme` differs from `ThemeStore.system_scheme`, call `on_system_scheme` with the current `[theme]` settings. Read settings from `BootSettings` until E20-A2 replaces it with `TlSettings`. The returned event is dropped here (follow-system switches show no toast; APP-036 lists no toast for them).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** follow-system on, `theme.light = "Default Light"`, `theme.dark = "Default Dark"`, Default Dark active **When** a snapshot with `color_scheme = 2` installs **Then** Default Light becomes active and settings are not written.
- **Given** follow-system on and Default Light active **When** `color_scheme` changes to 1 **Then** Default Dark becomes active; with 0 Default Dark as well.
- **Given** follow-system off **When** `color_scheme` changes **Then** `system_scheme` updates and the active theme does not change.
- **Given** follow-system just turned on with `system_scheme = 2` and Default Dark active **When** `on_follow_system_enabled` runs **Then** Default Light becomes active.
- **Given** two snapshots with the same `color_scheme` **When** both install **Then** `activate` runs at most once.
- **Given** an unknown scheme value 7 **When** handled **Then** `theme.dark` is used.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/theme/store.rs`: the three functions and tests.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs`: one hub subscription block in `TasklensUi::init`.

## Tests
- `theme::store::tests::follow_system_picks_light_for_2_dark_otherwise`.
- `theme::store::tests::follow_off_ignores_scheme`.
- `theme::store::tests::enabling_sync_applies_at_once`.
- `ui_theme::scheme_change_from_snapshot_switches_theme` (in `tests/ui_theme.rs`, FakeEngine publishes two snapshots with schemes 1 then 2).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: an `UnknownTheme` (a preferred theme that no longer exists) is logged with `warn!` and the theme stays.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one comparison per `SYSTEM` change; a switch only when the scheme changes.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- Blocked on open item 6 in docs/plan/b5-ui-foundation.md: ADR-003 has no `SystemSnapshot.color_scheme` field and no engine worker reads the portal `org.freedesktop.portal.Settings.ReadOne("org.freedesktop.appearance", "color-scheme")` with `SettingChanged`. Start only after E03 and the engine owner add them; use the field name the leader settles (recommended `SystemSnapshot.color_scheme: u8`).

title: E32-009 Low-memory rescue window frame, texts, filter, eased state
description:
## Context
The rescue window "tasklens - Low memory" is its own process (`tasklens --low-memory`), started by the watcher. It tells the user memory is critically low, lists the biggest apps and processes (E32-A2), and offers "Open Full tasklens". This bead builds the window, its texts, the filter, the eased state and the keys; the list rows are E32-A2. Sources: UI-PWN-032, PROC-098, PROC-097, R-062, R-073, R-120 and table (b) row `LowMemory`, UI-FND-021 (frame), R-132 (strings).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/windows/low_memory.rs`:

```rust
pub struct LowMemoryWindow { /* engine, filter input, list state, pressure history, focus */ }
impl LowMemoryWindow {
    /// Opens the window through TlSecondaryWindow::open with WindowKind::Floating and no parent.
    pub fn open(cx: &mut App, engine: Arc<dyn EngineClient>) -> WindowHandle<Self>;
}
pub fn bind_keys_low_memory(cx: &mut App);
actions!(tasklens, [LowMemEndTask, OpenFullTasklens, LowMemClose, LowMemClearOrClose]);
```

Layout (420 x 560 logical px, minimum 360 x 400, padding `sp6`):

```text
+--------------------------------------------------+
| tasklens - Low memory                [pin] [x]   | title bar, pin shown on
| Your device is running on critically low memory. | t_md 14 semibold, status.danger
| We recommend you close some of the processes     | t_base, text_secondary
| below.                                           |
| [Filter...                                   ]   | TlTextInput md, 28 high
| (list, E32-A2)                                   | rows 32
| [Open Full tasklens]                             | footer 52, Primary button on the left
+--------------------------------------------------+
```

- Title exactly "tasklens - Low memory". The pin starts toggled on; it can be turned off (PROC-056, R-073). How keep-above works in this process is open item OI-9.
- Minimal build: no charts, no process or app icons, only the pin and close frame icons (embedded SVGs); fonts Noto Sans Regular and SemiBold only (open item OI-10 for the init path).
- Filter: placeholder "Filter...", case-insensitive match on the row name. No match: the list area shows "No processes match the filter.".
- Eased state: when every pressure sample of the last 10 s is below the threshold (full share at most 10% and MemAvailable at least 3% of MemTotal), the two top lines are replaced by one line in `status.success`: "Memory pressure has eased. You can open the full tasklens or close this window." The list stays usable. When a sample is critical again, the two original lines return.
- "Open Full tasklens" (`OpenFullTasklens`, `TlButton` Primary): starts the main instance; the rescue window stays open. Route: open item OI-11 (recommended: `Command::Action` with `ActionKind::Launch(LaunchSpec { what: LaunchWhat::Command("tasklens".into()), as_admin: false, cwd: None })`, since a second `tasklens` activates the running instance and exits, APP-011).
- Keys, context `LowMemory` (table (b)): Esc clears the filter if it has text, else closes (`LowMemClearOrClose`); Ctrl+W closes (`LowMemClose`); a printable character with focus in the list starts filtering (focus moves to the filter with that character). Closing the window ends the `--low-memory` process (`cx.quit()`).
- Tab order: filter, list (one focus stop), Open Full tasklens, pin, close.
- Strings: append to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` (R-132 chain edit), keys:
  `lowmem-window-title = tasklens - Low memory`, `lowmem-text-critical = Your device is running on critically low memory.`, `lowmem-text-recommend = We recommend you close some of the processes below.`, `lowmem-text-eased = Memory pressure has eased. You can open the full tasklens or close this window.`, `lowmem-filter-placeholder = Filter...`, `lowmem-filter-empty = No processes match the filter.`, `lowmem-button-open-full = Open Full tasklens`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a FakeEngine with a critical sample **When** the window opens **Then** the title is "tasklens - Low memory" and both critical lines show, the first in `status.danger`.
- **Given** the window open **When** it first renders **Then** the pin is toggled on.
- **Given** FakeEngine samples below the threshold for 10 s of fake time **When** the next sample arrives **Then** the eased line replaces the two lines.
- **Given** the eased state **When** a critical sample arrives **Then** the two original lines return.
- **Given** samples below the threshold for only 8 s **When** the next sample arrives **Then** the critical lines still show.
- **Given** filter text "fire" **When** Esc is pressed **Then** the filter is cleared and the window stays open; **When** Esc is pressed again **Then** the window closes.
- **Given** the window **When** "Open Full tasklens" is clicked **Then** the FakeEngine records one launch command and the window stays open.
- **Given** a filter that matches nothing **When** the list renders **Then** "No processes match the filter." shows.

## Files

- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: chain edit, the seven keys above.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_low_memory.rs`: create.

## Tests

- `tests/ui_low_memory.rs::lowmem_eased_returns_on_pressure`.
- `tests/ui_low_memory.rs::lowmem_esc_clears_then_closes`.
- `tests/ui_low_memory.rs::lowmem_open_full_activates_or_spawns`.

PROC-098 and UI-PWN-033 say `KillUnit(name, "all", SIGKILL)`; ADR-006 takes precedence for app cgroups under `app.slice`, and the systemd worker does not run in `LowMemory` mode.

title: E32-004 Install or remove the lowmem unit when lowmem.enabled changes
description:
## Context
`lowmem.enabled` (canonical table (a), section `[lowmem]`, default `false`, P3) is the switch "Open rescue window on critical memory pressure" in the Settings menu (UI-SHL-040, owned by E21) and the Settings window page "Startup and window" (UI-SHL-069). When it turns on, tasklens installs and enables `tasklens-lowmem.service`; when it turns off, it disables and removes it (PROC-097). tl-ui holds settings and calls a `Box<dyn Fn(&Settings, &State)>` persist callback given by tl-app (ADR-011). This bead hooks that callback. Sources: PROC-097, ADR-011 (ownership), canonical table (a).

## Deliverable
1. In `crates/tl-app/src/lowmem_unit.rs`:
```rust
/// Wraps the persist callback. Keeps the last seen `settings.lowmem.enabled` (starting at
/// `initial`). When the value changes, it starts one std::thread named "tl-lowmem-unit" that
/// runs install_and_enable() (false -> true) or disable_and_remove() (true -> false), then
/// calls `inner` as before. At most one such thread runs at a time; a change that arrives
/// while one runs is applied after it finishes, using the newest value.
pub fn wrap_persist(inner: PersistFn, initial: bool) -> PersistFn;
```
`PersistFn` is the callback type E33-A2 defines for the persist callback (`Box<dyn Fn(&Settings, &State)>`). Use E33's alias if it has one.
2. Chain edit to `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: one line where the persist callback is built, before it is passed to tl-ui:
```rust
let persist = lowmem_unit::wrap_persist(persist, settings.lowmem.enabled);
```
No other change to `main.rs`.
3. Results: success and errors are logged at `info` and `warn` on target `tasklens::engine`. User-visible feedback for a failure and for the OOMScoreAdjust 0 fallback is open item OI-7; do not add a toast or notification in this bead unless the leader settled OI-7.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `initial = false` and a fake install function **When** the callback is called with `lowmem.enabled = true` **Then** install runs once and `inner` is called once.
- **Given** `initial = true` **When** the callback is called with `lowmem.enabled = true` again **Then** neither install nor remove runs.
- **Given** `initial = true` **When** the callback is called with `false` **Then** remove runs once.
- **Given** an install still running **When** the value goes true, false, true **Then** after the first install ends exactly zero further calls run (newest value equals the installed state).
- **Given** a failing install **When** the callback is called **Then** `inner` is still called and a `warn` line is logged.

title: E32-006 LowMemSource stripped process sweep
description:
## Context
In `EngineMode::LowMemory` (the `tasklens --low-memory` rescue process) only the `Processes` worker runs, with a stripped sweep every 2 s: `/proc/<pid>/stat`, `/proc/<pid>/status`, the cgroup path from `/proc/<pid>/cgroup`, and cgroup `memory.current` for app scopes, plus the memory pressure state. The engine publishes `Snapshot.processes` and `Snapshot.health` only. Actions still go through the ADR-006 pipeline with identity revalidation, so `ProcessKey` must be the same key the full sweep would build (U-50). Sources: ADR-004 (engine modes), PROC-098, UI-PWN-032, UI-PWN-033, R-137 (`memory.current` only in `EngineMode::LowMemory`; cgroup files opened with `openat` from a dirfd on `/sys/fs/cgroup` and closed in the same sweep), R-119, U-50, ADR-015 (sanitize).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/workers/lowmem.rs`:

```rust
pub const LOWMEM_PERIOD: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
pub const LOWMEM_PSI_FULL_PCT: f32 = 10.0;   // R-062
pub const LOWMEM_MEMAVAIL_MIN_PCT: u64 = 3;  // R-062

pub struct LowMemSource { /* SysRoot, cgroup dirfd, previous PSI full total and its time */ }

impl LowMemSource { pub fn new(root: SysRoot) -> Self; }

impl Source for LowMemSource {
    fn id(&self) -> SourceId { SourceId::Processes }
    /// Always Some(LOWMEM_PERIOD): the rescue window is always visible and ignores the hidden
    /// policy and processes.interval_ms.
    fn period(&self, _: &Demand, _: &EngineSettings) -> Option<Duration>;
    fn sample(self) -> (Self, SourceUpdate);
}
```

Per sweep, on the blocking pool:
1. List `/proc` numeric entries. For each pid read `stat` (parsed from the last `)`: ppid, state, `start_ticks` = field 22) and `status` (`Uid` real uid, `RssAnon`, `VmSwap`, `Threads`), and `cgroup` (the `0::` line). Use the tl-collect readers from E05-A1 (`proc/pid_stat.rs`, `proc/status.rs`, `proc/cgroup.rs`); do not write new parsers.
2. Build `ProcessKey` exactly as the full sweep does (pid, `start_ticks`, `boot_id`).
3. `ProcessMeta`: `comm` sanitized by `tl_collect::sanitize` (ADR-015), `name` = sanitized `comm`, `user` from the uid, `cgroup` path, `app_id` from the scope name parsed by E05-A2's `apps/cgroup_app.rs`; `exe`, `cmdline`, `icon`, `description` are `None`; no desktop-file index is loaded (open item OI-8).
4. Flags: `OTHER_USER` when uid differs from `getuid()`, `KERNEL_THREAD`, `IS_SELF`, `PROTECTED` with the same rules as the full sweep (ADR-006 protected list).
5. Groups: classify with E05-A2's `apps/classify.rs` (App, Background, System, Ungrouped). For each App group, open its cgroup directory with `openat` from the `/sys/fs/cgroup` dirfd, `fstat` it for the inode (the `CgroupRef.cgroup_id`), read `memory.current`, close it.
6. `/proc/meminfo` `MemTotal` and `MemAvailable`; `/proc/pressure/memory` line `full ... total=<us>`: full share = delta total / delta wall time over the sweep interval, in percent.
7. Fields not read in this mode (`cpu_pct`, `io_*`, `net_*`, `gpu_*`, `pss_bytes`, `uss_bytes`, `rss_bytes`) are 0 with `Validity::Unsupported` in `FieldValidity`, never shown as measured zeros.
8. Emit one `SourceUpdate` carrying the records, the app groups (name, process count, `CgroupRef`, `memory.current`, uid), MemTotal, MemAvailable and the pressure state. The variant and the snapshot fields that carry the groups and the pressure state are open item OI-1.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake root with 3 processes, one in `user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/app-org.kde.konsole-1234.scope` **When** `sample` runs with uid 1000 **Then** the update has 3 records and 1 app group whose `memory.current` equals the fake file value.
- **Given** a fake root and the same pid **When** the full sweep (E05-A1) and `LowMemSource` both run **Then** both build the same `ProcessKey` (U-50).
- **Given** a process owned by uid 0 and the sweep running as uid 1000 **When** `sample` runs **Then** that record has `OTHER_USER`.
- **Given** a `comm` with control characters **When** `sample` runs **Then** the record's name is the sanitized text (ADR-015).
- **Given** a pid that exits between listing and reading `stat` **When** `sample` runs **Then** it is skipped without error.
- **Given** `/proc/pressure/memory` missing **When** `sample` runs **Then** the pressure state is computed from MemAvailable only, and no error is returned.
- **Given** two samples 2 s apart with `full total` growing by 300000 us **When** the second `sample` runs **Then** the full share is 15.0% and the state is critical.
- **Given** any demand and settings **When** `period` is called **Then** it returns `Some(2 s)`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/lowmem.rs`: fill.
- Tests: `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `lowmem.rs`, using a fake root built in a `tempfile::TempDir` (dev-dependency `tempfile = "3.27.0"`, ADR-002).

## Tests
- `workers::lowmem::tests::sweep_fake_root_records_and_groups`.
- `workers::lowmem::tests::key_matches_full_sweep` (U-50).
- `workers::lowmem::tests::other_user_flag`.
- `workers::lowmem::tests::sanitized_names`.
- `workers::lowmem::tests::vanished_pid_skipped`.
- `workers::lowmem::tests::psi_missing_falls_back_to_memavailable`.
- `workers::lowmem::tests::psi_full_share_from_total_delta`.
- `workers::lowmem::tests::period_always_two_seconds`.
- `workers::lowmem::tests::unread_fields_unsupported`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: per-pid read errors skip the pid; a failed `/proc` listing returns the update with `Validity::Failed` and the error in `SourceHealth.last_error`.
- Validity: records use `Valid`, `Restricted` (other users' `status` fields when unreadable) and `Unsupported` (fields not read in this mode).
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one sweep under 15 ms for 2,000 processes (the E05 sweep gate); no `smaps`, no fd counting, no metadata refresh, no icon or desktop lookup; buffers reused across sweeps.
- Privacy: untrusted process text goes through `sanitize`; never log names, command lines or environment.

## Notes
- E10's processes worker selects this source by `EngineMode` in the chain-edit bead E32-007. E09's session must start only the `Processes` worker in `LowMemory` mode (ADR-004); if it starts others, report it to the leader rather than editing E09 files.
- The pressure rule matches the watcher: full share above 10% over the interval, or MemAvailable below 3% of MemTotal. The rescue window's "eased" state is computed in the UI from these samples (E32-009).
- Open items: this bead uses the recommended answer to OI-1, OI-8 in the E32 section of `docs/plan/b1-infra.md`. If the leader settled an item differently, the leader's answer written there wins over the value here.

title: E22-A1 Process table renders: ProcessesPage with the process delegate
description:
## Context
Anchor E22-A1. `ProcessesPage`, the entity behind the Processes tab: it subscribes to `SnapshotHub`, owns the `TlTreeTable<ProcessDelegate>`, sends table queries, accepts matching views and renders the table with its two-line header. Driven by `FakeEngine` it renders 2,000 rows, which the phase-0 `table-2000` scene (E01) measures. Other epics build on this page: E23 registers Properties and dialog handlers here, E26 mounts the minigraph panel, E30 mounts History mode, E27 and E28 reuse `ProcessRowCells` and the delegate cells. Sources: ADR-009 (entity structure, nothing notifies in render, tree-table), ADR-005 (hub), UI-PRC-001, UI-PRC-002 (data binding), UI-PRC-023, PROC-013, PROC-021 (no skeleton), UI-PRC-024 (first sweep).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs` (module lines from E22-010, E22-001 to E22-009 already present):
```rust
pub struct ProcessesPage {
    table: Entity<TlTreeTable<ProcessDelegate>>,
    hub_sub: Subscription,           // created in new(), never in render
    focus: FocusHandle,              // the table body focus (track_focus)
    client: Arc<dyn EngineClient>,
}
impl ProcessesPage {
    pub fn new(window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> Self;
    pub fn table(&self) -> &Entity<TlTreeTable<ProcessDelegate>>;
    pub fn focus_table(&self, window: &mut Window);
}
impl Render for ProcessesPage { /* key_context("ProcessTable") on the page div, containing the table (key_context "Table") */ }
```
Behaviour:
- `new` creates the table entity, sends the first `SetTableQuery` (generation 1) and subscribes to the hub. On a hub change whose `ComponentMask` intersects `PROCESSES | TABLE | WINDOWS | SETTINGS | DEVICES`, the page hands the new snapshot to the delegate; when `ProcessQuery::accept` returns true it calls `table.update(cx, |t, cx| cx.notify())`. Other changes are ignored. Nothing calls `notify` inside `render`.
- Registers `.on_action` for the E18 shared `CollapseAll` on the page div: `ProcessQuery::collapse_all` then send (PROC-020, Ctrl+L).
- First sweep not yet installed (`shown == None`): the header renders with `…` totals and the body is plain `list_bg` with no text, no skeleton, no spinner (PROC-021, UI-PRC-024).
- Settings observation: changes to `processes.mode` call `set_mode` and send; changes to `appearance.*`, `units.*`, `tables.*` clear the delegate's text cache through E18's `CellTextCache` clear on `style_version` (ADR-009).
- The page is constructed on first visit and kept (ADR-009); E22-011 registers it in `MainWindow`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a FakeEngine that publishes a 2,000-row view **When** the page renders in a 720 px viewport **Then** at most 27 row elements are built.
- **Given** the page is created **When** the FakeEngine log is read **Then** one `SetTableQuery` with generation 1 was sent.
- **Given** a hub change with only `SERIES` **When** handled **Then** the table is not notified (render counter unchanged).
- **Given** a hub change with `TABLE` and a matching generation **When** handled **Then** the table is notified once.
- **Given** no view yet **When** rendered **Then** the header shows `…` in CPU line 2 and the body has no row elements and no skeleton.
- **Given** expanded app rows **When** `CollapseAll` is dispatched **Then** one query is sent whose `expanded` holds only the group headers.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: add `ProcessesPage`.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_processes.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `ui_processes::tree_table_renders_visible_range_only_2000` (TestAppContext, FakeEngine scripted snapshot, seed 42).
- `ui_processes::first_query_sent_on_create`.
- `ui_processes::notifies_only_on_drawn_components` (render counter from E16 testing helpers).
- `ui_processes::no_skeleton_on_processes_tab` (UI-PRC-024).
- `ui_processes::collapse_all_action_sends_query`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: an engine error never empties the table; the last view stays with stale dimming (ADR-003) and the shell health item reports the worker (UI-PRC-024).
- Validity: WarmingUp `…` before the second sweep in rate cells; Stale dims.
- Accessibility: page div carries `key_context("ProcessTable")`; the table body has `tab_index(0)` (E18).
- Performance: ADR-014 `table-2000`: UI thread p99 ≤ 2.0 ms per frame while scrolling at 1,200 px/s with 1 Hz changes; this bead must not add per-frame allocation (the gate run is E22-028).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Anchor: E27, E28, E23, E26, E30 and E01 depend on this bead. Keep `ProcessesPage::new`, `table()`, `ProcessDelegate` and `ProcessRowCells` public.
- Hub and FakeEngine: E16-A1 (`hub.rs`, `testing/fake_engine.rs`). Tree table: E18-A1.
- gpui `uniform_list` and `track_scroll`: gpui-pre-0.3.7 `src/elements/uniform_list.rs:22`, `:683`.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, check, clippy or test through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_processes` (it takes the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope; the wait can be long, so run it in the background when your tool call has a timeout). On an OOM kill (exit 137) retry once, then report.

The English text in this bead is the value, exactly.

title: Process header line 2 system totals
description:
## Context
Header line 2 for the process table: the system total under each column that has one, formatted like the cells and right-aligned in `text_secondary`. The two-line header element itself is E18's; this bead supplies `header_total` for the process delegate. Sources: PROC-038, UI-PRC-005 (line 2 rules), PROC-033 (GPU N totals), PROC-003 (formats), R-050.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/header_totals.rs` (with `pub mod header_totals;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub fn header_total(col: &ProcColumn, totals: &TableTotals, settings: &Settings, out: &mut CellOut) -> bool;
```
Returns false (no line 2) for every column that has no total. Totals (PROC-038), each read from the `TableTotals` field with that meaning:
- CPU: total utilisation %, one decimal (`11.9%`).
- Memory: (MemTotal − MemAvailable) / MemTotal %.
- Swap: used %.
- Disk: highest busy % among physical disks.
- Network: total physical-interface throughput as % of the summed link speed; when the link speed is unknown, the rate in the `units.network` format.
- GPU: highest utilisation among GPUs; GPU N: that adapter's utilisation; VRAM: used / total % over all GPUs. With no GPU each of these writes `Validity::Unsupported` (drawn `n/a`).
- Threads: system thread count (Count format). Handles: `/proc/sys/fs/file-nr` field 1 (Count format).
- Every other column, including Name, User, PID, Description and Power usage: returns false.
- Before the second sample the rates write `Validity::WarmingUp` (drawn `…`).
- Header text style (applied by E18's header): `t_base` regular `text_secondary`, always right-aligned, same validity glyph rules as cells.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** totals with CPU 11.94 **When** `header_total` runs for `cpu` **Then** it returns true and text is `11.9%`.
- **Given** the `name`, `user`, `pid`, `description` columns **When** called **Then** it returns false.
- **Given** no GPU in the catalog **When** called for `gpu`, `gpu_mem_dedicated` and `gpu_0` **Then** each returns true with validity Unsupported.
- **Given** link speed unknown and 287_500 B/s total in bits mode **When** called for `network` **Then** text is `2.3 Mbps`.
- **Given** Handles total 41_234 **When** called **Then** text is `41 234` (U+2009).

title: Process table query state, generations and expansion
description:
## Context
The process table's query state: it owns the `TableQuery` the UI sends to the engine (mode, sort, filter, expansion, generation) and the rule that a view is shown only when its `query_generation` equals the last sent generation. The engine sorts, filters, groups and flattens; the UI never does (ADR-009, PROC-013). Sources: ADR-009 "Process tree-table", ADR-005 `Command::SetTableQuery`, PROC-004 (group expand persists), PROC-009 (Kernel threads row collapsed by default), PROC-014 (modes, expand state kept per identity for the session), PROC-020 (Collapse all), PROC-047 (sort, persistence), R-010, R-011, UI-PRC-002 data binding, UI-PRC-016 (generations).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/table.rs` (with `pub mod table;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub struct ProcessQuery {
    generation: u64,                     // starts at 0; +1 for every query sent
    mode: TableMode,                     // from processes.mode: grouped -> Grouped, tree -> Tree, flat -> Flat
    sort: SortSpec,                      // from state.toml [sort.processes]; default column "pid", ascending
    filter: Arc<str>,                    // lowercase, set by E22-021
    expanded: FxHashSet<NodeId>,         // session state per identity
    collapsed_by_user: FxHashSet<NodeId>,// rows the user collapsed, so defaults do not re-expand them
    shown: Option<Arc<ProcessTableView>>,// the view on screen
}
impl ProcessQuery {
    pub fn new(settings: &Settings, state: &UiState) -> Self;
    pub fn to_query(&self) -> TableQuery;             // expanded as Arc<[NodeId]>
    pub fn bump_and_send(&mut self, client: &dyn EngineClient); // generation += 1, then client.send(Command::SetTableQuery(self.to_query()))
    pub fn accept(&mut self, view: &Arc<ProcessTableView>) -> bool; // true and stores it when view.query_generation == generation
    pub fn set_mode(&mut self, m: TableMode);
    pub fn set_sort(&mut self, col: ColumnId, kind: ProcColumnKind) -> SortSpec; // first click: descending for numeric kinds, ascending for Text and PowerClass; same column again flips
    pub fn set_filter(&mut self, lower: Arc<str>);
    pub fn toggle(&mut self, id: NodeId);
    pub fn expand_path(&mut self, ids: &[NodeId]);    // used by the jump target (E22-A3)
    pub fn collapse_all(&mut self);                   // clears every expansion except the three group headers (PROC-020)
    pub fn shown(&self) -> Option<&Arc<ProcessTableView>>;
}
```
Rules:
- Initial expansion: the three group headers follow `state.toml [processes] group_expanded = { apps, background, system }` (default all true); the "Kernel threads (N)" row starts collapsed; every app and unit row starts collapsed. Expansion of process and app rows lives for the session only; group header expansion writes back to `group_expanded` through the state persist path (500 ms debounce, ADR-011).
- Every change of mode, sort, filter or expansion calls `bump_and_send` once.
- `accept` keeps the previous `shown` view when the generation does not match (stale results are ignored).
- Sort persists to `state.toml [sort.processes]` (`column`, `ascending`) on every change; it always persists (no "remember sorting" option).
- Mode changes come from `processes.mode` (written by E20/E21 actions); this bead observes the setting and calls `set_mode` plus `bump_and_send`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fresh state **When** `new` runs **Then** mode is Grouped, sort is pid ascending, the three groups are expanded and the Kernel threads row is not in `expanded`.
- **Given** generation 4 sent **When** a view with `query_generation = 3` arrives **Then** `accept` returns false and `shown` is unchanged.
- **Given** a view with generation 4 **When** it arrives **Then** `accept` returns true and `shown` is that view.
- **Given** sort pid ascending **When** `set_sort(cpu, Percent)` **Then** the new sort is cpu descending; again **Then** cpu ascending.
- **Given** sort by `name` (Text) **When** first clicked **Then** it is ascending.
- **Given** expanded app rows and groups **When** `collapse_all` **Then** only the three group headers stay expanded.
- **Given** the user collapses "Apps" **When** the state is saved **Then** `group_expanded.apps = false`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/table.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: add the `mod` line.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_processes.rs`: create with these tests (FakeEngine records the sent commands).

## Tests
- `ui_processes::query_defaults_from_settings_and_state`.
- `ui_processes::stale_generation_results_ignored`.
- `ui_processes::sort_first_click_desc_numeric_asc_text`.
- `ui_processes::collapse_all_keeps_group_headers`.
- `ui_processes::group_expand_persists_to_state`.
- `ui_processes::each_change_sends_one_query`: mode, sort, filter and toggle each produce exactly one `SetTableQuery` in the FakeEngine log with increasing generation.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: `to_query` allocates one `Arc<[NodeId]>` per sent query, never per frame.
- Privacy: the filter text is never logged.

## Notes
- `TableQuery`, `TableMode`, `SortSpec`, `NodeId`, `Command` are tl-model types (ADR-009, ADR-005). `EngineClient` and `FakeEngine` come from E16-A1.
- App and unit rows start collapsed because the UI-PRC-002 sketch draws them with `▸` ("Firefox (14)").
- Build rule: run every cargo build, check, clippy or test through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_processes` (it takes the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope; the wait can be long, so run it in the background when your tool call has a timeout). On an OOM kill (exit 137) retry once, then report.

title: ProcessDelegate: TreeTableDelegate for the process table
description:
## Context
`ProcessDelegate`, the `TreeTableDelegate` implementation for the process table. It maps the engine's finished `ProcessTableView` rows to row kinds, flags, Name cells and metric cells, reports visible keys as demand, and forwards sort, expand, column and activation events. Other tables (Services child rows, E27) reuse its cell code through `ProcessRowCells`. Sources: UI-PRC-001 (delegate trait), UI-PRC-002 (row kinds and data binding), UI-PRC-010 (visible demand), UI-PRC-005 (GPU N tooltip), ADR-009 (tree-table, visible demand, text cache), PROC-013, PROC-018, PROC-022, PROC-033, D-008.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/delegate.rs` (with `pub mod delegate;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub struct ProcessDelegate {
    query: ProcessQuery,                        // E22-008
    snapshot: Arc<Snapshot>,                    // the snapshot the rows came from (or the paused one, E22-024)
    row_index: FxHashMap<NodeId, u32>,          // rebuilt when view.header.version changes
    sibling: Vec<(bool /*last*/, u64 /*ancestor bits*/)>, // E22-006 pass, per row
    layout: ColumnLayout,                       // from state.toml [columns.processes]
    specs: FxHashMap<ColumnId, ColumnSpec>,     // built from PROCESS_COLUMNS for the offered columns
    name_cache: FxHashMap<NodeId, (SharedString, SharedString)>, // primary, secondary
}
impl TreeTableDelegate for ProcessDelegate { type RowId = NodeId; ... }
pub struct ProcessRowCells;  // reusable: fn fill(record: &ProcessRecord, kind: RowKind, col: ColumnId, ctx: &CellCtx, out: &mut CellOut)
                             //            fn render(out: &CellOut, col: ColumnId, width: Pixels, st: PaintState, theme, cx) -> impl IntoElement
```
Trait methods:
- `row_count` = `view.rows.len()`; `row_id(ix)` = `rows[ix].node`; `row_index` from the map.
- `row_kind`: `NodeId::Group` rows map by the `GroupRow` kind to `GroupHeader` (the three Task Manager groups), `App`, or `Unit`; `NodeId::Process` rows map to `KernelThread` when `ProcFlags::KERNEL_THREAD`, `Pseudo` for the two pseudo rows, else `Process`. The "Kernel threads (N)" row is a `Unit`-shaped row with the `cpu` icon.
- `row_depth` = `rows[ix].depth`; `row_expandable` = `has_children.then_some(expanded)`.
- `row_flags`: NEW, EXITED from `ProcFlags`; STALE when the component header validity is Stale; RESTRICTED when any field validity is Restricted; SUSPENDED when `state == Stopped`; FROZEN (P2, E22-032); LAST_SIBLING and ANCESTOR_CONTINUES from `sibling`.
- `columns` / `column_spec`: offered columns are those of `PROCESS_COLUMNS` with `phase <=` the current shipped phase constant `SHIPPED_PHASE: u8 = 1` in this file (later beads raise it), plus `gpu_N` only for adapters present in `Snapshot.devices` (numbered by PCI bus address ascending, PROC-033). GPU N header tooltip: `"<adapter name> (<PCI address>)"`.
- `cell` → `ProcessRowCells::fill` (E22-003); `name_cell` → `NameCellData` (E22-005) with primary `"<name> (N)"` for app and unit rows (N = member count), process rows `meta.name`.
- `header_total` → E22-007. `sort` / `on_sort` → `ProcessQuery::set_sort` then send. `on_toggle_expand` → `ProcessQuery::toggle` then send.
- `selectable(ix)`: false for `GroupHeader`.
- `on_columns_changed`: writes `[columns.processes]` (`order`, `visible`, `widths`) to `UiState` through the persist path (500 ms debounce).
- `on_visible_range(ids)`: forwards the process keys among `ids` (at most 512) to `DemandAggregator` as `Demand::ProcessDetail { keys }` (ADR-008, E16-A1 `demand.rs`).
- `on_activate(id)`: on a GroupHeader toggles expansion; on process, app and unit rows dispatches `OpenProperties` (D-008; the handler is E23's). Exited rows: E22-012.
- `row_tooltip` → None here (E22-013 fills it). `context_menu` → returns the menu unchanged here (E22-A2 fills it). `empty_text` → None here (E22-021).
- `header_lines` → `HeaderLines::Two`; `columns_fixed` → false.
- On every accepted view: rebuild `row_index` and `sibling` when `view.header.version` changed; prune `name_cache` keys not in the view.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake view with one row of every kind **When** the delegate answers **Then** kinds are GroupHeader, App, Unit, Process, KernelThread, Pseudo in that order, and `selectable` is false only for the group header.
- **Given** an app row with 14 members named Firefox **When** `name_cell` runs **Then** primary is "Firefox (14)".
- **Given** rows reordered in a new view version **When** `row_index(id)` is called **Then** it returns the new index.
- **Given** a scroll that shows 40 rows **When** `on_visible_range` is called with 120 ids **Then** DemandAggregator receives the process keys among them, at most 512.
- **Given** one GPU present **When** `columns` is built **Then** `gpu_0` is offered and `gpu_1` is not.
- **Given** a column of phase 2 and `SHIPPED_PHASE = 1` **When** columns are built **Then** it is not offered.
- **Given** Enter on a process row **When** `on_activate` runs **Then** `OpenProperties` is dispatched; on a group header the row toggles.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/delegate.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: add the `mod` line.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_processes.rs`: add tests.

## Tests

- `ui_processes::group_header_row_not_selectable`.
- `ui_processes::row_index_rebuilt_per_version`.

- `ui_processes::gpu_slots_only_for_present_adapters`.

- Accessibility: group headers are skipped by keyboard selection (`selectable`).
- Performance: no allocation per visible row per frame once caches are warm; `row_index` rebuild is O(rows) only on a version change (≈ 60 µs at 2,000 rows, UI-PRC-023).

title: Tree connector lines in the Name cell
description:
## Context
Tree connector lines in the Name cell (View > Process View > "Tree Connector Lines", `processes.tree_guide_lines`, default off). They show the ppid tree structure in Tree View and inside groups. Sources: PROC-017, UI-PRC-003 (connector anatomy), UI-PRC-001 (`RowFlags::LAST_SIBLING`, `ANCESTOR_CONTINUES`).

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/name_cell.rs`: `fn paint_connectors(depth: u8, last_sibling: bool, ancestor_continues: u64, in_group: bool, bounds: Bounds<Pixels>, theme: &TlTheme, window: &mut Window)` drawn in a `canvas` before the icon, called from `render_name_cell` only when `processes.tree_guide_lines` is true.
- For each ancestor depth k < depth − 1 whose bit k is set in `ancestor_continues`: a 1 px vertical `divider` quad at x = 8 + k × 18 + 8 over the full row height.
- For the row's own depth: a vertical quad at x = 8 + (depth − 1) × 18 + 8 from the row top to the row centre, continuing to the row bottom when not `last_sibling`; plus a horizontal quad from that x to the chevron's left edge at the row centre.
- Depth-0 rows under a group header draw from the group chevron centre x = 16. Group header rows draw none.
- Every quad snaps to 1 physical px (`window.pixel_snap` or rounding with `window.scale_factor()`).
- In the delegate (E22-009 owns the struct; this bead adds the computation): `last_sibling` and `ancestor_continues` are computed once per table version in one reverse pass over `view.rows` (a row is the last sibling when no later row at the same depth appears before a row of smaller depth; bit k of a row is set when its ancestor at depth k is not the last sibling).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `tree_guide_lines = false` **When** a depth-2 row renders **Then** no connector quad is drawn.
- **Given** it is true and a depth-2 row that is not the last sibling, whose depth-0 ancestor also continues (bit 0 set) **When** rendered **Then** 3 quads are drawn: a full-height vertical at x 16 (depth-0 ancestor), a full-height vertical at x 34 (own connector), and a horizontal at the row centre from x 34 to x 44 (the chevron's left edge).
- **Given** a depth-2 row that is the last sibling **When** rendered **Then** its own vertical quad ends at the row centre.
- **Given** rows A(d0), B(d1), C(d2), D(d1) **When** the pass runs **Then** B and C are not last for depth 1 ancestry (D follows), C is last sibling, D is last sibling.
- **Given** a group header row **When** rendered **Then** no connector is drawn.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/name_cell.rs`: add `paint_connectors`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/delegate.rs`: add the reverse pass that fills `last_sibling` and `ancestor_continues` per row.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_process_cells.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `ui_process_cells::connector_lines_only_when_enabled`.

title: New and exited row highlight with linger and fade
description:
## Context
New and exited row highlight: NEW rows get a green tint, EXITED rows a red tint with greyed text, for the linger time, fading over the last 300 ms. Exited rows stay in place and are not actionable. Sources: PROC-043, R-041, UI-PRC-011, ADR-009 highlight bullet and animation driver, UI-PRC-008 (selection wins), D-008.

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/cells.rs`: `pub fn row_tint(flags: ProcFlags, flag_since_ns: TimeNs, now_ns: TimeNs, interval_ms: u32, animations: bool, enabled: bool) -> Option<(TintKind, f32 /*alpha*/)>` and the row-background quad drawn by the delegate's row renderer; in `pages/processes/delegate.rs`: the call per visible row and the frame request.
- Linger `L = clamp(2 × processes.interval_ms, 1000, 3000)` ms, measured from the engine timestamp of the flag's first appearance (not UI time).
- NEW: `status.success` at alpha 0.35. EXITED: `status.danger` at alpha 0.35; all row text `text_secondary`; icons at 60 % opacity; the chevron stays.
- Fade: during the last 300 ms the alpha goes 0.35 to 0 with `ease_out_cubic`. With `motion.animations = false` or `App::reduce_motion()` true, the tint stays 0.35 and switches off at L.
- Layer order: zebra (`list_bg` even, `row_alt` odd, counted on the flattened index), then this tint, then heat (E22-004), then the selection fill. A selected row hides the tint: new-and-selected shows only the selection fill; exited-and-selected uses the selection fill with `text_selected_secondary` text.
- `processes.highlight_new_exited = false`: no tints; exited rows still linger and are still not actionable.
- Frames: the delegate calls E19's `AnimationDriver::request` only while at least one visible row is inside its 300 ms fade window; otherwise nothing is requested.
- Exited rows not actionable: `on_activate` on an EXITED row (Enter, double-click) shows the Warning toast "Process exited" through `ToastQueue::push(Warning, ..)` and does not dispatch `OpenProperties`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** interval 1000 ms and a NEW flag 500 ms old **When** `row_tint` runs **Then** it returns (New, 0.35).
- **Given** a NEW flag 1850 ms old (L = 2000) **When** run with animations on **Then** alpha is between 0 and 0.35 per `ease_out_cubic` at t = 150/300.
- **Given** the same with reduce motion **When** run **Then** alpha is 0.35; at 2000 ms it returns None.
- **Given** interval 250 ms **When** L is computed **Then** it is 1000 ms; interval 5000 ms gives 3000 ms.
- **Given** an exited row **When** rendered **Then** its text uses `text_secondary` and its icon opacity is 0.6.
- **Given** `highlight_new_exited = false` **When** rendered **Then** no tint quad is drawn.
- **Given** no visible row in a fade window **When** a frame ends **Then** no animation frame is requested.
- **Given** Enter on an exited row **When** handled **Then** the toast "Process exited" shows and no Properties action is dispatched.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/cells.rs`: `row_tint`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/delegate.rs`: tint drawing, frame request, exited `on_activate`.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_process_cells.rs`: tests.

## Tests
- `ui_process_cells::highlight_alpha_timeline`: 0.35 until L − 300 ms, 0 at L, the reduce-motion step.
- `ui_process_cells::linger_clamped_1_to_3_s`.
- `ui_process_cells::exited_row_text_and_icon_dimmed`.
- `ui_process_cells::driver_idle_when_no_fade_active`.
- `ui_processes::exited_row_enter_toasts_process_exited`.

## Cross-cutting

- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: the exited state is carried by grey text and the "Process exited" toast and tooltip, not colour alone.
- Performance: one quad per flagged visible row; the animation driver is armed only during fades (≤ 300 ms per row event).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes

- `AnimationDriver` is E19-A1 (`anim.rs`). This dependency is not in the E22 row of 00-epics.md section 4 (open item 5); it adds no cycle.

title: Process row hover tooltip
description:
## Context
The row hover tooltip on the Name cell: command line, path, user, unit, cgroup, package, desktop file and a restricted note, built only when shown. Sources: PROC-039, R-009, PROC-012 (pseudo-row sentences), UI-PRC-012, UI-FND-019 (`TlTooltip::lines`, 560 wide).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/tooltip.rs` (with `pub mod tooltip;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`): `pub fn row_tooltip_lines(row: RowRef, view: &ProcessTableView, out: &mut Vec<(Option<SharedString> /*label*/, SharedString /*value*/)>)` and the delegate's `row_tooltip` returning a `TlTooltip::lines` view.
Lines in this order, each only when it applies (labels `text_secondary`, values `text_primary`, `t_sm` 12, each line its own `div` so it wraps alone):
1. Command line: first 512 characters of `meta.cmdline`, no label. Kernel threads: `[comm]` instead.
2. `path: <exe>`, or `path: restricted` when `meta.exe` is None.
3. `user: <name> (uid N)`.
4. `Unit: <unit> (<Description>)` when the cgroup names a unit (Description from the services data when known, else `Unit: <unit>`).
5. `cgroup: <path>`.
6. `Package: <name> <version>` when known (P2; omitted until the package data exists).
7. `Desktop file: <path>` on app rows only.
8. `Some values need administrator access.` in `status.warning` on rows with any Restricted field.
- Pseudo rows show one line only: Interrupts "CPU time spent in hardware and software interrupts"; Memory compression "Memory held by zram compressed swap devices".
- Group headers: no tooltip.
- Show after 600 ms hover over the Name cell with no mouse button down; hide on mouse-down, on leaving the cell, on scroll and on any key. No grace switching between rows.
- Tooltip box: max width 560, padding `sp4` 8, `menu_bg` fill, 1 px `divider` border, radius `r_sm`.
- Wiring: `.id(("name", node)).tooltip(move |w, cx| ...).tooltip_show_delay(Duration::from_millis(600))` on the Name cell div; the delegate's `row_tooltip` builds the view lazily.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a process row with all fields and no restriction **When** the lines are built **Then** they are lines 1 to 5 in order.
- **Given** an app row **When** built **Then** the Desktop file line is present.
- **Given** a row with a Restricted field **When** built **Then** the last line is "Some values need administrator access." in `status.warning`.
- **Given** a 2,000-character command line **When** built **Then** line 1 has exactly 512 characters.
- **Given** a kernel thread `kworker/0:1` **When** built **Then** line 1 is `[kworker/0:1]`.
- **Given** the Interrupts row **When** built **Then** there is exactly one line, the Interrupts sentence.
- **Given** a hover of 500 ms **When** the pointer stays **Then** no tooltip; at 600 ms it shows.

title: Process action confirmation dialogs
description:
## Context
The process-action confirmation dialogs, in one helper that the Processes page, the Properties windows and Handle Search (E23) call. Every confirmation is a `TlDialog::confirm` window titled "tasklens", width 420, focus on Cancel, Esc cancels. Sources: UI-PRC-014 (texts), UI-PWN-025 (several-targets signal text), PROC-059, PROC-062, PROC-064, PROC-066, PROC-074, PROC-075, PROC-055, R-036, D-009, UI-FND-021, APP-045.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/confirm.rs` (with `pub mod confirm;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub enum ConfirmKind {
    Protected { action: SharedString /*e.g. "End"*/, tree_count: Option<u32> },
    EndTree { count: u32 },
    KillApp { app: SharedString, count: u32 },
    EndMany { count: u32, kill: bool },
    OtherUser { action: SharedString, name: SharedString, pid: u32, user: SharedString, destructive: bool },
    Realtime,
    SignalMany { count: u32, signal_name: SharedString, ends_process: bool },
    LargeDump { name: SharedString, size: SharedString },
    VirusTotalFirstUse,
    Picked { name: SharedString, pid: u32 },
}
pub enum ConfirmResult { Confirmed, Second /* only Picked: Terminate */, Cancelled }
pub fn confirm(kind: ConfirmKind, parent: AnyWindowHandle, cx: &mut App, done: impl FnOnce(ConfirmResult, &mut App) + 'static);
pub fn texts(kind: &ConfirmKind) -> ConfirmTexts; // { title, description, confirm_label, confirm_danger, second: Option<(label, danger)> }
```
Texts (title / description / confirm button / kind):
- Protected: "End <name>?" / "Ending <name> will end your desktop session. End it anyway?" / "End anyway" danger. With `tree_count = Some(N)` the description is "Ending <name> will end your desktop session. End N processes in this tree anyway?" (protected wins over the tree text and keeps N).
- EndTree: "End process tree?" / "End N processes in this tree?" / "End tree" danger.
- KillApp: "Kill <App>?" / "Kill all N processes of <App>?" / "Kill app" danger.
- EndMany (SIGTERM): "End N processes?" / "End N selected processes?" / "End tasks" danger. EndMany (SIGKILL): "End N processes?" / "End N selected processes immediately?" / "End processes" danger.
- OtherUser: "Act on another user's process?" / "<Action> on <name> (PID n), owned by <user>. Continue?" / "<Action label>", danger for End and Kill, primary otherwise.
- Realtime: "Set realtime priority?" / "Realtime priority can freeze the desktop if the process spins. Set it anyway?" / "Set realtime" danger.
- SignalMany: "Send signal to N processes?" / "Send SIG<NAME> to N selected processes?" / "Send signal", danger when the signal ends processes, primary otherwise.
- LargeDump: "Create a large dump?" / "<name> uses 3.4 GiB. The process pauses while the core is written and the file will be about that size. Continue?" / "Create dump" primary.
- VirusTotalFirstUse: "Open VirusTotal?" / "This opens virustotal.com with the file's hash. The file is not uploaded." / "Open" primary.
- Picked: "Picked <name> (PID n)" / "What do you want to do with this process?" / "Select" primary, second "Terminate" danger.
Every dialog: window title "tasklens"; Cancel `TlButton::Secondary` left of the action; destructive dialogs focus Cancel first, non-destructive focus the action button (UI-FND-021); Enter activates the focused button; Tab moves between buttons; Esc cancels; modal to `parent`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** each kind **When** `texts` runs **Then** title, description and labels equal the list above exactly.
- **Given** a protected target and End Process Tree with 7 processes **When** `texts(Protected { tree_count: Some(7) })` runs **Then** the description is "Ending plasmashell will end your desktop session. End 7 processes in this tree anyway?".
- **Given** an EndTree dialog **When** it opens **Then** focus is on Cancel and pressing Enter returns `Cancelled`.
- **Given** an EndTree dialog **When** Tab then Enter **Then** it returns `Confirmed`.
- **Given** a VirusTotalFirstUse dialog **When** it opens **Then** focus is on "Open".
- **Given** any dialog **When** Esc **Then** it returns `Cancelled` and the window closes.
- **Given** a Picked dialog **When** "Terminate" is clicked **Then** it returns `Second`.

title: Process action toast texts and request submission
description:
## Context
The toast texts and kinds for process actions, keyed per request so later states replace the same toast in place. The page builds the texts when it submits an `ActionRequest`; E16's `ActionTracker` shows them as `ActionEvent`s arrive. Sources: UI-PRC-015 (table), PROC-058, PROC-059 (refusals), PROC-060 to PROC-064, PROC-066 to PROC-069, R-035, ADR-005 (event order, ActionTracker, "Outcome unknown"), UI-FND-020 (kinds and durations).

## Deliverable

```rust
pub struct ActionToastTexts {
    pub requested: Option<(ToastKind, SharedString)>, // shown on Started
    pub success: (ToastKind, SharedString),            // final Succeeded for the whole request
    pub failure: (ToastKind, SharedString),            // final Failed when every target failed
    pub partial: Option<fn(done: u32, total: u32, failed: &[(u32, SharedString)]) -> SharedString>, // multi-target mixed result
}
pub fn texts_for(kind: &ActionKind, t: &CapturedTargets) -> ActionToastTexts;
pub fn refusal_text(reason: RejectReason, t: &CapturedTarget) -> Option<SharedString>;
pub fn submit(page: &mut ProcessesPage, req: ActionRequest, texts: ActionToastTexts, cx: &mut Context<ProcessesPage>);
```
`submit` sends `Command::Action(req)` through the client and registers the texts with the E16-A3 `ActionTracker` under `ToastKey(req.id.0)`, so every state of one request replaces one toast.
Texts (kind in brackets; Info 5 s, Success 5 s, Warning 5 s, Error 8 s, with a button 15 s, per UI-FND-020):
- End Task single: requested "End task requested." [Info]; success "Process terminated" [Success]; failure "Could not end task." [Error].
- End Process single: "End process requested." [Info]; "Process terminated" [Success]; "Could not end process." [Error].
- End Process Tree: "End process tree requested." [Info]; "Process tree terminated" [Success]; partial result in one toast.
- End Task or End Process with 2+ targets: requested "End task requested for selected processes." [Info]; result "Ended 4 of 5 processes (1 permission denied)" [Warning when any failed, else Success].
- Suspend / Resume: "Process suspended." / "Process resumed." [Success].
- Freeze App / Thaw App / Kill App: "App frozen" / "App thawed" / "App killed" [Success].
- Priority single: "Priority updated" [Success]. Multi: all ok "Selected process priority updated." [Success]; all failed "Could not update selected process priority." [Error]; partial "Priority updated for 3 of 4 processes. 1 failed: permission denied" [Warning].
- Affinity: single "Affinity updated" [Success]; multi all ok "Selected process affinity updated." [Success]; failure "Could not update selected process affinity." [Error]; partial in the priority form with "Affinity updated for …".
- I/O priority: single "I/O priority updated" [Success]; multi "Selected process I/O priority updated." [Success]; failure "Could not update selected process I/O priority." [Error]; partial "I/O priority updated for …".
- Identity mismatch (`Rejected(IdentityChanged)`): "The selected process changed; wait for the list to update and try again." [Warning].
- EPERM (`Failed` with the permission-denied `ActionError`): "Permission denied" [Error] (the P3 "Retry as administrator" button is E22-040).
- Outcome unknown: "Outcome unknown" [Warning] (the tracker's deadline + 5 s rule, ADR-005).
- Refusals, no dialog, no request sent (`refusal_text`, PROC-059): `IS_SELF` "Refusing to end tasklens itself."; PID 1 "PID 1 (systemd) cannot be ended."; `KERNEL_THREAD` "Kernel threads cannot be signalled." [Warning each].
- Exited row activated: "Process exited" [Warning].
- Partial reason text: "permission denied" for the permission `ActionError`; for any other error the reason is the first sentence of `ActionTracker::message(&err)` in lower case without the full stop. Several reasons join with ", " in the order of first occurrence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** End Task on one process **When** `texts_for` runs **Then** requested is (Info, "End task requested.") and success is (Success, "Process terminated").
- **Given** End Task on 5 targets with 4 Succeeded and 1 EPERM **When** the summary arrives **Then** one toast reads "Ended 4 of 5 processes (1 permission denied)" as Warning, replacing the "End task requested for selected processes." toast in place.
- **Given** a priority change on 4 targets with 3 ok and 1 EPERM **When** done **Then** the toast is "Priority updated for 3 of 4 processes. 1 failed: permission denied".
- **Given** a target with `IS_SELF` **When** `refusal_text` runs **Then** it is "Refusing to end tasklens itself." and no request is sent.
- **Given** `Rejected(IdentityChanged)` **When** the event arrives **Then** the toast text is "The selected process changed; wait for the list to update and try again.".
- **Given** two requests in flight **When** their events interleave **Then** each updates only its own toast (keys `ToastKey(id.0)` differ).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/toasts.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: add the `mod` line.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_process_menu.rs`: tests.

## Tests
- `ui_process_menu::toast_texts_match_spec`: string table over every row above.
- `ui_process_menu::action_toast_replaces_in_place_per_request`.
- `ui_process_menu::multi_target_result_counts_and_reasons`.
- `ui_process_menu::refusals_send_no_request`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: every failure path has a toast; nothing fails silently.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: text first, icon second; colour never carries the meaning alone.
- Performance: at most 4 visible toasts and a 16-entry wait list (UI-FND-020).
- Privacy: action logs record kind, target PID and result only (ADR-015); toast texts hold names and PIDs, never command lines.

## Notes
- `ToastQueue`, `ToastKind`, `ToastKey` are E16-A2; `ActionTracker` and `message(&ActionError)` are E16-A3. If E16-A3's submission API has another name, use it and keep these texts.
- The reason wording for failures other than permission denied is open item 6 in docs/plan/b8-ui-tables.md.
- `ActionId` allocation: the E16 `AtomicU64` starting at 1 (ADR-005).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, check, clippy or test through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_processes` (it takes the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope; the wait can be long, so run it in the background when your tool call has a timeout). On an OOM kill (exit 137) retry once, then report.
- Strings: every user-visible string in this bead is appended to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` in this bead (R-132), key `processes-<entry>-<slug>` (for example `processes-menu-end-task`), and read through `tr(key)` / `tr_args(key, args)` from `src/i18n.rs`. The English text in this bead is the value, exactly.

and the delegate's `context_menu` (E22-009) calling them after storing `targets` in `ProcessesPage.menu_targets`.

P1 items in order (P = process row, M = 2+ rows; hidden = not built; disabled items keep a tooltip):
1. "End Task" (M: "End Selected Tasks") → `EndTask`; app and unit rows in P1: "End App" → `EndTask`.
2. "End Process" (M: "End Selected Processes") → `EndProcess`; hidden on app and unit rows in P1. Tooltip "Ends the process immediately (SIGKILL)".

— separator —

6. "Set Priority >" submenu (same label on app and unit rows, tooltip "Applies to the app's current processes"): first line a disabled `text_secondary` item "With autogroup on, nice only orders processes within the same session.", then "High", "Above normal", "Normal", "Below normal", "Low" → `SetPriority { class }`; a check mark (Lucide `check` 14 px, left side) on the current class, on multi-select only when every target shares it.
— separator —
11. "Copy" → `CopyCell { col: clicked_col }` (built only when `clicked_col` is Some).
12. "Copy details" → `CopyDetails`.
13. "Copy all metrics" → `CopyAllMetrics`.
14. "Copy rows as table" → `CopyRowsAsTable`.
— separator —
21. "Open file location" → `OpenFileLocation`; P only (hidden on app, unit, M); disabled with tooltip "Executable deleted" when `exe_deleted` (E22-020).
— separator —
24. "Go to parent process" → `GoToParent`; P only; hidden when ppid is 0.
Rules:
- Exited rows (any target EXITED): every item disabled with tooltip "Process exited" except 11 to 14.
- Pseudo rows: only items 11, 12, 13.
- Kernel-thread rows: items as a process row (actions refuse with a toast).
- Protected targets keep the same labels (the confirmation warns).
- Group header rows: `group_header_menu` with one item "Expand" or "Collapse" → `ToggleExpand`.
- Right-click on an unselected row selects it first (E18); right-click inside the selection keeps it. Shift+F10 and the Menu key open the menu at the focus row's Name cell (E18 `OpenContextMenu`).
- Submenus open on hover after 150 ms or on Right / Enter. Esc closes and returns focus to the table.

title: End Task, End Process and End Process Tree handlers
description:
## Context
Handlers for End Task (SIGTERM), End Process (SIGKILL) and End Process Tree on process, app and unit rows: target capture, refusals, confirmations and the request. Keys and menu items dispatch the same actions (E22-026, E22-A2). Sources: PROC-001, PROC-010 (bwrap unwrap), PROC-058, PROC-059, PROC-060, PROC-061, PROC-062, PROC-069 (multi End), R-034 to R-037, D-009, ADR-005 (ActionRequest), ADR-006 (KillTree), UI-PRC-013, UI-PRC-014, UI-PRC-015.

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/mod.rs` (`ProcessesPage`):
- `pub fn capture_targets(&self, clicked_col: Option<ColumnId>, cx: &App) -> CapturedTargets`: the selection set in current view order, group headers excluded, at most 256 items (`truncated` set beyond that), built from the shown (or paused) snapshot.
- `menu_targets: Option<CapturedTargets>`: set by the row menu when it opens (E22-A2); a handler uses and clears it, else calls `capture_targets(None, cx)`.
- `.on_action` handlers for `EndTask`, `EndProcess`, `EndProcessTree`, each running these steps:
  1. Targets empty: do nothing. Pseudo rows are dropped. Exited targets are dropped; if every target was exited, Warning toast "Process exited" and stop.
  2. Refusals (no dialog, no request; one toast per distinct reason, E22-016 `refusal_text`): `IS_SELF` "Refusing to end tasklens itself."; pid 1 "PID 1 (systemd) cannot be ended."; `KERNEL_THREAD` "Kernel threads cannot be signalled.". Refused targets are dropped; stop if none remain.
  3. Targets: process rows give `ActionTarget::Process(key)`. App and unit rows (End Task only) give their primary processes: members whose ppid is not a member; a primary whose exe basename is `bwrap` is replaced by its first non-bwrap descendant (PROC-010, walking `ProcessSnapshot.records` by ppid). App and unit rows are skipped by End Process until E22-035 adds Kill App.
  4. End Process Tree: target set = the selected process plus every descendant found by walking `ProcessSnapshot.records` by ppid from the root's pid (matching each parent by pid among non-exited records), capped at 256 keys.
  5. Confirmation (E22-015), first matching rule wins: any target `PROTECTED` → `Protected { action: "End", tree_count }` (tree_count = Some(N) for End Process Tree); End Process Tree → `EndTree { count: N }`; 2+ targets → `EndMany { count, kill }`; any target `OTHER_USER` → `OtherUser { action: "End task" or "End process", name, pid, user, destructive: true }`. No dialog for one own, unprotected target (D-009). Cancel sends nothing.
  6. Request: `ActionRequest { id: next ActionId, kind, targets, privileged: false }` with `kind` = `Signal(Term)` (End Task), `Signal(Kill)` (End Process), `KillTree` (End Process Tree), sent through E22-016 `submit` with `texts_for`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** one own unprotected process selected **When** `EndProcess` is dispatched **Then** no dialog opens and one request `Signal(Kill)` with one target is sent; the toast reads "End process requested.".
- **Given** a `PROTECTED` target (plasmashell) **When** `EndTask` **Then** the Protected dialog opens; Cancel sends nothing.
- **Given** 3 own processes selected **When** `EndTask` **Then** the EndMany dialog "End 3 processes?" opens; confirming sends one request with 3 targets.
- **Given** the tasklens process selected **When** `EndTask` **Then** the toast "Refusing to end tasklens itself." shows and nothing is sent.
- **Given** a process with 7 descendants **When** `EndProcessTree` **Then** the EndTree dialog says "End 8 processes in this tree?" and the request is `KillTree` with 8 targets.
- **Given** an app row whose primary is `bwrap` with child `firefox` **When** `EndTask` **Then** the request targets firefox's key, not bwrap's.
- **Given** an other-user process **When** `EndTask` **Then** the OtherUser dialog opens with "End task on <name> (PID n), owned by <user>. Continue?".
- **Given** the menu captured target X and the rows moved before the click **When** the item runs **Then** the request targets X's key.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: `capture_targets`, `menu_targets`, three handlers.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_process_menu.rs`: tests.

## Tests
- `ui_process_menu::single_end_process_own_unprotected_has_no_dialog` (D-009).
- `ui_process_menu::protected_target_confirms`.
- `ui_process_menu::multi_end_confirms_with_count`.
- `ui_process_menu::refusals_self_pid1_kthread`.
- `ui_process_menu::end_tree_collects_descendants_capped_256`.
- `ui_process_menu::end_app_unwraps_bwrap`.
- `ui_process_menu::row_menu_targets_captured_on_open`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: refusals and failures show the E22-016 toasts.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: keyboard path Delete / Ctrl+E and Shift+Delete / Ctrl+X (E22-026); dialogs focus Cancel.
- Performance: descendant walk O(records) once per action; no work per frame.
- Privacy: requests carry keys only; logs record kind, PID and result (ADR-015).
- Security: identity is captured as `ProcessKey` and revalidated by the engine before acting (PROC-001, ADR-006); the UI never signals by bare PID.

## Notes
- The rule order of step 5 and the descendant walk are open items 7 and 8 in docs/plan/b8-ui-tables.md (recommended as written here).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, check, clippy or test through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_processes` (it takes the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope; the wait can be long, so run it in the background when your tool call has a timeout). On an OOM kill (exit 137) retry once, then report.

The English text in this bead is the value, exactly.
