title: Suspend, Resume and Set Priority nice-class handlers
description:
## Context
Handlers for Suspend Process, Resume Process and the P1 Set Priority classes (High, Above normal, Normal, Below normal, Low) on process rows and multi-selections, plus nice classes on app rows. Sources: PROC-063, PROC-066 (nice classes), PROC-069 (multi priority), PROC-059 (confirmations), R-034, R-038, ADR-006 (SetNice on every TID, Suspend and Resume through the pidfd), UI-PRC-013 item 4 and 6, UI-PRC-015.

## Deliverable
`.on_action` handlers in `pages/processes/mod.rs` for `SuspendProcess`, `ResumeProcess` and `SetPriority { class }`, using `capture_targets` / `menu_targets` (E22-017):
- Common steps 1 and 2 of E22-017 (drop pseudo and exited targets; refusals: `IS_SELF` "Refusing to end tasklens itself." applies to Suspend only; PID 1 "PID 1 (systemd) cannot be ended." applies to Suspend only; `KERNEL_THREAD` "Kernel threads cannot be signalled." applies to Suspend and Resume).
- Suspend / Resume: `ActionKind::Suspend` / `ActionKind::Resume`, one `ActionTarget::Process` per target. Confirmation: `PROTECTED` target → `Protected { action: "Suspend", tree_count: None }`; `OTHER_USER` target → `OtherUser { action: "Suspend" or "Resume", destructive: false }`. No confirmation for own processes, even with several targets. App and unit rows are skipped (Freeze App is E22-035).
- Set Priority High, AboveNormal, Normal, BelowNormal, Low: `ActionKind::SetNice(class.nice())` with nice -10, -5, 0, 5, 19. Targets: process rows; app and unit rows expand to every current member process ("Applies to the app's current processes"). Confirmation only for `OTHER_USER` targets (`OtherUser { action: "Set priority", destructive: false }`). Realtime and Idle are E22-036; Custom… is E23's.
- Toasts through E22-016: "Process suspended.", "Process resumed.", "Priority updated", multi "Selected process priority updated.", "Could not update selected process priority.", partial "Priority updated for 3 of 4 processes. 1 failed: permission denied".
- Menu label rule data for E22-A2: `fn suspend_or_resume(t: &CapturedTargets) -> SuspendLabel` returning `Resume` when every target has State T, else `Suspend` (multi: "Resume Selected Tasks" only when every target is stopped).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a running own process **When** `SuspendProcess` **Then** one request `Suspend` is sent with no dialog and the success toast is "Process suspended.".
- **Given** two stopped and one running process **When** `suspend_or_resume` runs **Then** it returns Suspend.
- **Given** two stopped processes **When** it runs **Then** it returns Resume.
- **Given** an app row with 3 members **When** `SetPriority { High }` **Then** one request `SetNice(-10)` with 3 process targets is sent.
- **Given** a kernel thread **When** `SuspendProcess` **Then** the toast "Kernel threads cannot be signalled." shows and nothing is sent.
- **Given** an other-user target **When** `SetPriority { Low }` **Then** the OtherUser dialog opens with the primary (not danger) button "Set priority".

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: three handlers, `suspend_or_resume`.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_process_menu.rs`: tests.

## Tests
- `ui_process_menu::suspend_resume_requests_and_toasts`.
- `ui_process_menu::suspend_or_resume_label_rule`.
- `ui_process_menu::priority_classes_map_to_nice`.
- `ui_process_menu::priority_app_row_targets_members`.
- `ui_process_menu::kthread_suspend_refused`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: EPERM shows "Permission denied" (E22-016); lowering nice needs CAP_SYS_NICE (PROC-066).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: menu items and their keys reach every handler.
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A
- Security: identities revalidated by the engine; no bare-PID calls from the UI.

- Priority partial results arrive as `Failed(Partial { done, total })` or per-target events (PROC-066, ADR-005); the E22-016 partial text uses the per-target final states.

title: Process copy commands: Copy, Copy details, Copy all metrics, Copy rows as table
description:
## Context
The four copy commands of the process table: Copy (clicked cell), Copy details (Ctrl+C), Copy all metrics and Copy rows as table (Ctrl+Shift+C). They work on exited rows too. Sources: PROC-070, R-012, R-091, R-094, ADR-015 (deliberate export; command lines only in Copy all metrics and the Command line cell), UI-PRC-011 (copy enabled on exited rows), UI-PRC-015 (copy toasts).

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/cells.rs`: pure text builders
```rust
pub fn copy_cell(rows: &[RowRef], col: &ProcColumn, ctx: &CellCtx) -> String;     // one displayed value per line, view order
pub fn copy_details(rows: &[RowRef], ctx: &CellCtx) -> String;                     // fixed block per row, blank line between rows
pub fn copy_all_metrics(rows: &[RowRef], ctx: &CellCtx) -> String;                 // Label: value lines, picker order, ending "Command line: …"
pub fn copy_rows_as_table(rows: &[RowRef], visible: &[ColumnId], ctx: &CellCtx) -> String; // TSV with a header line of labels
```
and in `pages/processes/mod.rs` `.on_action` handlers for E18's shared `CopyCell { col }`, `CopyDetails`, `CopyRowsAsTable` and this page's `CopyAllMetrics`, writing with `cx.write_to_clipboard(ClipboardItem::new_string(text))` and toasting.
Copy details block (exact field order and labels):
```
Name: firefox
PID: 4321
Parent PID: 2010
CPU: 3.27%
Memory: 812 MiB
Private bytes: 1490 MiB
Working set: 1104 MiB
Threads: 97
Handles: 412
Priority: Normal (0)
```
CPU is `%.2f%%` of the whole machine (R-094, the only two-decimal percent). Memory is RssAnon, Private bytes is VmData + VmStk, Working set is VmRSS, each in whole MiB (bytes / 1 048 576 rounded to the nearest integer). Handles is the fd count. Priority is the PROC-029 class with the nice value in parentheses. A Restricted value prints "restricted", an Unsupported one "n/a"; never 0.
Copy all metrics: per row one `Label: value` line for every registry column (E22-002 order) whose value is Valid, using the cell's displayed text, then `Command line: <full cmdline>` last; rows separated by a blank line. Environment values are never included.
Copy rows as table: header line of the visible column labels joined by tab, then one line per row of the displayed cell texts joined by tab; Restricted cells "restricted", Unsupported "n/a", other non-Valid cells empty.
Toasts (Success, E22-016 queue): Copy one row "Copied to clipboard", several rows "Selected process values copied."; Copy details "Process details copied."; Copy all metrics one row "Copied metrics to clipboard", several "Selected process metrics copied."; Copy rows as table "Copied to clipboard".
Targets: the captured targets (E22-017), group headers excluded; exited rows included.

- **Given** the fixture row above **When** `copy_details` runs **Then** the output equals `tests/golden/copy_details.txt` byte for byte.
- **Given** two rows **When** `copy_details` runs **Then** the blocks are separated by exactly one blank line.
- **Given** a Restricted Handles value **When** `copy_details` runs **Then** the line is `Handles: restricted`.
- **Given** a row with a command line **When** `copy_all_metrics` runs **Then** the last line starts with `Command line: ` and no line contains environment data.
- **Given** 3 selected rows and right-click on the CPU cell **When** Copy runs **Then** the clipboard has 3 lines and the toast is "Selected process values copied.".
- **Given** visible columns name, pid, cpu **When** `copy_rows_as_table` runs **Then** the first line is `Name\tPID\tCPU`.

title: Process filter binding, Include children and no-match state
description:
## Context
The Processes tab's side of the shell filter box: 100 ms debounce into `SetTableQuery`, the "Include children" checkbox visibility and toasts, and the no-match empty state with "Clear filter". The input itself, Esc, Enter, Ctrl+F and type-to-filter routing are the shell's (E20-A2). Sources: PROC-044, PROC-045, R-043, APP-028, UI-PRC-016, UI-PRC-024, UI-SHL-024, UI-SHL-025, ADR-009 (generations).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/filter.rs` (with `pub mod filter;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`):
- `pub struct FilterBinding { debounce: Option<Task<()>> }`: subscribes in `ProcessesPage::new` to the shell `FilterChanged { tab: Processes, text }` event (UI-SHL-024). Each event drops the previous task and starts a new one that waits 100 ms on the foreground executor timer, then lowercases the text (`str::to_lowercase`) and calls `ProcessQuery::set_filter` and `bump_and_send` (E22-008). Five keystrokes within 100 ms send one query.
- The table keeps showing the previous rows until the view with the matching generation arrives (E22-008 `accept`).
- Include children: `pub fn include_children_visible(filter_nonempty: bool, mode: TableMode) -> bool` = `filter_nonempty || mode == Tree`; the page reports it to the shell's checkbox slot (UI-SHL-025). Toggling dispatches `ToggleSetting(ProcessesFilterIncludeChildren)` (E20); this page observes `processes.filter_include_children` and pushes the Info toast "Including filtered process children." when it turns on and "Hiding unmatched filtered process children." when it turns off.
- Empty state (UI-PRC-024): when the shown view has zero rows and the filter is non-empty, the delegate's `empty_text` returns "No processes match the filter" and the table shows the E15 `TlEmptyState` centred horizontally at y = 96 from the body top, text `t_base` `text_secondary`, with a `TlButton::Secondary` "Clear filter" that dispatches `ClearFilter` (E20). Group headers are not shown when nothing matches at all; when some group matches, a group with zero matches shows "(0)" with no children (engine output, drawn as is).
- History mode: the same filter applies to the History table (E30 reads the same text).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** five characters typed within 80 ms **When** 100 ms pass after the last **Then** exactly one `SetTableQuery` is sent with the lowercased text and a new generation.
- **Given** a filter "FiReFox" **When** sent **Then** `TableQuery.filter` is "firefox".
- **Given** filter text and Grouped mode **When** visibility is computed **Then** the checkbox is visible; empty filter in Flat mode **Then** hidden; empty filter in Tree mode **Then** visible.
- **Given** the include-children setting turns on **When** observed **Then** the toast "Including filtered process children." shows.
- **Given** a filter that matches nothing **When** the view arrives **Then** "No processes match the filter" and the "Clear filter" button show and no group header row is drawn.
- **Given** "Clear filter" is pressed **When** handled **Then** `ClearFilter` is dispatched.

title: Hold Ctrl to pause the process table
description:
## Context
Hold Ctrl to pause: while Ctrl is held and the main window is active, the process table freezes rows, order, values and header totals; collection keeps running. Sources: PROC-050, R-042, ADR-009 Ctrl-pause, ADR-005 (at most one extra retained snapshot), UI-PRC-017, UI-PRC-010 (anchoring once on resume).

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/mod.rs`:
- Field `paused: Option<Arc<Snapshot>>` and `pub fn is_paused(&self) -> bool`.
- `window.on_modifiers_changed` (registered once in `new`): pause starts when `modifiers.control` becomes true with no other modifier held and `window.is_window_active()`; it ends when `control` becomes false. `cx.observe_window_activation` ends the pause when the window deactivates.
- On pause start: `paused = Some(current snapshot Arc)`; the delegate draws from it; hub changes are ignored (no table notify). Opening a menu or dialog does not end the pause.
- On pause end: `paused = None`; the delegate takes the latest hub snapshot and accepted view, notifies the table once, and E18's scroll anchoring runs once.
- Actions started while paused capture targets from the paused snapshot (E22-017 `capture_targets` reads the delegate's snapshot); the engine revalidates identities.
- The page emits `StatusChanged` on pause start and end so the shell's status chip appends " [PAUSED - Ctrl]" in `accent` (UI-SHL-050 draws it).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the window is active **When** Ctrl goes down **Then** `is_paused()` is true and a new snapshot with changed rows does not change the rendered rows.
- **Given** Ctrl+Shift down **When** handled **Then** no pause starts.
- **Given** paused **When** Ctrl goes up **Then** the table renders the latest view once.
- **Given** paused **When** the window deactivates **Then** the pause ends.
- **Given** paused and the row menu opened **When** End Task is chosen **Then** the request targets the paused snapshot's identity.
- **Given** paused **When** five snapshots arrive **Then** the table render count does not increase.

title: Processes status chip text
description:
## Context
The Processes tab's text in the shell's floating status chip: counts, filtered counts, selection size, the restricted count. Sources: PROC-051, PROC-048, PROC-050, PROC-076, UI-PRC-018, UI-SHL-050 (chip, `status_text`, `StatusChanged`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/status.rs` (with `pub mod status;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`) and `ProcessesPage::status_text(&self, out: &mut String)` per the UI-SHL-050 page method, emitting `StatusChanged` when the text changes:
- Segment 1: "296 Processes" (no filter) or "41 / 296 Processes" (filter set). The count excludes pseudo rows and includes kernel threads only when they are shown.
- Segment 2, 2 or more selected rows: " | 3 processes selected" (selected identities hidden by the filter are not counted).
- Segment 3, paused: drawn by the shell from `is_paused()` (" [PAUSED - Ctrl]" in `accent`); not written here.
- Segment 4, restricted rows exist: " | 42 restricted", plain text before P3 with tooltip "Some values for other users' processes need administrator rights." (the clickable P3 form is E22-041).
- Separators " | " drawn `text_secondary`, text `t_sm` 12 `text_primary` (shell).
- Counts (`total`, `shown`, `restricted`) come from the accepted `ProcessTableView` fields of that meaning (E03-A2).
- The text is rebuilt only when a count, the filter state or the selection size changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 296 processes and no filter **When** `status_text` runs **Then** it is "296 Processes".
- **Given** a filter showing 41 **When** run **Then** it is "41 / 296 Processes".
- **Given** 3 selected rows **When** run **Then** " | 3 processes selected" is appended.
- **Given** 1 selected row **When** run **Then** no selection segment.
- **Given** 42 restricted rows **When** run **Then** " | 42 restricted" is appended and its tooltip is the pre-P3 text.
- **Given** 2 pseudo rows and hidden kernel threads **When** counted **Then** neither is in segment 1.

title: E22-A3 Jump target: ProcessesPage::select_by_key
description:
## Context
Anchor E22-A3. The Processes tab's one "select process by identity" entry point, used by Go to parent, the Properties PPID link, Services and Connections "Jump to process", Handle Search "Go to process", the window picker, the History table, `--select-pid` and D-Bus `select-pid`. It switches to the tab, leaves History mode, expands the path, selects the row and centres it, or explains why it cannot. Sources: PROC-071, PROC-055 (picker result), PROC-088 (History row), UI-PRC-022, UI-PRC-010 (centre scroll), UI-PRC-015 (jump toasts and "Show" button), SYS-010, SYS-033.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/jump.rs` (with `pub mod jump;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub struct JumpTexts {
    pub switched_tab: Option<SharedString>, // shown when the tab changed; None = "Switched to Processes tab"
    pub success: Option<SharedString>,      // caller's success toast, replaces switched_tab when set (e.g. "Switched to owning process.")
    pub not_found: SharedString,            // default "Process not found in current view"
    pub hidden: Option<SharedString>,       // caller's "not visible" text; None = not_found text; always shown with a "Show" button
}
impl Default for JumpTexts { /* switched_tab None, success None, not_found "Process not found in current view", hidden None */ }
impl ProcessesPage {
    pub fn select_by_key(&mut self, key: ProcessKey, texts: JumpTexts, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>);
    pub fn select_by_pid(&mut self, pid: u32, texts: JumpTexts, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>); // resolves pid to the current non-exited record's key, then select_by_key; no record: not_found toast
}
```
Steps of `select_by_key`:
1. If the Processes tab is not active, dispatch E20's `SelectTab` for Processes; remember that the tab changed. If `UiState.processes.history_mode` is true, set it false (the live table is the only place a live identity can be shown).
2. Look the key up in the current `ProcessSnapshot.records`. Absent or EXITED: Warning toast `not_found`; stop.
3. Present but not in the current view (filtered out or hidden by Hide system processes): Warning toast `hidden.unwrap_or(not_found)` with a `ToastAction { label: "Show", action: ProcessesShowHidden }`. The page stores the pending key. On "Show": clear the filter (E20 FilterBox clear), set `processes.hide_system = false`, wait for the view with the matching generation, then continue at step 4.
4. Expand the path: in Grouped mode the record's group header and every collapsed ancestor; in Tree mode every collapsed ancestor (ancestors by ppid walk over the records). One `ProcessQuery::expand_path` and one `SetTableQuery`; the page keeps `pending_jump: Option<(ProcessKey, JumpTexts, bool /*tab changed*/)>`.
5. When a view with a matching generation contains the row: selection = {key} (anchor and focus = key), `scroll_to_item_strict(ix, ScrollStrategy::Center)`, focus the table. Toast (Info): `success`, else `switched_tab` or "Switched to Processes tab" when the tab changed, else no toast.
6. If the matching view still lacks the row: Warning toast `not_found`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the Services tab is active and a process inside a collapsed app in Grouped mode **When** `select_by_key` runs **Then** the tab becomes Processes, the app row is expanded, the row is selected, centred, the table focused, and the toast reads "Switched to Processes tab".
- **Given** a caller success text "Switched to owning process." **When** the jump succeeds from another tab **Then** that text is the only toast.
- **Given** a key whose process exited **When** called **Then** the toast is "Process not found in current view".
- **Given** a process hidden by the filter "foo" **When** called with hidden text "Owning process not visible in the current view." **Then** that toast shows with a "Show" button; pressing Show clears the filter, keeps hide_system false, and selects the row when the matching view arrives.
- **Given** History mode is on **When** called **Then** `history_mode` becomes false.
- **Given** Tree mode with two collapsed ancestors **When** called **Then** one query is sent whose `expanded` contains both.
- **Given** pid 4321 with a live record **When** `select_by_pid(4321, ..)` **Then** it behaves as `select_by_key` with that record's key.

title: Process table meets the table-2000 performance gate
description:
## Context
Performance gate for the production process table: with highlight, tooltips and every P1 cell in place, the ADR-014 `table-2000` scene must still pass. Sources: ADR-014 (`table-2000` gate: UI thread p99 ≤ 2.0 ms per frame while scrolling at 1,200 px/s with 1 Hz value changes and re-sorts; 0 missed frames in the median run; RSS ≤ 150 MB; a regression above 20 % blocks the phase), UI-PRC-023 (budget split, rules 1 to 8, in-GPUI fallback order), PROC-013, ADR-009 text cache.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_processes.rs`: an allocation and cache test using the FakeEngine with the E01 seed-42 synthetic 2,000-row source:
  - `CellTextCache` hit rate above 95 % over 10 identical table versions;
  - zero `CellOut` text writes for unchanged cells across two installs of the same values;
  - at most 27 row elements built per frame in a 720 px viewport;
  - no element id on metric cells (only row hitbox, Name cell and window button ids).
- Run `tasklens --bench table-2000 --duration 30 --warmup 5 --json out.json` three times through `cargo xtask bench` (E01-A1) and record p50, p99, missed frames and RSS in the commit message.
- If the gate fails, apply the in-GPUI fallback in this order and re-measure after each step, in the E22 page files only: (1) column culling: the row builder skips columns whose `[x, x + w)` misses the viewport (if E18 does not already); (2) merge heat quads per row into one quad with the max alpha; (3) drop zebra quads for one `list_bg` fill plus 1 px row dividers; (4) report to the leader with the numbers if it still fails (ADR-014 decision rule, no further change here).

- **Given** two installs with equal values **When** rendered **Then** no cell text is formatted.

title: App row window title as secondary text
description:
## Context
App rows show the title of the app's most recently active window as dimmed secondary text after the name, when the KWin bridge is up. Sources: PROC-008, PROC-053, UI-PRC-003 (secondary text rules), ADR-004 KWin bridge, `WindowsSnapshot`.

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/name_cell.rs` and `delegate.rs`: `NameCellData` gains `secondary: Option<SharedString>`. For app rows, the delegate looks up the member PIDs in `Snapshot.windows` and uses the caption of the most recently active window (the entry order or activation field E14 provides). Rendering: after an `sp4` 8 px gap on the same line, `t_base` regular `text_secondary` (selected: `text_selected_secondary`), ellipsis shared with the primary text so the primary text never truncates before the secondary text is gone; the secondary text is hidden entirely when the cell is narrower than primary text width + 8 + 40 px. No bridge (`windows` validity Unsupported): no secondary text. The delegate's name cache stores `(primary, secondary)` and re-shapes only when either string changes; the page re-renders on `ComponentMask::WINDOWS`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** Firefox with a window "Mozilla Firefox - Inbox" **When** rendered at 400 px **Then** the Name cell reads "Firefox (14)" then "Mozilla Firefox - Inbox" in `text_secondary`.
- **Given** a cell narrower than primary + 48 px **When** rendered **Then** the secondary text is not drawn.
- **Given** a narrow cell that fits primary + 48 but not both texts **When** rendered **Then** the secondary text is ellipsised and the primary text is whole.
- **Given** no bridge **When** rendered **Then** no secondary text.

description:
## Context

- `pages/processes/mod.rs` handlers:
  - Target per app or unit row: `ActionTarget::Cgroup(CgroupRef)` when the group's cgroup is under `user@<uid>.service/app.slice/`; `ActionTarget::Unit(UnitRef)` for every other unit (R-092). The refs come from the `GroupRow` fields of that meaning.

title: Retry as administrator on permission-denied toasts
description:
## Context
P3: the "Retry as administrator" button on process-action toasts that failed with EPERM. It re-sends the same request with `privileged = true` for the failed targets only, which the engine routes to the helper (E29). Sources: PROC-058, R-035, UI-PRC-015 (button rows), ADR-005 (`privileged`), ADR-006 helper boundary.

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/toasts.rs`: when a request's final state has one or more targets with the permission-denied `ActionError`, the result toast gets `ToastAction { label: "Retry as administrator", action: RetryPrivileged { request: ActionId } }` (data action declared here with namespace `tasklens`). The page keeps the last 16 requests' `ActionRequest`s in a ring (`VecDeque`, capacity 16) for this purpose. The handler builds a new `ActionRequest` with a new `ActionId`, the same `kind`, only the EPERM targets, and `privileged: true`, and submits it with the same texts. Toasts with a button stay 15 s (UI-FND-020). No automatic retry ever.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** End Task on 5 targets with 1 EPERM **When** the summary toast shows **Then** it has the button "Retry as administrator".
- **Given** the button is pressed **When** handled **Then** one request with 1 target and `privileged: true` is sent, with a new id.
- **Given** a failure that is not EPERM **When** the toast shows **Then** no button.
- **Given** a request older than the 16 kept **When** its button is pressed **Then** nothing is sent and the toast closes.

title: Processes page Actions and captured target types
description:
## Context
Declares every Processes-page GPUI Action and the captured-target types that the row menu, the keymap and the handlers share. One command is one Action: key binding, menu item and toolbar button dispatch the same Action (table b, PROC-013, PROC-057). Shared table actions (`OpenProperties`, `CopyCell { col }`, `CopyDetails`, `CopyRowsAsTable`, `SelectAll`, `CollapseAll`, `ToggleExpand`, `OpenContextMenu`, `MoveFocus*`) belong to E18 `table/actions.rs`; window-level actions (`FocusFilter`, `ClearFilter`, `ToggleHideSystem`, `CycleViewMode`, `SetViewMode`, `ToggleSetting`, `StartHelperSession`) belong to E20 `actions.rs` (docs/ui/INDEX.md "Actions"). Sources: UI-PRC-009, UI-PRC-013, UI-PRC-020, PROC-001, R-128, ADR-005, ADR-009.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/actions.rs`, plus the line `pub mod actions;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`.

Unit actions via `gpui::actions!(tasklens, [ ... ])`:
`EndTask`, `EndProcess`, `EndProcessTree`, `KillApp`, `SuspendProcess`, `ResumeProcess`, `FreezeApp`, `ThawApp`, `ShowWindow`, `CopyAllMetrics`, `FileProperties`, `OpenFileLocation`, `OpenVirusTotal`, `CreateDump`, `GoToParent`, `ProcessesShowHidden`.

Data actions (`#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Deserialize, JsonSchema, Action)] #[action(namespace = tasklens)]`):
- `SetPriority { class: PriorityClass }` with `pub enum PriorityClass { Realtime, High, AboveNormal, Normal, BelowNormal, Low, Idle }` and `fn nice(self) -> Option<i8>`: High -10, AboveNormal -5, Normal 0, BelowNormal 5, Low 19; Realtime and Idle return None (they map to `SetSched`, see E22-036).
- `SetIoPriorityClass { class: IoClass }` with `pub enum IoClass { Realtime, High, Normal, Low, Idle, Default }` and `fn to_model(self) -> tl_model::actions::IoPriority`: Realtime -> `Realtime(0)`, High -> `BestEffort(0)`, Normal -> `BestEffort(4)`, Low -> `BestEffort(7)`, Idle -> `Idle`, Default -> `None` (PROC-068, R-093).
- `RestartUnit { unit: tl_model::table::UnitRef }`.
- `ActivateWindow { internal_id: SharedString }`.

Captured targets (PROC-001: captured when the menu opens or the key is pressed, max 256):
```rust
pub const MAX_TARGETS: usize = 256;
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct CapturedTarget {
    pub node: NodeId,               // identity, never an index
    pub kind: RowKind,              // App | Unit | Process | KernelThread | Pseudo (never GroupHeader)
    pub name: SharedString,         // display name as drawn in the Name cell, without the " (N)" count
    pub pid: Option<u32>,           // None for app, unit and pseudo rows
    pub uid: u32,
    pub user: SharedString,
    pub flags: ProcFlags,           // NEW, EXITED, KERNEL_THREAD, OTHER_USER, IS_SELF, PROTECTED
    pub member_count: u32,          // processes of an app or unit row, 1 for a process row
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct CapturedTargets {
    pub items: SmallVec<[CapturedTarget; 1]>,  // view order, at most MAX_TARGETS
    pub clicked_col: Option<ColumnId>,         // column under the pointer at right-click; None from the keyboard
    pub truncated: bool,                       // true when the selection had more than MAX_TARGETS rows
}
impl CapturedTargets {
    pub fn is_multi(&self) -> bool;          // items.len() >= 2
    pub fn any_exited(&self) -> bool;        // any item has ProcFlags::EXITED
    pub fn process_keys(&self) -> SmallVec<[ProcessKey; 1]>;  // Process and KernelThread items only
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the module **When** `SetIoPriorityClass { class: IoClass::Normal }.class.to_model()` is called **Then** it returns `IoPriority::BestEffort(4)`.
- **Given** `PriorityClass::Low` **When** `nice()` is called **Then** it returns `Some(19)`; `PriorityClass::Realtime.nice()` returns `None`.
- **Given** a selection of 300 process rows **When** a `CapturedTargets` is built through the page helper (E22-017) **Then** `items.len()` is 256 and `truncated` is true.
- **Given** the action names **When** compared with `tl-ui/src/table/actions.rs` and `tl-ui/src/actions.rs` **Then** no name is declared twice.

- `actions::tests::io_class_maps_to_model`: all six mappings.
- `actions::tests::action_names_are_unique`: builds the list of `Action::name()` for every action here and asserts no duplicates and namespace prefix `tasklens::`.

title: Process column registry: ids, labels, groups, kinds, widths
description:
## Context
The process column registry: one static entry per process-table column with its id, label, picker group, kind, alignment, width template, default width, sort rule, heat reference and phase. The delegate (E22-009) returns `ColumnSpec`s built from it, the column picker (E18-A2) lists it, and the cell formatter (E22-003) dispatches on its kind. Sources: PROC-022 to PROC-036, PROC-047 (unsortable columns), PROC-040 and R-059 (heat references), R-006 (default set and widths), R-007 (ids and labels), R-065 (aliases), UI-PRC-004, UI-PRC-005 (header tooltips), UI-PRC-007 (groups).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/cells.rs` (created here; later beads add to it), plus `pub mod cells;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`:

```rust
pub enum ProcColumnKind { Text, IntegerId, Percent, MemorySize, DiskRate, NetRate, Count, BytesCumulative, Duration, Time, PowerClass }
pub enum HeatRef { CpuMachine, CpuOneCore, Memory, DiskIo, Network, GpuPercent, Vram, Power, None }
pub enum PickerGroup { Image, Identity, Security, Scheduling, Cpu, Memory, Io, Disk, Network, Gpu, Power, Objects, Linux }
pub struct ProcColumn {
    pub id: ColumnId,              // tl-model ColumnId, string from R-007
    pub label: &'static str,       // header line 1 and picker label
    pub alias: Option<&'static str>, // picker full name, shown as `<alias> - "<label>"`
    pub group: PickerGroup,
    pub kind: ProcColumnKind,
    pub template: Option<&'static str>, // PROC-023 width template
    pub default_width: Option<f32>,     // logical px at 100%
    pub sortable: bool,
    pub heat: HeatRef,
    pub phase: u8,                      // 1..=4; columns of a later phase are not offered
    pub header_tooltip: Option<&'static str>,
}
pub static PROCESS_COLUMNS: &[ProcColumn];
pub fn process_column(id: ColumnId) -> &'static ProcColumn;
pub const DEFAULT_VISIBLE: [&str; 9] = ["name","user","pid","cpu","memory","disk","network","gpu","description"];
```

Alignment: `Text` and `PowerClass` left; every other kind right. Minimum width (PROC-023): measured template width + 2 × 8 padding (+ 12 on the active sort column, applied by E18); kinds without a template use 60 px.

Templates: PID, Parent PID, SID `"999999 +99"`; every Percent column `"100.0%"`; NetRate `"xxx Mbps"` when `units.network = "bits"`, `"xxx MiB/s"` when `"bytes"`; DiskRate `"xxx GiB/s"`; MemorySize `"999 MiB"`; Count `"999999"`; Duration `"999:59:59"`; Text none (60 px minimum).

Default widths: name 248, user 92, pid 96, cpu 63, memory 92, disk 82, network 92, gpu 72, description 342, power 101. Every other column: max(minimum, header label width + 16).

Unsortable (PROC-047): pss, uss, cycles, cycles_delta, ctx_switches, ctx_switches_delta; their header tooltip is "Only measured for visible rows".

Header tooltips (UI-PRC-005): memory "Private memory (RssAnon). Shared and file-backed pages are not counted."; ws_total "Resident set size (VmRSS)"; network "Attributed TCP traffic. UDP and other users' sockets are not counted."; handles "Open file descriptors". GPU N tooltips are built at run time (E22-009).

Aliases: memory `Working set private`, gpu_mem_dedicated `GPU memory dedicated`.

The registry rows (id | label | group | kind | heat | phase):
- Image: name | Name | Text | None | 1; name_display | Name display | Text | 1; image_name | Image name | Text | 1; image_path | Image path | Text | 1; cmdline | Command line | Text | 1; description | Description | Text | 1; type | Type | Text | 1; start_time | Start time | Time | 1; version | Version | Text | 2; timestamp | Build date | Time | 2; file_mtime | File modified time | Time | 2; file_size | File size | MemorySize | Memory | 2; company | Package | Text | 2; signer | Packager | Text | 2; signature | Package status | Text | 2; architecture | Architecture | Text | 2.
- Identity: user | User | Text | 1; pid | PID | IntegerId | 1; ppid | Parent PID | IntegerId | 1; session | Session | Text | 2.
- Security: security_label | Security label | Text | 2; elevation | Elevated | Text | 2; sandbox | Sandbox | Text | 2.
- Scheduling: priority | Priority | Text | 1; affinity | Affinity | Text | 1.
- Cpu: cpu | CPU | Percent | CpuMachine | 1; cpu_kernel | CPU (kernel) | Percent | CpuMachine | 1; cpu_user | CPU (user) | Percent | CpuMachine | 1; cpu_relative | CPU (one core = 100%) | Percent | CpuOneCore | 1; cpu_time | CPU time | Duration | 1; cpu_time_kernel | CPU time kernel | Duration | 1; cpu_time_user | CPU time user | Duration | 1; cycles | Cycles | Count | 4; cycles_delta | Cycles delta | Count | 4; ctx_switches | Context switches | Count | 2; ctx_switches_delta | Context switches delta | Count | 2.

title: Process cell values and table (d) formatting
description:
## Context
Fills a cell's value bits, validity and text for every process-table row kind and column, using the registry (E22-002) and the table (d) formatters in `tl_model::units`. The cell text is produced only when `(value_bits, validity)` changed, so steady-state rendering formats nothing (ADR-009 text cache, UI-PRC-023 rule 2). Sources: PROC-003 (formats, canonical table d), PROC-008 (app row values), PROC-009 (unit rows), PROC-018 (PID +N), PROC-027 to PROC-036 (column sources), R-005, R-013 to R-015, R-050, UI-PRC-004 (content per kind), ADR-003 (ProcessRecord, FieldValidity), ADR-009 (CellTextCache).

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/cells.rs`:
```rust
pub struct CellCtx<'a> {
    pub view: &'a ProcessTableView,
    pub records: &'a [ProcessRecord],   // ProcessSnapshot.records
    pub settings: &'a Settings,         // units.network, units.network_auto_scale
    pub ncpu: u16,                      // online CPUs, for heat (E22-004)
    pub mem_total: u64,                 // MemTotal bytes, for heat
    pub vram_total: u64,                // sum of GPU VRAM bytes, for heat; 0 when no GPU
}
pub enum RowRef<'a> { Group(&'a GroupRow, RowKind), Record(&'a ProcessRecord, RowKind) }
pub fn fill_cell(row: RowRef, col: &ProcColumn, ctx: &CellCtx, out: &mut CellOut);
```
`CellOut` is E18-A1's buffer (value bits `u64`, `Validity`, text `String` written only on change, plus optional secondary text). Rules:
- Value bits: numeric values `f32::to_bits` or the `u64` itself; text values the address of the backing `Arc<str>` (`Arc::as_ptr as *const u8 as u64`), so a new metadata `Arc` re-formats and an unchanged one never does.
- Formats (table d), all through `tl_model::units` into `out.text`: Percent `%.1f%%`, a value that rounds to 0.0 is `0%`; MemorySize and BytesCumulative IEC base 1024 with 2 decimals from 1 KiB (`16.00 KiB`, `1.22 GiB`), below 1 KiB `512 B`, zero `0 B`; DiskRate fixed MiB/s 1 decimal (`0.4 MiB/s`, zero `0 MiB/s`); NetRate per `units.network`: bits SI fixed Mbps 1 decimal (`2.3 Mbps`, zero `0 Mbps`) or with auto-scale Kbps/Mbps/Gbps; bytes IEC fixed MiB/s or with auto-scale KiB/s/MiB/s/GiB/s; Count digits grouped with U+2009 thin space (`12 345`), zero `0`; Duration `h:mm:ss`, past 999:59:59 `Nd hh:mm`, zero `0:00:00`; Time today `HH:MM:SS`, else `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`; IntegerId plain digits.
- PID column: collapsed parent with descendants writes `"11528"` as primary text and `" +18"` as secondary text (drawn `text_secondary` by E22-004); expanded parent and leaf write the PID only (PROC-018).
- Blank cells (empty text, `Validity::Valid`): PID, Parent PID and Image name on app and unit rows; PID on pseudo rows; every column on group header rows.
- App and unit rows (PROC-008, PROC-009): Type "App" / "Unit"; User the owner name; Image path the desktop file path for apps; Memory the group's cgroup `anon` value; CPU, Disk, Network, GPU the group sums from `GroupRow`.
- Process rows: Type "App" for an app's primary process, else "Background process", "System process", "Kernel thread" by the record's group class and `KERNEL_THREAD` flag; "Pseudo" on pseudo rows (R-007).
- Image name: basename of `meta.exe`; Wine processes take the `.exe` name per PROC-007 (already in `meta.name` by E05; this cell reads `meta.exe`). A " (deleted)" suffix is kept in the text (coloured by E22-004).
- Validity: numeric fields take `record.validity.0[ProcessField::..]`; `meta.exe == None` gives `Validity::Restricted` for image_name and image_path; `meta.cmdline == None` gives Restricted for cmdline. Never write a zero for a non-valid value (ADR-003).
- Command line cell text: first 512 characters of `meta.cmdline` (R-008).
- Source fields: each column reads the `ProcessRecord`, `ProcessMeta` or `GroupRow` field with the meaning in PROC-027 to PROC-036. The fields named in ADR-003 cover: name, description, user, pid, ppid, image_name, image_path, cmdline, type, cpu (`cpu_pct`), memory (`rss_anon_bytes`), ws_total (`rss_bytes`), pss, uss, swap, disk (`io_read_bps + io_write_bps`), disk_read_rate, disk_write_rate, network (`net_rx_bps + net_tx_bps`), net_send_rate (`net_tx_bps`), net_recv_rate (`net_rx_bps`), gpu (`gpu_util_pct`), gpu_mem_dedicated (`gpu_mem_bytes`), threads, nice, state (`ProcState`: Running "Running", Sleeping "Sleeping", DiskSleep "Disk sleep", Stopped "Stopped", Zombie "Zombie", Idle "Idle", Other "Dead"). For any other column of phase 1, use the E03 field of that meaning; if E03-A1/E03-A2 has none, stop and report the column id to the leader (do not invent a source).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a record with `cpu_pct = 3.27` **When** the CPU cell is filled **Then** the text is `3.3%`.
- **Given** `cpu_pct = 0.04` and Valid **When** filled **Then** the text is `0%`.
- **Given** `rss_anon_bytes = 1_310_720_000` **When** the Memory cell is filled **Then** the text is `1.22 GiB`.
- **Given** `rss_anon_bytes = 512` **When** filled **Then** the text is `512 B`.
- **Given** `units.network = "bits"`, auto-scale off and 287_500 B/s **When** the Network cell is filled **Then** the text is `2.3 Mbps`.
- **Given** threads = 12345 **When** filled **Then** the text is `12 345` with U+2009.
- **Given** the `Memory` validity is `WarmingUp` **When** filled **Then** `out.validity` is WarmingUp and no number is written.
- **Given** an app row **When** the PID cell is filled **Then** the text is empty.
- **Given** a collapsed parent with 18 descendants **When** the PID cell is filled **Then** primary is `11528` and secondary is ` +18`; expanded, secondary is empty.
- **Given** an unchanged record and an existing cache entry **When** `fill_cell` runs **Then** `out.text` is not written (value bits and validity equal).
- **Given** `meta.exe = None` **When** the Image path cell is filled **Then** validity is Restricted.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/cells.rs`: add `CellCtx`, `RowRef`, `fill_cell`.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_process_cells.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `ui_process_cells::cell_formats_match_table_d`: one assertion per kind and per zero form (the criteria above).
- `ui_process_cells::validity_glyphs_never_show_zero`: every non-Valid state writes no digits.
- `ui_process_cells::pid_plus_n_only_on_collapsed_parent`.
- `ui_process_cells::app_and_unit_rows_blank_pid_and_type_text`.
- `ui_process_cells::cell_text_written_only_on_change`.
- proptest `ui_process_cells::prop_percent_one_decimal`: any finite f32 in 0..=100 gives text matching `^(0|\d+\.\d)%$`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: Valid, WarmingUp, Restricted, Unsupported, Missing, Failed, Stale are passed through to `out.validity`; glyphs are drawn by E22-004.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no `format!`; units functions write into `out.text` (a reused `String`); no allocation when bits and validity are unchanged.
- Privacy: the command line goes only into the visible cell text, never into logs (ADR-015).

## Notes
- `CellOut`, `CellTextCache` are E18-A1 (`table/cells.rs`, `text_cache.rs`). The process-specific painters stay in this page file (00-epics.md section 2, `src/table/*` row).
- `ProcessField` index list (ADR-003): Cpu, RssAnon, Rss, Pss, Uss, Swap, IoRead, IoWrite, NetRx, NetTx, GpuUtil, GpuMem, Threads.
- The descendant count N for "PID +N" is computed by the engine projection (PROC-018). ADR-009 `TableRow` has no such field; use the E03-A2 field that carries it, or stop and report (open item 1 in docs/plan/b8-ui-tables.md).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, check, clippy or test through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_processes` (it takes the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope; the wait can be long, so run it in the background when your tool call has a timeout). On an OOM kill (exit 137) retry once, then report.

The English text in this bead is the value, exactly.

title: Process cell painting: heat, validity glyphs, stale, selection text
description:
## Context
Paints a filled process-table cell: alignment, tabular figures, the heat tint, validity glyphs, stale dimming, selected-row text colours and the deleted-image suffix colour. Used by the process delegate for every non-Name cell. Sources: UI-PRC-004 (anatomy, heat, glyphs), UI-PRC-002 (stale at 60%, selected text), UI-PRC-008 (selected row hides heat), PROC-040, R-059, R-050, ADR-003 validity glyph table, ADR-009 heat bullet.

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/cells.rs`:
```rust
pub struct PaintState { pub selected: bool, pub exited: bool, pub heat_on: bool, pub heat_intensity_pct: u8 }
pub fn heat_alpha(col: &ProcColumn, value: f64, ctx: &CellCtx, intensity_pct: u8) -> f32;
pub fn render_metric_cell(out: &CellOut, col: &ProcColumn, width: Pixels, st: PaintState, theme: &TlTheme, cx: &App) -> impl IntoElement;
```
- Layout: a fixed-width `div` (`w(width)`, `h(row_h)`), padding 8 left and right, `overflow_hidden`, `whitespace_nowrap`, `text_ellipsis`; text `t_base` 13 regular; numeric kinds `text_right()` and font features `tnum` (the `TNUM` constant of E15 `text/style.rs`).
- Text colour: `text_primary`; secondary parts (`" +N"`, the " (deleted)" suffix excepted) `text_secondary`; on a selected row `text_selected_primary` and `text_selected_secondary`; on an exited row every part `text_secondary` (E22-012 owns the rest of exited styling).
- " (deleted)" at the end of an Image path value draws in `status.danger` (UI-PRC-004).
- Heat (PROC-040): only for kinds Percent, MemorySize, DiskRate, NetRate and PowerClass, only when `appearance.heat_coloring` is on, `out.validity == Valid` and the value is non-zero. One quad filling the whole cell bounds (no inset, no radius) in `value_heat` with `alpha = heat_intensity_pct/100 × clamp(value / reference, 0, 1)`. References: CpuMachine `400 / ncpu` %, CpuOneCore 400 %, Memory 10 % of MemTotal, DiskIo 100 MiB/s, Network 10 MiB/s in bytes mode or 80 Mbps in bits mode, GpuPercent 100 %, Vram 25 % of total VRAM, Power 25 W. Drawn above the zebra and highlight tints and below the selection fill; selected rows draw no heat. Counts, ids, text and durations are never tinted. With `vram_total = 0` the Vram reference gives alpha 0.
- Validity glyphs replace the content with the column's alignment, through E15 `TlValidityGlyph`: WarmingUp `…` in `text_secondary`; Restricted Lucide `lock` 12 px `text_secondary` with tooltip "Needs administrator access."; Unsupported `n/a` `text_secondary` (tooltip text from the column, E22-014); Missing `-` `text_secondary`; Failed `!` in `status.warning` with the error text as tooltip; Stale: the normal text at 60 % opacity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** ncpu = 32 (reference 12.5 %), intensity 50 and CPU 25 % **When** `heat_alpha` runs **Then** it returns 0.5 (ratio clamped to 1).
- **Given** the same reference and CPU 6.25 % **When** `heat_alpha` runs **Then** it returns 0.25.
- **Given** a selected row with CPU 25 % **When** rendered **Then** no heat quad is drawn.
- **Given** `appearance.heat_coloring = false` **When** rendered **Then** no heat quad is drawn.
- **Given** a Threads cell (Count) of 500 **When** rendered **Then** no heat quad is drawn.
- **Given** validity Restricted **When** rendered **Then** the cell shows the lock glyph and no text, aligned like the column.
- **Given** validity Stale and text `3.3%` **When** rendered **Then** the text draws at opacity 0.6.
- **Given** Image path `/usr/bin/foo (deleted)` **When** rendered **Then** " (deleted)" uses `status.danger`.
- **Given** a CPU cell **When** rendered **Then** text is right-aligned with the `tnum` feature.

## Files

- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_process_cells.rs`: add tests.

## Tests

- Validity: all seven states of ADR-003 as listed.
- Accessibility: heat is additive to the number; colour is never the only signal. Glyph tooltips carry the meaning as text.

title: Process Name cell: indent, chevron, icon, text, state glyphs
description:
## Context
The Name cell of the process table: indent by depth, the chevron with its reserved width, the 24 px app icon or 16 px icon, the primary text with count and qualifiers, and the state glyphs. Connector lines (E22-006), window titles (E22-033) and the window button (E22-034) build on it. Sources: UI-PRC-002 (row anatomy per kind), UI-PRC-003 (Name cell), PROC-006 (icon sizes), PROC-007 (names), PROC-008 (app Name cell), PROC-009 (unit rows), PROC-063 (pause glyph), D-011 (group header row).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/name_cell.rs` (with `pub mod name_cell;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub struct NameCellData { pub kind: RowKind, pub depth: u8, pub expandable: Option<bool>, pub icon: NameIcon,
                          pub primary: SharedString, pub state_glyph: Option<StateGlyph>, pub exited: bool }
pub enum NameIcon { File(Arc<str>), Lucide(IconName) }
pub enum StateGlyph { Suspended, Frozen }
pub fn render_name_cell(d: &NameCellData, width: Pixels, selected: bool, node: NodeId, theme: &TlTheme, cx: &mut App) -> AnyElement;
pub fn render_group_header(label: SharedString, expanded: bool, first: bool, theme: &TlTheme) -> AnyElement;
```
Geometry (logical px × ui_scale):
- Content starts at x = 8 + depth × 18 (8 is the cell padding).
- Chevron box 16 × 16, hit area 20 × `row_h`; Lucide `chevron-right` when collapsed, `chevron-down` when expanded; colour `text_secondary`, `text_primary` while its hit area is hovered; tooltip "Expand" / "Collapse". When the row has no children (`expandable == None`) nothing is drawn but the 16 px width is still reserved.
- Icon: app rows 24 × 24, vertically centred; every other row 16 × 16. `NameIcon::File(path)` draws `img(path)`; a missing file draws Lucide `binary` in `text_secondary`. Unit rows Lucide `cog`; "Kernel threads (N)" row and kernel-thread rows Lucide `cpu`. Gap after the icon `sp3` = 6.
- Primary text: `t_base` regular `text_primary` (selected: `text_selected_primary`; exited: `text_secondary`), one line, ellipsis. The count " (N)" and qualifiers "(Flatpak)", "(Snap)", "(Wine)" are part of the same string (format `%s (%s) (%s)`), built by the delegate.
- State glyph after the primary text, gap `sp2` = 4: `Suspended` Lucide `pause` 12 px `text_secondary`, tooltip "Suspended"; `Frozen` Lucide `snowflake` 12 px `text_secondary`, tooltip "Frozen" (Frozen is P2, drawn when the delegate sets it).
- Exited rows: icon at 60 % opacity; chevron unchanged.
- Group header row (D-011): full row width band in `header` colour, height `row_h`, 1 px `divider` line at the top edge except for the first row; chevron at x 8 (16 px, `text_primary`); label at x 30, `t_md` 14 semibold 600 `text_primary`, text like "Apps (11)", "Background processes (99)", "System processes (14)". No zebra, no hover fill, no other cell.
- Element ids: the Name cell div carries `.id(("name", node))` (the only per-row id besides the row hitbox, UI-PRC-023 rule 3).
- Chevron click calls the table's toggle (E18 `ToggleExpand { id }` path) and does not change the selection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a process row at depth 2 with a 16 px icon **When** rendered **Then** the text starts at x = 8 + 36 + 16 + 6 + 16 + 6 relative to the cell (indent, chevron box, gap, icon, gap) with `ui_scale = 1`.
- **Given** a leaf process row **When** rendered **Then** no chevron is drawn and the icon x equals that of an expandable sibling.
- **Given** an app row **When** rendered **Then** the icon is 24 px; a unit row icon is 16 px Lucide `cog`.
- **Given** a process in State T **When** the delegate sets `StateGlyph::Suspended` **Then** a 12 px `pause` glyph with tooltip "Suspended" follows the text.
- **Given** an icon path that does not exist **When** rendered **Then** the `binary` glyph is drawn.
- **Given** a group header that is not first **When** rendered **Then** a 1 px `divider` top line and the `header` band are drawn and the label is semibold 14.
- **Given** a chevron click **When** handled **Then** the row toggles and the selection set is unchanged.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/name_cell.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: add `pub mod name_cell;`.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_process_cells.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `ui_process_cells::name_cell_indent_by_depth`: the x formula for depths 0, 1, 2.
- `ui_process_cells::name_cell_icon_sizes_per_kind`: 24 for app, 16 for unit, process, kernel thread.
- `ui_process_cells::chevron_width_reserved_on_leaf`.
- `ui_process_cells::chevron_click_does_not_select`.
- `ui_process_cells::group_header_band_and_divider`.

title: E29-A1 Helper binary
description:
## Context
Anchor E29-A1: the finished `tl-helper` binary. It runs as root under `pkexec /usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper --session`, reads framed requests on stdin, answers on stdout, accepts only the ADR-006 allowlist with the R-004 extensions, re-verifies every process target, sets `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG = SIGKILL`, and exits after 300 s without a request or at stdin EOF (ADR-006, R-003, R-004, PROC-076, APP-003). This bead adds the session loop and the dispatch table over the operation modules written in E29-002 to E29-009 (the P4 `NetnsSockDiagDump` arm is added by E29-010). Sources: ADR-006, ADR-007 (framing), R-002 to R-004, R-098, PROC-076, APP-003.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-helper/src/main.rs`:
  1. Argument check from E29-001 (`--session` only, else exit 2).
  2. First action: `rustix::process::set_parent_process_death_signal(Some(Signal::Kill))`; then if `getppid() == 1` (parent already gone) exit 0.
  3. `umask(0o022)`. Read the boot id once from `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`.
  4. Loop: `poll` fd 0 for readability with the remaining idle time (300 s, reset after each request; test override `TL_HELPER_IDLE_MS` read once at start, used only when set). Timeout: exit 0. EOF: exit 0.
  5. Read one frame with `tl_model::wire` (max payload `MAX_HELPER_FRAME = 65_536`), receiving ancillary fds as in E29-006. Oversize length, short read or postcard error: write one line `tl-helper: protocol error` to stderr and exit 3.
  6. The first request must be `Hello { proto }` with `proto == HELPER_PROTO_VERSION`; reply `Hello { proto: HELPER_PROTO_VERSION, pid: getpid() }`. Any other first request, or a version mismatch, replies `Error(NotAllowed("protocol version"))` and exits 3.
  7. Every later request goes to `dispatch::handle(frame, &mut Ctx, &mut Writer)`.
  8. Replies go out through the `tl_model::wire` multi-frame writer on fd 1 (64 KiB frames). A single reply message over 4 MiB (4_194_304 bytes encoded) is replaced by `Error(TooLarge)`.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/dispatch.rs` (new; `mod dispatch;`): one `match` over `HelperRequest`, every arm explicit, no wildcard arm:
  - `Signal`, `SetNice`, `SetSched`, `SetAffinity`, `SetIoPriority` to `ops::run_process_op`;
  - `FreezeGroup`, `ThawGroup`, `KillGroup` to `ops::run_cgroup_op`;
  - `ReadProcessFiles` to `files::read_process_files`;
  - `ScanStrings` to `files::scan_strings` with the stdin cancel poll; `CancelScan` outside a scan replies `Done`;
  - `Dump` to `ops::run_dump` with the received fd;
  - `ResolveSocketInodes` to `sockets::resolve_socket_inodes`;
  - `SockDestroy` to `sockets::sock_destroy`;
  - `WriteServiceDropIn` to `dropin::write_service_dropin`;
  - `NetnsSockDiagDump`: `Error(NotAllowed("unsupported"))` until the P4 bead E29-010 replaces this arm;
  - `Hello` after the first: `Error(NotAllowed("hello twice"))`;
  - `ReadProcessDetail`: `Error(NotAllowed("unsupported"))` until open item E29-OI-9 defines its `what` set.
- Requests are handled one at a time in arrival order; the reply frames of one request are never interleaved with another's.
- The helper writes nothing else to stdout and logs nothing; tl-helper has no tracing dependency (ADR-001 row).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the built helper on a socketpair, started as the test user **When** the test sends `Hello { proto: HELPER_PROTO_VERSION }` **Then** it receives `Hello { proto, pid }` with the child's pid.
- **Given** a fresh helper **When** the first request is `Signal{..}` **Then** it replies `Error(NotAllowed("protocol version"))` and exits with status 3.
- **Given** a fresh helper **When** the test writes a frame header announcing 65_537 bytes **Then** the helper exits 3 without reading the payload.
- **Given** a running session **When** the test closes its end **Then** the helper exits 0 within 100 ms.
- **Given** `TL_HELPER_IDLE_MS=200` **When** no request arrives **Then** the helper exits 0 after 200 to 400 ms.
- **Given** the helper started by an intermediate parent `/bin/sh -c '<helper> --session & echo $! >&2; sleep 30'` (stdin and stdout on the socketpair) **When** the test SIGKILLs that `sh` **Then** the helper pid it printed on stderr is gone within 1 s (`PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`).
- **Given** a running session **When** `ReadProcessFiles` for a child of the test is sent **Then** the reply arrives in one or more frames, each payload at most 65_536 bytes, and decodes to `Files(..)`.
- **Given** a running session **When** `ReadProcessDetail` is sent **Then** the reply is `Error(NotAllowed("unsupported"))`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/src/main.rs`: session loop.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/dispatch.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-helper/tests/helper_proto.rs`: create (spawns `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_tl-helper")` with both stdin and stdout set to one end of a `socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC)`).

## Tests
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::hello_handshake`
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::first_request_must_be_hello` (security regression)
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::oversize_frame_exits` (security regression)
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::eof_exits`
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::idle_exit`
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::parent_death_kills_helper`
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::multi_frame_reply`
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::read_process_detail_unsupported`
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::every_request_variant_has_an_arm`: sends one well-formed request of each variant (targets the test's own child, a temp fd for `Dump`, a `user.slice` path that fails validation for the cgroup kinds) and checks that every reply decodes; none is a protocol error.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: protocol failure exits 3; operation errors are replies.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: idle helper uses no CPU (blocking poll).
- Privacy: no logging; stderr only for the one protocol error line.
- Security: this is the root boundary. No path, command or free-form file argument reaches any handler (R-004). Every process target is re-verified inside the handler (ADR-006).

## Notes
- Protocol names used below are those of `tl-model/src/helper_proto.rs` (E03-A2). This bead expects the shape recorded as open item E29-OI-1 in `docs/plan/b4-engine-workers.md`: every frame is `HelperFrame { req: u32, body }` (the engine picks `req`, the helper echoes it on every reply frame); requests `Hello { proto }`, `Signal { target, signal }`, `SetNice { target, nice }`, `SetSched { target, policy, rt_prio }`, `SetAffinity { target, set }`, `SetIoPriority { key, prio }`, `FreezeGroup(CgroupRef)`, `ThawGroup(CgroupRef)`, `KillGroup(CgroupRef)`, `ReadProcessFiles { key, files }`, `ScanStrings { key, opts }`, `CancelScan`, `Dump { key, mode }`, `ResolveSocketInodes { inodes }`, `SockDestroy { family, proto, four_tuple, cookie }`, `WriteServiceDropIn { unit, keys }`, `NetnsSockDiagDump { netns_ino }`, where `target` is `HelperTarget::{Process(ProcessKey), Thread { process: ProcessKey, tid: u32 }}`; replies `Hello { proto, pid }`, `Done`, `Error(HelperError)`, `Files(..)`, `Strings { .. , last }`, `Inodes(..)`, `SockDiag { bytes, last }`, with `HelperError::{IdentityChanged, NoSuchProcess, PermissionDenied, Partial { done, total }, Os(i32), NotAllowed(Arc<str>), TooLarge}`. If E03-A2 landed different names, use E03's names and keep the behaviour written here.
- Commit `dispatch.rs` before building (it is the largest new file of the crate), then build and test.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E29-007 Helper ResolveSocketInodes
description:
## Context
`ResolveSocketInodes { inodes }` maps socket inodes to the processes that hold them, for sockets of other users whose `/proc/<pid>/fd` the engine cannot read (SYS-030, PROC-032, R-004). The engine sends the inodes it could not attribute; the helper walks `/proc/*/fd` as root. Sources: SYS-030, ADR-016 (socket to pid map), R-004.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-helper/src/sockets.rs` (new; add `mod sockets;` to `main.rs`):
- `pub fn resolve_socket_inodes(inodes: &[u64], boot: BootId) -> HelperReply`.
- Build a `FxHashSet`-free sorted `Vec<u64>` of the requested inodes (tl-helper has no rustc-hash; use `sort_unstable` plus `binary_search`).
- Walk `/proc` numeric entries; for each pid open `/proc/<pid>` as a dirfd, read `stat` field 22 (`start_ticks`, parsed after the last `)`), `readdir` its `fd/`, `readlinkat` each entry; a target of the form `socket:[<n>]` with `n` in the set adds `(n, ProcessKey { pid, start_ticks, boot_id: boot })`.
- Pids that vanish mid-walk are skipped. Kernel threads have no fds and cost one readdir.
- Reply `Inodes(Vec<(u64, ProcessKey)>)` sorted by inode then pid; an inode held by several processes appears once per process (shared sockets after fork, SYS-030 "pid +N"). Inodes with no holder are absent.
- An empty request replies `Inodes([])` without walking.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the test opens a TCP listener and a UDP socket **When** their inodes (from `fstat`) are resolved **Then** both map to the test's own pid and `start_ticks`.
- **Given** a socket shared by the test and a forked child **When** resolved **Then** two entries with the same inode appear, one per pid.
- **Given** an inode no process holds (for example 1) **When** resolved **Then** the reply has no entry for it.
- **Given** an empty list **When** resolved **Then** the reply is `Inodes([])`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/src/sockets.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/main.rs`: add `mod sockets;`.

## Tests
- `sockets.rs::tests::resolves_own_sockets`
- `sockets.rs::tests::shared_socket_lists_both_pids`
- `sockets.rs::tests::unknown_inode_absent`
- `sockets.rs::tests::empty_request_no_walk`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: none beyond skipped pids; the walk never fails as a whole except on `/proc` open failure (`Error(Os(errno))`).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one walk per request; the engine sends at most one request per 2 s rebuild (SYS-030 cadence) and only while connections are demanded.
- Privacy: fd targets other than `socket:[n]` are discarded immediately and never logged or returned.
- Security: no path argument; only `socket:[n]` matches leave the helper.

## Notes
- Protocol names used below are those of `tl-model/src/helper_proto.rs` (E03-A2). If E03-A2 landed different names, use E03's names and keep the behaviour written here.

title: E29-008 Helper SockDestroy over raw netlink
description:
## Context
`SockDestroy { family, proto, four_tuple, cookie }` closes one TCP connection as root by sending a netlink `SOCK_DESTROY` message (SYS-031, R-004). The kernel matches the socket cookie, so a reused 4-tuple cannot be hit. tl-helper's dependency row has no netlink crates (ADR-001: rustix, postcard, serde), so the message is built by hand on a rustix netlink socket. Sources: SYS-031, ADR-006, R-004.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-helper/src/sockets.rs`: `pub fn sock_destroy(family: Family, proto: Proto, t: &FourTuple, cookie: u64) -> HelperReply`:
- Only `Proto::Tcp` is allowed (`Error(NotAllowed("only tcp"))` otherwise); `family` is `Family::V4` or `Family::V6`.
- Socket: `rustix::net::socket(AddressFamily::NETLINK, SocketType::RAW, Some(Protocol::from_raw(NETLINK_SOCK_DIAG = 4)))` with `SOCK_CLOEXEC`.
- Message (all little-endian host order except ports and addresses, which are network order), 88 bytes:
  - `nlmsghdr` (16 bytes): `nlmsg_len = 88`, `nlmsg_type = SOCK_DESTROY = 21`, `nlmsg_flags = NLM_F_REQUEST | NLM_F_ACK = 0x0001 | 0x0004`, `nlmsg_seq = 1`, `nlmsg_pid = 0`.
  - `inet_diag_req_v2` (56 bytes): `sdiag_family` = `AF_INET` 2 or `AF_INET6` 10; `sdiag_protocol = IPPROTO_TCP = 6`; `idiag_ext = 0`; `pad = 0`; `idiag_states = 0xFFFF_FFFF`; `inet_diag_sockid`: `idiag_sport` (be16), `idiag_dport` (be16), `idiag_src` `[be32; 4]` (IPv4 uses the first word, rest 0), `idiag_dst` `[be32; 4]`, `idiag_if = 0`, `idiag_cookie = [cookie as u32, (cookie >> 32) as u32]`.
- Send to the kernel (`SocketAddrNetlink::new(0, 0)`), then receive the `NLMSG_ERROR` ack: `error == 0` replies `Done`; `-EOPNOTSUPP (95)` replies `Error(Os(95))` (UI: "Kernel lacks CONFIG_INET_DIAG_DESTROY"); `-ENOENT (2)` replies `Error(NoSuchProcess)` (connection already gone); any other negative errno `Error(Os(errno))`. A receive timeout of 2 s (`SO_RCVTIMEO`) gives `Error(Os(ETIMEDOUT = 110))`.
- A pure builder `fn build_destroy_msg(family, t, cookie) -> [u8; 88]` is separate so it can be tested byte for byte.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** family V4, sport 40000, dport 443, src 192.168.1.5, dst 1.2.3.4, cookie `0x0000_0001_0000_00AB` **When** `build_destroy_msg` runs **Then** the bytes equal the committed expected array in the test (length 88, type 21, flags 5, family 2, protocol 6, ports `0x9C40` and `0x01BB` big-endian, cookie words `0xAB` and `1`).
- **Given** family V6 with `::1` addresses **When** built **Then** family is 10 and all four address words are filled.
- **Given** `Proto::Udp` **When** `sock_destroy` runs **Then** `Error(NotAllowed("only tcp"))` and no socket is opened.
- **Given** the test as an ordinary user and a real loopback TCP connection it owns **When** `sock_destroy` runs **Then** the reply is `Error(PermissionDenied)` or `Error(Os(1))` (CAP_NET_ADMIN missing), never `Done`; the root case is in `real_helper_root.rs` (E29-012).

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/src/sockets.rs`: add `sock_destroy` and `build_destroy_msg`.

## Tests
- `sockets.rs::tests::destroy_msg_v4_bytes`
- `sockets.rs::tests::destroy_msg_v6_bytes`
- `sockets.rs::tests::destroy_udp_refused` (security regression: only TCP)
- `sockets.rs::tests::destroy_without_cap_fails`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as listed.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one socket per call, closed on return.
- Privacy: addresses are not logged above `debug`; never log the cookie.
- Security: the cookie is always set, so the kernel refuses a socket that only matches the 4-tuple.

## Notes
- If rustix's netlink address type is not available at the pinned rustix version, stop and report; do not add `libc` or `unsafe` to tl-helper.
- Protocol names used below are those of `tl-model/src/helper_proto.rs` (E03-A2). This bead expects the shape recorded as open item E29-OI-1 in `docs/plan/b4-engine-workers.md`: every frame is `HelperFrame { req: u32, body }` (the engine picks `req`, the helper echoes it on every reply frame); requests `Hello { proto }`, `Signal { target, signal }`, `SetNice { target, nice }`, `SetSched { target, policy, rt_prio }`, `SetAffinity { target, set }`, `SetIoPriority { key, prio }`, `FreezeGroup(CgroupRef)`, `ThawGroup(CgroupRef)`, `KillGroup(CgroupRef)`, `ReadProcessFiles { key, files }`, `ScanStrings { key, opts }`, `CancelScan`, `Dump { key, mode }`, `ResolveSocketInodes { inodes }`, `SockDestroy { family, proto, four_tuple, cookie }`, `WriteServiceDropIn { unit, keys }`, `NetnsSockDiagDump { netns_ino }`, where `target` is `HelperTarget::{Process(ProcessKey), Thread { process: ProcessKey, tid: u32 }}`; replies `Hello { proto, pid }`, `Done`, `Error(HelperError)`, `Files(..)`, `Strings { .. , last }`, `Inodes(..)`, `SockDiag { bytes, last }`, with `HelperError::{IdentityChanged, NoSuchProcess, PermissionDenied, Partial { done, total }, Os(i32), NotAllowed(Arc<str>), TooLarge}`. If E03-A2 landed different names, use E03's names and keep the behaviour written here.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E29-009 Helper WriteServiceDropIn
description:
## Context
`WriteServiceDropIn { manager: System, unit, keys }` lets the Recovery tab editor change `Restart*`, `StartLimit*`, `FailureAction` and `OnFailure` of a system service by writing the fixed file `/etc/systemd/system/<unit>.d/50-tasklens-recovery.conf` as root; an empty key set deletes that file (`UnitRemoveRecovery`) (SYS-013, R-004, R-119, table (c)). The engine then calls `Manager.Reload()` (E11). The helper builds the file text itself from typed keys; it never accepts file text. Sources: SYS-013, UI-SYS-034 (ranges and the unit-name pattern), R-004, R-119, ADR-011 (atomic write).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-helper/src/dropin.rs` (new; add `mod dropin;` to `main.rs`):
- `pub fn write_service_dropin(unit: &str, keys: &RecoveryEdit) -> HelperReply`, using the `RecoveryEdit` fields of E03-A2 (each key optional: `restart`, `restart_usec`, `start_limit_burst`, `start_limit_interval_usec`, `start_limit_action`, `failure_action`, `on_failure`).
- Validation, each failure `Error(NotAllowed(<reason>))` with no file touched:
  - `unit` matches `^[A-Za-z0-9:_.\\@-]{1,255}\.service$`, does not start with `.`, and contains no `/` ("bad unit name").
  - `restart` is one of `no`, `on-success`, `on-failure`, `on-abnormal`, `on-watchdog`, `on-abort`, `always` ("bad Restart value").
  - `restart_usec` in `0..=3_600_000` ms ("RestartSec out of range").
  - `start_limit_burst` in `0..=1000`; `start_limit_interval_usec` in `0..=86_400` s ("StartLimit out of range").
  - `start_limit_action` and `failure_action` each one of `none`, `reboot`, `reboot-force`, `reboot-immediate`, `poweroff`, `poweroff-force`, `poweroff-immediate`, `exit`, `exit-force` ("bad action value").
  - every `on_failure` token matches `^[A-Za-z0-9:_.\\@%-]{1,255}\.(service|socket|target|timer|mount|path|slice|scope)$`; at most 32 tokens ("bad OnFailure unit").
- File text (`pub fn render(keys: &RecoveryEdit) -> String`), only the keys present, sections omitted when empty, LF line ends, no trailing spaces:
  ```
  [Unit]
  StartLimitIntervalSec=<n>
  StartLimitBurst=<n>
  StartLimitAction=<word>
  FailureAction=<word>
  OnFailure=<unit> <unit>

  [Service]
  Restart=<word>
  RestartSec=<n>ms
  ```
- Write: open `/etc/systemd/system` as a dirfd; `mkdirat(<unit>.d, 0o755)` if missing (an existing non-directory or symlink at that name gives `Error(NotAllowed("drop-in directory is not a directory"))`, checked with `fstatat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)`); write `50-tasklens-recovery.conf` with mode 0644 through `tl_ops::fs::write_atomic` (E07-A3) relative to that directory.
- Empty `keys` (every field `None`): `unlinkat` the file (absent is fine), then `unlinkat(<unit>.d, AT_REMOVEDIR)` only if the directory is now empty. Reply `Done`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** keys `restart = on-failure`, `restart_usec = 100` **When** `render` runs **Then** the text is exactly `[Service]\nRestart=on-failure\nRestartSec=100ms\n`.
- **Given** keys with `start_limit_burst = 5`, `start_limit_interval_usec = 10`, `on_failure = ["failure-notify@%n.service"]` **When** rendered **Then** the text is `[Unit]\nStartLimitIntervalSec=10\nStartLimitBurst=5\nOnFailure=failure-notify@%n.service\n`.
- **Given** unit `../../etc/passwd` or `sshd.service/x` or `.hidden.service` **When** written **Then** `Error(NotAllowed("bad unit name"))`.
- **Given** a value containing a newline (`restart = "always\nExecStart=/bin/sh"`) **When** written **Then** `Error(NotAllowed("bad Restart value"))` (security regression: no key injection).
- **Given** an `on_failure` token `a.service\n[Service]` **When** written **Then** `Error(NotAllowed("bad OnFailure unit"))`.
- **Given** a temp root (test-only constructor `write_service_dropin_in(dir_fd, ..)`) **When** a write and then an empty-keys call run **Then** the file exists with mode 0644 after the first and the file and the then-empty directory are gone after the second.
- **Given** `<unit>.d` is a symlink in the temp root **When** written **Then** `Error(NotAllowed("drop-in directory is not a directory"))` and nothing is written through the link.

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/src/dropin.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/main.rs`: add `mod dropin;`.

## Tests
- `dropin.rs::tests::render_service_only`
- `dropin.rs::tests::render_unit_only`
- `dropin.rs::tests::unit_name_rules` (security regression)
- `dropin.rs::tests::newline_injection_refused` (security regression)
- `dropin.rs::tests::write_then_remove_in_temp_root`
- `dropin.rs::tests::symlinked_dropin_dir_refused` (security regression)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as listed; the UI shows "Failed to save recovery settings: <error>".
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A
- Security: root write to `/etc`; fixed directory and file name, typed and range-checked values only.

title: E29-010 Helper NetnsSockDiagDump
description:
## Context
`NetnsSockDiagDump { netns_ino }` dumps TCP and UDP sockets of another network namespace as root, for the Connections tab's Namespaces dropdown (P4; SYS-037, R-004). tl-helper cannot link the sock_diag parser in tl-collect (ADR-001 row), so the helper returns the raw netlink dump bytes and the engine parses them with the E06 parser. This reply shape is part of open item E29-OI-1. Sources: R-004, SYS-037, ADR-016 (connections).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-helper/src/sockets.rs`: `pub fn netns_sock_diag_dump(netns_ino: u64, out: &mut dyn FnMut(HelperReply) -> std::io::Result<()>) -> std::io::Result<()>`:
- Find a process whose `/proc/<pid>/ns/net` link target is `net:[<netns_ino>]` by walking `/proc` (first match by ascending pid). None: `Error(NoSuchProcess)`.
- On a new thread (so the helper's main thread keeps its namespace): open that `ns/net` link with `O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC`, `fstat` it and check `st_ino == netns_ino` (else `Error(IdentityChanged)`), `rustix::thread::move_into_link_name_space(fd, Some(LinkNameSpaceType::Network))`, open a `NETLINK_SOCK_DIAG` socket there, send four dump requests (`SOCK_DIAG_BY_FAMILY = 20`, `NLM_F_REQUEST | NLM_F_DUMP`) for (AF_INET, TCP), (AF_INET6, TCP), (AF_INET, UDP), (AF_INET6, UDP) with `idiag_states = 0xFFFF_FFFF` and `idiag_ext = 1 << (INET_DIAG_INFO - 1)`, and forward every received datagram as `SockDiag { bytes, last: false }`, split so one reply stays under 60 KiB; after `NLMSG_DONE` of the fourth dump send `SockDiag { bytes: [], last: true }`. The thread exits after the dump.
- Total bytes per request capped at 4 MiB; past it the dump stops with `Error(TooLarge)`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the test's own network namespace inode **When** run as an ordinary user **Then** at least the test's own listening loopback TCP socket appears in the bytes (parse in the test with a minimal `inet_diag_msg` reader) and the last message has `last: true`.
- **Given** an inode no process uses **When** run **Then** `Error(NoSuchProcess)`.
- **Given** any run **When** it finishes **Then** the helper main thread's `/proc/thread-self/ns/net` is unchanged.

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/src/sockets.rs`: add `netns_sock_diag_dump`.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/dispatch.rs`: replace the `NetnsSockDiagDump` arm (it answered `NotAllowed("unsupported")` since E29-A1) with a call to `sockets::netns_sock_diag_dump`.

## Tests

- `sockets.rs::tests::netns_unknown_inode`
- `sockets.rs::tests::netns_main_thread_unchanged` (security regression)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as listed.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one dump per request; the engine asks only while the dropdown selects another namespace.
- Privacy: addresses are returned to the engine only, never logged.
- Security: namespace switch is confined to a short-lived thread.

description:

title: E29-012 Helper real-system tests as root
description:
## Context
Real-system tests of the helper binary as root on the owner machine (ADR-013 real-system layer, `#[ignore]`). They prove the root paths that the unprivileged unit tests cannot: another user's process, another user's cgroup, `SOCK_DESTROY`, and the system drop-in write. Sources: ADR-013, ADR-006 verification, R-004, SYS-031, SYS-013.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-helper/tests/real_helper_root.rs`, every test `#[ignore]` and skipped with a printed reason unless `rustix::process::geteuid().is_root()`. Run on the owner machine with `sudo -E cargo test -p tl-helper --test real_helper_root -- --ignored` (through the build rule; `sudo` is the owner's step, never an agent's). Each test spawns the built helper (`env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_tl-helper")`) directly as root on a socketpair (no pkexec) and sends real frames:
- `signal_other_users_process`: `runuser -u nobody -- sleep 60` child; capture its key; `Signal(Term)` gives `Done`; the child is gone.
- `stale_key_other_user_rejected`: same child, `start_ticks + 1`: `Error(IdentityChanged)`; child alive.

- `sock_destroy_loopback`: the test opens a loopback TCP connection, gets its cookie from a `sock_diag` dump, `SockDestroy` gives `Done`, and a read on the client side returns an error (ECONNABORTED or ECONNRESET).
- `dropin_write_and_remove`: on the test unit `tasklens-test.service` (table (c); the test installs `/etc/systemd/system/tasklens-test.service` with `ExecStart=/usr/bin/sleep 600` first and removes it at the end), `WriteServiceDropIn { restart: on-failure }` creates `/etc/systemd/system/tasklens-test.service.d/50-tasklens-recovery.conf` with mode 0644 and the exact text; the empty set removes the file and the directory.
