title: E29-013 Engine helper link: pkexec spawn, handshake, calls
description:
## Context
The engine's synchronous link to one running helper process: spawning `pkexec /usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper --session`, the `Hello` handshake that also tells a dismissed polkit prompt from a denial, and one request at a time with deadlines (ADR-006, R-003, R-117, APP-003). The async session task that owns it is E29-A2. Sources: ADR-006 (helper boundary), ADR-007 (framing, one outstanding request, kill and reap), R-003, R-117 (pkexec exit 126 dismissed, 127 not authorized), open item E29-OI-2 (socketpair transport).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/helper/session.rs` and a module stub `crates/tl-engine/src/helper/mod.rs` containing `mod session;` (E29-A2 fills `mod.rs`); `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs` gets `mod helper;` (chain edit to an E08 file, the only change to it in this bead; depends on E08-A1).

```rust
pub(crate) const HELPER_PATH: &str = "/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper";
pub(crate) const PKEXEC_PATH: &str = "/usr/bin/pkexec";
pub(crate) const START_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(120); // any call that may show a polkit prompt (ADR-006)

pub(crate) trait HelperLink: Send {               // real process or the test fake
    fn send(&mut self, frame: &HelperFrame<HelperRequest>, fd: Option<BorrowedFd<'_>>) -> io::Result<()>;
    fn recv(&mut self, timeout: Duration) -> Result<HelperFrame<HelperReply>, LinkError>;
    fn exit_status(&mut self, wait: Duration) -> Option<i32>; // reaps; None if still running after `wait`
    fn kill(&mut self);                                       // SIGKILL then wait()
    fn close(&mut self);                                      // shut down the write half (helper sees EOF)
}
pub(crate) enum LinkError { Timeout, Eof, Protocol }
pub(crate) enum StartError { Cancelled, NotAuthorized, Missing, Failed(Arc<str>) }
pub(crate) enum CallError { Timeout, Exited, Protocol }

pub(crate) struct ProcLink { child: std::process::Child, sock: OwnedFd }
impl ProcLink { pub(crate) fn spawn() -> Result<ProcLink, StartError>; }

pub(crate) struct HelperSession<L: HelperLink> { link: L, next_req: u32, helper_pid: u32 }
impl<L: HelperLink> HelperSession<L> {
    pub(crate) fn start(link: L) -> Result<Self, StartError>;   // Hello with START_DEADLINE
    pub(crate) fn call(&mut self, req: HelperRequest, fd: Option<BorrowedFd<'_>>, deadline: Duration,
                       on_reply: &mut dyn FnMut(HelperReply) -> ControlFlow<()>) -> Result<(), CallError>;
    pub(crate) fn end(self);                                     // close, wait 500 ms, then kill
    pub(crate) fn is_alive(&mut self) -> bool;                   // exit_status(Duration::ZERO).is_none()
}
```
- `ProcLink::spawn`: `HELPER_PATH` or `PKEXEC_PATH` not a regular file gives `StartError::Missing`. `rustix::net::socketpair(UNIX, STREAM, CLOEXEC)`; `std::process::Command::new(PKEXEC_PATH).arg(HELPER_PATH).arg("--session")`, `env_clear()`, `stdin` and `stdout` both from the child end (`Stdio::from(OwnedFd)`, one `try_clone`), `stderr` inherited. No `pre_exec`, no `unsafe` (the helper sets its own death signal). Never `asupersync::process` (zombie bug `bi2462.114`).
- `send` writes with `tl_model::wire` framing; with an fd it uses `rustix::net::sendmsg` with one `SCM_RIGHTS` fd on the frame's first byte.
- `recv` polls the socket (`rustix::event::poll`) up to `timeout`, then reads one complete reply message with the `tl_model::wire` multi-frame reader (frames of at most 65_536 bytes, message at most 4 MiB).
- `start`: sends `Hello { proto: HELPER_PROTO_VERSION }` with `req = 0`, waits up to `START_DEADLINE`. `Eof` before the reply: reap and map the exit status: 126 gives `Cancelled`, 127 gives `NotAuthorized`, anything else `Failed("helper exited with status <n>")`. Timeout: `kill()` and `Failed("no answer from the helper")`. A `Hello` with another `proto`: `end()` and `Failed("helper version mismatch")`.
- `call`: `req` ids count up from 1 and wrap; frames whose `req` differs from the current id are a `Protocol` error. Calls `on_reply` for each reply; a `Strings { last: false }` or `SockDiag { last: false }` reply keeps reading, any other reply ends the call. `on_reply` returning `Break` sends `CancelScan` and keeps reading until the final reply. The deadline covers the whole call; on `Timeout` the link is killed and reaped and the session is unusable (`CallError::Timeout`); `Eof` gives `CallError::Exited`.
- `end`: `close()`, `exit_status(500 ms)`, else `kill()`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a `FakeLink` that answers `Hello` correctly **When** `start` runs **Then** it returns a session with the fake's pid.
- **Given** a `FakeLink` that reports EOF and exit status 126 **When** `start` runs **Then** `StartError::Cancelled`; status 127 gives `NotAuthorized`; status 1 gives `Failed("helper exited with status 1")`.
- **Given** a `FakeLink` answering `Hello { proto: 99 }` **When** `start` runs **Then** `Failed("helper version mismatch")` and `close` was called.
- **Given** a session **When** `call(Signal ..)` gets `Done` **Then** `on_reply` saw exactly one reply and the call returned `Ok`.
- **Given** a session **When** a `ScanStrings` call gets three `Strings { last: false }` then `Strings { last: true }` **Then** `on_reply` ran four times.
- **Given** `on_reply` returns `Break` on the first batch **When** the call continues **Then** the fake received `CancelScan` with the same `req`.
- **Given** a fake that never answers **When** `call` with deadline 2 s runs **Then** `CallError::Timeout` and `kill` was called.
- **Given** a reply frame with a wrong `req` **When** read **Then** `CallError::Protocol`.
- **Given** `HELPER_PATH` absent (test override of the two path constants through a `#[cfg(test)]` constructor `ProcLink::spawn_at(pkexec, helper)`) **When** spawned **Then** `StartError::Missing`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/helper/session.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/helper/mod.rs`: create with `mod session;` only.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs`: add `mod helper;` (chain edit).

## Tests
- `helper/session.rs::tests::start_ok`
- `helper/session.rs::tests::start_exit_codes_map` (126, 127, 1)
- `helper/session.rs::tests::start_version_mismatch`
- `helper/session.rs::tests::call_single_reply`
- `helper/session.rs::tests::call_streams_until_last`
- `helper/session.rs::tests::break_sends_cancel`
- `helper/session.rs::tests::call_timeout_kills`
- `helper/session.rs::tests::wrong_req_is_protocol_error` (security regression)
- `helper/session.rs::tests::missing_paths`
- `helper/session.rs::tests::proc_link_socketpair_roundtrip`: a `#[cfg(test)]` constructor `ProcLink::spawn_program("/bin/cat", &[])` runs `cat` with stdin and stdout on the socketpair; a frame sent with `send` comes back byte-identical through the raw socket (proves both fds are wired to one socket).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `StartError` and `CallError` as listed; E29-A2 turns them into health state and action results.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: all functions block; callers run them inside `cx.spawn_blocking` (ASX section 4).
- Privacy: requests and replies are never logged; log only the request kind, req id and result at `debug` on target `tasklens::action`.
- Security: the helper path and pkexec path are fixed constants; no environment is passed.

## Notes
- Blocked on open item E29-OI-2 (socketpair on fds 0 and 1) and E29-OI-1 (frame and reply shapes).
- tl-engine may use rustix (ADR-001 row). No new dependency.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E29-014 E29: add privileged routing arm and actions/helper.rs to actions/mod.rs
description:
## Context
Routes actions the user asked to run as administrator (`ActionRequest.privileged == true`, sent by "Retry as administrator" and by privileged menu items) to the helper instead of the unprivileged `tl-ops` calls, with the same per-target events, summary and deadlines as E11's pipeline (PROC-058, PROC-076, ADR-005, ADR-006). There is no automatic retry and no automatic escalation. It also provides the helper hook that E11's `actions/{socket,recovery,dump}.rs` call for `SockDestroy`, `UnitWriteRecovery`/`UnitRemoveRecovery` on system units and privileged `Dump`. Sources: ADR-005 (event order, summary rule), ADR-006 (deadlines, helper allowlist, protected rules), R-004, R-117, PROC-058, PROC-060 to PROC-068, PROC-075, SYS-013, SYS-031.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/helper.rs` (new):
  - `pub(crate) async fn run_privileged(cx: &Cx, req: &ActionRequest, helper: &HelperHandle, ev: &EventSink)`: called after admission (E11 admission still applies: 16 in flight, 256 targets, identity, kernel thread; protected targets still need the UI confirmation, which happened before the request was sent).
  - Kind mapping per target: `Signal(s)` to `Signal { target, signal: s }`; `Suspend` to `Signal(Stop)`; `Resume` to `Signal(Cont)`; `SetNice`, `SetSched`, `SetAffinity`, `SetIoPriority` to the same-named requests; `ActionTarget::Thread` maps to `HelperTarget::Thread` (allowed for `Signal`, `SetNice`, `SetSched`, `SetAffinity`); `FreezeGroup`, `ThawGroup`, `KillGroup` on `ActionTarget::Cgroup` to the cgroup requests. `KillTree`: first a `Signal(Stop)` to every target, then `Signal(Kill)` to every target, in two passes, like E11's unprivileged tree (ADR-006). Any other kind or target type with `privileged = true` gives `Rejected(Unsupported)` for the request.
  - Deadlines: 2 s per target (ADR-006); when the session is `Locked` when the action starts, the first target also gets `START_DEADLINE` (120 s) for the polkit prompt.
  - Result mapping: `Done` to `Succeeded`; `Error(IdentityChanged)` to `Rejected(IdentityChanged)`; `NoSuchProcess` to `Failed(NoSuchProcess)`; `PermissionDenied` to `Failed(PermissionDenied)`; `Partial { done, total }` to `Failed(Partial { done, total })`; `Os(3)` (ESRCH after the call) to `OutcomeUnknown("process exited during the change")`; `Os(115)` to `OutcomeUnknown("freeze still in progress")`; other `Os(n)` to `Failed(Os(n))`; `NotAllowed(r)` to `Failed(Internal(r))`; call `Timeout` to `OutcomeUnknown("no answer from the administrator helper")`; `Exited` or `Protocol` to `Failed(Internal("administrator helper stopped"))`; start `Cancelled` and `NotAuthorized` to the two `ActionError` values named in open item E29-OI-3 (UI texts "Authentication cancelled" and "<failure text>: not authorized", R-117), applied to every remaining target; `Missing` to `Rejected(Unsupported)`.
  - Events in ADR-005 order: `Started`, one final state per target, then the summary with `target: None` (Succeeded only if every target succeeded; otherwise the worst in the order Failed, OutcomeUnknown, Rejected).
  - Hook for E11's P3 files: implement the hook E11-A1 defines for privileged operations (open item E29-OI-6 recommends `trait PrivilegedOps { async fn call(&self, cx: &Cx, req: HelperRequest, fd: Option<OwnedFd>, deadline: Duration) -> Result<Vec<HelperReply>, HelperCallError> }`) for `HelperHandle`.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/mod.rs` (E11 file, chain edit; the only change in it): `mod helper;` and one arm at the point where an admitted request is dispatched: `if req.privileged { helper::run_privileged(&cx, &req, &ctx.helper, &events).await; return; }`, plus the installation of `HelperHandle` as E11's hook (where E11-A1 expects it).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a LabRuntime engine with the fake helper and a privileged `Signal(Term)` on two targets **When** run **Then** the fake receives two `Signal` requests and the UI receives `Started`, two `Succeeded` and a summary `Succeeded`.
- **Given** the fake answers `Error(PermissionDenied)` for target 2 **When** run **Then** target 2 is `Failed(PermissionDenied)` and the summary is `Failed(PermissionDenied)`.
- **Given** a privileged `KillTree` on three targets **When** run **Then** the fake sees three `Signal(Stop)` requests before any `Signal(Kill)`.
- **Given** the session is `Locked` and the fake start returns 126 **When** a privileged `SetNice` runs **Then** every target ends with the "authentication cancelled" error and no `SetNice` frame is sent.

title: E29-A2 Helper session in the engine
description:
## Context
Anchor E29-A2: the helper session inside the engine. One task owns at most one running helper, starts it on `StartHelperSession` or on the first privileged request (one polkit prompt), ends it on `EndHelperSession`, notices the helper's 300 s idle exit, and publishes the shield state `HealthSnapshot.helper: HelperState { Missing, Locked, Starting, Unlocked }` so the UI shield, Grant access and Retry buttons follow it (APP-003, PROC-076, UI-FND-028, UI-SHL-011). Every privileged engine path (actions, Properties reads, handle search, socket attribution) calls the helper through the `HelperHandle` defined here. Sources: ADR-006, ADR-004 (task tree, no asupersync types in public API), ASX sections 4 to 6 (spawn_blocking, timeout, channels), R-003, R-117, APP-003, PROC-076, UI-FND-028.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/helper/mod.rs`:
```rust
pub(crate) enum HelperMsg {
    Start,                                   // Command::StartHelperSession (E29-OI-3)
    End,                                     // Command::EndHelperSession
    Call { req: HelperRequest, fd: Option<OwnedFd>, deadline: Duration,
           replies: async_channel::Sender<HelperReply>, done: oneshot::Sender<Result<(), HelperCallError>> },
}
pub(crate) enum HelperCallError { Missing, Cancelled, NotAuthorized, StartFailed(Arc<str>), Timeout, Exited, Protocol }

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct HelperHandle { tx: mpsc::Sender<HelperMsg> }   // mpsc capacity 64
impl HelperHandle {
    /// Queues the request; starts the session first when Locked (one polkit prompt, 120 s).
    /// Returns every reply in order. Err(Busy) if the queue is full.
    pub(crate) async fn call(&self, cx: &Cx, req: HelperRequest, fd: Option<OwnedFd>, deadline: Duration)
        -> Result<Vec<HelperReply>, HelperCallError>;
    /// Streaming form for ScanStrings and NetnsSockDiagDump.
    pub(crate) async fn call_stream(&self, cx: &Cx, req: HelperRequest, deadline: Duration)
        -> Result<async_channel::Receiver<HelperReply>, HelperCallError>;
    pub(crate) fn state(&self) -> HelperState;     // last published state, from a shared AtomicU8
}
pub(crate) async fn helper_task(cx: Cx, rx: mpsc::Receiver<HelperMsg>, updates: mpsc::Sender<EngineMsg>);
```
- `helper_task` runs in the engine session's region (spawned beside the action region by the session; the spawn line is part of open item E29-OI-5) and processes messages one at a time:
  - State at start: `Missing` if `/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper` or `/usr/bin/pkexec` is not a regular file, else `Locked`. Re-checked on every `Start`.
  - `Start` while `Locked`: publish `Starting`; run `HelperSession::start(ProcLink::spawn()?)` inside `cx.spawn_blocking`, wrapped in `time::timeout(START_DEADLINE + 5 s)`. Ok: `Unlocked`. `Cancelled`, `NotAuthorized`, `Failed`: back to `Locked` with a start outcome. `Missing`: `Missing`. `Start` while `Starting` or `Unlocked` is ignored.
  - `End` while `Unlocked`: `session.end()` in `spawn_blocking`; `Locked`; no start outcome (no toast).
  - `Call`: if `Missing`, answer `Missing`. If `Locked`, run the `Start` steps first and answer the start error if any. Then move the session into `spawn_blocking`, run `call` with the request's deadline, forward each reply to `replies`, move the session back. `Timeout`, `Exited` or `Protocol` drop the session and publish `Locked`.
  - Idle watch: while `Unlocked` and no message arrives, every 1 s check `session.is_alive()`; a helper that exited (its 300 s idle exit) publishes `Locked` with no start outcome (APP-003: no toast).
  - Cancellation (engine shutdown): `session.end()` then return `Outcome::Cancelled`; the helper also dies through `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`.
- Publishing: each state change sends `EngineMsg::Source(SourceUpdate::Helper { state, start })` (variant name per E29-OI-5) where `start: Option<HelperStartOutcome::{Cancelled, NotAuthorized, Failed(Arc<str>)}>` is set only on a failed start that the user caused. The reducer stores it in `HealthSnapshot.helper` and `HealthSnapshot.helper_start: Option<(u32 seq, HelperStartOutcome)>` (seq counts up so the UI toasts each failure once).
- Deadlines: the start is bounded by `START_DEADLINE` (120 s, ADR-006 "any call that may show a polkit prompt"); each call by its own deadline; `time::timeout` around every `spawn_blocking` join (ASX section 6; a stuck blocking job is not interrupted, its result is discarded).
- Never use `select!`, `race!`, `GenServer` or asupersync signals (ASX section 10).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a LabRuntime engine with a `FakeLink` factory (test hook replacing `ProcLink::spawn`) **When** `Start` arrives **Then** the published states are `Starting` then `Unlocked`.
- **Given** the fake reports exit 126 **When** `Start` arrives **Then** states `Starting` then `Locked` with `start = Some(Cancelled)`.
- **Given** the helper files are absent (fake path check) **When** the task starts **Then** the state is `Missing`, and a `Call` answers `HelperCallError::Missing` without spawning.
- **Given** `Locked` **When** a `Call(Signal..)` arrives **Then** one start happens, then the call, and exactly one `Starting` then `Unlocked` is published.
- **Given** `Unlocked` **When** `End` arrives **Then** the fake saw `close`, and `Locked` is published with `start = None`.
- **Given** `Unlocked` and a fake whose process exits by itself **When** 1 s of virtual time passes **Then** `Locked` is published with `start = None`.
- **Given** a fake that never answers a call **When** the call's 2 s deadline passes **Then** the caller gets `Timeout` and the state is `Locked`.
- **Given** two `Call`s queued **When** processed **Then** the second's frames are sent only after the first's final reply.
- **Given** the engine shuts down while `Unlocked` **When** the region drains **Then** `end()` ran and the drain is `Quiescent`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/helper/mod.rs`: fill in.
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_helper.rs`: create.

## Tests (LabRuntime, `LabConfig::new(seed).max_steps(1_000_000)`, `run_with_auto_advance()`, each ending with `run_until_quiescent_with_report().lab_test_passed()`)
- `lab_helper.rs::start_publishes_starting_then_unlocked`
- `lab_helper.rs::start_cancelled_126_back_to_locked`
- `lab_helper.rs::missing_helper_never_spawns`
- `lab_helper.rs::call_while_locked_starts_once`
- `lab_helper.rs::end_closes_and_locks_without_toast`
- `lab_helper.rs::idle_exit_detected_within_1s`
- `lab_helper.rs::call_timeout_drops_session`
- `lab_helper.rs::calls_are_serial`
- `lab_helper.rs::shutdown_ends_session` with `#[explore_seeds(seeds = 0..16, workers = 2, chaos)]`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: start outcomes and call errors as listed.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: idle cost one 1 s timer while `Unlocked`; nothing while `Locked`.
- Privacy: no request content in logs; `info!` on target `tasklens::action` for session start and end only (no user names).
- Security: no automatic escalation: a session starts only on a user action (shield, Retry as administrator, Grant access, Search all, restricted count, unlock at launch) because only those send `Start` or a privileged call (ADR-006 consequence).

## Notes
- Blocked on open items E29-OI-3 (`Command::StartHelperSession`, `Command::EndHelperSession`, `HelperState`, `helper_start` in `HealthSnapshot`, failure variants) and E29-OI-5 (who spawns `helper_task`, who routes the two commands to `HelperMsg`, the `SourceUpdate::Helper` variant and its reducer arm). Use the names the leader settles.

title: E29-019 Setup status probe and tasklens-setup runner in the engine
description:
## Context
The engine side of the Additional Setup window: `Command::SetupStatus` (journal group, lm_sensors, RAPL readability, helper presence, hwmon fans) and `Command::RunSetup { step }`, which runs `pkexec /usr/lib/tasklens/tasklens-setup <subcommand>` on the blocking pool and reports its output (ADR-005 Command list, UI-PRF-052, PERF-105 to PERF-108, APP-042, APP-049, R-028, R-029). The UI reads no system files itself (ADR-001 rule 1). How the answer reaches the UI is not defined; open item E29-OI-4 recommends a `setup` part of `HealthSnapshot`. The file `helper/setup.rs` is not listed in section 2 (open item E29-OI-13). Sources: ADR-005, UI-PRF-052, PERF-105, PERF-106, PERF-108, APP-049, R-028, R-029, R-117, table (c).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/helper/setup.rs` (new; `mod setup;` in `helper/mod.rs`):
- `pub(crate) fn probe_status(root: &SysRoot) -> SetupStatus` (blocking), with the E29-OI-4 fields:
  - `rapl`: `NoZone` when no `/sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl:*` directory with an `energy_uj` file exists; `Readable { tasklens_rule }` when every zone's `energy_uj` opens for reading, with `tasklens_rule = /etc/udev/rules.d/99-tasklens-powercap.rules exists`; `NotReadable` otherwise. `/etc/udev/rules.d/99-powercap.rules` is never opened for writing and only its existence may be read.
  - `journal_group`: the current process's supplementary groups (`getgroups`) contain the gid of `systemd-journal` from `/etc/group`.
  - `helper_installed`: `/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper` is a regular file.
  - `lm_sensors`: `/usr/bin/sensors-detect` is a regular file.
  - `hwmon_fan`: any `/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/fan*_input` exists.
  - `sensors_conf`: `/etc/modules-load.d/tasklens-sensors.conf` exists.
- `pub(crate) fn run_step(step: SetupStep, out: &mut dyn FnMut(&str)) -> SetupOutcome` (blocking): subcommand per step: `RaplEnable` `rapl-enable`, `RaplRevert` `rapl-revert`, `SensorsDetect` `sensors-detect`, `PolkitRuleOn` `polkit-rule on`, `PolkitRuleOff` `polkit-rule off`. Runs `std::process::Command::new("/usr/bin/pkexec").arg("/usr/lib/tasklens/tasklens-setup").args(sub)` with `env_clear()`, stdin null, stdout and stderr both to one pipe, reading lines as they come (`out` per line, output capped at 64 KiB, then "…" and the rest discarded). Deadline 120 s (ADR-006 polkit row): past it, SIGKILL and wait, outcome `Failed("timed out")`. Exit 0: `Succeeded`; 126 or 127: `Cancelled` (UI-PRF-052: no failure block, status unchanged); other: `Failed(<captured output>)`. Never `asupersync::process`.
- Command handling (called from the routing added in E29-020): `SetupStatus` runs `probe_status` in `cx.spawn_blocking` and publishes `setup.status`; `RunSetup { step }` publishes `setup.run = Running { seq, step }`, appends output lines into `setup.run.output` at most every 100 ms, then the final outcome, then runs `probe_status` again and publishes it. A second `RunSetup` while one is running is ignored (the UI disables the buttons).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake `SysRoot` with two RAPL zones, both readable, and no tasklens rule file **When** `probe_status` runs **Then** `rapl == Readable { tasklens_rule: false }` ("Enabled (existing rule)").
- **Given** a fake root with one unreadable zone (mode 0400 file owned by another user is not possible in a temp dir, so the test uses a missing read permission bit: mode 0200) **When** probed **Then** `NotReadable`.
- **Given** no powercap directory **When** probed **Then** `NoZone`.
- **Given** a fake script path (test-only `run_step_with(program, args, ..)`) that prints two lines and exits 0 **When** run **Then** `out` saw both lines and the outcome is `Succeeded`.
- **Given** the fake exits 126, then 127 **When** run **Then** both give `Cancelled`.
- **Given** the fake prints "boom" and exits 1 **When** run **Then** `Failed("boom\n")`.
- **Given** the fake prints 100 KiB **When** run **Then** the captured output is 64 KiB plus "…".
- **Given** the fake sleeps 200 s **When** run (deadline lowered to 1 s in the test constructor) **Then** `Failed("timed out")` and no zombie remains (`/proc/<child>` absent).

title: E29-021 Polkit policy file with three actions
description:
## Context
The polkit policy file with exactly three tasklens actions (R-002, table (c), ADR-006): the helper, the setup script, and the reserved network monitor. pkexec maps a program to its action through the `org.freedesktop.policykit.exec.path` annotation, so each action names its fixed binary. ## Deliverable
`packaging/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.policy`, installed by the PKGBUILD (E33) to `/usr/share/polkit-1/actions/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.policy`:

<!DOCTYPE policyconfig PUBLIC "-//freedesktop//DTD PolicyKit Policy Configuration 1.0//EN"
 "http://www.freedesktop.org/standards/PolicyKit/1/policyconfig.dtd">
<policyconfig>
  <vendor>tasklens</vendor>
  <icon_name>io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens</icon_name>
  <action id="io.github.oysteinkrog.tasklens.helper">
    <description>Run tasklens administrator actions</description>
    <message>Authentication is required to let tasklens act on other users' processes, system services and network connections.</message>
    <defaults><allow_any>auth_admin</allow_any><allow_inactive>auth_admin</allow_inactive><allow_active>auth_admin_keep</allow_active></defaults>

  </action>
  <action id="io.github.oysteinkrog.tasklens.setup">
    <description>Change tasklens system setup</description>

    <annotate key="org.freedesktop.policykit.exec.path">/usr/lib/tasklens/tasklens-setup</annotate>
  </action>
  <action id="io.github.oysteinkrog.tasklens.netmon">
    <description>Run the tasklens network monitor</description>
    <message>Authentication is required to run the tasklens network monitor.</message>
    <defaults><allow_any>auth_admin</allow_any><allow_inactive>auth_admin</allow_inactive><allow_active>auth_admin_keep</allow_active></defaults>
    <annotate key="org.freedesktop.policykit.exec.path">/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-netmon</annotate>

title: E29-023 tasklens-setup sensors-detect and sensors-revert
description:
## Context
P4 branch of `tasklens-setup`: `sensors-detect` runs `sensors-detect --auto`, writes the modules it finds to `/etc/modules-load.d/tasklens-sensors.conf` and loads them with `modprobe`, so fan pages appear and survive a reboot (PERF-108, table (c)). PERF-108's "Revert" removes that file, but table (c) lists no revert subcommand; open item E29-OI-14 recommends `sensors-revert`. This bead adds both and waits for the leader on the second.

## Deliverable
In `packaging/tasklens-setup` (same root and test-mode rules as E29-022):
- `sensors-detect`:
  - Test mode for this branch: the presence check looks at `$ROOT/usr/bin/sensors-detect`, and `sensors-detect --auto` is replaced by printing `would run: sensors-detect --auto` followed by the content of `$ROOT/sensors-detect.out`.
  - If `/usr/bin/sensors-detect` is missing: print `Install lm_sensors to detect fan sensors`, exit 3.
  - Run `sensors-detect --auto` and keep its output; print it.
  - Collect module names from output lines matching `^MODULE_[0-9]+=` (value after `=`, surrounding quotes removed); each name must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`, others are skipped with a line `skipped module name: <name>`.
  - No modules: print `No sensor modules found`, exit 0, and write nothing.
  - Else write one name per line to `$ROOT/etc/modules-load.d/tasklens-sensors.conf.tmp`, `chmod 0644`, `mv -f` to `tasklens-sensors.conf`, run `modprobe <name>` for each, print `Enabled`.
- `sensors-revert` (pending E29-OI-14): `rm -f "$ROOT/etc/modules-load.d/tasklens-sensors.conf"`, print `Reverted. The modules stay loaded until the next reboot.`
- The usage line gains `sensors-revert`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Given** an output line `MODULE_2=evil;rm` **When** parsed **Then** it is skipped with `skipped module name: evil;rm` (security regression).
- **Given** no `MODULE_` lines **When** run **Then** `No sensor modules found`, exit 0, no file.
- **Given** test mode and no `usr/bin/sensors-detect` under the root **When** run **Then** exit 3 with the lm_sensors line.
- **Given** an existing conf **When** `sensors-revert` runs **Then** the file is gone.

description:
## Context

- "Enable" opens `TlDialog::confirm`: title "Enable CPU power draw?", body "Lets every local user read CPU energy counters. This can leak information about other programs (CVE-2020-8694).", buttons "Enable" (primary) and "Cancel". Confirm sends `Command::RunSetup { step: SetupStep::RaplEnable }`.
- "Revert" opens: title "Revert CPU power draw?", body "Removes the tasklens udev rule. A reboot may be needed before the files return to mode 0400.", buttons "Revert" (danger) and "Cancel". Confirm sends `RunSetup { step: RaplRevert }`.
- Running (from `HealthSnapshot.setup.run` with `phase == Running` for this row's step): the card's buttons are disabled and the badge shows a 12 px spinner icon with the text `Running…`. The pkexec prompt is the system's own.
- Outcome (a `run` whose `seq` is newer than the last one this window handled):
  - `Succeeded`: a line under the buttons "Done. No restart needed." in `status.success`; for RAPL steps send `Command::ReprobeSource(SourceId::Cpu)` once, so the Power draw row changes within 2 s; the status badge follows the next `setup.status`.
  - `Failed(output)`: a block under the buttons: "Setup failed" (`t_sm`, weight 500, `status.danger`), the output in a mono read-only scroll area (max height 160), buttons "Copy output" (copies the output text, toast "Copied to clipboard") and "Retry" (sends the same `RunSetup` again).
  - `Cancelled` (pkexec 126 or 127): no block; the card keeps its old status.
- `send` returning `Err(CommandError::Busy)` leaves the card idle with no block.

title: E29-030 E29: add Shift-at-launch detection to window/main.rs (U-43)
description:
## Context
"Shift held at launch" unlocks privileged actions at start (table (b), APP-003). On Wayland a client gets no modifier state before its window has focus, so the main window counts Shift as held when its first `on_modifiers_changed` event within 500 ms of first focus has `shift` set; this must be verified on KWin (U-43, R-124). If KWin sends no modifiers on first focus, the Shift path is dropped on Wayland and `privilege.unlock_at_launch` remains. The detection code lives in E20's `window/main.rs` (and the X11 `XkbGetState` path in E33's `tl-app/src/main.rs`, which needs an X11 library outside tl-app's ADR-001 row); section 2 gives E29 no chain edit in either. Open item E29-OI-19 recommends one E29 chain edit in `window/main.rs` and the same first-focus rule on X11. This bead waits for the leader.

## Deliverable
Assuming E29-OI-19 is accepted as recommended:
- Step 1, verify U-43: run tasklens on the owner's KWin Wayland session with a temporary `info!(target: "tasklens::ui", shift = ?, ms_since_focus = ?)` in the first `on_modifiers_changed` handler, start it from KRunner and from a terminal with Shift held, and record whether the event arrives within 500 ms with `shift` set. Record the result (yes or no, with the measured ms) in this bead's close reason. Remove the temporary log.
- Step 2a (U-43 holds): chain edit to `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`: `MainWindow` records `first_focus_at` on its first focus; its `on_modifiers_changed` handler, while `now - first_focus_at <= 500 ms` and not yet decided, sets `shift_at_launch = event.modifiers.shift` and decides once. The step-11 launch hook (E20) dispatches `StartHelperSession` once when `shift_at_launch` or `privilege.unlock_at_launch` is true. The same rule runs on X11 (GPUI delivers modifier events there too); no `XkbGetState`.
- Step 2b (U-43 fails): no code; record "Shift at launch dropped on Wayland (U-43)" in the close reason and tell the leader so table (b) and R-124 can be updated.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a `TestAppContext` main window **When** focus arrives and a modifiers event with `shift = true` follows 100 ms later **Then** exactly one `StartHelperSession` is sent after the first frame.
- **Given** the shift event arrives 600 ms after focus **When** processed **Then** no `StartHelperSession` is sent (unless `unlock_at_launch` is on).
- **Given** two shift events within 500 ms **When** processed **Then** one start at most.
- **Given** `unlock_at_launch = true` and Shift also held **When** launched **Then** one start, not two.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`: chain edit (step 2a only).
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shield.rs`: add the four tests.

## Tests
- `ui_shield.rs::shift_within_500ms_starts_once`
- `ui_shield.rs::shift_after_500ms_ignored`
- `ui_shield.rs::shift_twice_starts_once`
- `ui_shield.rs::shift_and_setting_start_once`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one comparison per modifiers event during the first 500 ms.
- Privacy: N/A
- Security: the start still shows the polkit prompt; Shift only triggers it.

description:

title: E29-002 Helper process operations with own identity check
description:
## Context
The helper's process operations: signals, nice, scheduling policy, affinity and I/O priority on any user's process or thread, as root. They are the same `tl-ops` functions the unprivileged engine uses (ADR-001 consequence, ADR-006), and the helper re-runs `open_verified` itself on every target; it never trusts the engine's check (ADR-006, R-004). Sources: ADR-006 (identity revalidation, PID-based rules, thread targets, deadlines), R-004, R-097, PROC-060 to PROC-068, PROC-076.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-helper/src/ops.rs` (new; add `mod ops;` to `main.rs`):
- `pub fn run_process_op(req: &HelperRequest, boot: BootId) -> HelperReply` handling exactly `Signal`, `SetNice`, `SetSched`, `SetAffinity`, `SetIoPriority`. Any other variant returns `HelperReply::Error(HelperError::NotAllowed("not a process operation".into()))`.
- `boot` is read once at helper start from `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` with `tl_model::time::BootId` parsing and passed in.
- Per target:
  - `HelperTarget::Process(key)`: call `tl_ops::process::open_verified(key, boot)` first; on `IdentityChanged` reply `Error(IdentityChanged)` and do nothing else.
  - `HelperTarget::Thread { process, tid }`: allowed only for `Signal`, `SetNice`, `SetSched`, `SetAffinity`; `SetIoPriority` with a thread target replies `Error(NotAllowed("thread target"))`. Verify the process with `open_verified`, then the thread through the same tl-ops thread-target function the engine uses (it checks `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>` and uses `tgkill` for signals).
  - Then call the tl-ops function for the kind (signal through the verified pidfd; nice, sched, affinity, ioprio on every TID with the before and after pidfd poll). Map `OpsError` to `HelperError`: `IdentityChanged`, `NoSuchProcess`, `PermissionDenied` (EPERM, EACCES), `Partial { done, total }`, `Os(errno)`. A pidfd readable after the call (process exited during the change) maps to `Error(Os(libc ESRCH = 3))` so the engine reports `OutcomeUnknown("process exited during the change")`.
  - Success replies `Done`.
- Value checks before any syscall, each failing with `Error(NotAllowed(<reason>))` and no syscall: nice outside `-20..=19` ("nice out of range"); `rt_prio` not in `1..=99` for `Fifo`/`Rr` or not `0` for `Other`/`Batch`/`Idle` ("rt_prio out of range"); `IoPriority` level above 7 ("ioprio level out of range"); `Signal::Other(n)` with `n == 0` or `n > 64` ("signal out of range"); an empty `CpuSet` ("empty cpu set").
- The helper never targets PID 1 with `Signal(Kill)`, `Signal(Term)`, `Signal(Stop)` or any `Signal::Other`: it replies `Error(NotAllowed("pid 1"))`. (The engine refuses earlier; this is the helper's own guard.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a child `sleep 60` started by the test and its captured `ProcessKey` **When** `run_process_op(Signal { target: Process(key), signal: Term })` runs **Then** the reply is `Done` and the child exits by SIGTERM.
- **Given** the same key with `start_ticks + 1` **When** any process op runs **Then** the reply is `Error(IdentityChanged)` and the child is still alive.
- **Given** a key whose `boot_id` differs from `boot` **When** any op runs **Then** the reply is `Error(IdentityChanged)`.
- **Given** `SetNice { nice: 25 }` **When** run **Then** the reply is `Error(NotAllowed("nice out of range"))` and no syscall is made.
- **Given** `SetIoPriority` with a thread target **When** run **Then** the reply is `Error(NotAllowed("thread target"))`.
- **Given** a request for PID 1 with `Signal(Kill)` **When** run **Then** the reply is `Error(NotAllowed("pid 1"))`.
- **Given** a `FreezeGroup` request **When** passed to `run_process_op` **Then** the reply is `Error(NotAllowed("not a process operation"))`.
- **Given** a child and `SetNice { nice: 5 }` as the same user **When** run **Then** `Done`, and every TID of the child shows nice 5 in `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/stat` field 19.

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/src/ops.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/main.rs`: add `mod ops;`.

## Tests
- `ops.rs::tests::signal_verified_child` (spawns `sleep 60` as the current user; no root needed).
- `ops.rs::tests::stale_start_ticks_rejected` (security regression: the helper does its own `open_verified`).
- `ops.rs::tests::boot_id_mismatch_rejected` (security regression).
- `ops.rs::tests::value_ranges_rejected_before_syscall` (nice 25, nice -21, rt_prio 0 with Rr, rt_prio 5 with Other, ioprio level 8, Signal::Other(0), Signal::Other(65), empty CpuSet).
- `ops.rs::tests::pid1_guard` (security regression).
- `ops.rs::tests::thread_target_kinds` (ioprio on a thread is refused; nice on a thread of the child succeeds).
- `ops.rs::tests::set_nice_every_tid`: re-execute the test binary (`std::env::current_exe()`) with env `TL_HELPER_TEST_THREADS=3`; in that mode the test harness entry starts 3 threads and sleeps 60 s. `SetNice { nice: 5 }` gives `Done` and all 4 TIDs show nice 5.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: only the `HelperError` values above; the engine turns them into `ActionError`.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one syscall loop per TID; no allocation per TID beyond the TID list.
- Privacy: log nothing about the target except pid and the result at `debug` (ADR-015). Never log command lines.
- Security: this runs as root. Every target is re-verified here. No path or free-form argument exists in these requests.

## Notes
- Protocol names used below are those of `tl-model/src/helper_proto.rs` (E03-A2). This bead expects the shape recorded as open item E29-OI-1 in `docs/plan/b4-engine-workers.md`: every frame is `HelperFrame { req: u32, body }` (the engine picks `req`, the helper echoes it on every reply frame); requests `Hello { proto }`, `Signal { target, signal }`, `SetNice { target, nice }`, `SetSched { target, policy, rt_prio }`, `SetAffinity { target, set }`, `SetIoPriority { key, prio }`, `FreezeGroup(CgroupRef)`, `ThawGroup(CgroupRef)`, `KillGroup(CgroupRef)`, `ReadProcessFiles { key, files }`, `ScanStrings { key, opts }`, `CancelScan`, `Dump { key, mode }`, `ResolveSocketInodes { inodes }`, `SockDestroy { family, proto, four_tuple, cookie }`, `WriteServiceDropIn { unit, keys }`, `NetnsSockDiagDump { netns_ino }`, where `target` is `HelperTarget::{Process(ProcessKey), Thread { process: ProcessKey, tid: u32 }}`; replies `Hello { proto, pid }`, `Done`, `Error(HelperError)`, `Files(..)`, `Strings { .. , last }`, `Inodes(..)`, `SockDiag { bytes, last }`, with `HelperError::{IdentityChanged, NoSuchProcess, PermissionDenied, Partial { done, total }, Os(i32), NotAllowed(Arc<str>), TooLarge}`. If E03-A2 landed different names, use E03's names and keep the behaviour written here.
- tl-ops function names: use the public functions E07-A1 delivers in `crates/tl-ops/src/process.rs` (`open_verified`, signal, nice, sched, affinity, ioprio, thread-target variants). Do not add syscalls in tl-helper; there is no `unsafe` here.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E29-003 Helper cgroup freeze, thaw and kill for any user
description:
## Context
The helper's cgroup operations: `FreezeGroup`, `ThawGroup` and `KillGroup` for any user's cgroup under `/sys/fs/cgroup` (ADR-006 allowlist). The engine's own `tl_ops::cgroup::open_validated(cg, uid)` only accepts the current user's `app.slice`, so the helper needs a validation rule for other uids. The docs do not give that rule; this bead implements the rule recommended in open item E29-OI-8 and must not start until the leader accepts it. Sources: ADR-006 (cgroup operations, helper allowlist), R-004, PROC-062, PROC-063.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-helper/src/ops.rs`, `pub fn run_cgroup_op(req: &HelperRequest) -> HelperReply` for `FreezeGroup(cg)`, `ThawGroup(cg)`, `KillGroup(cg)`:
- Validation (E29-OI-8 recommendation), each failure `Error(NotAllowed(<reason>))` with no write:
  1. `cg.rel_path` is non-empty, at most 4096 bytes, relative (no leading `/`), has no NUL, and no component equal to `.` or `..` or empty ("bad cgroup path").
  2. The first component is `user.slice` or `system.slice` ("cgroup outside user.slice and system.slice").
  3. The last component ends in `.scope` or `.service` ("not a scope or service").
  4. Open each component with `openat(dirfd, name, O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC)` starting from a dirfd on `/sys/fs/cgroup`, never by joined path string; `fstat` the final dirfd: `st_ino == cg.cgroup_id`, else `Error(IdentityChanged)`.
  5. The helper's own cgroup (from `/proc/self/cgroup`) and the cgroup of the helper's parent process (tasklens, `getppid()`) are not equal to or inside the target ("would affect tasklens"). `init.scope` is refused ("init.scope").
- Writes through the validated dirfd with the tl-ops write helpers from E07-A2 (`cgroup.freeze` "1" or "0", `cgroup.kill` "1"), and for `FreezeGroup` the same `cgroup.events` wait as the engine (poll `frozen 1` every 50 ms for up to 2 s; not frozen in time replies `Error(Os(EINPROGRESS = 115))`, which the engine maps to `OutcomeUnknown("freeze still in progress")`).
- `run_process_op` from E29-002 still refuses these kinds; `dispatch` (E29-A1) calls `run_cgroup_op` for them.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a `systemd-run --user --scope sleep 60` scope and its captured `CgroupRef` **When** `FreezeGroup` runs as the same user **Then** the reply is `Done` and `cgroup.events` shows `frozen 1`; `ThawGroup` then gives `Done` and `frozen 0`.
- **Given** `rel_path` `user.slice/../system.slice/x.service` **When** run **Then** `Error(NotAllowed("bad cgroup path"))`.
- **Given** `rel_path` `/user.slice/a.scope` **When** run **Then** `Error(NotAllowed("bad cgroup path"))`.
- **Given** `rel_path` `machine.slice/x.scope` **When** run **Then** `Error(NotAllowed("cgroup outside user.slice and system.slice"))`.
- **Given** `rel_path` `user.slice/user-1000.slice` **When** run **Then** `Error(NotAllowed("not a scope or service"))`.
- **Given** a valid path with a different `cgroup_id` **When** run **Then** `Error(IdentityChanged)` and nothing is written.
- **Given** the cgroup that contains the test process itself **When** `KillGroup` runs **Then** `Error(NotAllowed("would affect tasklens"))`.
- **Given** a symlink component (test with a tmpfs fake root is not possible for cgroupfs; check through the `O_NOFOLLOW` unit of the open loop on a temp dir tree) **When** the loop meets it **Then** it fails with `bad cgroup path`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/src/ops.rs`: add `run_cgroup_op` and the validator `fn validate_cgroup(cg: &CgroupRef, root: BorrowedFd) -> Result<OwnedFd, HelperError>`.

## Tests
- `ops.rs::tests::cgroup_path_rules` (pure checks 1 to 3 on 8 strings; security regression).
- `ops.rs::tests::cgroup_open_loop_no_follow` (the per-component open loop against a temp directory tree with a symlink; security regression).
- `ops.rs::tests::cgroup_inode_mismatch` (real cgroupfs, own scope).
- `ops.rs::tests::cgroup_self_refused` (security regression).
- `crates/tl-helper/tests/real_helper_root.rs::freeze_other_users_scope` (`#[ignore]`, root only, written in E29-012).

- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A

- Security: root writes to cgroupfs; path handling is by dirfd only.

title: E29-004 Helper ReadProcessFiles
description:
## Context
`ReadProcessFiles { key, files }` lets the engine read root-only `/proc/<pid>` files of other users' processes, so Restricted cells and Properties tabs fill in once the helper runs (PROC-076, R-004, R-098). The set is fixed: `io`, `fd_list`, `fdinfo`, `environ`, `maps`, `smaps`, `smaps_rollup`, `ns`, `cwd`, `exe`, `status`. There is no path argument. Sources: ADR-006, R-004, R-098, PROC-078 to PROC-084, PROC-096, ADR-015 (privacy).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-helper/src/files.rs` (new; add `mod files;` to `main.rs`):
- `pub fn read_process_files(key: ProcessKey, files: HelperFiles, boot: BootId) -> HelperReply`.
- Steps: `tl_ops::process::open_verified(key, boot)` (keeps the pidfd open for the whole call, so `/proc/<pid>` cannot be reused); open `/proc/<pid>` as a dirfd with `O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC`; read each requested entry relative to that dirfd with `openat`, never by joined path:
  - `io`, `environ`, `maps`, `smaps`, `smaps_rollup`, `status`: file bytes.
  - `cwd`, `exe`: `readlinkat` bytes.
  - `fd_list`: `readdir` of `fd/`, then `readlinkat` of each entry; `Vec<(u32 fd, Vec<u8> target)>` sorted by fd.
  - `fdinfo`: for each fd in `fd/`, the bytes of `fdinfo/<fd>`; `Vec<(u32, Vec<u8>)>`.
  - `ns`: `readlinkat` of `ns/{cgroup,ipc,mnt,net,pid,pid_for_children,time,time_for_children,user,uts}`; `Vec<(Arc<str> name, Vec<u8> target)>`, missing names skipped.
- Each file's result is `Ok(bytes)` or `Err(errno)` (EACCES, ENOENT, ESRCH as read); one failing file never fails the others.
- Size: the reply's total payload is at most 4 MiB (4_194_304 bytes) per request (ADR-006). Files are read in the order of the list above; once the running total would pass 4_194_304 minus 4096 bytes of headroom, that file and every later one get `Err(EFBIG = 27)`. A single read is capped at the remaining budget, never more.
- After the reads, check the pidfd once more (poll timeout 0); readable (exited) gives `Error(NoSuchProcess)` for the whole reply, so no data from a different process is ever returned.
- The reply is sent through the `tl_model::wire` multi-frame writer (64 KiB frames), done by `dispatch` (E29-A1).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Given** a stale `start_ticks` **When** called **Then** the reply is `Error(IdentityChanged)` and no file was opened.
- **Given** a child that exits during the call (test hook: a child that exits after 50 ms and a read of `smaps` of a large mapping) **When** the post-check sees the pidfd readable **Then** the reply is `Error(NoSuchProcess)`.
- **Given** `MAPS | SMAPS` where `smaps` is larger than the remaining budget **When** called **Then** `maps` is `Ok`, `smaps` is `Err(27)`, and the encoded reply is at most 4_194_304 bytes.
- **Given** a request where the target is PID 1 and `ENVIRON` **When** run as an ordinary user (the test) **Then** `environ` is `Err(13)` (EACCES) and other files still return.

title: E29-005 Helper ScanStrings streaming
description:
## Context
`ScanStrings { key, opts }` runs the Strings tab scan as root and streams result batches (PROC-084, R-004), because with `ptrace_scope = 1` reading another process's memory needs CAP_SYS_PTRACE. The scanner already exists in `tl-collect` (E05-A3, `src/proc/strings.rs`), but ADR-001 does not let `tl-helper` depend on `tl-collect`, and PROC-084's 256 MiB result limit does not fit the 4 MiB per-request cap. Both are open item E29-OI-7. This bead is written for the recommended resolution and must wait for the leader's answer.

## Deliverable
Assuming E29-OI-7 is accepted as recommended (ADR-001 row `tl-helper: tl-model, tl-ops, tl-collect`; a streamed request's 4 MiB cap applies to each reply message, not the whole stream):
- `crates/tl-helper/Cargo.toml`: add `tl-collect = { workspace = true }`.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/files.rs`: `pub fn scan_strings(key: ProcessKey, opts: &StringScanOpts, boot: BootId, out: &mut dyn FnMut(HelperReply) -> std::io::Result<()>, cancel: &dyn Fn() -> bool) -> std::io::Result<()>`.
  - `open_verified(key, boot)` first; `Error(IdentityChanged)` stops.
  - Runs the E05-A3 scanner with `opts` (minimum length 4 to 64, default 4; encodings ASCII, UTF-8, UTF-16LE; "Include file-backed mappings" off by default; regions from `maps`: readable, private anonymous plus heap and stack, file-backed only with the option, skipping `[vvar]`, `[vsyscall]` and device mappings; 1 MiB read chunks).
  - Emits `HelperReply::Strings { batch, progress_pct, found, last: false }` whenever the batch reaches 2,000 strings or 48 KiB of encoded text, whichever first, so one batch fits one 64 KiB frame.
  - Between chunks calls `cancel()`; true ends the scan with a final `Strings { batch: [], last: true, stopped: Cancelled }`.
  - Stops at 1,000,000 strings or 256 MiB of text with `stopped: Limit` (the UI shows "String scan stopped: not enough memory."); target exit mid-scan gives `stopped: Exited`; read failure gives `Error(Os(errno))`.
  - Kernel threads (flag from `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 9 `PF_KTHREAD`): `Error(NotAllowed("kernel thread"))`.
- `cancel` is fed by `dispatch` (E29-A1): it polls stdin with timeout 0 between chunks and treats a `CancelScan` frame for the running `req` as cancel.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a child that holds the ASCII string `tasklens-marker-1234` and the UTF-16LE string `wine-marker` in heap memory **When** `scan_strings` runs with defaults **Then** both strings arrive in some batch and the final message has `last: true`.
- **Given** `min_len = 30` **When** the same scan runs **Then** neither marker is reported.
- **Given** a `cancel` that returns true after the first chunk **When** run **Then** the last message has `stopped: Cancelled` and no further batches follow.
- **Given** a stale key **When** run **Then** the only message is `Error(IdentityChanged)` (security regression).
- **Given** every emitted batch **When** encoded with postcard **Then** it is at most 65_536 bytes.

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/Cargo.toml`: add the tl-collect line.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/files.rs`: add `scan_strings`.

## Tests

- `files.rs::tests::scan_min_len_filters`
- `files.rs::tests::scan_cancel_stops`
- `files.rs::tests::scan_stale_key_rejected` (security regression)
- `files.rs::tests::scan_batches_fit_frame`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: "Failed to read process memory." and "Strings unavailable for this process." are the UI's texts for `Error(Os(_))` and `NotAllowed("kernel thread")`.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: batch buffers reused; no per-string allocation beyond the string itself.
- Privacy: found strings are never logged at any level.
- Security: memory of other users' processes leaves the helper only to the engine that asked for it.

title: E29-006 Helper Dump into a passed fd
description:
## Context
`Dump { key, mode, out_fd }` writes a core file of another user's (or a non-child) process with `/usr/bin/gcore` by fixed path, into a file descriptor that tasklens opened, so the core belongs to the user (PROC-075, R-004). An fd cannot travel over a pipe; open item E29-OI-2 recommends that the helper's stdin and stdout are one end of a Unix `socketpair` so the fd travels as `SCM_RIGHTS` ancillary data on the request frame. This bead implements that. Sources: ADR-006, R-004, PROC-075.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-helper/src/ops.rs`: `pub fn run_dump(key: ProcessKey, mode: DumpMode, out_fd: OwnedFd, boot: BootId) -> HelperReply`:
  - `open_verified(key, boot)`; stale gives `Error(IdentityChanged)`.
  - `fstat(out_fd)` must be a regular file (`S_IFREG`) with size 0, and `fcntl(F_GETFL)` must include write access; else `Error(NotAllowed("bad dump fd"))`.
  - Calls the E07-A3 function in `tl-ops/src/dump.rs` (gcore at the fixed path `/usr/bin/gcore`, Mini uses the process's own `coredump_filter`, Full writes `0x1ff` for the duration and restores the old value afterwards, output written to the passed fd). `/usr/bin/gcore` missing gives `Error(NotAllowed("gcore not installed"))`.
  - Success `Done`; gcore non-zero exit gives `Error(Os(EIO = 5))`.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/main.rs` (frame reader, owned by this epic): when reading a request frame from fd 0, use `rustix::net::recvmsg` with a `RecvAncillaryBuffer` sized for one fd. A `Dump` request must carry exactly one fd; any other request carrying an fd, or a `Dump` with zero or two fds, is answered `Error(NotAllowed("unexpected fd"))` and every received fd is closed. Received fds always get `O_CLOEXEC` (`RecvFlags::CMSG_CLOEXEC`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a child `sleep 60` of the test and an empty temp file opened write-only **When** `run_dump(key, Mini, fd)` runs (as the same user, `ptrace_scope` allowing a child) **Then** the reply is `Done` and the file starts with the ELF magic `\x7fELF`.
- **Given** `mode = Full` **When** the dump finishes **Then** the child's `coredump_filter` equals its value before the call.
- **Given** an fd opened read-only **When** called **Then** `Error(NotAllowed("bad dump fd"))` and gcore is not run.
- **Given** an fd for a directory **When** called **Then** `Error(NotAllowed("bad dump fd"))`.
- **Given** a `Signal` request frame that carries an fd **When** the frame reader handles it **Then** the reply is `Error(NotAllowed("unexpected fd"))` and the fd is closed (checked by `fcntl` on the sender's duplicate count through `/proc/self/fd` of the helper in-process test).
- **Given** a stale key **When** called **Then** `Error(IdentityChanged)` (security regression).

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/src/ops.rs`: add `run_dump`.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/main.rs`: ancillary fd receive in the frame reader.

## Tests
- `ops.rs::tests::dump_child_writes_elf` (skips with a message when `/usr/bin/gcore` is absent)
- `ops.rs::tests::dump_restores_coredump_filter`
- `ops.rs::tests::dump_rejects_bad_fd` (security regression)
- `ops.rs::tests::dump_stale_key` (security regression)
- `main.rs::tests::unexpected_fd_closed` (security regression; socketpair in-process)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: "Creating a dump needs administrator rights" is the UI's text when no helper is available; this bead returns only the codes above.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the call blocks for the whole dump; the engine's deadline bounds the reply, not the work (ADR-006).
- Privacy: the dump path is never sent to the helper and never logged.
- Security: root writes only into an fd the user opened; gcore is run by fixed path with no shell.

title: E18-A1 Generic tree table
description:
## Context
Anchor E18-A1 "Generic tree table". This bead finishes the A1 group: right-click target capture and the context menu, Shift+F10 and the Menu key, "Copy rows as table", and the integration test suite with the render counter and the text-cache hit rate. When it closes, `table/{tree_table,columns,selection,cells,actions}.rs`, `text_cache.rs` and the one-line header exist and are exported, and other epics (E22, E23, E24, E27, E28, E30, E32) can build tables on `TlTreeTable<D>`. Sources: ADR-009 (right-click selects then opens a menu bound to captured keys; Copy rows as table; verification list), UI-PRC-008 (right-click rows), UI-PRC-009 (Shift+F10 anchor point), UI-FND-022 (menu behaviour), ADR-015 "Exports and copy", UI-FND-026 (glyph copy texts), ADR-013 UI tests.

Closes the group: E18-001 Selection, E18-002 CellTextCache, E18-003 columns, E18-004 cells, E18-005 delegate trait, E18-006 body and one-line header, E18-007 actions and keymap, E18-008 scrolling and demand.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`:
- `pub enum TreeTableEvent { CopiedRows { rows: usize }, CopyFailed }` and `impl EventEmitter<TreeTableEvent> for TlTreeTable<D>`; the owner page turns them into toasts ("Copied to clipboard" / "Failed to copy to clipboard", APP-044).
- Right-click on a row (`MouseButton::Right` on the row hitbox): if the row is not selected, `selection.right_click(id)` makes it the only selection; a selected row keeps the whole set; a group header changes no selection. Then capture `targets: SmallVec<[D::RowId; 8]>` = the selection in view order (`Selection::in_view_order`; for a group header: just its id) and `clicked_col` = the column under the pointer, call `delegate.context_menu(&targets, clicked_col, TlMenu::new(), window, cx)`, and open the returned menu at the pointer with the kit `PopupMenu` deferred anchored popup. The captured targets travel inside the menu's data actions, so a re-sort or new version before the click does not change them.
- `OpenContextMenu` (Shift+F10, Menu key): same capture for the current selection; the menu opens at the focus row's Name cell text start x and the row's bottom y (UI-PRC-009). No focus row: nothing.
- Opening a menu closes any tooltip; a click outside closes the menu and is consumed (it does not select a row) (UI-FND-022, handled by `TlMenu`).
- One context-menu handler on the table element, never one per row.
- `CopyRowsAsTable`: TSV text, first line the labels of the visible columns in order joined by `\t`, then one line per selected row in view order with each visible column's text joined by `\t`, lines joined by `\n`. Cell text = the cached display text; Name column = `NameCell.primary`; glyph cells copy `…`, `n/a`, `-`, `!`, and the word `Restricted` for Restricted (UI-FND-026, ADR-015). Group header rows are never in the selection, so never copied. Write with `cx.write_to_clipboard(ClipboardItem::new_string(text))`, then emit `CopiedRows { rows }`. No selection: nothing is copied and nothing is emitted.
- `CopyCell { col }` is not handled here (owner page).

`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_tree_table.rs` gains the integration suite (TestAppContext with the `VecDelegate` from E18-005 and the `FakeEngine` from E16-001 where a snapshot is needed).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** rows A, B, C and selection {A} **When** right-clicking C **Then** the selection is {C} and the menu builder receives targets [C].
- **Given** selection {A, C} **When** right-clicking C **Then** the selection stays {A, C} and targets are [A, C] in view order.
- **Given** a menu opened with targets [C] **When** a new version re-sorts the rows before an item is clicked **Then** the dispatched action still carries C.
- **Given** a group header **When** right-clicked **Then** the selection is unchanged and targets are [group id].
- **Given** focus row B **When** Shift+F10 **Then** the menu opens with its top-left at B's Name text start x and B's bottom edge y.
- **Given** selected rows B and C with columns Name, PID, CPU and C's CPU WarmingUp **When** Ctrl+Shift+C **Then** the clipboard holds `Name\tPID\tCPU\nB\t12\t3.4%\nC\t13\t…` and `CopiedRows { rows: 2 }` is emitted.
- **Given** a Restricted cell in the selection **When** copied as table **Then** the cell text is `Restricted`.
- **Given** 10 identical table versions **When** rendered each time **Then** the `CellTextCache` hit rate is above 95%.
- **Given** a snapshot change that does not touch the delegate's data **When** the owner does not call `on_new_version` **Then** `render_count` does not increase.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`: right-click, `OpenContextMenu`, `CopyRowsAsTable`, `TreeTableEvent`.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_tree_table.rs`: the tests below.

## Tests
- `ui_tree_table::right_click_selects_unselected_and_captures_targets`.
- `ui_tree_table::right_click_keeps_multi_selection`.
- `ui_tree_table::right_click_targets_survive_resort` (ADR-009, ADR-013).
- `ui_tree_table::group_header_right_click_no_selection_change`.
- `ui_tree_table::shift_f10_opens_at_focus_row`.
- `ui_tree_table::copy_rows_as_table_tsv_with_header`.
- `ui_tree_table::copy_rows_glyph_texts`.
- `ui_tree_table::tree_table_text_cache_hit_rate` (UI-PRC-001, ADR-009: above 95% over 10 identical versions).
- `ui_tree_table::selection_survives_resort_in_entity` (ADR-009 verification, through the entity).
- `ui_tree_table::render_counter_unchanged_without_new_version`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: clipboard write failure emits `CopyFailed`.
- Validity: glyph copy texts per UI-FND-026.
- Accessibility: Shift+F10 and the Menu key open the same menu as right-click; menu items show key hints because they dispatch the bound Actions (`PopupMenu::action_context(table focus handle)`).
- Performance: the menu is built on open only; nothing per frame while closed.
- Privacy: copy uses the sanitized display text; command lines appear only if the owner shows a command-line column and the user selected the row (ADR-015).

## Notes
- This is the anchor bead; title stays "E18-A1 Generic tree table". Before closing, check that `table/mod.rs` exports `tree_table`, `columns`, `selection`, `cells`, `actions`, `header`, and `lib.rs` exports `table` and `text_cache`.

title: E18-008 Scroll anchoring, keep-visible, jump and visible-range demand
description:
## Context
Scroll behaviour of every tree table: keep the top visible row in place when rows move (re-sort, new rows above, expand above), keep the keyboard focus row visible, centre a jump target, and report the visible identities (plus one viewport of overscan, at most 512) to the delegate for demand, only when the set changes. Sources: UI-PRC-010 (all rules), PROC-013, PROC-071 (jump target centred), ADR-009 "Visible demand", ADR-008 (`detail_keys` max 512), ADR-014 `table-2000` scroll scene.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`:
- Fields: `visible_range: Range<usize>` (recorded in the `uniform_list` render closure), `anchor: Option<(D::RowId, usize /* rows from top */, Pixels /* sub-row offset */)>`, `last_wheel: Option<Instant>`, `thumb_dragging: bool`, `demand_hash: u64`, `demand_scheduled: bool`.
- `pub fn jump_to(&mut self, id: D::RowId, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> bool`: if `row_index(id)` is `Some(ix)`: `scroll.scroll_to_item_strict(ix, ScrollStrategy::Center)` (gpui `uniform_list.rs:163`), select it (`selection.click(id)`), notify; returns false when the id is not in the view. Expanding the path is the delegate's job before calling.
- Anchoring: when `on_new_version` installs a new table version, if the previous top-most visible selectable row identity still exists, scroll so it keeps its previous y (`scroll_to_item_with_offset(ix, ScrollStrategy::Top, offset_rows)` keeping the sub-row pixel offset); otherwise keep the scroll top index. Skip anchoring while the scrollbar thumb is being dragged, within 200 ms after the last wheel event, and while `paused` is true (nothing moves during Ctrl-pause).
- Keep visible: after every keyboard focus move (E18-007 handlers), `scroll_to_item_with_offset(ix, ScrollStrategy::Nearest, 1)` so one extra row of margin stays between the focus row and the header or the bottom edge. Mouse selection never scrolls.
- Visible-range demand: the render closure stores `visible_range`; render schedules one `window.on_next_frame` per render (guarded by `demand_scheduled`) that computes the identities of `visible_range` widened by one viewport above and below, capped at 512 ids (centred on the visible range when the cap bites), hashes the sorted ids into a 64-bit FxHash, and calls `delegate.on_visible_range(&ids)` only when the hash differs from `demand_hash`. It runs after every table version even when the range did not change (ADR-009).
- No header shadow when scrolled (the 1 px `divider` under the header is already there).
- Scrollbar drag is not frame-capped by the table (kit `Scrollbar.max_fps` left at default).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** row X at the top of the viewport **When** a new version moves X 40 rows down (re-sort) **Then** after render X is still the top row at the same y.
- **Given** a wheel event 100 ms ago **When** a new version arrives **Then** the scroll position index is unchanged and no anchoring happens.
- **Given** `paused == true` **When** a new version arrives **Then** nothing scrolls.
- **Given** the focus row on the last fully visible line **When** Down is pressed **Then** the list scrolls so one extra row is visible below the focus row.
- **Given** a row 900 rows down **When** `jump_to(id)` **Then** that row is selected and its centre is within half a row of the viewport centre.

title: E18-009 Two-line header: totals, sort arrows, sort click
description:
## Context
The two-line header used by the process, history and system tables: line 1 is the column label with the sort arrow, line 2 the system total (right-aligned, secondary colour). Clicking anywhere on a sortable header cell sorts by that column. Sources: UI-PRC-005 (anatomy, states, sort cycle, tooltips), PROC-038 (totals), PROC-047 (sort gestures), ADR-009 "Header", UI-FND-003 (header name `t_sm`/`t_base` note), UI-FND-051 (numbers never cut), D-004 (Memory tooltip text supplied by the owner).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/table/header.rs` (`TlTreeTableHeader`) gains the two-line mode:
- Height `header_h` 44 when `delegate.header_lines() == Two`, 28 for `One`; background `header`; bottom border 1 px `divider`.
- Line 1 (y 4..22): label `t_base` 13 weight 500 `text_primary`, aligned like the column (Left for Text and Path, Right for Numeric), padding 8, end ellipsis. The active sort column shows Lucide `arrow-up` (ascending) or `arrow-down` (descending), 12 px, `text_primary`, after a 2 px (`sp1`) gap, inside the 12 px reservation of PROC-023. On a right-aligned column the arrow sits at the right edge and the label moves left by 14.
- Line 2 (y 22..40): `delegate.header_total(col, &mut out)`; `false` leaves the line empty. Text `t_base` regular `text_secondary`, always right-aligned (also on the left-aligned Name column there is no line 2 because the owner returns false), formatted through `CellTextCache` with a header row key, validity glyphs as in cells (`…`, `n/a`, lock, `-`, `!`). Never cut: numbers clip at most (UI-FND-051).
- Column boundary lines (1 px `divider`) at all times, at the same x offsets as the body; translated by the shared `x_offset`.
- Hitboxes: one per header cell (`window.insert_hitbox`, gpui `window.rs:5109`). States: hover fills the cell `row_hover`; pressed fills `row_selected` at 50% alpha; unsortable columns (`ColumnSpec.sortable == false`) get no hover fill, no arrow, default cursor, and the tooltip "Only measured for visible rows".
- Tooltip (500 ms) per cell: `ColumnSpec.tooltip` when `Some`; else the picker full name when it differs from the label (for example `Working set private - "Memory"` style, from `full_name`); else none.
- Click on a sortable cell (release without a drag of more than 4 px): dispatch `SortByColumn { id }`. The table handles `SortByColumn` by calling `delegate.on_sort(id)`; the delegate computes the new `SortSpec` with `SortSpec::next_for` (E18-003): first click descending for Numeric, ascending for Text and Path, each further click flips.
- Painting: one `canvas` for fills, boundaries and arrows (`paint_quad`, `paint_svg`) plus one text `div` per line per visible column; at most 2 shaped lines per visible column; texts re-shape only when the cached text changes.
- The header is not focusable; keyboard sorting goes through the header menu and View > Columns.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** sort `pid` ascending **When** the header renders **Then** the PID cell shows "PID" and an `arrow-up` at its right edge, with the label 14 px left of where it sits without the arrow.
- **Given** column `cpu` (Numeric) not sorted **When** its header cell is clicked **Then** `on_sort(cpu)` runs and the delegate's next sort is cpu descending; clicking again gives ascending.
- **Given** column `user` (Text) **When** clicked first **Then** the sort is user ascending.
- **Given** an unsortable `pss` column **When** hovered and clicked **Then** no hover fill, no sort, and the tooltip "Only measured for visible rows" after 500 ms.
- **Given** `header_total(cpu)` returns "11.9%" Valid **When** rendered **Then** line 2 shows "11.9%" right-aligned in `text_secondary`; for `name` it returns false and line 2 is blank.
- **Given** a total with validity Unsupported **When** rendered **Then** line 2 shows `n/a`.
- **Given** `header_lines() == One` **When** rendered **Then** the header is 28 tall with no line 2.
- **Given** the mouse pressed on a cell and moved 6 px **When** released **Then** no sort happens (a drag started; reorder is E18-011).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/header.rs`: two-line mode, hitboxes, sort click, tooltips.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`: `SortByColumn` handler.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_columns.rs`: create with the tests below.

## Tests

- `ui_columns::header_sort_cycle_text_asc_first`.
- `ui_columns::header_line2_blank_for_text_columns`.
- `ui_columns::unsortable_header_no_hover_no_sort`.
- `ui_columns::sort_arrow_position_right_aligned`.
- `ui_columns::header_one_line_mode_height_28`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: totals show validity glyphs like cells.
- Accessibility: tooltips name the figure; sort state is visible as an arrow and repeated as a checked "Sort by" item in the header menu (E18-012).
- Performance: totals change at 1 Hz; cached texts; no work while idle.
- Privacy: N/A.

title: E18-010 Column resize and fit
description:
## Context
Column resizing by dragging a header boundary, in the two modes of `tables.column_resize` (one key for every table, R-075), double-click to fit one column, and "Resize columns to fit content" for all columns. Widths persist through `delegate.on_columns_changed` on release. Sources: UI-PRC-005 (resize handle, clamp, modes, double-click), UI-PRC-006 (`ResizeColumnsToFit` measurement scope), PROC-025, PROC-023 (minimums), R-075, canonical table (a) `tables.column_resize = "proportional"` (`proportional | last_column`), UI-FND-003 (cursor `col-resize` only over a header edge).

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/columns.rs`:
```rust
/// Drag of the right boundary of `col` to `new_width` (logical px at 100%).
pub fn resize(layout: &mut ColumnLayout, col: ColumnId, new_width: Pixels, mode: ColumnResizeMode,
              viewport: Pixels, mins: &FxHashMap<ColumnId, Pixels>);
```
  - The new width is clamped to the column's minimum (`min_width`, E18-003: template + 16, + 12 on the sort column; text columns 60).
  - `Proportional`: the dragged boundary moves; the visible columns to its right share the remaining width (viewport minus the widths left of and including the dragged column) in proportion to their current widths, each clamped to its minimum; when the minimums do not fit, they sit at their minimums and the table overflows horizontally.
  - `LastColumn`: only the dragged column and the last visible column change; the last column takes the difference, clamped to its minimum.
  - When the dragged column is the last visible column, only it changes in both modes.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/header.rs`:
  - Resize hit band: 8 px wide (4 each side) centred on each column boundary and after the last column, full header height; cursor `CursorStyle::ResizeColumn` over it; the boundary line turns `accent` while dragging (else 1 px `divider`).
  - Drag: live width change each mouse move (layout `rebuild`, table notify); release calls `delegate.on_columns_changed(&layout)` once.
  - Double-click on a boundary: fit that column (rule below) and call `on_columns_changed`.
  - `TlTreeTable::set_resize_mode(&mut self, mode: ColumnResizeMode)`: the owner passes the current `tables.column_resize` value (the table reads no settings itself).
- Fit rule (`ResizeColumnsToFit { table }` for every visible column, double-click for one): width = max(minimum, widest text of the column + 16, header label width + 16 + 12), measured over the currently visible rows plus the texts still in `CellTextCache` from the last 3 table versions (never a full pass over all rows), with the table font at the current scale and `tnum` for numeric columns. The table handles `ResizeColumnsToFit` itself and then calls `on_columns_changed`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a Numeric column with minimum 63 **When** dragged to 20 **Then** its width is 63.
- **Given** a Text column **When** dragged to 30 **Then** its width is 60.
- **Given** columns [name 200, a 100, b 100] in a 400 px viewport, Proportional **When** name is dragged to 240 **Then** a and b become 80 each.
- **Given** the same layout in LastColumn mode **When** name is dragged to 240 **Then** a stays 100 and b becomes 60.
- **Given** a drag over 10 mouse moves **When** released **Then** `on_columns_changed` was called exactly once.
- **Given** a column whose widest visible text is 150 px **When** its boundary is double-clicked **Then** its width is max(minimum, 166, label + 28).
- **Given** `ResizeColumnsToFit` **When** dispatched **Then** every visible column is fitted and no column is below its minimum.
- **Given** the pointer over a boundary band **When** hovering **Then** the cursor is the column-resize cursor; elsewhere the arrow.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/columns.rs`: `resize`, fit helper.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/header.rs`: hit bands, drag, double-click.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`: `set_resize_mode`, `ResizeColumnsToFit` handler.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_columns.rs`: tests below.

## Tests
- `columns::tests::resize_clamps_to_template_minimum` (UI-PRC-005).
- `columns::tests::resize_proportional_vs_last_column`.
- `columns::tests::resize_last_visible_column_only_changes_itself`.
- `ui_columns::drag_persists_once_on_release`.
- `ui_columns::double_click_boundary_fits_one_column`.
- `ui_columns::fit_columns_never_below_minimum` (UI-PRC-006).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: keyboard users fit columns through the header menu or View > Columns; dragging is mouse only (UI-PRC-005).
- Performance: a drag rebuilds offsets once per mouse move; fitting measures through `TextMetricsCache` and the cached texts only.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- Widths are stored at 100% scale in `ColumnLayout.widths`; convert the dragged pixel width by dividing by `ui_scale`.

title: E18-011 Column reorder drag
description:
## Context
Column reordering by dragging a header cell. Name is fixed first: it cannot be dragged and nothing can be dropped before it. The new order persists through `on_columns_changed`. Sources: UI-PRC-005 (reorder drag, ghost, insertion line, 4 px threshold, Esc cancels, Name fixed), PROC-025, PROC-022 (Name always first and visible).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/table/header.rs`:
- Pressing on a header cell (not on a resize band) and moving more than 4 px starts a reorder drag; up to 4 px it is a click (sort, E18-009).
- While dragging: a ghost of the cell follows the pointer (fill `header` at 85% opacity, the label, 1 px `divider` border, radius `r_sm` 4 × ui_scale); a 2 px `accent` insertion line spans the header and body height at the nearest column boundary to the pointer. The insertion line never shows before Name.
- Drop: `ColumnLayout::move_column(id, before)` (E18-003), `rebuild`, `delegate.on_columns_changed(&layout)` once.
- Esc during a drag cancels it with no change (handled on the table root while `header_state` is dragging, before the global Esc chain).
- Name (`ColumnSpec.hideable == false`) does not start a drag.
- Drag state lives in `HeaderState` on the table entity (or `with_element_state`), not in the delegate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** order [name, user, pid, cpu] **When** cpu is dragged and dropped between name and user **Then** order is [name, cpu, user, pid] and `on_columns_changed` runs once.
- **Given** a press on pid moving 3 px **When** released **Then** it is a click (sort), not a reorder.
- **Given** a drag of user to the left edge before name **When** dropped **Then** user lands right after name; the insertion line never appeared before name.
- **Given** a press on name **When** moved 50 px **Then** no drag starts.
- **Given** a drag in progress **When** Esc is pressed **Then** the order is unchanged and `on_columns_changed` is not called.
- **Given** a drag in progress **When** rendered **Then** the ghost has `header` fill at 85% opacity and the insertion line is 2 px `accent` over header and body.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/header.rs`: drag state, ghost, insertion line, drop.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`: Esc handling during a drag; insertion line over the body.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_columns.rs`: tests below.

## Tests
- `ui_columns::reorder_moves_column_and_persists_once`.
- `ui_columns::reorder_cannot_move_name` (UI-PRC-005).
- `ui_columns::reorder_never_before_name`.
- `ui_columns::reorder_threshold_4px`.
- `ui_columns::escape_cancels_reorder`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: reordering is mouse only; the column picker keeps keyboard access to visibility.
- Performance: the ghost and line are painted only during a drag.
