title: E15-004 Untrusted text display rules
description:
## Context
Process-derived text is already sanitized in tl-collect (ADR-015): C0/C1 controls became U+FFFD, bidi controls and U+200B..U+200F were removed. The UI marks U+FFFD visibly in Name cells and applies the name fallback chain. Sources: UI-FND-053 rules 1 to 8, ADR-015 "Untrusted process text", ADR-003. Spec phase P1; phase-0 slice.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/text/untrusted.rs`:
  - `pub fn split_fffd_runs(text: &str) -> SmallVec<[(Range<usize>, bool /*is_fffd*/); 4]>`: splits a string into runs, `true` for each run of U+FFFD characters.
  - `pub fn name_runs(text: &SharedString, normal: Hsla, warning: Hsla) -> SmallVec<[TextRun; 4]>`: one `TextRun` per run; U+FFFD runs use `status.warning`, others the normal colour. Used only by Name cells; other cells and tooltips draw U+FFFD in the normal colour.
  - `pub fn display_name<'a>(name: &'a str, comm: &'a str, pid: u32, scratch: &'a mut String) -> &'a str`: if `name` is empty or consists only of U+FFFD, return `comm`; if `comm` is empty or only U+FFFD too, write `[pid N]` into `scratch` and return it.
  - `pub fn debug_assert_clean(text: &str)`: in debug builds only, `debug_assert!` that no char in C0 (U+0000..U+001F), DEL, C1 (U+0080..U+009F), U+202A..U+202E, U+2066..U+2069, U+200B..U+200F, U+2028, U+2029 remains. Compiles to nothing in release. U+200D (ZWJ) is allowed.
  - The module header comment states rules 3 to 8 of UI-FND-053: each cell is one LTR paragraph; RTL letters are kept and shaped by cosmic-text; the ellipsis goes at the logical end; no UI mirroring; copy uses the sanitized text.
- Add `pub mod untrusted;` to `text/mod.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `"ab\u{FFFD}\u{FFFD}cd"` **When** `split_fffd_runs` runs **Then** it returns three runs: `ab` (false), the two U+FFFD (true), `cd` (false).
- **Given** that text and `name_runs` **When** colours are read **Then** only the middle run has `status.warning`.
- **Given** name `""`, comm `"bash"` **When** `display_name` runs **Then** it returns `bash`.
- **Given** name `"\u{FFFD}"`, comm `""`, pid 4242 **When** `display_name` runs **Then** it returns `[pid 4242]`.
- **Given** a debug build and text with U+202E **When** `debug_assert_clean` runs **Then** it panics; with U+200D it does not.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/text/untrusted.rs`: create, with tests.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/text/mod.rs`: add `pub mod untrusted;`.

## Tests
- `text::untrusted::tests::fffd_run_split_and_coloured`: runs and colours as above.
- `text::untrusted::tests::empty_name_falls_back_to_comm_then_pid`: both fallbacks.
- `text::untrusted::tests::debug_check_rejects_bidi_allows_zwj` (`#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`, `#[should_panic]` variant for U+202E).
- The RTL render test (`rtl_name_in_ltr_cell`) lives in E18-013 because it needs a table cell.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: U+FFFD is marked by colour and by the replacement glyph itself, not colour alone.
- Performance: no per-frame scan in release; split only when a Name cell's text changes (cached by the caller).
- Privacy: never log the text.

title: E15-005 Component module, TlFocusRing, icons and asset source (U-42)
description:
## Context
Creates the `components` module, the keyboard-only focus ring helper and the icon layer: Lucide names through `gpui_kit::assets::IconName` and an `AssetSource` that serves tasklens SVGs first and falls back to the kit assets. Settles U-42 (the "last input was keyboard" focus-ring heuristic). Sources: UI-FND-003 (icons, focus ring), UI-FND-028 (shield-unlocked glyph), ADR-009 "Icons", R-123, U-42, D-005. Spec phase P1; phase-0 slice (anchor E15-A1).

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/components/mod.rs`: `pub mod focus; pub mod icons;` (each later component bead adds its own line). Add `pub mod components;` to `crates/tl-ui/src/lib.rs`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/components/focus.rs`:
  - `pub struct TlFocusRing;` with `pub fn show(focused: bool, window: &Window) -> bool` returning `focused && window.last_input_was_keyboard()` (GPUI has the flag: gpui-pre `src/window.rs:3241`).
  - `pub fn ring(el: impl Styled, radius: Pixels, theme: &TlTheme) -> impl Styled`: 2 px solid `accent`, 2 px outside the border box, radius = element radius + 2 (UI-FND-003). Use the kit focus ring drawing where `Theme::focus_ring` is true, or an outer `div` with `border_2` and negative inset.
  - `pub fn row_focus_border(theme: &TlTheme) -> (Pixels, Hsla)` = (1 px, `accent`) for tree-table rows (inset border, because the list clips children).
  - Inputs show focus through `input_focus` background plus 1 px `accent` border, no ring (documented here; drawn by the input component).
  - Fallback if U-42 fails: `pub const KEYBOARD_ONLY_RING: bool = true;` set to `false` makes `show` return `focused` (the kit default of always showing the ring on focus, R-123).
- `crates/tl-ui/src/components/icons.rs`:
  - `pub enum TlIcon` covering every name UI-FND-003 uses, mapped to `gpui_kit::assets::IconName`: `check`, `chevron-right`, `chevron-down`, `chevron-up`, `x`, `search`, `pin`, `pin-off`, `lock`, `shield`, `shield-check`, `info`, `circle-check`, `triangle-alert`, `circle-x`, `loader-circle`, `copy`, `rotate-ccw-clock`, `minus`, `plus`, `eye`, `eye-off`, plus `arrow-up` and `arrow-down` (sort arrows, UI-PRC-005). All 24 exist in gpui-kit 0.7.0 `assets/assets/icons/`.
  - Seven of them are not in the kit's default component bundle (`default-icons.txt`): `x`, `pin`, `pin-off`, `lock`, `shield`, `shield-check`, `rotate-ccw-clock`. Embed them with `gpui_kit::assets::icon_assets!(TlExtraIcons, [X, Pin, PinOff, Lock, Shield, ShieldCheck, RotateCcwClock]);` (macro at kit `crates/assets/src/lib.rs:66`).
  - `pub struct TlAssets;` implementing `gpui::AssetSource`: first `assets/icons/*.svg` from tasklens (embedded with `include_bytes!`, path prefix `icons/tl/`), then `TlExtraIcons`, then `gpui_kit::assets::Assets`. `list()` merges, sorts and deduplicates.

  - Size tokens from `UiMetrics.icon`: `i_xs` 12 (lock, sort arrow, menu check, submenu chevron, tree chevron), `i_sm` 14 (tab suffix icons, status health icon, filter clear), `i_md` 16 (toolbar, menu icons, process icons, pin, toast icon, shield), `i_lg` 20 (dialog icon, empty-state icon). Helper `pub fn icon(name: TlIcon, size: Pixels, color: Hsla) -> Icon` = `gpui_kit::Icon::new(..).size(size).text_color(color)`.

title: E15-006 TlProgress and TlSpinner
description:
## Context
Progress bar and spinner wrappers with fixed sizes, 1% value bucketing and reduced-motion stand-ins. Used by toasts, dialog footers, the Properties hash row, the setup window, the Strings tab header and the Services status text, never in table cells, charts, sidebar cards or the main status bar. Sources: UI-FND-023, ADR-009 (no kit Spinner, Skeleton or Progress in cells or charts), APP-058. Spec phase P1 (toasts) and P2; phase-0 slice because TlButton's loading state needs the spinner (anchor E15-A1).

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/components/progress.rs`:
  - `pub struct TlProgress { value: Option<f32 /*0..=100*/>, size: TlProgressSize::{Sm /*4 px*/, Md /*6 px*/}, show_label: bool, reduced_motion: bool }` (`RenderOnce`). Track `scroll_track`, fill `accent`, radius full, width from the parent. Determinate: `.value(v)`. Indeterminate (`value = None`): a 30% wide segment moving left to right over 1.2 s, looping (kit `Progress::loading(true)`). Optional right-aligned `t_xs` percent label with `tnum` ("37%").
  - Value changes jump: the element `id` includes the 1% bucket (`(value as u32)`), so the kit transition never runs.
  - Reduced motion (`cx.reduce_motion() || !settings.motion.animations` passed in by the owner as `reduced_motion`): indeterminate becomes a static 30% segment at the left; the owner adds the text "Working…".
  - `pub struct TlSpinner { size: Pixels /*i_sm 14 or i_md 16 per UiMetrics*/, color: Option<Hsla> }`: Lucide `loader-circle`, default colour `text_secondary`, rotating 360° per 0.8 s (kit `Spinner`). Reduced motion: static `loader-circle` at 50% opacity.
  - Module doc lists the allowed uses above and the budget: at most 2 spinners or indeterminate bars visible per window. Owners remove them from the tree when work ends (never `visibility: hidden`), because they request frames while present.
- Add `pub mod progress;` to `components/mod.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `TlProgress` with value 37.4 then 37.9 **When** rendered twice **Then** the element id is the same (bucket 37) and no animation frame is requested.
- **Given** value 38.0 after 37.9 **When** rendered **Then** the id changes (bucket 38).
- **Given** reduced motion on **When** an indeterminate `TlProgress` renders **Then** no animation frame is requested and a static 30% segment is drawn.
- **Given** reduced motion on **When** `TlSpinner` renders **Then** it draws a static icon at opacity 0.5 and requests no frame.
- **Given** a spinner removed from the tree **When** the next frame runs **Then** no further frames are requested.

## Tests

- `components::progress::tests::value_bucket_id`: 1% bucketing.

title: E02-A1 Workspace compiles
description:
## Context
Capstone of the workspace setup. It generates and commits `Cargo.lock`, proves the whole workspace builds on the pinned toolchain with `--locked`, and runs the ADR-002 verification commands. Every other epic's first bead depends on this one. Sources: ADR-001, ADR-002 (Verification), U-1, 00-epics anchor row E02-A1.

## Deliverable
- `Cargo.lock`, generated by cargo (never hand-edited) and committed.
- A passing `cargo +1.98.1 build --workspace --locked` over the 8 skeleton members: `tl-model`, `tl-collect`, `tl-ops`, `tl-engine`, `tl-gpu-probe`, `tl-ui`, `tl-app` (bin `tasklens`), `xtask`.
- The outputs of the three ADR-002 verification commands, pasted into the bead close reason (`br close <id> --reason "..."`):
  1. `cargo +1.98.1 build --workspace --locked` succeeds.
  2. `cargo tree -p tl-engine -e features -i asupersync` shows no `nightly-outcome-try` and no `test-internals`.
  3. `cargo tree -p tl-app -i gpui-pre --prefix none` shows exactly one version, `0.3.7` (ADR-002 writes `-p tasklens`; use the package name E02-005 settled on).
- A first U-1 reading: `cargo tree -p tl-app -e normal,build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --prefix none --format "{p}"` contains none of `tokio`, `tokio-util`, `tokio-stream`, `tokio-macros`, `async-std`, `async-global-executor`, `actix-rt`, `reqwest`, `hyper`. Paste the result line (found or not found) into the close reason. E02-A2 turns this into the permanent check.
- A second reading for E02 open item 4: run `cargo tree -p tl-ui -e normal --prefix none --format "{p}"` and record whether `zbus` or `arc-swap` appear (gpui-kit may pull zbus through its portal code). Record the answer in the close reason and message the leader if either appears, because ADR-001 check 2 would then fail.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** E02-001 to E02-006 are merged **When** `cargo +1.98.1 build --workspace --locked` runs **Then** it exits 0.
- **Given** the build passed **When** `git status` runs **Then** `Cargo.lock` is tracked and has no uncommitted changes.
- **Given** the lock file **When** `cargo tree -p tl-engine -e features -i asupersync` runs **Then** neither `nightly-outcome-try` nor `test-internals` appears.
- **Given** the lock file **When** `cargo tree -p tl-app -i gpui-pre --prefix none` runs **Then** every `gpui-pre` line shows version `0.3.7` and no other version.
- **Given** the lock file **When** the banned-crate tree command above runs **Then** no banned crate is found; if one is found, stop and report to the leader (U-1 fails).

## Files
- `Cargo.lock`: create (generated)

## Tests
- No Rust tests. The build and the three verification commands are the test; outputs go in the close reason.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
Large-file rule: generate `Cargo.lock` with `cargo generate-lockfile` (through the build rule), commit it, then run the full build. Fix-ups go in a follow-up commit. If a pin fails to resolve on crates.io, stop and report the exact cargo error to the leader; do not change a pin (exact pins change only through an ADR change). Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`. title: E02-008 check-deps: allowed rows and closure rules
description:
## Context
Second half of `cargo xtask check-deps`: ADR-001 check 2. It reads `cargo metadata` and enforces the allowed-dependency table, the asupersync closure rule and the tl-ui closure rule. Sources: ADR-001 (allowed table, check 2, rules 1 and 2), R-130 (tl-ops in tl-app row), R-131 (ureq in tl-engine row), R-132 (fluent-bundle, unic-langid in tl-ui row).

## Deliverable
In `xtask/src/check_deps.rs`, add check 2, run by `run()` together with the other three.

Allowed direct normal dependencies (`[dependencies]` and `[build-dependencies]`; `[dev-dependencies]` are not checked by this table), as a constant table `ALLOWED: &[(&str, &[&str])]`:

| Package | Allowed direct deps |
|---|---|
| tl-model | serde, postcard, thiserror, async-channel, bitflags, smallvec, rustix |
| tl-collect | tl-model, rustix, memchr, thiserror, tracing, smallvec, rustc-hash, netlink-packet-core, netlink-packet-sock-diag, netlink-sys, sha2, md-5 |
| tl-ops | tl-model, rustix, libc, thiserror, tracing |
| tl-engine | tl-model, tl-collect, tl-ops, tl-history, asupersync, arc-swap, async-channel, zbus, futures-lite, rustix, postcard, serde, thiserror, tracing, rustc-hash, smallvec, ureq |
| tl-gpu-probe | tl-model, nvml-wrapper, rustix, postcard, serde, ash, khronos-egl |
| tl-ui | tl-model, gpui-kit, tracing, smallvec, rustc-hash, serde, serde_json, fluent-bundle, unic-langid |
| tl-app | tl-model, tl-engine, tl-ui, tl-ops, tl-tray, zbus, toml, serde, anyhow, tracing, tracing-subscriber, tracing-appender, rustix |
| tl-history | tl-model, zstd, crc32fast, postcard, serde, thiserror |
| tl-tray | tl-model, ksni |
| tl-helper | tl-model, tl-ops, rustix, postcard, serde |
| xtask | serde, serde_json, anyhow |

Violations:
1. A workspace member has a direct normal or build dependency not in its row: `<member> depends on <dep>, which is not in its ADR-001 row`.
2. A workspace member not in the table (for example `tl-netmon`, whose row is decided later): `<member> has no ADR-001 row`.
3. `asupersync` is in the normal-dependency closure of any member other than `tl-engine` and `tl-app`: `asupersync in the closure of <member>`.
4. `tl-ui`'s normal-dependency closure contains `tl-engine`, `tl-collect`, `tl-ops`, `arc-swap` or `zbus`: `tl-ui closure contains <name>`.

Closure: from `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --filter-platform x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, walk `resolve.nodes[].deps[]`, following only edges whose `dep_kinds` include an entry with `kind: null` (normal). Parse with `serde_json::Value`; no new dependencies.

The rustix feature limit on tl-model (feature `time` only) is not checked by this bead; it is reviewed by hand in E03.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the skeleton workspace **When** `cargo xtask check-deps` runs **Then** check 2 reports nothing and the run prints `check-deps: ok`.
- **Given** a scratch copy where tl-ops adds `serde` **When** check-deps runs **Then** it prints `tl-ops depends on serde, which is not in its ADR-001 row` and exits 1.
- **Given** a scratch copy where tl-collect adds `asupersync` **When** check-deps runs **Then** it reports both the row violation and `asupersync in the closure of tl-collect`.

title: E02-007 check-deps: banned crates and asupersync greps
description:
## Context First half of `cargo xtask check-deps`: the banned-crate check per shipped binary (ADR-001 check 1), the `asupersync::` grep outside tl-engine (check 3), and the banned asupersync API grep in tl-engine production code (ADR-004). E02-008 adds check 2 to the same file. Sources: ADR-001 ("No Tokio" definition, CI check), ADR-004 (banned API list), U-1. ## Deliverable `xtask/src/check_deps.rs` with `pub fn run(args: Vec) -> anyhow::Result<()>` that runs every check, prints each violation on its own line to stdout, prints `check-deps: ok` when there are none, and returns `Err` (exit status 1) when there is at least one. It runs all checks before failing, so one run lists every violation. Constants: ```rust pub const SHIPPED_BINARIES: &[&str] = &["tl-app", "tl-gpu-probe", "tl-helper", "tl-netmon"]; // package names pub const BANNED_CRATES: &[&str] = &["tokio", "tokio-util", "tokio-stream", "tokio-macros", "async-std", "async-global-executor", "actix-rt", "reqwest", "hyper"]; pub const TARGET: &str = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"; ``` (`tl-app` is the package of the `tasklens` binary; follow whatever name E02-005 settled on.) Check 1, banned crates: for each package in `SHIPPED_BINARIES` that exists in `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1` (P3 and P4 packages are skipped until they exist), run `cargo tree -p

-e normal,build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --prefix none --format "{p}"` and fail on any line whose first whitespace-separated word is in `BANNED_CRATES`. Message: `banned crate in the dependency graph of

`. Do not use `cargo tree -i`. Check 3, asupersync outside the engine: `rg -n "asupersync::" crates/ --glob '!crates/tl-engine/**'`. Any output line is a violation: `asupersync used outside tl-engine: `. rg exit status 1 (no match) is success; status 2 is an error. Check 4, banned asupersync APIs: scan every `.rs` file under `crates/tl-engine/src` (never `crates/tl-engine/tests`). Skip any `mod` item annotated `#[cfg(test)]`, found by brace counting from the `mod {` line that follows the attribute. In the remaining text, report each match of these patterns, as `banned asupersync API at :`: - whole-word: `AppSpec`, `GenServer`, `actor`, `race_drained`, `ctrl_c` - literal: `race!`, `select!`, `Cx::race_timeout`, `asupersync::signal`, `asupersync::process`, `asupersync::fs`, `Cx::for_request`, `Cx::for_testing`, `ChildSpec::depends_on` - ADR-004 also bans `JoinHandle` from `RuntimeHandle::spawn` (use `spawn_checked`) and `Budget::with_poll_quota` on long-lived tasks. A name grep cannot tell these cases apart. Until the leader decides (E02 open item 3), match the literals `RuntimeHandle::spawn(` and `.with_poll_quota(`, and accept a match only when the same line carries the comment `// check-deps: allow` followed by a reason. `xtask/src/main.rs`: add `mod check_deps;` and the arm `Some("check-deps") => check_deps::run(rest)`. The xtask uses only `std`, `anyhow`, `serde`, `serde_json` (ADR-001 xtask row). It shells out to `cargo` and `rg` with `std::process::Command`. ## Acceptance Criteria - **Given** the skeleton workspace **When** `cargo xtask check-deps` runs **Then** it prints `check-deps: ok` and exits 0. - **Given** a scratch copy where `crates/tl-ui/Cargo.toml` gains `tokio = "1"` under `[dependencies]` **When** check-deps runs **Then** it prints `banned crate tokio in the dependency graph of tl-app` and exits 1. - **Given** the same scratch copy with `tokio` under `[dev-dependencies]` instead **When** check-deps runs **Then** check 1 passes. - **Given** a file in `crates/tl-ui/src` containing `asupersync::time` **When** check-deps runs **Then** it reports `asupersync used outside tl-engine` and exits 1. - **Given** `crates/tl-engine/src/x.rs` containing `select!` outside a test module **When** check-deps runs **Then** it reports `banned asupersync API select! at crates/tl-engine/src/x.rs:`. - **Given** the same `select!` inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` **When** check-deps runs **Then** it is not reported. - **Given** `tl-helper` does not exist yet **When** check-deps runs **Then** check 1 skips it without error. ## Files - `xtask/src/check_deps.rs`: create - `xtask/src/main.rs`: add the `mod` line and the `check-deps` arm ## Tests - `xtask/src/check_deps.rs::tests::banned_word_matches_first_word_only`: the line `tokio v1.40.0` matches; `tokio-rustls v0.26` does not; `hyper-util v0.1` does not. - `xtask/src/check_deps.rs::tests::api_scan_skips_cfg_test_module`: a source string with `select!` inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { fn f() { select!(); } }` yields no hit; the same call outside yields one hit with the right line number. - `xtask/src/check_deps.rs::tests::api_scan_whole_word`: `actor` matches `let actor = 1;` but not `factory` or `actors_count`. - `xtask/src/check_deps.rs::tests::allow_comment_accepts_poll_quota`: `.with_poll_quota(8) // check-deps: allow short probe` yields no hit; without the comment it yields one. ## Cross-cutting - Errors: violations as listed above; tool failures (cargo or rg missing, cargo tree non-zero) are errors with the command line and stderr in the message. - Validity: N/A - Accessibility: N/A - Performance: N/A - Privacy: N/A ## Notes Make the scanner functions take `&str` input so the tests need no files. Never run the tokio experiment in the shared checkout: copy the repo to the session scratchpad (`cp -r --reflink=auto`) and run it there. description:

title: E01-008 Bench scene table-2000 with synthetic process table
description:
## Context
ADR-014 scene `table-2000` measures the production process table (E22-A1 on E18's `TlTreeTable`) with 2,000 rows that all change every second and re-sort, while it scrolls at 1,200 logical px/s. Gates: UI thread p99 <= 2.0 ms per frame while scrolling, missed frames as in the gate table, RSS <= 150 MB after the run. Sources: ADR-014, UI-PRC-023 (budget split, rules, test name), R-006 (default columns and widths).

## Deliverable
1. In `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/synth.rs`, add `pub struct TableSynth` with `pub fn new(rng: &mut BenchRng) -> Self` and `pub fn tick_1hz(&mut self, rng: &mut BenchRng, t_ns: TimeNs) -> Arc<ProcessTableView>`:
   - 2,000 process rows in 40 groups (grouped mode, `TableMode::Grouped`), sorted by CPU descending with the `ProcessKey` tie-break (so order changes every second).
   - 10 columns. The set is open item E01-OI-7 (R-006 now has 9 default columns; ADR-014 says 10). Recommended: R-006's `name, user, pid, cpu, memory, disk, network, gpu, description` plus `power` (101 px), with R-006 widths Name 248, User 92, PID 96, CPU 63, Memory 92, Disk 82, Network 92, GPU 72, Description 342.
   - Every metric value of every row changes on every tick (fresh draws). Names, groups and value ranges follow open item E01-OI-7.
   - The view is built directly with `tl-model` table types (E03-A2); group totals are sums of the member rows.
2. In `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/scenes.rs`, implement `BenchScene::Table2000`: the Processes page only (E22-A1 `ProcessesPage`) in the fixture window; `BenchEngine` publishes the `TableSynth` view once per second (component `TABLE` and `PROCESSES` change, nothing else); programmatic scroll at 1,200 logical px/s, bouncing between top and bottom, through the table's `UniformListScrollHandle`, advanced in the `FrameProbe` callback by `1200 px * frame_dt` and clamped to `[0, content_height - viewport_height]`, reversing direction at either end. `rss_mb` is read after the measured window.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** two `TableSynth` from seed 42 **When** each produces its first tick **Then** the row sets (keys in order) are identical (test `bench_table_2000_scene_exists_and_is_deterministic`, UI-PRC-023).
- **Given** a tick **When** inspected **Then** it has 2,000 process rows under 40 group rows and rows are in non-increasing CPU order with ties broken by `ProcessKey`.
- **Given** two consecutive ticks **When** compared **Then** every process row's CPU value differs and the order differs.
- **Given** the scene in a `TestAppContext` **When** 1 s of simulated frames at 144 Hz runs **Then** the scroll offset moved 1,200 +- 20 logical px from the start, and after reaching the bottom it moves upward.
- **Given** `--bench table-2000` **When** run **Then** the report has `"scene": "table-2000"` and a non-zero `rss_mb`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/synth.rs`: change, add `TableSynth`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/scenes.rs`: change, add the `Table2000` scene.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/bench_scenes.rs`: change, add the tests below.

## Tests
- `tests/bench_scenes.rs::bench_table_2000_scene_exists_and_is_deterministic`
- `tests/bench_scenes.rs::table_synth_sorted_grouped_2000`
- `tests/bench_scenes.rs::table_synth_changes_every_tick`
- `tests/bench_scenes.rs::table_scroll_bounces_at_1200_px_per_s`
Run with `cargo test -p tl-ui --features bench --test bench_scenes`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: every synthetic cell `Valid`; no `Restricted` or `Failed` cells (they are covered by E22's own render tests).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: carries the `table-2000` gates. The scene must not add per-frame work in the table path; the scroll update is one `set_offset` call per frame.
- Privacy: N/A (synthetic names).

## Notes
- The scroll needs access to the production table's `UniformListScrollHandle`. Open item E01-OI-8: recommended that E18-A1 exposes `TlTreeTable::scroll_handle(&self) -> &UniformListScrollHandle` and E22-A1 exposes the table entity from `ProcessesPage`. Do not edit E18 or E22 files from this bead.
- gpui-pre 0.3.7: `UniformListScrollHandle` wraps `UniformListScrollState { base_handle: ScrollHandle, .. }` (`src/elements/uniform_list.rs:113-145`); `ScrollHandle::offset` and `set_offset` are at `src/elements/div.rs:4258` and `:4394`. Offsets are negative downward; check the sign in source before writing the clamp.
- If the UI-PRC-023 fallback inside GPUI is needed (ADR-014 step 2), it is E22 work in the optimisation pass, not this bead.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`. Bench and gate runs are not builds: run them with nothing else heavy on the machine.

title: E01-009 tl-app bench entry: bench_main.rs
description:
## Context
`tasklens --bench <scene> --duration 30 --warmup 5 --json <out>` (ADR-014, table (c), APP-052) runs one scene. `tl-app/src/bench_main.rs` is the binary side: it supplies the clocks `tl-ui` cannot read, starts the real engine for the `bridge` scene, runs GPUI with the scene, and shuts down. Sources: ADR-014, ADR-010 (close and shutdown order), ADR-005 (`Engine::start`, `EngineHandle`), table (c).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/bench_main.rs`, compiled only with `#[cfg(feature = "bench")]`:

```rust
pub struct BenchArgs { pub scene: String, pub duration_s: u32, pub warmup_s: u32, pub json: Option<PathBuf> }
/// Returns the process exit code: 0 on a finished run, 1 on a scene failure, 2 on an unknown scene.
pub fn run(args: BenchArgs) -> i32;
fn thread_cpu_ns() -> u64;    // rustix::time::clock_gettime(ClockId::ThreadCPUTime), as ns
fn process_cpu_ns() -> u64;   // rustix::time::clock_gettime(ClockId::ProcessCPUTime), as ns
```

Steps of `run`:
1. `BenchScene::from_arg(&args.scene)`; `None` prints `unknown bench scene "<name>"; expected perf-cpu, table-2000, bridge or static` to stderr and returns 2.
2. For `Bridge` only: `Engine::start(EngineConfig::default())` (E09-A1), and set a `Demand` on it with the Performance tab visible, the CPU page shown and fast CPU (10 Hz, `cpu_fast`) on, as the Performance tab would (ADR-008). Wrap the handle as `Arc<dyn EngineClient>`.
3. Build the GPUI `Application` exactly as normal startup does up to fonts, kit init, assets and theme (UI-SHL-110 step 8, through `TasklensUi::init`, E16-A1), but open no main window; call `tl_ui::bench::run(cx, scene, opts, BenchClocks { thread_cpu_ns, process_cpu_ns }, real)`. When the task finishes: on `Ok(report)` keep exit code 0; on `Err(e)` print `bench failed: <e>` to stderr and set exit code 1; then `cx.quit()`.
4. After `Application::run` returns: if an engine was started, `handle.shutdown(Duration::from_millis(1500))` (ADR-010); log the `ShutdownReport` at `info` on target `tasklens::perf`.
5. Return the exit code.

The panic hook, logging and argument parsing are done by `main.rs` (E33-A1) before `run` is called.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `--bench charts` **When** run **Then** stderr has `unknown bench scene "charts"; expected perf-cpu, table-2000, bridge or static` and the exit code is 2, with no window opened.
- **Given** `--bench static --duration 2 --warmup 1 --json /tmp/x.json` on the owner machine **When** run **Then** the process exits 0 within 5 s and the file holds a report with `"scene": "static"`.
- **Given** `--bench bridge --duration 5 --warmup 1` **When** run **Then** the engine is started, the report has a non-null `bridge_latency_ms`, and after exit no `tl-engine` thread is left (process gone within 2 s).
- **Given** two calls of `thread_cpu_ns()` around a 10 ms busy loop **When** compared **Then** the delta is between 5 ms and 50 ms (sanity).

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/bench_main.rs`: create.

## Tests
- `bench_main::tests::unknown_scene_exit_2` (calls the scene parsing helper, no GPUI).
- `bench_main::tests::thread_cpu_clock_moves`: the 10 ms busy-loop delta check.
- Manual, recorded by E01-A1: the static and bridge commands above.
Run with `cargo test -p tl-app --features bench bench_main`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: exact texts above; exit codes 0, 1, 2.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no work between scenes and GPUI beyond startup; the engine is started only for `bridge`.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- `rustix` with feature `time` is in `tl-app`'s allowed row (ADR-001). `ClockId::ThreadCPUTime` and `ClockId::ProcessCPUTime` are rustix 1.x names; check the rustix source in `~/.cargo/registry` before use.

title: E01-011 cargo xtask bench: three runs per scene, median and table
description:
## Context
`cargo xtask bench` runs every scene 3 times and writes `target/bench/<date>-<git sha>.json` plus a table (ADR-014, UI-PRF-053). Each later phase re-runs it; a regression above 20% on any gated metric blocks the phase (ADR-014 verification). Sources: ADR-014, UI-PRF-053, ADR-013 layers table (performance gates run on the owner machine, not in CI).

## Deliverable
`xtask/src/bench.rs`:

```rust
pub struct BenchCmd { pub scenes: Vec<String>, pub runs: u32, pub compare: Option<PathBuf> }
pub fn run(cmd: BenchCmd) -> anyhow::Result<()>;
```

- Command line (parsed by hand in this file, xtask has no clap): `cargo xtask bench [--scene <name>]... [--runs <n>] [--compare <old.json>]`. Defaults: scenes `perf-cpu`, `table-2000`, `bridge`, `static` in that order; runs 3.
- Step 1: build once: `cargo build --release -p tl-app --features bench` (through the build rule wrapper when the environment variable `TL_BUILD_WRAP=1` is set; see Notes).
- Step 2: for each scene, `runs` times: `target/release/tasklens --bench <scene> --duration 30 --warmup 5 --json target/bench/tmp/<scene>-<i>.json`. A non-zero exit fails the whole command with `bench: <scene> run <i> failed with exit code <c>`.
- Step 3: for each scene pick the median run by `frame_cpu_ms.p99` (for `static`: by `process_cpu_pct`), and write `target/bench/<date>-<sha>.json` = `{ "date": "<YYYY-MM-DD>", "git_sha": "<sha>", "scenes": { "<scene>": { "median": <report>, "runs": [<report>, ...] } } }`. `<date>` is the UTC date from `SystemTime`, `<sha>` is `git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD`, with `-dirty` appended when `git status --porcelain` is non-empty.
- Step 4: print a Markdown table to stdout, one row per scene: `| Scene | frame CPU p50 ms | p99 ms | missed | process CPU % | RSS MB | stalls | bridge p99 ms |`, values from the median run, two decimals.
- `--compare <old.json>`: for every gated metric (frame CPU p50 and p99, missed frames, process CPU, RSS, bridge p99), print the change in percent and exit 1 with `bench: regression above 20% in <scene> <metric>` if any metric is more than 20% worse.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** three fake report files for one scene with p99 1.0, 1.4, 1.2 ms **When** the median is picked **Then** the 1.2 ms run is the median.
- **Given** an old summary with `perf-cpu` p99 1.0 ms and a new one with 1.25 ms **When** `--compare` runs **Then** the exit code is 1 and the message names `perf-cpu frame_cpu_ms.p99`.
- **Given** a new p99 of 1.15 ms **When** compared **Then** the exit code is 0.
- **Given** a child exit code 1 for `bridge` run 2 **When** the command runs **Then** it stops with `bench: bridge run 2 failed with exit code 1`.
- **Given** `--scene perf-cpu --runs 1` **When** run on the owner machine **Then** `target/bench/<date>-<sha>.json` exists with one scene and one run.

## Files
- `xtask/src/bench.rs`: create.

## Tests
- `bench::tests::median_by_p99`
- `bench::tests::median_static_by_process_cpu`
- `bench::tests::compare_flags_regression_over_20pct`
- `bench::tests::compare_passes_under_20pct`
- `bench::tests::summary_json_shape` (serialize a summary from fixture reports)
Run with `cargo test -p xtask bench`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: exact texts above; `anyhow` is allowed in `xtask` (ADR-015).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the command itself is not measured; it runs scenes one at a time, never in parallel.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- `xtask` allowed dependencies are `serde`, `serde_json`, `anyhow` (ADR-001); no clap, no chrono. Compute the UTC date from `SystemTime::now()` with a days-to-civil conversion in this file.
- The build rule wrapper: open item E01-OI-10 (recommended: `xtask bench` runs the build through the flock and `systemd-run` command of the build rule when `TL_BUILD_WRAP=1`, and plainly otherwise).

title: E01-015 Bench soak scene for zed#64499: three windows, 10 minutes
description:
## Context
zed#64499 (open) can stop GPUI redraws on KWin until input arrives. ADR-010 step 2 fixes the phase-0 soak: three tasklens windows (the main window plus two detached graph windows of the spike), 1 Hz updates, smooth charts on, 10 minutes with no input; pass is zero stalls longer than 250 ms, counted by the `AnimationDriver` stall detector (`FrameStats.stalls`, E19-A1). The docs name no command for the soak; this bead adds it as a bench scene. Sources: ADR-010 zed#64499 mitigation steps 1 and 2, ADR-014 gate "zed#64499 soak", U-9.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/scenes.rs` and `bench/mod.rs`, a fifth scene (pending open item E01-OI-12, which also covers adding the name to table (c)):

- `BenchScene::Soak`, argument name `soak`; default duration 600 s and warm-up 0 s when `--duration` and `--warmup` are not given (the `tl-app` arm passes 30 and 5 by default, so the soak is run with explicit `--duration 600 --warmup 0`).
- Window 1: the `perf-cpu` composition (UI-PRF-053) but with every series fed at 1 Hz (one `BenchEngine` tick per second instead of 10 Hz), smooth graphs on.
- Windows 2 and 3: bench-only windows, 600 x 300 logical px each, each with one `ChartView` (E19-A1) of one synthetic 1 Hz series (window 2: CPU total; window 3: Memory), titles "tasklens Soak Graph 1" and "tasklens Soak Graph 2". These are not the P3 detached graph windows of E26; they only exercise three frame loops.
- The `FrameProbe` is not started (it would force frames and hide the bug). Each window has its own `AnimationDriver`; at the end the scene sums their `FrameStats.stalls` into the report's `stalls` and logs each window's count at `info` on target `tasklens::perf`.
- No input is sent. The scene ends after the duration and quits.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `--bench soak --duration 600 --warmup 0` **When** run on the owner machine with no input **Then** three windows open and the run exits 0 after 600 s with a report whose `"scene"` is `"soak"`.
- **Given** a `TestAppContext` soak with 10 s of simulated time **When** it ends **Then** three windows existed and `FrameStats.requested > 0` in each (charts with smooth graphs request frames).
- **Given** a soak report **When** read **Then** `stalls` equals the sum of the three drivers' stall counts.
- **Given** `BenchScene::from_arg("soak")` **When** called **Then** it returns `Soak`.

title: E01-017 First-frame, minimized-CPU and RSS gate measurements
description:
## Context
Three ADR-014 gates are not covered by the scene JSON: first frame warm (<= 200 ms median of 5 launches, from process start time `/proc/self/stat` field 22 to the first frame callback), first frame cold (<= 500 ms after dropping the page cache, run by the owner), and process CPU with the window minimized and recording off (<= 0.3% of one core over 60 s). The first-frame time is logged by the startup sequence as `info!(target: "tasklens::perf", first_frame_ms)` (UI-SHL-110 step 11). Sources: ADR-014 gates, UI-SHL-110, ADR-015 log file location.

## Deliverable
Fill the section "First frame, minimized CPU and RSS" of `docs/spike/phase0-results.md`:

1. First frame, warm: run the normal release build (`target/release/tasklens`, without `bench`) 5 times in a row; after each first frame, close the main window (ADR-010: closing it quits the app when the tray is off). Read `first_frame_ms` from the log file in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/logs/` (the newest `tasklens.*.log`). Record the 5 values and the median; PASS if the median <= 200 ms.
2. First frame, cold: the owner runs `sync` and drops the page cache (`echo 3` into `/proc/sys/vm/drop_caches` as root), then starts tasklens once. Record the value; PASS if <= 500 ms. This step needs root: the implementer asks the owner to run it and records the owner's number.
3. Minimized CPU: start tasklens normally, minimize the window, wait 10 s, then read `utime + stime` (fields 14 and 15 of `/proc/<pid>/stat`, in clock ticks, `getconf CLK_TCK`) at t = 0 and t = 60 s; CPU % = 100 x delta ticks / CLK_TCK / 60. Recording is off (P0 has no history). PASS if <= 0.3%.
4. Copy the RSS after `table-2000` value from the gate-run section here with its PASS or FAIL, so this section lists every memory and startup gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 5 warm launches **When** recorded **Then** the section lists 5 `first_frame_ms` values, their median, and PASS or FAIL against 200 ms.
- **Given** the owner's cold run **When** recorded **Then** the value and PASS or FAIL against 500 ms are listed, marked "run by the owner".
- **Given** the minimized measurement **When** recorded **Then** the two tick readings, CLK_TCK, the computed percent and PASS or FAIL against 0.3% are listed.
- **Given** no `first_frame_ms` line in the log **When** step 1 runs **Then** the section says "first_frame_ms is not logged by this build" and the gate is FAIL (not skipped), and the leader is told which bead must add the log line.

title: E01-A2 Phase-0 results and decision recorded
description:
## Context
Anchor for the end of phase 0. ADR-014 decision rule: (1) all gates pass: GPUI is confirmed and production beads proceed; (2) any rendering or Wayland gate fails: one focused optimisation pass of at most 2 working days, limited to path merging (ADR-009 rule 7), decimation tuning, fewer grid quads, caching more views, text cache fixes, and the vendored zed#64499 patch, then re-run every gate; (3) still failing: switch to the predetermined fallback (eframe 0.36.2 with a custom wgpu chart pass, new crate `tl-ui-egui`); no other GPUI forks, gpui-ce or private renderer work; (4) collection-cost gates are engine work and never trigger the UI fallback. This is not a code dependency for other epics: the leader starts P1 UI beads only after this bead closes (00-epics section 4). Sources: ADR-014, ADR-010, 00-epics section 4, the U list.

## Deliverable
Complete `docs/spike/phase0-results.md`:
1. "Unverified items settled in phase 0": one line each for U-2, U-3, U-4, U-7, U-9, U-10, U-36, U-39, U-47, with confirmed, failed (and the fallback taken) or pending (with the bead that settles it). U-4 comes from E15-A3 (headless render tests on lavapipe) and U-7 from E15-A1 (Noto Sans `tnum` and loading); copy their recorded outcomes, or write "pending E15-A3" if that P1 bead has not run. U-10 is "pending E01-024" unless E01-024 has run.
2. "Decision": a table of every rendering and Wayland gate with its result (from the gate-run, first-frame, soak and checklist sections), then exactly one of these three lines:
   - "Decision: pass. GPUI is confirmed; production beads proceed."
   - "Decision: optimise. Failing gates: <list>. One optimisation pass of at most 2 working days, limited to the ADR-014 step 2 list, then every gate is re-run."
   - "Decision: fall back. Gates still failing after the optimisation pass: <list>. Switch to eframe with the custom wgpu chart pass (ADR-014)."
   Collection-cost results are listed under the table with the note that they never trigger the UI fallback.
3. Tell the leader the decision. On "optimise", the leader opens the optimisation beads; this bead stays open until the re-run gates are recorded and the final decision line is pass or fall back.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the results file **When** read **Then** all eleven sections are filled (GPU power baseline and Collection cost may say "pending E01-023" and "pending E01-024").
- **Given** the U section **When** read **Then** it has one line for each of U-2, U-3, U-4, U-7, U-9, U-10, U-36, U-39, U-47.

- **Given** any rendering or Wayland gate failed and no optimisation pass has run **When** the decision is written **Then** the line is the "optimise" line listing the failing gates, and the bead stays open.
- **Given** a collection-cost gate failed and every UI gate passed **When** the decision is written **Then** the line is "pass" (decision rule step 4).
- **Given** the file **When** committed **Then** the commit uses a pathspec for `docs/spike/phase0-results.md` only.

## Tests

| Gate | Pass |
|---|---|
| UI thread CPU per frame, `perf-cpu` | p50 <= 1.0 ms, p99 <= 2.0 ms |
| UI thread CPU per frame, `table-2000` while scrolling | p99 <= 2.0 ms |
| Missed frames, `perf-cpu` and `table-2000` | 0 in the median run; at most 2 in every run; none above 3 x period |
| Process CPU, `perf-cpu` | <= 30% of one core |
| Process CPU, `static` | <= 2% of one core |
| Process CPU, window minimized, recording off | <= 0.3% of one core (measured over 60 s) |
| Collection cost, real engine, Performance tab visible | <= 2% of one core |

| First frame after launch (warm cache) | <= 200 ms median of 5 launches, from process start time (`/proc/self/stat` field 22) to the first frame callback |

| RSS after `table-2000` | <= 150 MB |
| zed#64499 soak | 0 stalls over 250 ms in 10 minutes |
| Bridge | 10 Hz samples arrive; wake-to-render latency p99 <= 20 ms |

title: E01-019 Conditional: vendor gpui-pre-linux 0.3.7 with the zed#64499 fix
description:
## Context
Only if the soak (E01-018) failed. ADR-010 step 3: vendor `gpui-pre-linux 0.3.7` into `vendor/gpui-pre-linux/` (crates.io source as the first commit, the fix as the second) and patch it in. This is the only GPUI patch the architecture allows (ADR-002 rejected alternatives, ADR-014 decision rule step 2). If the soak passed, close this bead with the comment "Not needed: soak passed in E01-018." and change nothing. Sources: ADR-010 zed#64499 mitigation step 3, ADR-014 decision rule, U-9.

## Deliverable
1. Commit 1: the unmodified crates.io source of `gpui-pre-linux` version `0.3.7` in `vendor/gpui-pre-linux/` (from `~/.cargo/registry/src/*/gpui-pre-linux-0.3.7/`, including its `Cargo.toml`, without `target/`). Message: "Vendor gpui-pre-linux 0.3.7 from crates.io".
2. Commit 2: the fix in the Wayland frame scheduling code: in `schedule_frame()`, if the state is `AwaitingCallback` (or `Scheduled` or `RetryScheduled`) and the state has not advanced for more than 2 frame intervals, force a new frame request as from `Parked`. Message: "gpui-pre-linux: re-request a frame when the callback is overdue (zed#64499)".
The `[patch.crates-io]` line in the root `Cargo.toml` is E01-020.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** commit 1 **When** diffed against the registry copy **Then** there is no difference.
- **Given** commit 2 **When** reviewed **Then** it changes only the frame-scheduling state machine as described, and a unit test or a comment names zed#64499.
- **Given** the soak passed in E01-018 **When** this bead is picked up **Then** it is closed as not needed with no file changes.

title: E01-021 Phase-0 manual checklist: CSD, monitors, lock, suspend, restore, sharpness, run return
description:
## Context
ADR-014 and ADR-010 fix a manual checklist that headless tests cannot cover. It settles U-36 (CSD on KWin, with the predetermined fallback to server decorations), U-3 (KWin causes a render when a minimized window is restored) and U-2 (`Application::run` returns on Linux after `cx.quit()`). Sources: ADR-014 checklist, ADR-010 decorations, hidden state, multi-monitor, close behaviour, D-006, U-2, U-3, U-36.

## Deliverable
Fill the section "Manual checklist" of `docs/spike/phase0-results.md` with a table `| # | Check | How | Result (PASS or FAIL) | Notes |`, one row per check, run on the owner machine with the normal release build (main window, client-side decorations, the default):

CSD checks (ADR-010; U-36):
1. Drag the window by the title bar.
2. Double-click the title bar maximizes; double-click again restores.
3. Restore from maximized with the caption button.
4. Resize from all four edges and all four corners.
5. Right-click the title bar opens the KWin window menu.
6. Tiling (Meta+Left, Meta+Right, quick tile by dragging to a screen edge).
Multi-monitor and session (ADR-010):
7. Move the window across all three monitors.
8. Straddle two monitors; content renders on both parts.
9. Maximize on each monitor.
10. Unplug one monitor and plug it back while tasklens runs.
11. Lock and unlock the session.
12. One suspend and resume (zed#58382 atlas corruption check: text and icons intact after resume).
13. 10-minute zed#64499 soak: link to the soak section result (E01-018 and E01-020).
14. Minimize and restore re-renders: with the Performance tab showing moving charts, minimize for 30 s, restore; the charts show current data within 1 s without moving the mouse over the window (U-3).
15. Text sharpness at 110%: a screenshot viewed at 2x zoom shows no blur; attach the screenshot path (not committed if it shows personal data).
Run return (U-2):
16. Start tasklens from a terminal with `TASKLENS_LOG=info`, close the main window; record whether the log shows the line `main` writes after `Application::run` returns (the `ShutdownReport` log from E33-A1) or only the `on_app_quit` path ran. Record "U-2 confirmed" or "U-2 failed".

Then add to "Unverified items settled in phase 0":
- U-36: "confirmed, client-side decorations stay the default" if checks 1 to 6 all pass; otherwise "failed on check <n>: `appearance.decorations` default becomes \"server\" (ADR-010, no further discussion)" and tell the leader, who opens the bead that changes the default.
- U-3: "confirmed" if check 14 passes; otherwise "failed: the hidden-state timer calls `window.refresh()` every 1 s while hidden (ADR-010)" and tell the leader (E16's hub timer bead).
- U-2: from check 16.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the section **When** read **Then** it has 16 rows with PASS or FAIL each and a one-line note for every FAIL.
- **Given** any of checks 1 to 6 fails **When** recorded **Then** the U-36 line states the server-decorations fallback and names the failing check.
- **Given** check 14 fails **When** recorded **Then** the U-3 line states the 1 s `window.refresh()` fallback.

title: E01-022 Record the polkit dismissed and denied error names (U-39)
description:
## Context
U-39: on systemd D-Bus calls under `org.freedesktop.systemd1.manage-units`, a dismissed polkit prompt and a denial may come back as the same access-denied error. Phase 0 records both error names. R-117: until verified, systemd D-Bus paths show "<failure text>: not authorized" for both; if phase 0 finds a distinguishing error name, the dismissed case switches to "Authentication cancelled". Sources: U-39, R-117, UI-SYS-007.

## Deliverable
Fill the section "polkit error names (U-39)" of `docs/spike/phase0-results.md`:
1. Pick, with the owner, one system service that is safe to restart on this machine (the owner names it; record its name).
2. Dismissed case: run `busctl --system call --allow-interactive-authorization=yes org.freedesktop.systemd1 /org/freedesktop/systemd1 org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager RestartUnit ss <unit> replace` as the normal user, and press Cancel (or Esc) on the KDE polkit prompt. Record the full D-Bus error name and message printed by `busctl`.
3. Denied case: run the same command and enter a wrong password until polkit gives up (3 attempts), or, if the owner prefers, use a test user that is not an administrator. Record the error name and message.
4. No-agent case (for completeness, R-117): run the command with `--allow-interactive-authorization=no`; record the error (expected `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.InteractiveAuthorizationRequired`).
5. In "Unverified items settled in phase 0", write U-39: "confirmed: both cases return <name>" or "failed: dismissed returns <name1>, denied returns <name2>; the dismissed case shows \"Authentication cancelled\" (R-117)". Tell the leader the result, because E11 and E27 beads use it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the three runs **When** recorded **Then** each lists the exact error name and message.
- **Given** the names are equal for dismissed and denied **When** recorded **Then** the U-39 line says "confirmed".
- **Given** the names differ **When** recorded **Then** the U-39 line gives both names and the "Authentication cancelled" rule.

title: E01-023 GPU power baseline through the probe (report only)
description:

The probe and its client are P1 (E13-A1, E13-A2), so the phase-0 reports carry `gpu: null`; this bead adds the measurement once the probe exists. Sources: ADR-014, ADR-007, open question 7. title: E01-024 Collection-cost gates with the real engine (U-10)
description:
## Context
ADR-014 gates: collection cost with the real engine <= 2% of one core with the Performance tab visible, and <= 3.5% with the Processes tab visible with this machine's processes. U-10 asks whether both are reachable. Decision rule step 4: collection-cost gates are engine work and never trigger the UI fallback, so they do not block E01-A2. They need the P1 Processes worker (E10-A1) and system workers (E12-A2). The measurement method is open item E01-OI-15. Sources: ADR-014, ADR-016 verification (15 ms sweep), U-10, open question 1.

## Deliverable
Fill the section "Collection cost" of `docs/spike/phase0-results.md`:
1. Method (recommended in E01-OI-15): run the normal release build; for 60 s sum `utime + stime` of the engine threads, which are the threads in `/proc/<pid>/task/*/comm` whose name starts with `tl-engine` (ADR-004 `thread_name_prefix("tl-engine")`), plus the `tl-gpu-probe` child if running; percent of one core = 100 x delta ticks / CLK_TCK / 60.
2. Run once with the Performance tab visible (CPU page) and once with the Processes tab visible, on this machine's normal process set; record the process count from `ls /proc | grep -c '^[0-9]'`.
3. Record both values with PASS or FAIL against 2% and 3.5%, and the U-10 line: "confirmed" if both pass, else "failed: <which>", with the note that this is engine work (decision rule step 4).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the two 60 s runs **When** recorded **Then** each lists the tick deltas, CLK_TCK, process count, percent and PASS or FAIL.
- **Given** a FAIL **When** recorded **Then** the U-10 line names the failing gate and the leader is told; no UI fallback is triggered.

## Files

## Tests

## Cross-cutting

- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: carries both collection-cost gates.
- Privacy: do not record process names.

title: E01-004 Bench synthetic CPU, device and stats sources
description:
## Context
Every phase-0 scene uses deterministic synthetic data from `tl-ui/src/bench/synth.rs`, seeded with 42, so runs are comparable (ADR-014, UI-PRF-053). This bead writes the generators for the `perf-cpu` family: 32 per-core CPU series at 10 Hz, kernel and total series, 9 sidebar device series at 1 Hz, and the 12 live Details values at 1 Hz. The table generator for `table-2000` is added to the same file by E01-008. Sources: UI-PRF-053 (formulas, device list, stats values), UI-PRF-024 (rows 1 to 12), ADR-003 (`Sample`, `SeriesId`, `MetricId`, `DeviceIdx`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/bench/synth.rs`, plus the line `pub mod synth;` in `bench/mod.rs`.

- `pub const SEED: u64 = 42;`
- `pub struct BenchRng` : a deterministic PRNG with `new(seed: u64)`, `next_u64()`, `next_f32_unit()` (uniform in [0, 1)), `uniform(lo: f32, hi: f32) -> f32`, `gaussian(sigma: f32) -> f32`. Algorithm: see open item E01-OI-1 (recommended: SplitMix64 for `next_u64`, Box-Muller for `gaussian`, written in this file with no new dependency, because `tl-ui`'s allowed row in ADR-001 has no PRNG crate). Do not add a crate.
- `pub struct CpuSynth` with `pub fn new(rng: &mut BenchRng) -> Self` and `pub fn sample(&mut self, t_s: f64) -> CpuFrame`:
  - 32 logical CPUs. Per core c, drawn once at construction in core order: `base_c = uniform(5, 60)`, `P_c = uniform(3, 17)` seconds.
  - Per sample: `value_c = clamp(base_c + 25 * sin(2 * PI * t_s / P_c) + gaussian(4), 0, 100)`; `kernel_c = clamp(0.2 * value_c + gaussian(1), 0, 100)`; `total = mean(value_c)`; total kernel = `mean(kernel_c)`.
  - `pub struct CpuFrame { pub per_core: [f32; 32], pub per_core_kernel: [f32; 32], pub total: f32, pub total_kernel: f32 }`.
- `pub struct DeviceSynth` with `sample_1hz(&mut self, rng: &mut BenchRng) -> DeviceFrame` for the 9 sidebar cards, in this order: CPU, Memory, GPU 0, Disk 0, Disk 1, Disk 2, Disk 3, enp38s0, tailscale0. Values (UI-PRF-053): memory 55% with a random walk of +-1 (see E01-OI-2 for the step rule); GPU 10% +- 8; disks bursts 0..100% with p = 0.1 per second; networks bursts 0.01..5 Mbps. The CPU card uses the 10 Hz total from `CpuSynth`, not this generator.
- `pub struct StatsSynth` with `sample_1hz(&mut self, rng, t_s) -> StatsFrame` for Details rows 1 to 12 of UI-PRF-024: Utilization and Kernel time from `CpuSynth`; Processes 295 +- 3; Threads 5 596 +- 20; Handles 253 248 +- 500; Up time counting up from a fixed start; Speed 4631 +- 200 MHz; Temperature 52 +- 2 degrees C; Load average a random walk. Rows 8 (Base speed 4200 MHz), 9 (Sockets 1) and 10 (Power draw, hidden in P0 because it is a P2 row) are static. Rows 13 to 26 are static (`DEVICES`).
- `pub fn prefill(cpu: &mut CpuSynth, ...) -> PrefilledSeries`: produces 600 samples per 10 Hz series (60 s range) and 60 per 1 Hz series, timestamps ending at the scene start time, so decimation and geometry rebuild run from frame 1 (UI-PRF-053).
- Timestamps are `TimeNs` (CLOCK_BOOTTIME ns, ADR-003). Sample values are `f32` in `tl_model::series::Sample`.
- Generators never allocate per sample after construction (fixed arrays).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** two `BenchRng::new(42)` **When** each draws 1,000 `next_u64` **Then** the sequences are identical.
- **Given** two `CpuSynth` built from `BenchRng::new(42)` **When** each produces its first 1,000 samples at 10 Hz **Then** every `per_core`, `per_core_kernel` and `total` value is bit-identical.
- **Given** any sample **When** checked **Then** every per-core and kernel value is in [0, 100] and `total` equals the mean of the 32 per-core values within 1e-4.
- **Given** a `CpuSynth` from seed 42 **When** its 32 `base_c` and `P_c` are read **Then** every `base_c` is in [5, 60) and every `P_c` is in [3, 17).
- **Given** `prefill` at scene start `t0` **When** it returns **Then** each 10 Hz series has exactly 600 samples with the last timestamp `t0` and spacing 100 ms, and each 1 Hz series has 60 samples with spacing 1 s.
- **Given** `StatsSynth` **When** 100 samples are drawn **Then** Processes stays in 292..=298, Threads in 5 576..=5 616, Handles in 252 748..=253 748, Speed in 4431..=4831 MHz, Temperature in 50..=54 C.
- **Given** `DeviceSynth` **When** 10 000 one-second samples are drawn **Then** the fraction of non-zero disk samples per disk is 0.1 +- 0.02.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/synth.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/mod.rs`: change, add `pub mod synth;`.

## Tests
- `bench::synth::tests::synth_is_deterministic`: two runs with seed 42 produce identical first 1,000 samples (UI-PRF-053 test name).
- `bench::synth::tests::cpu_values_in_range`: range and mean checks above.
- `bench::synth::tests::prefill_lengths_and_spacing`: 600 and 60 samples, spacing, last timestamp.
- `bench::synth::tests::stats_ranges`: the StatsSynth ranges above.
- `bench::synth::tests::disk_burst_probability`: 0.1 +- 0.02 over 10 000 samples.
Run with `cargo test -p tl-ui --features bench bench::synth`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A (pure functions).
- Validity: every synthetic sample is a valid measured value (`SampleFlags` empty); no gaps.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no allocation per sample; the generators run on the bench publisher thread, whose CPU counts toward process CPU, so keep them cheap (32 sines per 100 ms).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Open item E01-OI-1 (PRNG algorithm) and E01-OI-2 (interpretation of "+- N", "random walk" and network burst probability) must be settled by the leader before this bead starts. The recommended reading, if accepted: "X +- N" means a fresh uniform draw in [X - N, X + N] each second (integers rounded for counts); "random walk +- 1" means each second add a uniform step in [-1, 1] and clamp to [0, 100]; load average walk step uniform in [-0.05, 0.05], clamped at 0, start 1.24 0.98 0.87; network bursts use the disk rule (p = 0.1 per second, else 0.01 Mbps).
- `std::f64::consts::PI`; `f32::clamp`.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`. Bench and gate runs are not builds: run them with nothing else heavy on the machine.

title: E01-005 BenchEngine: scripted EngineClient for the bench scenes
description:
## Context
The scenes replace the real `EngineClient` with `BenchEngine`, a fake engine with a scripted publisher (ADR-013 fake engine, UI-PRF-053), except the `bridge` scene, where the total CPU series comes from the real engine. `BenchEngine` builds full `Snapshot`s from the synthetic generators in `synth.rs` and publishes them like the real bridge: replace the latest snapshot, then send one wake token. Sources: ADR-005 (`EngineClient`, one-token wake), ADR-003 (`Snapshot`, `SeriesSet`, `SeriesView`, `DeviceCatalog`, `ComponentHeader`), UI-PRF-053.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/bench/engine.rs`, plus `pub mod engine;` in `bench/mod.rs`.

```rust
pub enum BenchFeed {
    /// Every series synthetic (perf-cpu, static, table-2000).
    Synthetic,
    /// CPU_TOTAL and CPU_KERNEL of the all-CPUs device come from this client; the 32 per-core
    /// series and every other value stay synthetic (bridge scene).
    Bridge(Arc<dyn EngineClient>),
}
pub struct BenchEngine { /* latest: Mutex<Arc<Snapshot>>, wake channel, recorded commands */ }
impl BenchEngine {
    pub fn start(feed: BenchFeed, seed: u64, t0: TimeNs) -> Arc<Self>;
    pub fn stop(&self);                          // joins the publisher thread
    pub fn commands(&self) -> Vec<Command>;      // recorded, for tests
    pub fn published_10hz(&self) -> u64;         // count of 10 Hz publishes
}
impl EngineClient for BenchEngine { ... }
```

- Publisher: one `std::thread` named `tl-bench-pub` with absolute deadlines every 100 ms from `t0` (no drift: next deadline = previous deadline + 100 ms, sleep until it). Each tick appends one `CpuFrame` sample to the 32 per-core, 32 per-core kernel, total and total-kernel series; every 10th tick also appends the 1 Hz device and stats samples. Then it builds a new `Snapshot` (sequence + 1, `published_ns = now_boot_ns()`), stores it, and sends one wake token with `try_send` on an `async_channel::bounded(1)` (a full channel means a wake is already pending; ignore it).
- Series rings: fixed-capacity buffers of 602 samples for 10 Hz series and 62 for 1 Hz series (ADR-003 fast tier), pre-filled with `synth::prefill`. Each publish creates a new `Arc<[Sample]>` only for series that changed; unchanged series reuse their `Arc<SeriesView>` (ADR-003 `SeriesSet` rule) and keep their `version`.
- Device catalog: `DeviceIdx(0)` = `CpuPackage` (display name "CPU"), `DeviceIdx(1..=32)` = `CpuLogical { id: 0..=31 }`, then Memory, GPU 0, Disk 0 to Disk 3, `enp38s0`, `tailscale0` with the identities of ADR-003 (`Gpu`, `Disk`, `Net`) and fixed placeholder fields (major/minor 259:0..3, ifindex 2 and 3, netns inode 1). `present = true`, `generation = 0`.
- Series ids: `MetricId::CPU_TOTAL`, `CPU_KERNEL` on each CPU device; `MEM_USED` on Memory; `GPU_UTIL` on GPU 0; `DISK_ACTIVE` on disks; `NET_RX` and `NET_TX` on networks (ADR-003 constants). `SystemSnapshot` carries the 12 live Details values and a `CpuTopology` of 32 logical CPUs, 16 cores, 2 per core, all `CoreKind::Standard`.
- Bridge feed: on each tick, read `client.latest()`; copy its newest `CPU_TOTAL` and `CPU_KERNEL` samples of the `CpuPackage` device into the bench series (no synthetic total); record for each copied sample `(sample.t_ns, real_snapshot.published_ns)` into a bounded ring of 1,024 entries exposed as `pub fn bridge_origin(&self, t_ns: TimeNs) -> Option<TimeNs>` for the latency measurement in `stats.rs`. Also wake when the real client's wake fires, so a real 10 Hz sample is republished within one tick; count real samples received in `pub fn bridge_samples(&self) -> u64`.
- `set_demand`, `set_settings` store the last value; `send` records the command and returns `Ok(())`; `action_events` returns a receiver that never yields; `journal` returns a handle whose channel is closed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `BenchEngine::start(Synthetic, 42, t0)` **When** 1.0 s of wall time passes **Then** `published_10hz()` is 10 +- 1 and the wake receiver yielded at least one token.
- **Given** two consecutive snapshots **When** compared **Then** `sequence` increased by 1 and the Memory series `Arc` is pointer-equal unless a 1 Hz tick happened between them.
- **Given** a fresh start **When** `latest()` is read before the first tick **Then** every 10 Hz series already has 600 samples (prefill).
- **Given** the catalog **When** read **Then** it has 41 entries: 1 package, 32 logical CPUs, and the 8 non-CPU sidebar devices in the order Memory, GPU 0, Disk 0, Disk 1, Disk 2, Disk 3, enp38s0, tailscale0.
- **Given** `BenchFeed::Bridge(fake)` where `fake` is a `testing::FakeEngine` publishing a CPU_TOTAL sample every 100 ms **When** 1 s passes **Then** the bench total series contains the fake's sample values and `bridge_origin(t)` returns the fake snapshot's `published_ns` for each.
- **Given** `stop()` **When** it returns **Then** the publisher thread has exited and no further wake tokens arrive.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/engine.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/mod.rs`: change, add `pub mod engine;`.

## Tests
- `bench::engine::tests::publishes_at_10hz`: 10 +- 1 publishes per second.
- `bench::engine::tests::unchanged_series_reuse_arc`: pointer equality rule.
- `bench::engine::tests::prefilled_before_first_tick`.
- `bench::engine::tests::catalog_has_41_entries_in_order`.
- `bench::engine::tests::bridge_feed_copies_real_total`: uses `crate::testing::fake_engine::FakeEngine` (E16-A1).
- `bench::engine::tests::stop_joins_thread`.
Run with `cargo test -p tl-ui --features bench bench::engine`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `send` never fails; a panic in the publisher thread is a bench bug and aborts the run (the scene reports it, E01-007).
- Validity: all synthetic components `Validity::Valid`; components the scenes do not draw (connections, services, startup, inventory, windows, details, history) are their `Default` empty values with `Validity::Unsupported` headers.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: per tick, allocate only the changed series' `Arc<[Sample]>` and one `Snapshot`; no per-tick `String` formatting.
- Privacy: N/A (synthetic data).

## Notes
- `tl-ui` may not depend on `tl-engine` or `arc-swap` (ADR-001 allowed rows); use `std::sync::Mutex<Arc<Snapshot>>` for `latest` and take the lock only to clone or replace the `Arc`.
- `async_channel` comes through `tl-model` (allowed there); if `tl-ui` needs it as a direct dependency, that is an allowed-row question: report it, do not add it.
- If any `Snapshot` component type has no `Default` in E03-A2, build an empty value explicitly; do not edit `tl-model`.
- Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`. Bench and gate runs are not builds: run them with nothing else heavy on the machine.

title: E01-006 Bench frame statistics and JSON report
description:
## Context
ADR-014 fixes how the bench measures: UI thread CPU per frame from `CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID` read in each `on_next_frame` callback, frame interval from `Instant::now()` in each callback, missed frames above 1.5 x the output period, process CPU over the run, `VmRSS` at the end, PSS reported only, stalls from the `AnimationDriver`. This bead writes the collector and the JSON report. Sources: ADR-014 measurement tools, UI-PRF-053 outputs, ADR-010 stall detection (E19-A1 `FrameStats.stalls`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/bench/stats.rs`, plus `pub mod stats;` in `bench/mod.rs`.

```rust
/// Clocks the UI crate cannot read itself (tl-ui has no rustix or libc, ADR-001).
/// tl-app supplies them (E01-009) with rustix::time::clock_gettime.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct BenchClocks {
    pub thread_cpu_ns: fn() -> u64,    // ClockId::ThreadCPUTime of the calling thread
    pub process_cpu_ns: fn() -> u64,   // ClockId::ProcessCPUTime (utime + stime of the process)
}
pub const OUTPUT_PERIOD_NS: u64 = 6_944_444;      // 144 Hz fixture output
pub const MISSED_FRAME_NS: u64 = 10_416_667;      // 1.5 x period (10.42 ms)
pub const LONG_MISS_NS: u64 = 20_833_333;         // 3 x period

pub struct FrameProbe { /* intervals_ns: Vec<u64>, cpu_ns: Vec<u64>, last: Option<(Instant, u64)>, active: bool */ }
impl FrameProbe {
    pub fn new(clocks: BenchClocks, capacity: usize) -> Self;   // capacity 144 * 40
    /// Registers window.on_next_frame; the callback records one frame and re-registers while active.
    pub fn start(this: Rc<RefCell<Self>>, window: &mut Window);
    pub fn stop(&mut self);
    pub fn reset(&mut self);   // drops samples taken during warm-up
}
pub struct Percentiles { pub p50: f64, pub p99: f64, pub max: f64 }
pub fn percentiles_ms(ns: &[u64]) -> Percentiles;   // nearest-rank on a sorted copy
pub fn count_missed(intervals_ns: &[u64]) -> (u32 /*> 1.5x*/, u32 /*> 3x*/);

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct BenchReport {
    pub scene: &'static str,
    pub frames: u64,
    pub frame_cpu_ms: Percentiles,
    pub missed_frames: u32,
    pub process_cpu_pct: f64,
    pub probe_cpu_pct: Option<f64>,
    pub rss_mb: f64,
    pub pss_mb: f64,
    pub stalls: u32,
    pub bridge_latency_ms: Option<LatencyPct>,   // { p50, p99 }
    pub gpu: Option<GpuReport>,                  // { power_w, util_pct }
}
pub fn read_rss_pss_mb() -> (f64, f64);   // VmRSS from /proc/self/status, Pss from /proc/self/smaps_rollup
pub fn write_json(report: &BenchReport, path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<()>;   // serde_json, pretty
```

JSON shape (UI-PRF-053, field names exact): `{ scene, frames, frame_cpu_ms: { p50, p99, max }, missed_frames, process_cpu_pct, probe_cpu_pct, rss_mb, pss_mb, stalls, bridge_latency_ms: { p50, p99 } | null, gpu: { power_w, util_pct } | null }` (UI-PRF-053). Field order as listed. `null` for `probe_cpu_pct`, `bridge_latency_ms` and `gpu` when not measured. MB means 1,000,000 bytes (open item E01-OI-4 if the leader wants MiB).

Rules:
- The probe records interval and thread-CPU delta between consecutive callbacks only; the first callback after `start` or `reset` records nothing.
- `process_cpu_pct = 100 * delta(process_cpu_ns) / delta(wall ns)` over the measured window (after warm-up).
- `stalls` is copied from the window's `AnimationDriver` `FrameStats.stalls` (E19-A1) at the end, minus its value at the end of warm-up.
- Missed frames: `count_missed` over the measured intervals. The 3 x count is needed for the gate "none above 3 x period"; the UI-PRF-053 shape has no field for it, see open item E01-OI-3 (recommended: add `long_missed_frames` after `missed_frames`). Until settled, log it with `info!(target: "tasklens::perf", long_missed_frames)`.
- Parsing `/proc/self/status`: the `VmRSS:` line, value in kB (x 1024 bytes). `/proc/self/smaps_rollup`: the `Pss:` line in kB. Missing file or line gives 0.0 and a `warn!(target: "tasklens::perf", ...)`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** intervals `[6.9, 6.9, 11.0, 25.0]` ms **When** `count_missed` runs **Then** it returns `(2, 1)`.
- **Given** 100 values 1..=100 ms **When** `percentiles_ms` runs **Then** p50 = 50.0, p99 = 99.0, max = 100.0 (nearest-rank).
- **Given** an empty slice **When** `percentiles_ms` runs **Then** all three are 0.0 and nothing panics.

title: E01-007 Bench scenes perf-cpu, static and bridge with the run loop
description:
## Context
This bead builds the scene runner and the three Performance-tab scenes of ADR-014 and UI-PRF-053. Each scene opens one window with the real production views (the CPU page with chart element, per-core grid, sidebar and Details grid from E24-A1) fed by `BenchEngine`, waits out the warm-up, measures for the duration, writes the JSON report and quits. Sources: ADR-014 (fixture, scenes, gates), UI-PRF-053 (exact composition), ADR-009 (AnimationDriver), ADR-010 (stalls).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/bench/scenes.rs`, `crates/tl-ui/tests/bench_scenes.rs`, and in `bench/mod.rs` the line `pub mod scenes;` plus the public entry point:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BenchScene { PerfCpu, Table2000, Bridge, Static }
impl BenchScene {
    pub fn from_arg(s: &str) -> Option<Self>;   // "perf-cpu", "table-2000", "bridge", "static"
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str;
}
pub struct BenchOptions { pub duration_s: u32, pub warmup_s: u32, pub json: Option<PathBuf> }  // defaults 30, 5, None
/// Called by tl-app inside Application::run. `real` is Some only for Bridge.
pub fn run(cx: &mut App, scene: BenchScene, opts: BenchOptions, clocks: BenchClocks,
           real: Option<Arc<dyn EngineClient>>) -> Task<Result<BenchReport, BenchError>>;
/// Failure text shown by tl-app; Display prints the inner string.
pub struct BenchError(pub String);
```

Scene composition (UI-PRF-053, exact):
- Common: Phase-0 fixture (ADR-014, UI-PRF-053): window 1600 x 1000 logical px, opened on the 144 Hz output at 110% compositor scale, focused, `motion.smooth_graphs = true`, theme Default Dark, `ui_scale_pct = 100`, `graph_range_s = 60`, synthetic data from `tl-ui/src/bench/` with PRNG seed 42. Window options: `size(px(1600.), px(1000.))`, opaque background, client decorations, `app_id` `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens`. The Processes tab and all other tabs are not built.
- `perf-cpu`: the Performance page with the CPU page selected, sidebar visible at `nav_width = 252`. The CPU page renders the total CPU chart (width W x 300 px, fill + line + kernel line) above the 32-core grid (8 x 4, kernel overlays on), through the bench-only flag `CpuPage.bench_show_both` (see open item E01-OI-5: the flag lives in E24's `cpu.rs`). Sidebar: 9 cards CPU, Memory, GPU 0, Disk 0, Disk 1, Disk 2, Disk 3, enp38s0, tailscale0. Details grid: rows 1 to 12 live at 1 Hz, rows 13 to 26 static. Per-core percent labels re-format at 10 Hz.
- `static`: `perf-cpu` with `motion.smooth_graphs = false`. The `FrameProbe` is not started. At the end assert `FrameStats.requested == 0` for the window's `AnimationDriver`; a non-zero value fails the run with error text "static scene requested animation frames".
- `bridge`: `perf-cpu` with `BenchFeed::Bridge(real)`. Extra measure: wake-to-render latency, from `Snapshot.published_ns` of the real snapshot that first carried a sample (via `BenchEngine::bridge_origin`) to the first `ChartElement::paint` that includes that sample; requires the paint hook of open item E01-OI-6. Report p50 and p99 in `bridge_latency_ms`. The run fails with "bridge: only N samples arrived" when fewer than 295 real samples arrive in 30 s.
Run loop: open window, start `BenchEngine`, start `FrameProbe` (not in `static`), wait `warmup_s`, `reset()` the probe and take baselines (process CPU ns, wall ns, stalls), wait `duration_s`, stop, build `BenchReport`, write JSON if requested, print the report as one JSON line on stdout, then `cx.quit()`. Timers use `cx.background_executor().timer(..)`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a `TestAppContext` **When** the `perf-cpu` scene view is built with `BenchEngine` **Then** the CPU grid has 32 cells and the sidebar has 9 cards (test `bench_scene_perf_cpu_builds_32_cells_and_9_cards`, UI-PRF-053).
- **Given** `BenchScene::from_arg("table-2000")` **When** called **Then** it returns `Table2000`; `from_arg("charts")` returns `None`.
- **Given** the `static` scene in a `TestAppContext` with 2 s of simulated time **When** it ends **Then** `FrameStats.requested == 0` and the report has `frames == 0` from the probe (probe not started).
- **Given** `opts.json = Some(path)` **When** a scene ends **Then** the file exists, parses as JSON, and has `"scene": "perf-cpu"` (or the scene name run).
- **Given** a bridge run where the fake real client publishes nothing **When** the run ends **Then** the task returns the error "bridge: only 0 samples arrived".
- **Given** warm-up 5 s and duration 30 s **When** a real run ends **Then** `process_cpu_pct` covers only the 30 s window (baseline taken after warm-up).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/scenes.rs`: create (large file, see Notes).
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/mod.rs`: change, add `pub mod scenes;` and re-export `BenchScene`, `BenchOptions`, `run`, `BenchClocks`.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/bench_scenes.rs`: create, `#![cfg(feature = "bench")]`.

Run with `cargo test -p tl-ui --features bench --test bench_scenes`.

- Validity: N/A (all synthetic values valid).
