description:
## Context
The `Connections` worker (`SourceId::Connections`, `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/connections.rs`, ADR-004): every 2 s while the Connections tab or the process Network columns need it, one sock_diag dump plus the socket-inode to pid map, producing the connection records and the per-process TCP attribution. It wraps the tl-collect readers from E06-A1 in a `Source`. Sources: SYS-028, SYS-029, SYS-030, ADR-008 row "Connections and socket attribution", ADR-016 rows "Per-process network", "Socket to pid map", "Connections", PROC-032, U-23.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/connections.rs` (new), a `Source` (E08-A1 trait) run by the standard worker loop:
  - `id()` = `SourceId::Connections`.
  - `period()` = `Some(2 s)` when `Demand.connections` is true, or when `Demand.process_table` is true and `Demand.process_columns` contains any of the column ids `network`, `net_send_rate`, `net_recv_rate`; otherwise `None` (off).
  - `sample()` (on the blocking pool, one job at a time, the whole thing in one job): read `t_ns`; dump TCP over IPv4 and IPv6 with `INET_DIAG_INFO`; dump UDP over IPv4 and IPv6 only when `Demand.connections` is true; rebuild the socket-inode to pid map from `/proc/<pid>/fd`; build the connection records and the per-process attribution (Δ`tcpi_bytes_acked` as send, Δ`tcpi_bytes_received` as receive, per socket inode, over the actual elapsed time; a socket shared by several processes counts for each). All of this uses the E06-A1 functions in `tl-collect/src/net/`.
  - Address strings are formatted once per socket cookie: the source keeps `FxHashMap<u64 cookie, (Arc<str> local, Arc<str> foreign)>` across samples and drops cookies not seen in the latest dump.
  - Rates follow ADR-008 counter rules: first sample of a socket gives no rate (`WarmingUp`); a counter that goes backwards resets the baseline; a boottime-versus-monotonic jump over 250 ms between samples drops all rates for that sample.
  - Publishes one `SourceUpdate` carrying the records (sorted by cookie) and the attribution map `FxHashMap<ProcessKey, (send_bps, recv_bps, shared: bool)>`; owners whose `/proc/<pid>/fd` cannot be read are marked restricted per SYS-030 (the record shows PID "?" and the restricted glyph).
  - Logs the socket-map rebuild time at debug level on every sample, for the phase-0 U-23 check (target under 20 ms).
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs`: add `mod connections;` (chain edit, the only change to that file).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `Demand.connections = false`, `process_table = true` and `process_columns` without network columns **When** `period()` is called **Then** `None`.
- **Given** `process_columns` containing `net_recv_rate` and `process_table = true` **When** `period()` is called **Then** `Some(2 s)`.
- **Given** the Connections tab hidden but the Network column shown **When** a sample runs **Then** no UDP dump is made.
- **Given** two samples 2 s apart where a socket's `tcpi_bytes_acked` grew by 2 000 000 **When** attribution is computed **Then** the owner's send rate is 1 000 000 B/s.
- **Given** a socket seen for the first time **When** attributed **Then** its contribution is `WarmingUp`, not 0.
- **Given** a socket shared by pids 10 and 11 **When** attributed **Then** both get its rate and `shared = true`.
- **Given** the same cookie in two samples **When** records are built **Then** the address strings are the same `Arc`.
- **Given** a boottime jump of 5 s with a monotonic jump of 10 ms **When** sampled **Then** no rates are produced for that sample.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/connections.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs`: one `mod` line.

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `connections.rs`, with the E06-A1 fixtures fed through a sampler function parameter:
- `period_off_without_demand`, `period_on_for_network_columns`, `period_on_for_tab`, `no_udp_dump_when_tab_hidden`, `attribution_rate_from_elapsed_time`, `attribution_first_sample_warming_up`, `attribution_shared_socket`, `address_strings_cached_per_cookie`, `suspend_gap_drops_rates`.
- `demand_switches_rate` (LabRuntime): with the E08-A1 loop and a fake sampler, demand off gives zero samples over 60 virtual seconds, demand on gives one sample every 2 s.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: a dump failure (netlink error) is `Validity::Failed` with `SourceHealth.last_error`; `EACCES` on a pid's fd dir is per-owner `Restricted`.
- Validity: `WarmingUp`, `Valid`, `Restricted`, `Failed`.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one blocking job per 2 s; socket map rebuild target under 20 ms (U-23, measured in phase 0).
- Privacy: never log addresses or ports above debug level.

## Notes

- Close TCP connection (`SockDestroy`, P3) and `destroy_supported` are E11 and E29 work; other namespaces (P4) need the helper (E29).

title: E14-015 Connections worker: reverse DNS for Remote host
description:
## Context
P4. The Remote host column: reverse DNS names for the foreign addresses of the visible connection rows, looked up only while the column is shown. Sources: SYS-035, UI-SYS-069, ADR-008 row "Reverse DNS", Demand field `remote_host_cookies`.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/connections.rs`:
- For each cookie in `Demand.remote_host_cookies` whose record has a foreign address (not `*`): look up the address with the reverse-DNS function in `tl-collect/src/net/rdns.rs` (E06, `getnameinfo` with `NI_NAMEREQD`).
- At most 4 lookups run at once, each in its own `cx.spawn_blocking` job; further addresses wait in a FIFO queue. Lookups are started from the worker loop, never block the 2 s sample.
- Cache by address (not by cookie): positive answers 10 minutes, negative answers 1 minute (SYS-035). A cached address is not looked up again before it expires.
- Each record carries `remote_host: Option<Arc<str>>`: `None` while pending (the UI shows the address), `Some(name)` after a positive answer, `None` again after a negative one.
- When `remote_host_cookies` is empty, no lookups start and the queue is cleared; finished jobs still fill the cache.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 10 demanded cookies with different addresses **When** lookups start **Then** at most 4 run at the same time.
- **Given** a positive answer cached at t=0 **When** the same address is demanded at t=9 min **Then** no new lookup; at t=11 min a new lookup runs.
- **Given** a negative answer at t=0 **When** demanded again at t=61 s **Then** a new lookup runs.
- **Given** `remote_host_cookies` becomes empty **When** the next wake runs **Then** the queue is empty and no new lookup starts.

## Files

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `connections.rs`, LabRuntime with a fake resolver (scripted delays and answers): `rdns_max_four_in_flight`, `rdns_positive_ttl_10_min`, `rdns_negative_ttl_1_min`, `rdns_queue_cleared_without_demand`.

## Cross-cutting

- Performance: at most 4 blocking threads for lookups; the pool max is 4 (ADR-004), so while 4 lookups run the 2 s sample waits for a thread. Record this in the commit message if it shows in the phase-4 measurements.

title: E14-A2 KWin bridge
description:
## Context
Anchor E14-A2. The KWin bridge worker `SourceId::KWin` in `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_kwin.rs` (R-046, ADR-004): on KDE Plasma it loads the `tasklens-bridge` script into KWin, serves the `WindowBridge` object the script calls, and publishes the window list as `Snapshot.windows` (`WindowsSnapshot`, keyed by pid). Commands (E14-018) and the picker (E14-019) follow. Sources: PROC-052, PROC-053, PROC-056, ADR-003 (`WindowsSnapshot`), ADR-004 (KWin bridge worker), canonical table (c), R-046, R-086, U-13, ADR-015 (untrusted text).

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_kwin.rs` (new):
  - `pub(crate) fn factory(io: WorkerIo) -> impl ManagedChildFactory<WorkerError>`.
  - Availability, checked at generation start: `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` contains `KDE` (colon-separated list, case-sensitive) and the name `org.kde.KWin` has an owner on the session bus (`org.freedesktop.DBus.NameHasOwner`). If not: publish an empty `WindowsSnapshot` with `header.validity = Unsupported`, then idle (wake every 60 s with `cx.checkpoint()`, no further calls). This is not a failure.
  - Session connection from the E08-A2 helper. Serve object `/io/github/oysteinkrog/Tasklens/WindowBridge`, interface `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.WindowBridge`, method `Update(s json)` with zbus `#[interface]`.
  - Script: write `include_str!("../../../../assets/kwin/kwin-bridge.js")` with `__TL_BUS_NAME__` replaced by the JSON string of this connection's unique name (open item 5) to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/tasklens/kwin-bridge.js` (directory mode 0700, file 0600, `write_atomic` from tl-ops, E07-A3). Then `org.kde.kwin.Scripting.unloadScript("tasklens-bridge")` (clears a stale copy from a crashed run), `loadScript(path, "tasklens-bridge")`, and `start()` on `/Scripting`.
  - `Update` handler, security checks first: reject (log at debug, return an error reply) when the message sender is not the current owner of `org.kde.KWin` (`GetNameOwner`, refreshed on `NameOwnerChanged`) or when the JSON is longer than 1 MiB. Then parse with `serde_json` into window entries: `internal_id`, `pid`, `caption`, `resource_class`, `desktop_file_name`, `minimized`, `maximized`, `keep_above`, `frame_geometry { x, y, width, height }`, `window_type`. `internal_id` must match a braced UUID `{xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx}` (lowercase hex); entries that fail are dropped. `caption`, `resource_class` and `desktop_file_name` pass through the tl-collect `sanitize` rules (ADR-015: C0 and C1 controls to U+FFFD, bidi controls U+202A to U+202E and U+2066 to U+2069 and U+200B to U+200F removed) and are cut at 4 KiB.
  - Each accepted `Update` publishes one `SourceUpdate` with the new `WindowsSnapshot` (entries grouped by pid, order within a pid as received, which is topmost first), `header.validity = Valid`.
  - Cancellation (shutdown): call `unloadScript("tasklens-bridge")` with a 500 ms timeout and delete the script file before returning `Outcome::Ok(())` (PROC-052 "On exit tasklens calls unloadScript").
  - KWin restart (`NameOwnerChanged` for `org.kde.KWin` to a new owner): reload the script as above. Owner gone: publish `Unsupported` until it returns.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs`: add `mod dbus_kwin;` (chain edit, the only change to that file).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=GNOME` **When** the worker starts **Then** it publishes `WindowsSnapshot` with validity `Unsupported` and makes no KWin calls.
- **Given** an `Update` whose sender is not the owner of `org.kde.KWin` **When** received **Then** it is rejected and nothing is published.
- **Given** an `Update` of 1 MiB + 1 byte **When** received **Then** rejected.
- **Given** an entry with `internalId` `"x"); evil("` **When** parsed **Then** that entry is dropped and the others are kept.
- **Given** a caption containing U+202E and a newline **When** parsed **Then** the stored caption has no U+202E and the newline is U+FFFD.
- **Given** two windows with pid 42 **When** published **Then** both are under pid 42 in received order.
- **Given** the substituted bridge script **When** checked **Then** no `__TL_` remains and the unique name appears once.
- **Given** the owner machine on Plasma 6.7.5 **When** tasklens runs and a new window opens **Then** it appears in `Snapshot.windows` within 1 s (manual check, record in the commit message, together with any KWin API name that differed).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_kwin.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs`: one `mod` line.

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `dbus_kwin.rs`:
- `unsupported_without_kde` (environment value passed as a parameter).
- `update_rejected_wrong_sender`, `update_rejected_oversize` (handler logic as a pure function taking sender, owner and payload).
- `update_drops_bad_internal_id` (security regression: injection-shaped id).
- `update_sanitizes_caption` (security regression: bidi and control characters).
- `update_groups_by_pid`.
- `bridge_script_placeholder_replaced`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: bus failures after a successful start return `Err(WorkerError::Bus)` so the supervisor restarts the generation; KWin absent is `Unsupported`, not an error.
- Validity: `Valid` or `Unsupported` on the component header.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: no polling; one parse and one publish per KWin event.
- Privacy: window captions are never logged.
- Security: only KWin's connection may call `Update`; window text is sanitized; the bus name is inserted as a JSON string.

## Notes
- Depends on E14-016 (script), E07-A3 (`write_atomic`), E08-A1, E08-A2. Uses `serde_json` (open item 3) and tl-collect `sanitize` (E05-A1, open item 4).
- tl-app owns the well-known name `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens` on its own blocking connection (ADR-010 single instance), so KWin cannot reach the engine through that name; open item 5 asks the leader to confirm the unique-name approach used here.
- The WindowsSnapshot field names come from tl-model (E03-A2).
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...` (for example `... cargo test -p tl-engine`).
- Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead.
- asupersync rules (ADR-004, docs/research/claude-asupersync-apis.md): every zbus call and every signal-stream `next()` is wrapped in `time::timeout` (2 s for reads) followed by `cx.checkpoint()`; blocking work only through `Cx::spawn_blocking` joined with `TaskHandle::join`; never `race!`, `select!`, `asupersync::process`, `asupersync::fs`, `asupersync::signal`, `GenServer`, `ChildSpec::depends_on`. Proxies never outlive their worker generation.

title: E14-016 KWin bridge script kwin-bridge.js
description:
## Context
The KWin script that feeds the KWin bridge (PROC-052, R-046): it runs inside KWin as plugin `tasklens-bridge` and calls tasklens's `WindowBridge.Update(s json)` with the full window list. The file is embedded into tl-engine with `include_str!` and written to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/tasklens/kwin-bridge.js` at run time by E14-A2 (R-138 item 12). Sources: PROC-052, ADR-004 (KWin bridge worker), canonical table (c), R-046, R-086, PERF-083, U-13.

## Deliverable
`assets/kwin/kwin-bridge.js` (new), KWin 6 JavaScript:
- Placeholder `__TL_BUS_NAME__` (a JSON string literal, quotes included, replaced by E14-A2 with the engine connection's bus name; open item 5 of the B4 plan).
- Constants: path `/io/github/oysteinkrog/Tasklens/WindowBridge`, interface `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.WindowBridge`, method `Update`.
- `entry(w)` returns an object with exactly these keys: `internalId` (`w.internalId.toString()`, a braced UUID), `pid` (integer), `caption` (string), `resourceClass` (string), `desktopFileName` (string), `minimized` (bool), `maximized` (bool), `keepAbove` (bool), `frameGeometry` (`{ x, y, width, height }` integers), `windowType` (integer, KWin's window type value).
- `send()` calls `callDBus(<bus name>, <path>, <interface>, "Update", JSON.stringify(list))` where `list` is every window of `workspace.stackingOrder`, topmost first (reverse of KWin's bottom-to-top order), mapped with `entry`.
- Sends the full list once at start, then on `workspace.windowAdded` (also hooks the new window), `workspace.windowRemoved`, `workspace.windowActivated` and each window's `captionChanged` (PROC-052). It also sends on each window's `minimizedChanged`, `maximizedChanged` (or the KWin 6.7.5 equivalent), `keepAboveChanged` and `interactiveMoveResizeFinished`, so state and geometry in the snapshot stay current (PERF-083 reads window moves back from the snapshot); see open item 6 of the B4 plan.
- No other D-Bus calls and no timers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the script text **When** E14-A2's unit test substitutes the bus name **Then** the result contains no `__TL_` placeholder and the bus name appears exactly once as a JSON string.
- **Given** KWin 6.7.5 on the owner machine **When** the script is loaded by E14-A2 **Then** `Update` is called once at load and again within 1 s of opening a new window (manual check recorded in the E14-A2 commit message).

## Files
- `assets/kwin/kwin-bridge.js`: create.

## Tests
- Covered by `dbus_kwin::tests::bridge_script_placeholder_replaced` in E14-A2 (text check) and the manual load check recorded there.
- Lint: `node --check assets/kwin/kwin-bridge.js` passes if `node` is installed; otherwise state in the commit message that it was not run.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A in the script; KWin logs script errors to its journal.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one D-Bus call per window event; geometry is sent only when a move or resize finishes, never per pixel.
- Privacy: window captions are sent only to tasklens's own connection.

## Notes

- No build step; this bead touches no Rust.
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first.

title: E14-017 KWin one-shot scripts cmd-template.js and pick.js
description:
## Context
The two one-shot KWin script templates used by the KWin bridge worker: `cmd-template.js` for window commands (activate, close, keep above, set geometry) and `pick.js` for the window picker's pid lookup. Commands must be one-shot scripts because KWin scripts cannot receive D-Bus signals (U-13). Sources: PROC-052, PROC-054, PROC-055, PROC-056, APP-009, PERF-083, canonical table (c), R-138 item 12.

## Deliverable
- `assets/kwin/cmd-template.js` (new):
  - Placeholder `__TL_ARGS__`, replaced by E14-018 with a JSON object literal `{ "plugin": "tasklens-cmd-<n>", "id": "<internalId>", "op": "activate" | "close" | "keep_above" | "geometry", "on": <bool>, "x": <int>, "y": <int>, "width": <int>, "height": <int> }`.
  - Finds the window with `workspace.windowList().find(w => w.internalId.toString() === args.id)`.
  - `activate`: `w.minimized = false; workspace.activeWindow = w;` (PROC-054). `close`: `w.closeWindow()`. `keep_above`: `w.keepAbove = args.on`. `geometry`: `w.frameGeometry = { x: args.x, y: args.y, width: args.width, height: args.height }`.
  - Missing window: does nothing.
  - Last statement unloads itself: `callDBus("org.kde.KWin", "/Scripting", "org.kde.kwin.Scripting", "unloadScript", args.plugin)`.
- `assets/kwin/pick.js` (new):
  - Placeholders `__TL_BUS_NAME__` (as in `kwin-bridge.js`) and `__TL_ARGS__` = `{ "plugin": "tasklens-pick", "uuid": "<uuid>" }`.
  - Finds the window by `internalId.toString() === args.uuid` and calls back tasklens with its pid (`0` when not found) through the WindowBridge method named in open item 7 of the B4 plan, then unloads itself like the command template.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** each template **When** E14-018 and E14-019 substitute their placeholders **Then** no `__TL_` text remains.
- **Given** `op = "activate"` on the owner machine **When** the command runs **Then** a minimized window is restored and focused (manual check recorded in E14-018).

title: E14-018 KWin worker: window commands as one-shot scripts
description:
## Context
Window commands for the KWin bridge worker: `Command::KWin(KWinCommand)` activate, close, keep above and set geometry, each run as a one-shot KWin script `tasklens-cmd-<n>` built from `assets/kwin/cmd-template.js`. Used by Show Window (PROC-054), the Name-cell window list (PROC-053), the pin on tasklens windows (PROC-056, APP-009) and detached graph and mini window placement (PERF-083, PERF-093). Sources: PROC-052, PROC-053, PROC-054, PROC-056, APP-009, PERF-083, ADR-005 (`Command::KWin`), U-13.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_kwin.rs`:
- Handle every non-pick `KWinCommand` variant defined in tl-model (E03-A2): activate a window, close a window, set keep-above on or off, set frame geometry. Each names its window by KWin `internalId`. A command whose id is not a braced lowercase UUID, or is not in the current window list, is dropped and logged at debug.
- Per command: `n` = a per-worker `u64` counter starting at 1. Build the args object with `serde_json` (`{ "plugin": "tasklens-cmd-<n>", "id": .., "op": "activate" | "close" | "keep_above" | "geometry", "on": .., "x": .., "y": .., "width": .., "height": .. }`), replace `__TL_ARGS__` in `include_str!` of `assets/kwin/cmd-template.js`, write it to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/tasklens/tasklens-cmd-<n>.js` (0600), call `loadScript(path, "tasklens-cmd-<n>")` and `start()` with a 2 s timeout each, then delete the file. Geometry values are clamped to `i32` and width and height to at least 1.
- Commands run one at a time in arrival order. While the bridge is `Unsupported`, commands are dropped.
- The UI decides "No window found" and "Process window shown." from `Snapshot.windows` before sending (PROC-054); this worker sends no result events.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** activate for a known id **When** handled **Then** the written script contains `"op":"activate"` and that id as a JSON string, and the file is deleted afterwards.
- **Given** an id `{0000…}"); workspace.windowList().forEach(w=>w.closeWindow()); ("` **When** handled **Then** the command is dropped and no script is written (security regression).
- **Given** an id not in the current window list **When** handled **Then** dropped.
- **Given** three commands **When** handled **Then** plugin names `tasklens-cmd-1`, `-2`, `-3` in order.
- **Given** the owner machine **When** activate is sent for a minimized window **Then** it is restored and focused; keep-above on a tasklens window keeps it above others (manual check, recorded in the commit message).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_kwin.rs`: change.

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `dbus_kwin.rs` (script building is a pure function): `cmd_script_activate_args`, `cmd_rejects_injection_id`, `cmd_unknown_id_dropped`, `cmd_plugin_counter_increments`, `cmd_geometry_clamped`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: a load or start timeout drops that command and logs at debug.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one script load per command.
- Privacy: N/A.

title: E14-A3 Startup and connections workers, launcher, opener
description:
## Context
Anchor E14-A3. The shared launcher `crates/tl-engine/src/launcher.rs` (R-134): runs `ActionKind::Launch(LaunchSpec)` for the Run dialog (PROC-095) and Startup "Run now" (SYS-023). Programs start detached in a new transient user scope so they group as apps. E11 admits the action, applies the deadline and reports events; this bead writes the launch functions. The Startup worker (E14-011 to E14-013) and the Connections worker (E14-014) are separate E14 beads. Sources: R-134, ADR-005 (`LaunchSpec`, `LaunchWhat`), ADR-006 (deadlines, Run as administrator), PROC-095, SYS-023, R-117, canonical table (c) (scope names).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/launcher.rs` (new), `pub(crate)`:
- `enum LaunchOutcome { Launched, AlreadyRunning }`.
- `async fn launch(cx: &Cx, session: Option<Arc<zbus::Connection>>, spec: &LaunchSpec) -> Result<LaunchOutcome, ActionError>`. Working directory: `spec.cwd`, else `$HOME`.
- `LaunchWhat::Command(text)` (Run dialog, PROC-095):
  1. Text containing NUL or any C0 control character other than tab: `Err` (the UI shows "Command contains invalid text.").
  2. Trimmed text matching `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:` (a URI scheme): `opener::open_uri` (E14-020).
  3. Trimmed text that is an existing path (absolute, or starting with `~/` expanded to `$HOME`) and is a directory or not executable by the current user (`access(X_OK)` fails): `opener::open_uri` with that path.
  4. Text matching `^kcm_[A-Za-z0-9_]+$`: argv `["systemsettings", <text>]`.
  5. Anything else: argv `["/bin/sh", "-c", <text>]`.
  Spawn detached with the tl-ops launch helper (E07-A3: `posix_spawn`, `setsid`, stdio `/dev/null`, the cwd above), then create the scope `app-tasklens-run-<rand>.scope` (below).
- `as_admin = true` with `Command(text)`: argv from the tl-ops administrator form `pkexec env DISPLAY=<$DISPLAY> WAYLAND_DISPLAY=<$WAYLAND_DISPLAY> XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=<$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR> /bin/sh -c <text>` (only variables that are set are passed), under `org.freedesktop.policykit.exec`, never tl-helper (ADR-006). No transient scope. Exit status handling follows open item 11 of the B4 plan: 126 = dismissed prompt ("Authentication cancelled"), 127 = not authorized (R-117).
- `LaunchWhat::DesktopEntry(id)` (Startup Run now, SYS-023):
  1. Generated unit `app-<escaped id>@autostart.service` (escape with the tl-collect systemd-escape function, E06-A2) on the user manager: if it is loaded or loadable (`LoadUnit` gives `LoadState` not `not-found`): when its `ActiveState` is `active`, return `AlreadyRunning`; else `StartUnit(name, "replace")`, adding the `JobRemoved` match before the call, and wait for `JobRemoved` of the returned job path up to 30 s: `done` gives `Launched`, any other result gives `ActionError::UnitJob(result)`.
  2. Otherwise find `<id>.desktop` in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autostart`, then each `$XDG_CONFIG_DIRS` entry plus `/autostart` (same precedence as SYS-019), parse it with the E06-A2 desktop entry parser, build argv from `Exec` with the tl-ops Exec parser (E07-A3: field codes `%f %F %u %U` removed, `%i %c %k` expanded, quoting rules), cwd from `Path=` if set, spawn as above, then create the scope `app-tasklens-<escaped id>-<rand>.scope` with `Description` = the entry's `Name`.
- `LaunchWhat::Unit(unit)`: `StartUnit(name, "replace")` on that unit's manager with the `JobRemoved` wait above (30 s).
- Transient scope (SYS-023, PROC-095): `StartTransientUnit(name, "fail", [("PIDs", au [pid]), ("Description", s <text or Name>), ("CollectMode", s "inactive-or-failed")], [])` on the user manager. Failure (or no session connection) is logged at warning and is not an error; the program still runs.
- `<rand>`: 8 lowercase hex digits from 4 bytes read from `/dev/urandom` (open item 12).
- All `zbus` calls use 2 s timeouts except the 30 s `JobRemoved` wait; `pkexec` waits are bounded by the 120 s deadline E11 applies (R-134).
- `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs`: add `mod launcher;` (chain edit, the only change to that file).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** text `"echo\u{0}x"` **When** launched **Then** `Err` and nothing is spawned (security regression).
- **Given** `https://example.org` **When** launched **Then** `open_uri` is called and nothing else is spawned.
- **Given** an existing non-executable file `/tmp/x.txt` **When** launched **Then** `open_uri("/tmp/x.txt")`.
- **Given** `kcm_kwin_effects` **When** launched **Then** argv is `["systemsettings", "kcm_kwin_effects"]`.
- **Given** `firefox --new-window` **When** launched **Then** argv is `["/bin/sh", "-c", "firefox --new-window"]` and a scope named `app-tasklens-run-<8 hex>.scope` is requested with that pid.

- **Given** a desktop entry without a generated unit and `Exec=foo %U --bar` **When** launched **Then** argv `["foo", "--bar"]` and scope `app-tasklens-<escaped id>-<8 hex>.scope` with Description = Name.
- **Given** `StartTransientUnit` fails **When** launching a command **Then** the result is still `Launched`.

title: E14-A4 Journal
description:
## Context
Anchor E14-A4. The `Journal` worker: one `journalctl` child per open `JournalHandle`, used by the Service Properties Logs tab. This bead delivers the initial fetch (last 200 entries of the current boot), JSON parsing, the access check, the error events and the hookup of `EngineClient::journal`. Follow mode and Load older are E14-009. Sources: ADR-005 (`EngineClient::journal`, `JournalQuery`, `JournalHandle`, `JournalEvent`, `JournalEntry`, `JournalAccess`, `JournalError`), ADR-016 row "Service logs", SYS-015, R-074, R-118, UI-SYS-036, UI-SYS-038.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/journal.rs` (new):
  - `pub(crate) fn open(rt: &RuntimeHandle, query: JournalQuery) -> JournalHandle`: creates the event channel `async_channel::bounded::<JournalEvent>(64)` and the control channel of the tl-model `JournalHandle`, spawns one task with `spawn_checked` that owns the session, and returns the handle.
  - Command line, run with `std::process::Command` inside `cx.spawn_blocking` (never `asupersync::process`):
    - system unit: `journalctl -u <id> -b -n 200 -o json --no-pager`
    - user unit: `journalctl --user-unit <id> -b -n 200 -o json --no-pager`
    The unit id is passed as one argument (no shell). stdin `/dev/null`, stdout and stderr piped.
  - 5 s timeout on this fetch: the blocking closure polls the stdout and stderr fds with `rustix::event::poll` against a deadline of 5 s from spawn; past it, kill the child, `wait()` it and report `JournalError::Timeout`.
  - Parsing, one JSON object per line (`serde_json`): `__REALTIME_TIMESTAMP` (decimal string, µs) to `realtime_us`; `PRIORITY` (decimal string "0" to "7") to `priority`, missing or invalid gives 6; `MESSAGE` as a string, or as an array of bytes decoded with `String::from_utf8_lossy`, missing gives an empty message; `_PID` (decimal string) to `pid`; `__CURSOR` to `cursor`. A line that is not valid JSON or lacks `__CURSOR` is skipped and counted; the count is logged at debug.
  - Events, in order: first `Access(..)`, then one `Batch { entries, older: false, exhausted: entries.len() < 200 }`, or one `Error(..)` instead of the batch.
  - Access (SYS-015): for a system unit, `All` when the effective uid is 0 or the process is a member of group `wheel`, `adm` or `systemd-journal` (gids from `/etc/group`, membership from `getgroups()` plus the primary gid); otherwise `OwnOnly`. For a user unit, always `All` (see open item 9).
  - Errors: spawn fails with `NotFound` gives `JournalError::NotFound`; timeout gives `Timeout`; non-zero exit gives `Exit { code, stderr_first_line }` with the first stderr line, at most 200 characters.
  - The task keeps the last cursor and the oldest cursor for E14-009.
  - When the handle's event receiver is dropped (`Sender::is_closed()`), the task kills any running child, waits for it, and ends.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs`: add `mod journal;` (chain edit, the only change to that file).
- `crates/tl-engine/src/bridge.rs`: `EngineClient::journal` calls `crate::workers::journal::open(&self.runtime_handle, query)` (one-line chain edit in an E09-owned file; open item 2 of the B4 plan asks the leader to allow it).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fixture with 3 valid JSON lines and 1 broken line **When** parsed **Then** 3 entries with the right `realtime_us`, `priority`, `pid`, `message`, `cursor`, and the broken line is skipped.
- **Given** a `MESSAGE` that is a byte array `[104,105]` **When** parsed **Then** the message is "hi".

title: E14-001 systemd worker: connect, list units, unit records
description:
## Context
First bead of the systemd workers `SourceId::SystemdSystem` and `SourceId::SystemdUser` (ADR-004 worker table), both in `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_systemd.rs`. This bead connects to one manager, lists every unit, reads its properties and publishes the unit records that feed `ServicesSnapshot` (ADR-003). Signals, cgroup data, unit details and the table projection follow in E14-002, E14-003, E14-004 and E14-A1. Sources: SYS-001, SYS-002, SYS-003, ADR-004 (D-Bus workers), ADR-016 (Services row), UI-SYS-014, UI-SYS-015, R-117.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_systemd.rs` (new):
  - `pub(crate) fn factory(manager: Manager, io: WorkerIo, conn_slot: ManagerConnSlot) -> impl ManagedChildFactory<WorkerError>`: one worker body for both managers. `Manager::System` uses the system bus, `Manager::User` the session bus. `SourceId` is `SystemdSystem` or `SystemdUser`.
  - `pub(crate) struct ManagerConnSlot(Arc<arc_swap::ArcSwapOption<zbus::Connection>>)` with `new()`, `set(conn)`, `clear()`, `get() -> Option<Arc<zbus::Connection>>`. The worker sets it after a successful connect and clears it when the generation ends. E11 unit actions read it to call the manager on the same connection (ADR-006, R-092). It is `Clone`.
  - Connection: built with the E08-A2 helper in `crates/tl-engine/src/dbus/mod.rs` (`.internal_executor(false)`, executor tick task, 2 s read timeouts).
  - Listing on connect: `org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager.ListUnitsByPatterns([], [])` (loaded units) and `ListUnitFilesByPatterns([], [])` (installed files). For every unit file not in the loaded list, call `LoadUnit(name)` to get its object path. For every unit: `org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.GetAll("org.freedesktop.systemd1.Unit")`, plus `GetAll` of the type interface: `.Service` for `.service`, `.Socket` for `.socket`, `.Mount` for `.mount`, `.Timer` for `.timer`.
  - Always hidden (never published): `LoadState == "not-found"` with no unit file; uninstantiated templates (id contains `@.` such as `foo@.service`); `.device` units (SYS-002).
  - Per unit record (fields of the tl-model unit record in `snapshot.rs`, E03-A2): `unit: UnitRef { manager, name }`, `description` (`Description`), `status`, `startup`, `main_pid` (`MainPID`, services only, else 0), `user`, `path`, `kind` (from the id suffix: service, socket, timer, mount, automount, path, target, swap, slice, scope), `sub_state` (raw `SubState`), `load_state` (raw `LoadState`), `active_since` (`ActiveEnterTimestamp`, µs realtime, 0 = none), `unit_file` (`FragmentPath`), `triggered_by` (`TriggeredBy`, `as`), `control_group` (`ControlGroup`), `can_reload` (`CanReload`).
  - Status mapping (SYS-003): `active` + sub `running` = Running; other `active` = Active; `activating` = Starting; `deactivating` = Stopping; `reloading` or `refreshing` = Reloading; `inactive` = Stopped; `failed` = Failed; `maintenance` = Maintenance.
  - Startup type from `UnitFileState`: `enabled` Enabled; `enabled-runtime` Enabled (runtime); `disabled` Disabled; `static` Static; `indirect` Indirect; `masked` and `masked-runtime` Masked; `generated` Generated; `transient` Transient; `alias` Alias; `linked` and `linked-runtime` Linked; empty or any other value "-" (no unit file).
  - User (SYS-003): real uid of `MainPID` from `/proc/<pid>/status` `Uid:` (first field) mapped to a name with the tl-collect uid-to-name lookup used for `ProcessMeta.user` (E05-A1); else the `User=` property; else "root" for the system manager or the current user's name for the user manager.
  - Path (SYS-003): services `ExecStart[0].path` (first element of `a(sasbttttuii)`); sockets the address of the first `Listen` entry (`a(ss)`, second string); mounts `What`; timers `Unit`; every other kind empty.
  - Manager state: `Connected` after a successful listing. If the bus cannot be opened or `org.freedesktop.systemd1` is not on it: publish the manager as `Unavailable` with an empty unit list, then wait for `RefreshNow(<this SourceId>)` or 60 s and try again. This is an expected condition, not a worker failure (ADR-004).
  - Publishes one `SourceUpdate` per completed listing carrying `(Manager, ManagerState, Arc<[unit record]>)`.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: E14-002 systemd worker: signals, resync schedule, reconnect
description:
## Context
Second bead of `workers/dbus_systemd.rs`. It makes the Services data live without polling: subscribe to the manager, apply unit signals, resync on schedule and handle a dropped bus. Sources: SYS-005, ADR-004 (D-Bus workers, full resync on reconnect), ADR-008 schedule row "systemd units", UI-SYS-014 (Reconnecting state).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_systemd.rs`:
- After the first listing call `Manager.Subscribe()` and add match rules for these signals on `/org/freedesktop/systemd1` and the unit objects (`path_namespace=/org/freedesktop/systemd1/unit`): `UnitNew(s id, o path)`, `UnitRemoved(s id, o path)`, `JobNew(u, o, s)`, `JobRemoved(u id, o job, s unit, s result)`, `UnitFilesChanged()`, `Reloading(b active)`, and `org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.PropertiesChanged(s iface, a{sv} changed, as invalidated)`.
- Signal handling:
  - `UnitNew`: `GetAll` that unit (and its type interface) and add or replace its record, unless it is in the always-hidden set (E14-001).
  - `UnitRemoved`: if the unit has a unit file in the last `ListUnitFilesByPatterns` result, keep the record with `ActiveState=inactive`, `SubState=dead`; otherwise remove it.
  - `PropertiesChanged` on a unit object: update the changed fields among `ActiveState`, `SubState`, `LoadState`, `UnitFileState`, `Description`, `ActiveEnterTimestamp`, `FragmentPath`, `TriggeredBy`, `ControlGroup`, `CanReload`, `MainPID`, `User`, `ExecStart`, `Listen`, `What`, `Unit`; any name in `invalidated` triggers one `GetAll` for that unit.
  - `UnitFilesChanged`: re-run `ListUnitFilesByPatterns([], [])` and update `startup` of every record.
  - `Reloading(false)`: full resync (the E14-001 listing).
  - `JobNew` and `JobRemoved`: no state change in this worker (E11 tracks its own jobs on the same connection, ADR-006).
- Publishing: after each batch of signals drained from the stream without waiting, publish one `SourceUpdate` with the full record list (records are `Arc`-shared; unchanged records keep their `Arc`).
- Schedule (ADR-008): full resync on every connect, and every 60 s while `Demand.services` is true; no resync while it is false (signals still applied). `RefreshNow(SystemdSystem | SystemdUser)` triggers an immediate full resync (SYS-016).
- Dropped bus (stream ends, or a call times out after a successful connect): publish the manager as `Reconnecting` with the last records unchanged, then return `Err(WorkerError::Bus)` so the supervisor restarts the generation (backoff 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 30 s). The new generation does a full listing and publishes `Connected`.
- The signal loop awaits the stream with `time::timeout(.., 500 ms)` and calls `cx.checkpoint()` after every wake so cancellation stops the worker within 500 ms.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a record list and a `PropertiesChanged` with `ActiveState=inactive`, `SubState=dead` **When** applied **Then** that unit's status is Stopped and every other record keeps the same `Arc`.
- **Given** `UnitRemoved` for a unit with a unit file **When** applied **Then** the record stays with status Stopped.
- **Given** `UnitRemoved` for a transient scope without a unit file **When** applied **Then** the record is gone.
- **Given** `invalidated = ["SubState"]` **When** applied **Then** exactly one `GetAll` is requested for that unit.
- **Given** `Demand.services = false` for 180 virtual seconds **When** the schedule runs **Then** no resync happens.
- **Given** `Demand.services = true` **When** 60 virtual seconds pass **Then** exactly one resync happens.
- **Given** the signal stream ends **When** the worker sees it **Then** it publishes `Reconnecting` and returns `Err`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_systemd.rs`: change.

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `dbus_systemd.rs`:
- `apply_properties_changed_keeps_other_arcs`: pure state model, Arc pointer equality for untouched records.
- `unit_removed_with_and_without_file`.
- `invalidated_requests_getall`: the state model returns the list of units to fetch.
- `resync_schedule_follows_demand`: LabRuntime (`LabConfig::new(42).max_steps(1_000_000)`, `run_with_auto_advance`) with the resync timer and a demand `watch`; counts resync requests over 180 virtual seconds for demand off and on; ends with `run_until_quiescent_with_report().lab_test_passed()`.
Keep the signal-application logic in a pure `ServicesState` struct so these tests need no bus.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: bus drop gives `ManagerState::Reconnecting` then a supervised restart; no toast from this worker.
- Validity: records during `Reconnecting` are the last good data; the UI draws them as stale (UI-SYS-014).
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: no polling; one `GetAll` per new or invalidated unit; one publish per signal batch.
- Privacy: N/A.

title: E14-003 systemd worker: unit cgroup pids and resource stats
description:
## Context
Third bead of `workers/dbus_systemd.rs`: the processes inside each unit's cgroup (child rows, UI-SYS-016) and the unit resource columns CPU, Memory, Disk and Tasks (SYS-003, UI-SYS-013). Sources: SYS-001 (child processes from `ControlGroup`), SYS-003 (resource columns at 1 Hz only while visible), ADR-008 rows "Unit cgroup stats", ADR-016 row "App and unit cgroup stats" (R-137), UI-SYS-016 (`cgroup_pids`, `has_cgroup_procs`).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_systemd.rs`:
- `has_cgroup_procs`: for every unit with a non-empty `ControlGroup`, read `/sys/fs/cgroup<ControlGroup>/cgroup.procs` and its descendants' `cgroup.procs` (recursive walk) on each listing and resync; true when any pid is found. Opened with `openat` from a dirfd on `/sys/fs/cgroup`, closed in the same pass (R-137).
- `cgroup_pids: Arc<[ProcessKey]>`: while `Demand.services` and `Demand.process_table` are both true (the Services page sets `process_table` while a unit row is expanded, UI-SYS-016), at 1 Hz, for every unit with `has_cgroup_procs`: the pids from the recursive walk, flat, each turned into a `ProcessKey` with `start_ticks` from `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 (tl-collect `proc/pid_stat.rs`, E05-A1) and the current `BootId`. A pid whose stat cannot be read is skipped. Otherwise `cgroup_pids` keeps its last value and is not refreshed.
- Resource fields, only while `Demand.service_cgroup_stats` is true, at 1 Hz, per unit with a cgroup:
  - `cpu_pct`: Δ`cpu.stat usage_usec` / Δt / online CPUs × 100 (whole-machine percent, same scale as the process `cpu` column).
  - `memory_bytes`: `memory.stat` `anon` (R-137, ADR-008 memory math: app and unit rows use cgroup `anon`).
  - `disk_bps`: Δ(`io.stat` `rbytes` + `wbytes`, summed over devices) / Δt.
  - `tasks`: `pids.current`.
  - Rates use actual elapsed time; the first sample after a cgroup appears, a counter reset or a rate change is `WarmingUp` (ADR-008 counter rules). A unit without a cgroup has `Validity::Missing` for these fields (the UI shows "-", never 0). `EACCES`/`EPERM` gives `Restricted`.
  - Use the cgroup stat readers in tl-collect that E05-A2 adds for app scopes (`memory.stat`, `cpu.stat`, `io.stat`, `pids.current`); do not write a second parser.
- The 1 Hz timer runs only while one of the two demands above is true; otherwise no cgroup reads happen.
- All cgroup and `/proc` reads for one tick run inside one `cx.spawn_blocking` job.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fixture cgroup tree with pids in a nested child cgroup **When** the walk runs **Then** `has_cgroup_procs` is true and the nested pids are listed flat.
- **Given** `Demand.service_cgroup_stats = false` **When** 60 virtual seconds pass **Then** zero cgroup stat reads happen.
- **Given** `Demand.services = true` and `Demand.process_table = false` **When** 10 virtual seconds pass **Then** no `/proc/<pid>/stat` reads happen and `cgroup_pids` is unchanged.
- **Given** both demands true and a unit cgroup with pids 100 and 200 **When** one tick runs **Then** `cgroup_pids` holds two keys whose `start_ticks` match the fixture stat files.
- **Given** two stat samples 1 s apart with `usage_usec` +500 000 on 8 online CPUs **When** the rate is computed **Then** `cpu_pct` is 6.25.
- **Given** `usage_usec` going backwards **When** sampled **Then** the field is `WarmingUp` with no rate.
- **Given** a unit with an empty `ControlGroup` **When** stats are computed **Then** its resource fields are `Missing`.
- **Given** an unreadable `memory.stat` (EACCES) **When** sampled **Then** `memory_bytes` is `Restricted`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_systemd.rs`: change.

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `dbus_systemd.rs`, using a temp-dir cgroup tree (`tempfile`):
- `cgroup_walk_nested_pids`.
- `cgroup_stats_cpu_rate`, `cgroup_stats_reset_warming_up`, `cgroup_stats_missing_without_cgroup`, `cgroup_stats_restricted_on_eacces` (the EACCES case through a reader that returns the error, not by chmod).
- `cgroup_pids_follow_process_table_demand`: LabRuntime, both demand cases above.
- `cgroup_stats_off_without_demand`: LabRuntime, 60 virtual seconds, read counter stays 0.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: per-field `Validity`, never a worker failure.
- Validity: `WarmingUp`, `Valid`, `Missing`, `Restricted` as above.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: at most one blocking job per second; reads only while demanded (ADR-008).
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes

- The walk and the stat reads take their roots (`/sys/fs/cgroup`, `/proc`) as parameters, so tests point them at a temp dir.
- SYS-003 names `memory.current` for the Memory column; R-137 and ADR-008 (later, higher precedence) use `memory.stat` `anon` for unit rows. Use `anon`.

title: E14-004 systemd worker: UnitDetails for Service Properties
description:
## Context
Fourth bead of `workers/dbus_systemd.rs`: the data behind the Service Properties window (General, Log On, Recovery and Dependencies tabs) for the units the UI has open. Sources: SYS-011, SYS-012, SYS-013 (P2 view), SYS-014, ADR-003 (`ServicesSnapshot.details`, `UnitDetails`), ADR-008 row "Unit details", Demand field `unit_details` (max 10), UI-SYS-031 to UI-SYS-035.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_systemd.rs`:
- For each `UnitRef` in `Demand.unit_details` whose manager is this worker's: `GetAll` on `org.freedesktop.systemd1.Unit` and `.Service` once when it enters demand, then keep it current from `PropertiesChanged` (E14-002). Drop a unit's details when it leaves demand. At most 10 units (the demand cap); ignore extras beyond 10.
- `UnitDetails` fields (tl-model type, E03-A2):
  - General (SYS-011): `id` (`Id`), `description`, `documentation` (`Documentation`, `as`), `exec_start_argv` (argv of `ExecStart[0]`, `as`; the UI joins and shell-quotes), `fragment_path`, `drop_in_paths` (`DropInPaths`), `startup` (as E14-001), `active_state`, `sub_state`, `active_enter_us` (`ActiveEnterTimestamp`), `main_pid`, `memory_current` (`MemoryCurrent`; `u64::MAX` means not available and maps to `Validity::Unsupported`), `tasks_current` (`TasksCurrent`, same rule), `cpu_usage_ns` (`CPUUsageNSec`, same rule), `manager`.
  - Log On (SYS-012): `user` (`User`), `group` (`Group`), `dynamic_user` (`DynamicUser`), `supplementary_groups` (`SupplementaryGroups`), `pam_name` (`PAMName`), `runs_as` (real `Uid` and `Gid` of `MainPID` from `/proc/<pid>/status`, `None` when MainPID is 0 or unreadable), `graphical_session` (true when `PartOf` or `BindsTo` contains `graphical-session.target`).
  - Recovery (SYS-013, view): `recovery: RecoverySettings { restart (Restart), restart_usec (RestartUSec), restart_steps (RestartSteps), restart_max_delay_usec (RestartMaxDelayUSec), start_limit_burst (StartLimitBurst), start_limit_interval_usec (StartLimitIntervalUSec), start_limit_action (StartLimitAction), failure_action (FailureAction), on_failure (OnFailure, as), n_restarts (NRestarts) }`, and `recovery_dropin_exists`: whether the file exists, checked with `stat`: system units `/etc/systemd/system/<unit>.d/50-tasklens-recovery.conf`, user units `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user/<unit>.d/50-tasklens-recovery.conf` (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` defaults to `~/.config`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `Demand.unit_details = [sshd.service (System)]` **When** the system worker runs **Then** details for `sshd.service` are published and the user worker publishes none.

title: E05-A1 Process sweep
description:
## Context
Anchor E05-A1 "Process sweep". It closes the process-sweep set: `ProcessSampler::sweep` turns one pass over `/proc` into `ProcessRecord`s sorted by `ProcessKey`, each with its `Arc<ProcessMeta>`, `GroupKey`, flags and `FieldValidity`, plus the app cgroup samples and the per-process values of the P1 extra columns. The engine's `Processes` worker (E10-A1) runs it in one `spawn_blocking` job per `processes.interval_ms`. Sources: PROC-002, PROC-004 to PROC-008, PROC-027 to PROC-031, PROC-035, PROC-036, PROC-059 (flags), ADR-003 `ProcessRecord`, `ProcessMeta`, `ProcFlags`, ADR-008, ADR-015, ADR-016, R-005, R-008, R-043, R-064, R-103, R-137.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/sweep.rs`:
- `sweep_core` gains a per-pid hook so metadata is read through the same dirfd before it closes: `pub fn sweep_core_with(&mut self, ctx: &SweepCtx, out: &mut Vec<SweptProc>, per_pid: &mut dyn FnMut(&SweptProc, BorrowedFd<'_>))`; `sweep_core` calls it with a no-op.
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)] pub struct ProcessExtras` (one per record, same index), the values of the P1 extra columns that `ProcessRecord` does not carry: `cpu_kernel_pct: f32`, `cpu_user_pct: f32`, `cpu_relative_pct: f32`, `utime_ticks: u64`, `stime_ticks: u64`, `start_boot_ns: u64` (`start_ticks × 1e9 / ticks_per_sec`), `ws_peak: Option<u64>` (VmHWM), `ws_shared: Option<u64>`, `commit: Option<u64>`, `vsize: Option<u64>`, `vsize_peak: Option<u64>`, `page_faults: u64`, `page_faults_delta: u64`, `policy: u32`, `rt_priority: u32`, `affinity: Arc<str>` (`Cpus_allowed_list`, interned), `fd_count: Option<FdCount>`, `disk_read_bps: f32`, `disk_write_raw_bps: f32`, `image_name: Option<Arc<str>>`, `image_path: ExeLink`, `unit: Option<Arc<str>>`, `class: ProcClass`, `state_letter: u8`, `frozen: bool`, `is_app_primary: bool`. How these reach `tl-model` is an E05 open item; this bead only produces them.
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct AppCgroupSample { pub group_key: GroupKey, pub rel: Arc<str>, pub cgroup_id: u64, pub app_name: Option<Arc<str>>, pub icon_app: Option<Arc<str>>, pub qualifier: Option<&'static str>, pub stats: CgroupStats, pub io_read_bps: f32, pub io_write_bps: f32, pub io_validity: Validity }`: one per app unit from the scan. `io_*_bps` are Δ`rbytes`/Δt and Δ`wbytes`/Δt from `io.stat` with the same ADR-008 rules as process rates (first sample `WarmingUp`), used when a member's Disk is Restricted (R-103).
- `#[derive(Default)] pub struct SweepOutput { pub observed_start: TimeNs, pub observed_end: TimeNs, pub records: Vec<ProcessRecord>, pub extras: Vec<ProcessExtras>, pub apps: Vec<AppCgroupSample>, pub coverage: Coverage }`.
- `pub struct SweepInputs<'a> { pub protect: &'a ProtectInputs, pub detail_keys: &'a [ProcessKey], pub want_pss: bool, pub window_pids: Option<&'a FxHashSet<u32>>, pub wm_class: Option<&'a FxHashMap<u32, Arc<str>>> }`.
- `pub struct ProcessSampler { core: SweepCore, meta: MetaCache, apps: AppResolver, cg: CgroupRoot, pss: PssReader, users: Box<dyn UserNames + Send>, interner: Interner, metas: FxHashMap<ProcessKey, Arc<ProcessMeta>>, app_prev: FxHashMap<u64 /*cgroup_id*/, (TimeNs, u64, u64)> }` with `pub fn new(root: SysRoot, paths: &AppPaths, users: Box<dyn UserNames + Send>) -> Result<Self, CollectError>` and
  `pub fn sweep(&mut self, ctx: &SweepCtx, inp: &SweepInputs<'_>, out: &mut SweepOutput)`:
  1. `apps.begin_sweep(&cg, ctx.self_uid, now)`;
  2. `sweep_core_with`; in the hook, `meta.get_or_refresh(key, dirfd, &stat.comm_raw, ..)`;
  3. per process: `apps.resolve(key, ..)` (E05-A2); `display_name` and `image_name` (E05-018); the user name from `users.name(ruid)`; `search_lower` from display name, image name, cmdline, user, description, app name, unit name (R-043);
  4. `ProcessMeta { comm, name, exe, cmdline, user, cgroup: Some(rel) or None, app_id, icon: icon_process, description, search_lower }`; `exe` is `Some(path)` only for `ExeLink::Path`. When none of the inputs changed since the last sweep (`MetaChange::Unchanged` and the same `Arc<AppInfo>`), the previous `Arc<ProcessMeta>` is reused (pointer equal), so the reducer and the UI see no change;
  5. `ProtectedSet` from this sweep's processes (E05-017), then `flags_for` per record;
  6. `ProcessRecord { key, ppid, uid: ruid, meta, group: group_key, state: map_state, flags, nice, threads: status.threads (or stat.num_threads), cpu_pct, rss_anon_bytes, rss_bytes, pss_bytes: 0, uss_bytes: 0, swap_bytes, io_read_bps, io_write_bps, net_rx_bps: 0.0, net_tx_bps: 0.0, gpu_util_pct: 0.0, gpu_mem_bytes: 0, validity }`; missing memory values are 0 with the validity from E05-010 step 6;
  7. app units: `CgroupRoot::read_stats` with `memory_stat`, `swap`, `cpu_stat`, `io_stat`, `pids`, `events` wanted (`memory_current` never, R-137) into `AppCgroupSample`; members of a unit whose `frozen == Some(true)` get `extras.frozen = true` (State column "Frozen", PROC-036);
  8. `is_app_primary` per record from the app pid set (PROC-008);
  9. when `inp.want_pss`, `PssReader::read` for `inp.detail_keys` and `apply_rollups`, filling `out.coverage`;
  10. sort `records` (and `extras` in the same order) by `ProcessKey`; `meta.retain_live`, `apps.end_sweep`, drop `metas` of dead keys.
- `pub fn reset_baselines(&mut self)`: core and app-io baselines.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the `owner-desktop` fixture (E04-A1) plus the `process-edge` fixture merged into one temp root **When** two sweeps run with `ticks_per_sec = 100`, `online_cpus = 32`, `self_uid = 1000` **Then** the insta snapshot of `(pid, name, user, group class, flags, state, threads, cpu validity, rss_anon)` per record matches, and records are sorted by `ProcessKey`.
- **Given** pid 4201 (firefox in its app scope) **When** swept **Then** its group is `App { app_id: "firefox" }`, `meta.name == "Firefox"` when it is the app primary, and `extras.class == App`.
- **Given** pid 57 (kernel thread) **When** swept **Then** `name == "[kworker/0:1]"`, flags contain `KERNEL_THREAD`, `RssAnon` validity is `Unsupported`.
- **Given** a process with `ruid` 0 **When** swept with `self_uid = 1000` **Then** flags contain `OTHER_USER` and its io validity is `Restricted` (fixture io mode 0000, non-root run).
- **Given** two sweeps without metadata changes **When** compared **Then** each record's `meta` is the same `Arc` (pointer equal).
- **Given** the firefox app unit with `frozen 1` in `cgroup.events` **When** swept **Then** its member processes have `extras.frozen == true`.
- **Given** a fixture process with cmdline `secret-token-123 --x` **When** a full sweep runs under a `tracing` subscriber at `trace` level that records every formatted event and span field **Then** no recorded text contains `secret-token-123` (ADR-015 verification, sweep part).
- **Given** `want_pss = true` and `detail_keys = [own test process]` on the real root **When** swept **Then** that record's PSS validity is `Valid` and coverage contains its key.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/sweep.rs`: change, add the sampler (large file).
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_process.rs`: add the integration tests.
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/process-edge/proc/4209/{stat,status,statm,io,comm,cmdline,cgroup}`: create (the `secret-token-123` process).

## Tests
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_full_snapshot`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_app_member_grouped`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_kernel_thread_record`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_other_user_flags_and_restricted`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_meta_arc_reused`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_frozen_app_members`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_never_logs_cmdline`: security regression; uses `tracing-subscriber` as a dev-dependency (workspace pin) with a capturing layer.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_pss_for_detail_keys`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: per-process problems become validity; `ProcessSampler::new` fails only when the cgroup root cannot be opened (`ProcRead { file: "cgroup" }`).
- Validity: as E05-010 step 6, plus `Pss`/`Uss` from E05-021; `Ungrouped` group for unreadable cgroups.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: part of the 15 ms per 2,000 processes gate (E05-023). No allocation per process in the steady state: reuse `out` vectors (`clear` keeps capacity), reuse `Arc<ProcessMeta>`, intern repeated strings.
- Privacy: no command line, environment, path or other user's name is logged; only `pid` and `comm` at `debug` or below.

## Notes
- Large file: commit `sweep.rs` before building or testing (CLAUDE.md large-file rule).
- The 24 px app icon lives in `AppCgroupSample.icon_app`; `ProcessMeta.icon` holds the 16 px icon (members inherit the app icon, PROC-006).
- `UserNames` real lookup is an E05 open item; until it is settled the engine passes `NumericUserNames`.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...` (for example `... cargo test -p tl-collect`). Run `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p tl-collect --all-targets -- -D warnings` the same way before committing.
- Commit with a pathspec of only this bead's files: `git commit -m "..." -- <files>` (run `git add` on new files first). Never switch branch, reset, rebase or amend.
- `tl-collect` has no async code and no runtime (ADR-001 rule 3). Allowed dependencies: tl-model, rustix (workspace features fs, process, net, event, system, thread, time, pipe), memchr, thiserror, tracing, smallvec, rustc-hash, sha2, md-5, the netlink crates. No `unsafe`: only `tl-ops/src/sys.rs`, `tl-engine/src/gpu/spawn.rs` and `tl-app/src/main.rs` may hold it. No `procfs` crate (ADR-016). Dev-dependencies (insta 1.48.0, proptest 1.11.0, tempfile 3.27.0, criterion 0.8.2) come from `[workspace.dependencies]`.
- Never log command lines, environment, working directories, open file paths, executable paths of other users' processes or user names other than the current user, at any level (ADR-015). Processes are logged as `pid` plus `comm`, and `comm` only at `debug` or below. No logging above `trace` inside the per-process loop.

title: E05-007 cgroup stat file readers for apps and units
description:
## Context
App rows and unit rows take Memory from cgroup `memory.stat` `anon`, Swap from `memory.swap.current`, and fall back to `io.stat` when a member's per-process Disk is Restricted (R-103). The State column shows "Frozen" when `cgroup.events` has `frozen 1`. The low-memory mode reads `memory.current`. Files are opened with `openat` from a dirfd on `/sys/fs/cgroup` and closed in the same sweep (R-137). This bead adds those readers to `proc/cgroup.rs`. Sources: PROC-008, PROC-009, PROC-031, PROC-036, R-103, R-137, ADR-016 "App and unit cgroup stats", D-004.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/cgroup.rs`:
- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)] pub struct CgroupStats { pub anon: Option<u64>, pub swap_current: Option<u64>, pub memory_current: Option<u64>, pub usage_usec: Option<u64>, pub rbytes: u64, pub wbytes: u64, pub rios: u64, pub wios: u64, pub io_valid: bool, pub pids_current: Option<u64>, pub frozen: Option<bool>, pub denied: bool }` (`denied` is true when any wanted file gave EACCES or EPERM).
- Selector of files to read: `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)] pub struct CgroupWant { pub memory_stat: bool, pub swap: bool, pub memory_current: bool, pub cpu_stat: bool, pub io_stat: bool, pub pids: bool, pub events: bool }`.
- `pub struct CgroupRoot { dirfd: OwnedFd }` with `pub fn open(sys: &Path) -> Result<Self, CollectError>` (opens `<sys>/fs/cgroup` with `O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC`; `sys` is `SysRoot.sys` from E04-A1, so fixtures work).
- `pub fn read_stats(&self, rel: &str, want: CgroupWant, buf: &mut Vec<u8>, out: &mut CgroupStats) -> Result<(), CollectError>`: opens the cgroup directory with `openat(root, rel, O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC)` (an empty `rel` is the root itself), then for each wanted file `openat(dir, name, O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC)`, reads, closes:
  - `memory.stat`: the `anon <bytes>` line into `anon`;
  - `memory.swap.current`: one integer into `swap_current`;
  - `memory.current`: one integer into `memory_current` (used only by `EngineMode::LowMemory`, R-137);
  - `cpu.stat`: the `usage_usec <n>` line into `usage_usec`;
  - `io.stat`: lines `<maj>:<min> rbytes=<n> wbytes=<n> rios=<n> wios=<n> dbytes=.. dios=..`; sums `rbytes`, `wbytes`, `rios`, `wios` over all device lines; `io_valid = true` when the file was read (an empty file is valid with zeros);
  - `pids.current`: one integer;
  - `cgroup.events`: the `frozen 0|1` line into `frozen`.
  A missing file leaves its field `None` (or `io_valid = false`); EACCES leaves it `None` too. A missing directory gives `Err(ProcRead { file: "cgroup", errno: ENOENT })`.
- `pub fn read_procs(&self, rel: &str, recursive: bool, buf: &mut Vec<u8>, out: &mut Vec<u32>) -> Result<(), CollectError>`: reads `cgroup.procs` of the directory and, when `recursive`, of every child directory (depth-first, `readdirat`), appending pids.
- `pub fn dir_ino(&self, rel: &str) -> Result<u64, CollectError>`: `fstat` inode of the cgroup directory (the `cgroup_id` used by `CgroupRef`, ADR-006).

Fixture `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/process-edge/sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/app-firefox@3a1b.service/` with `memory.stat` (contains `anon 524288000`), `memory.swap.current` (`4096`), `cpu.stat` (`usage_usec 123456789`), `io.stat` (two device lines), `pids.current` (`14`), `cgroup.events` (`populated 1` and `frozen 0`), `cgroup.procs` (`4201`), plus a child directory `sub/` with `cgroup.procs` (`4210`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the firefox fixture directory and every file wanted **When** `read_stats` runs **Then** `anon == Some(524_288_000)`, `swap_current == Some(4096)`, `usage_usec == Some(123_456_789)`, `pids_current == Some(14)`, `frozen == Some(false)`, and `rbytes`, `wbytes`, `rios`, `wios` are the sums of both device lines.
- **Given** a cgroup directory without `memory.swap.current` (no swap configured) **When** `read_stats` runs **Then** `swap_current` is `None` and the call succeeds.
- **Given** `want.memory_current = false` **When** `read_stats` runs **Then** `memory.current` is not opened (checked by a fixture without that file still giving `None` and no error, plus a counter in the test build).
- **Given** a `rel` that does not exist **When** `read_stats` runs **Then** it returns `Err(ProcRead { file: "cgroup", .. })`.
- **Given** the firefox fixture and `recursive = true` **When** `read_procs` runs **Then** `out` is `[4201, 4210]`.
- **Given** `cgroup.events` containing `frozen 1` **When** read **Then** `frozen == Some(true)`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/cgroup.rs`: change, add the readers.
- Fixture tree above: create.
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_process.rs`, `crates/tl-collect/tests/prop_process.rs`: add tests.

## Tests

title: E05-008 fd count reader and U-34 check
description:
## Context
The Handles column (id `handles`, tooltip "Open file descriptors") shows the fd count. R-064 chose `fstatat` `st_size` of `/proc/<pid>/fd`, with a readdir count as fallback, and U-34 says the `st_size` trick is unverified on kernel 7.2. This bead builds the reader and settles U-34 with a real-system test. The count is read only while demanded (a visible column, a Properties window). Sources: PROC-002, PROC-035, R-064, U-34.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/proc/fdcount.rs`:
- `pub enum FdCount { Count(u32), Restricted, Gone }`.
- `pub fn fd_count(pid_dir: BorrowedFd<'_>) -> FdCount`:
  1. `rustix::fs::statat(pid_dir, "fd", AtFlags::empty())`; on success with `st_size > 0`, return `Count(st_size as u32)`;
  2. if `st_size == 0` (older kernels report 0), open `fd` with `openat(.., O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC)` and count entries whose name is not `.` or `..`;
  3. `EACCES` or `EPERM` at any step gives `Restricted`; `ENOENT` or `ESRCH` gives `Gone`.
- `static FALLBACK_USED: AtomicU32` counting fallback calls (relaxed ordering) and `#[doc(hidden)] pub fn fd_count_fallbacks() -> u32` returning it, for tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the test process itself (`/proc/self`) with 3 extra fds opened by the test **When** `fd_count` runs **Then** the result is `Count(n)` where `n` equals the readdir count of `/proc/self/fd` taken in the same test (within 1 for the directory fd the readdir opens).
- **Given** PID 1 as a non-root user **When** `fd_count` runs **Then** the result is `Restricted` (PID 1's `fd` gives EACCES to uid 1000 on the owner machine, proc.md machine facts).
- **Given** a `/proc/<pid>` dir fd of a `sleep 60` child, opened while it ran, after the child is killed and reaped **When** `fd_count` runs **Then** the result is `Gone`, never a count.
- **Given** kernel 7.2 on the owner machine **When** the real-system test runs **Then** step 1 answers (no fallback), and the bead records "U-34 confirmed" or "U-34 failed, fallback used" in its commit message.

- Errors: none returned; states are `Restricted` and `Gone`.
- Validity: `Restricted` for other users (lock glyph, never zero).
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one `statat` per demanded pid; the fallback costs a readdir and is expected only on old kernels.
- Privacy: fd targets are never read here (counting only).

title: E05-009 Process metadata cache with 10-sweep refresh
description:
## Context
`comm`, `cmdline`, `exe` and `cgroup` change rarely, so they are cached per `ProcessKey` and refreshed every 10 sweeps, and at once when `comm` changes (an exec) (R-064, ADR-016). Every string passes through `sanitize` (E05-002) before it is kept. This bead builds that cache and the user-name lookup seam. Sources: PROC-002, PROC-007, PROC-027, PROC-028, R-008, R-064, ADR-015, ADR-016 "Process metadata".

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/proc/meta.rs`:
- `pub const META_REFRESH_SWEEPS: u32 = 10;`
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct RawMeta { pub comm: Arc<str>, pub exe: ExeLink, pub cmdline: Option<Arc<str>>, pub argv: SmallVec<[Arc<str>; 4]>, pub cgroup: Option<CgroupPath>, pub cgroup_denied: bool }`
  - `comm`: `comm` file (falls back to the sanitized `PidStat.comm_raw` when the file read fails), sanitized with `sanitize_comm`.
  - `pub enum ExeLink { Path { path: Arc<str>, deleted: bool }, Restricted, None }`: `readlinkat(dir, "exe")` read up to `EXE_LINK_MAX` (4096) bytes and sanitized with `sanitize_link`; a target ending in ` (deleted)` sets `deleted = true` and keeps the suffix in `path`; `EACCES` or `EPERM` gives `Restricted`; `ENOENT` (kernel threads, zombies) gives `None`.
  - `cmdline`: `cmdline` file read up to `CMDLINE_MAX + 1` bytes then `sanitize_cmdline` (adds `…` past 32 KiB); `None` when empty (kernel threads) or unreadable.
  - `argv`: the first 4 NUL-separated tokens of the raw cmdline, each sanitized with `sanitize_text(.., 4096, ..)`; used by naming, Wine matching and app disambiguation (`--app-id=`, `--profile-directory=`, `--class=` may appear anywhere, so `argv_has_prefix(&self, prefix: &str) -> Option<Arc<str>>` scans the full sanitized `cmdline` split on spaces as a second step).
  - `cgroup`: `parse_cgroup_file` of the `cgroup` file (E05-006); `cgroup_denied = true` on EACCES or EPERM.
- `pub struct MetaCache` with `pub fn new() -> Self` and
  `pub fn get_or_refresh(&mut self, key: ProcessKey, dir: BorrowedFd<'_>, stat_comm_raw: &[u8], bufs: &mut ReadBufs) -> (&RawMeta, MetaChange)`:
  - first sight of `key`: read everything, `MetaChange::New`;
  - otherwise increments the entry's sweep counter; when it reaches `META_REFRESH_SWEEPS`, or when `stat_comm_raw` differs from the raw comm stored at the last refresh, re-reads everything and resets the counter: `MetaChange::Refreshed`; else `MetaChange::Unchanged`.
- `pub fn retain_live(&mut self, live: &FxHashSet<ProcessKey>)`: drops entries for keys not seen this sweep.
- `pub struct Interner` (`FxHashMap<Box<str>, Arc<str>>`, cap 16,384 entries, cleared when full) used for cgroup path parts and user names so equal strings share one `Arc`.
- User names: `pub trait UserNames { fn name(&mut self, uid: u32) -> Arc<str>; }` and `pub struct NumericUserNames` that returns the uid as decimal text (for example `"1000"`), cached per uid. The real lookup is an open item (see the E05 plan section); the sweep takes `&mut dyn UserNames`.
- `pub struct ReadBufs { pub small: Vec<u8>, pub cmdline: Vec<u8>, pub text: String }`, reused across processes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** pid `4201` in `process-edge` with cmdline `firefox\0-P\0default\0` **When** `get_or_refresh` runs the first time **Then** `MetaChange::New`, `cmdline == "firefox -P default"`, `argv == ["firefox", "-P", "default"]`.
- **Given** the same key and an unchanged comm **When** called 9 more times **Then** each returns `Unchanged` and no file is re-read (counted by a test-only read counter); the 10th call returns `Refreshed`.
- **Given** the same key and a stat `comm_raw` of `bash` where the stored comm was `sh` **When** called **Then** it returns `Refreshed` at once.
- **Given** an `exe` symlink whose target is `/usr/bin/foo (deleted)` **When** read **Then** `ExeLink::Path { deleted: true, path: "/usr/bin/foo (deleted)" }`.
- **Given** a fixture pid whose cmdline file is 40 KiB **When** read **Then** `cmdline` has 32,768 characters plus `…`.
- **Given** PID 1 on the owner machine as uid 1000 **When** read **Then** `exe == ExeLink::Restricted` (real-system test).
- **Given** a kernel thread fixture (`57`, empty cmdline, no exe link) **When** read **Then** `cmdline == None` and `exe == ExeLink::None`.

## Files

- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/process-edge/proc/{4201,57,4208}/{comm,cmdline,exe}`: create (`4208` has the 40 KiB cmdline; `exe` entries are symlinks committed with git).
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_process.rs`, `crates/tl-collect/tests/real_restricted.rs`: add tests.

## Tests

- `tests/fixture_process.rs::meta_refresh_every_10_sweeps`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::meta_refresh_on_comm_change`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::meta_deleted_exe_kept`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::meta_cmdline_over_32k_truncated`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::meta_kernel_thread_has_no_cmdline`.
- `tests/real_restricted.rs::meta_pid1_exe_restricted` (`#[ignore]`).

## Cross-cutting

title: E05-010 Process sweep core with rates and validity
description:
## Context
The process sweep reads every pid once per `processes.interval_ms` (default 1000, range 250..=10000) inside one `spawn_blocking` job of the engine's `Processes` worker (E10). This bead writes the sweep core: list pids, open each `/proc/<pid>` as an `O_DIRECTORY` fd, read `stat`, `statm`, `status`, `io` (and the fd count when demanded) relative to it, close it, and compute rates with the ADR-008 counter rules. E05-A1 adds metadata, groups and flags on top. Sources: PROC-002, PROC-029, PROC-030, PROC-031, ADR-008 "Tick semantics", "Counter rules", "CPU math", ADR-016 "File descriptor policy", ADR-003 `ProcessKey`, `FieldValidity`.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/proc/sweep.rs`:
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct SweepCtx { pub boot_id: BootId, pub self_uid: u32, pub ticks_per_sec: u64, pub online_cpus: u32, pub want_fd_count: bool }`. The engine fills it: `self_uid` from `rustix::process::getuid()`, `online_cpus` from the CPU topology (E04-A2), `ticks_per_sec` per the E05 open item on `CLK_TCK`.
- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)] struct Prev { t_ns: TimeNs, mono_ns: u64, utime: u64, stime: u64, minflt: u64, majflt: u64, io: Option<PidIo> }` kept per `ProcessKey` in an `FxHashMap`.
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct SweptProc` with: `key: ProcessKey`, `t_ns: TimeNs`, `stat: PidStat`, `status: PidStatus`, `statm: PidStatm`, `io: IoState` (`pub enum IoState { Valid(PidIo), Restricted, WarmingUp }`), `fd_count: Option<FdCount>` (`None` when not demanded), `cpu_pct: f32`, `cpu_kernel_pct: f32`, `cpu_user_pct: f32`, `cpu_relative_pct: f32`, `io_read_bps: f32`, `io_write_bps: f32`, `disk_read_bps: f32`, `disk_write_raw_bps: f32`, `page_faults_delta: u64`, `validity: FieldValidity`.
- `pub struct SweepCore { root: SysRoot, prev: FxHashMap<ProcessKey, Prev>, bufs: ReadBufs }` with:
  - `pub fn new(root: SysRoot) -> Self`;
  - `pub fn sweep_core(&mut self, ctx: &SweepCtx, out: &mut Vec<SweptProc>) -> (TimeNs, TimeNs)` returning `(observed_start, observed_end)`:
    1. `observed_start = now_boot_ns()`; read `<proc>` directory entries, keep names that are all digits;
    2. for each pid: `openat(<proc> dirfd, pid, O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC)`; read `t_ns = now_boot_ns()` and `mono_ns = now_mono_ns()` immediately before the first read; read `stat` (E05-003), `statm`, `status` (at most 8 KiB, E05-004), `io` (E05-005), and `fd_count` (E05-008) when `ctx.want_fd_count`; close the dirfd; a pid that disappears (ENOENT or ESRCH on `openat` or `stat`) is skipped silently;
    3. `key = ProcessKey { start_ticks: stat.start_ticks, boot_id: ctx.boot_id, pid }`;
    4. rates against `prev[key]` with `dt_s = (t_ns - prev.t_ns) as f64 / 1e9`:
       - `cpu_pct = 100 × Δ(utime + stime) / ticks_per_sec / dt_s / online_cpus`; `cpu_kernel_pct` uses Δstime only, `cpu_user_pct` Δutime only; `cpu_relative_pct` is `cpu_pct × online_cpus` (column "CPU (one core = 100%)");
       - `io_read_bps = Δread_bytes / dt_s`; `io_write_bps = Δ(write_bytes - cancelled_write_bytes) / dt_s` (so Disk = read + write - cancelled, PROC-031); `disk_read_bps` equals `io_read_bps`; `disk_write_raw_bps = Δwrite_bytes / dt_s` (Disk write rate column);
       - `page_faults_delta = Δ(minflt + majflt)`;
    5. ADR-008 rules: no previous entry (new key, after `reset_baselines`), any counter with `cur < prev` (reset), or a suspend gap (`(t_ns - prev.t_ns) - (mono_ns - prev.mono_ns) > 250 ms`, checked with the `counters.rs` helper from E04-A1) gives no rate: the rate fields are 0.0 with validity `WarmingUp` and the baseline is replaced;
    6. `validity` per `ProcessField`: `Cpu` Valid or WarmingUp (step 5); `RssAnon` Valid when `status.rss_anon` is `Some`, else `Unsupported` (kernel threads); `Rss` the same with `vm_rss`; `Swap` the same with `vm_swap`; `Pss` and `Uss` `WarmingUp` (filled by E05-021 for demanded keys); `IoRead` and `IoWrite` `Restricted` when `io` was denied, else Valid or WarmingUp; `NetRx`, `NetTx`, `GpuUtil`, `GpuMem` `WarmingUp` (the engine fills them from E06 and E13 data); `Threads` Valid;
    7. after the loop, drop `prev` entries for keys not seen; `observed_end = now_boot_ns()`.
  - `pub fn reset_baselines(&mut self)`: clears `prev` (engine calls it on `ResetBaselines`, epoch change and rate change).
- Nothing in this file logs per process above `trace`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** two sweeps of a fake root where pid 4201's `utime + stime` grows by 50 ticks in 1.0 s, `ticks_per_sec = 100`, `online_cpus = 32` **When** the second sweep runs **Then** `cpu_pct` is 1.5625 (±0.001) and `cpu_relative_pct` is 50.0, both `Valid`.
- **Given** the first sweep of any pid **When** it runs **Then** `cpu_pct == 0.0` and `validity[Cpu] == WarmingUp`.
- **Given** a second sweep where `utime` went down **When** it runs **Then** the Cpu validity is `WarmingUp` and the third sweep is `Valid` again (reset rule).
- **Given** two sweeps whose boottime delta is 5 s and monotonic delta 10 ms (injected through a test clock hook `SweepCore::with_clock(fn() -> (TimeNs, u64))`) **When** the second sweep runs **Then** no rate is produced and validity is `WarmingUp`.
- **Given** a pid whose `start_ticks` changed between sweeps (PID reuse) **When** the second sweep runs **Then** it is a new key with `WarmingUp`, and the old key is gone from `prev`.
- **Given** a pid directory that vanishes between listing and `openat` **When** the sweep runs **Then** the pid is skipped and no error is returned.
- **Given** a process whose `io` gives EACCES (fixture copy with mode 0000, non-root run) **When** swept **Then** `validity[IoRead] == Restricted` and `io_read_bps == 0.0`.
- **Given** `want_fd_count = false` **When** the sweep runs **Then** `fd_count` is `None` for every process and no `fd` directory is stat-ed.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/sweep.rs`: create (core part; E05-A1 extends it).
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_process.rs`: add tests; builds two-sweep fake roots with `tempfile` copies of `process-edge`.

## Tests
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_cpu_rate_from_elapsed_time`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_first_sample_warming_up`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_counter_reset_warming_up`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_suspend_gap_no_rate`: ADR-008 verification (5 s boottime gap with 10 ms monotonic gap).
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_pid_reuse_new_key`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_vanished_pid_skipped`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_io_restricted_not_zero`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::sweep_fd_count_only_when_wanted`.
- `tests/prop_process.rs::sweep_random_fake_root_never_panics`: proptest that writes 1 to 20 pid dirs with arbitrary bytes in each file and sweeps twice; never panics.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: per-process read failures map to validity; `sweep_core` itself only fails silently per pid. A missing `<proc>` directory gives an empty result.
- Validity: as step 6.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: part of the 15 ms per 2,000 processes gate (E05-023): one dirfd per pid, reuse every buffer and `SweptProc` slot (`out.clear()` keeps capacity), no `format!` (open pid directories by the directory entry name).
- Privacy: no command lines are read here.

No `unsafe`: only `tl-ops/src/sys.rs`, `tl-engine/src/gpu/spawn.rs` and `tl-app/src/main.rs` may hold it. No `procfs` crate (ADR-016). title: E05-011 App id from app.slice unit names and app scan
description:
## Context
Every running app instance becomes one App row. The app id comes from the unit name under `user@<uid>.service/app.slice/`, in the five naming forms systemd launchers use, and the app's pids come from `cgroup.procs`, recursively. Sources: PROC-005, ADR-016 "App grouping", ADR-003 `GroupKind::App`, R-137.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/apps/cgroup_app.rs`:
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct UnitAppId { pub app_id: Arc<str>, pub alt: Option<(Arc<str>, Arc<str>)>, pub kind: AppUnitKind, pub autostart: bool }` with `pub enum AppUnitKind { Scope, KdeService, Flatpak, DbusActivated, Snap }`.

  1. `app-<rest>-<rand>.scope`: strip `app-` and the last `-<rand>` (the final `-`-separated token), then remove an `@<instance>` part. The launcher prefix is optional in this form, so the parser cannot decide it alone: `app_id` is the whole remainder and `alt: Option<(Arc<str>, Arc<str>)>` holds `(launcher, id)` from splitting the remainder at its first `-` (when it has one). The resolver in E05-A2 uses `alt` only when the whole remainder is not a desktop-file id and the split id is one. Kind `Scope`.
  2. `app-<id>@<rand>.service`: id is the part between `app-` and `@`. Kind `KdeService`. When `<rand>` is `autostart`, `autostart = true`.
  3. `flatpak-<id>-<n>.scope`: id between `flatpak-` and the last `-<n>`. Kind `Flatpak`.
  4. `dbus-:<n>-<id>@<n>.service`: id between the second `-` and `@`. Kind `DbusActivated`.
  5. `snap.<a>.<b>-<uuid>.scope`: id is `<a>_<b>`. Kind `Snap`.
