title: E05-031 Handle walk and pipe peers in proc/handles.rs
description:
## Context
Search File Handles (P3) walks every process's open files, memory-mapped files, working directory, executable and root, like `lsof`, on the blocking pool, cancellable between pids. The File descriptors tab (P2) names a pipe by its peer ("pipe:[ino] ↔ cat (5678)"), which needs the same walk limited to a set of pipe inodes. This bead writes both on one walker in `proc/handles.rs`. It is pulled into P2 because anchor E05-A3, which E10 depends on, delivers `handles.rs`. Sources: PROC-096, PROC-080 (pipe peers), ADR-016, UI-PWN `HandleSearchState { search, phase, progress, chunks, searched, total, skipped }` data binding.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/proc/handles.rs`:
- `pub struct Pattern { ... }` with `pub fn new(text: &str) -> Pattern`: case-insensitive; when the text contains `*` or `?` it is a glob over the whole path (`*` any run, `?` one char), else a substring match. Matching works on the lowercased path; no regex crate.
- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum HitKind { Fd, Mmap, Cwd, Exe, Root }` with labels `fd`, `mmap`, `cwd`, `exe`, `root`.
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct HandleHitInfo { pub key: ProcessKey, pub pid: u32, pub comm: Arc<str>, pub uid: u32, pub kind: HitKind, pub fd: Option<u32>, pub path: Arc<str> }`.
- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)] pub struct WalkProgress { pub searched: u32, pub total: u32, pub skipped: u32, pub handles: u64 }`.
- `pub struct HandleWalk { pids: Vec<u32>, next: usize, pattern: Pattern, include_maps: bool, progress: WalkProgress }` with:
  - `pub fn start(root: &SysRoot, pattern: &str, include_maps: bool) -> Self`: lists numeric `<proc>` entries; `total` = their count;
  - `pub fn step(&mut self, root: &SysRoot, ctx_boot: BootId, budget: usize, bufs: &mut ReadBufs, hits: &mut Vec<HandleHitInfo>) -> StepResult` where `pub enum StepResult { More, Done }`: processes up to `budget` pids, then returns, so the caller can check its cancel flag between calls (cancel is "between pids", PROC-096). Per pid: open the dirfd, read `stat` for the key and comm, readlink every `fd/*` (`Fd`, counted in `handles`); when `include_maps`, also the unique file paths of `maps` (`Mmap`), `cwd`, `exe` and `root` links. EACCES on `fd/` counts the pid in `skipped` (other users without the helper); a vanished pid is neither searched nor skipped (decrements `total`). Paths are sanitized with `sanitize_link`; matching paths are pushed as hits.
  - `pub fn progress(&self) -> WalkProgress`.
- `pub fn find_pipe_peers(root: &SysRoot, inodes: &FxHashSet<u64>, skip_pid: u32, bufs: &mut ReadBufs, out: &mut FxHashMap<u64, SmallVec<[(u32, Arc<str>); 2]>>)`: walks all `fd/*` of every other readable pid once and records `pid` and sanitized `comm` for every `pipe:[ino]` link whose inode is in `inodes` (P2, File descriptors tab).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fixture root with pids 4201 (fds to `/home/user1/notes.txt` and `pipe:[99]`, cwd `/home/user1`) and 4214 (fd to `pipe:[99]`) **When** a walk for `notes` runs to `Done` **Then** one hit `{pid: 4201, kind: Fd, path: "/home/user1/notes.txt"}`.
- **Given** pattern `*.TXT` **When** walked **Then** the same hit (glob, case-insensitive).
- **Given** pattern `user1` and `include_maps = true` **When** walked **Then** hits include kind `Cwd` for 4201.
- **Given** `include_maps = false` **When** walked **Then** no `Mmap`, `Cwd`, `Exe` or `Root` hits.
- **Given** `budget = 1` **When** `step` is called repeatedly **Then** it returns `More` until every pid is done, and `progress().searched` grows by at most 1 per call.
- **Given** a pid whose `fd` dir has mode 0000 (non-root run) **When** walked **Then** `skipped` is 1 and no error is returned.
- **Given** inode 99 and `skip_pid = 4201` **When** `find_pipe_peers` runs **Then** `out[99] == [(4214, "cat")]`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/handles.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/process-edge/proc/{4201,4214}/{fd,maps,cwd,exe,root,stat,comm}`: extend or create.
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_process.rs`, `crates/tl-collect/tests/prop_process.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::handles_substring_hit`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::handles_glob_case_insensitive`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::handles_include_maps`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::handles_exclude_maps`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::handles_step_budget`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::handles_restricted_skipped`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::pipe_peers_found`.
- `tests/prop_process.rs::pattern_arbitrary_never_panics`: arbitrary pattern and path strings never panic.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: none surface; unreadable pids are skipped and counted.
- Validity: N/A (the footer note "Searched 412 of 530 processes. 118 need administrator rights." is UI text built from `WalkProgress`).
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one pass, cancel checks between pids; no per-path allocation unless the path matches (match on a reused lowercase buffer).
- Privacy: paths are open file paths and are never logged.

## Notes
- Phase: P3 feature (Search File Handles), P2 for `find_pipe_peers`; written in P2 because E05-A3 delivers it.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...` (for example `... cargo test -p tl-collect`). Run `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p tl-collect --all-targets -- -D warnings` the same way before committing.

title: E05-032 Strings scanner core
description:
## Context
The Strings tab (P3) scans process memory for printable strings in ASCII, UTF-8 and UTF-16LE, with a minimum length of 4 to 64 (default 4), optional file-backed mappings, a cancel, and stop limits of 1,000,000 strings or 256 MiB of text. This bead writes the scanner core: region selection from `/proc/<pid>/maps` and the string finder over byte chunks. How memory is read is behind a trait, because the read mechanism is an E05 open item (`process_vm_readv` needs `libc` and `unsafe`, which `tl-collect` may not use). It is pulled into P2 because anchor E05-A3 delivers `strings.rs`. Sources: PROC-084, UI-PWN `StringScanState` and `StringHit` data binding.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/proc/strings.rs`:
- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct ScanOpts { pub min_len: u8, pub ascii: bool, pub utf8: bool, pub utf16le: bool, pub include_file_backed: bool }` with `min_len` clamped to 4..=64; default `{ 4, true, true, true, false }`.
- `pub const CHUNK: usize = 1024 * 1024; pub const MAX_STRINGS: u32 = 1_000_000; pub const MAX_TEXT_BYTES: u64 = 256 * 1024 * 1024;`
- `pub fn select_regions(maps: &[MapRegionInfo], include_file_backed: bool, out: &mut Vec<(u64, u64)>)`: keeps readable (`perms[0] == b'r'`) regions that are private anonymous (no path, `perms[3] == b'p'`), `[heap]` or `[stack]`; plus file-backed regions when `include_file_backed`; always skips `[vvar]`, `[vsyscall]`, `[vdso]` and paths under `/dev/`.
- `pub trait MemSource { fn read(&mut self, addr: u64, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, CollectError>; }` (returns bytes read; 0 or an error for an unreadable page range, which the scanner skips).
- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum Encoding { Ascii, Utf8, Utf16Le }`; `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct StringHitInfo { pub address: u64, pub encoding: Encoding, pub length: u32, pub value: Box<str> }` (`length` in characters).
- `pub enum ScanEnd { Finished, Cancelled, Stopped, Failed }`.
- `pub struct StringScanner { opts: ScanOpts, regions: Vec<(u64, u64)>, region: usize, offset: u64, found: u32, text_bytes: u64, carry: Vec<u8> }` with `pub fn new(opts: ScanOpts, regions: Vec<(u64, u64)>) -> Self` and
  `pub fn step(&mut self, mem: &mut dyn MemSource, buf: &mut Vec<u8>, out: &mut Vec<StringHitInfo>) -> Option<ScanEnd>`: reads one `CHUNK` (or the rest of the region), finds strings, returns `None` while more work remains, else the end state. Rules:
  - ASCII: runs of bytes 0x20..=0x7E plus `\t`, length at least `min_len`;
  - UTF-8: runs of valid UTF-8 whose chars are printable (not control, not U+FFFD) and that contain at least one non-ASCII char, at least `min_len` chars (pure-ASCII runs are reported once, as ASCII);
  - UTF-16LE: runs of 2-byte units that decode to printable BMP chars (no surrogates), at least `min_len` chars;
  - a string that crosses a chunk boundary is joined through `carry` so it is reported once;
  - values are sanitized with `sanitize_text(.., 4096, ..)` and longer strings are cut there with `…`;
  - stops with `Stopped` when `found` reaches `MAX_STRINGS` or `text_bytes` reaches `MAX_TEXT_BYTES` (the UI text is "String scan stopped: not enough memory.").
  - `pub fn progress_pct(&self) -> u8`: bytes scanned / total region bytes × 100.
- `pub struct VecMem(pub u64, pub Vec<u8>)` implementing `MemSource` for tests (base address and bytes).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** maps with `[heap]` r/w private, a private anonymous region, `/usr/lib/libc.so.6` r-x, `[vvar]` and `/dev/dri/card1` **When** `select_regions` runs with `include_file_backed = false` **Then** only the heap and anonymous regions are kept; with `true`, libc is added and `[vvar]` and `/dev/` stay out.
- **Given** memory `"\0\0hello world\0ab\0"` at base 0x1000 and `min_len = 4` **When** scanned **Then** one ASCII hit `{address: 0x1002, length: 11, value: "hello world"}`.
- **Given** UTF-16LE bytes for `Wine path` **When** scanned **Then** one `Utf16Le` hit with value `Wine path`.
- **Given** UTF-8 `"grüße\0"` with `min_len = 4` **When** scanned **Then** one `Utf8` hit `grüße`.
- **Given** a 6-byte ASCII string split across a 1 MiB chunk boundary **When** scanned **Then** it is reported once with the right address.
- **Given** a scanner built with `with_limits(10, MAX_TEXT_BYTES)` and 20 strings in memory **When** scanned **Then** the end state is `Stopped` with 10 hits.
- **Given** a scanner and a caller cancel flag set after the first `step` **When** the caller stops calling `step` **Then** the caller reports `Cancelled` (the scanner holds no thread and needs no cleanup).

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/strings.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_process.rs`, `crates/tl-collect/tests/prop_process.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::strings_region_selection`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::strings_ascii_hit`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::strings_utf16le_hit`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::strings_utf8_hit`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::strings_chunk_boundary_once`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::strings_stop_limit`.
- `tests/prop_process.rs::strings_arbitrary_memory_never_panics`: arbitrary byte buffers up to 3 MiB and arbitrary options never panic, and every hit's value is at most 4,097 chars.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `MemSource` errors skip the range; `Failed` only when no region could be read at all ("Failed to read process memory.").

- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one 1 MiB chunk per `step`; the engine sends payloads at most 4 times per second.

## Notes

title: E05-033 Launcher split: Steam, Lutris and Heroic games
description:
## Context
Scope grouping puts every game under the Steam (or Lutris, Heroic) app. PROC-011 (P4) splits them: each game becomes its own child app row named after the game. ## Deliverable

title: E05-002 Sanitizer for untrusted process text
description:
## Context
Process metadata is untrusted and can be hostile: control characters, bidirectional overrides, invalid UTF-8 and huge command lines. ADR-015 requires one sanitizer in `tl-collect/src/sanitize.rs`, applied before any string enters `ProcessMeta`, so the UI, logs and copy text never see raw bytes. Sources: ADR-015 "Untrusted process text", R-008, PROC-002, PROC-007.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/sanitize.rs`:
- Constants: `pub const COMM_MAX: usize = 64;`, `pub const CMDLINE_MAX: usize = 32 * 1024;`, `pub const EXE_LINK_MAX: usize = 4096;`, `pub const STATUS_MAX: usize = 8 * 1024;`, `pub const ELLIPSIS: char = '\u{2026}';`.
- `pub fn sanitize_text(raw: &[u8], max: usize, out: &mut String)`: clears `out`, then
  1. if `raw.len() > max`, uses only `raw[..max]` and remembers that it truncated;
  2. decodes with `String::from_utf8_lossy` (a cut multi-byte sequence becomes U+FFFD);
  3. maps every char: `'\n'`, `'\r'` and NUL become a space (lines and NUL separators are joined with spaces); other C0 controls U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F and C1 controls U+0080 to U+009F become U+FFFD; U+202A to U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069 and U+200B to U+200F are removed;
  4. trims trailing spaces;
  5. if it truncated, appends `…` (U+2026).
- `pub fn sanitize_cmdline(raw: &[u8], out: &mut String)`: drops one trailing NUL, then `sanitize_text(raw, CMDLINE_MAX, out)`. A raw cmdline with only NULs or empty gives an empty string.
- `pub fn sanitize_comm(raw: &[u8], out: &mut String)`: drops one trailing `\n`, then `sanitize_text(raw, COMM_MAX, out)`.
- `pub fn sanitize_link(raw: &[u8], out: &mut String)`: `sanitize_text(raw, EXE_LINK_MAX, out)`; keeps a ` (deleted)` suffix as text (PROC-027).
- No allocation when `out` already has capacity for the result.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** cmdline bytes `b"/usr/bin/foo\0--bar\0baz\0"` **When** `sanitize_cmdline` runs **Then** `out` is `/usr/bin/foo --bar baz`.
- **Given** comm bytes `b"evil\x1b[31m\n"` **When** `sanitize_comm` runs **Then** `out` is `evil\u{FFFD}[31m`.
- **Given** text containing U+202E (RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE) and U+200B **When** `sanitize_text` runs **Then** both are absent from `out`.
- **Given** bytes `b"a\xff\xfeb"` **When** `sanitize_text` runs **Then** `out` is `a\u{FFFD}\u{FFFD}b`.
- **Given** a 1 MiB cmdline of `b'x'` **When** `sanitize_cmdline` runs **Then** `out` has 32,768 `x` characters followed by `…` and no more.
- **Given** a raw cmdline of exactly 32,768 bytes **When** `sanitize_cmdline` runs **Then** no `…` is appended.
- **Given** C1 control U+0085 encoded as UTF-8 **When** `sanitize_text` runs **Then** it becomes U+FFFD.
- **Given** a link `b"/usr/bin/foo (deleted)"` **When** `sanitize_link` runs **Then** the suffix ` (deleted)` is kept.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/sanitize.rs`: create the module.
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/sanitize.rs`: tests.

## Tests
- `tests/sanitize.rs::cmdline_nul_to_space`: first criterion.
- `tests/sanitize.rs::control_chars_replaced`: C0 (including tab), DEL and C1 become U+FFFD, `\n` and `\r` become spaces.
- `tests/sanitize.rs::bidi_and_zero_width_removed`: every char in U+202A..=U+202E, U+2066..=U+2069, U+200B..=U+200F is removed.
- `tests/sanitize.rs::invalid_utf8_lossy`: invalid bytes give U+FFFD.
- `tests/sanitize.rs::cmdline_1mib_truncated_to_32kib`: the 1 MiB case (ADR-015 verification).
- `tests/sanitize.rs::exact_limit_not_marked`: 32,768 bytes, no ellipsis.
- `tests/sanitize.rs::proptest_output_clean`: proptest over arbitrary `Vec<u8>` up to 70,000 bytes: never panics, output has no char in the removed or replaced sets, and output char count is at most `max + 1`.
- `tests/sanitize.rs::reuses_buffer`: with `out` pre-reserved to 64 KiB, capacity is unchanged after a 32 KiB input.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A (infallible).
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one pass, no allocation when `out` has capacity; runs for every new or refreshed process, so no regex.
- Privacy: this is the privacy gate for process text. Security regression tests above must stay.

## Notes
- `from_utf8_lossy` returns `Cow`; iterate its chars and push into `out` to avoid a second allocation.

description:
## Context

description:
## Context

## Deliverable

- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)] pub struct PidStatm { pub size: u64, pub resident: u64, pub shared: u64, pub text: u64, pub data: u64 }` in pages (fields 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 of `statm`).

title: E05-006 cgroup v2 path parsing and placement
description:
## Context
The cgroup v2 path of a process decides its group (Apps, Background, System), its unit row and its app id. This bead parses the `0::` line of `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` into the path and its slice, unit and scope parts, with systemd `\xNN` unescaping. The current uid always comes from `getuid()` and is never hard-coded. Sources: PROC-004, PROC-005, PROC-036 (Unit, Cgroup columns), ADR-016 "App grouping", ADR-003 `ProcessMeta.cgroup`.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/proc/cgroup.rs`:
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct CgroupPath { pub rel: Arc<str>, pub unit: Option<Arc<str>>, pub slices: SmallVec<[Arc<str>; 4]> }`. `rel` is the v2 path without the leading `/` (relative to `/sys/fs/cgroup`, the form `ProcessMeta.cgroup` and `CgroupRef.rel_path` use). `unit` is the innermost path component that ends in `.service` or `.scope` (escaped form kept). `slices` are the components that end in `.slice`, outermost first.
- `pub fn parse_cgroup_file(buf: &[u8]) -> Option<CgroupPath>`: picks the line that starts with `0::`; returns `None` if there is none (cgroup v1 only, or an empty file). The root path `/` gives `rel = ""` with no unit.
- `pub fn unescape_unit(name: &str, out: &mut String)`: replaces every `\xNN` (two hex digits) with that byte, so `chrome\x2dwork` becomes `chrome-work`. A malformed escape is copied as is.
- `pub enum UserPlacement { InUserManager { uid: u32 }, InSessionScope { uid: u32 }, OutsideUserSlice }` and `pub fn placement(p: &CgroupPath) -> UserPlacement`: `user.slice/user-<uid>.slice/user@<uid>.service/...` is `InUserManager`, `user.slice/user-<uid>.slice/session-<n>.scope` is `InSessionScope`, anything else (`system.slice`, `init.scope`, `machine.slice`) is `OutsideUserSlice`.
- `pub fn app_slice_unit<'a>(p: &'a CgroupPath, uid: u32) -> Option<&'a str>`: when the path starts with `user.slice/user-{uid}.slice/user@{uid}.service/app.slice/`, returns the first component after `app.slice/` (the app unit, which may itself be a `.slice`); else `None`.

Fixtures (`crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/process-edge/proc/<pid>/cgroup`): `4201` in `0::/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/app-firefox@3a1b.service`; `4205` in `0::/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/app-chrome\x2dwork@00bca6.service`; `4206` in `0::/user.slice/user-1000.slice/session-2.scope`; `4207` in `0::/system.slice/pipewire.service`; `57` in `0::/` (kernel thread).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `4205/cgroup` **When** parsed **Then** `unit` is `app-chrome\x2dwork@00bca6.service` and `app_slice_unit(p, 1000)` returns the same string.
- **Given** the escaped unit `app-chrome\x2dwork@00bca6.service` **When** `unescape_unit` runs **Then** it gives `app-chrome-work@00bca6.service`.
- **Given** `4206/cgroup` **When** `placement` runs **Then** it returns `InSessionScope { uid: 1000 }`.
- **Given** `4207/cgroup` **When** `placement` runs **Then** it returns `OutsideUserSlice` and `unit` is `pipewire.service`.
- **Given** a cgroup file with only v1 lines (`12:cpu:/foo`) **When** parsed **Then** it returns `None`.
- **Given** `4205/cgroup` and uid 1001 **When** `app_slice_unit` runs **Then** it returns `None` (no hard-coded uid).

- Fixture files above: create.
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_process.rs`, `crates/tl-collect/tests/prop_process.rs`: add tests.

## Tests

- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: read with the metadata (every 10 sweeps and on `comm` change, R-064); `Arc<str>` parts are shared between processes of the same unit through the interner in E05-009.
- Privacy: N/A (cgroup paths are not secret, but they are not logged per process either).

## Notes
- `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` is world-readable.
- E05-007 adds the cgroup file readers to this same file; keep the path code at the top.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...` (for example `... cargo test -p tl-collect`). Run `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p tl-collect --all-targets -- -D warnings` the same way before committing.
- Commit with a pathspec of only this bead's files: `git commit -m "..." -- <files>` (run `git add` on new files first). Never switch branch, reset, rebase or amend.
- `tl-collect` has no async code and no runtime (ADR-001 rule 3). Allowed dependencies: tl-model, rustix (workspace features fs, process, net, event, system, thread, time, pipe), memchr, thiserror, tracing, smallvec, rustc-hash, sha2, md-5, the netlink crates. No `unsafe`: only `tl-ops/src/sys.rs`, `tl-engine/src/gpu/spawn.rs` and `tl-app/src/main.rs` may hold it. No `procfs` crate (ADR-016). Dev-dependencies (insta 1.48.0, proptest 1.11.0, tempfile 3.27.0, criterion 0.8.2) come from `[workspace.dependencies]`.
- Never log command lines, environment, working directories, open file paths, executable paths of other users' processes or user names other than the current user, at any level (ADR-015). Processes are logged as `pid` plus `comm`, and `comm` only at `debug` or below. No logging above `trace` inside the per-process loop.

title: E19-A1 Chart element
description:
## Context
Anchor bead. Other epics (E24 pages and sidebar, E25 device pages, E26 minigraphs, E01 bench scenes, E30 history) compile against the chart element from here on. This bead closes the chart core: it exports the public API from `chart/mod.rs`, wires the state table into the element paint, and adds the end-to-end tests that ADR-009 and ADR-013 name. Sources: ADR-009 "Chart element" and "Verification"; ADR-013 UI tests; UI-PRF-001 states; UI-PRF-007.

## Deliverable

- `chart/element.rs`: state painting per UI-PRF-001:
  - `WarmingUp`: background, grid, baseline, outline; no paths.
  - `Failed(_)`, `Restricted`, `Unsupported`: background, outline and the dotted baseline across the whole plot width (`paint_gaps` with one span `0..pw`); no grid lines, no paths.
  - `Stale`: paths as E19-007 (half-alpha tail).
  - `Live`: paths.
- `chart/view.rs`: `pub fn value_now(&self) -> Option<(f32, Validity)>`: newest sample value of series 0 with `Validity::Valid`, or `Stale`, or the owner state mapped to `Validity::{Failed, Restricted, Unsupported}`, or `WarmingUp` (E19-009 formats it; owners such as the sidebar card read it too).

title: E19: ChartView data binding: hub subscription, series lookup, re-render rules, derived state
description:
## Context
A chart must re-render only when one of its own series changed, when the style changed, or when it is sliding. This bead wires `ChartView` to the `SnapshotHub`, resolves `SeriesId`s to `SeriesView`s by binary search, and derives `WarmingUp` and `Stale` from the data. Sources: ADR-009 entity rules ("views subscribe to SnapshotHub and notify themselves only for components they draw", "nothing calls notify inside render"); ADR-005 hub `install` and `SnapshotChanged { mask, changed_series }`; UI-PRF-001 "Data binding"; ADR-013 render counters.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/chart/view.rs`:

```rust
impl ChartView {
    pub fn new(spec: ChartSpec, labels: ChartLabels, hub: &Entity<SnapshotHub>, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> Self;
    // subscribes with cx.subscribe(hub, Self::on_snapshot) in the constructor only
    fn on_snapshot(&mut self, hub: Entity<SnapshotHub>, ev: &SnapshotChanged, cx: &mut Context<Self>);
    pub fn resolve(&mut self, snap: &Snapshot);    // binary search Snapshot.series.series (sorted by SeriesId) for each spec series id; stores Arc<SeriesView> clones
    pub fn derived_state(&self, now_boot_ns: u64) -> ChartState;
}
```

Rules:
- `on_snapshot`: if `ev.mask` has `SERIES` and `ev.changed_series` contains any of `spec.series[i].id`, call `resolve(&hub.read(cx).current())` and `cx.notify()`. Also notify when `ev.mask` has `DEVICES` and one of the view's series was absent before (a device appeared). Nothing else notifies.
- `set_spec` re-resolves against the hub's current snapshot and notifies. The `style_version` change is caught by the geometry key in paint (the owner page re-renders on theme change, which re-renders the chart).
- `derived_state(now)`: if `self.state` is `Failed | Restricted | Unsupported` (owner-set), return it. Else if no series resolved or every resolved series has zero samples: `WarmingUp`. Else if `geometry::is_stale(newest_ns, now, period_ns)`: `Stale { age_ns }`. Else `Live`.
- The element (E19-007) calls `derived_state` once per paint and paints per the state table in UI-PRF-001.
- `render_count` increments in `Render::render`, not in paint, so a test can tell "re-rendered" from "re-painted while sliding".

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a `FakeEngine` publishing a snapshot that changes series `A` only **When** a `ChartView` for series `B` receives the hub event **Then** its `render_count` stays at 1 (`chart_not_rerendered_on_unrelated_series`).
- **Given** a snapshot that changes series `B` **When** the event arrives **Then** `render_count` becomes 2 and `resolve` stored the new `Arc<SeriesView>` (pointer differs).
- **Given** a snapshot with 80 series **When** `resolve` runs **Then** it performs at most 2 × ⌈log₂ 80⌉ comparisons (binary search; assert through a counting comparator in a unit test on the search helper) and no allocation (`Arc::clone` only).
- **Given** a view whose series is absent from the snapshot **When** `derived_state` runs **Then** `WarmingUp`; after `set_state(Restricted)` it returns `Restricted` whatever the data.
- **Given** samples whose newest is 2 s old at 100 ms period **When** `derived_state` runs **Then** `Stale { age_ns: 2_000_000_000 }`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/chart/view.rs`: change
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_chart.rs`: change, add the tests below

## Tests
- `ui_chart.rs::chart_not_rerendered_on_unrelated_series` (ADR-009 verification, render counter)
- `ui_chart.rs::chart_rerendered_on_own_series`
- `ui_chart.rs::chart_resolves_by_binary_search`
- `ui_chart.rs::chart_state_warming_up_then_live_then_stale`
- `ui_chart.rs::owner_state_wins`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `Failed(last_error)` text comes from the owner (`SourceHealth.last_error` through `Snapshot.health`); the chart only displays it (E19-009 tooltip "Could not read: {last_error}").
- Validity: the full UI-PRF-001 state table.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the subscription callback does one `SmallVec` membership test per event (`changed_series` is at most 64 ids); `resolve` is two binary searches.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
`SnapshotHub`, `SnapshotChanged { mask: ComponentMask, changed_series: SmallVec<[SeriesId; 64]> }`, `ComponentMask::SERIES`, `FakeEngine` are E16-A1 (ADR-005, ADR-013). `Snapshot.series: Arc<SeriesSet>` with `series: Arc<[Arc<SeriesView>]>` sorted by `SeriesId` (ADR-003); `SeriesId` derives `Ord` in E03-A1 (device then metric); if it does not, compare `(device.0, metric.0)` tuples. Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E19: chart labels: heading, value, legend, axis max, range label as cached ShapedLines (chart/labels.rs)
description:
## Context
Every chart's text is shaped once and re-shaped only when its string changes: the heading, the newest value, the legend swatches and labels, the axis maximum and the range label. This bead writes `LabelCache` and the paint step 6 of UI-PRF-001. Sources: ADR-009 rule 10; UI-PRF-001 (heading, value, legend, axis max, range label, states); UI-PRF-003 (the legend table, visibility rules, strings); PERF-016 (range words); PERF-019; PERF-026; UI-FND-003 text tokens; UI-FND-026 glyphs; table (d).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/chart/labels.rs`:

```rust
pub struct LabelCache {
    heading: CachedLine, value: CachedLine, axis_max: CachedLine, range: CachedLine,
    legend: SmallVec<[CachedLine; 2]>,
    #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-hooks"))] pub shape_count: u32,
}
struct CachedLine { text: String, line: Option<ShapedLine>, font_size: Pixels, color: Hsla }
pub struct LabelPaint<'a> { pub box_bounds: Bounds<Pixels>, pub plot: Bounds<Pixels>, pub labels: &'a ChartLabels, pub spec: &'a ChartSpec, pub state: &'a ChartState, pub value: Option<(f32, Validity)>, pub axis_text: Option<&'a str>, pub metrics: &'a UiMetrics, pub theme: &'a TlTheme, pub network_unit: NetworkUnit }
pub fn paint(window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App, cache: &mut LabelCache, p: &LabelPaint, scratch: &mut String);
pub fn range_label(range_word: &str, range_ns: u64, out: &mut String);  // "<word> over 30 seconds" | "60 seconds" | "5 minutes" | "10 minutes"
pub fn format_value(fmt: ValueFormat, value: f32, unit: NetworkUnit, out: &mut String);  // table (d) through tl_model::units
```

Layout at 100% (every px × `ui_scale`): `chart_pad = sp3 (6)`, `chart_label_row = 18`.
- Heading: `t_sm` (12) weight 500 `text_primary`, left inset `chart_pad`, baseline-aligned in row 1 (top inset `chart_pad`). Hidden when `labels.heading` is `None`.
- Value: `t_sm` 400 `tnum` (`FontFeatures` with `("tnum", 1)`), right-aligned in row 1 with right inset `chart_pad` when `value_align == Right`; left inset `chart_pad` when `Left` (then `t_sm` 500 per UI-PRF-011); none when `Hidden`. Text by `Validity`: `Valid` the formatted value in `text_primary`; `WarmingUp` `…`; `Restricted` the lock icon 12 px (painted through `TlValidityGlyph`'s icon path, see Notes); `Unsupported` `n/a`; `Missing` `-`; `Failed` `!` in `status.warning`; `Stale` the last value in `text_secondary`. Glyph colours `text_secondary`.
- Legend (row 2, left inset `chart_pad`): only when `labels.legend` is non-empty; items 12 px apart, each a 12 × 2 px line swatch (a quad in the series line colour; dashed style draws three 3 px dashes with 2 px gaps), `sp2` gap, label `t_xs` 400 `text_secondary`. Vertical stack (one item per row) when the box width is under 200 px, horizontal otherwise.
- Axis maximum (row 2, right-aligned, right inset `chart_pad`): `t_xs` 400 `text_secondary`; shown only when `labels.show_axis_max`, the plot height ≥ 100 px and `axis_text.is_some()`.
- Range label: bottom-left, inset `chart_pad` from left and bottom, `t_xs` 400 `text_secondary`; hidden when plot height < 100 or box width < 160.
- Re-shape rule: `format_value` writes into `scratch`; the line re-shapes only when `scratch != cached.text` or the font size or colour changed (bytes compare; then `cached.text.clear(); push_str`). Heading, legend and range label follow the same rule. `shape_count` increments per `shape_line` call.
- Shaping: `window.text_system().shape_line(SharedString::from(text), font_size, &[TextRun { len, font: metrics.font_sans with weight, color, .. }], None)`; painting with `ShapedLine::paint(origin, line_height, window, cx)`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** two snapshots with the same formatted value `12.0%` **When** painted twice **Then** `shape_count` increased by 1 in total for the value line (`chart_value_label_reshapes_only_on_text_change`).
- **Given** `range_label("Utilization", 60e9)` **Then** `"Utilization over 60 seconds"`; `("Throughput", 300e9)` gives `"Throughput over 5 minutes"`; `("Memory usage", 30e9)` gives `"Memory usage over 30 seconds"`; `("Power draw", 600e9)` gives `"Power draw over 10 minutes"`.
- **Given** a 116 × 56 box **When** painted **Then** no range label and no legend lines are shaped (visibility rules).
- **Given** a 600 × 300 box with legend `[("Total", Solid), ("Kernel", Dashed)]` **When** painted **Then** two legend lines are shaped side by side (second item x > first item x) and two swatch quads of 12 × 2 are painted, the second as three dashes.
- **Given** a 180 × 150 box **When** painted with the same legend **Then** the second legend item is below the first (vertical stack).
- **Given** `axis_text = Some("100 Mbps")` and `show_axis_max` **When** the plot height is 90 **Then** no axis line is shaped; at 150 it is shaped and right-aligned.
- **Given** `value = Some((_, Validity::Failed))` **When** painted **Then** the value text is `!` in `status.warning`.
- **Given** `format_value(RateNetwork, 1.2e6, Bits)` **Then** `"1.2 Mbps"`; `(Bytes, 1.5 × 1024², Bytes)` gives `"1.5 MiB/s"`; `(Percent, 0.0)` gives `"0%"`; `(Mhz, 4631.4)` gives `"4631 MHz"`; `(Celsius, 52.4)` gives `"52 °C"`; `(Watts, 31.94)` gives `"31.9 W"`; `(Count, 12345.0)` gives `"12 345"` (thin space).

## Files

- `crates/tl-ui/src/chart/element.rs`: change, call `labels::paint` at step 6 and pass `scale_state` axis text
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_chart.rs`: change

- Validity: full glyph table (UI-FND-026) on the value line.
- Accessibility: these labels are the chart's text alternative.
- Performance: ≤ 5 `ShapedLine::paint` per frame; re-shape only on text change; `scratch` reused; no `format!`.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
`shape_line` is gpui-pre 0.3.7 `src/text_system.rs:638`; `ShapedLine::paint` `src/text_system/line.rs:108`. Font family `"Noto Sans"` and the `TNUM` feature constant are E15-A1 `text/style.rs` (UI-FND-051); use them, do not build `FontFeatures` by hand. The lock glyph: `TlValidityGlyph` (E15-A2) is an element and cannot be painted from inside `paint`; draw the same Lucide `lock` SVG through `window.paint_svg(bounds, path, transform, color, cx)` with the asset path `components/icons.rs` exposes (`icons::svg_path(IconName::Lock)`, E15-A1). If E15 exposes no path helper, stop and report; do not substitute a text character for the lock. title: E19: ChartGridElement and ChartGridView: one element for n cells with merged paths (chart/grid_element.rs)
description:
## Context
The CPU per-core grid (32 cells on this machine) and the GPU engine grid are one element each: one fill path, one total-line path and one overlay-line path for every cell, so the `perf-cpu` scene clones 3 paths per frame instead of 96. This bead writes the layout math, the per-cell geometry offsets, and the paint. Sources: ADR-009 rule 7; UI-PRF-002 (layout formula, anatomy, build, performance); PERF-028; PERF-063; ADR-014.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/chart/grid_element.rs`:

```rust
pub struct GridCellSpec { pub heading: SharedString, pub fill_series: SeriesId, pub overlay_series: Option<SeriesId>, pub offline: bool, pub mark: Option<IconName> /* P2 core marks */, pub tooltip: Option<SharedString> }
pub struct ChartGridSpec { pub cells: Vec<GridCellSpec>, pub fill: Hsla, pub line: Hsla, pub overlay_line: Hsla, pub y: YScale, pub range_ns: u64, pub smooth: bool, pub cell_min_w: Pixels /* 120 */, pub cell_h: Pixels /* 112 */, pub gap: Pixels /* sp4 8 */, pub legend: SmallVec<[(SharedString, LegendStyle); 2]> /* drawn in cell 0 only */, pub value_fmt: ValueFormat }
pub struct ChartGridView {
    pub spec: ChartGridSpec,
    cache: Rc<RefCell<ChartCache>>,          // all cells in one cache: fills[0], strokes[0] (total), strokes[1] (overlay)
    series: Vec<(Option<Arc<SeriesView>>, Option<Arc<SeriesView>>)>,
    headings: Vec<CachedLine>, values: Vec<CachedLine>, legend: LabelCache,
    scale_state: ScaleState,
    #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-hooks"))] pub render_count: Cell<u32>,
}
pub fn grid_layout(n: usize, width: Pixels, cell_min_w: Pixels, gap: Pixels) -> GridLayout { cols, rows, cell_w }
    // cols = min(ceil(sqrt(2n)), floor((W + gap) / (cell_min_w + gap))), at least 1; rows = ceil(n / cols); cell_w = (W − (cols − 1) × gap) / cols
pub fn grid_height(layout: &GridLayout, cell_h: Pixels, gap: Pixels) -> Pixels;   // rows × cell_h + (rows − 1) × gap
pub struct ChartGridElement { view: Entity<ChartGridView> }  // Element impl like ChartElement; request_layout returns width = available, height = grid_height
```

Behaviour:
- `ChartGridView::new(spec, hub, cx)` subscribes to the hub exactly like `ChartView` (notify when any of its series ids is in `changed_series`).
- Geometry build (same key rule as E19-007, with `series_versions` as the sum of all cell versions plus the cell count, and physical cell size): for each cell `i` at origin `(col × (cell_w + gap), row × (cell_h + gap))` in physical px, build that cell's runs through `geometry::decimate` with the cell's plot width, emit the fill polygon into one shared `PathBuilder::fill()` and the stroke into the shared total builder, the overlay into the overlay builder, with every vertex offset by the cell origin plus the 1 px plot inset. Each cell's x values are clipped to `0..cell_plot_w` at build time (points outside are dropped, the boundary point is interpolated), because one content mask covers the whole element.
- Paint per frame: background, grid quads, baseline and outline for every cell (`grid.rs` functions per cell, outline colour `spec.line`; offline cells use `divider` and skip grid and baseline); then one `with_content_mask(whole element)` and 3 path clone-translate-paint calls (+ 3 for stale sets when present); then per cell the heading line (left, row 1) and value line (right, row 1), the legend in cell 0 only (horizontal when `cell_w ≥ 200`, else vertical).
- The scroll offset `dx` is the same for every cell (same `right_edge` and `range`), so one translate serves all.
- Offline cell (`offline == true`): no plot, the text "Offline" centred in `t_sm` `text_secondary`; outline `divider`.
- Values re-shape only when their text changed (per-core percent changes ~10 times a second; that is the budgeted case).
- `with_content_mask` rule: cells' paths were clipped at build time, so the single mask is the element bounds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `n = 16`, `W = 1000`, `cell_min_w = 120`, `gap = 8` **When** `grid_layout` runs **Then** `cols = 6`, `rows = 3`.
- **Given** `n = 32`, `W = 1300` **When** `grid_layout` runs **Then** `cols = 8`, `rows = 4`; `grid_height` with `cell_h = 112` is `4 × 112 + 3 × 8 = 472`.
- **Given** `n = 16`, `W = 500` **When** `grid_layout` runs **Then** `cols = 3` (width cap; `floor((500 + 8) / 128) = 3`).
- **Given** 32 cells with overlays on **When** geometry is built **Then** `cache.fills.len() == 1`, `cache.strokes.len() == 2` (`grid_one_fill_path_for_all_cells`).
- **Given** cell 5 `offline` **When** painted **Then** no vertex of any path lies inside cell 5's bounds and the text "Offline" is shaped once.
- **Given** a snapshot that changes one core's series **When** the hub event arrives **Then** the grid view re-renders (`render_count` + 1); a snapshot changing only memory series does not.
- **Given** 10 snapshots where every core value changes **When** painted **Then** the value `shape_count` is 32 × 10 and the heading `shape_count` is 32.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/chart/grid_element.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-ui/src/chart/geometry.rs`: change, add `pub fn build_cell(input: &BuildInput, origin: (f32, f32), clip_w: f32, fill: &mut PathBuilder, stroke: &mut PathBuilder, overlay: Option<&mut PathBuilder>, scratch: &mut Scratch)` used by the grid (shares the run and decimation code with `build`)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_chart.rs`: change

## Tests
- `ui_chart.rs::grid_columns_for_16_is_6`
- `ui_chart.rs::grid_columns_for_32_is_8`
- `ui_chart.rs::grid_columns_drop_when_narrow`
- `ui_chart.rs::grid_one_fill_path_for_all_cells`
- `ui_chart.rs::grid_offline_cell_draws_no_path`
- `ui_chart.rs::grid_rerenders_only_on_own_series`
- `ui_chart.rs::grid_values_reshape_per_change`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: per-cell value glyphs as E19-009; a cell whose series is `Missing` (CPU offline) is `offline`.
- Accessibility: per-cell values are text; the Details grid repeats the total (E24).
- Performance: 3 path clones per frame for 32 cells plus 32 × (3 to 13) grid quads ≈ 400 quads and 64 label paints; geometry rebuild once per 100 ms tick (one `PathBuilder` per colour). ADR-014 `perf-cpu` gate p50 ≤ 1.0 ms.
- Privacy: N/A

title: E19: overlaid and stacked multi-series charts (n lines at 1/n alpha, cumulative bands)
description:
## Context
The CPU page's "All cores overlaid" and "All cores stacked" modes draw every core in one chart: overlaid as n lines at alpha `max(1/n, 0.08)` without fill, stacked as cumulative filled bands with a `Stacked(n)` scale. The chart element needs to accept n series and build bands. Sources: PERF-030; UI-PRF-023 (modes); UI-PRF-006 (`Stacked`); ADR-009 rule 7 (merge).

## Deliverable
- `ChartSpec.series` type changes from `SmallVec<[ChartSeries; 2]>` to `SmallVec<[ChartSeries; 4]>` with the same API (the inline size grows; n = 32 spills to the heap once at construction, never per frame).
- `geometry::build` with `input.stack == true`: series are processed in order; for series `k`, each point's value is the sum of series `0..=k` at the same bucket (series are aligned by `t_ns`; a missing sample in a lower series contributes 0 and marks the point `partial`); the fill polygon of band `k` goes from band `k`'s line down to band `k − 1`'s line (band 0 to the baseline). Fills are not merged across bands when their colours differ; the owner passes per-band colours (E24 computes them from `cpu_fill` with alpha steps). Strokes are emitted per band in the band's line colour.
- `build` with `input.stack == false` and `fill == None` for every series (overlaid): one stroke per distinct `(line, dashed)`; the owner passes each series with `line = cpu_line.alpha(max(1/n, 0.08))`, which is one colour for all n, so they merge into one path (rule 7).
- Overscan and decimation apply per series as before.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 3 series with values `[10, 20, 30]` at every sample and `stack = true`, `Stacked(3)` **When** built **Then** band 2's top vertices are at `y_of(60)`, band 1's at `y_of(30)`, band 0's at `y_of(10)`, and `cache.fills.len() == 3` when the three fill colours differ.
- **Given** 16 series with the same `line` colour and no fill **When** built **Then** `cache.strokes.len() == 1` and `cache.fills.is_empty()`.
- **Given** a stacked build where series 1 has a gap at bucket 100 **When** built **Then** band 2's point at bucket 100 equals `s0 + s2` and the band has no gap (the gap belongs to series 1's own run split).
- **Given** 32 series **When** `ChartSpec` is constructed **Then** no allocation occurs after construction across 100 rebuilds (count with a test allocator or assert `SmallVec::spilled()` is stable).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/chart/mod.rs`: change (`SmallVec<[ChartSeries; 4]>`)
- `crates/tl-ui/src/chart/geometry.rs`: change (stack bands)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/chart_geometry.rs`: change

## Tests
- `chart_geometry.rs::stacked_bands_cumulative`
- `chart_geometry.rs::overlaid_merges_to_one_stroke`
- `chart_geometry.rs::stacked_gap_in_middle_series`
- `chart_geometry.rs::many_series_no_per_rebuild_allocation`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: a series without any valid sample in the window contributes nothing to the stack and is skipped.
- Accessibility: the axis max text ("1600%") is painted by E19-009 from `Stacked(n)`.
- Performance: stacked build is O(n × points); for 32 cores × 600 points it is 19,200 additions per rebuild, 10 times per second, inside budget.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
Alignment by `t_ns` assumes the per-core series share timestamps (they come from one `/proc/stat` read, ADR-008); tolerate ±period/2 jitter by bucket index, not exact equality. Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E19: 5 and 10 minute ranges read the 1 Hz tier (TIER_1HZ series selection)
description:
## Context
From P2 the engine publishes a second `SeriesView` per series holding the per-second maximum over the last 10 minutes. Ranges up to 60 s read the fast tier; 300 s and 600 s read the 1 Hz tier. The chart picks the tier from `range_ns` when resolving series. Sources: PERF-016; PERF-017; R-016; ADR-003 ring tiers; UI-PRF-001 "Data binding" (`TIER_1HZ` metric flag bit).

## Deliverable

- `tl_model::ids::MetricId::with_tier_1hz(self) -> MetricId` and `is_tier_1hz` are E03's (plan file open item 2 fixes the bit); this bead uses them. The `ChartGeometryKey` already includes `range_ns`, so switching range rebuilds once.

title: E19: hover readout: marker, dots and the value box (chart/hover.rs)
description:
## Context
On large graphs and minigraph cards, hovering shows a vertical marker pinned to the nearest sample time, a dot per series, and a box with the time offset, each series value, avg, peak and the sample count. The chart gets a hitbox only when hover is enabled. Sources: PERF-023; UI-PRF-004 (anatomy, states, interaction, build); ADR-009 rule 1.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/chart/hover.rs`:

```rust
pub struct HoverState { pub pinned_t_ns: Option<u64>, pub index: Option<usize>, pub lines: SmallVec<[CachedLine; 5]>, pub last_index: Option<usize> }
pub fn nearest_index(samples: &[Sample], t_ns: u64) -> Option<usize>;   // binary search by t_ns, nearest of the two neighbours, only VALID samples
pub fn pointer_time(map: &TimeMap, plot_right_physical: f32, x_physical: f32) -> u64;  // right_edge_ns − (plot_right − x) × range_ns / plot_width
pub fn offset_text(dt_ns: u64, range_ns: u64, out: &mut String);   // "-12 s" for ranges ≤ 60 s; "-4 m 12 s" for 300 and 600 s
pub struct Stats { pub avg: f32, pub peak: f32, pub samples: u32 }
pub fn window_stats(samples: &[Sample], from: usize) -> Stats;      // over VALID samples in the visible window of the first series
pub fn paint(window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App, state: &mut HoverState, p: &HoverPaint);
```

Element changes (`chart/element.rs`):
- `prepaint`: when `spec.hover`, `insert_hitbox(plot, HitboxBehavior::Normal)` and return `Some(hitbox)`.
- `paint`: when the hitbox is hovered, register `window.on_mouse_event::<MouseMoveEvent>` that sets `pinned_t_ns = pointer_time(..)` and `cx.notify(view)`; `on_mouse_event::<MouseDownEvent>` clears the pin; window deactivation (`!window.is_window_active()`) clears it on the next paint. When `pinned_t_ns` is set and at least one valid sample is in view: compute `index = nearest_index(series0, pinned_t_ns)`, `x = x(t_index)` (recomputed every frame so the marker moves left with the data), paint inside `window.paint_layer(box_bounds, ..)`: a 1 physical px vertical quad in `text_secondary` at alpha 0.8 over the plot height; per series a dot (circle quad radius 3 px with `corner_radii` 3, series line colour, 1 px `window_bg` border); the box: `menu_bg` fill, 1 px `divider` border, `r_sm`, padding `sp3`, min width 140, placed 12 px right of the marker, flipped to the left when `x + 12 + box_w > plot.right`, clamped vertically inside the box bounds; lines: offset text `t_xs` 500 `text_primary`; per series a 12 × 2 swatch (dashed when the series is dashed), label (`labels.legend[i].0`, or the heading when no legend), value right-aligned `tnum` via `labels::format_value`; then "avg 18.2%  peak 61.0%" and "600 samples" in `t_xs` `text_secondary` (first series only). Lines re-shape only when `index != last_index`.
- Hidden when the pointer leaves the plot (`!hitbox.is_hovered`), on any mouse button down, and when the window is not active.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `spec.hover == false` **When** prepaint runs **Then** no hitbox is inserted.
- **Given** samples at 0, 100, 200 ms and `t = 140 ms` **When** `nearest_index` runs **Then** 1; at `t = 160 ms` 2; with sample 2 invalid, 1.
- **Given** `range = 60 s` and `dt = 12.4 s` **When** `offset_text` runs **Then** `"-12 s"`; with `range = 300 s` and `dt = 252 s`, `"-4 m 12 s"`.
- **Given** a hover at a sample whose x is 20 px from the plot's right edge **When** painted **Then** the box's right edge ≤ `plot.right` (flipped left) (`hover_box_flips_at_right_edge`).
- **Given** a chart in `WarmingUp` **When** hovered **Then** nothing is painted by `hover::paint` (`hover_hidden_without_valid_samples`).
- **Given** a mouse-down inside the plot **When** the next paint runs **Then** the marker is gone.
- **Given** two consecutive frames with the same `index` **When** painted **Then** `shape_line` is not called again.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/chart/hover.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-ui/src/chart/element.rs`: change (hitbox, events, paint call)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_chart.rs`: change

## Tests
- `ui_chart.rs::hover_no_hitbox_when_disabled`
- `ui_chart.rs::hover_picks_nearest_sample`
- `ui_chart.rs::hover_offset_text`
- `ui_chart.rs::hover_box_flips_at_right_edge`
- `ui_chart.rs::hover_hidden_without_valid_samples`
- `ui_chart.rs::hover_cleared_on_mouse_down`
- `ui_chart.rs::hover_reshapes_only_on_index_change`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: only `VALID` samples are candidates; invalid ones are skipped by `nearest_index`.
- Accessibility: the readout is text; keyboard users read the Details grid (avg and peak are not there; accepted per UI-PRF-004).
- Performance: one binary search per frame while hovered; shaping only on index change; no work when not hovered (no hitbox when `hover == false`).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
`paint_layer` is gpui-pre 0.3.7 `src/window.rs:4351`; `is_window_active` `window.rs:2807`; `MouseMoveEvent`, `MouseDownEvent` in `src/interactive.rs`. title: E19: curved lines hook (monotone cubic through decimated points)
description:
## Context
With `performance.curved_lines = true` (off by default) the straight segments become a monotone cubic (Fritsch-Carlson) through the decimated points, which never overshoots. Sources: PERF-021; UI-PRF-009.

## Deliverable
- `geometry.rs`: `pub fn emit_run(points: &[Pt], curved: bool, map, y.., builder: &mut PathBuilder)`; when `curved`, compute Fritsch-Carlson tangents per point and emit `cubic_bezier_to(c1, c2, p)` with 4 subdivisions per segment (each subdivision evaluates the cubic and emits `line_to`, so dashes and fills stay correct); fills follow the same curve.
- `BuildInput.curved: bool`, read by the element from `settings.performance.curved_lines` through `SettingsGlobal` (E20-A2); `style_version` already bumps on settings change, so toggling rebuilds once.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** points `[0, 100, 0, 100]` **When** emitted curved **Then** no emitted vertex has `value > 100` or `< 0` (`monotone_curve_never_overshoots`).
- **Given** 10 points on a straight line **When** emitted curved **Then** every emitted vertex lies on that line within 0.01 px.
- **Given** `curved_lines` toggled **When** painted **Then** geometry is rebuilt once.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/chart/geometry.rs`: change
- `crates/tl-ui/src/chart/element.rs`: change (read the setting)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/chart_geometry.rs`: change

- Privacy: N/A

title: E19: chart data types, ChartSpec, ChartCache and the ChartView skeleton
description:
## Context
Every graph surface in tasklens (page charts, per-core grid, sidebar cards, minigraph cards, tray graphs, mini window) is drawn by one custom GPUI element whose data contract is defined here. This bead writes the types only, so the geometry, scale, grid and paint beads can compile against one frozen shape. Sources: ADR-009 "Chart element" (struct shapes, rules 1 to 10), UI-PRF-001 (anatomy, states, data binding), UI-PRF-003 (`ChartLabels`, `ValueFormat`), UI-PRF-006 (`YScale` kinds), PERF-015, PERF-016, PERF-024, PERF-026, R-016.

    pub fills: SmallVec<[PathSet; 2]>,   // one per distinct fill colour (rule 7)

pub enum ValueFormat { Percent, Bytes, RateIec, RateNetwork, Mhz, Celsius, Watts, Rpm, Count }

title: E19: chart geometry, part 1: time mapping, run splitting, decimation, stale rule
description:
## Context
The chart element turns a `SeriesView` into points in chart-local pixels. This bead writes the pure functions that do that: the time mapping, splitting samples into runs at gaps, decimation with absolute-time buckets, and the stale rule. No GPUI paths yet (E19-003). Sources: ADR-009 rules 2, 3, 5; UI-PRF-005 (time mapping); UI-PRF-007 (decimation, gaps, stale); PERF-022; R-051.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/chart/geometry.rs` with:

```rust
pub struct TimeMap { pub anchor_ns: u64, pub right_edge_ns: u64, pub range_ns: u64, pub plot_width: f32 /* physical px */ }
impl TimeMap {
    pub fn px_per_ns(&self) -> f64;                         // plot_width / range_ns
    pub fn x_local(&self, t_ns: u64) -> f32;                // (t_ns − anchor_ns) × px_per_ns, chart-local, may be negative
    pub fn dx(&self, plot_right: f32) -> f32;               // plot_right − (right_edge_ns − anchor_ns) × px_per_ns  (ADR-009 rule 4)
}
pub fn right_edge_ns(now_boot_ns: u64, newest_ns: u64, period_ns: u64, smooth: bool) -> u64;
    // smooth: min(now_boot_ns − period_ns, newest_ns); else newest_ns (ADR-009 rule 5)
pub fn window_start(samples: &[Sample], right_edge_ns: u64, range_ns: u64, period_ns: u64) -> usize;
    // index of the first sample with t_ns ≥ right_edge_ns − range_ns − 2 × period_ns, found by walking back from the newest sample; 0 when every sample is inside
pub struct Run { pub start: usize, pub end: usize }   // half-open index range into samples; every sample VALID; no GAP_BEFORE inside except at start
pub fn split_runs(samples: &[Sample], from: usize, out: &mut SmallVec<[Run; 8]>);
    // a sample without VALID ends the run and is not part of any run; a sample with GAP_BEFORE starts a new run; consecutive invalid samples form one gap
pub struct Pt { pub t_ns: u64, pub value: f32 }
pub fn decimate(samples: &[Sample], run: Run, bucket_ns: u64, out: &mut Vec<Pt>);
    // bucket = t_ns / bucket_ns (absolute time). Per bucket with > 1 sample keep min and max in time order; always keep the run's first and last sample; a bucket with one sample keeps it. Output length ≤ 2 × buckets + 2.
pub fn bucket_ns(range_ns: u64, physical_width: u32) -> u64;   // max(range_ns / physical_width, 1)
pub fn is_stale(newest_ns: u64, now_boot_ns: u64, period_ns: u64) -> bool;  // now − newest > max(3 × period, 1_500_000_000)
pub fn stale_age_ns(newest_ns: u64, now_boot_ns: u64) -> u64;
```

All functions are allocation-free given the caller's buffers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 100 samples at 100 ms and `GAP_BEFORE` on sample 50 **When** `split_runs(samples, 0, out)` runs **Then** `out` has two runs `[0,50)` and `[50,100)`.
- **Given** samples 10 to 19 without `VALID` **When** `split_runs` runs **Then** the runs are `[0,10)` and `[20,n)` and no run contains index 10 to 19.
- **Given** 2,000 samples of value 0 with one sample of value 100 at index 1,000 and `bucket_ns` for 200 px **When** `decimate` runs **Then** the output contains a point with value 100 and has at most 402 points.
- **Given** the same series built twice with `right_edge_ns` 100 ms apart **When** `decimate` runs with the same `bucket_ns` **Then** every output point's bucket index `t_ns / bucket_ns` is identical in both outputs (no shimmer).
- **Given** `smooth = true`, `now = 10.000 s`, `newest = 9.950 s`, `period = 100 ms` **When** `right_edge_ns` runs **Then** it returns 9.900 s; with `smooth = false` it returns 9.950 s.
- **Given** `period = 100 ms` and `now − newest = 1.4 s` **When** `is_stale` runs **Then** false; at 1.6 s true; with `period = 1 s` and gap 2.9 s false, 3.1 s true.
- **Given** a 600-sample 10 Hz series and `range_ns = 60 s` **When** `window_start` runs **Then** it returns the index of the sample 60.2 s before the right edge (two periods of overscan) or 0.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/chart/geometry.rs`: create, the functions above
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/chart_geometry.rs`: create, the tests below

## Tests
- `chart_geometry.rs::chart_geometry_splits_runs_at_gaps`: two runs, as above.
- `chart_geometry.rs::invalid_samples_form_one_gap`: runs skip the invalid span.
- `chart_geometry.rs::chart_geometry_keeps_spike_under_decimation`: the 100 point survives, count bound holds.
- `chart_geometry.rs::chart_bucket_alignment_is_stable`: identical bucket indices 100 ms apart.
- `chart_geometry.rs::right_edge_is_one_period_behind`: the smooth and non-smooth values.
- `chart_geometry.rs::stale_threshold_matches_r051`: the four threshold cases.
- `chart_geometry.rs::decimation_point_count_bound`: 10,000 samples into 50 px gives ≤ 102 points.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: `VALID`, `GAP_BEFORE` and `STALE` flags are the only inputs; `STALE` samples stay in their run (E19-003 draws them at half alpha).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: O(n) per build over the visible window only; buffers are caller-owned and reused across rebuilds. This code runs 10 times per second per 10 Hz chart (ADR-014 `perf-cpu`).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
`Sample { t_ns: TimeNs, value: f32, flags: SampleFlags }` and the flag constants are `tl_model::series` (ADR-003). Use `u64` arithmetic for time and `f64` for `px_per_ns` (60 s × 10⁹ ns against 1,600 px loses precision in `f32`). Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E19: chart geometry, part 2: fill and stroke paths, stale sets, dotted gaps, merge by colour
description:
## Context
With runs and points in hand, the chart builds GPUI `Path`s once per geometry change and reuses them every frame. This bead writes the path emission into `ChartCache`: one closed fill polygon per run, one stroke per run, the half-alpha stale set, the dotted-gap spans, and merging of series that share a colour and dash pattern into one path. Sources: ADR-009 rules 2, 4, 6, 7; UI-PRF-001 (fill, line, gap, stale tail, overscan); UI-PRF-007 (flat continuation of the stale tail); PERF-026 (dash 5/5).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/chart/geometry.rs`:

```rust
pub struct BuildInput<'a> {
    pub series: &'a [(ChartSeries, Option<&'a SeriesView>)],   // spec series paired with the resolved views (None = absent)
    pub map: TimeMap,
    pub plot_height: f32,            // physical px
    pub y_min: f32, pub y_max: f32,  // from scale (E19-004)
    pub now_boot_ns: u64,
    pub stack: bool,                 // P2 (E19-012); false in this bead
}
pub fn build(input: &BuildInput, cache: &mut ChartCache, scratch: &mut Scratch);
pub struct Scratch { runs: SmallVec<[Run; 8]>, pts: Vec<Pt>, stale_pts: Vec<Pt> }  // reused across rebuilds; Default
pub fn y_of(value: f32, y_min: f32, y_max: f32, plot_height: f32) -> f32;  // plot_height − (value − y_min) / (y_max − y_min) × plot_height, clamped to 0..=plot_height
```

Rules implemented by `build`:
1. For each series: `from = window_start(..)`, `split_runs`, then per run `decimate` with `bucket_ns(range_ns, plot_width)`.
2. Fresh points (no `STALE` flag) go to the live paths; points with `STALE`, and the span from the last fresh sample to the right edge when `is_stale(..)`, go to the stale paths. The stale tail is a flat continuation: a point at `(right_edge_ns, last_fresh_value)` is appended so the line hangs at the last value.
3. Fill: `PathBuilder::fill()`; per run `move_to(x0, plot_height)`, `line_to` each point, `line_to(xn, plot_height)`, `close()`. Only when `ChartSeries.fill.is_some()`.
4. Stroke: `PathBuilder::stroke(line_width)`; `dash_array(&[px(5.0), px(5.0)])` when `dashed`; per run `move_to` first point then `line_to` the rest. A run with one point emits a 1 px horizontal segment at that point.
5. Merge: fills with equal `fill` colour share one `PathBuilder`; strokes with equal `(line, dashed)` share one. Builders are keyed in insertion order; the result is `cache.fills` / `cache.strokes` as `PathSet`s. Each `PathSet.path` is `builder.build().ok()`; an `Err` (empty path) adds no set.
6. Gaps: between consecutive runs of the first series, push `x_local(last_of_run_a) .. x_local(first_of_run_b)` into `cache.gaps`. Also from the window's left edge to the first run when the first visible sample is not at the left edge by more than 2 periods, and from the last run to the right edge when the series is stale (the gap starts where the stale tail ends; UI-PRF-007 "then a gap").
7. Set `cache.anchor_ns = map.anchor_ns`, `cache.px_per_ns`, `cache.y_min`, `cache.y_max`.
8. All x and y are chart-local physical pixels; `build` never reads `window.scale_factor()` (the element converts).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** one series with a gap at index 50 and `fill` set **When** `build` runs **Then** `cache.fills.len() == 1`, that path has two subpaths (two polygons), `cache.strokes.len() == 1`, and `cache.gaps.len() == 1` spanning from sample 49's x to sample 50's x.
- **Given** two series with the same `fill` and `line` colours and `dashed == false` **When** `build` runs **Then** `cache.fills.len() == 1` and `cache.strokes.len() == 1`.
- **Given** two series with the same `line` colour where one is `dashed` **When** `build` runs **Then** `cache.strokes.len() == 2`.
- **Given** a series whose newest sample is 5 s old at `period = 1 s` **When** `build` runs **Then** `cache.stale_strokes` has one set whose path's right-most vertex x equals `map.x_local(right_edge_ns)` and whose y equals `y_of(last_value)`.
- **Given** a series with no `fill` **When** `build` runs **Then** `cache.fills` is empty.
- **Given** `value = 0` and `y_min = 0, y_max = 100, plot_height = 100` **When** `y_of` runs **Then** it returns 100; `value = 100` returns 0; `value = 150` returns 0 (clamped).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/chart/geometry.rs`: change, add `build`, `BuildInput`, `Scratch`, `y_of`
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/chart_geometry.rs`: change, add the tests below

## Tests
- `chart_geometry.rs::build_two_subpaths_and_one_gap`: the gap case; subpath count is read from `Path.vertices` being split into two fans (count `move_to` through a test-only `PathBuilder` wrapper that records commands, or assert `cache.gaps.len() == 1` and `fills.len() == 1`).
- `chart_geometry.rs::build_merges_equal_colours`: 1 fill set, 1 stroke set.
- `chart_geometry.rs::build_separates_dashed`: 2 stroke sets.
- `chart_geometry.rs::stale_flat_continuation_present`: right-most stale vertex at the right edge and last value.
- `chart_geometry.rs::gap_dotted_span_coordinates`: `gaps[0]` start and end equal the two sample x values within 0.01 px.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `PathBuilder::build` errors (lyon tessellation failure on a degenerate path) are ignored per set; the chart draws without that set and logs nothing (empty paths are normal for a one-sample series).
- Validity: `STALE` flag and the `is_stale` rule decide the stale set; invalid samples never produce vertices.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one `PathBuilder` per distinct colour (2 to 4 builders per chart); `Scratch` buffers are reused so steady state allocates only inside lyon's tessellator. Budget: a 600-point stroke plus fill tessellates in well under 100 µs; ADR-014 `perf-cpu` rebuilds at most 3 paths per 100 ms tick (the grid element, E19-010, builds through this same function).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
`PathBuilder` is gpui-pre 0.3.7 `src/path_builder.rs`: `stroke(width)` line 88, `fill()` line 96, `dash_array` line 108, `move_to` 125, `line_to` 131, `close` 199, `build` 244. Clone-and-translate at paint time follows gpui-component `crates/base/src/plot/path_cache.rs` lines 44 to 56 (`translated`): the path is built at a zero origin here. Build rule: run cargo through `flock -w 7200 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/heavy-build.lock" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --slice=builds.slice -p MemoryHigh=16G -p MemoryMax=18G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p OOMPolicy=kill env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo ...`.

title: E19: Y scale rules and axis rounding (chart/scale.rs)
description:
## Context
Each chart maps values to pixels through a `YScale`. Percentages are fixed; rates rise at once and fall only after 10 s below half the ceiling; temperatures are sticky in 5 °C steps; power and clocks are sticky up or fixed at a hardware maximum. This bead implements every kind and the axis-maximum text. Sources: ADR-009 rule 9; UI-PRF-006 (the kind table and rules); PERF-018; PERF-019; PERF-030; canonical table (d) (axis rounding).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/chart/scale.rs`:

```rust
pub struct ScaleState {
    pub ceiling: f32,                 // current max (AutoRate, StickyUp, StickyTemp max, Symmetric m)
    pub floor: f32,                   // StickyTemp min; 0 otherwise
    pub below_half_since: Option<u64>, // boot ns when the visible max first stayed below ceiling / 2
    pub initialised: bool,
}
pub struct ScaleResult { pub y_min: f32, pub y_max: f32, pub axis_text: Option<SharedString> }
pub fn compute(scale: &YScale, visible_min: f32, visible_max: f32, now_boot_ns: u64, state: &mut ScaleState, fmt: ValueFormat, network_unit: NetworkUnit, out_text: &mut String) -> ScaleResult;
```

Rules per kind (`visible_*` are over the valid samples in the window; absent samples give `visible_max = 0`):

| Kind | `y_min..y_max` | `axis_text` |
|---|---|---|
| `Fixed { min, max }` | `min..max` | `None` |
| `FixedTotal(total)` | `0..total` (`total ≤ 0` gives `0..1`) | `None` |
| `Commit(limit)` | `0..max(limit, visible_max)` | `Some("{p}%")` with `p = round(y_max / limit × 100)` only when `visible_max > limit`; else `None` |
| `AutoRate { iec }` | `0..ceiling`; `ceiling = ceil_pow2(visible_max)` when `iec`, else `ceil_125(visible_max)`; rises at once when the new ceiling is above `state.ceiling`; when `visible_max < state.ceiling / 2` record `below_half_since` (keep the earliest); when that has been set for ≥ 10 s, set `ceiling` to the new lower value and clear it; when `visible_max ≥ ceiling / 2` clear it. Minimum ceiling: 1 KiB/s for `iec`, 1 Kbps for bits | the ceiling formatted with its unit through `tl_model::units` (`"100 Mbps"`, `"4 GiB/s"`) |
| `LinkSpeed(bps)` | `0..bps` | `"1 Gbps"` style (`units::fmt_rate_network` of the link speed) |
| `StickyTemp` | first call: `35..45`; `y_max = max(y_max, ceil5(visible_max))`; `y_min = min(y_min, floor5(visible_min))` but never above 35; falls after 10 s below half the span with the same timer rule as `AutoRate` | `"{y_max} °C"` |
| `StickyUp { hw_max: Some(m) }` | `0..m` | `"{m} W"`, `"{m} MHz"`, `"{m} RPM"` by `fmt` |
| `StickyUp { hw_max: None }` | `0..ceil_125(visible_max)`, never falls | same |
| `Stacked(n)` | `0..100 × n` | `"{100 n}%"` |
| `Symmetric` | `−m..m`, `m = ceil_125(max(|visible_min|, |visible_max|))`, min `m = 1` | `"±{m} W"` |

`ceil_pow2(f64) -> f64` and `ceil_125(f64) -> f64` come from `tl_model::units` (E03-A1; `ceil_125(1234) = 2000`, `ceil_125(60) = 100`, `ceil_125(0.3) = 0.5`, `ceil_pow2(3 MiB) = 4 MiB`). `ceil5(x) = ceil(x / 5) × 5`, `floor5` likewise, defined here. `NetworkUnit` is `tl_model::settings` `units.network` (`Bits | Bytes`): `AutoRate` for network uses `iec = (unit == Bytes)`, which the owner sets in `YScale`; this function only formats. The scale is computed once per geometry rebuild (E19-007 calls it), not per frame.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `AutoRate { iec: false }`, state empty, `visible_max = 3.2e6` **When** `compute` runs **Then** `y_max = 5e6` and `axis_text == "5 Mbps"`.
- **Given** the state ceiling 5e6 and `visible_max = 7e6` **When** `compute` runs **Then** `y_max = 1e7` at once.
- **Given** ceiling 1e7, `visible_max = 2e6` at `now = 0`, then again at `now = 9 s` **When** `compute` runs **Then** `y_max` stays 1e7; at `now = 10 s` it becomes 2e6's ceiling `2e6`.
- **Given** ceiling 1e7, `visible_max = 2e6` at `now = 0` and `visible_max = 6e6` at `now = 5 s` **When** `compute` runs **Then** `below_half_since` is cleared and the ceiling stays 1e7.
- **Given** `AutoRate { iec: true }` and `visible_max = 3 × 1024²` **When** `compute` runs **Then** `y_max = 4 × 1024²` and `axis_text == "4 MiB/s"`.

title: E19: AnimationDriver with FrameStats and stall detection (anim.rs)
description:
## Context
Smooth graphs slide at the compositor's frame rate, but only while a visible chart is moving, and one `on_next_frame` per window drives every chart. The driver also records frame statistics for the phase-0 bench and detects the zed#64499 stall. Sources: ADR-009 "Animation driver"; ADR-010 "zed#64499 mitigation" step 1 and "Hidden state"; ADR-014 measurement tools; UI-PRF-005.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/anim.rs` and the line `pub mod anim;` in `crates/tl-ui/src/lib.rs` (chain edit).

```rust
pub struct AnimationDriver {
    requests: FxHashSet<EntityId>,
    armed: bool,
    last_frame: Option<Instant>,
    pending_since: Option<Instant>,     // when the current armed request was made
    hidden: bool,
    pub stats: FrameStats,
}
#[derive(Default, Clone)]
pub struct FrameStats {
    pub requested: u64,     // on_next_frame arms
    pub frames: u64,        // callbacks received
    pub stalls: u64,        // armed and no callback for 250 ms while visible
    pub missed: u64,        // callback interval > 1.5 × period_hint
    pub period_hint_ns: u64, // set by the bench (6_944_444 at 144 Hz); 0 = no missed-frame counting
    pub last_interval_ns: u64,
    pub sampling: bool,
    pub samples: Vec<FrameSample>,   // only while sampling; capacity 65_536, then stops growing
}
pub struct FrameSample { pub interval_ns: u64, pub thread_cpu_ns: u64 }
impl AnimationDriver {
    pub fn new(cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> Self;
    pub fn request(&mut self, id: EntityId, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>);
    pub fn set_hidden(&mut self, hidden: bool);     // called by the hub's hidden-state timer (ADR-010); hidden stops arming; the next request after visible re-arms
    pub fn is_armed(&self) -> bool;
    pub fn take_stats(&mut self) -> FrameStats;      // bench: copy and reset counters
    pub fn global(window: &Window, cx: &App) -> Entity<AnimationDriver>;  // the driver of this window, stored in the window's root view state by the owner (one per window, created by the window's constructor)
}
```

Behaviour:
- `request(id)`: insert `id`. If not `armed` and not `hidden`: `window.on_next_frame(move |window, cx| driver.update(cx, |d, cx| d.on_frame(window, cx)))`, set `armed = true`, `pending_since = Some(now)`, `stats.requested += 1`.
- `on_frame`: `armed = false`; take the request set (keeping capacity: `std::mem::take` then `requests = taken; requests.clear()` after notifying, or drain); `stats.frames += 1`; interval from `last_frame` into `last_interval_ns` and `missed` when `period_hint_ns > 0 && interval > period_hint_ns × 3 / 2`; when `sampling`, push `FrameSample { interval_ns, thread_cpu_ns }` where `thread_cpu_ns` is `tl_model::time::thread_cpu_ns()` (see Notes); then `cx.notify(id)` for every id. Charts re-request inside their render, which re-arms.
- Stall detection: a 250 ms `cx.spawn` timer loop runs while `armed`; if `armed && !hidden && pending_since.elapsed() > 250 ms` it logs `tracing::warn!(target: "tasklens::frame", "frame stall", elapsed_ms)` once per stall and increments `stats.stalls`, then waits for the callback. A stall never re-arms by itself.
- When nothing requests, no frame is scheduled and the timer loop stops.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a driver with no requests **When** 500 ms pass in a `TestAppContext` **Then** `stats.requested == 0` and `stats.frames == 0`.
- **Given** 32 entities each calling `request` in one frame **When** the frame callback runs **Then** `stats.requested == 1`, every one of the 32 entities was notified once, and `is_armed()` is false afterwards.
- **Given** an armed driver **When** `set_hidden(true)` is called and entities call `request` **Then** no new `on_next_frame` is armed (`stats.requested` unchanged) until `set_hidden(false)` and the next `request`.
- **Given** an armed driver and no frame callback for 300 ms (the test platform does not deliver frames) **When** the timer runs **Then** `stats.stalls == 1` and a `tasklens::frame` warning was logged (capture with `tracing_test` or a test subscriber).
- **Given** `period_hint_ns = 6_944_444` and two callbacks 12 ms apart **When** the second runs **Then** `stats.missed == 1`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/anim.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-ui/src/lib.rs`: add `pub mod anim;` (chain edit)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_anim.rs`: create

## Tests
- `ui_anim.rs::driver_requests_no_frame_when_static` (ADR-009 verification).
- `ui_anim.rs::driver_one_frame_for_many_charts` (32 requesters, one arm, 32 notifies).
- `ui_anim.rs::driver_hidden_stops_arming`.
- `ui_anim.rs::driver_counts_stall_after_250ms`.
- `ui_anim.rs::driver_counts_missed_frames`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: reduced motion is decided by the charts (they do not request); the driver does not read `App::reduce_motion()`.
- Performance: one `on_next_frame` per window per frame; `FxHashSet` keeps its capacity so steady state allocates nothing; `samples` is pre-allocated to 65,536 when sampling starts.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
`Window::on_next_frame` is gpui-pre 0.3.7 `src/window.rs:2602`; `request_animation_frame` (line 2622) must not be used (ADR-009: no other code requests frames). `tl-ui`'s allowed dependencies (ADR-001) do not include `rustix`, so the thread CPU clock comes from `tl_model::time::thread_cpu_ns()` (open item 10 in the plan file: E03 confirms or adds it; until it exists, `thread_cpu_ns` is 0 behind a `// TODO(E03)` and the bench reports `frame_cpu_ms` as null). The window's hidden flag comes from the hub's 500 ms timer (E16-A1, ADR-010); that bead calls `set_hidden`. title: E19: chart grid quads, baseline, outline and dotted gaps (chart/grid.rs)
description:
## Context
Besides the data paths, a chart paints a background, a scrolling vertical grid placed from absolute time, three horizontal lines, a baseline, a 1 px outline and dotted baselines across gaps. These are all quads. Sources: ADR-009 rule 8; UI-PRF-001 (grid, fill order, gap, baseline, outline, box); PERF-015; UI-FND-003 (`hairline`, radii).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/chart/grid.rs`:

```rust
pub struct GridPaint<'a> { pub plot: Bounds<Pixels>, pub box_bounds: Bounds<Pixels>, pub map: &'a TimeMap, pub dx: Pixels, pub scale_factor: f32, pub theme: &'a TlTheme, pub style: GridStyle, pub outline_color: Hsla, pub radius: Pixels }
pub fn paint_background(window: &mut Window, box_bounds: Bounds<Pixels>, bg: Hsla, radius: Pixels);
pub fn paint_grid(window: &mut Window, p: &GridPaint);      // vertical and horizontal hairlines
pub fn paint_baseline(window: &mut Window, p: &GridPaint); // 1 physical px along the plot bottom, outline colour @ 0.40
pub fn paint_gaps(window: &mut Window, p: &GridPaint, gaps: &[Range<f32>]); // dotted baseline: 1 × 1 physical px quads every 3 physical px within each span, colour outline_color @ 0.40
pub fn paint_outline(window: &mut Window, p: &GridPaint);  // border-only quad, 1 physical px, outline colour @ 0.40, corner radius `radius`
pub fn grid_k_range(map: &TimeMap) -> (u64, u64);           // the k values with k × (range_ns / 10) inside [right_edge − range, right_edge]
```

Rules:
- Background: `paint_quad(fill(box_bounds, bg).corner_radii(radius))` where `bg` is `theme.graph.chart_bg` (ADR-009 theme model: `chart_bg` is the plot background of every chart; `ChartSpec.background` picks `window_bg`/`list_bg` for the 1 px frame ring outside the plot only).
- Vertical grid: for `k` in `grid_k_range`, `x = plot.left + px((map.x_local(k × step) + dx_local) / scale_factor)` where `step = range_ns / 10`; a quad `hairline` wide (1 physical px: `px(1.0 / scale_factor)`), full plot height, colour `theme.graph.grid`. Lines outside the plot are skipped.
- Horizontal grid: at 25%, 50%, 75% of the plot height, `hairline` high, full plot width, same colour.
- No grid when the plot height is under 40 logical px (tray; sidebar cards are 56 high and keep it).
- Baseline: `hairline` high quad at `plot.bottom − hairline`, colour `outline_color` with alpha 0.40.
- Gaps: for each span `a..b` (chart-local physical px), quads at `x = a + 3 i` physical px while `x < b`, each 1 × 1 physical px at the plot bottom, same colour as the baseline; the span is clipped to the plot.
- Outline: `paint_quad(quad(box_bounds, radius, transparent_black(), Edges::all(hairline), outline_color.alpha(0.40), BorderStyle::Solid))`.
- Paint order is the element's (E19-007): background, grid, fills, strokes, gaps, baseline, outline.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `range_ns = 60 s` and `right_edge = 123.4 s` **When** `grid_k_range` runs **Then** it returns `k` in `11..=20` (the times 66 s to 120 s, step 6 s).
- **Given** a plot 600 × 300 at scale 1.0 **When** `paint_grid` runs in a headless window **Then** `painted_quads()` contains 3 horizontal quads of height 1 and width 600 at y = 75, 150, 225 and 10 or 11 vertical quads of width 1.
- **Given** a plot of height 32 **When** `paint_grid` runs **Then** no quads are painted.
- **Given** one gap span `100.0..130.0` **When** `paint_gaps` runs at scale 1.0 **Then** 10 quads of 1 × 1 are painted at x = 100, 103, …, 127.
- **Given** scale 1.1 **When** `paint_baseline` runs **Then** the quad height is `1 / 1.1` logical px.

- Performance: 3 to 13 grid quads plus up to 2 × (gap length / 3) dotted quads per frame; no allocation.
- Privacy: N/A

`paint_quad` is gpui-pre 0.3.7 `src/window.rs:4502`; `fill`, `quad`, `Edges`, `BorderStyle` are in `src/elements` and `src/style.rs`. `TlTheme` and `GraphPalette` (`grid`, `chart_bg`) are E17-A1; `UiMetrics::hairline(window)` is E15-A1 (UI-FND-003). `painted_quads()` is the headless test helper from E16's `testing/render.rs`; if it is not available yet, assert through a test-only `QuadRecorder` trait object passed instead of `Window` (keep the paint functions generic over a `trait QuadSink { fn quad(&mut self, PaintQuad) }` implemented for `Window`).
